title: Cheonggyecheon Stream
short_description:
Cheonggyecheon Stream is an 11 km-long stream that runs through downtown Seoul. Created as part of an urban renewal project, Cheonggyecheon Stream is a restoration of the stream that was once there during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910). The stream was covered with an elevated highway after the Korean War (1950-1953), as part of the country's post-war economic development. Then in 2003, the elevated highway was removed to restore the stream to its present form today. The stream starts from Cheonggye Plaza, a popular cultural arts venue, and passes under a total of 22 bridges before flowing into the Hangang River, with many attractions along the way.

Cheonggyecheon’s turbulent history is on display at the Cheonggyecheon Museum, which opened in September 2005. The museum offers visitors the chance to learn about the many changes the stream has seen, including being buried underground and being restored. The story is told with the help of a scale-model and period photographs.

Frequently Asked Questions about Cheonggyecheon Stream
Is the Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade always open?
Yes. The Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. However, in the case of rain, access may be restricted for safety reasons.
What festivals are held at the Cheonggyecheon Stream?
The "Seoul Lantern Festival" is held annually at the end of the year around the Cheonggyecheon Stream area. (As of 2026)
What is the nearest subway station to Cheonggyecheon Stream?
There are a total of 11 subway stations connected to Cheonggyecheon Stream: City Hall Station (Subway Line 1, 2), Jonggak Station, Jongno 3-ga Station, Jongno 5-ga Station, Dongdaemun Station, Dongmyo Station, Sinseol-dong Station (Subway Line 1), Eulji-ro 1-ga Station, Eulji-ro 3-ga Station, Eulji-ro 4-ga Station, Dongdaemun History and Culture Park Station, Yongdu Station (Subway Line 2).

title: Lotte Duty Free Shop
short_description:
Global travel retail brand Lotte Duty Free Shop is a one-stop shopping complex providing shoppers a wide range of products. There are 19 locations in 7 countries, with an online website. 

The main store is on 9-12F of Lotte Department Store located in Myeong-dong, which is the center of Seoul.  They offers luxury brands such as HERMES, LOUIS VUITTON, CHANEL, CARTIER, and others. Also, you can enjoy a unique experience of purchasing beauty products using innovative digital technology at the Smart Store on floor 1. 

There is Star Avenue on floor 1, which promote K-Culture more actively in time for global customers to travel to Korea. You can find handprints of Lotte Duty Free models and Mirror Zone, where you can take selfies with the models, at Star Avenue. Also, Hi-Five zone in Star Avenue shows individual videos of Lotte Duty Free models.

title: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
short_description: The Sejong Center for the Performing Arts is a multipurpose arts center that is one of the world's best performance venues. The exterior of the building blends traditional Korean architecture with modern design the building spans six stories tall with three underground floors. The center houses several theaters, the largest being the Grand Theater, art museum, a convention center, a conference hall, and meeting rooms. There is also an outdoor fountain and a lovely garden on the grounds.

title: Myeongdong Real Gun Shooting Range
short_description:
The Myeongdong Real Gun Shooting Range is an indoor live firing range located in Myeong-dong. With over a 100 firearms to choose from, visitors can try their best to shoot at targets with a real gun.

※ Visitors must present photo ID in order to shoot at the range. Participants must be at least 14 years old.

title: Lotte World Ice Rink
short_description:
The Lotte World Ice Rink is located inside the Lotte World indoor theme park. Open year-round, the skating rink has seating able to accommodate up to 850 people and many other facilities to enjoy. Facilities include a food court offering international cuisine and a game room. Visitors can also take lessons in figure skating and speed skating.


Frequently Asked Questions about Lotte World Ice Rink
How much is the Lotte World Ice Rink pass?
Lotte World Ice Rink pass prices are as follows. (As of 2026)

  • • Weekdays : General admission 15,000 KRW / Children 13,000 KRW
  • • Weekends and public holidays : General admission 18,000 KRW / Children 15,000 KRW
What are the opening hours of the Lotte World Ice Rink?
Lotte World Ice Rink’s opening hours are as follows. (As of 2026)


  • • Sunday-Thursday : 11:00 ~ 20:50
  • • Friday-Saturday and public holidays : 11:00 ~ 21:20

title: Bongeunsa Temple
short_description:
Bongeunsa is a Buddhist temple founded in 794 during the Silla (one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea) period. The temple has more than 1,000 years of history and has many interesting historic and cultural features, including woodblock carvings of the Avatamsaka Sutra (Flower Garland Sutra). The temple is also a very popular tourist destination, offering various programs relating to traditional Korean Buddhist culture, in a variety of languages.


Bongeunsa is more than a just temple. It provides a place to relax for busy city people and also gives people a chance to reflect upon themselves. The templestay program gives an opportunity to experience everyday life in the temple, which includes traditional Korean Buddhist culture and practices. Visitors can experience some simple Buddhist practices such as the daily dawn service, Korean Zen meditation, Dado (a tea drinking ceremony), and Balwoogongyang (a Buddhist meal with traditional bowls).  Every May on Buddha's birthday, Bongeunsa holds the Lotus Lantern Festival on nearby Samseong-don g.

title: Culture Station Seoul 284
short_description: Culture Station Seoul 284 is a multipurpose arts and cultural complex. It was once known simply as Seoul Station and it was the city's biggest rail station. The station was built during the Japanese colonial era. The first floor is used as a space for performances and exhibitions. The second floor is used for exhibitions, seminars, and meetings. Though admission to Culture Station Seoul 284 is free, performances and exhibitions may charge admission.

title: Galleria Luxury Hall
short_description: Galleria Department Store features two luxury halls, EAST and WEST. Galleria Luxury Hall WEST is a store targeting young people, while Galleria Luxury Hall EAST (or Galleria EAST) offers only carefully premium select brands, making it a luxury department store that showcases popular fashion labels. Galleria EAST also provides differentiated services, capturing the interest of foreign visitors, as well as locals, as a prized shopping destination.

title: The War Memorial of Korea
short_description:
The War Memorial of Korea was established to remember the Korean War (6. 25. 1950 - 7. 27.1953) and to symbolize the desire for peaceful reunification of Korea. The museum consists of 6 individual exhibition halls and a combat experience room, a screening room and an outdoor exhibition area with memorial statues.  The Statue of Brothers located in the south-west corner of the outdoor exhibition area at the museum symbolizes the Korean War and the hope for reunification. The statue depicts a scene where a family’s oldest son, a South Korean soldier and his younger brother, a North Korean soldier meet on a battlefield. Their embrace expresses reconciliation, love and forgiveness.

There is also an extensive garden area around the memorial with an artificial waterfall, and a lake where visitors can picnic whilst enjoying the beautiful landscape. The museum houses more than 10,000 artifacts in the indoor and outdoor exhibition areas. It takes visitors about three hours to complete the tour. The first floor exhibition hall features a history of war from prehistoric times up to the Korean War. The combat experience room on the third floor offers visitors a special opportunity to experience a simulated life and death situation on the battlefield through special effects.

title: Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery
short_description:
Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery is the final resting place for Korea's western residents, including Dr. Horace Allen, the first director of Gwanghyewon, the first western-style hospital in Korea, founded in 1885. The cemetery is known as Foreign Missionary Cemetery because of the number of foreign missionaries buried here. Tombs and headstones were built in a western style creating an exotic atmosphere. The cemetery is located near the Hangang (River), an ideal spot for taking a pleasant stroll.


Yanghwajin Foreigners' Cemetery is situated on the other side of Yanghwajin, opposite the martyrs’ shrine. It is regarded as a Protestant shrine because many Protestant missionaries are buried there.  The “100th Anniversary Memorial Church” was established in Yanhwajin by the “Council for the 100th Anniversary of the Korean Church” to commemorate a century of missionary work in Korea. 


Many of the foreigners who have contributed to the story of modern Korean history are buried in the Yanghwajin cemetery, such as Thomas Bethell, the founder of Daehan Maeil Sinbo (Newspaper); Mary Scranton, the founder of Ewha Hakdang (a mission school for girls, now Ewha Womans University); and Henry Appenzeller, the founder of Chungdong First Methodist Church.


A guided tour in English or Japanese is available in Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery when booked in advance. These are conducted four times a day (10:00, 11:30, 14:00, 15:30) except during the New Year's holiday, Chuseok holiday and on Christmas day. 


Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery is located in Hapjeong-dong, Mapo-gu. It is a haven for foreign missionaries and their families who loved, and wished to lie in, Korea. The cemetery is managed by 100th Anniversary Memorial Church and contains Mission Memorial Hall.

title: Leeum Museum of Art
short_description:
The Leeum Museum of Art is the perfect place to enjoy traditional and contemporary art created by Korean and international artists. Most of the exhibits on display at the museum are based on the large collection of the founder, the late Lee Byeong-cheol, once president of the Samsung Group. Three world-renowned architects, Maria Botta, Jean Nouvel, and Rem Koolhaas, were commissioned to design the outstanding museum complex. The name Leeum is the acronym of the family name of its founder, “Lee” and an abbreviated word for museum, “um”. The museum is composed of three individual buildings linked together as a composite complex. Museum 1 showcases traditional Korean arts and crafts such as calligraphy, ceramic arts and metal craft work, while Museum 2 displays dynamic modern and contemporary art by domestic and international artists, this section includes the Samsung Child Education & Cultural Center which offers cultural education for children.  In the museum basement, a sunken garden and Gabion wall, which is a cylindrical metal container filled with stones, can be found. Art, architecture and nature exist together in perfect harmony.





Frequently Asked Questions about Leeum Museum of Art
Do I need to make a reservation to visit the Leeum Museum of Art?
Leeum Museum of Art operates under a reservation system. Reservations can be made 14 days before the visit. The maximum number of people per reservation is four. On-site ticketing is possible and limited to remaining tickets per reservation time (As of 2025)
Is the Leeum Museum of Art digital guide available for free?
Digital guides that automatically provide explanations when one approaches the exhibits can be borrowed free of charge. The devices are available to elementary school students and anyone older. You must present an identification card such as a passport or resident registration card. The digital guide is available in Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese. (As of 2025)
Can I visit the Leeum Museum of Art permanent exhibitions for free?
Yes. Permanent exhibitions are free. They are also operated under a reservation system, so please make a reservation before visiting. (As of 2025)

title: Space C
short_description:
Space C is a venue created and run by Coreana, a Korean cosmetics company. It spans 10 levels comprising a museum, gallery, beauty shop, café, and rooftop garden. On the 5th and 6th floors, visitors will find Korea’s largest cosmetics museum where visitors can learn about the history and development of Korean cosmetics. Space C also houses a large number of cosmetics-related artworks and other artifacts.


The Cosmetics Museum is Space C’s main exhibition hall, presenting the history of Korean cosmetics through a collection of more than 5,300 beauty-related items used by women in the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910). The C Gallery on the first basement level is a traditional exhibition hall that displays fine art while C Cube on the second basement level plays host to more experimental work. The museum café on the 1st floor reflects the nature of its setting with art exhibits created from everyday objects, giving visitors the chance to continue their cultural odyssey even as they relax. The Beauty Space on the 2nd to 4th floors is a peaceful haven where women can consult a beauty therapist in the skin clinic and indulge in a range of body treatments. The Outdoor Cosmetics Museum on the rooftop of Space C is a garden featuring a collection of important plants which provide key ingredients for the cosmetics industry. From here, visitors can also enjoy spectacular views of the Seoul skyline.

title: LATT Children’s Theater
short_description: LATT Children’s Theater is the only English-language children's theater in Korea. Located in Dogok-dong, the theater is a cultural complex for children that also offers a fun way to learn English. Because the stage is right in front of the theater's seats, the arrangement feels familiar and friendly. In addition to performances, the theater hosts children's workshops on in which children can learn how to create English plays.

title: Seoul Museum of Art (Seosomun Main Building)
short_description:
The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) opened in 1988 and has earned a reputation as one of Korea’s leading art venues with a series of world-famous exhibitions. Situated in the center of Seoul, its convenient location and outstanding collections attract large numbers of locals and tourists. The specially-designed building features large windows that fill the interior with natural light. This attracts not only tourists but also artists and even movie directors, some of whom have used the location for filming.


Since it was established in 1988, the main museum building has been relocated to Seosomun-dong in Seoul. The museum has a variety of annexes such as SeMA Gyeonghuigung, located on the historic site of Gyeonghuigung Palace, and the Nam Seoul Annex Building, which is situated in a building that was once the Belgian Embassy. The museum also runs the Naji Art Studio which offers workshops and financial support to new generations of Korean artists to nurture their creativity.


The beautiful Renaissance façade which forms the entrance to the museum was originally part of the Supreme Court, built in 1928. Today it is better known as the iconic image of the Seoul Museum of Art. In March 2006, the arch and the beautifully constructed museum building were designated as Cultural Property No. 237 in recognition of their great historical and architectural value.

title: Jump Theater
short_description:
Jump Theater located on the 3rd floor of the Myeongbo Art Hall and it is the home theater for the famed non-verbal show, "Jump." 

"Jump" is an exciting non-verbal show that tells the story of a band of thieves who decide to break into a house. What the thieves don't realize is that the house is home to a family of martial artists. 

Visit the Jump Theater to see what happens with this merry family and the band of thieves. The show is popular with all ages and mixes music, comedy, and martial arts for an unforgettable performance.

title: Arumjigi
short_description: Arumjigi is a non-profit cultural foundation dedicated to globally promoting the beauty and value of Korean art and culture. Emphasizing the importance of basic elements like clothes, food, lives, and actions of a modern man, the foundation hosts various educational and research programs, exhibitions, and design events aiming to develop and increase creative ideas for modernizing tradition.  So that Korean traditions won't die out as a thing of the past, Arumjigi hopes to deeply understand and modernize tradition so that it will be successfully integrated into the lives of the next future generations.

title: Gallery Hyundai
short_description: Gallery Hyundai is a famous gallery located on Sagandong Gallery Street. The street is known for its many galleries, hence the name, yet Gallery Hyundai stands out from the crowd. The gallery exhibits major contemporary Korean artists, such as Park Su-Geun and Lee Jung-Seob, as well as many major foreign artists. The gallery also has a superb restaurant with a great wine selection.

title: National Museum of Art at Deoksugung Palace
short_description: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art at Deoksugung opened in 1998 as an annex of the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea. The museum building, Seokjojeon Hall, is located at Deoksugung Palace. Seokjojeon Hall is an exquisite example of Western architecture from the early 20th century. It is the only Korean palace to have an outdoor garden and fountain designed in a Western style. The museum’s location inside the palace means that many visitors choose to combine their visit with a tour of Deoksugung. Jeongdong Park, the Seoul Museum of Art, and Namdaemun Market are some of the nearby tourist attractions. Admission fees vary depending on exhibition but visitors will be able to see beautiful works of art from Korean and international artists.

title: Seoul Norimadang
short_description: The Seoul Norimadang is a performance venue for Korean folk arts located at Seokchon Lake Park. The facility is styled after a traditional hanok and visitors can enjoy a range of folk performances. A visit to the Seoul Norimadang is a wonderful way to see Korea's folk traditions and arts firsthand. Many of the performing arts seen here are have been designated Important Intangible Cultural Properties.

title: Mokdong Ice Rink
short_description: Mokdong Ice Rink, located in Yangcheon-gu, Seoul, is an international-standard ice skating arena. Since August 2019, it has been operated under private management by Waikiki Mokdong Ice Rink through a business agreement with the Seoul Sports Facilities Management Office.

title: Folk Theater Pungryu
short_description: The Folk Theater Pungryu is dedicated to traditional Korean performance arts. The theater features traditional design elements and is located within the Training Center for Important Intangible Cultural Properties. Visitors can enjoy many different performances of traditional dance and music at the Folk Theater Pungryu.

title: Yakhyeon Catholic Church
short_description: Yakhyeon Catholic Church was the first Western-style church ever built in Korea. Located in Jungnim-dong, the church can be seen from Seoullo 7017. Yakhyeon Catholic Church has historical significance as a religious site and its architecture was hugely influential on the architectural styles of other churches in Korea. The building was destroyed by fire in 1998 but it was subsequently restored.

title: Wonhyoro Catholic Church
short_description: Wonhyoro Catholic Church is located beside Sacred Heart Girls' High School (once the Yongsan Seminary) and was consecrated in 1902. The church is small in scale but notable for its French Gothic architecture. Visitors to Seoul can visit an important piece of modern Korean history with a stop at Wonhyoro Catholic Church.

title: Hakgojae Gallery
short_description: Hakgojae Gallery is a modern art gallery and its motto is “creation of the new by understanding the old.” The architecture of the gallery reflects this motto. The main building of Gallery Hakgojae was designed to look like a hanok, (a traditional Korean house), while the new hall was designed in a modern, 21st-century style of architecture. Though the two architectural styles are different, they harmonize beautifully. Hakgojae Gallery also has a branch in the Shanghai art district of Moganshan Road. Admission to the gallery is free.

title: Sungkok Art Museum
short_description: The Sungkok Art Museum was established in 1995 to promote and foster Korean arts. The museum also commemorates the late founder of the Ssangyong Group, Kim Sungkok, and the museum was built on the site of Kim Sungkok's house. Creative work from all artistic genres such as photography, design, and fashion, is showcased in various exhibitions. The museum typically hosts more than a dozen exhibitions each year. There are three exhibition halls and an outdoor sculpture garden.

title: Gwangnaru Safety Experience Center
short_description: The Gwangnaru Safety Experience Center is an experience center that educates the public on disaster response and safety awareness. Visitors can take part in interactive disaster simulations in order to learn how to cope in a disaster situation and get valuable safety training. The different themed experience zones include an earthquake zone, storm and flood zone, fire and smoke zone, and a disaster prevention zone. In total there are 20 different zones. Visit the center and learn how to handle dangerous situations and how to prevent accidents.

title: Yeouido Hangang Park Swimming Pool
short_description: The Yeouido Hangang Park Swimming Pool is an outdoor pool that boasts magnificent views of the Hangang River. The pool opens during the summer months and has a capacity of more than 3,500 people. There are a variety of shops selling snacks and light refreshements by the pool. The pool is a great place to swim and visitors can take advantage of the wealth of events and activities that take place at the park.

title: Myeongbo Art Hall
short_description: The Myeongbo Art Hall is a cultural complex that hosts various exhibitions and performances. It was once known as Myeongdo Theater but was renovated and renamed the Myeongbo Art Hall. Myeongbo produces new cultural and arts projects, fosters new artists, and offers venue rentals for events. The building is equipped with advanced lighting and sound equipment.

title: Boramae Park Climbing Wall
short_description: The Boramae Park Climbing Wall is located at Boramae Park. The wall is an outdoor artificial climbing wall with a considerable scale and height and it's popular with climbing enthusiasts. The wall is open for use on weekends and during the winter season, classes are held on climbing.

title: Gyeomjae Jeong Seon Art Museum
short_description: The Gyeomjae Jeong Seon Art Museum is dedicated to the Joseon-era artist Jeong Seon. Located in Gangseo-gu, the museum has 4 levels. In addition to the special exhibition halls, there is a permanent memorial hall with information about the life and works of Jeong Seon. The museum's multipurpose facility can be used for lectures, seminars, and video screenings.

title: Jungnangcheon Stream Embankment
short_description: In spring, the embankment of Jungnangcheon Stream is covered with canola flowers. The 5.15-kilometer section from Jangpyeonggyo Bridge to Wolleunggyo Bridge is a land of bright yellow flowers. In the summer, you can see a colorful tunnel of 40,000 roses, and in autumn, silver grass, reeds, cosmos, and sunflower flower paths create a unique autumn scenery. If Jungnangcheon is famous for its spring, summer, and autumn flowers, winter is definitely the time for migratory birds. The 3.3-kilometer section where Jungnangcheon Stream joins the Hangang River from the confluence of Cheonggyecheon Stream and Jungnangcheon Stream is a protected area for migratory birds and is perfect for sightseeing. More than 4,000 birds of more than 40 species, including herons, herring gulls, and cormorants, fly in, and 21 species of migratory birds, such as mallards and kestrels, visit especially in winter. When migratory birds visit in winter, a birdwatching program and a migratory bird observation class also take place, making the place an ecological learning center for children.

title: Andong Presbyterian Church's Soheodang
short_description: Andong Presbyterian Church is located in Bukchon Hanok Village. The church dates back to the early 20th century. Most churches at the time were founded and built by Western missionaries. However, Andong is unique in that the church was founded by Koreans. Soheodang is part of the church complex and it is a rest area run by the church. Visitors to Soheodang are welcome to sit and rest while enjoying free tea provided by the church.

title: Kyungin Museum of Fine Art
short_description: Founded in 1983 by Gyeongin Lee Geum-hong, Gyeongin Museum of Art is not only a cultural space for artists but also a widely known tourist attraction. The Gyeongin Museum of Art reflects the founder's desire to show that the museum is not the exclusive property of a particular group, but a place where people of all ages and backgrounds can feel at home. The interior consists of six exhibition halls, including an atelier, an outdoor garden, and a traditional tea garden, and concerts are held in the outdoor garden in spring and autumn.

title: Hwagyesa Temple
short_description: Hwagyesa Temple is located in the Samgaksan Woods, at the foot of Samgaksan Mountain in Seoul. Since the temple is close to center of the city, many people visit to feel the nature. Hwagyesa Temple has established a reputation as a temple that brings Korean Buddhism to an international audience. The temple attracts many Zen masters from all over the world and in addition to Korean and expat Buddhists. Hwagyesa Temple also offers a range of temple stay programs that are open to the general public. Visitors can choose from a one day program, a meditation-focused program, and an activities-focused temple stay program.

title: Seoul Anglican Cathedral
short_description: The Seoul Anglican Cathedral was built during the Japanese colonial era and it is located beside Deoksugung Palace. The cathedral was constructed under the direction of the Rt. Reverend Mark Trollope, the third bishop of the Anglican Church of Korea and British architect Arthur Dixon. Although construction was completed in 1926, the Anglican Church of Korea considers 1890 as the date of the cathedral's foundation, since this was the year when the first service of Holy Communion was held. The cathedral is the seat of the Seoul Anglican Diocese and Tangible Cultural Property of Seoul No. 35.

title: Kim Chong Yung Museum
short_description: The Kim Chong Yung Museum was established to honor the legacy and art of the modern artist Kim Chong Yung and to provide support to young artists. Kim was a pioneer of modern scultpure and the museum's main hall has a permanent exhibition with Kim's works and the new hall showcases artwork from new artists. Art and cultural classes are offered at the museum in two semesters during the calendar year. Admission to the Kim Chong Yung Museum is free.

title: Gana Art Center
short_description: The Gana Art Center is a multipurpose art space that holds exhibitions, performances, classes, and auctions. The sprawling center was designed by the world-renowned architect Jean Michel Wilmotte. The Gana Art Center operates a convenient shuttle bus for visitors. The shuttle bus runs every day except Mondays and national holidays.

title: Seoul World Cup Stadium
short_description:
The Seoul World Cup Stadium was constructed to host games for the 2002 FIFA World Cup. Though the 2002 World Cup has long ended, it has continued to be a major presence on the Korean sporting and cultural scene. The Seoul World Cup Stadium is the home stadium of FC Seoul, a professional K-League soccer team. The stadium hosts cultural events in addition to sporting events and the stadium is open to the public for tours on non-game days.

 

During the 2002 FIFA World Cup, the stadium was full of cheer and excitement. Through Seoul World Cup Stadium Tour, visitors will have an opportunity to look around the very site of that momentous event and come to marvel at the architecture and unique structure of the stadium.

 

<Seoul World Cup Stadium Tour>

- Description: A paid tour for visitors to sight-see around the stadium

- Open to: Koreans, tourists, groups (10 or more), individuals

- Hours: 10:00 - 15:00 (4 tours in total, 11:00 - 13:00 Lunch Break)

- Payment: On-site transaction (Cash/Credit)

- Tour Course: Stadium Tour Lobby → On-site transaction → Main Stadium → Locker Room A, Practice RoomA (FC Seoul) → Locker Room B, Practice Room B (2002 FIFA World Cup) → Video Room → History Exhibit → Souvenir Shop → End

title: Chungdong First Methodist Church
short_description: Chungdong First Methodist Church is Korea’s first Protestant church, established in 1885 by American Methodist missionary Henry Appenzeller. The church is Korea's representative Protestant church. Chungdong First Methodist operates many religious and missionary programs such as medical services, education services, and missionary training for dispatch to foreign countries.

title: Ilmin Museum of Art
short_description: Ilmin Museum of Art is a private art museum that mainly exhibits Korean contemporary art. It was originally established to commemorate Kim Sangman, former president of the Donga Ilbo, one of Korea's leading media outlets. The museum's name was taken from Kim's pen name, Ilmin (meaning “one people” or “a nation united” in Korean). The museum is run by the Ilmin Cultural Foundation and a variety of special exhibitions and art classes are held throughout the year. The museum has a cafe and restaurant on the first floor.

title: Bulgwangcheon Stream
short_description: Bulgwangcheon Stream, which originates in Bulgwang-dong, Eunpyeong-gu, flows through Yeokchon-dong, Eungam-dong, and Jeungsan-dong, and extends to Bukgajwa-dong in Seodaemun-gu and Seongsan-dong in Mapo-gu, covering a length of approximately 9.21 km. In 2002, wastewater prevention facilities were installed, and groundwater was pumped to create the current flowing stream. Named after the nearby Bulgwangsa Temple, the upper stream of Bulgwangcheon Stream features riverside stands and fountain shows. Along the stream are well-developed bike paths and walking trails, with various trees and aquatic plants offering diverse landscaping throughout the seasons. This restored ecosystem makes Bulgwangcheon Stream a beloved walking path for residents.

title: National Museum Of Modern And Contemporary Art: Changdong Residency
short_description: The Changdong Residency of the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) is an arts and cultural space that is designed to allow visitors to get more familiar with modern art. The museum offers various exhibitions, region-linked programs and educational programs. The residency space also provides art studios for Korean and international artists.

title: Hongjecheon Stream
short_description: Hongjecheon Stream is the first tributary of the Hangang River. The stream runs 13.92km-long  and flows through Jongno-gu, Seodaemun-gu and Mapo-gu. The stream was historically also referred to as Hongjewoncheon Stream due to its proximity to the Joseon-era Hongjewon rest area. Visiting Chinese envoys and officials would often stop by here to refresh. Today, Hongjecheon is famous for its waterfall and bicycle path.

title: Taereung International Skating Rink
short_description: Taereung International Skating Rink is a world-class skating facility that is operated by the Korean Olympic Committee. The rink runs skating classes for skaters of all levels. Total beginners to professionals can take lessons here and the facility is used by both the general public and top athletes. The facility is located near the Korea Institute of Sport Science and the UNESCO World Heritage site, Taereung and Gangreung Royal Tombs.

title: Bulgwangcheon Haedamneundari Bridge
short_description: The Bulgwangcheon Haedamneundari Bridge is a 62m-long bridge that stands over Bulgwangcheon Stream in northern Seoul. The bridge offers great views of Bukhansan Mountain and is popular as a photo spot. It was recently selected as one of Seoul's top 50 viewpoints as voted for by residents of Seoul.

title: Arario Gallery Seoul
short_description:
Over the years, Arario Gallery Seoul has led the way in curating a harmonic fusion and variety of different art forms in Korea's art community through bold collaborations with international artistry that have never been attempted before. Also, the gallery takes the forefront in introducing artwork from today's more modern Korean artists having implemented an ongoing and structured system of exclusively-contracted artists. Currently, a wide range of artworks from artists native to India and Southeast Asia, who have yet to come to Korea despite having already experienced China's art community, are finally getting some spotlight in Korea. What's better is that with the help of continued promotional activity, the search and funding for up-and-coming talent in the respective regions is ongoing as well. Thanks to the gallery's efforts grounded in a system of exclusive artists displaying excellence; various collaborations with other galleries, both at home and abroad; introductions of varied artworks from numerous places around the world; and more, the Arario Gallery is set to play out its role as Asia's signature gallery that expands upon the possibilities for the future of Korea's art community while leading the market as well.


Since its first opening in Sogyeok-dong, Jongno-gu, in 2006, Arario Gallery Seoul has been leading the contemporary art scene based on its solid artist system and bold exhibition planning capabilities. In March 2014, it relocated near the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, and from April 2018 to November 2019, Arario Gallery Seoul Ryse Hotel, its second exhibition space in Seoul, opened near Hongik University. This effort aimed to inherit and develop the youthful and innovative spirit symbolized by the area. In 2022, Arario Gallery Seoul ended its Sogyeok-dong era and reopened with a new look in Wonseo-dong, Jongno-gu, in February 2023. The gallery aims to collaborate and support artists, striving for mutual growth through proactive exploration and consistent support. At the same time, it seeks to realize experimental and serious exhibition planning to continuously contribute to the advancement of the Korean art scene.

title: Art Sonje Center
short_description: Whereas the Sonje Museum of Art typically focuses exclusively on contemporary artwork, the Art Sonje Center has a multi-pronged focus on art. The museum exhibits art from various genres and the museum also hosts cultural events such as concerts, short film screenings, and performance arts shows by Korean and foreign artists. Major pieces in the museum's collection are Wings of Jupiter by Kwak Hoon and Curtains by Hwang Kyu-Baik.

title: Yangjaecheon Stream & Tancheon Stream
short_description: Yangjaecheon Stream and Tancheon Stream are two tributaries of the Hangang River. The streams offer picturesque walking trails for visitors to enjoy. Yangjaecheon Stream, sometimes referred to as Hanyeoul Stream, is a tributary of the Hangang River. The stream is 18.5 km long and flows from Gwacheong in Gyeonggi-do Province to the southern part of Seoul. The stream's name is derived from the area in Seoul it flows through, Yangjae-dong. Tancheon Stream is another one of the Hangang's tributaries. The stream is 35.6 km long and starts in the city of Yongin in Gyeonggi-do Province and ends at the Hangang River in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. With its gently sloping walking paths and well-maintained cycling routes stretching along the stream, this urban waterway is a popular spot for walking, running, and riding. It is especially famous as a tourist destination for cherry blossoms in spring and colorful foliage in autumn.

title: Jogyesa Temple
short_description: Jogyesa Temple was established in 1910 under the name Gakhwangsa by monks who aspired for the independence of Korean Buddhism and the restoration of the national capital. At the time, Gakhwangsa was the first temple to be situated within the four main gates of Seoul. In 1937, efforts began to relocate Gakhwangsa to its present site, now known as Jogyesa. Positioned in the heart of Jongno, Seoul, it is the only traditional temple in the city center, offering a place for visitors to rest. The temple grounds are open 24/7, welcoming locals and foreigners anytime. The temple hosts a temple stay program and the annual Lotus Lantern Festival.

title: Jamsil Baseball Stadium
short_description: When Jamsil Baseball Stadium opened in 1982, it was Korea's first baseball stadium. Located in the southern part of Seoul, it remains one the country's major sporting arenas. It serves as the home stadium for two professional baseball teams, the LG Twins and the Doosan Bears. During baseball season, games take place everyday except Monday.

title: Hangang River Cycling Trail
short_description: The Hangang River Cycling Trail stretches almost the riverside and spans a total of 240km. It is the longest cycling route in Korea. The trail connects the Nanji District, Mapodaegyo Bridge, Banpodaegyo Bridge, Seoul Forest (Seongsudaegyo Bridge) and Gwangjindaegyo Bridge. Because the trail spans from Seoul’s downtown out to satellite cities, the trail is popular with both commuters and tourists.

title: PKM Gallery
short_description: The PKM Gallery was established in 2001 and a range of art from diverse mediums can be found on display. Exhibitions include paintings, sculptures, and videos, while the gallery's goal is to be known for its quality of art. Prominent Korean and foreign artists fill the gallery's rosters and some of the more prominent names are Lee Bul, Jorge Pardo, Michael Joo, and Stephen Prina.

title: Kukkiwon World Taekwondo Headquarters
short_description:
Kukkiwon is the official headquarters for the Korean martial art of Taekwondo. At Kukkiwon, practitioners of Taekwondo can become certified instructors, undergo tests to climb the ranks, and attend the institute's Taekwondo academy. Another of Kukkiwon's aims is to develop and promote awareness of Taekwondo as a sport and as part of Korea's cultural heritage.


Frequently Asked Questions about Kukkiwon

What are the opening hours and admission fees for the Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters)?

The Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters) is open from 9 am to 5:30 pm from Monday to Friday. It is closed for lunch from 11:30 am to 1:00 pm. Admission is free and it is closed on public holidays, national holidays, and Kukkiwon closed days. (As of 2026)

How do I search for Taekwondo mementos, Dan numbers and certificates?

You can check out mementos, Dan numbers, and certificates on the Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters) website. (As of 2026)

• Contact the Korea Taekwondo Association (02-420-4271) for competition performance certificates, player registration confirmations, and referee qualifications.
• For general instructors and professional instructors, contact the Sports Instructor Training Center ( 1670-1859 )

Where can I inquire about Kukkiwon?

To ensure your call is directed properly, find the contact information of the department you’d like to reach on the Kukkiwon website and contact them. (As of 2026)

Go to the Kukkiwon Organization Guide

title: Grand Hyatt Seoul Ice Rink
short_description:
The Grand Hyatt Seoul Ice Rink is an outdoor ice rink, located at the Grand Hyatt Hotel. Thousands of tiny, twinkling lights hang from the trees surrounding the ice rink. The beautiful scenery and romantic atmosphere makes the rink a popular date spot and the rink even offers special "Propose on Ice" events for couples. Helmets and gloves are required and refreshments are available for purchase at the rink.



Frequently Asked Questions about Grand Hyatt Seoul Ice Rink

How much does the Hyatt Seoul Ice Rink pass cost?

The price of the Hyatt Seoul Ice Rink 2-hour pass is as follows. The price may vary from year to year. (As of 2025)

  • • Monday-Friday : 55,000 KRW for customers / 44,000 KRW for guests

  • • Saturday-Sunday and public holidays : 58,000 KRW for customers / 46,400 KRW for guests

Where can I reserve the Hyatt Seoul Ice Rink pass?

Reservations can be made through the Hyatt Ice Rink Customer Center.

What are the opening hours of the Hyatt Ice Rink?

The Hyatt Ice Rink is only open in winter, and the opening hours are as follows. (As of 2025)

  • • Monday-Friday : 12:00~21:00

  • • Saturday-Sunday and public holidays : 10:00~21:00


The detailed operating period and hours may vary from year to year.

title: Korea University Main Hall & Old Main Library
short_description: Korea University is one of best universities in all of Korea. Visitors to Seoul can visit the Korea University Main Hall located in Anam-dong, Seoul. This beautiful three-story tall building was built in 1932 during the Japanese colonial period. In 1981 the hall was designated Historic Site No. 285 in 1981. The Old Korea University Main Library, located nearby, was designated Historic Site No. 286 in 1981.

title: National Theater of Korea
short_description: The National Theater of Korea opened in 1950 and it was the first national, government-supported theater in Asia. There are four theaters where performances take place. The Haeoreum Theater is a large hall, the Daloreum Theater, a small hall, and the Byeoloreum Theater with a stage that is changed according to each performance. The Haneul Theater is a dome-shaped outdoor theater. Performances from a variety of genres including ballet, kabuki, theater, and full pansori take place at the National Theater of Korea.

title: Kumho Museum of Art
short_description: The Kumho Museum of Art showcases artwork from famous, established artists as well as works from outstanding new artists. The museum hosts a concert series in their recital hall called the Kumho Gallery Concert. The concerts take place every Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday at 20:00 in the evening. There are also presentations on the artists and artworks on exhibition at the museum. These sessions are opened to the public as part of the museum's Kumho Academy. The Kumho Museum of Art is located near Gyeongbokgung Palace.

title: Kukje Gallery
short_description: The Kukje Gallery is one of Korea's major art galleries and visitors can see artworks from new and established artists. Founded in 1982, the Kukje Gallery exhibits works from prominent foreign artists, but the gallery also exhibits and fosters promising Korean artists. Enjoy incredible contemporary art at the Kukje Gallery.

title: Gilsangsa Temple
short_description: Gilsangsa Temple was once one of the foremost yojeong, a place where powerful men used to convene behind the scenes.The temple is named after the woman who donated the buildings, a gisaeng (a female entertainer and/or courtesan) named Kim Yeong-han who had a change of heart after reading "Non-Possession" by Venerable Beopjeong Sunim. The monk initially denied her request, but in 1995 decided to turn the buildings into a temple.  As a result, the temple has a very unusual atmosphere because it kept many of its original features. The temple is highly regarded for its involvement in cultural exchanges with other religions, and its programs to help visitors experience Buddhism.

title: Myeongdong Theater
short_description: Situated on the former site of the National Theater of Korea, Myeongdong Theater is a mid-sized venue that hosts many arts events. The theater is located between Euljiro 1(il)-ga Station and Myeongdong Station and stands five stories tall with one basement level. Myeongdong Theater presents experimental plays, musicals, classic plays, and nonverbal performances. There are also special events held here such as theater festivals and arts festivals. The proximity of the seating area to the stage also lends an intimacy and immediacy to the venue's performances.

title: Maehun Yun Bong-Gil Memorial Hall
short_description: The Maehun Yun Bong-Gil Memorial Hall is dedicated to the resistance fighter, Patriot Yun Bong-gil. Yun's pen name was Maehun and he was active in the Korean independence movement during the Japanese colonial era. Located in Seoul's Yangjae dong, the first floor of the memorial is an exhibition hall that displays relics and biographical information about Yun Bong-gil in chronological order. On the second floor, the exhibition hall contains photographs and other materials of the Korean independence movement organized by theme. Admission to the memorial hall is free.

title: Songeun Art Cube
short_description: Songeun Art Cube (formerly known as Songeun Gallery) is a space for new artists to exhibit their artworks. Operated by the Songeun Art Foundation, the space functions as a gallery but various arts events also take place here. Ever since it opened in 2002, Songeun Art Cube has held an annual arts award ceremony. Winners are sponsored by the foundation and receive support to exhibit their work.

title: Seoul Arts Center
short_description:
Seoul Arts Center is home to many artistic disciplines, comprising an Opera House, Music Hall, the Hangaram Art Museum, the Hangaram Design Museum and the Seoul Calligraphy Museum. The center also features a fountain plaza and outdoor café, making ita popular year-round destination.
Seoul Arts Center was established to develop and promote Korean arts and culture of the highest caliber and to forge links with the international art scene. Now considered one of the world’s 10 leading arts centers, Seoul Arts Center also runs an ArtsAcademy which acts as a cultural bridge to help improve public access to the arts.
As the center’s signature building, the Opera House is its principal performance space, and was designed in the shape of a gat (traditional Korean hat made of bamboo and horsehair).

title: Myeongdong Cathedral
short_description: Myeongdong Cathedral is the very first Roman Catholic parish church in Korea. It is also the first Gothic building ever built in Korea and was designated as Historic site No. 285 in Korea. On the basement floor, there is a small sanctuary where the remains of the martyrs are enshrined, and where visitors to the cathedral can pay their respects. Every May, Myeongdong Cathedral holds a cultural festival. The construction of the cathedral started in 1892 and was completed in 1898. Unlike most Gothic buildings, Myeongdong Cathedral was built with bricks instead of stones. It gives the cathedral a characteristic atmosphere. The splendid high ceilings inside the church and the arches in between the magnificent inner pillars show the beautiful Gothic style well. The basement contains the remains of nine saints and martyrs, who devoted their lives to the propagation of Catholicism in Korea. Behind the cathedral, Seongmo Dongsan (St. Mary's garden) is situated. During lunch hour, pipe organs are playing here. The garden offers a peaceful resting space after visiting the cathedral.

title: An Jung-geun Memorial Hall
short_description: The An Jung-geun Memorial Hall was established to memorialize the Korean patriot An Jung-geun. An fought for Korean independence from Japan and was ultimately executed by Japanese authorities for assassinating Ito Hirobumi in 1909. Ito was a major force behind the Japanese annexation of Korea. The memorial hall is composed of 12 exhibition halls and galleries, an auditorium, a reference library, and a rest area. In addition to exhibition information about An's life and some of his calligraphy, the memorial hall also hosts the An Jung-guen Academny and other events each year. Events include visits to historic sites abroad that were important to independence movements and calligraphy contests. Admission to the An Jung-geun Memorial Hall is free.

title: Hangaram Art Museum
short_description: Hangaram Art Museum is situated on the left side of the main front area of the Seoul Arts Center. It is integrated with various programs offered by the Seoul Arts Center. The museum includes exhibition halls, storage rooms, and an art shop, providing an optimal exhibition environment. It often hosts special exhibitions by world-renowned artists such as Edvard Munch, Bernard Buffet, and Pablo Picasso. Most exhibitions prohibit photography, and observing proper viewing etiquette is important. The outdoor stair plaza serves as an open space for art markets, outdoor festivals, and an outdoor café during the summer season. It also accommodates various public programs, offering a unique cultural experience.

title: Korea Central Mosque
short_description:
Located in Hannam-dong, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, the Seoul Central Mosque is the first Islamic Mosque in Korea. It was established on May 21, 1976, after construction began in October 1974. The Korean government provided the site in May 1969 with approximately 4,958 square meters of land, and the construction costs were supported by Islamic countries worldwide, including Saudi Arabia. Situated between the Hangang River and Namsan Mountain, the mosque features prayer halls on the first and second floors, with ablution rooms for men and women in the basement of the annex building. The first floor of the annex houses classrooms, while the second floor has office spaces. The adjacent Islamic Center includes facilities such as an Islamic mission center for children, a Muslim congregation, a women's association, and a library. The exterior of the Seoul Central Mosque features a variety of amenities, including halal restaurants, a halal butcher shop, an Islamic bookstore, a halal supermarket, and a travel agency, making it convenient for Muslims and non-Muslims to visit.



Frequently Asked Questions about Korea Central Mosque
What is the nearest subway station to the Seoul Central Mosque?
The nearest subway station to the Seoul Central Mosque is Itaewon Station (Subway Line 6).
Are there any precautions when visiting the Seoul Central Mosque?
You are not allowed to wear revealing clothing such as sleeveless tops, short skirts, or shorts, and smoke inside the mosque. If you enter the mosque wearing revealing clothing, you must put on appropriate attire (such as skirts and hijabs) available in the dressing room next to the security office. Non-Muslims are allowed to enter the mosque, but be careful not to interfere with the prayers by pointing the camera in front of people.
I am curious about the Seoul Central Mosque worship schedule.
You can check the Seoul Central Mosque monthly worship schedule on the website below.
Seoul Central Mosque Worship Schedule

title: Daegaksa Temple
short_description: Daegaksa Temple is a Buddhist temple founded in 1911 by Yongseong Seunim and located not far from Changdeokgung Palace. Yongseong Seunim was one of the 33 citizen representatives who took part in the March 1st Movement. He was active in the Korean independence movement and his legacy includes significant reforms of modern Buddhism in Korea. The temple was originally just a small hanok and in 1986 the temple was completely ry reconstructed. Today, Daegaksa has a main gate, belfry, and three-story temple.

title: Seoul Art Space - Sindang Creative Arcade
short_description: The Sindang Creative Arcade is a creative space for artists and an art market. The arcade was re-born into a space for the arts following renovation of empty storefronts at the Sindang Underground Shopping Center in the Jungang Market. The Jungang Market was established in 1917 and the renovation that created the Sindang Creative Arcade has revitalized the area. The creative arcade houses workshops and an art market. Dozens of artists create artworks and crafts in nearly every art medium there is. At the art market, shoppers can purchase unique artwork and items.

title: Hongdae NANTA Theatre
short_description: Nanta Theater is Korea’s first exclusive venue for Nanta performances, which are based on the rhythm of the samulnori (traditional Korean percussion quartet) and are comic non-verbal plays set in a kitchen. Nanta has been a sell-out success at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in the UK and was also the first long-running Korean show on Broadway in New York City. The shows have been so successful that they now run at three exclusive theaters in Seoul which are equipped with special lighting and sound systems to create maximum audience impact. Around 380,000 international tourists visit Nanta Theater every year.

title: Universal Arts Center
short_description: The Universal Arts Center was established in 1981 as a multipurpose arts and cultural center. The center spans three stories above ground and one level below ground. The center's capacity is 1,200 seats and visitors can enjoy dance and performing arts from various genres such as ballet, and opera. Major awards ceremonies and competitions have also been held at the Universal Arts Center.

title: Seoul Olympic Museum
short_description: The Seoul Olympic Museum was established to commemorate the 1988 Olympics in Seoul and to promote the Olympic spirit. Located within Olympic Park, the museum is multipurpose space that is a combination of a park and sports scenter. Visitors can take part in activities and education programs. The museum offers various types of information relating to sports, culture, business, and the Olympics. Comprised of five major zones, each themed area is dedicated to different aspects of the Seoul Olympics: Place of Harmony, Place of Prosperity, Place of Hope, Place of Glory and Place of Peace. There is also a cafeteria on the second floor and a museum shop for souvenirs.  Admission to the Seoul Olympic Museum is free.

title: Ttukseom Hangang Theme Park
short_description:
The Ttukseom Theme Park boasts magnificent views of the Hangang, and with a capacity of more than 3,500 people, it hosts a variety of cultural events and activity programs for visitors all year around.  


In summer, Ttukseom, which was originally designed as a large swimming pool, boasts special features including a fountain in the adult pool and a long winding pool resembling a stream. In winter, the area is covered in snow, giving visitors the chance to go sledding, build snowmen and enjoy snowball fights. The Glistening Snow Village with its Christmas decorations adds to the festive spirit, and at the Soft Play Village, visitors can enjoy 3D movies or make clay models and hand-mirrors using hanji (traditional Korean paper made from mulberry trees).

title: Myeongdong Nanta Theater
short_description: Nanta Theater is Korea’s first exclusive venue for Nanta performances, which are based on the rhythm of the samulnori (traditional Korean percussion quartet) and are comic non-verbal plays set in a kitchen. Nanta has been a sell-out success at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in the UK and was also the first long-running Korean show on Broadway in New York City. The shows have been so successful that they now run at three exclusive theaters in Seoul which are equipped with special lighting and sound systems to create maximum audience impact. Around 380,000 international tourists visit Nanta Theater every year.

title: National Gugak Center
short_description: The National Gugak Center is an organization intended to promote and develop traditional Korean dance and music. The center has several performance venues and also runs educational programs. Among their lauded educational programs, their gugak class for foreign nationals is especially popular. The class is best for visitors who will be in Korea for several weeks. The gugak class runs for 12 weeks and the program culminates with a student performance at the center.

title: Jinkwansa Temple
short_description: Jinkwansa Temple is a centuries-old temple located in Bukhansan National Park. The temple was built by order of King Hyeonjong of the Goryeo Dynasty in gratitude to the great Buddhist priest Jinkwan. History has it that Jinkwan saved King Hyeon-jong's life when he was young and the king repaid the priest by building the temple. Jinkwansa Temple is comprised of several buildings and some of the notable buildings include Daeungjeon Hall, Myeongbujeon Hall, and Nahanjeon Hall. The temple also operates temple stay programs where visitors can experience Buddhist culture firsthand. There are programs for groups, children, and youths.

title: Son Kee Chung Memorial Hall
short_description: The Son Kee Chung Memorial Hall honors the athlete and gold medalist, Son Kee Chung. The memorial hall opened on October 14th, 2012, marking the centennial anniversary of Son's birth. The memorial hall was once a school and was in fact Son's alma mater. Son Kee Chung was a gold medalist in the 1936 Berlin Olympics Marathon. Though Son Kee Chung was registered as a Japanese athlete, due to the Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula, his victory was cherished and praised by Korean nationals. Visit the memorial hall to learn more about Son's life and how he won his gold medal. Admission is free and there are sometimes special exhibitions.

title: Hyundai Department Store
short_description: The flagship store of Hyundai Department Store is located in Apgujeong-dong, a popular area for shopping in Seoul. Since its grand opening in 1985, the flagship store has been one of the leaders in upscale shopping culture in the Korean distribution industry and has become one of the best shopping destinations with its directory of exquisite brands and supreme customer services. Offering customers an enticing selection of merchandise and exceptional customer services, the flagship store has been loved by customers for meeting their needs and aspirations for a better lifestyle.

title: Lotte Duty Free Main Store
short_description:
Global travel retail brand Lotte Duty Free Shop is a one-stop shopping complex providing shoppers a wide range of products. 

The main store is on 9-12F of Lotte Department Store located in Myeong-dong, which is the center of Seoul.  They offers luxury brands such as HERMES, LOUIS VUITTON, CHANEL, CARTIER, and others.

There is Star Avenue on floor 1, which promote K-Culture more actively in time for global customers to travel to Korea. You can find handprints of Lotte Duty Free models at Star Avenue. Also, Hi-Five zone in Star Avenue shows individual videos of Lotte Duty Free models.

title: The Face Shop
short_description: Most of the items from the Face Shop are inspired by nature and environmentally friendly for a reasonable price. You will clearly be able to feel the benefits that come from using these natural products and will see them reflected in your skin.

title: Galleria Department Store EAST
short_description: Galleria EAST is the largest single luxury store in Korea. In line with its status, the store features a unique variety of exclusive world-class brands. From the first floor to the fourth floor, every level features luxury brands. The first floor houses various designer labels, such as Chanel, Hermès, Cartier, Tiffany and Goyard. From the second to the fourth floors, a wide variety of men’s and women’s fashion labels and brands of accessories are displayed. The third floor also features convenience facilities including a café, Beans & Berries, and Customer Service Center, and provides a tax refund service, while the fourth floor houses a wine shop, Enoteca.

title: Noeul Campground
short_description:
Noeul means "sunset" in Korean, and Noeul Park got its name because here you can experience a gorgeous, expansive panorama of the city as well as views of the Han River, Bukhansan (Mountain), and more, making any sunset breathtaking.  

This spot is particularly special because it boasts camping grounds, where a camping festival as well as a family camping program took place last year. The park takes up a vast amount of space with over a million pyeong, and there are the camp sites are equipped with wood stoves, electrical outlets, outdoor tables, and even electric blanket and other amenities.

title: Seoul Metropolitan Library
short_description: The former Seoul City Hall has reopened its doors as the city's main public library. Seoul Metropolitan Library is the city's main public library and it's easily accessible from City Hall Station's exit 4 or 5. The "Tong Tong" Seoul City Walking Tour takes visitors through the library and the new Seoul City Hall building. Tours are free and led by a cultural tour guide.

title: Lotte Young Plaza (Myeongdong Branch)
short_description:
Lotte Young Plaza, located near Exit 7 of Euljiro 1(il)-ga Station, is a shopping center with seven above-ground floors and one basement level. The basement has stores selling figures, K-pop albums, and seasonal pop-up stores. The first-floor features clothing stores showcasing K-fashion and popular character shops like Kakao Friends. Other floors offer a variety of clothing stores, including sportswear and casual wear for different genders and age groups, as well as various SPA brands. This allows for a more casual shopping experience compared to traditional department stores.



Frequently Asked Questions about Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong

What kind of stores are in Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong?

You can find stores by floor or type on the website below.

Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong Branch Store Guide

When is Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong closed?

The Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong branch has different monthly closed days, so you must check the website.

Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong Branch Closed Days Notice

What is the phone number of the customer center at Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong?

The representative phone number for Lotte Young Plaza Myeongdong is 1577-0001.

title: Ttukseom Hangang Park
short_description: Ttukseom Hangang Park is one of Seoul's public parks along the Hangang River. The Ttukseom park is located in the Ttukseom area of Seoul and has various facilities, such as an outdoor swimming pool, a playground, skateboarding area, and a rock-climbing site. Visitors can enjoy water sports in the summer, and sledding and skating in the winter. The biggest flea market in Korea is takes place annually at the park, from April to October.

title: Rolling Hall
short_description: Rolling Hall is a performance venue in Hongdae, Seoul. Various genres of music can be heard at Rolling Hall and both Korean and international musicians often perform here. Audiences can enjoy music from big name artists as well as underground and indie performers. The stage and audience area are close together which creates an intimate atmosphere.

title: Seoul Energy Dream Center
short_description: The Seoul Energy Dream Center a museum and educational center and it is also Korea's first energy-independent building in Korea. It is an environmentally friendly building that provides exhibitions and fun educational programs such as games and activities like building a solar powered car. Guided tours take place four times and tours have a capacity of 30 people.

title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
short_description: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA), Seoul is the newest of the four branches. The Seoul branch focuses on introducing global contemporary art. Equipped with multiple facilities, including a library, theater, and a multipurpose hall, MMCA, Seoul strives to accommodate every mode of new artistic endeavors and communication with the public.

title: Gimpo International Airport Tourist Information Center
short_description: The Gimpo International Airport Tourist Information Center is located on the 1st floor the international terminal at Gimpo International Airport. The center offers free guidebooks and maps of Seoul in Japanese, and Chinese (simplified and traditional).The center also assists tourists with questions and gives information on events, festivals, and Seoul-related tourism.

title: Incheon International Airport Terminal 1 Tourist Information Center (East)
short_description: The Seoul Tourism Information Center at Incheon International Airport T1, located on the east side of Incheon International Airport, is open year-round for international travelers visiting Korea. Visitors can receive travel information necessary for touring Seoul and find promotional materials for various tourist attractions.

title: Jung Saem Mool Inspiration
short_description: Jung Saem Mool Inspiration is a beauty shop, salon, and makeup academy in Cheongdam-dong run by the celebrity makeup artist Jung Saem Mool. The salon offers hair styling and makeup services as well as educational beauty courses. The salon is very popular with celebrities and regular people alike so advance reservations are recommended. The salon's customers include Hallyu stars such as Kim Tae-hee, Lee Hyo-ri, Bae Yong-jun, Kwon Sang-woo, and Song Seung-heon.

title: Olive Young (Myeongdong Flagship Store)
short_description: The Olive Young Lifestyle Experience Center in Myeongdong is the country's largest beauty store. The store is divided into 14 themed zones with different concepts where shoppers can try out and select various kinds of beauty and lifestyle items. Popular zones are the perfume bar, beauty care zone, and body care zone where customers can find imported products and luxury perfumes.

title: Hangang River
short_description:
The Hangang River is the most important physical landmark in the city, dividing the north and south. Lined with parks and recreational facilities on both banks, it’s the perfect place to rent bikes, go on cruise up the river, enjoy bird-watching, or splash around and cool off in public swimming pools during the summer months. 


※ Check out related articles on the Hangang River below!

title: Gocheok Skydome
short_description:
Gocheok Skydome is the largest capacity stadium in South Korea. In addition to sporting events, arts events such as concerts and awards ceremonies are also often held here.


The stadium was completed in September, 2015 and is a cultural sports complex that is open year round. During the baseball season, visitors can watch exciting games and enjoy Korean baseball culture. During the off-season, there are concerts and other cultural events held at Gocheok. The stadium's design is dome-shaped and there are 2 basement levels and 4 above-ground levels. Thanks to its ceiling cover, games and events are unaffected by weather conditions. There are baseball facilities, a swimming pool, gym, soccer field, basketball field and many other facilities open for public use. The stands have 18,000 seats, but for cultural events like concerts, audiences of 20,200 can be accommodated. Gocheok Skydome is the home stadium for the Nexen Heroes from 2016 to 2017. 


G ocheok Skydome's size makes it one of the largest indoor concert venues in South Korea.  The stadium has hosted many K-pop concerts and awards shows such as the KBS Music Awards and more.



Frequently Asked Questions about Gocheok Skydome

What is the nearest subway station to the Gocheok Sky Dome?

The nearest subway station to Gocheok Sky Dome is Guil Station (Subway Line 1).

Is there a cafeteria at the Gocheok Sky Dome?

There are thirty-two shops inside the Gocheok Sky Dome serving chicken, snack food, and pizza, and a convenience store. Outside, there is a management building with one store, so you can use it when watching baseball. (As of 2024)

Can I bring food inside the Gocheok Sky Dome?

Bringing food and drinks to the Gocheok Sky Dome may be restricted depending on the nature of the event. Food and beverages in plastic bottles of 1L or less may be brought in during professional baseball games. However, alcoholic drinks, cans, and beverages in glasses are not permitted. In addition, according to Kiwoom Heroes' regulations, food cannot be brought into the stadium when re-entering.

title: Seonyudo at Night
short_description:
Seonyudo Park is a popular tourist destination that is located on the Hangang River. The park is on Seonyudo Island and it is located right under Yanghwadaegyo Bridge. Though the park is popular year round, visitor numbers tend to peak in the spring andautumn. Seonyudo Park may be familiar even to those who have never been to Seoul as it's a popular filming location for Korean TV shows. "Infinite Challenge" and "Running Man" have both filmed here. After the sun sets, visitors can enjoy beautiful nightviews of Seoul and the twinkling lights of the Hangang's bridges and Seoul skyline. 

For more information:
Seonyudo Park

title: Gallery Art Zone at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
short_description:
The Gallery Art Zone is located on the 1st floor of MMCA and is about 570㎡ in size There are three zones and five gallery spaces. The Gallery Art Zone was borne out of a collaboration with the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) and Hyundai Motor Company. The Gallery Art Zone’s aim is to expand the breadth of audiences when it comes to art. Art shouldn’t just be for walls and showcases. The works on display in the Gallery Art Zone can be bought, and regular visitors can bring a piece of art or design home.
The Gallery Art Zone shows different aspects of Korean contemporary art and design in each zone. The first zone (Gallery 1) exhibits Korean design and sells works by promising artists, particularly those from the craft sector. The second zone (Galleries 2 and 3) exhibits and sells cultural products that were developed for MMCA, or on display at MMCA. The third zone (Galleries 4 and 5) displays and sells textiles, fashion products, and art books. Additionally, in part as a result of Hyundai Motor Company’s sponsorship, many art related events and special events will be held at the Gallery Art Zone.

title: Shinsegae Department Store (Main Store)
short_description: Situated between Myeong-dong and Namdaemun Market, the Shinsegae Department Store (Main Store) catches people’s attention with its vintage, early 20th century style architecture. Famous for being Korea’s first department store, the classic main building and the sophisticated modern style of the new wing create the perfect harmony. Shoppers can find numerous Korean and international brands here. Many of the employees of companies nearby eat lunch here because the food court includes some of the most famous restaurants in Seoul.

title: Gangnam Station Underground Shopping Center
short_description: In Gangnam Station on Subway Line 2, below the extravagant world of Gangnam-daero, a new world awaits shoppers. Spread out like a spider’s web, here you can find street shops and some of the most famous beauty brands in Korea. The main customers are female college students and young employees of nearby companies, so you can buy hot items at affordable prices.

title: Arko Art Center
short_description: ArkoArtCenter is a public art gallery and art center in the Daehak-ro area. By curating temporary exhibitions, and creating a platform for emerging experimental artists, the gallery has successfully become a staple of the Korean contemporary art scene. The Arko Art Center is also home to INSA Art Space, an alternative space aimed at promoting upcoming artists, as well as maintaining archives and providing seminar rooms and project space. There is no admission fee for the center.

title: A. by BOM
short_description: A. by BOM is a beauty salon which is responsible for styling Sandara Park, Jessica, Han Ye Seul, Lee Yun Hye, Park Soo Jin, Boa, and many other stars. It has a massive space, which is roughly 1,000㎡. The salon is separated into two floors; the second floor is for hair care and the third floor is for makeup servicing. For the clients receiving beauty service, there are works by cutting-edge artists being displayed. The second shop, which is near the original store, has a botanical garden concept, and is a popular film location for dramas like: The K2, Entourage, and many others.

title: Union Star Bowling Alley
short_description: A quick walk from exit 4 of Seongsu Station, visitors in Seongsu-dong will be able to find Union Star Bowling Club. Located on the basement of a red-brick building, the venue is often visited by a number of Hallyu stars including Kim Soo-hyun (who was recently on Infinity Challenge to test his bowling skills), G-Dragon and the members of former girl-group 2NE1. Bowling pins signed by the Hallyu stars are proudly displayed throughout the venue. A unique aspect of Union Star Bowling Club is that it is divided into two floors. The first basement floor is Rock Bowling Alley featuring ten lanes. Dimly lit with pink and blue florescent lights, it functions as a bowling-pub serving a wide selection of domestic and imported beer. Club music gets the energy going while darts and video games are available for those waiting for their turn. The second basement floor is General Bowling Alley offering twelve lanes. Opening from 11am, the whole floor is brightly lit and modestly decorated. Visitors to the Union Star Bowling Club should ask about the Red Pin Game event: anyone who scores a strike when a red pin appears as the head pin will receive a free bottle of beer.

title: Sungjae Museum of Traditional Architecture
short_description: Visitors can learn about traditional Korean architecture and construction methods at the Sungjae Museum of Traditional Architecture. The museum has many interesting and educational displays for visitors to enjoy. The museum exhibits exquisite miniature replicas of Korean palaces and temples. Visitors can also see the tools used to construct these miniatures. The first and second exhibition halls contain miniature traditional edifices that showcase the beauty of traditional architecture. In the third exhibition hall, museum-goers can learn about traditional architecture and see tools used in traditional construction.

title: Jung Saem Mool Plops
short_description: K-makeup artist Jung Saem Mool, who has been working with numerous Hallyu stars has opened up a flagship store in the Garosu-gil area. Jung’s skills and expertise as a seasoned makeup artist, consultant and entrepreneur with twenty eight years of industry experience are well-reflected in the store. Comprised of three floors with varying themes, Jung Saem Mool Plops offers brand showcases, beauty classes as well as a charming cosmetics-themed garden. Makeup products that are loved by Jun Ji-hyun, Kim Tae-hee, Song Hye-kyo, Lee Min-jung and Han Ga-in can be found at the store.

title: SeMA Nam June Paik Memorial House
short_description: The SeMA Nam June Paik Memorial House is a space that commemorates the artist Nam June Paik (1932~2006). Built on the site of the house where the world-renowned artist spent his childhood from 1937 to 1950, the Nam June Paik Memorial House restores the original single-story traditional Korean hanok house built in 1960 to trace the internationally acclaimed artist’s origins. The Nam June Paik Cafe, operated by local residents, provides a comfortable space for visitors to rest.

title: Shinsegae Duty Free
short_description: Shinsegae Duty-Free Myeongdong is located on the 8th to 12th floors of the Shinsegae Department Store Main Branch. With an area of 14,545㎡, it is close to popular tourist attractions like N Seoul Tower and Namdaemun Market, making it convenient for shopping before or after sightseeing.

title: KT&G Sangsang Madang
short_description: KT&G Sangsang Madang opened in September 2007 at the Picaso Street near Hongik Univ. and it is a multi-culture complex with seven stories above ground and four below.

title: Seoul Donhwamun Traditional Theater
short_description: The Seoul Donhwamun Traditional Theater, named after Donhwamun, the iconic gate of Changdeokgung Palace, is a premier venue for experiencing the finest Korean traditional music. It is located next to Changdeokgung Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the grand and refined Jongmyo Shrine, making it a specialized performance hall for Gugak.

title: Jeongdong Maru
short_description: Unique Venues and it is located in the middle of Seoul down town; Jeongdong-gil in where cultural heritages from Korea’s modern society are located. Jeongdong Maru is a cultural space for various events such as house concert, seminar, business events and promotional events etc.

title: SJ. Kunsthalle
short_description: SJ. Kunsthalle was made as a cultural-artistic platform for meetings and discussions, providing everyday art linked programs, such as exhibitions, parties, performances, fashion shows, and workshops.

title: Golden Blue Marina
short_description: Golden Blue Marina is a place where you could partake in the luxurious yacht experience. Open to everyone, they provide yacht tours and rentals. Enjoy the view while you leisurely float along the Han River.

title: Incheon Int'l Airport Terminal 2 Tourist Information Center
short_description: The Tourist Information Center located within Incheon Int'l Airport Terminal 2 opened on January 18th, 2018. Visitors can get information on Seoul's tourist attractions, the airport and its facilities, transportation, and various other informationin English, Japanese, and Chinese.

title: Talbang
short_description: Located in Insadong since 1984, Talbang offers a wide variety of traditional handmade masks. In the show window, you can see the hahoe, which symbolizes the Korean face, as well as gakshi, yangban used in snadae nori. The workshop uses wood to restore traditional Korean masks, and all the pieces are handmade. The process of making a hahoe-tal is also on display. Although it is a small store of about 4 square meters, the owner of Talbang has been working on various creative works here.

title: Reopening of Dongdaemun History Museum Exhibition Hall
short_description: The Dongdaemun History Museum, operated under the Seoul Museum of History, reopened the doors to its permanent exhibition hall following the two-year renovation project on Tuesday, August 11, 2020. The entire, all-new remodeled interior floor is set with carvings and gobo projectors that capture the blueprint of the excavation site of historical remains by layer to emulate the historical, figurative layers that are stacked upon each other at this very geographical site. The exhibition is characterized into the following four different themes: I. Military Training Administration & Lower Directorate; II. City Wall Floodgates; III. Two Centuries of Change; and IV. Excavated History. There are also various, fun programs for children within the exhibition and hands-on space provided that feature sand-crafting, 3D photo zones, and more.

title: Starfield Library
short_description:
Located in the center of COEX Mall, Starfield Library is an open public space where anyone can freely come to sit down, take a break, and immerse themselves in books along with other bibliophiles. A wide selection of books in various genres such as humanities, economics, hobbies, etc. are readily available. Whole sections of the library are dedicated to foreign books and famous authors. iPads can be used to read e-books. Close to 600 magazines, domestic and foreign, are available for browsing. All these qualities set Starfield Library apart from other ordinary libraries. In addition, a plethora of events take place here such as meeting with authors, book talks, poetry reading, lectures, book concerts, and more.



Frequently Asked Questions about Starfield Library
