I am curious about the lectures and performances held at the Starfield Library.
The latest lectures and performances scheduled at the Starfield Library can be found on the website below.
This month’s lectures at the Starfield Library – Check out the performances’ schedule
What are the Starfield Library operating hours?
The Starfield Library is open from 10:30 to 22:00. (As of 2025)
Can I enter the Starfield Library for free?
Yes. The Starfield Library is open to all, free of charge. (As of 2025)

title: Gongpyeong Historic Sites Museum
short_description: Gongpyeong Historic Sites Museum was created when well preserved 16th century Joseon sites were dug up during redevelopment phases of Gongpyeong district 1, 2, and 4. The museum is largely divided into 4 parts: “Coexistence of Development and Preservation”, “Gyeonpyeong-bang of the Joseon Dynasty Period”, “Modern Gongpyeong-dong”, and “Historic Sites Archives.” The completed Gongpyeong Historic Sites Museum displays the various relics and building structures of a neighborhood which managed to remain undisturbed for over 600 years, allowing visitors a closer look at the daily lives of people who had lived back in the Joseon Dynasty.

title: Gallery Kong
short_description: Since its opening in 2005, Gallery Kong has showcased a wide range of globally famous photographers, greatly influencing the photography industry in Korea.  When the gallery moved into the newly built facility next to Cheongwadae’s Chunchugwan in Samcheong-dong, it expanded from being just a photo gallery to a multimedia gallery displaying all kinds of modern art, including communication arts, sculpture, video installations, etc.  By showcasing works of globally famous artists like Bernard Faucon (France), Chen Ruo Bing (China), Michael Kenna (UK), and Erwin Olaf (Netherlands), Gallery Kong is a gallery which shows the trend of contemporary art in 21st century Korea. This gallery also plays a very crucial role in helping Korean artists establish presence abroad by connecting them to galleries and shows outside Korea.

title: Modern History Memorial Hall
short_description: Modern History Memorial Hall was built for the purpose of remembering and spreading awareness of Korean democracy and past independence movements. Spreading awareness of Korean forefathers who’ve valued and fought for ideals of freedom, equality, and democracy, the institution hopes to deliver a message that Korea is the land where forefathers dreamt of independence and achieved it.

title: Peace Culture Bunker
short_description: Peace Culture Bunker was formerly a military bunker which was transformed into a public culture and art space through recent urban regeneration efforts. The new facility was constructed in such a way as to preserve the past traces of war left on the old building and built for purpose of providing a cultural space for the local residents. The Peach Culture Bunker is currently lending out its facilities as accommodation and work spaces to writers participating in various art residency programs in an effort to revitalize local culture and art community.

title: Bukchon Village Information Center
short_description:
Nestled in a portion of Jeongdok Public Library, Bukchon Village Information Center offers tourists travel brochures, travel information, and interpretation services in English, Japanese, and Chinese.

 

As a public space, this facility displays travel books and brochures, offering tourists information about traveling Korea. Free Wi-Fi is also available so that tourists can easily look up information through their phones or laptop.

title: Mapo Tourist Information Center
short_description: Mapo Tourist Information Center is located a 3-minute walk away from Exit 7 of Hongik Univ. Station. Offering free brochures and leaflet to visitors, this facility also offers information on the various festivals, events, and performances happening in and outside of Seoul.

title: Songpa Tourist Information Center
short_description:
Songpa Tourist Information Center was created on May 1, 2015 for the convenience of visiting tourists.

Inside the center, there are computers, information on festivals, and maps readily available for visitors. There’s also chroma key technology installed on-site to provide visitors with special memories of Songpa as they take pictures of themselves with special landmarks in the background. Right outside the facility is a small resting area where visitors can sit down and take a small break admiring the view of Seokchon Lake.

title: Dongdaemun Tourist Information Center
short_description: Located in front of Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station, this facility offers travel information, interpretation services, reservation assistance, maps, guidebooks, and various facilities for the convenience of visiting travelers. Language assistance is available in English, Japanese, and Chinese. Discover Seoul Pass can be also be purchased here.

title: Itaewon Tourist Information Center (Itaewon Station)
short_description: Located inside Itaewon Station, this facility offers travel information, interpretation services, reservation assistance, maps, guidebooks, and provides various facilities for the convenience of visiting travelers. Language assistance is available in English, Japanese, and Chinese.

title: Namdaemun Market Tourist Information Center
short_description: Located within Namdaemun Market, this facility offers travel information, interpretation services, reservation assistance, maps, guidebooks, and various facilities for the convenience of visiting travelers. Language assistance is available in English, Japanese, and Chinese.

title: Seoul Tourism Souvenir Shop∙Tourist Information Center
short_description: Located in Jongno, this facility displays Seoul tourism souvenirs and resolves inconveniences during travel such as offering travel information, dealing with the overcharged and mediating other problems. Language assistance is available in English, Japanese and Chinese.

title: Gwanghwamun Tourist Information Center
short_description: Located in Gwanghwamun, this facility offers travel information, interpretation services, reservation assistance, maps, guidebooks, and various facilities for the convenience of visiting travelers. Language assistance is available in English, Japanese, and Chinese.

title: Sinchon Tourist Information Center
short_description: Located at the former Sinchon Station, this facility offers travel information, interpretation services, reservation assistance, maps, guidebooks, and various facilities for the convenience of visiting travelers. Language assistance is available in English, Japanese, and Chinese.

title: Seoraeseom Island
short_description: Seoraeseom Island is a small artificial island located between Dongjakdaegyo Bridge and Banpodaegyo Bridge. Although it's an island, it's located closer to the river banks, making it easily accessible via the 3 bridges connecting it to Banpo Hangang Park. Featuring magnificent weeping willows and widespread canola flower fields during springtime, this site is commonly used for natural and environmental research. Unlike other sites which take advantage of their higher vantage points to attract visitors, Seoraeseom Island takes advantage of it being on the same surface level as Hangang River, offering visitors spectacular views of the city's buildings and sunsets.

title: CGV Cine Library
short_description: CGV Cine Library is the first cinema library and art house to exist in Korea. Possessing over 10,000 books on various movies, it’s a place where people can come to read, discuss, and share their love of movies and cinema.

title: Bongwonsa Temple
short_description: Originally built on the site of Yonsei University by Queen Jinseong of the Shilla Dynasty in 889 A.D., Bongwonsa Temple was moved to its current site by King Yongjo of the Joseon Dynasty in 1748. The temple grounds holds a pond filled with lotus flowers. This attracts a lot of visitors, especially in the summer, as many gather to view the beautiful blooming flowers as they enjoy the festivities. It's the perfect place to visit for calming your mind and spirit.

title: Baekbeom Square Park
short_description: Located in Namsan Mountain, Baekbeom Square Park can be found by walking up the mountain path from Hoehyeon-dong. A statue of Kim Gu - a leader, an educator, a politician - symbolizes the spirit of patriotism which led to the Korea's independence. In front of the statue is a large grassy square and road leading up the mountain. Statues of General Kim Yu-shin's horse and Yi Si-yeong can also be found inside the park.

title: Oh!Zemidong
short_description: Oh!Zemidong is a Chungmuro film center and public media center sponsored by Seoul Metropolitan Government and sponsored by Seoul Film Commission. Equipped with various film projects, art books, editing rooms, and film equipment, this facility is open to the everyone. A cultural playground made up of an archive, gallery, theater, education hall, editing room, and a film equipment rental station, Oh!Zemidong also provides regular monthly screenings and educational programs on film culture.

title: Korean Catholic Martyrs’ Museum
short_description: To publicize the persecution of Catholic martyrs who lost their lives during the Byeongin Persecution back in 1866, Jeoldusan Matyrs' Memorial Hall changed its name into Korean Catholic Martyrs’ Museum. Its facilities include a pilgrimage church, a sacred r ​ oom containing the remains of a martyr, a museum showcasing Catholic records, documents, and relics, and an outdoor exhibition.

title: Seoul Women's Plaza
short_description: Seoul Women's Plaza is a public center offering its facilities for community events and programs for the women and their families residing in the neighborhood. Also equipped with a library full of books on gender equality and a playground (offering part-time childcare services), Seoul Women's Plaza is operated as a NGO to support women in Korea.

title: Mugyewon
short_description:
Mugyewon is a traditional cultural space located in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu. It is a restored hanok, reconstructed using materials from Ojinam, the first registered restaurant in Seoul. Nestled at the foot of Inwangsan Mountain, visitors can experience the serene beauty of Korean architecture and appreciate the tranquil scenery. 

The site of Mugyewon, known as Mugaejeongsa, was the villa of Grand Prince Anpyeong, the third son of King Sejong. Inspired by its resemblance to the utopian paradise he saw in a dream, Grand Prince Anpyeong built a pavilion where he composed poetry and practiced archery. This historically significant location is also where An Gyeon, the foremost painter of the time, created the famous "Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land" in just three days. 

Since its opening in 2014, Mugyewon has offered a variety of cultural programs, including performances, exhibitions, lectures, education, and hands-on experiences. If you wish to experience Korean tradition and culture amidst scenery as beautiful as the mythical Peach Blossom Land, we recommend visiting this place.

title: Jungnang Adventure Zone : Youth Experience Forest
short_description: Located in Jungnang-gu, Jungnang Adventure Zone : Youth Experience Forest is an outdoor adventure park and learning center where children can partake in a variety of activities and educational programs. In order to preserve the park's natural habitat and ecology, the park was built in a non-invasive method using the minimum of man-made materials.

title: Seoul Book Bogo
short_description: Seoul Book Bogo is a new cultural space created by Seoul Metropolitan Government to house old, secondhand books they gathered from old bookstores around the city. Featuring an old secondhand bookstore, library, and cultural programs, Seoul Book Bogo is separated into 4 spaces for value, sharing, enjoyment, and experience. Visitors can feel the value of old books in the space for value, read books donated by famous intellectuals in the space for sharing, experience unique indie books in the space for enjoyment, and participate in various cultural book programs in the space for experience.

title: Amore Pacific Museum of Art (APMA)
short_description: Amore Pacific Museum of Art (APMA) is a newly opened museum inside Amore Pacific's Yongsan headquarters. Aiming for "an open space to find beauty in the ordinary", this museum was established as a space for fostering open communication. To this end, the museum collects, studies, and exhibits anicent Korean and contemporary arts, also supporting researchers, academic societies, and young writers in the process. The basement floor features an exhibition showcasing ancient Korean art and contemporary art. Connecting the first three floors, the "Atrium" features the museum lobby, museum shop, another exhibition space called "APMA Cabinet," and a library for museums around the world (apLAP).

title: Seoul Science Park
short_description:
Created to foster children's creativity, Seoul Science Park is an interactive science experience center featuring close to 21 different experience exhibits including a Science Playground (with 24 different exhibits), Eco Experience Center, and Nature Observatory (made up of an agricultural farm and floral garden).

 

A place to learn the principles of science naturally through play, Seoul Science Park utilizes activities like Squirrel Jump and water to promote interest in science and foster creativity in children.

 

Inside the research lab, visitors can interact with exhibits to understand Foucault's pendulum and other scientific principles. Inside the central garden, visitors can enjoy beautiful aquatic plants like iris and lotus. The Eco Experience Center features insects, fish, and birds while the Nature Observatory features various crops, flowers, and wild plant life.

title: Nodeul Island
short_description:
Located under the Han River Bridge connecting Yongsan and Noryangjin, Nodeul Island is a cultural space with a great focus on nature, books, and music. Officially opened on Sept. 28th, 2019, Nodeul Island features a variety of facilities such as Live House, Nodeul Gallery, Nodeul Lounge, Nodeul Book Store, Multi Hall, and more.



Frequently Asked Questions about Nodeul Island

What are the operating hours of Nodeul Island?

Nodeul Island’s operating hours are as follows. (As of 2025)

  • • Summer season (March-October) : Tuesday-Friday 10:00~21:00 / Weekends and holidays 10:00~22:00

  • • Winter season (November-February) : Tuesday-Sunday 10:00~20:00

  • • Outdoor space: open 24 hours


※ Closed on Mondays, and each facility may have different operating hours.

What kind of facilities are there on Nodeul Island?

There are various facilities such as concert hall, gallery, lounge, multi-purpose hall, restaurants, and more. You can check the detailed information on the website below.

Nodeul Island facilities floor guide

Are pets allowed on Nodeul Island?

Pets are permitted if on a leash or in a cage. However, admission to the indoor space is not allowed. (As of 2054)

title: Jeongdong 1928 Art Center
short_description: The Jeongdong 1928 Art Center was built in 1928 as the headquarters for the Salvation Army officers to do their missionary and social work. As one of the 10 buildings in Seoul with great historical significance, the center was designated as Seoul Monument No. 20 in 2002. Since 2019, it has been used as a public space for culture and art.

title: Neorang Narang Urirang Stamp Healing Tour
short_description: Participants in the stamp tour can receive discount benefits from nearby partner stores (restaurants, cafes, etc.) if they get stamps by finishing the four courses (Meeting Plaza, Pine Tree Rest Area, April 19 Observatory, and Modern History Memorial Hall),while those excelling in posting postscripts are presented with souvenirs. As cultural heritage commentators are located at important positions, participants can listen to explanations about historical and cultural heritages during the stamp tour.Professionalhealth counselors and CPR instructors stick around to measure blood pressure, blood sugar levels, and body composition, while providing CPR training and offering smart health tour services for workout consultation.

title: Seoul Sewerage Science Museum
short_description: Established in 2017 to promote the history and science of sewerage, the Seoul Sewerage Science Museum is the nation's first science museum specializing in sewerage. It was constructed at the site of the Cheonggyecheon Sewage Treatment Plant, the country's first sewage disposal plant, to continue the historical significance and values of the facility. The museum is also a space that is centered on on-site experience, comprised of a science exhibition hall that displays the history, technology, and future of domestic and overseas sewerage, as well as a water reclamation center where visitors can take a look around sewerage facilities. As the center of environmental education, the Seoul Sewerage Science Museum offers various programs to teach the process of sewage purification and the significance of water.

title: Hwagyesa Temple
short_description:
Hwagyesa Temple was founded by Seonsa (Seon master) Sinwol in 1522 (17th year of King Jungjong's reign). Originally, Daesa (a high Buddhist priest) Beopin, or Tanmun, built a hermitage called Bodeokam near the site of Hwagyesa Temple, preserving long-standingBuddhist tradition. Later on, Seonsa Sinwol would move the hermitage to the current location and rename it Hwagyesa. During the Joseon Period, the royal family frequented the temple and Regent Heungseon Daewongun supported the temple during the latteryears of Joseon.

A cradle of the enlightenment movement, Hwagyesa Temple produced a number of figures who embroiders the modern history of Korea, including Mubul and Cha Hong-sik, and is also known to have served as a place for monks who participated in the Gapsin Revolutionto prepare for the enlightenment movement.

Hwagyesa Temple is a historic venue where the Korean Language Society organized a stay of nine Korean language scholars, including Lee Hui-seung and Choe Hyeon-bae, wherein they completed the Unified Korean Orthography in 1933. Recently, the temple becameinternationally known as being a center for worldwide propagation. In 1991, the Daejeokgwangjeon Hall was established and an international seonwoen (Seon monastery) was opened on the 4th floor to accommodate buddhists from other countries.

Programs
ㆍ Prayer/ceremonial offering to Buddhaㆍ Buddhist University/Citizens' Seonwoen (meditation practice)ㆍ Hwagyesa Templestay: A program to experience the temple's daily life, traditional culture of Korean Buddhism and spirit of practice while stayingin the temple

title: 1Million Dance Studio
short_description: Located in Seongsu-dong, 1Million Dance Studio is Korea's largest dance studio and management agency, offering both group and one-on-one dance lessons. Come and experience the joy of dancing with some Korea's most renowned dancers.

title: Lumiere
short_description: Originally a French term meaning "to shine," the name, Lumiere, came from the idea to "instill beauty" within its customers so they may shine all the more beautiful! Lumiere# strictly adheres to the use of 100% natural, premium hair extensions for a gorgeous hair texture. The salon most specializes in hair braiding that keeps to the natural shape of the head, while also offering scalp treatment to promote a healthier scalp and beautiful looking hair.

title: Smashing Bowl (Cheongdam)
short_description: Smashing Bowl combines the best of both worlds, bowling and food & drink, for a unique experience you'll never forget! The Cheongdam location, in particular, offers more of a luxurious vibe with a chic interior and private VIP and VVIP rooms that are very popular among visitors! Brings your friends, or maybe just that special someone, to enjoy a vibrant bowling atmosphere with delicious cocktails and beer.

title: Seoul Metropolitan Archives
short_description: As an public archive providing records services for the public, the Seoul Metropolitan Archives collects a number of records and memoirs tracing the history of the city government, as well as the residents of Seoul, and specializes in the preservation and management of such records. The SMA also plans and operates several public programs, including exhibitions, openings, and more.

title: Jeon Tae-il Memorial Hall
short_description: Having been built by the Seoul city government, the Jeon Tae-il Memorial Hall is a labor complex facility erected to illuminate upon the historical significance of Jeon Tae-il, whose self-sacrifice served as a pivotal point in time in the history of the Korean labor movement. The young man gave everything he had to create a world that centered itself around the mentality that workers are people that have the right to live, work, and study in good health. In order to help bring Jeon Tae-il's dream into fruition, the hall urges unity between the labor force, the youth of the country, and the public, brought together around the ideals of love and solidarity.

title: Kimdaljin Art Archives & Museum
short_description:
All posters featured in the exhibition:

  

  ○ Have been archived within the museum after either being donated, or created on museum grounds

  ○ Encapsulate a form of artistry that appeals primarily to the human senses 

  ○ Maintain significant usability as a visual symbol that beckons memories of the past, as well as history

  ○ Offer a chance for expo-goers to further expand their view of cultural history through provided commentary that pinpoints the artistic significance of each poster


The Kimdaljin Art Archives & Museum opens its exhibition, Art Posters Outliving Their Exhibitions, which is grounded in the idea of the "art poster." As the oldest form of media used to market and advertise for exhibitions and galleries within the art community, the art poster is something that, once a certain period has passed, loses its practical use, leaving only its artistic and archival value intact. Especially for a solo exhibition, art posters are viewed prior to works displayed at an exhibition and uniquely function as the first impression of the artist among the public.

title: National Hangeul Museum
short_description:
The National Hangeul Museum was opened on October 9, 2014, to create and promote the literary and cultural value of Hangeul, the nation's most significant cultural heritage. The National Hangeul Museum investigates, collects, and researches materials scattered around the country and abroad and shows the cultural diversity and future value of Hangeul through exhibitions. It is a place where Hangeul culture blossoms through education that aims for communication and empathy across generations and nationalities.


- Closed from October 2024 to the second half of 2028

title: Geumseonsa Temple
short_description: Located in Gugi-dong of Jongno-gu, the Geumseonsa Temple is a beautiful temple that was restored in 1955 following its destruction during the Japanese Occupation and later came to be officially designated as Tangible Culture Heritage no. 161. The temple stay program featured at the temple attracts a number of Koreans and foreigners alike. There is also a great overlook view of the city from the southwest foot of Bukhansan National Park.

title: KCDF Gallery
short_description:
Located along the street of tradition itself, Insadong, KCDF Gallery is a space dedicated to the exhibition of crafts and was created to help promote the rise of the crafts industry, while contributing to a communicative platform for craftsmen and women, as well as the dissessimation of the consumer culture of crafts. The KCDF Library is also available, serving as a ground for research activity that offers literature and various data on a wide array of crafts designs along with exhibitions, training programs, and seminar spaces for artists in the crafts design culture industry. On the first-floor shop of the gallery, visitors may also purchase premium crafts created by some of the finest specialists and artists in the country.
* The Korea Craft & Design Foundation is a public government organization operated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism that was established for the promotion of crafts, public design, and traditional & lifestyle culture. The foundation focuses on establishing a cultural identify of Korea through the dissessimation and promotion of crafts, design, and tradtional & lifestyle cultures , in addition to contributing to an improved quality of life by strengthening the country's compeitive capactiy.

title: Tourist Information Center in Seoul Tourism Plaza
short_description: The Seoul Tourism Plaza Tourist Information Center, located in the Samil Building in Jongno-gu, is an open space where visitors can obtain comprehensive tourism information about Seoul. It provides tourist guide services in Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese. The center also features amenities for tourists, such as rest areas, as well as a souvenir shop called Seoul My Soul Shop. This makes it a destination for foreign visitors and locals seeking tourist information about Seoul.

title: Amore Pacific Flagship Store (Seongsu)
short_description: Amor Pacific, a well-known cosmetics manufacturer, holds its headquarters in Seongsu. Previously operated as an auto repair shop, the three-story building has been reborn into something that resembles more a cultural complex rather than a basic shop. There are many plants and trees that are placed around Amor Pacific. On the ground floor, visitors can enjoy the view of the green garden out of the large windows while sitting on the comfortable sofas. It has a large space called the Beauty Library, where visitors can personally test out over 2,000 products and have access to the services of professional makeup artists. Visitors can also enjoy drinks at the Osulloc Cafe on the 2nd floor, and enjoy the view of Seoul from the rooftop.

title: Sulwhasoo Flagship Store
short_description: The Sulwhasoo flagship store is a five-story building with a golden design and is located in Gangnam. The building's interior is based off of a lantern-inspired motif, following a philosophy that represents the brand's commitment to illuminate beauty. The Sulwhasoo flagship store, which has years of beauty experience and wisdom, is a space where visitors can experience eternal beauty. On the first floor of the building, visitors can see the history of the brand, which started in 1996, and they can test and purchase a variety of Sulwhasoo products. There is also a terrace space where visitors can enjoy the beautiful scenery of Seoul.

title: Yongmasan Mountain
short_description: Yongmasan Mountain is the highest mountain in Jungnang-gu and the highest peak of Achasan Mountain. Yongmasan Mountain, famous for its wonderful views, has a hiking course that's good for beginners. Before beginning your hike, visit Yongma Waterfall Park to view the man-made waterfalls and stop by Yongmasanjeong Pavilion to take a break and view the scenery. The course to Yongmabong Peak consists of many stairs. From the Yongmasan Observatory, you can easily see the views of Seoul in one glance. When you arrive at the summit of Yongmasan, Yongmabong Peak, you will also find a road to the summit of Achasan Mountain. Thanks to the beautiful sunset and night view from Yongmasan Mountain it is a very popular place for night hiking.

title: National Meteorological Museum of Korea
short_description:
It is the first meteorological science and history museum that researches and preserves the meteorological culture of Korea from the Joseon Dynasty to modern times. The museum owns the world's last surviving rain gauge instrument, known as the Rain Gauge of the Chungcheonggamyeong Provincial Office, Gongju, invented 200 years earlier than the West.
The Seoul Meteorological Observatory (52 Songwol-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul), where the National Meteorological Museum was established, is the center of Korea's modern and contemporary meteorological history. The modern meteorological observation started in Wonnam-dong, Gyeongseong, in 1907 and moved to Songwol-dong via Nakwon-dong. The building at the time of its establishment in 1932 and extension in 1939 have been maintained and served as the Korea Meteorological Administration until the administration moved to Dongjak-gu, Seoul, in 1998. For this continuity, it was selected as a ‘100-year observatory’ by the World Meteorological Organization in 2017. In 2016, when the museum was being built, the Seoul Meteorological Observatory was restored to its original form based on the architectural drawings of the 20th-century meteorological station kept at the National Archives. Please enjoy the change of weather and history at the National Meteorological Museum, the heart of Korea's meteorology.

title: Yongsan Park Partially Open Site
short_description: The site was a previous residence for US military officers. It was named Sobinggo during the Joseon Dynasty because ice was stored nearby. It is now called Yongsan Garrison, including the site of the U.S. Army officers' quarters. Still, the American soldiers stationed in Yongsan right after the defeat of Japan did not call it Yongsan Garrison but Camp Sobinggo. From the Liberation to the Korean War, it was called Camp Sobinggo, but after the ceasefire agreement was reached, it was named Yongsan Garrison when the 8th US Army moved in.

title: National Hangeul Museum Permanent Exhibition <Hunminjeongeum, The Design of a Writing System Beyond the Millennia>
short_description: In 1443, King Sejong created the Korean character Hunminjeongeum. In 1446, King Sejong created Hunminjeongeum, a book that revealed the purpose and principle of creating new characters. At the beginning of the book, a new world that he dreamed of was designed. The exhibition hall was composed of 7 spaces according to the sentence in the introduction of Hunminjeongeum Follow the Hunminjeongeum designed by King Sejong, which contains a writing system, and feel the brilliant history and the culture timelessness achieved by Hangeul.

title: The 12th Seoul Mediacity Pre-Biennale 《Station》
short_description: Seoul Mediacity Biennale is an exhibition and workshop that examines the perception of media art from an experiential level by revisiting media practices and experiments in Korean art history along with the collection resources. The Nam-Seoul Museum of Art in Seoul exhibition hall introduces works and materials from the previous biennale, and workshops are held every Saturday.

title: Shinhan Museum
short_description: Let's look at the development of Korean finance at the Shinhan Museum operated by Shinhan Bank. In addition, a free audio guide is provided so that anyone can easily understand the history of currency and finance on the Korean Peninsula, so make sure to use the service.

title: House of Aromatica
short_description: This sustainable beauty & lifestyle brand advocates healthy beauty with the essence of aromatherapy

title: Kim Geun-tae Memorial Library-Archives
short_description: Kim Geun-tae Memorial Library-Archives which is located at the corner of the way going to Bukhansan National Park, as a Larchiveum, it is a library to read a book but at the same time, it's a museum that has a story of democracy and human rights, and also an art gallery to appreciate art works. A courtyard, which was naturally made at the center which was created by connecting the both ends of the two buildings with the bridge, is the most opened space in Kim Geun-tae Memorial Library-Archives and it's a space where you can directly feel the sunlight and the wind. As a library and an art gallery, the installation work is located on the courtyard so you can see an art work in the nature. At the rooftop called 'Sanbaramgil',  various plays and events will be held with the background of the nature.

title: Incheon International Airport Terminal 1 Tourist Information Center (West)
short_description: The Seoul Tourism Information Center at Incheon International Airport T1, located on the west side of Incheon International Airport, is open year-round for international travelers visiting Korea. Visitors can receive travel information necessary for touring Seoul and find promotional materials for various tourist attractions.

title: Kkummaru(Dream Park) in Children's Grand Park
short_description: This park, filled with thedreams and hopes of childhood, is actually a place that holds a painfulhistory. This place was originally where the tomb of Empress Sunmyeong, thewife of Sunjung, the last king of the Joseon Dynasty, was enshrined. However, the tomb was moved to another location during the Japanese occupation, while a golf course was built for the Japanese and remained even after liberation. Kkummaru (Dream Peak) in Children's Grand Park was Korea's first "clubhouse" for tourist visiting Korea. After the opening ofChildren’s Grand Park, Kkummaru wasused for different purposes such as an academic hall, exhibition space, andsuperintendent’s office. Later, Kkummaru was able torecover its original structure that was iconic of Korea’s modern andcontemporary architecture through the hands of famous renovation architects,Cho Sung-ryong and Choon Choi. They erased the superimposed layers and filledthe building with programs for a book cafe and picnic area to reintroduce it asa space to help children dream again, hence the kkum (dream) part of the name.

title: ParkNoSoo Museum
short_description: Pro-Japanesepolitician Yoon Deok-young built the house for his daughter in 1937, whichlater became painter Park No-soo’s house in 1973. Park No-soo, who devotedhimself to art over the 40 years he lived in this house, donated it back tosociety along with his artwork. The historical residence was reborn as an artmuseum in 2013 through the Jongno Cultural Foundation. Despiteits long history of 80 years, this well-maintained building was recognized forits cultural value and was registered Cultural Heritage Material No. 1 of Seoulin 1991.

title: ChoiManLin Museum
short_description: Theelegant two-story, Western-style building was built in the 1970s. Here,sculptor Choi Man Lin created his world of art for about 30 years from 1988. Evenwith all its traces of artistry intact, it eventually grew to become the ChoiMan Lin Museum with the help of the Seongbuk-gu District and EMA Architects. Reborn as an art museum in2019, this building contains the traces of sculptor Choi Man Lin, which werepreserved through a remodeling method that protects the appearance of theexisting building as much as possible. Thisbuilding, which shows off its architectural beauty while maximizing itsfunction as an art museum, won the Excellence Award at the 2020 Public BuildingAwards of Korea.

title: Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture
short_description: Built in the 1970s, this two-story detached house was remodeled in 1986 by Kim Joong-up, who added exotic elements to every corner of the house based on traditional Korean architecture. This is a place where you can get a glimpse of the housing culture of the middle class at the time, and was designated as a Seoul Future Heritage in 2017. The KimJoong-up House of Architectural Culture harmoniously integrates Korean and Western architectural styles. The second-floor living room has an umul-maru, rafter structure, and windows covered with changhoji paper, which are mainly used in hanok, but with a modern interpretation. In contrast, the bathroom was designed in a European style. The dry bathroom with a dressing room attached, something that wasn’t common in Korea during the '70s and '80s, has a vintage jade-colored interior that stands out. Stepping out to the elegantly decorated garden, a water element, a characteristic of Kim Joong-up's architecture, is located on one side of the yard. Even equipped with its own small greenhouse, the Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture contains immense nature in the garden.

title: National Geographic Special Exhibition — OCEAN: The Greatest Record
short_description: Please check the Interpark Ticket website for more details

title: Songjeong Jebang gil
short_description: Songjeong Jebang gil is located along Jungnangcheon, extending from Seongdong Bridge to Gwangnaru gil Jebang. It is famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot in spring, a green shaded walkway filled with cicada sounds in summer, and a colorful foliage path in autumn. It has been selected by the city of Seoul as one of the top 220 summer green roads and one of the top 93 autumn foliage roads, and is known as a walking path along the water. It is also recognized as a cherry blossom attraction and has been featured as a filming location for commercial advertisements. Enjoy a healing walk along the trail colored by the special seasonal tones of five thousand king cherry trees and ginkgo trees that create a dense woodland.

title: Samilro Changgo Theater
short_description: Samilro Changgo Theater is a small-theater-based complex cultural space centered around a 50-seat adaptable performance hall, along with studios and an exhibition space called Samilro Space, located in Jeo-dong, Jung-gu, Seoul. As a Seoul Future Heritage site that has continued the flow of the Korean small theater movement and experimental theater since its opening in 1975, it currently functions as an open culture and arts platform where creators and citizens meet by operating its own planning programs for performances, exhibitions, and the incubation of young artists.

title: NONFICTION Hannam
short_description: NONFICTION is a lifestyle beauty brand created for moments when you face your truest self. Based on the finest ingredients and delicate perfumery, it offers perfumes that create a mysterious and unique mood and body care products that make the start and end of your day more special. NONFICTION Hannam is a flagship store for lifestyle beauty brands where you can shop for perfumes, hand creams, and more. There is a sink where you can try hand washes and lotions, and a fragrance testing station is available to help you experience the scents you desire.

title: Ktown4u COEX
short_description: Ktown4u COEX is a K-Culture complex cultural space located in COEX, Samseong-dong, Gangnam-gu, a densely populated area. Visitors can experience Hallyu culture through collaborations with K-POP and in various fields such as beauty, fashion, and lifestyle.  On the 2nd floor, SQUARE is a permanent store that sells products based on K-Culture. It primarily offers the latest released K-POP albums, goods, magazines, various Hallyu lifestyle items, clothing, and beauty products. The 3rd-floor Academy is an experiential space open to everyone who loves K-POP. It offers unique tourist experience programs, including one-day classes where participants can experience K-POP artists’ dance and vocals. The 4th floor, SPACE, is where K-POP artists and fans can interact directly. It hosts themed pop-up events, such as artist comeback events, dramas, art exhibitions, and more.

title: Nubim Kim Group Korea Tour
short_description: Korean composer Nubim leads the Dutch superband Nubim Kim Group in Connectivity, a performance that reinterprets Korean tradition and world art through jazz and a contemporary lens. From shamanic music and Jindo Arirang to flamenco and Hemingway, the concert brings a genre- and border-defying musical dialogue to the Seoul stage.

title: SM Entertainment
short_description: SM Entertainment is one of the leading entertainment agencies in South Korea, representing popular K-pop groups such as Girls' Generation, SHINee, EXO, NCT, and aespa. The headquarters of SM Entertainment is located in Seoul Forest, and within the headquarters, there is an SM Store where albums, merchandise, and goods of their artists are sold.

title: Seokpajeong Seoul Museum of Art
short_description: It not only exhibits world-class works themed on contemporary art but also operates appreciation programs and various creative activities tailored to children's eye levels. With an integrated admission ticket, you can view both the museum exhibitions and Seokpajeong.

title: Kim Jihee’s Solo Exhibition: DIVINITY
short_description: Museum Wave is celebrating its first anniversary with its inaugural full-scale exhibition featuring Kim Ji-hee's solo exhibition “DIVINITY.” Known domestically and internationally for her imagery of girls wearing glasses and animals, Kim Ji-hee has gained significant popularity, particularly in China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. This exhibition will showcase the 10-meter masterpiece "Eternal Golden," first presented at the K11 Art Museum in China earlier this year. This work, debuting in Korea, was meticulously created over four years using traditional Korean paper (jangji) and fine brush techniques. It depicts the finite nature of life, likening it to a single day, and portrays humans' desires and adventures from dawn to night. This exhibition provides a rare opportunity to view one of the artist's most significant works. This exhibition, spread across four galleries, begins on the first floor with the 10-meter masterpiece "Eternal Golden," exploring the theme of “desire.” On the second floor, the Dongja Gallery features traditional paintings inspired by the Museum Wave's predecessor, the Old Stone Museum, unveiling the artist's first digital work themed around divinity. The main exhibition hall on the second floor will host the Trunk Show series, which has garnered immense domestic and international popularity. On the third floor, visitors can watch videos showcasing the artist's creative process and international blockbuster exhibitions and explore new works depicting various scenes of a girl, symbolizing the possibility of hope.

title: Bosingak Pavilion: Echoes of Time
short_description:
Bosingak Pavilion is a well-known landmark that can be easily spotted by anyone passing through Jongno Street. The street's name, Jongno, which means "Bell Street," is derived from the presence of this historic bell. The chime of the Bosingak Bell, especially during the transition to the new year, has become a cherished tradition. Historically, Bosingak Pavilion functioned as a public clock maintained by the government. When the water clock at Borugak indicated the time, the bell at Bosingak would be rung to announce the time throughout Hanyang. During the Joseon Dynasty, the residents of Hanyang began and ended their days with the sound of the Bosingak bell.
The exhibition "Bosingak Pavilion: Echoes of Time" delves into the history and evolution of the Bosingak Pavilion. Through this exhibit, visitors can explore the daily lives of Joseon-era Hanyang residents, who lived according to the rhythmic chimes of the Bosingak bell.

title: SeMA Omnibus : Planet Nine
short_description: The Seoul Museum of Art will present “SeMA Omnibus: Planet Nine” at the Nam Seoul Museum of Art from July 31 to October 27. SeMA Omnibus is a large-scale exhibition of the museum’s collection that explores the institution’s 2024 theme, "Connection," from various perspectives through an omnibus format. Between July and August, the exhibition will open sequentially across four locations, including the main and branch museums. As the first installment of SeMA Omnibus, Planet Nine focuses on non-human entities embedded in contemporary art, inviting visitors to explore planetary thinking beyond human-centered perspectives. The exhibition contemplates the possibility of coexistence between diverse beings, depicting rich connections between humans and non-humans. Visitors are invited to a journey to the solar system's ninth planet, a world filled with new possibilities.

title: Seoul Museum of Art Buk Seoul Branch
short_description: Opened in 2013, the Buk Seoul branch of the Seoul Museum of Art is the first and largest branch of the Seoul Museum of Art. As a contemporary art space representing northern Seoul, it is a cultural landmark where art and everyday life naturally meet. It was designed as a cultural communication space where the museum and park come together, and where people, nature, and art live and breathe in harmony. Reflecting the place name Nowon, which is derived from the meaning 'Reed Hill', the museum is located on a small hill that appears to bring the beautiful natural scenery of Suraksan and Bulamsan, once hidden behind apartment complexes, into the heart of the city. All exhibitions, except for special exhibitions, can be viewed free of charge, making it a beloved and accessible destination for tourists as well.

title: Jinchan
short_description:
People in royal palace are busy more than ever as preparing a banquet. A dancer comes to the palace to assist the banquet now tells us the story about jinchan. The elegant and refined movements of dancers in colorful costumes and vivid attire will bring you to the true beauty of royal banquet. 
*The language of the performance is in English

title: Medicube Flagship Store
short_description: Medicube Seongsu is an interactive beauty flagship store that expresses the skin regeneration image of PDRN with a 'Pink Fairy' and butterfly motif. On the 1st floor, you can explore the brand's worldview and popular products, and on the 2nd floor, you can directly test AGE-R beauty devices and skincare products. By adding participatory content such as a photo booth, device decoration, and a pinball event, it provides a beauty experience that goes beyond product purchases.

title: Keep Calm and Give a Shit
short_description:
Keep Calm and Give a Shit introduces the paintings and animations of four artists, Hun Kyu Kim, SOON.EASY, Tala Madani, and Wong Ping, are gaining attention in the domestic and international art scene with their cuteness and familiarity. The common point among these four artists is their ability to capture the audience's attention through cute characters, comic elements, and techniques and that they tell stories about various social issues through imaginative, fairytale-like images and satirical wordplay.

The canvases and screens, which depict characters and events from refined comics or animations, seem to remind us of the LCD frames of media that we gaze at all day. The subjects and images in each work are also filled with familiar imagery that feels like something we've seen somewhere before, whether through various repetitive feeds on our mobile devices or well-known memes. However, these familiar images and characters do not simply remain cute. They embody the sharp sense of humor and insightful interpretation of the four artists regarding the acute issues that surround us here and now - including the Ukrainian war, political problems in Hong Kong, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and media, surveillance symbolized by panopticon, and ideologies. As such, they demand active engagement from the audience in their interpretation. The narratives that traverse excessive narratives and broad topics in the paintings of Hun Kyu Kim and SOON.EASY and the stories depicted in Wong Ping's animations that resemble his own diary are similar to stories about the absurdities of our daily life and the world around us. These stories concocted by the artists feel as if they are our own experiences because the artists delve into universal themes to such an extent. Moreover, as we lead similar lives in an information-driven city, rather than experiencing the world firsthand, we perceive the world through symbols and images that have been edited and reconstructed beyond the glass screens, as evident in the artists’ works. Tala Madani sharply exposes in "Fan" how we rely entirely on the constant feed of unreliable information. Madani states, "We need art that triggers shifts in consciousness and new ideas, rather than art like morphine that weakens reality with beauty or alleviates pain.

At this juncture, the art we need should be cute and familiar, presented smoothly without any aversion, yet above all, it should be art capable of revitalizing our paralyzed perception, like our sense of smell during the pandemic. Through this exhibition, the hope is for the viewers to contemplate whether, like the artists, they construct their daily lives with a sensitive perspective that reflects their own thoughts and emotions or if they are inundated with indiscriminate assaults of superficial images and information. The hope is to become more sensitive and connected to the present "here and now" of life.

title: Take My Eyes Off
short_description:
"Take my eyes off' focuses on contemporary painting caught in a complex and passionate entanglement with “vision” and “images.” This exhibition examines the strategies employed by today’s painters who, in response to an overwhelming visual landscape saturated with images, attempt to break free and search for a new visual language.

Using “eyes” as a central metaphor, the exhibition presents contemporary paintings that challenge established modes of seeing, thus revealing painting’s potential as a practice of resistance and renewal. 'Take my eyes off' invites viewers to encounter works that strive to “pull our eyes away” from today's image overload, offering insight into the story of painting as it confronts its own limitations."

title: Hanyang  Adventure Begins!
short_description: The Seoul Museum of History's Children's Museum, an interactive historical playground where children can embark on a time expedition to Hanyang, Seoul during the Joseon Dynasty, has officially opened its doors. <Hanyang Adventure Begins!> consists of three thematic courses (science, education, and professions) comprising a total of 13 sections. Child visitors wear "Paerongi," a smart device for experience missions, around their necks as they navigate throughout the exhibition halls, solve missions independently, and naturally learn about the history and culture of Seoul. Shall we embark on a special time travel journey to Hanyang, Seoul during the Joseon Dynasty with family at the Children's Museum of the Seoul Museum of History?

title: BEAUTY, TRANSLATED
short_description: B the B is a permanent exhibition space that curates Seoul's attractive beauty brands with B the B's unique sensibility. Diagnose your skin and scalp through AI-based beauty-tech devices that are not easily encountered elsewhere, and experience various interactive programs such as virtual makeup and Life Four Cuts photo booths. Additionally, you can receive a one-stop service where you can test products recommended through your diagnosis and purchase them online. <BEAUTY, TRANSLATED> is an exhibition designed to read and experience the different languages of beauty for each brand, rather than defining beauty by a single standard. Encounter the ways of beauty proposed by each brand, such as moisture and soothing, color and expression, technology and diagnosis, and recovery and ritual, all in one space, providing new beauty experiences and inspiration beyond just products.

title: Collection of Moments
short_description:
From September 1st to October 13th, 2023, the Vivian Choi Gallery will host a three-person exhibition titled 'Collection of Moments,' featuring artists Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil. In this exhibition, three artists who have collaborated in the realm of painting techniques come together to illuminate the subtle relationship between memory and the subconscious through artworks that uniquely express inner landscapes preserved within the time and space of the past, using their distinctive visual languages.

Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil, the artists, capture moments unconsciously stored in memory within spaces they casually overlook. The subtle emotions of the artists, intertwined with the current inner consciousness, intersect with the spaces and objects that once existed in the subconscious. This unique painterly expression by the three artists highlights their ability to capture this delicate relationship as they reconfigure it in a dreamlike manner. The works of Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil do not spotlight any particular events, figures, or objects as protagonists. Instead, they breathe life into places and objects that often go unnoticed, like the modest roofs of an obscure neighborhood, a secluded and unnamed beach, or a small potted plant guarding a desk corner. These surroundings, taken for granted yet filled with the artists' momentary feelings and emotions, are reconstructed to become unique landscapes with different memories, offering a special perspective.

Through the three-person exhibition "Collection of Moments" by Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil, the hope is that you'll experience the opportunity to observe the infinite world unfolding around you. Ordinary objects that go unnoticed, places casually passed by, elements of life that remain inconspicuous in the periphery, and those that construct life with simplicity come together. Gain the experience of seeing the limitless world that surrounds you.

title: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon
short_description: The Seoul Museum of Art will hold the exhibition "The Hanging Gardens of Babylon" from August 30th to November 19th. The Hanging Gardens of Babylon is an exhibition exploring the concept of 'gardens' as both artists' responses and symbolic representations of the world surrounding nature and us. The exhibited works attempt methodological experiments, referencing and reproducing issues of reality and fiction, imitation and replication, and various ways to address the contemporary environment and ecosystem. Through the independent ecosystems created by participating artists Kohui, Kim Joon, Yang Seungwon, Cho Leesop, and Hyun Nahm, it examines the sensitive perspectives and senses of the artists toward the world.

title: Cheonggyecheon Media Art : Cheonggye Soul Ocean
short_description: Cheonggye Soul Ocean, operated by Seoul Tourism Organization, is a media art tourism content featuring media art exhibitions that utilize Cheonggyecheon's waterside resources. Operating year-round as a nighttime exhibition, it can be experienced in the area around the lower section of Gwanggyo Bridge and Gwanggyo Gallery on Cheonggyecheon. The media art is divided into various works, including the Cheonggyecheon water surface media art exhibition (underwater video), the Gwanggyo Gallery wall video, and interactive media art video on the walkway in front of the Gwanggyo Gallery.

title: Musical 《BILLY ELLIOT》
short_description: Set against the backdrop of a northern English coal-mining village in the 1980s, this is the moving story of "Billy," a boy who accidentally encounters ballet during a boxing class and discovers his talent, depicting his journey toward his dream against the walls of prejudice and reality. "The greatest British musical of our time," , harmonizes beautiful music, fantastic choreography, and a heartfelt narrative.

title: Cho Kyoungjae: : Absolute Reconstruction
short_description: Gallery Jiwooheon is pleased to announce Cho Kyoungjae’s solo exhibition titled “Absolute Reconstruction” from June 21 to July 29. Cho, an artist who presents new perspectives for ways to view images, has been creating unique works of art by forming objects like large pavilions and photographing them. This exhibition aims to look back on the artist’s works of art, while putting on show new works that embody new techniques. This exhibition also aims to shed new light on the behavior of “looking into object/world/universe” through the image frames that Cho has reconstructed.

title: 2024 DOH KYUNG SOO ASIA FAN CONCERT TOUR BLOOM THE FINAL
short_description: For more details, please refer to the Interpark Ticket website

title: 99 Art Company   “The Corridor of Return; Seeking Totality"
short_description:
▪ Date: November 29 (Fri) - 30 (Sat), 2024  
   Fri 19:30 / Sat 17:00 
▪ Venue: Seoul Namsan Traditional Theater Crown Haitai Hall

This work adopts a research performance format to offer a more intuitive understanding of dance as an art form.  

This journey explores the relationship between tradition and the present and between dance and the dancer, inviting the audience to join the path toward a return to totality.

title: Veil Undrawn
short_description:
"Veil Undrawn" explores the contradictions of contemporary psychology and the delicate boundaries between surface and depth, as seen through the eyes of three Korean female artists born in the 1990s who navigate our digital age—an era where we consume social media images indiscriminately while simultaneously witnessing their infinite potential for expansion.

"Veil Undrawn" illuminates the thoughts and emotions of our time: the psychological contradictions of modern life—material abundance paired with spiritual emptiness, the belonging we find through social media alongside the isolation it creates—and examines how the AI-digital generation consumes imagery in entirely new ways, all filtered through the distinctive perspectives of these 1990s-born artists.

title: Rest and Rise: What Remains and What Rises
short_description: What remains does not disappear but stays quietly, breathing anew. The time that permeates through clay, metal, and small fragments comes to us as a form of rest. This exhibition, <Rest and Rise: What Remains and What Rises>, captures the perspectives of two artists who have each sought to grasp the traces left by nature in their own ways. The materials that have disappeared and remained are collected and embraced in their own manner, reborn into new forms. Here, where different materials and fingertips meet, we encounter the story of nature in which stillness and creation, disappearance and revival coexist.

title: Patriots and Veterans Month Commemorative Performance <To the Heroes>
short_description:
Patriots and Veterans Month Commemorative Performance <To the Heroes>

Honoring Our Heroes: Patriots and Veterans Month Performance


Program / Korean Traditional Dance

1. Guksuho-ryu Ipchum (Introductory Dance)

2. Guksuho-ryu Janghanga

3. Creative Dance <To the Heroes>

4. Imaebang-ryu Seungmu (Monk’s Dance)

(*Image source: Korea Traditional Performing Arts Foundation)


The performance opens with Ipchum and Guksuho-ryu Janghanga, followed by the original piece <To the Heroes>, dedicated to all patriotic heroes who devoted themselves to our country.

The performance closes with Seungmu in the Imaebang tradition, designated as Korea’s Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 27, regarded as one of the most artistically profound forms of Korean traditional dance.

This program offers a tribute to the spirit of patriotic sacrifice through a curated repertoire of Korean traditional dance.


Admission: Free for all seats


On-site Participation Events

Date & Time: June 28, 2025 (Saturday)

10:00–11:00 / 12:00–13:00

Venue: Cheonwugak Plaza, Namsangol Hanok Village (In case of rain, in the Hanok Village Courtyard)

Participants: Open to all visitors


Event 1: <To My Hero>

Write a message to our heroes on the Taegukgi

In commemoration of Patriots and Veterans Month, visitors can recreate the spirit of the Taegukgi signed by student soldiers from Gyeongju.

Leave your message to the heroes on the flag, and receive a hibiscus flower sticker to help decorate a symbolic Korean Peninsula in full bloom.


Event 2: <To My Mugunghwa>

Decorate your own flower-shaped fan in honor of the fallen heroes who now rest in fields of mugunghwa (hibiscus), Korea’s national flower.

Receive a hibiscus sticker and help fill the Korean Peninsula with flowers of remembrance and gratitude.

title: K-Drama Spotlight
short_description: The K-Drama Spotlight exhibition offers fans a chance to experience becoming a K-Drama star. From 'Zone 1: A Space for the Transition to a New Self, to Zone 2: Becoming an Actor, Zone 3: Delving into Destinations Inside Books, Zone 4: An Actor's Dressing Room, Zone 5: The Home of Fantasy, Zone 6: My Drama Lounge, Zone 7: Variations of the Four Seasons, Zone 8: Into Our Daily Lives, Zone 9: Enjoying the Korean Vibes with International Fans, Zone 10: Featuring in the Hall of Fame, Zone 11: Historic Handprint, and Zone 12: Spotlight on Me' - visitors can experience the rare opportunity of becoming the leading role of a K-Drama.

title: Jamwon Hangang Park Swimming Pool
short_description: Jamsil Hangang Swimming Pool, one of the Hangang Park swimming pools that opens every June, has three pools with depths of 0.4m, 0.8m, and 1.1m. Sunbeds are placed alongside the pools, and parasols are available in rows to provide shade. Sunbeds are available for rent, while parasols can be used free of charge. Lifeguards are stationed at each pool to ensure safe and enjoyable water activities. Tickets can be reserved online or purchased on-site. Outside food is not allowed, but fruits, drinks, and packed meals brought in reusable containers to avoid leaving waste are permitted.

title: 2025 Title Match 《Jang Young Hye Heavy Industries vs. Hong Jin Hwon: There Is No Middle Ground》
short_description: The Title Match, a representative annual exhibition of the Seoul Museum of Art Buk-Seoul branch, marks its 12th edition in 2025 by inviting artists Jang Young Hye Heavy Industries and Hong Jin Hwon. The exhibition begins from the awareness that, although society constantly advocates for the ideal of being “one community,” in reality, complex interests clash, and communities remain fractured. Instead of focusing on reconciled unity, the exhibition highlights the conflicts and fractures within communities and the resulting political discord. Through the works of Jang Young Hye Heavy Industries and Hong Jin Hwon, the exhibition examines the conditions under which political actions emerge and explores how art can intervene in social phenomena and create new political possibilities.

title: 2025 Nodeulseom , Art Space_Edge
short_description:
A space where art resides on Nodeulseom, Art Space_Edge

The once unnoticed “edge” has been reborn into a space full of character. In 2024, Art Space_Edge opened within the Nodeul Bookstore. Here, spontaneous encounters between citizens and artists take place naturally in everyday life.


In 2025, Art Space_Edge presents an even more diverse collection of new artists and works. Explore the currents of contemporary visual arts through the works of current and former resident artists from the Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture's creative spaces.


1st Floor: Shindang Creative Arcade Nodeulseom Island Permanent Exhibition – Atelier “Crafts Accidentally Encountered”


2nd Floor: Permanent exhibition of works by resident artists from Seoul Disability Arts & Culture Center and Geumcheon Art Factory

title: 2025 Aechae Forest
short_description: A special space where small nature and great art harmonize, <Aechae Forest>, hosted by Atelier Aechae, is an artistic venue where different forms of art converge in one space, breaking down boundaries between them and providing visitors with new visual and emotional experiences. Bonsai, containing nature's delicacies, and craft works showcasing the different charms of each material, along with moving paintings, each unfold their unique stories within Aechae's space. Just as various natural elements come together to form an ecosystem, we hope you will join us for the extraordinary moment of the 1st <2025 Aechae Forest>, where different artistic genres cooperate and communicate with each other to form a rich and diverse 'forest'.

title: BLUE SQUARE
short_description: BLUE SQUARE is Korea’s largest performing arts complex offering artists a dream stage and audiences unforgettable experiences. It houses the 1,766-seat Shinhan Card Hall, dedicated to musicals, and the SOL Travel Hall, a multipurpose venue with 1,379 seats (plus a standing area that can accommodate 2,800 people). Tickets can be easily booked via the Interpark website. In addition to performances, BLUE SQUARE also features NEMO, a trendy exhibition space; Book Park Lounge, a premium cultural space featuring a café with reading areas; Café Philos, offering a striking unobstructed view of Namsan Mountain; Stage B, a fine-dining restaurant ideal for savoring a glass of wine after a show; and Solos Kitchen, specializing in Asian cuisine.

title: Reign of Peace: Reminiscent of 18th-century Seoul Urbanscape
short_description: Taepyeongseongdae (太平聖代) refers to an era governed by a wise king, in which the people live in peace and harmony. To modern individuals constantly exposed to news of war and division, it may seem like a distant utopia. However, looking back at history, there have been several eras remembered as periods of peace and prosperity. Although perspectives may differ, the eras of King Yeongjo and King Jeongjo during the Joseon Dynasty are often regarded as periods of Taepyeongseongdae. This exhibition highlights 18th-century Seoul, a period remembered for its historical resurgence. It focuses on the era of two rulers who, guided by the ideology of Tangpyeong (a policy of political stability and harmony), sought to bring about change and improve the lives of the people. The urban landscape of 18th-century Seoul, remembered as an era of peace and prosperity, welcomes you.

title: KIDZANIA SEOUL
short_description:
KID (Kinder) + Z (Zany) + ANIA = KidZania, a Wonderful World for Children

KidZania is a special place where children can explore their dreams and experience the world of grown-ups through fun and realistic role-play.

In this kid-sized city, they can earn and spend “KidZos,” KidZania’s very own currency, learning the value of work and money in a natural and enjoyable way.

From being a firefighter or pilot to a fashion model or police officer, every experience at KidZania helps children discover their interests, build confidence, and imagine a brighter future.

title: Huh Sang-wook《 Buncheong Stroll》
short_description:
This exhibition highlights the serene beauty of Buncheong ceramics, characterized by a harmonious blend of tradition and nature. As an exhibition that magnifies the soothing aesthetic of Buncheong ceramics, characterized by the harmony of tradition and nature, it sheds light on the world of artist Huh Sang-wook, who has dedicated over 30 years to Buncheong ceramics.

The exhibition Buncheong Stroll presents a collection of large-scale new works. As you enter the exhibition hall, the first thing that catches your eye is a nonchalantly placed piece that resembles stones on sand in the center of the floor. This piece features tones resembling ink-washed grasses etched into it, offering viewers a place to sit and a sense of relaxation.

title: 2023 HOME TABLE DECO FAIR
short_description:
The Home & Table Deco Fair has a history of accompanying home styling and leading the lifestyle culture. As an exhibition encompassing the entire furniture and product design spectrum, from classic to innovative designs, it provides business opportunities and creative inspiration in home styling and lifestyle.

Based on the extensive home curation expertise and nationwide network established by the two organizers, the fair meets the business needs of the interior and home living industries while broadening the perception of lifestyle and enhancing accessibility to premium home styling. Experience a practical marketing platform that caters to the changing trends in lifestyle and premium home styling.

title: Seoul's Youth and Popular Music
short_description: In the 1930s, a small group of intellectuals led the trends in popular music. However, today, in the 2020s, it is the everyday young people from neighborhoods who shape these trends. Over the years, the hangout spots for young people have evolved with the times, from Jongno and Myeong-dong to Sinchon, Apgujeong, and Hongdae. This evolving diversity has provided the foundation for K-POP's global reach. Through the exhibition "Seoul's Youth and Popular Music," you’re invited to experience the romance, sensibility, spirit, and passion of the youth from each era.

title: [Space Tone Gallery] Ko So-mi Solo Exhibition: Multiplicity
short_description: Space Tone hosts the solo exhibition 《Multiplicity》 by fiber installation artist Ko So-mi.

title: Barbershops in Seoul
short_description: "Barbershops of Seoul" is a reimagined work based on the third research outcome of the Seoul Future Heritage project, titled "The Barbershops of Seoul." This work explores "The Evolution of Seoul's Barbershops and the Lives of Its Residents." It delves into the transformation of barbershops, spaces intimately connected to the community, through three phases: "The Emergence of Barbershops," "The Golden Age of Barbershops," and "The Rebirth of Barbershops." We hope that by exploring the stories of Seoul's barbershops, which have consistently engaged with residents, you will take a moment to appreciate and reflect on these seemingly ordinary yet significant everyday spaces.

title: 2023 Autumn Seoul Light DDP
short_description:
Global pandemics and climate change have brought about significant changes in our daily lives. We have grown accustomed to encountering artificial nature within residential and commercial spaces, and through devices equipped with video systems like TVs and smartphones, we experience virtual nature on screens. As a result, our desire for a real nature has been fulfilled. Virtual Reality (VR) has also enabled us to immerse ourselves in vivid nature experiences within virtual spaces previously only accessible in reality.

In 2023, Seoul Light DDP began with the question, "Can real nature, which has existed since the beginning, coexist with the technological nature created by humans?"

Our current focus is exploring the "sensation of coexistence," where humans and nature coexist in harmony instead of attempting to control or dominate nature. By harnessing the power of 'light (projection),' which is one of the earliest phenomena in the world, achieved through scientific technology, we have curated an encounter with nature using advanced technology. We aim to transcend the sense of coexistence and evoke the profound feeling of biophilia – a deep affection and love for nature.

title: Munassi 《The Season We Fade Away》
short_description:
Space K Seoul is pleased to present The Season We Fade Away, a solo exhibition by Moonassi (b. 1980). Rooted in the traditions of Korean painting, the artist has long explored the mind, human relationships, and the subtle inner currents that flow between them. In this exhibition, his paintings serve as both a journey following the flow of emotions and a site for quiet contemplation of the self.

For Moonassi, each stroke that remains on paper resembles a ripple spreading across the surface of the mind—like a tremor that gently disturbs still water. Just as the faintest vibration expands into waves, the movements of the inner self—elusive and resistant to words—slowly take shape on the picture plane.

The Season We Fade Away reflects on how emotions are born from and fade within relationships. Emotions are awakened and stirred by encounters with others. Like waves on the water, relationships and emotions seep into one another, exchanging light. The artist captures these moments of delicate balance: from figures facing one another, to sharing a gaze toward a single point, to pausing for a breath before a face reflected on the water’s surface.

Moonassi does not suppress or define emotions. Instead, he chooses to let them be. This attitude of acceptance becomes a way of seeing the self reflected through others, leading to a quiet observation of one's own being amidst these fluctuations.

As suggested by the characters in his name—"Mu (無: non-)" and "Na (我: self)"— his work traverses the boundaries between fullness and emptiness, the self and the other, peering into the space that lies between. In his compositions where the traditional ink meets modern sensibility, emotions do not simply disappear. Rather, they linger, changing form, only to resurface when the time is right.

The Season We Fade Away is an exhibition that reflects our own faces on the surface of the water where emotion and relationship intersect. Viewers are invited to accept emotions as they are and, in passing through the tremors of relationships, encounter a quiet moment of return to the self.

title: Seoul Mini Mountains
short_description:
The “Seoul Mini Mountains” exhibition is rooted in a research project by Borio-Lab, led by Géraldine Borio, an assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong’s Department of Architecture. With over 17 years of architectural and urban research experience across Asian cities such as Bangkok, Hong Kong, and Seoul, Professor Borio’s work forms the foundation of this exhibition.
Jointly presented with the Seoul Museum of History, the exhibition revisits Seoul’s urban landscape by investigating the role and impact of voids (empty spaces) in the city center on its urban narrative and identity. The exhibition highlights Seoul's distinctive topography through photographs and drawings created by Professor Borio and her students.
This research delves into how historical developments have shaped the voids in Seoul and how their ‘boundaries’ have changed. It analyzes these spaces through the observation of the ‘activities’ occurring within these undeveloped areas. You are invited to take part in this meaningful opportunity to experience a foreign scholar’s fresh perspective on Seoul and to reflect on the value of seeing spaces and objects in a new light. We look forward to your visit.

title: Seoul Metropolitan Dance Theatre <Mimesis>
short_description: The cradle of Korean creative dance, the essence of traditional dance reinterpreted with modern sensibilities presented by the Seoul Metropolitan Dance Theatre. Along with globally noted K-style traditional costumes, it presents a metaphorical yet intense stage incorporating the eight colors of water, wind, earth, lightning, void, sky, fire, and light. We hope you join the moment when traditions passed down across eras come alive again within our bodies.

title: Happy voyage
short_description: In October 2024, his exhibition at Samseyoung, showcasing cheerful and optimistic pigs, is expected to provide an opportunity to experience the pursuit of dreams, hope, and humor through the joyful imagery of pigs.

title: Space K Seoul
short_description: Operated by the Kolon Group, Space K Seoul is a non-profit art museum that presents a wide range of exhibitions highlighting contemporary art. It introduces the creative works of both Korean and international artists, serving as an open platform for cultural exchange accessible to citizens. With modern architecture and sophisticated exhibition design, it has become a noted destination for art enthusiasts.
