title: Mixed Orchestra : Next Level
short_description: Centering on Korean traditional orchestra, the performance creates a new resonance that harmonizes diverse sound bodies including Western instruments, merging tradition and modernity, past and future. Expanding the possibilities of Korean orchestral music, the Seoul Metropolitan Traditional Orchestra presents an evolved identity of K-Orchestra through this <Next Level> stage, the representative series Mixed Orchestra. The program features Manchun-gok, the starting point of creative Korean orchestral music; Susang-gok, highlighting the clear tone of the Danso; a collaborative performance by geomungo performer and producer Park Daul; and premieres of new works by composers Kim Hyunseop and Lee Gowoon. The performance brings together tradition and creation, past and future, on one stage, showcasing a new dimension of Korean orchestral sound. Celebrating its 60th anniversary this year, the Seoul Metropolitan Traditional Orchestra shares the resonance of our music that combines the depth of tradition with contemporary sensibility. Experience the new leap of the Korean-style orchestra at Mixed Orchestra <Next Level>.

title: Seongbuk Young Art Space
short_description: Seongbuk Young Art Space is the first branch of the Seongbuk Museum of Art, established as a 'living creative space' to support and nurture creators in the visual arts field and to continue experiments across the diverse terrain of creation. Opened in April 2013, the Seongbuk Young Art Space has made continuous attempts to discover creative and experimental artists, and furthermore, to build an open art culture through networking and collaboration based on the local community. As a specialized space for visual arts, the Seongbuk Young Art Space is establishing itself as a venue of experience where creators from multiple genres, including youth and emerging artists, prepare for the future and accumulate experiences together.

title: Drawing Room
short_description: Drawing Room (dR) is a commercial exhibition space aimed at delivering a familiar experience of contemporary art that pursues the spirit of the times and the artist's spirit. dR strives to be faithful to its role as a medium that draws and leads the visual language of contemporary artists. It pursues diversity in the art market as a space that creates synergy by connecting the ideas presented by artists to the public, and as a supporter that encourages the discovery of new tastes.

title: [2025 Cheonggyecheon Public Art Project : Cheonggye Coexistence] Docent Program
short_description:
The citizen docent program of the 2025 Cheonggyecheon Public Art Project Cheonggye Coexistence, celebrating the 20th anniversary of the Cheonggyecheon Restoration, offers an opportunity to revisit the history and spatial meaning of Cheonggyecheon and to deeply understand how various artworks connect the city, people, and nature. Stroll along the works as if taking a walk through the city center, and experience a time of sharing thoughts embedded in each piece beyond simple appreciation.


[Schedule]

English docent program for foreigners: November 20 (Thursday), 15:00–15:50


[How to Apply]

Apply by email at cheonggye.art@gmail.com

 from October 27 (Monday) to November 7 (Friday).

Please include your name and contact information. Participants will be contacted separately regarding selection results.


[Capacity] 15 people

Children may participate when accompanied by a guardian.


[Program Structure]


Orientation (5 minutes) – Introduction to the history and spatial significance of Cheonggyecheon, and explanation of the purpose and concept of the Cheonggye Coexistence project


Artwork Tour (40 minutes) – A docent-led walking tour of six public art pieces, sharing insights on the planning, design, and production of each work, as well as the artists’ intentions, followed by a Q&A and discussion with participants


Conclusion (5 minutes) – Sharing impressions of the artworks, guidance on satisfaction survey participation


Walk along the flow of Cheonggyecheon and immerse yourself in the world of public art. A new artistic experience awaits, beginning with your own perspective.

title: Again, Earth: Responding with Other Senses
short_description: This exhibition questions what art should do and how it should exist in the age of climate crisis and the Anthropocene, moving away from anthropocentrism to practice art with “other” senses, thoughts, and attitudes. It welcomes visitors with a new exhibition that shares serious yet engaging imagination about the art needed in the present and future.

title: The Hyundai Seoul's Christmas 'H-Village'
short_description: The Hyundai Seoul, a landmark of Yeouido, presents a special experiential exhibition every Christmas season, immersing visitors in the festive atmosphere. In 2024, the theme of “The Moving Grand Theater” is a beautiful journey where Baby Bear Harry and a girl set out to find the world's greatest Christmas show. LE GRANDE THEATRE will be held at The Hyundai Seoul's Sounds Forest, offering an enchanting experience akin to a grand Christmas circus show. This meticulously designed space provides unforgettable memories and opportunities to capture stunning photos that will last a lifetime. This winter, escape the cold and visit The Hyundai Seoul's H Village for a delightful indoor experience.

title: Gallery Chosun
short_description: Established in 2004, Gallery Chosun traces its roots to Chosun Gallery, which played a pioneering role by participating in international fairs such as ART COLOGNE in Germany, NICAF in Tokyo, and CIGE in Beijing, and organizing over 400 domestic exhibitions. Since its founding, Gallery Chosun has participated in Art Cologne and Art Basel Miami, focusing on contemporary art exhibitions to promote Korean contemporary art internationally.

title: Gaze At Exhibition
short_description:
Superior Gallery presents Gave At Exhibition by artists Baek Ji-hye and Jeong Yeon-yeon to welcome the refreshing autumn.


The artist Baek Ji-hye applies traditional portrait techniques to contemporary portrayals, emphasizing feminine sensibilities with a focus on 'girls' and infusing emotional elements into her work. She researched and reinterpreted portraits from the Joseon Dynasty era, giving birth to “realistic girl painting” and creating traditional color paintings from a feminine perspective. Artist Jeong Yeon-yeon addresses women's diversity and social reality in a bright and honest tone, expressing her hope for peace by breaking down discrimination with classic blue, which symbolizes male authority. Experience the unique perspectives of two artists searching for hope beyond boundaries at Superior Gallery. The Gaze At exhibition by artists Baek Ji-hye and Jeong Yeon-yeon will run until November 9th.

title: KooBohnchang’s Voyages
short_description:
In anticipation of the opening of the Seoul Metropolitan Museum of Photography in 2024, a major retrospective exhibition titled "KooBohnchang’s Voyages" will be held, featuring the works of Koo Bohnchang (born 1953), an icon of modern Korean photography as well as contemporary art.

This exhibition will display over 500 works and around 600 materials, ranging from Koo Bohnchang's first work, "Self-Portrait" (1968), to his most recent works. It showcases the deep and expansive world of the artist's creations. Following the artist's artistic journey, we invite you to embark on a new voyage, starting from the 'Room of Curiosity,’ passing through 'Adventurous Journey, One World, Temple of the Soul,’ and concluding with 'The Open Room.’

title: Namsan Sky Forest Trail
short_description: Namsan Sky Forest Trail is a one point four five kilometer accessible deck trail that connects Namsan Fitness Park (Huam-dong, Yongsan-gu) to Namsan Library, allowing visitors to enjoy the refreshing natural environment of Namsan under the clear sky. It offers complete immersion in nature through observatories overlooking the Seoul cityscape as well as gardens. By utilizing Namsan’s natural environment effectively, eight scenic viewing points and eight attraction points have been created, forming a space for ecology, healing, and culture.

title: My Art Museum One Grove Branch
short_description:
My Art Museum One Grove Branch provides a pleasant and sophisticated exhibition environment so that modern people can comfortably encounter art even in their busy daily lives. Along with a spatial composition allowing quiet contemplation and appreciation of works, it is equipped with sensational lighting, spacious pathways, and comfortable resting spaces, allowing anyone of all ages to naturally feel the charm of art.

It is drawing attention as a famous Gangseo exhibition and Magok exhibition attraction that everyone can enjoy together, from family visitors to couples, friends, and office workers. It is highly suitable as a date spot for special days or a weekend outing course, serving as an open art museum where anyone can comfortably experience the world of art.

For the convenience of visitors, it is located near Magok Station, offering excellent accessibility. Various cultural facilities and commercial spaces co-locate within the One Grove Mall, allowing you to enjoy dining or shopping together after viewing exhibitions.

title: The Exhibition 《I Will Come to Like》
short_description:
Superior Gallery presents a three-artist exhibition The Exhibition 《I Will Come to Like》 by Oksuk, Phonormal, and Frida Ok in October 2025. The three participating artists, who work on both illustration shared in digital environments and original paintings, reconstruct moments of daily life into memories and show a wide range of diversity in works through their respective colors and distinctive expressions.

Oksuk calmly yet vividly depicts scenes of rest and travel discovered in urban daily life, expanding into “emotional landscapes” that record brief moments of rest within a busy life. Phonormal humorously expresses daily life and inner emotions, and through playful color contrasts and composition, completes scenes in which remembered thoughts and new imagery are naturally combined. Frida Ok portrays stories of elderly couples and natural landscapes with warm sentiments, visually conveying the warmth and accumulated time of life through repetitive brushstrokes and the dense flower paths in which the elderly couples appear.

This exhibition aims to deliver visual pleasure and empathy through the works of the three artists and to provide a place where viewers can encounter “scenes they will come to like” within their own memories and emotions. The Exhibition 《I Will Come to Like》 runs until November 6, 2025.

title: "Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?” Exhibition
short_description: Artist Jung In-sung's solo exhibition, “Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?” will be free at the Superior Gallery in Samseong-dong until June 3. Enjoy the summer with artwork filled with a variety of colors.

title: YMCA Seoul : A Civic History Shaped by Youth
short_description: Every year, the Gongpyeong Historic Sites Museum (26, Ujeongguk-ro, Jongno-gu) hosts a special exhibition that highlights the history and significance of the Jongno area. This year marks the museum’s seventh special exhibition, spotlighting the story of YMCA Seoul, which began in the heart of Jongno. The exhibition traces the YMCA’s 120-year journey, offering an in-depth look at its role in Korea’s modern history, particularly in education, civil society, and sports.  Part 1 covers the founding of the YMCA, the construction of its headquarters, and its involvement in nationalist movements during the Japanese occupation period. Part 2 focuses on post-liberation civic movements, while Part 3 presents the introduction and development of everyday sports in modern Korea through photographs, blueprints, publications, and various other materials.

title: GanaArt Collection Permanent Exhibition《80 Urban Reality》
short_description: The curated exhibition 《80 Urban Reality》 in the GanaArt Collection at the Seoul Museum of Art explores the realities surrounding cities in the 1980s from various perspectives through the collection and artworks. The 1980s in Korean society marked a significant era of rapid industrialization and economic growth, ushering in a new phase of urbanization. During that time, artists had their own attitudes towards cities and created various artworks reflecting their perspectives. This exhibition is organized into three sub-themes: ‘The Other Side of Urbanization,' 'Urbanites,' and 'Beyond Urban Surroundings: Origin of Life,' based on a common thematic consciousness that runs through the exhibited works. Through the artists' perspectives from that era, we hope this exhibition provides an opportunity to empathize with the realities of that time and contemplate their significance in our present lives.

title: The replica of an old mayor’s office
short_description: The Reconstructed Former Mayor’s Office is a workspace used by former mayors of Seoul for over 60 years, from the post-liberation period until May 2008. Located at the center of the 3rd floor of the Seoul Metropolitan Library, this space comprises a planning room, reception room, and office, featuring faithfully restored furniture and office equipment from that time.

title: Seoul Olympic Stadium
short_description: The Seoul Olympic Stadium, the centerpiece of the Seoul Sports Complex in Jamsil, has a seating capacity of approximately 66,500 and can accommodate up to 100,000 spectators. It features eight running tracks and a grass field measuring 110 m by 75 m. The stadium has a two-tiered spectator area, partially covered by a canopy roof. It holds significant symbolic value as the main venue for the 1986 Asian Games and the 1988 Seoul Olympics.

title: SeMA Public Space Project 《The Dance That Crosses Forever》
short_description:
The Seoul Museum of Art presents its 2025 Public Space Project featuring world-renowned artist Ernesto Neto, who has broadened the horizon of contemporary sculpture. His new work Ba Ka Ba, The Dance That Crosses Forever is a large-scale installation traversing the lobby and open areas of the Seosomun Main Building. The work is crafted by crocheting industrial cotton fabrics in brown, reminiscent of tree trunks and night, and in pink, symbolizing flowers and day, filled with locally sourced guava leaves and tea tree leaves.


The spirit of Brazil’s Neo-Concrete movement—emphasizing sensory engagement, participation, and subjective experience—finds new life in Neto’s work within today’s urban spaces, extending the possibilities of art. The SeMA Public Space Project 《The Dance That Crosses Forever》 aims to present a venue where art awakens the senses in everyday life, as city and museum converge.

title: DOEZNY《MOVEMENT》
short_description: Focusing on the movement of resistance, Doezny delves into more fundamental narratives in his solo exhibition “MOVEMENT.” Through a deeper exploration of the theme of liberation, which he has previously addressed, the exhibition traces the sources of oppression and the pathways of action toward freedom. Images of citizens holding protest signs by day and street artists wielding spray cans by night intersect, highlighting the nature of the street as a medium for conveying messages. The works capture the process of resistance and liberation toward freedom through these street movements.

title: Seoul Art Center Doam Gallery
short_description: Doam Gallery is a gallery with a large exhibition area of 593 square meters (approximately 179 pyeong) and a variety of ceiling heights ranging from 3.3 meters to 6.4 meters. It aims to serve as a platform where artistic capacity is brought together through curated exhibitions, invitational exhibitions, and rentals.

title: CHUN Kyung-ja Centennial 《Turbulent Times: Women Life Art》
short_description: The Seoul Museum of Art will host the exhibition “Turbulent Times: Women Life Art” in 2024 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of Chun Kyung-ja’s birth (1924–2015). This exhibition will feature works and archives from 22 female artists who lived during the same period as Chun Kyung-ja. Unlike previous exhibitions or research, this exhibition highlights Chun Kyung-ja’s modern mindset and influence on her era. It also sheds light on other female artists of her time who, unlike Chun, struggled to break free from the traditional confines of Eastern painting during the Japanese occupation. These women collectively lived through a tumultuous era marked by significant historical events, including the Japanese colonial era (1909–1945), Korea’s liberation on August 15, 1945, the Korean War (1950–1953), the April 19 Revolution (1960), the May 16 military coup (1961), military dictatorship (1961–1979), the December 12 military rebellion (1979), the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement (1980), the new military regime (1980–1993), and the ongoing democratization movements following the establishment of the South Korean government. Society, personal life, and art are inseparable, and this exhibition aims to explore the interconnectedness of political, social, and artistic trends from the Japanese colonial period to the 1990s. By examining the broader context of the Eastern art scene during that time, it seeks to reveal the influence of these movements on the artists. The exhibition will cover various aspects, including educational institutions during the colonial period, the development of the Joseon Art Exhibition (Chosun Misun), post-liberation educational institutions, and the National Art Exhibition (Gukjeon), along with the political and social interventions that occurred in between. It will also provide a detailed and objective look at the trajectory of Eastern painting, group activities, achievements, and individual biographies of the artists. This approach helps to better understand their artistic worlds and trace their evolution from being labeled as "female Eastern painters" to becoming the "artists" they are recognized today. This exhibition delves deeply into various materials, including Chun Ja's candid autobiography, various articles, writings, and artworks. By thoroughly researching these sources, the exhibition aims to uncover the many individuals who played a role in her life and explore her relationships with them. A carefully organized biography will correct past misunderstandings and inaccuracies about the artist, paving the way for more in-depth research in the future. Through this exhibition, we honor Chun Kyung-ja, a pioneer of modern Korean art, while shedding light on the works of other artists who lived through the "era of turbulence" and contributed to the development of modern Korean art with their diverse creations. The exhibition reexamines the artistic worlds of Chung Chan-young, Lee Hyun-ok, Chung Yong-hee, Bae Jeong-rye, Park Rae-hyun, Chun Kyung-ja, Park In-kyung, Geum Dong-won, Moon Eun-hee, Lee In-sil, Lee Kyung-ja, Jang Sang-eui, Ryu Min-ja, Lee Sook-ja, Oh Nang-ja, Yoon Ae-geun, Lee Hwa-ja, Shim Kyung-ja, Won Moon-ja, Song Su-ryeon, Joo Min-sook, Kim Choon-ok, and Cha Myung-hee, without boundaries or limitations, within the context of contemporary art movements.

title: Harmony of Notes and Moves
short_description: Music is not merely an accompaniment to the dance in this concert. All of the moves and notes interact with each other on equal footing to build this dynamic performance. Highlighting the aesthetic value of traditional dance that exudes vitality.

title: PEAK FESTIVAL 2025
short_description: Please check the Interpark Ticket website for more details

title: Pansori Azit Nohlae Box 'Pansori Short Stories Vol.2'
short_description:
As the second story in the “Pansori Azit Nohlae Box <Pansori Short Stories Vol.2,” this solo pansori performance embodies the subtlety of human 

affairs and the charm of short stories depicted by Guy de Maupassant. Singers Lee Ye-rin, Lee Seung-min, and Hwang Ji-young bring  "A Piece of String," "The Colonel's Ideas," and "Bed No. 29" to life, each infusing their unique style into Maupassant's delicate realism,

 showcasing their talents not only as singers but also as storytellers.

These are short stories akin to fleeting dreams from the night before—brief yet lingering in the mind all day. Director Park In-hye focuses on the 

nature of short stories that compel us to move on even when left feeling unsettled, wistful, or caught off guard, portraying this as a reflection of 

human life. As pansori ends with a whirlwind, so too do Maupassant’s stories portray the diverse realities of human experience, seen through the 

eyes of the  singers. This invites the audience to ponder "How do humans live?" and ultimately, "How should humans live?"

title: Seoul Vibe
short_description: When it comes to the city of Seoul, there are several different images that come to mind. And among those images, Seoul captures a variety of contrasts from light and dark; cold and warm, busy and peaceful, beautiful and ordinary, and more. Seoul Vibe is a project that seeks out to find these dualities through a myriad of ways.

title: IBK Moduda Family Concert 2026
short_description:
The ‘IBK Moduda Family Concert’ where families with diverse cultures and stories gather together to share warm music and unforgettable memories is waiting for you!


From singer Tei, show choir group Showmust, a cappella group Ojik Moksori (Only Voice), to pansori singer Choi Jae-gu!

Meet a special stage that everyone of all ages and genders can enjoy together


[Performance Information]

title: Ttukseom Hangang Park X Game Zone
short_description: The X-Game Area at Ttukseom Hangang Park is a dedicated space for skateboards, inline skates, and BMX bikes. It features a spacious area with flat surfaces, jumps, slanted rails, and various other obstacles for free use. There are also side tracks accessible to everyone, making it suitable for beginners. If you want to try a unique sport in Hangang Park, this is the perfect spot. Occasionally, professional competitions are held here, filling the park with sports excitement throughout the year. Remember to wear protective gear such as helmets and knee pads when using the park. The X-Game Area is exclusively for skateboards, aggressive inline skates, and BMX bikes.

title: Special Exhibition for the Eightieth Anniversary of Liberation: Our Yi Sun sin
short_description: The National Museum of Korea presents the special exhibition <Our Yi Sun sin>, commemorating the four hundred eightieth anniversary of the birth of Admiral Yi Sun sin and the eightieth anniversary of Liberation. Centered on records left by Yi Sun sin himself, this exhibition sheds light on his inner thoughts and emotions beyond his role as a war hero, as well as on how he became a symbol shaped by later generations. This is the first comprehensive Yi Sun sin exhibition by the National Museum of Korea and includes twenty items (thirty four pieces) from the Yi Sun sin family, including the handwritten Nanjung Ilgi and the Yi Sun sin Long Sword, along with six National Treasures (fifteen pieces), thirty nine Treasures (forty three pieces), six Registered Cultural Heritage items (nine pieces), totaling two hundred fifty eight items (six hundred sixty nine pieces).

title: Samgak G7: The Place of Beginning
short_description:
Are you familiar with ‘Samgakji’, a fiercely artistic space where countless unknown painters maintained their livelihoods and never let go of their brushes until the very end?


A visual arts exhibition by seven artists, which modernly reinterprets the historical context of the Samgakji gallery street formed after the Korean War, will be held at the Yongsan Cultural Foundation Pop-up Hall.


We invite you to the 'The Place of Beginning' exhibition, where the creative energy accumulated in Samgakji in the past and today's artistic perspectives intersect.

title: Artside Gallery
short_description: Opened in Insadong in 1999, Artside Gallery operates under the motto “art is the constant centralization of the surroundings.” It aims to bridge artists and the art market by providing various creative directions to domestic and international artists. Based on its beliefs and perspectives, Artside Gallery has been at the forefront of introducing the diverse works and artistic worlds of talented artists from Korea, China, Asia, Europe, and beyond to the domestic and international art scene. Since relocating to Tongui-dong in 2010, the gallery has continued to curate exhibitions that reflect its distinct identity. Through its participation in various domestic and international art fairs, Artside Gallery has opened the door to the global art market and solidified its position as an internationally recognized gallery.

title: Sunrise to Sunlight
short_description:
B the B is a permanent exhibition space that curates Seoul’s attractive beauty brands with B the B’s unique sensibility. Explore AI-powered beauty tech devices that are rarely accessible, diagnose your skin and scalp, and experience virtual makeup and photo booth sessions. You can also test recommended products based on your diagnosis and enjoy a one-stop service for online purchases.


This special exhibition is designed so you can experience your morning beauty routine step by step—from Step 1. Skincare to Step 9. Cleansing—from morning to night. As you stroll through the biophilia-themed exhibition hall, you’ll feel as if you’ve stepped into a forest with lush green leaves and birdsong. Participate in various regularly updated events and receive gifts.

title: A Thousand Wishes
short_description: In the season that bears the marks of enduring the long summer of 2025, Samseyoung Gallery presents an exhibition by artist Song Sunhee. Every human being experiences a period of helplessness. The artist too has lived through such a time, and what that time offered her was a profound insight into fundamental existence. At the root of her work lies the theme of “nature.” The artist whispers to us about what nature means to humankind. Through this essential reflection, she seeks to share the roots of her artistic practice, inviting us to reconsider the global theme of “nature.”

title: Broadening of visions
short_description:
To mark its 20th anniversary, Gongganhye Gallery presents the second part of its special exhibition, running from September 15 to October 4, 2025.


The exhibition revisits the gallery’s journey: from its beginnings as a photography-specialized gallery in 2005, to its relocation next to the Blue House in Samcheong-dong in 2010, and its expansion into painting, sculpture, video, and installation art, shaping the trajectory of contemporary art.


The exhibition will feature works by three artists who have steadily developed their unique artistic worlds in collaboration with Gongganhye Gallery: Jen Pak, Chen Ruo Bing, and Kwak Intan. Through their diverse generational, regional, and formal languages, the exhibition seeks to map out the expanded landscape of contemporary visual arts.

title: Empty Houses on the Coast
short_description:
The artist’s paintings ‘A series of empty houses’ are deep multidimensional structures containing improbable transpositions of time and space. She re-assembles the fragments of memory that she has gathered from the shoreline. We are drawn in to the structures and we find ourselves surrounded by floors made of ice, windows through which we can see a raging sea by moonlight and where, the sea itself is advancing in to the room and we are really standing on a beach. Viewrs could be active participants in a multi-faceted space where gravity has been suspended.
Film stories are fiction, but when those single frames are assembled and viewed together they create the powerful illusion of having witnessed an 'event', no matter how unlikely that event might be. 'Empty Houses on the Coast' leaves me with exactly that sensation of having witnessed the improbable come to life.

title: seon-upung-wol(扇友風月)
short_description: Please check the Interpark ticket website for more information.

title: Kwon Jin Kyu's Forever Home
short_description:
In commemorating Kwon Jin Kyu's 50th anniversary, Seoul Museum of Art's Nam Seoul Museum is launching the "Kwon Jin Kyu's Forever Home" exhibition in 2023. Having received the Kwon Jin Kyu collection in 2021, the Seoul Museum of Art has transformed five exhibition rooms on the 1st floor of Nam Seoul Museum into a permanent exhibition space dedicated to Kwon JinKyu's valuable works and materials.

This exhibition succinctly presents Kwon Jin Kyu's entire artistic realm, where he continuously observes and studies the subjects around him, capturing only their essence to manifest an enduring soul and eternity that never fades away.

Kwon Jin Kyu (1922–1973) navigated through the Japanese colonial era and post-liberation during the severed diplomatic ties between Korea and Japan. Despite the challenges, he engaged as a sculptor, shuttling between the two countries. He established a unique artistic realm. For him, true art was incessantly observing and studying the subjects around him, capturing only their essence. He pursued not realism or beauty but an enduring soul, an eternity that never fades away. Seoul Museum of Art's Nam Seoul Museum aims to be both a perpetual resting place for his works and a nurturing ground for new research.

Please explore his works in the exhibition inspired by the architectural structures, wooden furniture, shelves, and more from Tokyo Musashino Art University, where Kwon Jin Kyu dedicated himself to his work and the Seoul studio.

title: Arko Kkumbat Theater
short_description: The name 'Kkumbat' (Dream Field), decided by public vote, means a place where children's dreams grow. The steering committee improved the seating, dressing rooms, and performance halls through Kkumbat Funding, and it is a children-centered theater in Korea that promotes the development of children's and youth performances.

title: My Treasures, My Heritage
short_description:
The museum is a place where memories are preserved and shared. The Seoul Museum of History actively encourages citizen donations to collect materials that embody Seoul’s history and culture and introduces newly donated items through exhibitions.

This year, they have prepared a special exhibition focusing on items donated from 25 different places last year. Although each piece varies in the time it holds and its rarity, every item is a precious treasure to both the donors and the museum.

To better highlight the value of these materials, the museum restores items in poor condition, translates classical Chinese texts into modern Korean for better understanding, and creates a more visitor-friendly exhibition environment.

As you explore the exhibition, they hope you enjoy the time spent sharing these diverse treasures and memories.

title: Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall
short_description: Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall is a space honoring the independence activist Woodang Lee Hoe-young, his five brothers, and their comrades. This house is one of the early 20th-century Western-style buildings constructed by Westerners who entered Seoul, along the hills of Hongpa-dong, Sajik-dong, and Haengchon-dong in the Seodaemun area. Reborn as the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall, this house possesses rich historical backgrounds and values even from an architectural history perspective. To remember its significance together, the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall gave this old Western-style building the nickname 'The Old House on Sajik-dong Hill' while reshaping the site. Mr. Lee Hoe-young devoted himself to the anti-Japanese independence movement, contributing his entire family wealth to establish the Shinheung Military Academy. At the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall, encounter the history of the independence movement expressed with modern aesthetics, alongside the stories of the finest family of the Joseon Dynasty, the greatest revolutionaries of Joseon, the people who turned darkness into light, and the people who turned orchid leaves into blades.

title: You and I, and There
short_description: Superior Gallery presents the exhibition "You and I, and There," featuring artists Kim Chan-joo, Ahn Hee-jin, and Lee Gyeo-re, who work under the theme "Human, Relationships, Coexistence." These artists expand various social issues from personal reflections to broader social concepts, displaying them in the gallery. The landscapes on canvas, which begin with the question of what role art can play in contemporary society, reflect the artists' beliefs that painting can change the world. Experience the perspective of coexistence that starts from the individual and extends to everyone at Superior Gallery. The "You and I, and There" exhibition runs until September 2.

title: Korean Dance - peaceful, The Prince's Way
short_description:
The story of four men who dreamed of peace.

Taejong, who ascended to the throne covered in the blood of countless vassals, relatives, and brothers, gave his sons the title "Nyeong (寧)," meaning "peace." Why did he choose this word? The princes who received the name "Nyeong" had to desperately search for what peace meant to them, navigating days and nights filled with desire and duty, despair and discipline, joy and fear. This work questions the meaning of "peace" through the lives of Taejong and his three sons.

title: Groundseesaw Seochon
short_description: Groundseesaw is a platform that curates and presents exhibitions featuring cultural and artistic IPs from domestic and international sources. The exhibitions at Groundseesaw showcase its ability to adapt to shifting trends in the art world, responding flexibly to current cultural issues while reflecting its ongoing growth and evolution. A must-visit spot in Seochon, it draws visitors with its sleek, well-organized exhibition spaces and carefully planned routes. The building itself is an architectural gem, making it a popular destination for leisurely walks. From the top floor, visitors can also enjoy stunning views of Seochon, with Inwangsan Mountain serving as a beautiful backdrop.

title: piknic
short_description:
Opened in 2018, piknic is an urban cultural space. As architect Florian Beigel said, "Design is not about planning a picnic, but preparing a mat," piknic was planned as a single venue where various artistic activities such as exhibitions, performances, gardens, gastronomy, and reading are possible.


The old building, which was used as a pharmaceutical company's headquarters in the 1970s, has been reborn as a cultural space where an exhibition hall, cafe, shop, restaurant, garden, and vegetable garden coexist while retaining the mood of the past. Currently, at piknic, various cultural programs are regularly held, including diverse special exhibitions, creative performances such as a play theater, a novel theater, and a silent film theater, as well as a garden school, music appreciation sessions, and piknic kids.

title: 2026 Seongbuk Museum of Art Special Exhibition 《Lee, Jung yoon: Singing ornaments in the house》
short_description: The Seongbuk Museum of Art is holding the 2026 special exhibition ≪Lee, Jung yoon: Singing ornaments in the house≫ at the Kim Chung-up Architecture Culture House, a space embodying Kim Chung-up's architectural philosophy. Inspired by Kim Chung-up's thought and architecture, artist Lee Jung-yoon newly transforms the Kim Chung-up Architecture Culture House into a 'Singing House,' centering on her  work. We hope you experience the moment when various senses intersect and expand in the correspondence between the two artists, crossing boundaries between architecture and art, form and rhythm, settlement and movement.

title: Minyoung Choi: Dreams for Hire
short_description: Space K Seoul is pleased to present 《Dreams for Hire》, a solo exhibition by London-based artist Minyoung Choi (b.1989). The artist gathers fragments of memories from her childhood and experiences of migration and presents them as dreamlike scenes between dreams and reality. Dolphins appear in the Han River at sunset, penguins appear next to a person asleep in the living room, or a rainbow in the middle of the night shines like a cluster of moons, creating a new landscape where elements that wouldn't coexist on the same screen are mixed together. The artist's magical realist landscapes invite us to imagine unique narratives and meanings. Minyoung Choi's strange and familiar world feels like dreams where the impossible is realized, and they allow us to look at the various realities we encounter in a new light.

title: THEO
short_description: Gallery THEO, known for showcasing Korean art's broad spectrum and diversity, was established in 2020 by two directors with experience in the UK and the international art market. They aimed to introduce global expertise and networks to the Korean art scene. Located in front of the UNESCO World Heritage site Seonjeongneung, THEO is dedicated to supporting young and talented Korean artists, regardless of artistic genre, and uncovering the potential in their works. The gallery actively provides a platform for Korean artists to grow and thrive. In addition, THEO introduces international artists to the Korean and Asian art communities, fostering cross-cultural exchanges and expanding artistic discourse beyond national borders. THEO continues to host exhibitions featuring diverse artists worldwide. It aims to create a space where artists can coexist and flourish, driven by a commitment to challenging projects and artistic excellence.

title: Kim Byung-gu Solo Exhibition: 7 am Green pew
short_description:
One early morning in early April, while strolling in the corner of Paju as usual, I unexpectedly came across a certain scenery.

The dense fog gradually cleared, revealing a place filled with dew-covered grass awakening from sleep, permeating the air with freshness. The sounds of footsteps on the ground and leaves rustling harmonized. Finding a space where I could be free brought me great joy.

Since then, I found myself returning to that spot even when the grass grew wildly uncontrollable during the torrential rains of the monsoon season or when the snow piled up thickly.

Around the middle of April, a week with the most rapid changes occurs there. The same plants grow in different locations each year, and accordingly, the impressions of the place change each time. Although they quickly disappeared, it was an attempt to capture the most beautiful week.

Pause for a moment and immerse yourself in the presence of artworks that capture the essence of both existence and non-existence within 7 am Green pew.

title: SeMA Omnibus - I Want to Love Us
short_description:
The SeMA Omnibus is a largescale collection-based exhibition presented at the main branch and three branches of the Seoul Museum of Art under the theme of the museum’s 2024 institutional agenda, “connection.” The exhibition SeMA Omnibus: I Want to Love Us, at the Buk-Seoul Museum of Art, reflects the diverse stories of minorities that cannot be reduced to a collective narrative and envisions a new community connected by individuals who are all unique in their own right.  This exhibition is focused on social minorities oppressed and/or discriminated against due to various reasons, such as race, nationality, gender, age, physical condition, sexual orientation, sociocultural environment, and/or economic status. In any highly competitive neoliberal society, the problems faced by minorities are often treated as secondary or not recognized as problems at all, and attempts at collectivization frequently fall apart. On the other hand, even when minorities are collectivized through social welfare policies or collectivized to assert their rightful place in society, individual lives are overlooked, and only the aspects of the collective identity that society expects are reduced to “a single story.” Minorities need collectivization to eliminate oppression and discrimination, but they face the paradox in which individual diversity is erased during the process of unification in and among minority groups. This exhibition aims to demonstrate ways to include the diversity of individuals without collectivizing minorities. Through art, it seeks ways for vulnerable individuals to affirm themselves and find love for the “us” composed of individuals with unique bodies and minds. Instead of categorizing the works by specific identities, the exhibition focuses on the shared experiences of social minorities. Furthermore, it explores the possibility of individuals uniting while respecting each other's diversity.


* The title of this exhibition is borrowed from the book Minor Feelings, with permission from Cathy Park Hong and Jeff Chang.

title: Snow
short_description: Atelier Aechae invites you to the special exhibition "Snow" which heralds a warm new year in 2025. In the cold winter, with gently falling snow, you can experience the strong vitality of plants that grow new buds, and the charm of white and clean Hanji (Korean traditional paper) like snow. The New Year's special exhibition "Snow" showcases works by artist Kim Hyun-Joo, who primarily works with stone and Hanji, and bonsai works with attractive new buds particularly prominent in winter. We bring you the purity of nature, breaking through the cold air with the white void of snow, the texture of hanji, and the resilience of plants. See it with your own eyes, feel it with your heart, and treasure it in your "eyes".

title: Hangang Story Exhibition Hall
short_description:
The Hangang River is a foundation for life and a vibrant space for cultural enjoyment, always present in daily life. It stands as a symbolic place that connects nature, the city, and people—a vast natural wonder running through the heart of South Korea and a cherished cultural heritage of the nation. At the Hangang Story Exhibition Hall, visitors can experience the history and cultural significance of the Hangang River, exploring its evolution through different eras and stories intricately tied to everyday life.


*Temporarily closed from July 1, 2025 for improvement of aging facilities

title: K-Idol Beauty Experience Zone : WINTER GLAM SEOUL
short_description:
K-Idol Beauty Experience Zone 'WINTER GLAM SEOUL'

Create your own glam transformation at a winter festival in the heart of the city.

A special three day experience with K beauty, featuring beauty classes by professional makeup artists, a beauty talk show with K-Idol makeup experts, and a special fan meet up with K-Idol RESCENE. The Winter Glam Seoul Beauty Experience Zone welcomes you.


Programs:

② GLOW Master Beauty Talk Show

title: A Wardrobe of Imagination - E-Land Collection Special Exhibition
short_description:
We recall the moment of opening a wardrobe door. The time brushing past fabrics, the memories lingering on our fingertips, countless garments and stories, and small attempts accumulate to become a single legacy. This exhibition focuses on the unseen, initial moments before fashion is completed. It is a journey tracing how the smallest fragments of thought—an unfamiliar object, a passing landscape, a sudden imagination—are realized into a single garment.


A single flower, a folded piece of paper, and a moment of light and shadow are reborn as wearable art through a designer's perspective. Through a carefully selected collection from the 500,000 authentic archives amassed by the E-Land Museum over 30 years, you can encounter the magnificent beginnings of global designers, from Alexander McQueen to Yves Saint Laurent, in one place.

title: Kylie Manning: Yellow Sea
short_description: On view from August 9 to November 10, Space K Seoul is pleased to present "Yellow Sea", a solo exhibition of works by Kylie Manning. Informed by coastal experiences from her upbringing in Alaska and Mexico, the works combine seascapes and ambiguous figures, moving between moments of clarity and abstraction. In a technique employed by Dutch Baroque painters, the artist builds up layers of thin paint, refracting light through the oils in each layer to create a self-luminous effect. The result is a lush harmony of radiant textures and delicate colors. This exhibition features the artist’s most ambitious project to date, submerging viewers in the rippling compositions of a new installation created specifically for Space K. Three large paintings on silk scrim will cascade through the exhibition space like film strips of the surrounding compositions. Measuring nearly 7 meters wide, three silk scrims by Manning are suspended in the center of the exhibition space, creating a stage-like effect. Each scrim is divided into five individual strips, acting as live gridded capsules. This allows the audience to traverse the oscillating vistas of Manning’s work alongside her represented figures. Manning draws inspiration from the tides of the ‘Yellow Sea’ that joins China and the Korean peninsula, meditating on ‘what is distilled after a tide removes excess debris, noise, and marks’. This exhibition will be an exciting opportunity to immerse visitors in the majestic seascapes alchemized by ‘Kylie Manning'.

title: MCKITHAN HOTEL
short_description: Built on the former site of Daehan Theater, the MCKITHAN HOTEL is an exclusive theater for the immersive performance <Sleep No More>, a sensuous and cinematic reinterpretation of Shakespeare’s tragedy Macbeth.

title: WORLD STAMP EXHIBITION PHILA KOREA 2025
short_description: World Stamp Exhibition PHILA KOREA 2025 is an international stamp exhibition held at COEX Magok Exhibition Center in Seoul from September 17 to 21, 2025. Under the theme 'Stamps, Connecting the World (CONNECT)', stamps from countries around the world, as well as various hands-on programs and events, are prepared. Anyone can view it for free, and it's conveniently accessible by public transportation, including the subway and bus. PHILA KOREA 2025 is a meaningful event that communicates with the world through stamps and promotes Korea's postal culture.

title: crosswalk
short_description: Gallery Planet will host a two-person exhibition 《Crosswalk》 featuring artists Kim Jung-in and Cho Hyun-seo from August 8 to September 13, 2024. 《Crosswalk》 begins by examining the perspectives of two artists who set out from different directions, meet, and diverge at an intersection. Through Kim Jung-in's images, which actively reveal subjective judgments uniquely human through a mixture of internalized and externalized memories, and Cho Hyun-seo's works, which seek to define aesthetic taste through the judgments of trained artificial intelligence, we ultimately find ourselves contemplating the paintings of our current era. As the exhibition title 'Crosswalk' suggests (a place where paths cross or meet), following the viewpoints of the two artists standing at the intersection leads us to a time of selected memories that have become filters. We experience numerous moments of (un)conscious choices as internal and external memories mix, pass through external memory, and reappear before our eyes. Based on their unique qualities, reflecting innate senses and learned tastes, the artists technically preserve images in their own memory vessels. The divergent perspectives of the two artists, which this exhibition highlights, are revealed at this point.

title: 《Proximities》
short_description: Co organized with the Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation, 《Proximities》 introduces more than forty artists across three generations connected to the United Arab Emirates, a Gulf nation shaped by migration, abundant natural resources, and rapid urban transformation over the past half century since its founding. The exhibition consists of three sections developed through collaboration with artists and curators, exploring phenomena that arise when unstable and subjective worlds at personal, social, and urban levels come into contact. Expanding from the most intimate and imaginative realms to geopolitical and foundational dimensions, the exhibition asks how relationships can remain close without collapsing into sameness.

title: Souimun, the Lost Gate of Seoul City Wall
short_description: Souimun Gate was a gate of the Hanyangdoseong (the Seoul City Wall), located between Sungnyemun Gate and Donuimun Gate, serving as the southwestern passage of Hanyang during the Joseon Dynasty. The area around Souimun Gate was a bustling hub of land and water transportation, filled with goods and people from all over the country. Outside the gate, executions of serious criminals and Catholic believers who were thought to threaten Confucian ideology were carried out, making it widely known that severe punishments awaited those who committed crimes. During the Japanese occupation, Souimun Gate was demolished in 1914 for road improvements, as it was perceived as an obstacle to urban modernization. This exhibition provides an opportunity to explore the bustling scenes and the history of demolition of Souimun Gate, which guarded the southwestern part of the Seoul City Wall.

title: A Century and a Day : From Memory to Imagination
short_description: At Culture Station Seoul 284, located in the heart of Seoul and holding one hundred years of history, a special exhibition is held where visitors can encounter the past and present of Seoul. The Old Seoul Station is not merely a building but was the gateway of the city that accompanied Seoul’s history, from modernization and industrialization to division, liberation, and democratization. This exhibition vividly brings back the memories of the Old Seoul Station through a wide range of artifacts, photographs and videos, and contemporary art works. It is a meaningful exhibition where visitors can see, feel, and experience one hundred years of Seoul at a glance.

title: Exhibition 《Where Warmth Shines》
short_description: Superior Gallery will present in November 2025 the solo exhibition 《Where Warmth Shines》 by artist Choi Hyun Hee, who depicts memories of daily life, light, and the warmth of life through landscapes and objects. This exhibition focuses on light and objects that the artist has painted for a long time and conveys the memory of time and experience that connects treasured memories with the present. Based on oil painting, Choi Hyun Hee observes objects in daily life and reconstructs them on canvas. The warm memories recalled by the artist resonate with memories within us and lead to another kind of warmth. It is hoped that this exhibition will become a moment in which visitors once again encounter the gentle memories that have remained in their hearts and in which each person’s light connects with another. The exhibition 《Where Warmth Shines》 will continue until December 11, 2025.

title: B the B
short_description: Connected to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park, DDP, and the surrounding Dongdaemun markets, B the B is a beauty complex and cultural space where Seoul’s beauty companies and residents can closely interact. It also serves as a creative lounge where visitors can relax in an urban natural setting. You can enjoy various free content, including brand pop-ups from leading Seoul beauty companies, curated product exhibitions aligned with the latest trends, and experiences with products that combine innovative technology. Additionally, seasonal events are frequently held in the healing space reminiscent of a forest retreat, offering beauty-related content and information.

title: The Records of this Place at that Time - Cheonggyecheon Shanty Town
short_description:
The exhibition features over 80 photographs of Cheonggyecheon shantytowns and their residents, captured by photographers Kuwabara Shisei, Nomura Motoyuki, and Hong Soon-tae, and held in the collections of the Seoul Museum of History and Cheonggyecheon Museum. Divided into three sections, the exhibition provides a photographic glimpse into the diverse scenes of Cheonggyecheon’s shantytowns from the 1960s to the 1970s.
Part 1, “Scenes of the Shantytown,” showcases images of the shantytown around Cheonggyecheon and the huts in the lower area during the 1970s. Part 2, “People of the Shantytown,” portrays the residents' daily lives. Part 3, “Demolition and Overpass,” highlights the displacement of shantytown communities due to Cheonggyecheon’s redevelopment and the construction of the new overpass.
You are invited to take a meaningful journey to reflect on the lives of Cheonggyecheon’s former residents, now transformed by urban development.

title: SEOUL ROBOT & AI MUSEUM (RAIM)
short_description: At the Seoul Robot and AI Museum (RAIM), visitors can directly engage with and learn about robots and artificial intelligence, developed and advanced through human intellect and imagination. You can experience dazzling robot movements and fascinating AI technologies, and go beyond simple observation to explore how these technologies are transforming our lives and society. The museum is divided into several levels. The public area welcomes visitors with robots and AI. The multipurpose space introduces and offers hands-on experience with robotics and AI technologies from various companies. The permanent exhibition hall encourages reflection and questions about the relationship between robots, AI, and humans. The special exhibition floor hosts rotating themed and planned exhibitions.

title: 《Electric Shock》
short_description: 《Electric Shock》 is a report on electricity. Electricity, defined as the totality of energy generated through electrons, is a key resource that operates modern society. From household appliances to digital consumption, advanced production lines, and logistics systems, it is difficult to imagine life without electricity. The recent commercialization of artificial intelligence and the expansion of big tech companies have exponentially increased power consumption. Securing and supplying electricity in a stable manner has become a critical issue in rapidly adopting advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, beginning to determine the competitiveness of nations and corporations. The era of electrical hegemony has arrived, and alongside endless desires for technological advancement, various efforts to develop power within finite resources are underway. Electricity is no longer merely an energy source that enriches daily life but has become an essential weapon that determines survival. This urgency has led to indiscriminate development, turning even efforts for carbon neutrality into romantic promises seen as delaying technological progress. Reflective movements that once called for sustainable coexistence such as posthumanism and the Anthropocene are fading into history already written over the immediate electric war unfolding before us. Electric Shock reveals and traces the sharp relationship between technology and the environment occurring today through a single circuit called electricity.

title: Ttukseom Artificial Rock Climbing Wall
short_description: The outdoor artificial rock-climbing wall in Ttukseom Hangang Park is a facility with a height of 15 meters and a width of 40 meters. Established in 2006, it is a beloved recreational sports facility for climbing enthusiasts, operated free of charge. The wall is divided into three sections: the left wall at 15 meters, the central wall at 18 meters, and the right wall at 13 meters, making it important for users to choose a course that matches their skill level. Additionally, users can access a changing room behind the management office. For beginners, a separate wall is installed next to the left wall, and training can be arranged in advance with the facility manager. There are also places to wash hands and feet after climbing.

title: [Faint Memories, Deep Longing]
short_description: A woman who has carried the pain of separation in her heart for over 70 years shows the last handwritten letter she received from her husband before they became separated due to the Korean War. Through videos of maps drawn by separated families depicting their hometowns and the stories behind them, viewers can virtually visit these childhood places beyond the armistice line, places they can no longer reach. Although no one knows when a reunion might happen, videos containing the life stories and memories of separated families are shown, with the hope they may one day reach their relatives still in North Korea.

title: Yuichi Hirako <Travel>
short_description: Hirako, who studied painting at Wimbledon College of Art in London and continues to work internationally based in Tokyo, seeks the coexistence of man and nature. He created a hybrid character as a medium to connect human with nature. The character, who has a human body and tree head, travels with dogs, cats, and various plants in the exhibition. Sometimes by the river, sometimes in the forest, and other times in a room, these scenes with flora and fauna are transformed into a variety of media, including painting, sculpture, and installation, to give the viewers a more sensory understanding of nature. Through this, Hirako questions anthropocentric attitudes toward nature, suggesting that nature be viewed on an equal footing rather than as an object to be explored and conquered.

title: The Exhibition <Connecing Time>
short_description: Superior Gallery presents the exhibition <Connecting Time> by artists Yeye, Yoon Yeojin, and Nogang Lee. Yeye records her special and joyful moments spent with her dog 'Moonge' over 15 years, capturing the emotions within her artwork. Yoon Yeojin meticulously captures everyday scenes, objects, and subconscious feelings, expressing them through her art. Nogang Lee tells the stories of modern life through his 'hermit series' reinterpreting symbols of traditional Korean art and his 'bear series', which anthropomorphizes bears. Reconnect with precious memories and look forward to new beginnings by warmly embracing the works of these three artists at Superior Gallery.

title: A World of Paintings: On the Lee Kun-hee Collection
short_description:
This exhibition begins with 36 works from the Lee Kun-hee Collection, donated to the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) and regional art museums in 2021, as well as pieces from the Leeum Museum of Art. To deepen the understanding of each artist’s world, it also includes 24 additional works borrowed from public and private institutions including the Seoul Museum of Art, various public and private galleries, and personal collections.

Based on the concepts of landscape, color, and materiality, the exhibition is organized under three major themes:

'Forms, Scenes, and Nature', 'Color Comes Alive', and 'When Creation Is Performed Through Matter'

The title, A World Beyond the Canvas, is inspired by Korean modernist painter Lee In-sung’s metaphor for painting as a “separate world that reflects the aesthetic consciousness of the artist.” It encapsulates the artists’ pursuit of an ultimate world they sought to reach through their art.

title: One Step at a Time: Heehwan Seo, a Master of Hangul Calligraphy
short_description:
Seoul Arts Center is delighted to present One Step at a Time: Heehwan Seo, a Master of Hangul Calligraphy, an exhibition highlighting the life and art of Pyeongbo Heehwan Seo. Held in commemoration of the 30th anniversary of Seo’s passing, this large-scale retrospective provides a comprehensive overview of Seo’s extensive oeuvre, spanning works from his early years to his later life.


Seo, also known by his art name “Pyeongbo [one step at a time],” was a representative Hangul calligrapher of 20th-century Korea. In 1968, his presentation won the Presidential Award at the 17th National Art Exhibition of Korea, marking the first time a work of calligraphy received this particular honor. Until his death at the age of 61 in 1995, Seo devoted his entire life to exploring Hangul’s calligraphic potential. This incomparable artistic achievement cements his status as an indispensable figure in the history of Korean calligraphy. 


This exhibition was designed to trace Seo’s journey in achieving the feat of Hangul calligraphy being accepted as an art form. Establishing Hangul calligraphy as an art form — and more importantly, as a calligraphical art — was his lifelong goal, and his perseverance eventually realized this dream. Seo once said, “A turtle in a lake waits a thousand years for its turn to perch atop a lotus leaf,” and his 61-year journey was, indeed, true to his art name, Pyeongbo — one step at a time — in both art and life, advancing step by step without rushing or resting. We hope this exhibition offers visitors an opportunity to deepen their understanding of Seo’s life and art and to keep his memory alive.

title: THART
short_description: THART is a dedicated media art exhibition hall located in Hongdae. This story-immersive media art theater fuses theater and media art, transforming a former performance venue once filled with the passion of countless artists into an exhibition space. Combining digital technology and art creates mesmerizing lights and sounds, offering visitors a sensational experience. Additionally, the story-immersive exhibitions allow for deep engagement, providing artistic emotion and inspiration through interaction. THART is where one can experience a new form of artistic expression through the convergence of art, technology, and storytelling.

title: THE PAINTERS
short_description:
Premiered in 2008, 'THE PAINTERS' is a new-concept art performance that merges dynamic choreography, live drawing, and media art. The show dramatically portrays the creation of artwork through each scene, with unexpected twists, witty performances, and stylish urban dance.

With vivid lighting, stunning visual effects, and thrilling music, the performance offers a high level of immersion and is designed to be easily enjoyed by audiences of all ages. It is especially popular among families.
