title: Hangang River, Flowing with Folk Songs and Stories
short_description:
<Our Songs Where the Han River Appears>

Representative folk songs featuring the Han River include <Han River Lament>, <Nodeul Riverside>, <Ferryman's Song>, and <Inje Log Raft Arirang>, which were sung while working on the Han River.

The exhibition enables visitors to view the Han River in various contexts as depicted in folk songs from all regions of the country. It also features rare folk song SP and LP records, lyric books containing lyrics, and musical scores.


<[Experience] Han River in Memory>

This is an experience zone designed to allow visitors to appreciate the various aspects of the Han River through ASMR videos, landscape paintings, and maps, and share precious memories of the Han River.

We hope this special exhibition, <Han River, Flows with Sound>, which illuminates the Han River that has flowed alongside Seoul citizens for a long time, will be a meaningful opportunity to feel the emotions of our people through folk songs deeply.

title: Photography Seoul Museum of Art 《All That Photography》
short_description: This exhibition is presented for the first time using the entire building since the opening of the Photography Seoul Museum of Art. It is composed of works held by the Seoul Museum of Art and by the artists, centering on works created from the late 1950s, which is generally regarded as the starting point of Korean contemporary art, and which used “photography” or “photographic images” as a medium of creation. Through this, the exhibition sheds light on the process in which photography has functioned as a creative tool that opens new worlds for artists, as well as the role it has performed within the expansion of contemporary art. (Exhibition photo: ⓒ Jeong Youngdon)

title: Immersive-K: Kansong Art and Culture Foundation Media Art Exhibition
short_description:
In a maze that transcends time and space, IMMERSIVE is the world's first Korean‑ style media art exhibition using traditional Korean art, the foundation of K‑ Culture. It is being presented for the first time at the Kansong Art Museum.  


1. [Hunminjeongeum] Haeryebon: The Haeryebon of Hunminjeongeum, opening a world of equality in the universe.
2. [Haeakjeonsincheop, Gwandong Myeongseungcheop]: Capturing the breathtaking scenery of Geumgangsan (Diamond Mountain) and the Gwandong region.
3. [Miindo, Portrait of a Beauty]: The allure of that fleeting moment.
4. [Hyewonjeonsincheop]: The world of Hyeon transcending time and space.
5. [Gyemimyeong Geumdong Samjonbul Ipsang]: The light and time reflecting enlightenment.
6. [Geumgangnaesan]: The time of Geumgangsan painted with light through the brush of Gyeomjae, [Samcheongcheop]: A message of hope and comfort from Samcheongcheop.
7. [Kansong Graphic Archive]: A magical space where past treasures are reborn in the modern language, crossing the river of time.
8. [Chusa Kim Jeong-hui]: The dynamic unfolding of the artistic world of Kim Jeong-hee, the master of Chusa calligraphy.

title: Suraksan Byeokung Valley
short_description: On the southwestern side of Suraksan Mountain lies the stunning Byeokun Valley. The name Byeokun Valley originates from the inscription “Byeokun Dongcheon (碧雲洞天)” carved into a rock in the valley. The name was given because the spectacular white rock formations of Suraksan, exposed throughout the valley, blend with the ravine’s scenery in a way that resembles white clouds resting in the area. For those who enjoy hiking, a recommended course begins at Byeokun Valley and leads up to the summit of Suraksan. For those who prefer valleys over hiking, a well-maintained wooden deck along the stream provides a refreshing spot for a picnic.

title: Selected for the 2024 Samgaksan Geumam Art Museum Craft Exhibition Contest - EUNPYEONG <Variety of Shapes and Colors>
short_description: The 2024 Samgaksan Geumam Art Museum Craft Exhibition Contest is the first contest held since the museum’s opening in 2018. Unlike other prestigious competitions, this contest is divided into three categories: 'EUNPYEONG,' which focuses on works that harmonize with the unique characteristics of the Hanok village; 'ECO,' for works that blend with nature, including Bukhansan Mountain; and 'EVERY,' for interactive content created with the audience. The first theme to kick off the exhibition is the EUNPYEONG category with the exhibition “Variety of Shapes and Colors.” It features works by artist Ha Shin-hyuk, who presents monochrome landscape ceramics, and Shin Ye-won, who explores the boundary between craft and industry using plastic, a byproduct of industrial society. This exhibition reflects our hopes for the union of nature and industrial society, striving for natural harmony. We hope you enjoy a unique reflective experience through the works of these two artists, displayed in the traditional Hanok setting.

title: From unfamiliar gaze
short_description:
Forming a relationship begins with sensing the subject. Among these senses, sight, or our eyes’ path, is the easiest and fastest way to establish a relationship. A gaze that doesn't stray from everyday life is conducive to forming connections. However, if the subject is unfamiliar, desire becomes entwined with the gaze. To start a relationship with that subject, one might actively explore it, desperately avoid forming a connection, or even experience frustration in their desire.

In this exhibition, invited artists Manwook (b.1975) and Kimi Jaak (b.1976) discuss their respective ways of forming relationships based on their deep contemplation of unfamiliar subjects that have long held their attention. The results of their gazes are fundamentally different. In the case of artist Manwook, an active exploration of the subject ultimately leads to the erasure of boundaries with the unfamiliar subject. On the other hand, the unfamiliar gaze of artist Kimi Jaak results in narratives that revolve around and observe from the periphery, unable to be integrated.

title: 2023 Sejong Museum Special Exhibition《 'Ink and Brush Transformation: Song Soo-nam and Hwang Chang-bae》'Two Perspectives on Contemporary Ink Painting'
short_description:
Namcheon Song Soo-nam (1938-2013) and Sojeong Hwang Chang-bae (1947-2001), who liberated themselves from the traditional use of ink and brush at the end of the 20th century, marked a milestone in their times through change and innovation and had a great influence on later generations. We present the spirit of the times and the world of work.

This exhibition offers an opportunity to encounter the works of Namcheon Song Soo-nam and Sojeong Hwang Chang-bae, who departed from tradition and always aimed for contemporary reality, firmly rooted in a pragmatic space-time for Korean painting. This exhibition conveys the messages of the two masters regarding the visual resonance and their perspective on life, which their works uniquely emit directly to the audience.

title: 2025 YeoYuJak Concert
short_description:
During the Chuseok holiday, when hearts become as abundant as the full moon, enjoy a stage of Korean traditional music for all generations. Under the blue autumn sky, colorful and cheerful melodies will fill the air, painted with the sounds of Samsan and Simple. At the Yeo-Yu-Jak Concert, let yourself be carried away by the rhythms of autumn!


Performers: Samsan (Oct. 8), Simple (Oct. 9) at 15:00/17:00

title: 2026 Kong Sung-hwan Solo Exhibition <Ripple>
short_description: On Kong Sung-hwan's canvas, water appears clear and transparent, yet it is an object that can never be fully captured. His paintings are abstract works emerging through his sensations and thoughts rather than realistic depictions. Light settling on the water's surface vibrates finely, waves spread like invisible breath, and shapes within the transparent depth seem to reveal themselves before receding again. Observing these moments of subtle change for a long time, the artist translates natural landscapes into a single sensation. The 'abstraction' spoken of by artist Kong Sung-hwan does not mean an abstraction where forms disappear, but rather a state where the concreteness of reality is converted into sensation, rhythm, light, and vibration through the process of gazing at the water before his eyes for a long time. In his canvas, abstraction is not the absence of form, but a process in which form shakes and transitions into another sensation. Therefore, Kong Sung-hwan's water appears realistic, yet quietly flows into abstraction within. It is another landscape starting at the end of what is visible, an inner ripple revealed through the surface of water.

title: MINSEONG KIM: False Alarm
short_description:
The artist explores the screens and boundaries we encounter in today's digital age, delving into the temporal nature and reconfiguration of images through various painterly experiments. In this exhibition, dynamically explosive and attention-grabbing scenes are arranged randomly to depict the endless, one-way cycle of information. Images selected from platforms like YouTube and Instagram are visually arranged using a 'dendrogram' method, which pairs and merges similar attributes based on algorithmic data.

Through this exhibition, artist Kim Min-seong aims to highlight the paradox of displayed images and invites us to reflect on how we consume algorithm-driven images on these platforms.

title: Nowon Light Garden (Old Hwarangdae Station)
short_description: The Nowon Light Garden, nestled in the nostalgic setting of the old Hwarangdae Station, is Seoul's first night-time light garden. Nowon District created this healing cultural space, freely accessible all year. The garden features a variety of themes, such as a light tunnel and firefly garden, adorned with light tunnels, LED sculptures, and 3D mapping installations. By day, it serves as Hwarangdae Railroad Park, and by night, it transforms into a luminous garden, making it an ideal place to create lasting memories with family or loved ones.

title: Special Exhibition of Contemporary Crafts 《Material–Practice》
short_description:
The participating artists restore “discarded objects” as materials, experiment with production methods reliant on “nature’s circulation systems,” and explore the compatibility between “matter and information.” Through their ways and attitudes of working with materials, this exhibition senses the future practices of craft, showing that craft techniques are not limited to manual skills but expand into creative sensibilities and critical practices that correspond with the world.


Organized into sections such as Reconstruction of Ash, Primitive Creation, and Flowing Matter, the exhibition invites visitors to explore contemporary craft and its future possibilities.

title: Shunita, Oh Jeisung, Dokkaebi: Multi Persona
short_description:
Gallery Jiwooheon is pleased to announce a two-person exhibition titled Dokkaebi: Multi Persona by Shunita and Oh Jeisung from 22 May to 22 June. 
This exhibition extends and reinterprets the concept of ‘Korean fantasy’ that emerged in the domestic novel scene in the early 2000s into the realm of art. Through a perspective that encompasses both tradition and modernity, it aims to present a new form of visual fantasy by combining Korea's unique cultural elements with an exploration of identity in contemporary society. Unlike the typical images seen in media, Dokkaebi with unclear origins and sources, and Multi persona referring to an individual's diverse identities in digital culture, these two concepts evoke something mysterious and unpredictable. In this context, two artists, Shunita and Oh Jeisung, who approach fantasy structures in their own ways, collaborate. Shunita's Moomyeong(nameless) is the artist's signature character that reflects the empty inner self of modern people. Moomyeong, an alien who came to Earth, takes on various appearances in relationships with humans. Its simple yet ambiguous gestures, colorful monochrome fur, round body, and flexible limbs give a strange sense of familiarity. Moomyeong dramatically represents the empty emotions in one corner of the young generation who use multiple identities in the digital world as a breakthrough in life, while simultaneously reflecting some substance behind the Multi persona. Oh Jeisung is an artist who has gained attention for his research-based sculptural work that investigates and archives undesignated cultural properties across the country. Various folk sculptures such as animals from Folktales, Dokkaebi, Abandoned dolmens, and Stone Maitreyas are reinterpreted in a contemporary context in his works, gaining contemporary forms. In this exhibition, he presents works that newly adapt the attributes of Dokkaebi from folk tales, which have been around humans, sometimes helping and sometimes hindering, but still with unclear forms, by grafting them onto the belief in the twelve zodiac animals. His work, which commemorates marginalized folk sculptures and revives folktales and legends as modern sculptures, offers a new interpretation of Korean fantasy. 
Dokkaebi: Multi Persona is an exhibition that calls upon imaginary beings infused with human life history from a modern perspective and loosely sketches the past and present of Korean fantasy. Through this, we aim to provide an opportunity to contemplate together the unique imagination of our culture and the identity of modern society

title: Lee Youngjun Ingoing Escape
short_description: Lee Youngjun's solo exhibition “Ingoing Escape” is organized to coincide with the Kiaf and Frieze seasons to introduce noteworthy emerging artists. It is also part of the 2024 Seoul Art Week. Based in Munich, Germany, Lee Youngjun has been expanding his activities in Korea since last year. He is an experimental artist who reinterprets space and form, drawing on personal narratives and emotions. The exhibition's theme, “Ingoing Escape,” means “escape inward,” emphasizing the artist's distinctive multidimensional abstraction. Lee Youngjun's works are created using a technique of layering various materials on canvas, with each layer maintaining its unique form without blending, effectively showcasing the dimensionality of time. Through this exhibition, viewers will experience a paradoxical encounter, simultaneously delving into their consciousness and confronting the multi-layered aspects of perception.

title: [S-TCEP] 2023 Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra: Sibelius' Second
short_description:
The original version of Sibelius' Second makes its first showing here in Korea with conductor, Osmo Vänskä, at the helm and violinist, Elina Vahala. Conductor Vänskä is the first conductor to even earn recognition by the Sibelius family. This highly technical and exceptional concerto is slated to be performed at the Seoul Art Center on March 24 and 25.







※ This content is provided by the S-TCEP (Seoul - Tourism, Culture, Exhibitions, Performing Arts) Alliance.

title: Happiness Recipe Found in a Gallery
short_description: The Superior Gallery is showcasing a two-person exhibition featuring the artists Jeong Yeon-hee and Pdohk, who depict characters inspired by their happiness. The exhibition introduces artist Jeong Yeon-hee who conveys the warmth of comfort and hopes to a weary life with a colorful abstract series along with new character series and the works of Pdohk, who discovers happiness hidden in everyday life and gives happiness and comfort to people through his characters’ delicate facial expressions. Discover their happiness recipe at the Superior Gallery. The <Happiness Recipe Found in a Gallery> exhibition will run until June 8th.

title: Musical -The First Great Show
short_description:
Set in the 1960s when the concept of “musical” was barely known in Korea, this comedy musical follows Director Yoo Deok-han and producer Kim Young-woong as they embark on a mission to create Korea’s very first musical—one that could rival even North Korea’s Pibada Opera Troupe.

The First Great Show is a well-made original musical developed over three years by the Seoul Metropolitan Musical Theatre in collaboration with Korea’s top creative team—director Kim Dong-yeon, writer Park Hae-rim, and composer Choi Jong-yoon. With leading musical actors Lee Chang-yong and Cho Hyung-kyun, as well as talented Seoul City Musical Theatre members Park Sung-hoon and Lee Seung-jae, the show promises a unique and delightful comedy experience.

title: Pace Gallery Seoul
short_description: Pace Gallery is one of the world’s foremost contemporary art galleries, representing some of the most influential artists of our time. It has also maintained decades-long relationships with the estates of artists such as Alexander Calder, Jean Dubuffet, Agnes Martin, Louise Nevelson, and Mark Rothko. Since its early years, Pace has supported artists associated with Abstract Expressionism and those working with light and space, establishing itself as a uniquely distinguished gallery across the United States. Today, Pace operates exhibition spaces worldwide, including two galleries in Chelsea, New York, as well as in London, Geneva, Berlin, Hong Kong, Seoul, Los Angeles, and Tokyo.

title: K-Pop Square Hongdae
short_description: The Line Friends Hongdae flagship store, a popular destination for foreign tourists, has reopened under the new name 'K-Pop Square Hongdae', Korea’s only specialized K-POP store. Experience unique pop-ups and exhibitions that let you directly see, hear, and feel the worldview of your favorite artists, along with limited-edition goods. A must-visit space filled with delights for K-POP fans worldwide.

title: Seokguram
short_description: Seokguram Grotto is nestled halfway up Inwangsan Mountain, just below Chimabawi Rock, and can be reached via the Inwangsan Mountain Trail. Inside, you'll find the Three Buddha Statues, while the surrounding forest path features a Buddha statue and a Maitreya Buddha carved into the rocks. Above the main hall at Sanshingak Shrine, a large rock bears a painting of the Mountain Spirit and a tiger that guards Inwangsan. About 30 meters to the right of Seokguram, you can also visit the Cheonhyangam Hermitage. From Seokguram, you'll enjoy stunning panoramic views of Seoul, with Namsan Tower visible on the opposite mountain and, on clear days, even Lotte Tower. Below, Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Blue House come into view.

title: Pixel Space 2025
short_description: 2025, the Wall Project will feature the adhesive film artwork Pixel Space 2025 by artist Choo Mirim. The work will be displayed on the white wall next to the entrance passage on Basement Level 1 of GS Tower. In an era of rapid change, we simultaneously live through screens and in cities. The artist weaves together pixels, satellite maps, the complex sensations of urban life, and a sense of nostalgia for early internet culture. Through landscapes that are both familiar and unfamiliar, the exhibition explores the intersections of digital and urban space, past and present, offering a new sensibility the artist calls “Netstalgia” (Internet + Nostalgia).

title: A Walk Around the City Wall: Hanyangdoseong through the Eyes of 19th-Century Literature
short_description:
After the cold winter passes and spring arrives with its budding flowers, many people visit Seoul City Wall. Originally, "Soonseong" referred to the patrols conducted by Joseon soldiers along the fortress walls to defend and manage the Seoul City Wall. In the late Joseon period, however, the term also came to refer to the leisurely activity of springtime visitors walking along the fortress walls to enjoy the scenery.
Additionally, Soonseong was a tradition for scholars who traveled to Hanyang to take the state exams and walked around the fortress walls, hoping for success. Here, we have a record of a Soonseong journey left by a scholar over 100 years ago. This writing, which describes his experience of walking the Soonseong path with a light heart after passing the exam, captures the image of the Seoul City Wall as it was in the past. This exhibition aims to follow the journey of Soonseong as documented in the record and reflect on how the tradition has continued to the present day. Today, why not walk along the fortress path in ancestors’ footsteps?

title: The Day of Our Liberation
short_description:
To commemorate the 80th anniversary of Korea’s Liberation, the special exhibition 'The Day of Our Liberation' is being held. The exhibition is composed of three parts: Part 1 'Records of Liberation Day', Part 2 'Memories of Liberation Day', and Part 3 'Recollections of Liberation Day'. It highlights the Liberation Day commemorative ceremonies and related events, shedding light on how citizens have remembered Liberation Day and the changes in the spirit of the times. In addition, literature, film, music, and other popular culture materials related to Liberation Day are on display, allowing visitors to understand the broader social context of the era.


The exhibition focuses particularly on Liberation Day commemorative ceremonies held after independence, showing how citizens commemorated the event and how the zeitgeist evolved. A highlight of the exhibition is the first public display of a diary donated by a former schoolteacher, covering daily life from June 3 to November 20, 1945. The diary holds special significance as it was written in Japanese before liberation and switched to Korean after news of independence was received.


Through 'The Day of Our Liberation', visitors are invited to reflect on the sacrifices of independence activists and share in the meaning of liberation.

title: KUOCA SEONGSU
short_description: Kuoca takes its name from cuoca, the Italian word for chef, embodying the idea of delivering delicate, heartfelt quality that pleases all five senses—just like fine dining. This premium skincare brand focuses on fresh, handcrafted products made in small batches by artisans rather than mass production. Only items manufactured within 30 days are sold, ensuring exceptional freshness and care.

title: e-Sports Hall of Fame
short_description: The E-Sports Hall of Fame, operated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea e-Sports Association, is a place dedicated to recording the development of e-sports in Korea and exhibiting and commemorating the achievements of legendary e-sports players. The Hall of Fame offers domestic and international visitors a variety of rich experiences related to e-sports, including player and studio experience booths, VR exhibits, and a wide range of themed displays.

title: Welcome to Hanseongbu: Governing the Capital of Joseon
short_description:
Hanseongbu was the institution that managed the affairs of the capital, much like today's Seoul City Hall, and its head, the Panyun, oversaw the entire capital city and led its urban administration. Furthermore, it also possessed the characteristics of a central administrative agency, directly participating in state administration. Therefore, Hanseongbu was in charge of urban administration—such as household registry compilation, housing management, and the processing of various civil complaints—while concurrently undertaking nationwide duties, including maintaining order in the royal capital, storing household registries, and handling legal disputes. This exhibition comprehensively illuminates the various functions and aspects of Hanseongbu, aiming to reflect on the appearance and significance of modern-day Seoul through this historical lens.


The realities of administration captured in historical records and the stories of the people who lived within those systems continue to offer valid questions and profound insights for us living today. We hope that the familiar yet unfamiliar story of Hanseongbu unfolding in this exhibition will serve as an opportunity to look anew at Seoul, the city where we work and live today.

title: Yoo Youngkuk : A Mountain Within Me
short_description: 《Yoo Youngkuk: A Mountain Within Me》 is the largest retrospective to date commemorating the 110th anniversary of the birth of Yoo Youngkuk (1916–2002), a pioneer of Korean abstract art, and the inaugural project of the newly presented 'Korean Modern Masters Exhibition' series by the Seoul Museum of Art. This exhibition comprehensively illuminates his 60-year artistic career, from his early abstract experiments in Tokyo in 1935 to his later introspective abstraction, through over 170 works, including previously unreleased paintings, reliefs, photographs, drawings, and archival materials. Penetrating the turbulence of the Japanese colonial period, the Korean War, and the era of rapid economic growth, his paintings, which practiced abstraction, the avant-garde of his time, in both life and art, speak to us once again with profound resonance from today's perspective, questioning the very essence of creation.

title: North Korean Human Rights Opera <Naengmyeon>
short_description: The original opera "Naengmyeon" is a large-scale North Korean human rights cultural and arts project featuring the collaboration of over 90 participants, including leading domestic artists, production staff, and North Korean defectors. Through the story of Naengmyeon, a Korean dish that originated in North Korea and has since spread across the Korean Peninsula and the world, the opera sheds light on the hardships faced by North Korean residents and defectors, as well as the reality of human rights violations. It is a production dedicated to defectors, displaced people, families separated by the Korean War, and all who have experienced the pain of a divided nation, as well as those preparing for reunification and anyone who loves music.

title: <The magnificent Hermitage> Official Digital Special Exhibition
short_description: Culture Tank hosts the digital exhibition <The magnificent Hermitage> from the State Hermitage Museum in Russia, which is considered one of the world's top three museums. This special exhibition utilizes official digital content from the Hermitage Museum to present world-class masterpieces and the architectural beauty of the museum through immersive media art, providing citizens with the opportunity to experience world-class cultural content within the city.

title: Utopia: Nowhere, Now Here
short_description:
A special space, curated according to the storytelling adapted from the short story "Symbiosis Theory," included in Kim Cho-yeop's bestselling book "If We Can't Move at the Speed of Light," unfolds. Utopian images lingering in the authors' memories unfold thematically. Seven works by different artists, comprising over 200 pieces, are presented under one unified worldview, each depicting their interpretation. 
Discover more than a typical exhibition, drawing inspiration from cinematic direction and literary techniques. Encounter emotions that extend beyond the confines of the gallery space. Within the artists' creations, find the utopia that mirrors the ideal world you envision.

title: Mandy El-Sayegh : For Theresa
short_description: Space K Seoul, Kolon’s cultural art sharing space, hosts the solo exhibition "For Theresa" by Mandy El-Sayegh (b.1985), who is based in London. Born in Malaysia with Palestinian and Chinese heritage, the artist has developed unique archival installation works using data collection and editing methods based on the 'outsider's perspective' she experienced while growing up in Western society. Mandy El-Sayegh questions what the institutionalized systems of knowledge and classification systems that have defined our world have excluded and what they have naturalized. In particular, for this exhibition, she extensively incorporates printed materials such as old maps, calligraphy, and banknotes that she directly collected while visiting museums, old bookstores, and flea markets in Korea. Through the archival techniques of collection and classification, she traces the political implications of how such material traces have contributed to the accumulation and maintenance of power.

title: Unprecedented Great Flood: The 1925 Eulchuk Year
short_description:
In the summer of 1925, the Han River flood claimed numerous lives and destroyed houses and buildings. The city of Gyeongseong was left isolated with electricity and transportation cut off, and farmlands surrounding the city that sustained its residents were washed away or turned into sand fields. The flood even changed the course of the Han River and erased entire villages. Known as the “Great Flood of the Eulchuk Year,” this disaster had both direct and indirect significant impacts on Seoul. Later, when flood control facilities were installed on the Han River, the flood served as the benchmark, and flood control became a major issue in urban planning.


A century later, as continuous flood control efforts have led to floods fading from public memory, the climate crisis has struck. Faced with extreme downpours that have become part of daily life, we are once again reminded of the severity of great floods. On the centennial of the Eulchuk Year Great Flood, this exhibition revisits this historic disaster, serving as an opportunity to collectively consider measures for future climate change preparedness.

title: Celestial Whisper
short_description: Celestial Whisper is an exhibition by sculptor Meekyoung Shin, who has built a unique body of work using soap as her main material. The theme of the exhibition, angels, is a religious symbol that connects God and humans. More than that, however, angels serve as symbolic beings that have become a natural part of our perception. Visualizing the image of angels as those that lie somewhere between what exists and what is absent, the artist first became interested in angels when she came across a fragrance called “Angel.” In this exhibition, Shin highlights the meaning of angels, something that everyone knows of yet has never seen. Her angel is a being in the realm of illusion, hovering between heaven and earth, life and death, body and soul, and is presented metaphorically through the material properties of soap. The artist has used soap as a material for her sculptures for more than 30 years. For Shin, soap also has a materiality to it that wavers between transparency and opacity. Still, it is destined to wear down over time, while its scent can only be experienced by those who have come in contact with it in person. These characteristics of soap are connected to the symbolism of angels, who are intermediate beings between heaven and earth. In particular, the transparency of soap, the light that maximizes its transparency, and its many different scents allow visitors to experience the presence of angels that oscillate between existence and absence. Visitors can draw closer to contemporary art by appreciating sculptures made from everyday soap, allowing their imagination to run wild through angels, a familiar yet unseen entity. We hope that this exhibition, which is filled with the light and fragrance of angels that evoke a kind of fantasy across generations, will inspire you to rediscover the very same angels you have always felt are familiar.

title: Choong Ang High School
short_description: It is the first private school in the Republic of Korea, established in 1908 during the Japanese colonial period to save and establish the country through education. The school actively participated in national movements such as the March 1st Movement during the Japanese colonial period, the June 1st Movement, and the Gwangju Student Movement. Monuments commemorating the March 1st Movement and the June 10th Movement are erected, allowing visitors to reflect on history. Additionally, the school is famous for its exotic architectural style and is a popular tourist destination, as it was a filming location for the drama “Winter Sonata.”

title: Seoul Metropolitan Traditional Orchestra Chamber Music Series  - Sori Island: Arirang Through the Ages
short_description:
Arirang, the most iconic Korean folk song, embodies the soul of the Korean people. Passed down across time and borders, this song carries the memories of migration, solidarity, loss, and hope, and it is both the voice and emotional record of a nation.

Sori Island: Arirang Through the Ages is a chamber concert by the Seoul Metropolitan Traditional Orchestra, held in celebration of the 80th anniversary of Korea’s Liberation. This performance captures the breath of each era expressed through Arirang, delicately interpreted through the tones of traditional Korean instruments.

From the Imjin War and resistance militias to forced migrations, armed independence movements, and globalization, travel through modern Korean history following the melodies of Arirang.

This is a stage where Korea's history and emotions are conveyed not in words but in sound, through the rich, resonant timbre of traditional instruments. Highly recommended for those wishing to experience the depth of Korean traditional music.

title: Seoul Museum of Photography 《Martin Parr : We Are Martin Parr》
short_description: The retrospective exhibition of contemporary photography master Martin Parr, 《Martin Parr: We Are Martin Parr》, is the first large-scale retrospective in Asia held since the passing of Martin Parr. Completed in collaboration with Magnum Photos and the Martin Parr Foundation, this exhibition encompasses Martin Parr's artistic world spanning over 50 years, from his early black-and-white works in the 1970s to his late works, through 14 representative series of the artist, over 500 photographic works, and 90 photobooks. Going beyond a retrospective of a single photographer, this exhibition aims to re-examine the way images are produced and consumed today. (Panoramic photo: ⓒ Genie Project)

title: Looking at the Calm Light and the Blue Sky
short_description: This exhibition centers around the emotional flow of taking a pause in the midst of a hectic life to reflect on the present and confront the potential of tomorrow. Artist Yoon Eui-jin uses repeated brushstrokes on traditional Korean paper to depict surreal landscapes that embody the dark hours of life and the quiet hope found within them, capturing the lingering impressions of fleeting emotions. Artist Lee Chae-il transforms everyday objects such as classic cars, cats, and the sea into fairy-tale-like scenes, evoking warm memories and hope. Together, their landscapes retrace the memories of yesterday and the familiarity of today, shining a light on hope for the future. We hope that this exhibition offers a meaningful moment to confront the present and imagine a hopeful tomorrow through the works of these two artists.

title: In Silence, the Resonanace Remains
short_description: The primary subjects of this exhibition are Buddhist statues and natural objects. Among them, the artist has depicted Vairocana Buddha, Bodhisattva statues in the contemplative pose, stone pagodas, and other cultural treasures observed closely over many years. These works are created with ink and brush, capturing the beauty and gentle smile of our national treasures beyond religious boundaries, offering viewers a sense of comfort. The background patchwork drawn with ramie fabric is composed thread by thread, reflecting the artist’s connections and relationships. The exhibition seeks to present experimental works in both materials and technique, extending beyond traditional ink painting.

title: Exhibition POSTER HOUSE
short_description: Experience artistic works by illustrators, designers, and independent publishers—reimagined in the form of posters. Over 200 high-quality pieces are presented in various formats and styles, including paper, fabric, drawing, and risograph prints. Browse the collection and purchase posters from your favorite artists.

title: Jeong Kwan, Kim Hyeju: Unresolved Chapter
short_description: This two-person exhibition features Jeong Kwan and Kim Hyeju, who create works that redefine the craft format through paradoxical and audacious methods, highlighting the limitations of ceramics. This exhibition, which focuses on fresh attempts to break through the boundaries of craft in contemporary art, reveals the limitless potential of craft through the incompleteness of ceramics expressed by the two artists, encouraging a deeper exploration due to their unresolved nature.

title: Somatic Ground - Small Studio Semi
short_description: How does our body operate in an art museum? While gazing at the artworks and walking through the exhibition hall, the viewer's body moves amidst concentration and tension. Nevertheless, when talking about viewing, the body rarely appears. The exhibition pays attention to the 'body', which is easily overlooked within the art museum experience in this way. An interlude is originally music played between acts in an opera or play, changing the atmosphere and preparing for the transition to the next scene. Like an interlude, the exhibition is situated amidst the journey of viewing, providing a buffer time to relax the body and tune the senses.

title: Walpurgis Night: THE WITCHES FROM KOREA
short_description: With Walpurgis Night, the festival of witches, as the subject, we will shed light on the genealogy of Korean feminist art and explore changes in the Korean feminist art between the 1st and 4th generations, looking back on the changed social image through critical mind. Pioneers of Korean feminist art and new artists meet, sympathize and solidarity through the history of changes in Korean society dwelling in their works, in 2023. We publicize Korean feminist art to the public living in the present, and through feminist art between various generations, we want to open a meeting place that can promote a sense of solidarity.

title: Goto·Sebit Tourist Information Center
short_description: The Goto·Sebit Tourist Information Center is within the underground public pedestrian transfer connecting Express Bus Terminal Station (Exit G2) to Banpo Hangang Park. This center is staffed by professional tourist interpreters who offer services in English, Chinese, and Japanese, ensuring smooth assistance for international visitors. Inside, you'll find a variety of tourist information booklets, WOWPASS devices for foreign tourists, coin exchangers, and kiosks. The nearby Goto Mall is a transportation and shopping hub, providing a wide range of activities and easy access to Banpo Hangang Park. For travel plan inquiries, please visit the center for convenient assistance and help schedule your itinerary.

title: UAUS 14th Pavilion Exhibition  Ask Nature : Biomimicry
short_description:
'Ask Nature: Biomimicry' is an exhibition centered on architectural wisdom inspired by nature. Students from 26 universities nationwide gather to explore the potential of sustainable architecture through architectural experiments that imitate natural forms, behaviors, and systems.

This exhibition goes beyond a simple display of works. It investigates and interprets the principles and orders inherent in nature from an architectural perspective, proposing a new architectural language through the experimental structure of a pavilion. It also explores the public value of architecture and the potential for communication through interaction with citizens.

Moreover, students take full initiative in every stage, from design to production, construction, and dismantling, making the exhibition a laboratory for directly experiencing and sharing the interconnections between architecture and nature, city and environment.

title: World Heritage and Capital Fortifications of Hanyang
short_description:
2025 Seoul City Wall Museum First Half Special Exhibition


World Heritage and Capital Fortifications of Hanyang


The "Capital Fortifications of Hanyang" were built to defend Hanyang, the capital of Joseon. While many fortresses of historical heritage in many contemporary cities have disappeared due to urban development, Hanyang's capital fortifications have maintained their form to the present day, preserving both tangible and intangible historical value. To promote and conserve these values worldwide, Seoul City, Gyeonggi Province, Goyang City, and the National Heritage Administration are collaborating to inscribe Hanyang's capital fortifications on the World Heritage List.


This exhibition examines the meaning of UNESCO World Heritage, the World Heritage Convention and its operating bodies, the World Heritage inscription process, and the international value of Hanyang's capital fortifications, aiming to explore how Hanyang's capital fortifications are progressing from being solely Korea's heritage to becoming heritage for the entire world.

title: Gathering Vibrance
short_description: The special exhibition "Gathering Vibrance" at the Samgaksan Geumam Museum of Art showcases the aspirations of women during the Joseon Dynasty through the works of two female artists, Jeong Myoung-jo and Choi Yoon-ha, each presenting their interpretation in different genres.Jeong Myoung-jo expresses the back profile of women wearing traditional Hanbok in hyperrealistic style. As a university student,Jeong began drawing the charm of traditional garments at a Hanbok shop near her school. Choi Yoon-ha (Maison de Yoon) presents jewelry pieces that reinterpret traditional elements with a modern twist. The artist has created Hanbok accessories for K-pop idols such as IU, BLACKPINK's Rosé, and NMIXX's Seolyoon.During the Joseon Dynasty, a Confucian society with distinct gender roles and rigid class divisions, women were expected to minimize exposure. In the Yeongjo and Jeongjo periods, hair accessories were banned due to a royal decree. The only areas where women could express their femininity and adorn themselves were their styled hair and accessories worn on their clothes.This exhibition aims to reflect women’s instinct for adornment and their desires for wealth, fertility, and happiness through their decorative choices.

title: [S-TCEP] 2023 Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra: Shostakovich Concerto
short_description:
Violinist, Patricia Kopatchinskaja, takes to the Korean stage for the first time, alongside conductor, Ingo Metzmacher, following the unfortunate cancelation of their initial show due to the pandemic. The concerto is set to be held on March 10 and 11 at the Lotte Concert Hall located on the eighth floor of the Lotte World Mall. Brace yourselves for a powerful showing from these two exceptional artists.







※ This content is provided by the S-TCEP (Seoul - Tourism, Culture, Exhibitions, Performing Arts) Alliance.

title: Yeouinaru Station Runner Station
short_description: The Yeouinaru Station Runner Station is a complex cultural space where existing subway station space has been innovatively reinterpreted to create a new form of living space in the city center, featuring a Runners Base Camp for Han River runners. It is equipped with lockers, changing rooms, powder rooms, shoe sanitizers, and InBody measurement devices, and provides real-time running event information, weather updates, and running course information on media boards. Storage lockers are located on basement levels 1 and 2, and installation of a smartphone application is required.

title: BEOM: Ji Min Sun Exhibition
short_description: Focusing on the representative works of artist Ji Min Sun, who has combined the symbolism of traditional folk paintings (Minhwa) with modern sensibilities, this exhibition modernly reinterprets symbols in folk paintings under the theme of 'BEOM' (Tiger). In particular, it has expressed human emotions and narratives of life through the tiger motif. While maintaining this pictorial language, this exhibition has realized the three-dimensional texture of the artworks through SIMULAQUE's unique "Physical Art-Tech (UV 3D print)" technology.

title: Sonic Planet – Hertz and Dough
short_description:
Since 2017, the Buk-Seoul Museum of Art has been experimenting with flexible communication with audiences through its Vacant Space Project, displaying artworks in spaces other than exhibition halls.

The 2025 vacant space exhibition “Sonic Planet – Hertz and Dough” continues this approach, inviting visitors to sense both their own sounds and those of surrounding beings, and to feel the resonance of coexistence.

The participating artist team Hertz and Dough is also the first artist group to launch the museum’s “Artist Research” program, which explores the ways in which artistic inquiry and contemplation expand within the creative process. They perceive the world through sound and develop their own narratives by studying the act of listening itself. In the world of sound, where technology and ecology, human and non-human, space and environment intersect, they are asking questions about what and how we hear and understand. 

The exhibition proposes the following attitudes to create different access points to connect with each other through sound. First, rather than looking for more, close your eyes and listen to the sounds of the here and now. Second, establish listening as an active act rather than mere reception; and third, move beyond an anthropocentric auditory experience to a more sensitive observation of the diverse sounds of the planet. Through these approaches, the soundscape that surrounds us may be transformed into a complex “sonic planet”a sensory field of sound environments.

title: Someday, we will be in the same.
short_description:
Artist Choi Jae-Yi continues her work under the belief that the deeply personal is also universal. After enduring a period of illness, she found inspiration in the sight of trees lying exposed to the sea breeze in Jeju, using this as a motif in her work. She began to express the contrast between wind and home—where wind represents abstraction and freedom, and home serves as a final point of emotional expression. Through her work, she engages in an internal dialogue, finding both emotional liberation and healing in the act of creation. 

On the other hand, artist Hwang Ho-Seok jots down striking words or ideas for his work. He reflects on them over time, creating stories and images, often choosing photos he has previously taken. He then discovers and expresses unnoticed details or emotions within these photos. He seeks to translate intimate feelings drawn from everyday life and relationships into his paintings, hoping viewers will find healing through this expression. 

Through Roland Barthes' concept of nuance, the works of these two artists encompass more than mere differences; they depict emotions in distinct ways, allowing for varied interpretations. This divergence shapes the mood of each piece, offering viewers a more profound emotional connection. Despite their contrasting motifs and approaches, both artists share a common purpose: to explore emotional healing. They invite viewers to freely interpret and find solace in their works, subtly whispering that each person can find personal healing within the relationship between their everyday lives and surroundings. 

– Curator Sim Da-Seul

title: Art Cube 2R2
short_description: Art Cube 2R2 is a complex exhibition space operated by Art Token Inc., an art content solution company. It serves as an exhibition platform that expands and connects digitally generated art into offline exhibition experiences. Based on the convergence of art and technology, it is designed to allow visitors to multi-dimensionally experience works of various genres, such as painting, drawing, installation, media art, and digital content, within a single space. Furthermore, as a space of connection bridging the inside and outside of boundaries, it oversees the flow of contemporary art where the past and present, reality and imagination, and the local and global intersect. By connecting domestic and international artists, content, technologies, and platforms, it expands the possibilities of exchange. Going beyond a simple exhibition hall, it experiments with the physical realization of digital art and new distribution methods for art content. Through these endeavors, it continuously explores new possibilities for art appreciation and exhibition formats, presenting a new gallery model reflecting contemporary art and media environments.

title: 《The Mindscape ; Encounters of the Third Kind (Imaginary Landscape: Encounter with the Unknown)》
short_description: This exhibition presents the works of three artists who explore the unknown world through "imaginary landscapes" that unfold personal and social emotions encountered in various spaces as reflections of the artist's inner flow. The scenes remembered from past times and places are reimagined in a dreamlike manner, where the subtle emotions felt at that moment intersect with the current state of consciousness. This transforms everyday spaces into unknown worlds, adding a lyrical resonance to ordinary landscapes. The exhibition, featuring paintings and photographs by the participating artists, delves into how the theme of "liberalization from restriction"—the most fundamental human pursuit of escaping the familiar to dream of new worlds—is perceived in our contemporary lives.

title: 2025 BIBI 1st WORLD TOUR ［EVE］ IN SEOUL
short_description: Please check the Interpark Ticket website for more details

title: Dilkusha
short_description: Dilkusha, meaning "a joyful heart" in Persian, is the historical name given to the residence of Albert W. Taylor and Mary L. Taylor. The Taylor family commenced construction in 1923 and completed Dilkusha in 1924. Following a devastating fire in 1926, the structure was rebuilt in 1930. After the Japanese colonial authorities deported the Taylor couple in 1942, the property was briefly managed by Albert's younger brother, William W. Taylor. In 1959, the house was purchased by lawmaker Cho Kyeong-kyu of the Liberal Party. However, following the forfeiture of his assets to the state in 1963, ownership of Dilkusha transferred to the government. Left neglected for decades, the property severely deteriorated and lost its original form. In 2005, Professor Kim Ik-sang of Seoile University located the estate at the request of Albert’s son, Bruce T. Taylor. In 2006, Bruce finally returned to his childhood home after 66 years, bringing Dilkusha back to public prominence.

title: NUMAZ WHOLESALE WEEK
short_description: Character pop artist Lemar Kim and hop-funk artist Yakgwa present innovative works, seamlessly navigating between physical and digital mediums. Choreographer Kim Se-ryung and painter Hwang So-young also create their works with entirely different palettes and methods, focusing on canvas works. This exhibition, through collaborations across various arts like visual arts, digital art, and dance, creates a harmonious blend of seemingly incompatible works. Through the "NUMAZ WHOLESALE WEEK" exhibition, we invite you to experience the distinctive works and collaborations of NUMAZ members firsthand. The NUMAZ WHOLESALE WEEK exhibition will run until August 27th.

title: Sketching Heart's Delight
short_description:
The special exhibition "Sketching Heart's Delight" at Dilkusha is a collaborative project with Urban Sketchers Seoul, consisting of four themes: 'The Red Brick House in Eunhaengnamugol, Dilkusha' capturing Dilkusha's exterior, 'Golden Bouquet Illuminating Dilkusha' featuring the symbolic ginkgo tree, 'The Colors of Joy' depicting the living rooms on the first and second floors of Dilkusha, and 'Dilkusha, Home of an Independence Activist' portraying Albert's independence activities.

For this exhibition, Dilkusha held 'Dilkusha Day' three times last year, and 64 out of 176 drawings of either the interior, exterior, or meaning of Dilkusha submitted by 122 Urban Sketchers Seoul members who were invited to Dilkusha through pre-registration are on display.

In addition, there is a video space showcasing 'Dilkusha Day' moments, an area displaying sketchers' art supplies, and an experience space called 'My Drawing of Dilkusha' with paper and art supplies prepared for visitors to participate in the exhibition by drawing Dilkusha themselves.

title: Warm&Cool ART Collection Exhibition
short_description: Superior Gallery presents the Warm & Cool ART Collection exhibition by artists Kwon Kyung-yeop, Kim In, and Brian Kims, who communicate with cold reason and warm sensibility. In his works, Kwon Kyung-yeop conveys healing experiences and hopes for life, portraying the relationship between humans and animals and harmony with nature. Artist Kim In creates cheerful images by repeating and rhythmically arranging familiar images in a new combination. Meanwhile, artist Brian Kims expresses emotions and thoughts through over 100 characters depicting various appearances and behaviors. Experience the Warm & Cool artworks brimming with new discoveries and pure emotions at Superior Gallery. The Warm & Cool ART Collection exhibition is until May 27th.

title: ICON: The Chair Series
short_description: This exhibition, 《ICON: The Chair Series》, intensively showcases the world of painting that Kwon Young-sool has built. Inside the chairs, cities and architecture, music and landscapes, traces of humanity, and forms of nature are mixed together. The different images float freely like scenes in a dream, yet they are connected within a single organic order. Past memories, present sensations, and future imaginations coexist within a single canvas, allowing the viewer to experience various layers of time by following the form of the chair.

title: SeMA Anthology: Ten Orders
short_description: In celebration of the 10th anniversary of its opening, the Seoul Museum of Art presents an exhibition titled "SeMA Anthology: Ten Orders," featuring ten artists who envision new landscapes transcending the past and future. Rather than organizing the present through an archival listing of the Seoul Museum of Art's trajectory, this exhibition attempts to actively sense the coming time by focusing on imagination as an active, creative act that connects the past and the future. To explore how the formal and thematic essence of imagination connects with art, the exhibition examines the unique grammar inherent in the language of imagination and replaces it with the particularity embedded in contemporary artworks. This will serve as a kind of aesthetic exploration and creative experiment about how our present embraces the past, anticipates the future, and pioneers the constantly emerging unknown world.

title: Korea lnt’l EDUCATION WEEK 2023
short_description: From August 10 to 12, 2023, for 3 days, the 2023 Korea lnt’l EDUCATION WEEK will be held on the 1st floor, Hall A of COEX mall. The expo is organized by the Korean Association of Elementary, Middle, and High School Principals, the Korean Association of Middle School Principals, and the E Korea lnt’l EDUCATION WEEK Organizing Committee. Hosted by Global Biz Market and co-hosted by the Korea Smart Edutech Cooperative Association, the education-specific exhibition will hold an education professional workshop and conference on the topics of presenting the direction of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Edutech education and practical applications in actual classrooms, together with education experts/organizations and AI specialists.

title: 2026 The 2nd Garak Table Concert
short_description: The 2nd Garak Table Concert, where you can enjoy music and relaxation together in the heart of the city, will be held at Haneul Park on the 3rd floor of the Garak Mall sales building. Along with musical performances of various genres such as indie pop, country, and fusion Gugak, we plan to present a sensuous weekend cultural space with the unique leisure of Garak Mall through diverse contents including a food market, book picnic, and kids' zone. Especially encouraged by the favorable response from many visitors last year, we have prepared a special time where music, food, and relaxation harmonize with an even more expanded program and space direction this year. We invite you to Haneul Park at Garak Mall, where the 2nd Garak Table Concert, a midsummer night rooftop concert with everyday leisure, will be held.

title: 《Jae-Eun Choi : Promise (Where Being Be)》
short_description: 《Promise (Where Being Be)》 presents the concept of mutual coexistence beyond linguistic meaning, recalling the interconnected solidarity of nature that has traversed time and space long before civilization. Just as the origins of the words promise and bind are intertwined, beings have long been entangled like threads and have existed together through vast stretches of time. The exhibition consists of five subthemes Lucy, Warning Bell, Microcosm, Subtle Name, and Natural State Beyond Boundaries, along with an archive that surveys the artist’s major body of work. By summoning the long timeline shared by early humans and ourselves, the exhibition reveals the responsibility humanity must bear for the destruction of nature and life, evoking the possibility of coexistence through bleached coral, life in the Demilitarized Zone, and disappearing wildflowers, and leading toward the path of ecological solidarity proposed by the artist. Amid rapidly changing global environments, 《Jae-Eun Choi : Promise (Where Being Be)》 asks what kind of life we should aspire to.

title: Seochon Hanok Village
short_description: To the west of Gyeongbokgung Palace is a village where various middle-class officials such as court nobles and government officials lived during the Joseon Dynasty. This neighborhood has long been guarded by old shops and hanok houses, along with newly emerged stores, creating a harmonious blend of unique charm and simplicity that can be felt.

title: Alchemy of Souls: Light and Shadow Immersive Media Art Exhibition
short_description:
Alchemy of Souls: Light and Shadow Immersive Media Art Exhibition, based on the original drama of the same name, will be held at Gallery Gwanghwa from June 15th to October 15th. The exhibition reimagines ten major themes from the drama, including the main storyline and the characters Jung Jin Gak and Jin Yo Won, through media art that provides an interactive space for visitors.

In this exhibition, various themed experiential scenarios, including the world of the drama "Alchemy of Souls" in the country of Daeho, and the four seasons of the world in Daeho, are arranged to allow visitors to experience the universe of "Alchemy of Souls” directly. Using holograms, projection mapping, and media art that utilize light and graphics, the exhibition conveys a dreamlike and elegant depiction of Daeho, the world of "Alchemy of Souls," and the fusion of souls. It creates a sensation of being the protagonist simply by standing there, immersing visitors in the experience.

When purchasing a ticket, you will receive a barcode that can be used in the exhibition hall. After the viewing, you can scan the barcode in the kiosk to check the contents you have experienced.

title: Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul
short_description:
'Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul' is a cultural journey to experience Louis Vuitton's travel, craftsmanship, and heritage, serving as an immersive exhibition illuminating the brand's legacy.

It is a space that unravels the philosophy of travel and the creative heritage that the Maison has continued for over 170 years into a single narrative. The story, starting from trunk production in 1854, introduces the journey of Louis Vuitton's development into a global cultural house through thematic spaces. Following the exhibition route leading from the 5th floor down to the 4th floor, the narrative of Louis Vuitton's creation and travel unfolds naturally.

The exhibition consists of a total of 12 spaces, unfolding the brand's history starting with trunks, the origin of the monogram, the artisan's workshop, the evolution of iconic bags, and Louis Vuitton's cultural narrative expanded through art and design collaborations, music, and fashion, just like a single journey.

title: Seongsu Ready Young drug store
short_description: Ready Young drug store is a premium pharmacy where you can experience specialized pharmaceuticals suggested by pharmacists, carefully selected K-beauty cosmetics, and highly functional derma cosmetics available only at pharmacies, all in one place. We precisely analyze your skin condition with state-of-the-art AI technology and recommend cosmetics suitable for your skin type.

title: 2025 Donhwamun Night of the Bright Moon II: Korean Masks, Faces Filled with Laughter and Excitement Exhibition
short_description: The mask that contains the life and spirit of our people, and the stage of traditional mask dance filled with laughter and satire. A vibrant performance unfolds, where lively dance and exciting rhythms come together to express the beauty of tradition. A time to find the laughter hidden behind the mask and discover our true face. You are invited to the delightful story told by Korean masks.

title: Bae Yun Hwan Solo Exhibition 《Deep Diver》
short_description:
Those who dive deep underwater know how to move toward the light.

Space K Seoul, Kolon’s cultural and artistic sharing space, hosts the solo exhibition 《Deep Diver》 by Bae Yun Hwan (b. 1983). The artist peels away the familiar layers of light and guides us into the achromatic world of black. That darkness is not emptiness, but rather a space of dense contemplation. His work abandons color and even minimizes form, forcing the gaze inward, deeper and deeper. Just as a diver holds their breath and enters stillness, viewers are invited to halt their thoughts before the canvas, open their senses, and confront its depth.


Bae Yun Hwan is an artist who begins with personal experiences and expands his vision to global issues. In his creative process, he unravels not only individual anguish but also the disintegration of communities and the signs of the times such as disasters and wars, expressed through his own allegorical techniques, thereby leading contemporary painting. This exhibition unfolds his narratives more broadly and deeply through works across various genres, including painting, drawing, installation, and video.

title: Rembrandt to Goya, Master of European Painting from the Toledo Museum of Art
short_description:
Where you can directly encounter original paintings by European masters such as Rembrandt, Goya, Jacques-Louis David, and Turner, will be held at the ALT.1 Museum in The Hyundai Seoul from March 21 to July 4, 2026.

This exhibition is a large-scale classic painting exhibition that carefully selects and presents over 50 paintings by masters who led the flow of Western art history from the mid-16th century to the mid-19th century, among the representative collections of the Toledo Museum of Art located in Ohio, USA. You can observe in one place the works that formed major turning points in the history of European painting, from the post-Renaissance period to Baroque, Rococo, Neoclassicism, and Romanticism.

The exhibition is composed of a total of 6 sections, structured so that visitors can also examine the social and cultural roles that painting has played within the history of European art. Visitors can broadly experience not only the pictorial perfection of the works but also the historical background, philosophical context, patronage structures, and the flow of the art market contained within them.

This exhibition, which introduces the European painting collection of the Toledo Museum of Art with a history of over 100 years to Korea, is expected to be a special opportunity to directly verify the flow of Western art history and the artistic achievements of the masters as a blockbuster exhibition centered on original paintings.

title: Mixed Orchestra 26
short_description:
Highly recommended for these individuals!


-Tourists who want to experience the depth of Korean culture beyond K-pop.

-Couples/friends/family travelers who want to make a night in Seoul special.

-Those who previously found traditional Korean music difficult but are looking for a 'fun' introductory performance.


Performance Introduction


〈Mixed Orchestra 26〉 is a performance that preserves the roots of traditional Korean music while boldly expanding it with contemporary sensibilities. Over the rich scale of a Korean traditional music orchestra, the piri and gayageum clearly draw the textures of tradition, and beatboxing adds rhythm and energy, completing an attractive sound where tradition and modernity coexist.

This performance is a stage where you can encounter the elaborate melodies, improvisation, and deep emotions of Korean music all in one place. Beyond the familiar travel courses, it will be a live experience that will make you remember the night in Seoul in the most Korean way.

title: The Persistence of Self
short_description:
The story of Kim Young-sik, a master potter recognized as an intangible cultural heritage of Gyeongsangbuk-do, traces back to the Joseon Dynasty. According to Hajae Diary, written by Ji Kyushik, an official supplier of various wares to the royal court and government offices, Kim’s great-grandfather, Kim Bi-an, constructed a Mangdaengi kiln in 1903, confirming Kim’s lineage as a descendant of royal porcelain artisans. For nearly 300 years, the family has upheld the tradition of Joseon white porcelain, and Kim Young-sik, as the eighth-generation master, brings a unique artistic "persistence" to his craft.
The “Persistence of Self” exhibition showcases Kim’s dedication to the tradition of Joseon white porcelain. Through his resolute commitment, he creates hard and beautiful porcelain fired at high temperatures. This exhibition highlights his blue-and-white porcelain's purity and understated elegance, born from his unwavering craftsmanship. Bonsai plants, radiating a vibrant energy, are also displayed to enhance his artistic vision. The exhibition celebrates the depth and value of Korean cultural heritage, sustained through one man’s determination and dedication.

title: 2024 Delight Seoul
short_description:
A digital content media art exhibition called 'delight,' which is enjoying popularity in London, dynamically reinterprets the past and future of Seoul. The Delight exhibition has reinterpreted the past and future of Seoul, metaphorically represented the city’s stories, and expressed these dynamic aspects through creative media art.


The Delight exhibition began in Seoul and has since been presented in various cities worldwide including New York, Washington D.C., Paris, Mexico City, Dubai, and Tokyo. It has received numerous accolades and positive reviews. As of November and December 2023, it also holds the record for ranking first in ticket sales for its exhibition in London.
In 2023, marking its third anniversary and a standalone exhibit in London, the Delight exhibition returns to Gallery Gwanghwa in Gwanghwamun. The exhibition features a refreshed arrangement and staging of over 22 varieties of content, including both acclaimed existing works and newly created pieces.
