title: From dawn to dusk - National Museum Stockholm Collection
short_description:
This exhibition, jointly curated by the National Museum of Sweden and MyArt Museum, showcases 75 masterpieces by renowned artists representing Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. This unique exhibition commemorates the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between South Korea and Sweden. 
Featuring the collection from the National Museum of Sweden, it offers a unique opportunity to experience the charm of Nordic Impressionism and the distinctive sensibilities of Nordic art, which have not been previously accessible in Korea. The aim is to promote the relatively unfamiliar Nordic and Swedish art in Korea through this exhibition, shedding light on the spirit and footsteps of young Swedish artists who have contributed to the advancement of art and the diversity of international art.

title: Seo-Seoul Museum of Art Inaugural Special Exhibition 《Our Time Begins Here》
short_description:
《Our Time Begins Here》 is an exhibition that illuminates the construction process of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art and the narrative of time engraved in the southwestern region (and its people) as a 'record of memories'. Through the resonance of works that reflect the scenes of West Seoul remaining amidst the processes of creation and extinction, and the time differences that occur in between using the language of art, it constructs the memories of the construction of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art, its surrounding time, places, and community into a multi-layered structure. By weaving together the diverse layers of relationships surrounding the museum—from the people who passed through the birth of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art together, to the region and future generations—under the name of 'us', it seeks to explore the meaning of 'time' that new media art possesses within the accumulated narratives.


You can encounter the artworks in niche spaces at address 0, which deviate from existing exhibition categories, such as the museum learning space, lobby, loading dock shutters, and grass plaza. Now, as the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art takes its first breath, we ask for your great interest in our time that will unfold 'here'.

title: National Theater Madangnori <Hong Gildong Is Coming>
short_description: A refreshing blow to the world, K-Hero Hong Gildong is on his way. Hong Gildong, the first hero of Joseon who will overturn a corrupt world. The best performance of the year end and New Year season, the National Theater Madangnori. This time it is Hong Gildong. Overcoming the sorrow of being born as a concubine’s child and becoming the leader of the Hwalbindang, Hong Gildong delivers a thrilling strike of justice against a fallen world. A spectacular stage that combines duplication techniques, gliding, acrobatics, and magic, along with witty dialogue, refreshing satire, and delightful humor. Madangnori <Hong Gildong Is Coming> blends laughter, satire, action, and catharsis into one joyful celebration. A festive scene like a banquet. From children to grandparents, everyone is invited to enjoy an exciting time this winter at the National Theater.

title: Kyungguksa
short_description: Gyeongguksa Temple, nestled on the eastern slopes of Samgaksan (now known as Bukhansan), is a historic temple founded in the late Goryeo period. Renowned for its scenic mountain surroundings and fresh spring water, it attracts many visitors. The temple complex has 17 buildings, including Geungnakbojeon (Hall of Supreme Bliss), Yeongsanjeon, Myeongbujeon, Gwaneumjeon, and Sibangseonwon. Geungnakbojeon houses the Amitabha Buddha triad, along with wooden Buddhist paintings (designated as Treasure No. 748), Shinjungtaenghwa, and Palsangtaenghwa. Sibangseonwon offers a weekly Sunday meditation session, and the temple also hosts temple stay programs at Hwanheodang and Manwoldang. As one of Seoul's significant temples, Gyeongguksa was frequently visited by former President Syngman Rhee. During his tenure as Vice President, Richard Nixon of the United States visited the temple and later described it as one of his most memorable experiences in his memoirs, even including a photograph of his visit.

title: Exhibition Filling the Heart
short_description:
Superior Gallery will hold a two-person exhibition 《Exhibition Filling the Heart》 by artists Min Yul and Lee Dong Hoon in September 2025. This exhibition seeks to fill the emotional voids forgotten in the fast flow of daily life and portrays an inner journey to discover small, precious moments of happiness and rest.


Artist Min Yul delicately captures moments of tranquility and contemplation found in ordinary sceneries such as wooden chairs, the sky, and the wind, depicting imaginary sanctuaries where one can pause and reflect inwardly. Artist Lee Dong Hoon conveys warmth and leisure of everyday life through his symbolic character “Bruno the Goose,” using concise colors and layered brushstrokes to express emotional depth.


Although different in perspective, both artists capture the essence of emotions that resonate universally, encouraging viewers to reflect on their own hearts and experience small happiness and recharging moments. The exhibition 《Exhibition Filling the Heart》 will run until September 24, 2025.

title: JW Lee Jong Ho Foundation Exhibition for Artists with Disabilities : JW Art Awards
short_description: The JW Lee Jong Ho Foundation, based on the philosophy of respecting life and practicing sharing, has operated an art awards program for artists with disabilities since 2015, discovering and supporting their talents. In this continuing journey, we invite you to pause for a moment in the exhibition hall and experience the perspectives and stories contained in the artworks. The world of creation approaches with originality and profound resonance, offering new viewpoints on life and presenting meaningful questions.

title: SeMA Museum of Photography
short_description:
The SeMA Museum of Photography, newly opened in Changdong, Dobong-gu, Seoul, is a branch of the Seoul Museum of Art and the first and only public art museum in Korea specializing in photography, established after 

more than a decade of preparation. The museum plans to continue diverse activities to become a new center for photographic art in Korea and 

Asia through creative and experimental exhibitions and programs encompassing the entire photography culture and in-depth research, collection, and preservation activities.

Notably, the museum is equipped with facilities where visitors can experience the influence and artistic value of photography, including exhibition

 halls, education rooms, darkrooms, a photo library, and a photobook café for educational programs covering all age groups.

The architecture was designed by Austrian architect Mladen Jadric (representative of Jadric Architektur ZTGmbH) and 1990 Urban Architecture 

(representative Yoon Geun-ju), who visualized and implemented the pixel of photography, which is a picture drawn with light.

title: Healswing Wangsimni(K-Swing)
short_description: The Healswing in Wangsimni is Seoul's only extreme sports ride that offers a 360-degree rotation, providing an exhilarating experience for all ages. As the world’s first and only 360-degree rotating swing, the Healswing can be enjoyed in a variety of ways, including team-building battle games. With a robust five-layer safety system, it guarantees a secure adventure, and its rooftop location on the 4th floor adds an extra thrill by offering stunning views of the Seoul skyline. After experiencing the Healswing, visitors can indulge in authentic K-Food at nearby hotspots like Hanyang-dong Food Alley, Wangsimni Gopchang Alley, and Majang-dong Hanwoo Alley.

title: The Depth of the Characters, 1.5mm
short_description: Based on the Seoul Museum of History's 'Seoul Future Heritage Records' survey, this exhibition illuminates Seoul's seal shop culture closely connected to citizens' daily lives. By displaying materials used and sold at seal shops and seal makers located in Seoul, it provides an opportunity to examine Seoul's living culture deeply.

title: From Impressionism to Early Modernism: Collectors of Light – From The Metropolitan Museum of Art
short_description: The National Museum of Korea presents the special exhibition <From Impressionism to Early Modernism, Collectors of Light>, featuring the collection of American financier Robert Lehman, including French paintings from the late nineteenth century Impressionism to early twentieth century Modernism. This exhibition showcases eighty one works of painting and drawing from the Robert Lehman Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, including Auguste Renoir’s Two Girls at the Piano, Vincent van Gogh’s The Flowering Orchard, and Mary Cassatt’s Spring: Margot Standing in the Garden.

title: You, As You Are - SimLee Da Eun
short_description: This exhibition is a story about an imaginary being, 'Mr. Cat A'. Mr. Cat A, a small being in the city, wanders around the Buk-Seoul Museum of Art today as well. The artist installs a real-time audio streaming device around the museum area and flows the sound into the structure of Lounge 3. When you turn the handle, the friction sound of the cogwheel and cotton cloth mixes with the real-time environmental sound of the surrounding area, and familiar everyday sounds gradually turn into unfamiliar sounds. Your movement is connected to the circular screen in Lounge 2. After witnessing the moment your movement overlaps with the cat's in the screen, viewers unknowingly step onto the travel path that Mr. Cat A left around Nowon-gu. Passing the wondrous moment of witnessing your movement overlapping with the cat's trajectory on the screen, the  composed of drawers unfolds before your eyes. Opening the drawers, you will be greeted by the vivid texture of the soil he must have passed, the bird feathers he loved the most, the small pebbles rolling by the water, and finally, the complete life of a single cat.

title: Strange K-Beauty: Mom's Drawer
short_description:
B the B is a permanent exhibition space that curates the charming beauty brands of Seoul with its own unique sensibility. At B the B Downtown, it showcases unique collaboration pop-ups that combine popular brands leading Seoul's beauty trends with the latest trends.

Currently ongoing, 'Strange K-Beauty: Mom's Drawer' is an experiential story exhibition designed to allow children to experience K-beauty easily and enjoyably from their own perspective. Beyond simple viewing, it is a children-tailored K-beauty experiential exhibition where they can explore inside their mother's Drawer and directly create cosmetics.


1. Story-type Exhibition Viewing


- Experience objects and photo zones under the theme of 'Mom's Drawer'

- Watch K-beauty and cosmetic story videos tailored to children's eye levels


2. Experiential Content


-Making My Own Cosmetic (Compact): An experiential activity where children creatively make cosmetics by directly selecting colors and elements.

-Treasure Hunt Mission: A participatory activity searching for hidden treasures within the exhibition space.

-Coloring Wall Play: An activity where children can freely color and play.

title: Unwinding Mind
short_description:
Do you have something that represents you? For artist Lee Dong-hoon, Bruno serves that role. Bruno stands as a representative of the artist and a protagonist in the world he wishes to express. In this exhibition, Bruno is depicted as more peaceful and safe than ever before. We encapsulate this peace and safety with the word ‘rest.’ In response to the question 'What is rest?', author Lee Ki-joo describes it as 'a time to gather energy in life' in his book <Universal Words>. Nowadays, everyone prides themselves on living a busy life. "However, isn’t living without true rest like ignoring the low battery warning on your phone, knowing it will soon run out, and feeling anxious?" Through his paintings, the artist seeks to remind us of the importance of rest in our lives. Moreover, he emphasizes the need for purity, sincerity, and even childhood innocence as human beings. Through depictions of daily life or stories of rest, the artist aims to convey happiness, peace, and comfort of the mind using the medium of painting. Did you find yourself in the image of Bruno in the artwork? If so, you are already someone who fully relaxes your mind. If not, then we can find it together right now. We hope your hearts find complete rest at Samseyoung Galary.
Curator Shim Da-seul

title: Han Unsung Collection 《Between Image & Reality》
short_description: Seoul Museum of Art will hold the Han Unsung Collection Donation Planned Exhibition 《Between Image & Reality》 from December 9, 2025 to March 22, 2026. This exhibition aims to examine the lifelong artistic exploration and experimentation of the artist based on 195 prints donated to Seoul Museum of Art by artist Han Unsung in 2023 and the museum collection.

title: Kim Jihye : PADO
short_description:
*Performance Details
A showcase for the first studio album *Wave* by traditional percussionist and composer Kim Ji-hye, blending Korean traditional music and jazz. The album features eight tracks inspired by natural phenomena related to the sea, such as waves, sea fog, and starlight. The performance combines traditional Korean percussion, daegeum, alto saxophone, piano, and bass, presenting a bold and diverse musical exploration.
*Performance Information
- Date & Time: Saturday, November 30, 2024, at 19:00   
- Venue: Veloso, Hongdae  
- Duration: 60 minutes  
- Tickets: Interpark Tickets (https://tickets.interpark.com/goods/24015200)  
- Price: 30,000 KRW (30% discount for Arts Pass holders and students)

title: Kwon Byungjun: I Embrace You
short_description: The Children+ exhibition, an annual showcase at the Seoul Museum of Art's Buk-Seoul Museum of Art, presents a solo exhibition by artist Byungjun Kwon, who has long explored the intersection of technology and art. Based on Kwon's artistic universe, this exhibition focuses on the modalities of symbiosis between technology and humans, and further between non-humans and humans, examining another possibility for diverse beings to coexist together. Through this, it seeks to propose a new sense of inclusion and sharing, and to contemplate the meanings of solidarity and community. The 2026 Children+ exhibition, Byungjun Kwon: You Are in My Heart, is centered around new works visualizing the concept of "a space that embraces children," and is designed with a perspective tailored to children, providing an experience that anyone can easily understand and enjoy.

title: Bathtub & Feather
short_description: In the solo exhibition [Bathtub & Feather], artist Sea Choi showcases works from the participatory upcycling series "Bathtub" and the abstract painting series "Feather," which depicts the companionship of God and angels using the motif of feathers reminiscent of wings. The exhibition includes early and new works from the 'Feather' series, a sculptural painting project that vividly and dynamically portrays the image of feathers with added sculptural elements. Additionally, the exhibition features <Bathtub 5>, a viewer-interactive piece made from repurposed bathtubs and recycled materials, emphasizing sustainability. Visitors can enter or touch the installation and engage their senses of hearing, smell, and touch while exploring the various objects within the work.

short_description:

Concert footage will be uploaded to Arirang TV afterward. 
Join with family, friends, or loved ones to enjoy this unique musical experience!

title: Christian Hidaka: Theatres of the Sky, Skies of the Theatre
short_description: Japanese-British artist Christian Hidaka presents a compelling experience by blending the painting traditions and techniques of East and West. Based on his unique perspective, the exhibition introduces a new visual language that bridges cultural and geographical heritages, creating a vivid and immersive painterly composition. The exhibition includes large-scale murals and showcases Hidaka’s distinctive experiments in painting, rarely seen until now. Notably, the artist integrates Western linear perspective and Eastern three-distance perspective, as well as Renaissance tempera and traditional Asian pigments like seokcheong, all made from natural materials. Through this harmony of East and West, nature and art are brought together on a single canvas. This exhibition aims not only to explore a practical approach to painting for the next generation but also to offer a moment to rediscover our presence and perception of the world. By stepping beyond the square boundaries of a canvas into a nonlinear chronology of imagination, visitors are invited to open the door to a visionary world reminiscent of ancient cave murals.

title: A Stroll Through Records: Seoul’s Parks
short_description: The exhibition "A Stroll Through Records: Seoul's Parks" showcases over 90 related records, highlighting Seoul's green space policies, stories of its prominent parks, park records categorized by keywords, and photographs of Seoul's parks taken by residents. Part 1, "The Path of Seoul's Parks," showcases the historical evolution of Seoul's park and green space policies through various documents, blueprints, photos, and videos. Part 2, "Parks Through Records," delves into the histories of notable parks like Namsan Park and Hyochang Park, utilizing records preserved by the Seoul Archives. Part 3, "Park Records Through Keywords," investigates the history and policies of parks, focusing on themes such as children, ecology, and urban regeneration. Additionally, the exhibition features 20 photos collected from a public event, allowing residents to share their personal memories of Seoul's parks.

title: The Kim In Soon Collection <Rise Up for Life>
short_description:
Rise Up for Life explores Kim In Soon’s artistic engagement with the theme of women. Her feminist perspective originates from the longstanding trials and jubilations of the female experience. Kim believed that women's robust will and life energy are pivotal in steering humanity toward a future marked by equality and brightness. The exhibition is structured in three sections, featuring 20 works and accompanying archives. 
[1] The first section, “As Being a Woman,” examines how the narratives of women, often marginalized and erased in historical and contemporary times, are reconstructed in art.  
[2] The second section, “Grasping Beauty,” observes the resilience of women who have triumphed over adversities and the inherent femininity of nature that blooms even in desolate environments. 
[3] The final section, “Life, a Journey of Light,” reflects Kim’s contemplation of women's cosmic and creative value, encapsulating the blessings and joy of procreation in the national art style. 
Through the Kim In Soon Collection, Rise Up for Life aims to enhance interest in Korean feminist art and foster diverse research and discussions.

title: Samgaksan Geumam Art Museum: "Elementary Art Textbooks Unleashed"
short_description: Samgaksan Geumam Art Museum, located in Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul, is hosting an art exhibition for children from July 10 to September 22 to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the Eunpyeong History & Hanok Museum. This diverse exhibition features 18 works from the current revised elementary school art textbooks for grades 3 to 6, including paintings, photographs, installations, sculptures, and media art. The exhibition is divided into six themed spaces. In the first space, "Absorbed into White Paper," visitors can enjoy portraits, nature, landscapes, and still-life paintings that emphasize the material properties of ink and paper. This space features works by Kim Seok, Yoon Byung-rak, Haru.k, and Hong Beam. In the second space, "Click! Capturing Everything," visitors can appreciate uniquely staged photographs that go beyond the traditional functions of photography, featuring works by Koo Sung-yeon, Won Seong-won, and Yoon Jung-mi. In the third space, "The Ever-Reproducing Spirit of the Artist," you will find media artworks by Lee Lee-nam and Lee Jae-hyung that highlight light and movement. The fourth space, "Art by My Side," features three-dimensional paintings by Yoon Suk-nam inspired by daily life events. The fifth space, "Layering Dreams and Hopes," presents oil and acrylic paintings by Kang Ik-jung, Kwon Ki-soo, Kim Duk-ki, Park Jung-yong, and Lee Man-ik, offering inspiration and empathy to many living in modern society. The sixth space, "Wow! The Transformation of Materials," showcases works by Kim Eun-hyun, Kim Hyun-joon, and Ji Yong-ho, who transform everyday materials into the main subjects of their art.

title: River City Water Ski Park
short_description: You can safely enjoy water sports under the guidance of highly qualified instructors certified to teach water skiing and wakeboarding. In addition to inboard boats for wakeboarding and outboard boats for water skiing, the facility is equipped with various water leisure rides such as fly fish, peanut boat, banana boat, and band wagon. It offers a fun and safe environment not only for those who enjoy water sports but also for those who may be somewhat afraid of water or for children.

title: Platform-L Contemporary Art Center
short_description: Platform-L Contemporary Art Center was established to provide audiences with diverse artistic experiences through the creative endeavors of contemporary artists and to contribute to a society enriched with imagination and inspiration. Since its opening in spring 2016, Platform-L has housed facilities including galleries, a live hall, an open courtyard, and lecture rooms. The center presents exhibitions, performances, and video works across a wide range of genres and media.

title: Seoul Science Museum
short_description: The Seoul Science Museum, located in Hageo-dong, Nowon-gu, opened its doors for the first time in Seoul in 2017. It was established to enhance science and cultural facilities in the Gangbuk area, aiming to bridge the gap in science and culture among different regions and promote balanced development across Seoul's districts. As a science experiential facility aimed at youth, it operates six permanent exhibition halls with 221 exhibits and a special rotating exhibition hall featuring exhibits related to the history of objects. It offers various educational programs and events, including family-friendly science-making experiences, group science classes for elementary, middle, and high school students, expert lectures, science experiments, and nature ecology programs that families can enjoy together.

title: The 13th Seoul Mediacity Biennale: Spell – The Art of the Soul
short_description: The 13th edition of the Seoul Mediacity Biennale, titled 'Spell – The Art of the Soul', will take place from August 26 to November 23, 2025, at the Seoul Museum of Art and various venues throughout the city. This biennale features newly commissioned works, recreations, and existing pieces by artists from around the world, drawing inspiration from the occult, mysticism, and spiritual traditions. It aims to offer the biennale as an “alternative technology” that counters the accelerating, rationalist logic of capitalist modernity and the political and intellectual structures that shape our lived experiences. As a “biennale that proposes mediumistic experience,” the exhibition explores the long-standing human desire to connect with worlds beyond conscious life and examines how communication with the spiritual realm has transformed the language and methods of artistic creation.

title: Seonyudo: Silent Coexistence
short_description: Seonyudo Park was once a water purification plant and industrial site, but it has since been transformed into an ecological sanctuary within the city. It is also a living ecosystem where various naturalized plants grow. Naturalized plants are non-native species that have adapted to new environments and now grow independently, quietly leaving traces of life in the ecology and landscape of Seoul. Artist Nahyun focuses on the life stories of migration, settlement, boundaries, and identity of these naturalized plants. In her exhibition Seonyudo: Silent Coexistence, she invites visitors to engage with plants and experience the ongoing flow of transformation.

title: Yoojin Lee Solo Exhibition 《Microclimate Salon – A Dependent Solo Exhibition》
short_description:
Just as the tiny air currents created by mushroom spores can influence the climate, micro-level relationships connect us and create an interdependent ecology.

At the <Dead Tree Post Office> in the exhibition space, you can send a postcard to someone you depend on—or someone who depends on you. In other works, natural objects and imaginary lifeforms are intertwined like collages, revealing unexpected scenes of symbiosis.

Come awaken your dormant "microclimate sense" through encounters with small beings.

title: Play : Crying While Eating Garlic
short_description: Crying While Eating Garlic is a play themed around “the fatigue of coexistence and relationships,” reinterpreting the “Transformation of the Bear and the Tiger into Humans” from the Dangun myth in a contemporary context. The work begins with the question of why the tiger failed to endure “one hundred days in the cave eating only mugwort and garlic.” The play imagines that the reason was the difficulty of coexisting with the bear, and from this perspective, it explores the exhaustion, failures, and subtle efforts of coexistence that we encounter today. The performance is composed not as a single narrative but as a collage of short, repeated scenes.

title: 2024 Seongbuk Newspaper Persona Project: 'Lee Tae-jun: It Seemed Even the Moonlight Was Regrettable to Him' Exhibition
short_description: Lee Tae-jun is recognized as an outstanding novelist in Korean literary history, but he also embodied various personas beyond literature. In the 1930s and 1940s, he was the editor of the prominent literary magazine Munjang, an antique enthusiast, the head of the cultural affairs department at a newspaper, a museum curator, and an art critic. Five creators—Kwon Hye-won (visual arts), Kim Seon-joo (architect), Kim Won-jin (visual arts), Park Sun-min (visual arts), and Layers Lab (book curation)—have brought Lee Tae-jun into the present-day. They immersed themselves in his life and literary works through a preliminary reading session. After more than six months of processing, they each transformed their experiences into creative works. This event is expected to create a space where literature and other forms of art can naturally meet across time, much like how Lee Tae-jun traversed the boundaries of art in the 1930s.

title: Gangnam Fine Craft Art Club Exhibition
short_description: Superior Gallery is proud to present the Gangnam Fine Craft Art Club Exhibition, featuring 14 talented artists: Kim Dong-pyo, Kim Soo-yeon, Kim Jung-woo, Park Sung-geuk, Park Jin-hyuk, Shin Hyun-min, Eun Sung-min, Lee Moon-jung, Jung Young-yoo, Jung Yoo-na, Jung Joon-young, Ji Seung-min, Choi So-jung, and Do Jae-myung. This exhibition, running until July 29, 2024, showcases a new wave in ceramic art. United like a soccer team, these 12 artists share and explore new perspectives and challenges in ceramic art, focusing on tea and crafts. Visitors are invited to enjoy and reflect on the latest currents in crafts, appreciating the aesthetics shaped by clay and time. Experience the beauty and flavor of these artistic works at Superior Gallery.

title: Calendar Exhibition 2024
short_description: Everyday scenery and the unfamiliarity of travel destinations are captured in ingenious and charming characters and typographic art, unfolding across various formats like fabric, posters, mini-books, and notebooks. These creatively designed calendars boast high quality and are produced as limited-edition artworks for the year-end and New Year, quickly becoming a subject of keen interest. This winter, as the New Year approaches, experience young creators' fresh energy and artistic depth exclusively at the Calendar Exhibition.

title: Please Protect Us
short_description: When the roads for cars were removed from Cheonggyecheon, clear water began to flow again, and trees and grasses were planted, attracting fish and birds. Plants are the foundation of all life; a thriving ecosystem depends on their growth. In this exhibition, you’re invited to envision a healthy future where all living beings on Earth support one another and coexist harmoniously.

title: club Seolhwa
short_description: CLUB Seolhwa is an audience-participatory performance that modernly reinterprets Korean traditional fairy tales, folktales, and myths. The audience directly listens to the unfair stories of the tiger, goblin (dokkaebi), Nolbu, and the nine-tailed fox (gumiho), and votes for the most unfairly treated being. The performance proceeds in a new form combining a musical, a club, and a party, and you can watch while moving freely. During the performance, you can communicate with the actors and participate in games and events. After the performance ends, a special salpuri (exorcism) ritual unfolds for the selected being.

title: Goya, the Spanish Master : The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters Exhibition

title: DMAU Project "Init"
short_description:
Director Kim Sung-yong's latest work, "Init," is the first piece of the DMAU (Dance Makes Asia become the Universe) project, planned by the Korea National Contemporary Dance Company based on the aspiration to expand the exchange of Asian dance and lead the world of contemporary dance.
Based on the paradoxical keywords of "complexity within simplicity," "depth within repetition," and "coexistence of unconsciousness and consciousness," “Init” unfolds intricate traces focusing on the unique history of the dancer's body and the essence of dance, together with the top dancers in Asia.
Developed from choreographer Kim Sung-yong's methodology, "Process InIt," aims to evolve, removing barriers between choreographer and dancer, as well as between dancer and audience. Stage design, geared towards highlighting the individualistic movements of the dancers, is crafted in collaboration with Yoo Jae-heon (YouJam Studio), with whom the choreographer has shared a long-standing creative partnership. Meanwhile, musician Yoo Ji-wan of the band “Alligators” joins as the music director to present a more innovative stage.

title: Architecture, Space Time Scenarios
short_description:
The Seoul Museum of Art, including the upcoming new building, operates its branches throughout Seoul in various ways, in line with the flow of time and art trends.
“Architecture, Space Time Scenarios” is an exhibition planned to explore in depth the internal and external changes surrounding the Seoul Museum of Art at this point and to consider the museum's architecture with a focus on ‘time.’
Various discussions regarding architectural deterioration have taken place at national public art museums, including the Seoul Museum of Art, in response to national events and policies since the 1980s.
Furthermore, witnessing urban redevelopment and reconstruction sites altering the city's landscape, this exhibition focuses on the 'life cycle of architecture' implied within art museums' special and symbolic public architecture.

title: Cheongwoon Literature Library
short_description: Cheongwoon Literature Library is Jongno-gu's 16th library, built in hanok style, creating an attractive space for reading, contemplation, and rest. It houses a diverse collection of literary books, focusing on poetry, novels, and essays. Not only does it provide various reading group venues for residents, but it also operates curated exhibitions centered on domestic literary works and authors, as well as humanities lectures and poetry writing classes. This space, where you can feel the ambiance of hanok and nature, won the grand prize at the 2015 Korea Hanok Competition. We hope you will experience the charm of traditional Korean architecture and find solace in nature.

title: Sleep No More Seoul
short_description: For detailed performance information, please visit the Interpark Ticket website.

title: Cheonggyecheon Museum, Twenty
short_description:
The year 2025 marks both the twentieth anniversary of the completion of the Cheonggyecheon restoration and the twentieth anniversary of the opening of the Cheonggyecheon Museum. The Cheonggyecheon Museum began as an exhibition hall to promote the Cheonggyecheon Restoration Project. Ten years after its opening, it was remodeled into a professional museum that comprehensively highlights the history of Cheonggyecheon. Since then, it has actively presented exhibitions, education, research, and cultural events that help citizens better understand Seoul through the history of Cheonggyecheon and its riverside.

This exhibition looks into what the past twenty years of the museum have been filled with through the “Room of a Twenty-Year-Old Youth.” In addition, it provides an opportunity to think about what new horizons Cheonggyecheon, as a historical and cultural content that remembers Seoul, can open in the future.

title: 2025 SPO RIVERSIDE CONCERT
short_description:
The Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra will hold the "2025 Seoul Philharmonic Riverside Concert in Collaboration with the Federation of Korean Industries." Under the baton of Jaap van Zweden, the orchestra’s third music director and a Dutch conductor, the performance will take place against the romantic backdrop of the Han River on a summer night. The concert will feature orchestral music as well as collaborations with cello, trumpet, soprano, and baritone soloists. The performance will culminate in a spectacular fireworks display illuminating the early summer night sky, accompanied by beautiful classical melodies. This event is part of the "80th Anniversary of Liberation Commemoration Project" and is sponsored by the Federation of Korean Industries, which has led efforts to promote free market economy, sound economic development, and globalization.


The riverside concert is free and open to all citizens without prior registration. Entry to the 2,000-seat venue at Hangang Park will be on a first-come, first-served basis. Audience members may also enjoy the music freely around the venue using their own mats and portable chairs. Convenient access to the concert site is available via Subway Line 5, Yeouinaru Station. For those unable to attend in person, the concert will also be livestreamed on the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra’s and Seoul City’s “Live Seoul” YouTube channels.

title: Artist Research: 《Unfinished Flora―Soyo Lee》, 《Time Blooms―Anna Ridler》
short_description: Artist Research: 《Unfinished Flora―Soyo Lee》 and 《Time Blooms―Anna Ridler》, part of the Artist Research series at the Buk Seoul Museum of Art, introduce creative worlds based on artist research meticulously constructed through original approaches that traverse various academic and technological fields. This exhibition was planned to reexamine the academic, artistic, and social value of research conducted by artists. The two artists’ explorations of human constructed systems of knowledge and time intersect with studies of natural orders such as vegetation zones and flowering rhythms and are realized through art. This exhibition, which presents different research based artistic practices addressing the relationship between humans and non humans, aims to step away from human centered global thinking and to awaken a planetary sensibility that imagines possibilities of coexistence among the diverse beings that make up the Earth.

title: "Ilgagi", the first Korean traditional music performance series
short_description:
"Though this short time feels like three autumns, how many autumns will there be in ten days?”


We present the ambiance of a traditional hanbok-style autumn evening, accompanied by the melodies of our traditional Korean musical instruments and classical vocal performances.


“Ujo Dugeo Ilgagi” expresses the anxious feeling of waiting for a beloved one. “As the flowers bloom and fall” conveys the emotions of departing. “Love lies” speaks of a longing that can't be seen even in dreams.


Program

1. As the flowers bloom and fall – Ost. “The Throne” (2015 film)

2. Ujo Dugeo “Ilgagi”

3. Love Lies – Ost. “Love, Lies” (2016 film)

4. Carpenters – Close to you

5. Folk Songs Medley – Arirang / Miryang Arirang / Ballad of the Roasted Chestnut


Refreshments Offered

Enjoy 'Cheong Tae Jeon,” a traditional tea from Jangheung Cheongwandawon with traditional snacks.


Cast

Chae-young Kim (Vocalist), Seok-eon Kim (Flute/Saenghwang), Yun-hee Jang(Haegeum), Min-song Kim (Keyboard), Yu-a Lee (Korean Calligraphy)


Ticket Reservation: https://3d9efgulalc.typeform.com/to/vbu9YNNi

title: Masterpieces of ceramics : Greatness Revealed in the Small
short_description: This opening exhibition of The Prima Art Center unveils for the first time 487 small ceramic pieces collected by the late Lee Woobok, founder of Daewoo Group and a key contributor to Korea’s industrial and economic development. Alongside his corporate career, he deeply appreciated the beauty of Korean art and ceramics and dedicated himself to preserving cultural heritage. He was particularly captivated by the serene and generous beauty of Joseon white porcelain and blue-and-white porcelain, collecting numerous small ceramic works over many years with great care. The exhibition title Sojunghyundae (小中顯大) means “Greatness revealed within smallness.” The 487 artifacts on display include 103 Goryeo celadon pieces, 3 Joseon buncheong ware pieces, and 381 Joseon white porcelain pieces.

title: TOY CON SEOUL
short_description:
As Korea's sole toy fair where you can encounter art toys from around the world in one place, various global artists and IP brands participate directly to become the center of collectible culture. A memorable summer for collectors who have wanted to meet global art toys, as well as those encountering art toys for the first time. This event, held at COEX Seoul, goes beyond a simple exhibition, featuring various collections and lifestyle content, including curated keyrings, a second-hand market, and IP collaboration content.

TOY CON SEOUL keeps pace with the globally growing art toy market, promoting brand collaborations between global brands, distinctive emerging IPs, and local artists. Through this, it values the discovery and nurturing of next-generation artists as a key principle, aiming to cultivate the value of the collectible toy market beyond simple exhibition by bringing together brands, artists, and companies. Additionally, special collaborations between global art toy brands and local artists, limited-edition art toys available only at the event venue, keyring curation, and merchandise are prepared.

title: Innocence of Childhood
short_description: The current exhibition is designed to provide a comprehensive view of the world captured through the eyes of photographers Im In-sik, Jung Bum-tae, Han Young-soo, Hong Soon-tae, and Hwang Heon-man, showcasing their perspectives on children. The exhibition features photographs of children from the 1950s to the 1970s, which can be seen as depicting grandparents' childhoods. It looks at the innocent expressions of children and the various cultural games of that era, including games like Gonggi Nori, horseback riding, and sledding with friends in nature.

title: 2026 International Sleep & Healing Expo | Sleep & Wellness Fest
short_description: The '2026 International Sleep & Healing Expo (Sleep & Wellness Festa)' is Korea's first and largest specialized sleep healing expo co-hosted by The Korea Economic Daily, Coex Co., Ltd., and the Korea Sleep Industry Association. Held on a scale of 150 companies and 300 booths across the entire Hall B on the 1st floor of COEX, you can encounter all areas of sleep environment and lifestyle in one place, including sleep tech, healthcare, sleep medical products and services, mattresses, bedding, and sleep lighting. A Special Pavilion for Healing Tourism & Wellness and Korea's first Special Pavilion for Silver Towns will be operated together, alongside colorful side events such as an industrial conference featuring global speakers, sleep trail, interactive event zone, sound sleep zone, healing zone, and prize zone. Free admission is available upon pre-registration, and benefits such as a welcome sleep kit gift, prize draw, and priority seminar seat reservation are provided.

title: Jung Jaeil Concert - Listen
short_description:
The solo concert of Jung Jae-il, the music director of the Netflix series <Squid Game>, which was a mega-hit worldwide, and the movie <Parasite>, which showcased the strength of K-Content, will be held in December at Sejong Center for the Performing Arts.

On October 1st, Jung Jae-il performed with the London Symphony Orchestra at the opening concert of the 10th anniversary of the K-Music Festival held at the Barbican Centre in London, earning a standing ovation from the local audience.

In this solo concert, audiences can experience live performances of popular soundtracks from Squid Game and Parasite and songs from his recently released solo album Listen. This event will showcase his charm as a performer and his broad and deep musical spectrum as a composer, music director, and conductor, allowing attendees to witness his diverse musical talents firsthand.

The Jung Jae-il concert will take place in December at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts, Korea's leading performing arts institution. Located in the heart of Seoul at Gwanghwamun, it is surrounded by iconic tourist attractions such as Gwanghwamun Square and Gyeongbokgung Palace. Enjoy not only the Jung Jae-il concert at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts but also explore the surrounding tourist spots of Seoul.

title: The Boundary Unmade: The Destruction of the Seoul City Wall
short_description:
In the second half of 2025, the Hanyangdoseong Museum opens its special exhibition Demolition of Hanyangdoseong, Breaking the Boundaries of Hanyang.


King Taejo Yi Seong-gye, founder of the Joseon dynasty, established palaces, the Jongmyo Shrine, and the Sajik Altar in Hanyang based on Confucian ideals, and in 1396 began construction of Hanyangdoseong to defend the capital. The city wall functioned as both a physical boundary separating the capital from the provinces and a symbol of royal authority. After Japan’s victory in the Russo-Japanese War, it began interfering in the Korean Empire, establishing the Wall Disposal Committee in 1907 to commence the full-scale demolition of Hanyangdoseong. Under the pretext of modernization and urban development, gates and walls were destroyed, replaced with colonial government facilities and residential areas.


To mark the 80th anniversary of Liberation, this exhibition presents the process of the demolition of Hanyangdoseong by Japan and the transformation of Seoul into a colonial city, using a wide range of historical materials.

title: Yoo Eui Jeong 《The Baek-Ja 》
short_description:
Ceramic art, considered one of humanity's oldest forms of expression, embodies the symbolic language and imaginative structures refined through history. 

As the artist notes, ceramics have reflected their time's philosophy, aesthetics, lifestyles, and trends through color, shape, and pattern. Yoo Eui-jeong focuses on this inherent nature of ceramics, creating works with a hybrid temporality.

One of Yoo's signature techniques involves allowing glaze to drip over white porcelain and layering it with iconic imagery from both the past and present. The way the glaze's form fades and distorts as it flows downward symbolizes the evolving cultural symbols shaped by the passage of time.

In this exhibition, Yoo Eui-jeong draws inspiration from Baekja, which reached its zenith during the Joseon Dynasty, presenting works that reflect contemporary relevance. White porcelain, originally a symbol of the royal court's dignity, also became widely cherished by commoners for its simplicity, with blue-and-white porcelain and iron-painted porcelain dominating different social strata. Yoo experiments with how baekja, imbued with such historical context, can manifest in meaningful ways from a modern perspective.

title: Kim So-jin's Complete Performance of Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga
short_description: Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga is a precious form of traditional Korean music that retains the old-fashioned charm of Gojesori. It is characterized by its robust and dignified sound, primarily in the Ujo mode. This musical lineage, which began with Park Yu-jeon and continued through Jeong Jae-geun, Jeong Eung-min, and Jeong Gwon-jin, was on the brink of extinction until it was revived by Yoon Jin-cheol, who was recognized as a holder of the National Intangible Cultural Heritage. Recently, it has been actively performed again. This performance is particularly notable as it marks a female singer's first complete rendition of Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga. Audiences will experience Kim So-jin's unique interpretation and color.

title: GWTF: Go with the Flow
short_description: Canvas N Gallery will host "GWTF: Go with the Flow" featuring two artists, Kim Yeon-hong and Ahn Rio, from October 13th, 2023, to November 12th, 2023. They all immerse themselves in the flow of things that are not visible. While artist Kim Yeonhong follows the "flow of phenomena" such as light and wind, artist Ahn Rio explores another universe created by the "flow of thoughts." This exhibition was planned to focus on ‘flow,’ a common theme between the two artists, with the meaning of ‘going with the flow.’ Each exhibition room is divided into light, water, and wood, highlighting things that flow or the artist's results that result from the flow.

title: Garden Beau
short_description:
Garden Beau, inspired by “Gardens by the Bay” in Singapore, is a beauty, health, and organic specialty store located near Seoul Botanic Park. It is a multi-store where visitors can experience a wide range of products across various categories, featuring both domestic and international brands, making it a beloved destination.


The store offers Global Tax-Free services and multilingual assistance (English, Japanese, Chinese). Various ongoing events are provided for foreign visitors, making it especially popular among tourists.

title: 2026 Yeongdeungpo Art Square X KAIST Experience Design Lab Special Exhibition <Living Geometry>
short_description: Based on Yeongdeungpo's complex landscape where industry, finance, and culture intersect, this exhibition reinterprets the city as a living, moving organism. Planned by the KAIST Experience Design Lab, this exhibition sheds new light on the relationship between the city and humans through data visualization and immersive media.

title: COMPANY World Affair
short_description: The Helsinki-based design studio COMPANY has traveled the world for the past 20 years in search of unique manufacturing techniques and the local artisans who have preserved them. Their exploration is a process of deeply understanding the cultures and people of unfamiliar lands and falling in love with the whole world, which is 'World Affair' itself. The exhibition showcases the journey of intimate conversations and collaborations that the two artists have shared with makers from all over the world. The exhibition unfolds the 'cycle of ideas' where inspiration gained on-site is realized through the hands of artisans via drawings, and the finished objects meet people in the market and spread out into the world. By following the long journey of a single object from its birth to its encounter with the world, we invite you to feel the value of respect and affection contained in the artists' touch.

title: Technology Connecting Heritage, the Most Human Future
short_description:
How can we carry forward heritage through digital technology?

And in that process, how can human creativity and values be respected?


This exhibition, held in collaboration with the NC Cultural Foundation and the 2025 Arumjigi Academy, intersects Arumjigi’s expertise accumulated in the fields of traditional culture and crafts with the NC Cultural Foundation’s long-standing insights into AI, ethics, and creativity. It has been organized as an opportunity to present diverse tangible works that demonstrate the potential of technology to connect past and future, and to bridge generations.


Here, you can discover the new heritage created by AI and digital technology and envision a future where technology coexists as a tool while human creativity and values are respected.

title: Weaving Relations
short_description:
Weaving Relations is an exhibition that spans the theme of "Architecture" for the 2024 Seoul Museum of Art exhibition. It delves into the essential attributes of architecture as a process of creating value and experience through relationship building and examines this process through various conceptual approaches.
Weaving Relations induces a shift in perspectives on life by exploring various ways of relationship building, facilitated by physical spaces that serve as fundamental conditions for self-recognition. Through the works of seven artists, the exhibition prompts contemplation on the transformations in how we perceive life.
Through this, the aim is to awaken modern individuals to the dynamic value of relationship building, which can counter feelings of isolation and identity loss.
The exhibition title, Weaving Relations, borrowed from Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's literary work "The Little Prince," encapsulates the essence of relationship building.
Weaving Relations refers to forming relationships based on temporality, repetition, and process while also being grounded in communal nature, which is the essence of architecture. What are we weaving, and what are we being weaved by? The exhibition aims to produce various narratives that accumulate deep relationship moments.

title: 2024 Kung Festival
short_description: The "Gung Festival" goes beyond the typical concert-style event, offering a “comprehensive cultural space” where music, beverages, and food seamlessly blend. Centered around the theme of the "palace," the festival provides a distinctive experience, treating attendees like VIP guests. The festival promises to evoke new emotions with a stage that harmonizes dynamic traditional cultural elements like electronic music, sangmo spinning, and laser shows. Audiences will experience “music that can be seen and heard” and “music that can be heard and seen,” creating an immersive experience that transcends the boundaries of conventional festivals. It is a pioneering cultural event where tradition and modernity coexist perfectly.

title: Ttukseom Windsurfing Park
short_description:
Ttukseom Windsurfing Park offers a variety of water sports on the Hangang River. 

This park hosts several private companies that provide activities like windsurfing, kayaking, paddleboarding, paddle yoga, and banana boating. It features a range of educational programs, including single-visit, one-day, and multiple-visit passes, making it accessible for both beginners and enthusiasts. With rental services available, the park is increasingly popular among foreign visitors. 


Renowned for its exotic scenery and stunning summer sunsets, Ttukseom Windsurfing Park is a must-visit for those seeking active and unique sports experiences.

title: [S-TCEP] DDP Design Archive KSVD: 1972-1993
short_description:
The Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) Design Archive KSVD: 1972-1973 exhibition celebrates the 50th anniversary of the founding of the KSVD that established the identity of modern design in Korea. It offers a chance for expo-goers to witness the transformation of social awareness of the development and concept of Korean modern-day visual design that began during the first and second phases of the Five-Year Economic Development Plan back in the '70s, thanks to the proactiveness of designers at the time.







※ This content is provided by the S-TCEP (Seoul - Tourism, Culture, Exhibitions, Performing Arts) Alliance.

title: Mood, sunday
short_description: In June, Superior Gallery presents a two-person exhibition by artists Jung Hwa Baek and Joyce Jin, who embody nature, human beings, and love. Both artists showcase their paintings that depict subtle yet heartwarming scenes observed through their unique perspectives on nature and humanity, establishing their own artistic realms. Both artists portray evocative artworks by observing ordinary moments in the surrounding landscapes and interpersonal relationships through their unique perspectives. The colors and visual elements presented by the two artists will create a pleasant and heartwarming experience, evoking feelings of coziness, warmth, and love for the viewers. The exhibition Mood, sunday will run until July 11th.

title: Summer Table : Six Hands, One Table
short_description: We bring you news of , a special exhibition by six craft artists. This exhibition, which introduces a table embracing the temperature of summer and the beautiful items that will fill it, presents a total of 26 works completed with various materials such as ceramics, metal, and lacquerware under the theme of 'Six Hands, One Table.' It is also a special opportunity to go beyond the joy of visual appreciation and directly own a piece that lingers in your mind, bringing it into your daily life. Please join us at the KIT Gallery to feel the tranquil depth of summer where cold metal, warm ceramics, and lacquerware harmonize.

title: Where Writing Breathes
short_description: 《Where Writing Breathes》 is an exhibition that explores 'Creation', the institutional agenda of the Seoul Museum of Art for 2026. The word 'author' is widely used not only in the art world but also in various fields such as literature and music, strongly connotes the meaning of creation or expressing an artwork originally. This exhibition is inspired by the general perception of an 'author' as a person who writes, namely a litterateur, and seeks to understand artistic creation through 'writing,' paying attention to the texts produced by artists. The exhibition's title, 'Geuljit' (Writing), refers to the gestures of writing that have taken on various forms of movement, metaphorically representing the vitality of writing that passes through the artist's body and unfolds in the exhibition space.

title: Strikezon Seoul Jamsil Stadium
short_description: Strikezon is an indoor screen baseball stadium where visitors can enjoy baseball simulation games. You can play batting games solo or team up with others for a full baseball match experience. The system goes beyond simply displaying a stadium backdrop—it recreates the 18-meter distance from the pitcher’s mound to home plate with impressive realism. Players can customize pitch types, speed, and difficulty level, making for an immersive and thrilling baseball experience.

title: Always-Already-There
short_description: Kang Young-hee's solo exhibition, 《Always-Already-There》, is a painting exhibition capturing the moments when existence and sensation naturally emerge. Through the spreading of ink, empty spaces, and the flow of layered colors, it quietly evokes memories and emotions preceding language, allowing viewers to confront their own inner sensations once again. This exhibition delicately unfolds the state of sensations that have already existed within us, rather than representing an "arrival."

title: Water Music Project : Wave
short_description: Inspired by Kim Hong-do’s painting Moonlit Night Boating, this performance presents a reinterpretation of traditional Korean sentiments where water, people, music, and space harmonize through a contemporary lens. The Seoul Metropolitan Traditional Orchestra held a nationwide competition for new compositions themed around the Han River. In Part 1 of the performance, five selected works by emerging composers will premiere. Part 2 features celebrated Korean traditional orchestral pieces, including The Song of Crossing the River by Kim Seong-guk and Breath of Hangaram by Im Hee-seon. This program, noted for its sensitive and creative blend of tradition and modernity, space and emotion, presents a meaningful stage that introduces a new wave in the Korean traditional orchestra scene.

title: Seoul Metropolitan Archives Exhibition <A City’s Boarding Log>
short_description:
Another story of records at the Seoul Metropolitan Archives

The Seoul Metropolitan Archives presents the exhibition A City’s Boarding Log, introducing the journey of Seoul’s transportation. The exhibition traces the city’s growth from the aftermath of the Korean War to the 1980s, as it built the foundations of its transportation system through archival materials. It showcases more than 120 records owned by the Seoul Metropolitan Archives, as well as donated materials from an engineer involved in the construction of the subway, vividly conveying the atmosphere of that era. In addition, a new permanent space has been created by relocating and reconstructing the exhibition contents of the Seoul Archives and Culture Center on the third floor of the Seoul Metropolitan Library, allowing visitors to explore Seoul from multiple perspectives. Follow the traces of time along the roads of Seoul and reflect on the paths we have taken and those that lie ahead.

title: 2036 Seoul, Second Olympics
short_description: The special exhibition <Seoul 2036, The Second Olympics> will be held in the Special Exhibition Hall lobby at the Seoul Museum of History to wish for the successful hosting of the 2036 Summer Olympics. This exhibition reflects on the half-century of history transformed since the Seoul Olympics and reexamines the achievements of the 1988 Seoul Olympics. It showcases the arduous journey of 1980s Seoul, a time when most believed hosting the Olympics was impossible. Despite a short preparation period, systematic efforts enabled the city to secure the Olympics, marking a leap forward on the global stage. Additionally, visitors can explore the changes in Seoul before and after the 1988 Seoul Olympics, one of the most significant international events in Korea's modern history, and how it impacted the lives of Seoul citizens. With hopes for a successful bid for the 2036 Seoul Olympics, we invite you to visit and take a moment to envision a renewed and further developed Seoul after hosting its second Olympics.

title: RISING NORTH SEOUL
short_description:
Since Korea’s liberation, the Buk-Seoul (northern Seoul) area has undergone rapid transformation through urbanization.


It became a settlement area for those pushed out from central Seoul and later saw the rise of factories along Jungnangcheon during the period of industrialization. As housing developments were introduced to accommodate the growing population, the area turned into a large apartment district. More recently, various cultural facilities have been established to enhance civic access to the arts, adding more diversity to the urban landscape.


As a major cultural institution in northern Seoul, the Seoul Museum of Urban Life presents this exhibition to explore the changing cityscape of Buk-Seoul and the evolving lives of the people who have lived there.

title: The Day and Night of Cheonggyecheon
short_description:
This exhibition presents a collection of works depicting Cheonggyecheon in the 1950s to 1970s by renowned cartoonist Kim Seong-hwan, best known for the satirical comic Mr. Gobau.


Though it was an era of great scarcity, Kim once said, “Even under the moonlight, there was romance in the humble shacks.”


Following his warm perspective, this exhibition shares the stories of Cheonggyecheon’s days and nights.

Through these works, we hope visitors will encounter the radiant moments of those who lived difficult yet heartfelt lives.

title: 2023 KOREA BUILD WEEK
short_description:
From August 3rd (Thursday) to 6th (Sunday), Korea Build will be held at COEX in Seoul. This event will be held concurrently with Korea Build Week, featuring five events. It includes opportunities for tailored consultations through specialized advisors and 1:1 matching consultations. Various seminars and conferences on trending topics will also be conducted during the event.


<Simultaneous Events>
1. Seoul Future DX-CON WORLD: A specialized exhibition showcasing smart information and communication future technologies.
2. NEXT-CON 2023: An exhibition introducing cutting-edge construction technologies, including AI, big data, drones, and IoT, in construction and architecture.
3. Space Design Fair: An interior design exhibition presenting hospitality and retail trends based on spatial design.
4. Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Expo: The only specialized exhibition in Korea focusing on electric vehicle charging stations.
5. Building Maintenance and Management Industry Expo: A specialized exhibition for building maintenance, management, and repair industries.

<Special Exhibitions>
1. Carbon-Neutral Architecture Special Exhibition: Explore eco-friendly building materials and technologies such as carbon neutrality and zero-energy concepts.
2. Construction Tools Special Exhibition: Experience and compare high-performance tools from various brands firsthand.
3. Japanese Wood Special Exhibition: Showcasing excellent domestic and international wood materials like Hinoki and Sugi.
4. Space Art Fair: A special section displaying various art genres that match different spaces' characteristics and purposes.
5. Interior Materials Special Exhibition: Featuring interior components such as fittings, flooring, and finishes that compose a space.

title: 2Gil29Gallery
short_description:
Located in the vibrant Garosu-gil area of Sinsa-dong, Gangnam, where diverse interests and dynamic Seoul culture converge, 2Gil29 Gallery has been actively introducing contemporary art to the public since its opening in 2015. The gallery has fostered active exchanges with prominent Korean artists such as Hong Jung-hee, Choi Sun-ho, Nam June Paik, Lim Young-kyun, and Kang Suk-young while also showcasing works by artists like Kwon Young-ho and Charlie Han to diversify the Korean art market.

The gallery’s curatorial approach is based on a wide range of creative works, fostering a more positive and progressive discourse on art. Through deeper communication and interaction with art, it transcends mere visual and auditory engagement, offering meaningful aesthetic and spiritual exchanges with artists. This, in turn, enhances the value of their creative endeavors.

In addition, 2Gil29 Gallery is committed to discovering and nurturing emerging talents such as upcycling artist Hong Ji-hee, singer-turned-painter Yoo Hyun-suk, and Kwon Jae-hyuk, a graduate of the University of the Arts London (UAL).

title: Theatre des Lumieres: Dali, The Endless Enigma
short_description: The Seoul 'Theater des Lumieres,' which opened in 2022, has effectively utilized the identity of the Warhol Theater, establishing itself as a multifaceted cultural and art space where visitors can enjoy a sensory experience beyond a simple exhibition space. Through immersive experiences that unfold in an expansive area of up to 1,500 square meters and an imposing height of 21 meters, the audience is transported into the heart of the artwork, providing them with a unique artistic experience akin to becoming the protagonists of a masterpiece.

title: the SamE
short_description: The Same is a special space where fans can communicate more closely with artists. It not only provides fans with a new shopping experience but also delivers unforgettable joy through various events and promotions.

title: Hongik University Museum Special Exhibition 《After White 1975–1995》
short_description: In 2025, the Hongik University Museum presents the special exhibition After White 1975–1995. This exhibition re-examines the critic Lee Il’s essay White Thinks, which laid the foundations for the aesthetics of Korean monochrome painting (Dansaekhwa), retracing the trajectory of his thought and practice, which deeply influenced the formation and development of Korean contemporary art. From the museum’s collection, visitors will encounter the flow of Korean contemporary art beginning with monochrome painting and the color white, viewed within the context of art criticism. The exhibition provides an opportunity to experience how art and criticism interacted to shape the flow of Korean contemporary art and to newly encounter the influence criticism exerted in Korean art history. It is hoped that this exhibition will re-examine the meaning of criticism within the history of Korean contemporary art and offer an occasion to reflect anew on contemporary art discourse today.

title: GALLERY J. ONE
short_description: GALLERY J. ONE is a contemporary art gallery located at 13 Palpan-gil, where Samcheong-dong and Bukchon meet. Starting in 2008 at Bongsan Cultural Street in Daegu, GALLERY J. ONE is further expanding its flow through its Seoul space in 2025, based on domestic and international activities and a long exhibition history. The white-cube-based gallery building evokes a small-scale European contemporary cultural art space, harmonizing a white linear structure, grid-patterned iron glass windows, and an open traffic line leading to an outdoor staircase. The varying window locations and space depths on each floor naturally adjust the rhythm of viewing artworks, while natural light entering through the windows and refined interior lighting create a calm viewing environment. Beyond the windows and rooftop terrace, the mud-tile roofs of Hanoks, the ridge line of Bugaksan Mountain, and the roofline of the National Folk Museum of Korea come into view at a glance. As Seoul's ancient scenery and Oriental mood quietly seep into the modern exhibition space, the exhibition here goes beyond viewing artworks to become an experience where urban time and artistic contemplation meet. GALLERY J. ONE is a serene and dignified culture and arts space you can encounter along the Samcheong-dong walking trail.

title: Eddie Martinez 《To Be Continued》
short_description:
Space K Seoul presents a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based artist Eddie Martinez (b.1977). The exhibition, titled 《to be continued》, sheds light on the artist’s oeuvre, which effortlessly fuses figuration and abstraction, from 2005 to the present, arranged both chronologically and thematically. His paintings are characterized by swift lines and bold colors, while everyday found materials add a unique texture to the flat canvases.
The exhibition features about 30 drawings and paintings, including a new series, focusing on Martinez's practice of 'constant drawing'. Surrounding objects that catch his eye are transferred onto paper and canvas and transformed into entirely new landscapes, while repeated motifs give a sense of coherence to unfamiliar landscapes. The familiar objects of everyday life that are gradually revealed among the shapes which may be difficult to interpret at first glance stimulate our imagination through the artist’s personal experience.

title: Jo Yongjin · Hwang Taein <A Gentle Change>
short_description: A Gentle Change begins by asking whether Korean dance can offer something new to contemporary audiences. Jo Yongjin and Hwang Taein, who have been part of the National Dance Company of Korea for over ten years, aim to present "Korean dance" as a free and open expression unbound by fixed frameworks or limitations. They view Korean dance not as something owned by anyone or tied to a specific origin but as a living art form with the potential for continuous growth and expansion. They focus on finding a contemporary sensibility through a fresh perspective. By showcasing various interpretations of this long-preserved art form, they seek to draw out the dance's inherently captivating elements. At the same time, they explore the idea that Korean dance is not merely an ancient cultural heritage but a living art form with the potential for continuous growth and expansion.

title: JEJU HAENYEO : DISAPPEARING WORLDS
short_description:
In the summer of 2025, five artists traveled to Jeju. They shared meals with the Haenyeo, sat together at the bulteok, exchanged stories, and observed the tools, discipline, and bodily memories of time. Thus, this exhibition began from two weeks of shared experiences with the Haenyeo. Céline Park examines the hierarchy and silence embedded within the Haenyeo community, Kim Yi-hwa explores the survival of 'nomadic Haenyeo' in the face of climate change, and Moon Su-hyuk critiques how tradition is consumed as a language of capital. Son Ji-min reconsiders the labor of Haenyeo through the lens of femininity and care, while Choi Mi-jin investigates the transmission of knowledge through oral narratives and relationships.


《JEJU HAENYEO: DISAPPEARING WORLDS》 begins in Seoul in November 2025 and continues in Jeju. The Haenyeo, once the mainstay of livelihood, have become symbols of tourism and consumption. Rather than recreating this surface image, the exhibition poses a question: In what forms do the Haenyeo’s bodies, tools, discipline, silence, ecology, and desires persist today, and who is now voicing this legacy anew?

title: Seoul Archives Children’s Record Experience Room <Twisting Record Exploration>
short_description: The Seoul Archives has prepared an interactive exhibition for children, “The Twisting Record Exploration”, designed to help them easily and enjoyably experience records. The exhibition is divided into three main sections. Part 1, “From Memory to Record”, allows visitors to explore various methods of remembering, learn about recording tools, and understand different types of records. Part 2, “Record Exploration”, features an interactive experience where participants can examine records of Seoul and their records and even build landmarks based on the records held by the Seoul Archives. Part 3, “The Record Keepers”, introduces the roles of record researchers and preservation scientists who collect and preserve records. As a specialized public archive, the Seoul Archives not only collects and preserves Seoul's records and residents' memories but also strives to provide diverse record information services. We hope this children’s interactive exhibition will inspire more citizens to take an interest in records and actively participate in the documentation world.

title: A Magical day
short_description:
Superior Gallery presents a two-person exhibition by artists Kim Ki-tae and Shin Sun-ae, capturing life's moments between boundaries and the conscious and unconscious realms. Kim Ki-tae portrays realistic yet dreamlike scenes of nature's light and fleeting spectacles through strong brightness contrasts. With its soft and radiant illumination, Shin Sun-ae's artwork revives precious and special memories latent within, offering romance and happiness. Even in the dim atmosphere, these artworks, filled with brightness and warmth, create beautiful memories out of fleeting moments.

The exhibition "A Magical Day" will be held at Superior Gallery until August 9th.

title: Joke: Spreading from Me, Passing to You
short_description:
Joke: Spreading from Me, Passing to You is a three-artist exhibition by Lee Jeong-hee, Lee Fero, and Joo Yoo-jin, which was curated with a focus on the multiple meanings of "농담" (pronounced "nongdam" in Korean). The exhibition encompasses both the notion of a small gesture or playful act intended to make someone feel good and the concept describing the degree of lightness and darkness in color and shading in art. This exhibition is divided into three spaces: "Spreading Deeply," "Gently Passing By," and "Anticipating a Smile."

In the first part, "Spreading Deeply," artists Lee Jeong-hee and Joo Yoo-jin explore their personal solitude. With various shades of blue accumulating, Lee Jeong-hee reflects on her solitude in the paradise of Arcadia, where despair coexists. Joo Yoo-jin expresses her contemplation of her solitude through the color blue.

In the second part, "Gently Passing By," you can encounter the works of artists Lee Jeong-hee and Lee Fero. Lee Fero's distinctive approach involves delicately drawing desserts and then pushing them away with swift strokes to reshape their forms. In her works, the subjects become distorted, and the original shapes are briefly touched upon and then become ambiguous, much like the concept of "swipe to unlock" on a mobile phone. It reveals hidden elements, and paradoxically, the intention to reveal becomes clearer, according to the artist.

Finally, in the innermost section, "Anticipating a Smile," artist Joo Yoo-jin creates a small garden. In this bright and colorful garden filled with blooming flowers, the artist positions someone other than themselves. Unlike the spread of their own loneliness through the blue light, they hope that the loneliness of others will not be lonely and that they will experience the spread of various colors.

title: Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra Park Concert 2023
short_description:
