title: Joseon Yangban Hospitality Culture Experience Performance 'Onggi Concert'
short_description:
[Performance Introduction]

The Onggi Concert goes beyond simple appreciation of traditional Korean music (Gugak); it is a 'participatory prestige Gugak performance' where the audience becomes the protagonist of the Sarangbang (reception room) elegance of the Joseon Dynasty.


[Program Composition]


▶ Greeting (Approx. 10 minutes)

A docent personally welcomes each audience member in the lobby. Upon entry, an individual table (dok-sang) — tea and refreshments on a traditional small dining table — is set, allowing you to experience the essence of the Yangban guest reception culture of the Joseon Dynasty.


▶ Explanation and Performance (Approx. 75 minutes)


• Historical stories of the individual table culture, Dadam (tea conversation), and Gwangmudae (Docent explanation, approx. 15 minutes)

• The 'Simcheong falling into the water' scene from the Pansori  (Approx. 15 minutes)

• Detailed explanation of the music and Chuimsae (exclamations) experience (Approx. 10 minutes)

• The 'Blind Man Sim opening his eyes' scene from the Pansori  (Approx. 15 minutes)

• Q&A and conversation with the singer (Soriggun) and drummer (Gosu) (Approx. 20 minutes)


▶ Farewell (Approx. 10 minutes)

Souvenir presentation, photo taking, and guestbook signing.


[Viewing Points]


• 'Gwangmudae', a historic theater revived in its original location in Dongdaemun after 96 years

• The two most visually striking scenes from , which possesses the clearest dramatic contrast among the five Pansori madangs

• Personalized hospitality with a choice of alcohol or tea, operated on a small scale for up to 30 audience members

• 'Appreciation conversation (review discussion)' shared directly with the docent, singer, and drummer

• Raw Pansori experience with natural acoustics intact

title: Alone but Together
short_description:
Superior Gallery has organized a joint painting exhibition titled “Alone but Together” by artists Kang Ji-hye and Ahn So-young. Through their unique canvas, they unfold their stories, enhancing their relationships with the surroundings and depicting inner growth and understanding.

Artist Kang Ji-hye beautifully and dreamily expresses true satisfaction in life and a harmonious world. On the other hand, artist Ahn So-young describes the process of self-discovery through travel, seeking inner peace and true tranquility.

We hope the hopeful stories of these two artists, beautifully unfolding the journey from "I" to "we," resonate with your hearts and convey a warm message of togetherness. Kang Ji-hye and Ahn So-young's joint painting exhibition, "Alone but together," will be held until September 26th.

title: Transparence_ Sense and Mind: The Exhibition of Gapado AiR Artists 2018-2022
short_description: The concept of "transparency" is derived from Susan Sontag's book "Against Interpretation" (1966). It refers to experiencing the shimmering of objects and experiencing them as they are. Transparency allows us to perceive our actual experiences in art, and through that, it helps us recover our lost human sensitivity in a mass-production and mass-consumption society. The statement "We need to learn to see better, hear better, feel better" reflects the artist's work at Gapado AiR.

title: 50th Anniversary of Seoul Metropolitan Subway <Subway in Seoul>
short_description:
On August 15, 1974, marking the 29th anniversary of Korea's liberation, the country's first subway line, the 'Jongno Line,' opened. Since then, Seoulites have lived in the “Subway Age” for five decades. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway is familiar to everyone who has traveled to and from Seoul. It was not just a convenient public transportation system that eases commutes to school and work; it was a vehicle for a ‘new era of modern life.’ Back then, the subway was a new experience for everyone in Seoul. Over time, as we adapted to this new era, the subway gradually changed our mindset, lifestyle, culture, and the city itself. It has served as a commuter train for the city’s many workers, a transportation service that makes it easy for everyone to get around and keep appointments, a meet-up point, and a venue for consumption. The subway also provided a social space where people could mingle, fostering both a sense of community and deep aloneness. Furthermore, it has reshaped urban spaces and living areas, and as a comfortable cultural space accessible anywhere, it has expanded people's cultural enjoyment.
The Seoul Metropolitan Subway has been “connecting” Seoul through its underground network and to the outlying areas, shaping the capital city as we know it today. To mark the 50th anniversary of the Seoul Metropolitan Subway, the Seoul Museum of History and Seoul Metro have partnered to present this commemorative exhibition. We cordially invite you to this exhibition, which we hope will offer an opportunity to reflect on Seoul’s story, created by the subway and its people, and to envision what the future holds for the city.

title: The Garden of Simwon : Ink and Silence
short_description: Looking at nature closely resembles looking into one's own inner self. Park Kyung-mook's work contains the journey of reaching the silence of muk (默) through the material of meok (墨, ink). The traces of ink accumulated and permeated on the canvas are an accumulation of time and a process of thought, and the shapes resembling black rocks and islands, rather than explaining or defining something, allow the viewer to pause for a moment and observe their own mind. The path to Simwon (心源), the root of the mind where all thoughts begin, is not far away. Through the act of letting one's gaze linger along the deep empty spaces created by the ink, and quietly observing the vitality of trees that embrace a long period of time, we naturally confront our inner selves. The deep ink, the empty spaces, and the trees holding time form a single garden within the space. Rather than a real garden, it is a landscape of thought unfolding in the mind, and a place where one can stay for a while, catch their breath, and listen to the source of their inner self. The Garden of Simwon: Ink and Silence is a place where thoughts built up with ink and landscapes formed by time meet. Walking through the garden of Simwon, we hope it will be a time to face the tranquil landscape existing in each person's mind.

title: Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh
short_description: 《Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh》 is a two-person exhibition featuring Camille Norment and Min Oh that sheds new light on what is commonly referred to as "noise," including irregular sounds, unpredictable variables, and elements pushed outside the boundaries of established systems. Noise is recontextualized not as an obstruction to be eliminated, but as a fertile ground where new relationships and meanings emerge. Camille Norment and Min Oh respond to this inquiry through their respective creative methodologies. Min Oh presents her time-based installation series, Simultaneous, displayed together in one place for the first time—a body of work researched and produced over several years as part of the Arko Multi-disciplinary Arts Support Project. Concurrently, Camille Norment marks her inaugural solo presentation at a domestic museum with Plexus (Rhizome) Seoul, a sound installation commissioned specifically by the Arko Art Center.

title: DDP Fall Special Tour: Design & Art Tour
short_description:
The Seoul Design Foundation will operate a DDP Fall Special Tour connected to the “Design & Art” exhibition. Under the theme “Extreme Design Experience: From Street to Gallery,” the program will offer enthusiasts a sensory journey.

As part of the seasonal DDP Special Tour series, this autumn’s program contrasts “Touchable Design vs. Collectible Design,” ranging from hands-on, experiential design objects to unique collectible pieces expressing value, meaning, story, and identity.

title: Van Gogh, Captured at Your Fingertips
short_description: This exhibition not only allows visitors to visually appreciate Van Gogh's works, but also provides an opportunity for them to deeply experience his art by directly touching the textures of the pieces. In particular, the exhibited works of Van Gogh are part of the 'Masterpiece Original Series,' a simulacrum created using patented 3D UV printing technology. This technology recreates Van Gogh's brushstrokes and colors, allowing visitors to feel the texture of the original works at their fingertips.

title: Chubun: The Beginning of Autumn
short_description: As the season deepens, leaves gradually change color, fruits ripen fully, and nature meets its moment of fruition. Aechae’s autumn exhibition Chubun: The Beginning of Autumn resembles this seasonal flow. Just as a single tree takes root over time, blossoms, and eventually bears fruit, may you enjoy the maturity and abundance of this season before Chuseok, achieving stronger results and generous accomplishments in your own place.

title: Sleep No More Seoul
short_description: A production by Punchdrunk, the British company that pioneered immersive theater, this work is a sensorial and cinematic reinterpretation of Shakespeare’s tragedy Macbeth. As a groundbreaking performance that has introduced a new paradigm to the global performing arts scene, it offers the ultimate experience of meeting performers face-to-face and feeling the performance through all five senses.

title: Childhood under the shield
short_description: What was your childhood like? This exhibition begins with that question. The international exchange exhibition, “Stories of Children Who Lived Through the War: Childhood under the Siege,” aims to convey the preciousness of peace through 38 stories of children who endured the longest siege in modern history, which took place in Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia, from 1992 to 1995. For 1,425 days, children in Sarajevo lived isolated from the world, experiencing a different daily life than ordinary children. Their lives, filled with the pain of war and the preciousness of everyday moments, are told with quiet resilience. These deeply personal stories are not just about Sarajevo, a city 8,465 kilometers away from Seoul. They are stories of families, friends, and neighbors, resonating deeply with the audience. Through this exhibition, the hope is for you to feel that "people are strong, and children are strong!"

title: Super Moon on My Hand: Moon Jar Exhibition
short_description:
Superior Gallery has organized an exhibition titled 'Super Moon on My Hand: Moon Jar' featuring the artists Kang Min-sung, Kim Kyung-hee, and Jo Sung-hyun, who are furthering the tradition while evolving it into contemporary lifestyle art. Showcasing works that reinterpret traditional techniques and imagery in a modern way, these pieces fuse contemporary images with various materials and forms, embodying unique stories crafted by the artists. Their creations capture the personal joy, wishes, and happiness evoked by moon jars while incorporating diverse perspectives through subjective creativity.

The three artists are forging a new wave in tradition, harmoniously blending inherited values with contemporary narratives. Using moon jars as a medium, each artist conveys their unique artistic value and cultural expression, infusing unchanging values with new emotions to deliver their distinctive messages. Amid rapid changes, we invite you to fully experience the jars created by three artists at Superior Gallery, where they skillfully blend their unique realms into the living, breathing fabric of everyday life.

title: Open-Air Museum - Pungnap
short_description:
Open-Air Museum_Pungnap 
Welcome to Open-Air Museum_Pungnap. 
Here is Pungnaptoseong, an earthen mound built by the people of the Hanseong Baekje period to defend their city along the windy Han River. Over time, a city has been built within the fortress, burying traces of past eras underground. With relics buried one to two meters below the surface, the inside of the fortress itself becomes a vast, hidden museum. Now, please take a moment to imagine this immense museum, and remember that a museum has exhibition halls where relics or artworks are displayed. This exhibition envisions the excavation sites within the fortress as exhibition halls. That said, these halls come to be sites where visitors encounter contemporary artworks while walking along the streets or turning a corner, thus blending the past with the present. So, what kind of works would you expect to encounter in such a museum? This exhibition consists of “reappearing” works that can metaphorically represent the characteristics of space and time. You will encounter the emergence of traditional media experiments, historical works, images, and others. In today’s time of immense interest in nonlinear temporality, the exhibition showcases works by artists who have meticulously experimented with and restructured the content, form, and structure of traditional media in the Korean art scene; these works metaphorically and materially represent the layers of time and space in contemporary Pungnap-dong. Additionally, it explores the spatial boundaries of art and museums by installing mediums such as Korean painting, painting, video, photography, and ceramics, which are usually exhibited indoors, outdoors. These works by the mound are realized like small openings to a portal to another time and space, with even the flow of the wind between them becoming visible. Artist Seung-taek Lee, who has established a unique artistic practice through the concept of “non-art,” presents another track in this exhibition by circulating through the city. Lee’s bicycle carrying the earth symbolizes the reappearance of historical works and becomes a ritual of circulation. To add, Lee’s wind extends beyond the city to the fortress; the red cloth flying across the wind, along with the earth running through the fortress, reaches back to a time older than the Hanseong Baekje period, older than ancient times, making one perceive the planet Earth and its life. How did you feel after walking through this vast museum and discovering the hidden artworks? We hope this exhibition provides an opportunity for you to transform your view of Pungnaptoseong, a historical yet everyday space, and discover new possibilities within the city. 

□ Performance information
Open Air Museum_Pungnap is pleased to present renactments of Seung-taek Lee's iconic reproduced works, Wind-Folk Amusement (1971) and Earth Play (1994). These are visualizations of ""Wind,"" a red cloth that forms the shape of a bicycle and wind carrying an PVC balloon.
It will be held four times on August 24, August 31, October 4, and October 11, and anyone can watch Earth, Let's Play from 15:00 to 16:00 and Wind, Let's Play from 16:00 to 16:30 at the Pungnaptoseong Namseong-Wall.

title: Seoul Museum of Art Nanji Residency 20th Anniversary Exhibition 《AMOR EX MACHINA》
short_description: The 20th-anniversary exhibition of the Seoul Museum of Art's Nanji Residency, 《The Origin of Love (AMOR EX MACHINA)》, is structured as a journey to look back on the meaning of love by borrowing the archetypes of old stories in an era where technology rewrites relationships. Technology is no longer a tool placed outside of life, but has become an environment that conditions our senses and relationships. We wake up to smartphone alarms, move along paths indicated by satellites, and spend our days encountering news selected by algorithms. Within this, the ways we remember and form relationships are also changing. The exhibition proposes that our destination amidst the changing landscape of technology lies in love, the sense that makes us human.

title: BAZAAR Exhibition : IN-BETWEEN
short_description: The third exhibition by fashion magazine Harper’s BAZAAR. This exhibition is held under the theme of IN-BETWEEN in collaboration with three artists; Nikki S. Lee, Christine Sun Kim, and Emmanuel Hahn. IN-BETWEEN carries a layered meaning, combining “IN” (inside) and “BE” (to exist), and delves into questions of identity, boundaries, and human consciousness. The three contemporary artists, each gaining attention in the art world, reexamine the space of “boundaries” from their own perspectives. Experience their exploration through photography, video, and drawing in BAZAAR Exhibition, IN-BETWEEN.

title: SeMA Omnibus : At the End of the World Split Endlessly
short_description:
At the End of the World Splits Endlessly seeks to interpret SeMA’s collection through the keywords of connection and combination between mediums. In this post-medium/post-media era, the exhibition explores the inevitable structure between artists and their works, mediated by technology, while showcasing the multi-layered structure of media today. It examines how old and new media, virtual and real, AI and the body, and the interplay of technology and society create complex media environments. The term "medium" originates from the Greek word for "middle" or "between," signifying how, in contemporary art, mediums function as a bridge—linking the artist, the artwork, the viewer, and the museum. As visitors follow the exhibition's key concepts—Old & New, Yellow Block, Layered Medium, Open End—it reveals our current media landscape's singular and plural structures.

Inspired by anthropologist Anna Tsing’s The Mushroom at the End of the World and Jorge Luis Borges’ The Garden of Forking Paths, this exhibition grapples with the questions posed by the climate crisis and the end of capitalism. Through their works, artists ask where we stand in the world as it fractures. Just as artists traverse a spectrum of media, choosing and renewing their mediums, we, too, dream of new connections in a world that endlessly diverges. These connections, however, are not seamless but fragmented and partial. Art encourages us to confront this imperfection, urging us to find life, reflection, resistance, hope, and imagination among the ruins and potentialities of our time.

title: Takahata Isao  Exibition
short_description:
This exhibition showcases the entire production process of all the works directed by the master of animation, Takahata Isao, from his debut to his masterpieces. It includes works such as “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)”, “Anne of Green Gables (1979)”, “Grave of the Fireflies (1988)”, “Only Yesterday (1991)”, “Pom Poko (1994)”, and “The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (2013)”.
His directorial materials include layouts, which can be likened to blueprints for animated film production, and sketches and handwritten notes that he wrote and drew.
In addition, it is packed with previously unreleased materials from Miyazaki Hayao, who was responsible for the layouts during Takahata Isao's directorial era at Zuiyo Video, including “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)” and “Anne of Green Gables (1979).”

title: National Jeongdong Theater Cecil
short_description: The National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil, is a historic performance hall in Jung-gu, Seoul. Originally opened in 1976 as Cecil Theater, it’s a small yet iconic venue with a capacity of 232 seats. During the late 1970s, it became the heart of Korea's theater scene, hosting the Korea Theater Festival from 1977 to 1980. Despite its prominence, financial difficulties led to its closure in 2018 after being operated by private theater groups 'Madan' and 'Rodem.' In April 2018, the Seoul Metropolitan Government spearheaded a cultural regeneration project to reopen Cecil Theater and handed its management to a non-profit organization. Designed by renowned architect Kim Joong-up, the theater has long been a cornerstone of Korean performing arts and cultural heritage. In 2022, the theater was revitalized under the management of the National Jeongdong Theater, taking on the new name 'National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil.' Today, it serves as a vibrant space for artists and audiences to connect through innovative and experimental performances, upholding its legacy and creative core values.

title: Garden of Gratitude
short_description: Newly established in Gwanghwamun Square, the Garden of Gratitude is a space designed to reflect upon the gratitude toward Korean War veterans and the achievements and prosperity of the Republic of Korea, which has transitioned from an aid-recipient country to a donor country. The "Light of Gratitude 23" comprises 23 symbolic sculptures situated quietly yet magnificently at the center of Gwanghwamun Square. It stands as a symbol of the deepest respect and gratitude dedicated to the noble devotion of the participating nations that willingly extended their hands to safeguard the freedom and peace of the Republic of Korea. "Freedom Hall," situated underground at Gwanghwamun Square, is an immersive multimedia space where visitors can multi-dimensionally experience the sentiments of freedom, sacrifice, peace, and gratitude toward the nations that participated in the Korean War.

title: Bonds of the Heart, Waves of Resonance
short_description:
This landmark exhibition celebrates 60 years of normalized diplomatic relations between Korea and Japan and the 80th anniversary of Korea’s liberation. It serves as a meaningful moment to reflect on the Korea-Japan relationship. While Japan remains Korea’s closest neighbor, many unresolved issues still hinder deeper cooperation. The more we reflect on the past and examine the present, the better we can prepare for a new turning point.


'Bonds of the Heart, Waves of Resonance' explores the essence of trust and exchange—between nations and between individuals—through the story of the Tongsinsa, the diplomatic missions of the Joseon Dynasty. While Tongsinsa refers to formal diplomatic delegations and systems, their deeper significance goes beyond diplomacy and cultural exchange. These missions were based on mutual respect, trust, and understanding, fostering friendship between nations and bonds between people.


History is not merely a record of the past—it is a force that connects the present and future. Through this historical legacy of Tongsinsa, which bridges state and individual, diplomacy and culture, past and present, this exhibition reflects on the meaning of "diplomacy based on trust" and encourages us to envision a peaceful future together.

title: Dobong  Kim Sun-young : Solo Exhibition 「Here, Standing on the Star」
short_description:
Stars are not abstract symbols in the distant sky, they are the very spot where I stand, breathing and living in the present moment. The small tremors and deep immersion we experience in everyday life create a resonance of consciousness, within which a universe, a world, emerges. This exhibition is a condensation of moments deepened and contemplated in prolonged silence and stillness.


Time spent alone, detached from relationships, reflects the paths I have walked and the traces of pauses I have taken, while simultaneously serving as a gateway to another world. Within the context of traditional calligraphy, I evoke the primal forms and energies of ancient scripts, especially oracle bone characters, and reconstruct them with Hangul’s formal possibilities through a contemporary sensibility. The characters go beyond mere tools for communication; they manifest as traces of existence and as visual sculptural forms. Letters that breathe like living hearts engrave a pulse into each stroke, leaving trajectories that pierce through time.


“Here, Standing on a Star” does not refer to any particular star. It is the “here” where I stand, the moments of now. The characters that bloom in this space transcend personal records and explore how humans perceive and sense the world. I hope this exhibition becomes, for visitors, another star and a pathway to their inner selves. Along this journey, I envision embracing even severed relationships without fear, and standing as a radiant being in one’s own right.

title: Happy Holidays
short_description: The excitement that arrives at the end of the year, the festive atmosphere, and the desire to linger a little more. We introduce the exhibition <Happy Holidays>, which captures the temperature of the year end season. Warm crafts placed throughout the space, bonsai expressing the colors of the season, soft textures and sparkling decorations, and the witty scenes created by the illustrator Drawingdaum. Cheerful and pleasant energy fills the space like selecting a gift box. May the end of this year be a little warmer and a little more sparkling. Atelier Aechae’s winter story welcomes you. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year.

title: 1st Hanbyeol Art Fair | Yeoyeo Nature 如如自然
short_description:
《1st Hanbyeol Art Fair – Yeoyeo Nature 如如自然》, a new sensory venue that fuses Korea's unique aesthetics with contemporary artistic philosophy, will be held from Saturday, July 5 to Saturday, August 16 at K Auction Exhibition Hall in Buam-dong, Seoul. 《Hanbyeol Art Fair》 is an exhibition co-hosted by Arterati and K Auction, exploring how art leaves rhythms of sensation and textures of existence in the flow of time through approximately 250 works encompassing Korean ancient art, modern and contemporary art, and international contemporary art.


This 《Yeoyeo Nature 如如自然》 exhibition proposes artistic practice that recovers 'natural as it is' nature and unmanipulated sensation based on the philosophy of 'wu wei (無爲)' derived from Taoist thought. By materializing the invisible concepts of 'breath', 'texture', and 'void' into four sensory spaces, visitors will be able to unfold a sensory journey of direct response and dwelling.


The exhibition brings together the breath of tradition and contemporary aesthetics on a single trajectory through works of various genres, including ceramics, painting, printmaking, ink painting, and poetry. 'Star One' contains the silence of ceramics centered on earth and fire, the molding of wu wei, while 'Star Two' traces the texture of emotion in repeated lines and resonance. 'Star Three' shows the temporal transition of sensation by placing ancient and contemporary art side by side, and 'Star Four' demonstrates how the void and silence become the language of thought.

title: Oh Jiyoon Solo Exhibition, 《Dignity: Accumulated Time》
short_description: Artist Oh Jiyoon is drawing the attention of the international art world, having been invited to the Venice Biennale for two consecutive sessions, from the 60th to the 61st. This exhibition is held to coincide with the opening period of the Biennale, and visitors can encounter the same series of works exhibited there. “Dignity: Accumulated Time” originates from questions concerning human existence. Through her work, the artist seeks to discuss life itself, unraveling on the canvas the anguish and pain encountered in the course of life, as well as the compassion and introspection regarding them. This process simultaneously serves as a gesture of comfort extended to the viewer.

title: Sangjaru : PLUG in Namsan
short_description: The "PLUG in" series by Sangjaru is a Korean traditional music concert that connects with the audience at specific places and times, offering a transcendent musical experience across space and time. Since their debut, Sangjaru has actively performed both domestically and internationally, promoting themselves as "Korean Gypsies." In 2024, they focused on expanding their presence overseas. For Sangjaru, the term "Gypsy" symbolizes the free and fluid life of musicians who wander and create music. Traveling both within and beyond Korea, Sangjaru absorbs the unique musical essence of each region, crafting their distinctive blend of traditional and modern Korean Gypsy music. With a stronger identity, they have come to Seoul Namsan Gugakdang after a year to reconnect with Korean audiences. Plug into Sangjaru’s woven tapestry of "Korean Gypsy Music.

title: Dalmasa Temple
short_description: Enveloped by Seodalsan Mountain, an important mountain forming the waist of the green axis connecting Bukhansan Mountain through Namsan Mountain to Gwanaksan Mountain, Dalmasa Temple is a sanctuary where you can enjoy the beautiful nature that changes with the seasons while overlooking the Hangang River and Namsan Mountain. For over 80 years, as the only traditional temple in the region, it has been a haven providing physical and mental rest and comfort to residents, as well as a modern cultural space that carries on the elegance of classics and the beauty of tradition.

title: Marriage Stories of Seoul Families
short_description: Marriage, once seen solely as a duty, is now considered a choice. To examine the pivotal moments behind these changes, the Seoul Urban Life Museum conducted an era-by-era study of the marriage culture of Seoul residents last year, culminating in this year's special exhibition. Although Korean society faced the Korean War following the 1945 liberation, it rapidly advanced, achieving the Miracle on the Hangang River, which significantly impacted marriage culture. The marriage culture of Seoul, shaped by a blend of tradition and foreign influences, continues to evolve today. We hope that looking back on the 80-year transformation of Seoul residents' marriage culture since liberation will encourage reflection on our society’s journey and foster greater generational understanding.

title: Everything Dance Hall
short_description: 《Everything Dance Hall》 is an exhibition curated by FLUX614, an emerging curator collective from the Department of Art Studies at Hongik University. This exhibition looks at our lives living in an uncertain era through the metaphor of 'dance'. Through the works of artists Kim Ga-jin, Kim Da-sol, Kim Jae-woo, Dew Kim, Seo Hye-rim, Son Ye-in, Shin Sang-jun, Shin Jong-chan, Ahn Jin-sun, Yoon Dae-won, Lee Ga-eun, Jeong Deul-dol, and Choi Ji-woo, you can encounter the rhythms and movements of different lives. The exhibition space is structured like a single dance hall, becoming a venue where different gestures and stories intersect. In addition, through participatory programs and performances, visitors can also participate as part of the exhibition.

title: Make a Wish
short_description: "Make a Wish" is an exhibition that focuses on what we have lost and need to reclaim while living in an era of lightness. Unlike the past, when unchanging universal values prevailed, in the era of lightness, where only constant change becomes the sole truth, unstable daily life has become the “new normal.” People feel the lightness of existence more than ever, drifting by clicking on links as algorithms lead them through another new normal in the digital world. In this reality, we find ourselves pondering what we can rely on to alleviate anxiety and prevent ourselves from being consumed by sadness and emptiness. We inevitably contemplate how to reclaim important things like communication, symbiosis, peace, and happiness that we are losing. Perhaps now is the time to summon the genie from the lamp and make a wish. This exhibition, presented as a kind of “spiritual journey,” aims to demonstrate the belief that humans can still uphold conditions for dignity and spiritual freedom even amidst the scattering of life's lightness. Stories initiated by the artists evolve into the audience's narratives, creating their tales, myths, and earnest prayers. These interconnected narratives are hoped to become wisdom passed down through generations.

title: The Rosy-Cheeked Pigs' Paper Adventure
short_description: To commemorate the official opening of the Children's Museum at the Seoul Museum of History, a special exhibition by FRida & freD, a world-renowned children's museum in Graz, Austria, is visiting. This exhibition is an analog interactive exhibition that focuses entirely on paper and drawings instead of flashy screens. Step away from the digital world for a moment and present a magical time where children can touch and make things themselves, becoming the main characters in their own storybooks. We invite you to a fantastic paper world filled with warm illustrations by Julie Völk, a Bologna Ragazzi Award-winning author.

title: "More, Natural" Exhibition
short_description: Superior Gallery presents the "More, Natural" Exhibition, which reminds us of the meaning of human existence in our rapidly moving modern society and awakens us to the reality that life's journey ultimately connects with the flow of nature. Artist Park Jung-yong presents his 'Stone People' series, which embodies human figures through combinations of natural elements such as rocks, trees, grass, and flowers, showcasing the organic connection between nature and humans and the resulting surreal landscapes of comfort. Artist Han Jun-ho uses elements of urban nature, such as trees, benches, and grass, as subjects to sculpturally express spaces filled with rest and relaxation that modern people instinctively crave. We hope you will feel the breath of nature conveyed through the works of these two artists, experiencing forgotten tranquility and moments of healing from seeking happiness in ordinary daily life at Superior Gallery.

title: Beauty For All: Beauty Without Boundaries
short_description:
B the B is a permanent exhibition space that curates the charming beauty brands of Seoul with its own unique sensibility.

Diagnose your skin and scalp through AI-based beauty tech devices that were previously difficult to find, and experience various programs such as virtual makeup and Life Four Cuts (photo booths). Additionally, you can receive a one-stop service where you can test recommended products based on your diagnosis and even make online purchases.

<Beauty For All: Beauty Without Boundariesis> is an exhibition curated under the theme of beauty and wellness for all. It introduces beauty brands and products that people of diverse backgrounds and lifestyles can enjoy without prejudice, while showcasing new beauty trends and sensational experiences.

title: BANKSY: Still Here
short_description: The street artist Banksy, who operates while concealing his identity, is one of the world's most famous artists, yet his true identity remains shrouded in mystery. Nevertheless, people are captivated by the powerful messages he leaves on street walls. The exhibition <BANKSY: Here Still> introduces his artistic world through images and major projects that represent Banksy. By following works that contain messages of war and peace, satire and humor, as well as hope and solidarity, we aim to examine why so many people still discuss Banksy today. The questions posed by the anonymous artist remain ongoing. While his identity remains a mystery, the messages he left behind continue to live on beside us today.

title: Geoan
short_description: Geoan, a handmade solid wood furniture store specializing in zelkova wood located on Ssamji-gil, Insadong, is an artisan brand that has been carrying on its tradition for over 30 years since it opened in 1981. The name "Geoan" is a Chinese character that means "using our products makes you feel comfortable". Founded by his father, a designer, his son, who studied furniture in Chicago, has since added new technology and design flair to create even more beautiful furniture. The products are made of the best quality wood, mainly zelkova, and are made with the highest quality.

title: Special Exhibition for the 80th Anniversary of Liberation "Prologue: With a Heart Singing to the Stars" from the Gana Art Collection
short_description:
Seoul Museum of Art has organized a special exhibition from the Gana Art Collection to commemorate the 80th anniversary of Korea's liberation. The Gana Art Collection consists of 200 artworks donated to the Seoul Museum of Art in 2001 by Lee Ho-jae, representative of Gana Art, encompassing minjung art and realism works that actively reflected the 1980s-90s Korean social realities.


Eighty years after liberation, generations who directly experienced Japanese colonial rule, liberation, the Korean War, and the division of North and South Korea have been succeeded by generations who did not experience these events. Currently, 95% of South Korea's population was born after liberation, and they have learned about modern Korean history through historical records. This exhibition aims to provide an opportunity for more profound empathy with the era by examining social, political, and historical contexts and personal narratives that were not highlighted in the grand narrative of modern Korean history through artistic works.


The exhibition is organized into four parts. The first part examines the history of hardship and sacrifice during Japanese colonial rule and the independence movement. The second part addresses the devastation of the Korean War and the tragedy of fratricidal conflict. The third part reflects on the tragedy and socio-political issues caused by the continued division after the war. The final part explores possibilities for the future through works depicting peaceful coexistence beyond war and conflict.


This exhibition particularly incorporates poetry from the 1940s-50s that conveys resistance and the will to overcome reality alongside the artworks, vividly delivering the resonance of the era. The poems contain earnest wishes for liberation, the cruelty of war overshadowed by death, and sorrow over the reality of North and South divided by ideological opposition, allowing visitors to indirectly experience that era when people persevered despite adversity.


The freedom we enjoy today is indebted to the sacrifices of previous generations. The freedom achieved through their dedication and courage is a precious heritage we must pass on to future generations. Through this exhibition commemorating the 80th anniversary of liberation, we hope to reflect on the value of liberation and create a prologue opening to a future of peace and reconciliation.

title: Kwangya@Seoul
short_description: The Kwangya@Seoul flagship store is a K-POP cultural experience space where K-POP fans can interact with artists without boundaries between reality and virtuality. It is a space crafted by celebrities, fandoms, and prosumers, merging virtual and physical realms to create a metaverse where both exist in harmony.

title: Park Hyunsung, Yoon Sukone: The rest of today going to tomorrow
short_description:
Recently, the art market, hosting grand festivals like never before, has been saturated with similar and repetitive works, overshadowing its dazzling spectacle. The era is marked by a lack of contemporary spirit, with image-based works that depict an era devoid of its essence. The selection of artists and artworks based on investment value, as well as exhibition planning focused on leisure activities and social media, are rapidly departing from the unique path of art. In this context, Park Hyunsung and Yoon Sukwone's work centers on recreating the mimetic experiences from the inception of art and challenging the categorization within the art world. Gallery Jiuhun presents the exhibition "The Rest of Today Going to Tomorrow," where the two artists connect the ever-changing time of modern society, bridging yesterday with today.

What the two artists create through "relationships" is the restoration of the space of mimetic experience. "Mimesis" is the practice of capturing the object’s appearance as it is without alteration. Amidst the absence of the subject, in a world teeming with splendid objects, their work will restore a space where more flexible relationships can be formed, taking us back to the beginning of the vivid moments of thought.

title: Maria Svarbova: The Future of Yesterday
short_description: This exhibition showcases 174 photographic works by Maria Svarbova, divided into five sections: Nostalgia, Futuro Retro, Couple, The Swimming Pool, and Lost in the Valley. It provides a comprehensive view of Svarbova's major works from 2010. These five sections delve into the artist's artistic and personal experiences, featuring her iconic series, The Swimming Pool, collaborative works with companies, and latest creations, encompassing both her past and present works. “The Future of Yesterday: Maria Svarbova Exhibition” is held at Ground Seoul, an exhibition space in the cultural heart of Insadong. It offers an immersive experience with various photo zones and invites visitors to explore Maria Svarbova's modern sensibility and artistic world.

title: Kansong Art Museum
short_description: The Kansong Art Museum has established itself as the backbone of Korean art history research based on the cultural assets collected by Kansong, who sought to protect the spirit and soul of our nation and awaken pride in our history and culture in future generations.

title: Gallery Jiwooheon
short_description: Gallery Jiwooheon is an exhibition venue operated by Designhouse, Inc., located in Bukchon Hanok Village. It was selected as the 2016 Seoul Excellent Hanok for its distinctive structure remodeled from a hanok, which offers both trad itional aesthetics and contemporary convenience and has remarkable architectural beauty. It aspires to identify outstanding new artists at home and abroad while supporting the trend of contemporary art as a gallery with temporal and spatial qualities that shines a light on contemporary art in a space possessing the history of the past.

title: Anyangcheon Stream
short_description:
Anyangcheon Stream is a tributary of the Han River that flows through Anyang-si, Gwangmyeong-si, and the Seoul districts of Geumcheon-gu, Guro-gu, Yangcheon-gu, and Yeongdeungpo-gu, eventually joining the Han River west of Seongsandaegyo Bridge.

Strolling along the Yangcheon Dulle-gil trail, you’ll discover a variety of charming sights and attractions. Highlights include the Anyangcheon Stream Embankment Cherry Blossom Road, the longest cherry blossom path in Seoul, as well as peaceful spaces like the Ecological Park, Family Garden, and Sports Park. In particular, you can enjoy seasonal scenery in the heart of the city along the Anyangcheon Stream : the Autumn Foliage Road (Anyangcheon Walkway) between Yangpyeong Bridge and Mok-dong Bridge, the Cherry Blossom Road between Mok-dong Bridge and Omokgyo Bridge, and the Anyangcheon Stream Ecological Plants Center between Sinjeonggyo Bridge and Ogeumgyo Bridge.

title: AiF children 2nd Anniversary 𝙎𝙋𝙀𝘾𝙄𝘼𝙇 𝘼𝙍𝙏 𝙁𝙀𝙎𝙏𝘼
short_description: The "AiF Children 2nd Anniversary Special Art Festa” exhibition will feature a variety of on-site programs and meaningful side events, such as commemorative performances. Over 90 supporting artists will participate. The event will also occur on October 3rd and 9th, so your participation is encouraged.

title: 2024 Creative Artist Support Project
short_description:
In October 2024, three young artists will share their special stories at the Seoul Namsan Traditional Theater!  
Creative Artist Support Project is a flagship program by Seoul Namsan Traditional Theater that discovers and supports young artists working in traditional arts, such as music, dance, and performance, by assisting with the development of new works.  Since its launch in 2018, supported by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and Crown Haitai, the Creative Artist Support Project has been dedicated to helping artists who embody contemporary values within the tradition and aims to contribute to the creative network in traditional arts.

title: Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall
short_description: During the site preparation construction process for the new Seoul City Hall in 2008, a large number of structural remains and artifacts presumed to be from the Joseon Dynasty were identified, leading to an excavation investigation. Here, various artifacts such as ceramics, coins, and roof tiles were excavated alongside structural remains like building sites and stone revetments constructed during the modern era and the Joseon Dynasty. In particular, many weapons from the Joseon Dynasty were identified, including Chongtong (gun barrels), Cheolhwan (iron cannonballs), and the Bullanggi Japo (breech-loading swivel gun) designated as a Treasure. As a result of investigating old maps and related materials, it was determined that Gungisi, a government office in charge of manufacturing weapons during the Joseon Dynasty, was located near Seoul City Hall. The Seoul City Hall site is presumed to have been part of the past Gungisi, and the Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall was created to preserve related structural remains and exhibit excavated artifacts.

title: Gallery Mosoon
short_description: Located on Jeongdong-gil, within the 100-year-old modern cultural heritage site “Shina Memorial Hall,” this gallery showcases Korean crafts and art. It was established with the hope that visitors traveling from afar will feel that their journey to and from the gallery is part of the exhibition experience itself. Unlike other spaces in Shina Memorial Hall, the gallery has been remodeled with white cube walls and ceilings to give it a more contemporary feel. With each changing exhibition, the gallery introduces new playlists, scents, and furniture, creating a fresh experience every time. Come and appreciate Korean crafts in this cozy and serene space.

title: Diffusione
short_description:
Park Eunsun, as an artist, primarily engages in works where he breaks and stacks marble slabs of two different colors and alternately or repetitively constructs unit structures in cylinders or spheres that extend endlessly toward the sky. His geometric and abstract sculptures, reaching infinitely towards the sky, demonstrate humanity’s boundless potential. Simultaneously, through the cracks in the marble slabs, his works symbolize the inner wounds of the human condition. By alternating and stacking these fractured marble slabs, Park Eunsun expresses the process of healing and reconciliation, where wounded hearts come together.


The cracks in Park Eun-sun's artworks embody his distinctive sculptural characteristic and are the central philosophy behind his creations. This is precisely why his sculptures have captivated the hearts of people worldwide. While Western sculptors often aimed to represent marble in its natural state as a solid mass, Park Eunsun's unique approach involves cutting and stacking layers of marble. These cracks also serve as the channels that touch our hearts. By intentionally breaking the strong marble and juxtaposing rough and smooth stones and stones of different colors within a single artwork, Park Eunsun's creations reflect the artist's experiences of striving fiercely to survive in a foreign country.


It is said that art reaches a higher level of completeness when there is a harmonious unity between form and ideology, and when the spirit idealizes nature and creates a faithful image of itself. Park Eunsun's works, which evoke images of ancient Egyptian obelisks or traditional stone towers in Korea, transcend time and cultural boundaries, achieving the perfect harmony between the ancient and the modern, the East and the West. These works have been born beautiful masterpieces, representing the artist perfectly internally and externally.


Park Eunsun's new work, Colonna Infinita, features a lighting installation composed of various colored marble beads, forming a pillar-shaped light artwork. With the subtitle diffusion, these works aim to convey a message of hope, particularly during the challenging times of the COVID-19 pandemic. They symbolize the infinite hope that lies ahead, offering us a message of boundless optimism for the future.


The upcoming Park Eunsun exhibition at Stellar Gallery is the artist's first solo exhibition in five years in South Korea. It serves as a celebration of the artist's world, past achievements, and honors. The exhibition will showcase Park Eunsun's works, which contain messages of infinite human potential, unity, and hope.

title: Gesture Beyond the Canvas Exhibition
short_description:
Superior Gallery has curated the exhibition 《Gesture Beyond the Canvas》 for July 2025. This exhibition demonstrates how brushstrokes, the fundamental element of painting, can function as a creative language with the power to lead artistic innovation, rather than merely being simple techniques or traces. The 《Gesture Beyond the Canvas》 exhibition focuses on the experimental spirit and creative acts of three artists who break away from the conventional framework, where traditional brushstrokes remain confined to reproduction, and attempt new expressions and reinterpret nature. Artists Kwon Jae-na, Lee Chae, and Choi Je-i each convey their artistic philosophy through their works, employing different perspectives and original brushwork.

In the 《Gesture Beyond the Canvas》 exhibition, we can see how the brushstrokes of these three artists do not simply remain within the canvas but extend to nature, life, and inner emotions. We anticipate that this exhibition will open new horizons in art, where the original brushwork and artistic challenges of artists Kwon Jae-na, Lee Chae, and Choi Je-i transcend the traditional painting framework, presenting new perspectives and sensations.

title: Where Happiness Arrives
short_description: For the artists, working evokes emotions similar to childbirth. The time of anguish and the energy condensed within that time culminate in a moment comparable to the birth of life. Choi Seung-yoon’s abstract works, which serve as the background of the exhibition, reveal the fundamental energy inherent in humanity without reservation. Behind this force lies the artist’s effort to capture on canvas countless emotions that cannot be explained one by one. The fine-brush paintings of artist Cho Jung-eun, who pays attention to vanishing things with affection, are added to the canvas, combining emotion with emotion. This exhibition thus contains narratives of anticipation and joy, as well as responsibility and fear.

title: What We Want to Talk About When We Talk About Haruki
short_description: Please check the Interpark Ticket website for more details

title: 2026 Donhwamun Traditional Korean Music Week <Between… Sound… Breath…>
short_description:
In an era filled with sounds, we are increasingly becoming accustomed to a 'state of not hearing.' You pause that familiarity for a moment and experience the 'empty space' existing between sounds.

Cast: Sound Ritual Ensemble : Cy_樂 (Won Il, Kim Bo-ra, Hwang Jin-ah, Han Ji-soo, Ven. Myeongjin)

title: Drawing Again Exhibition
short_description: Superior Gallery is pleased to present the Drawing Again exhibition by artists Kim Si-hyun and Yoo Chung-mok, who showcase original works that explore tradition within the diversity of contemporary art. Kim Si-hyun paints traditional patterned bojagi (wrapping cloth) using hyper-realistic techniques, revealing traces and beauty within their intricate designs. Yoo Chung-mok combines the five cardinal colors of Korean art with hwangma (a type of hemp) and glass, infusing traditional motifs with modern elements to suggest new possibilities in contemporary abstraction. Experience the richness of Korean sentiment in the Drawing Again exhibition at Superior Gallery, running until July 4, 2024.

title: Seoul Light DDP 2025 Fall
short_description: The Seoul Design Foundation presents Seoul Light DDP 2025 Fall under the theme “EVERFLOW: Moving Fields.” French conceptual artist Laurent Grasso will unveil a monumental media façade combining cosmic data and historical imagery. Leading digital design studio d’strict will showcase an immersive series. In addition, a laser installation by Taiwanese media artist Aka Chang will be revealed at the DDP Miraero underpass.

title: The Shape of Touch
short_description:
As in a sculpture park, how about strolling through the art gallery?

The shape of touch started from a desire to share the fun and the value of work derived from using the hands and the body to make art in the era where all materials are digitalized. This exhibition represents how materials in our surroundings are shaped into forms, all crafted by the skilled handiwork of the artist.

Artist Lee Eun-woo starts her day by heading to her studio for work. The artist sets a one-hour timer and engages in her 'drawing' without a specific purpose, simply allowing her hand to create whatever it desires. It's a repetitive habit that resembles a daily routine. Various shapes combine and accumulate by connecting dots with lines, forming interesting patterns. The finished work is transferred onto grid paper and complemented with textures and colors that suit the shapes.

The entire space of the Children's Gallery has been structured using a square grid. For the artist, the grid serves as a crucial tool for quantifying the size of objects and is the fundamental framework for her drawings. The drawing results that have become part of a regular daily routine are visualized in various ways in a grid-standardized exhibition space. Lines and shapes in a drawing may go beyond the ground and become three-dimensional as a sculpture or may be enlarged into an architectural form and pass through the structure.

Large and small sculptures throughout the exhibition hall are made from various materials around us. The artist has molded her sculptural world by spending a long time cutting and shaping materials by hand, harmonizing them with everyday objects. The sculptures' visuals reminiscent of furniture and toys, can evoke one’s favorite object.

Could there be significance in doing something 'just because' without a specific purpose? The Shape of Touch results from accumulating simple and repetitive acts of 'drawing' and 'creating' over a long period. The hope is that this exhibition serves as an opportunity to contemplate the value of the immersive experience and the sense of peace that comes from the ordinary labor of starting a day well and finding inner tranquility.

title: The 4th Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism
short_description:
The Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism, which began in 2017, addresses various issues stemming from rapid urban growth. As one of the world's prominent high-density cities, Seoul aims to rediscover the vision of a human-centered, eco-friendly city under the "Urban Architecture" theme.

The 4th Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism presents the theme "Land Architecture and Land Urbanism: City of Mountain Ranges, Waterways, and Wind Breezes- drawing of Seoul’s Next 100 Years," aiming to connect the past, present, and future by illustrating Seoul's blueprint.

title: Klimt and Laciotti: The Miracle
short_description: Please visit the Interpark Ticket website for detailed exhibition information.

title: 2025 Summer Project 《HUH, Yun-hee: The Eternal within a Moment》
short_description:
Seongbuk Museum of Art presents the 2025 Summer Project 《HUH, Yun-hee: The Eternal within a Moment》 exhibition as part of the Mid-Career Artist Revitalization Planning Exhibition project. Through the artistic world of HUH, Yun-hee, a capable artist who won the 2024 Lee In-sung Art Award, we explore the beautiful and profound essence of nature and life, focusing on 'ecological art,' one of the key themes in contemporary art.

From the <Sunrise Diary> series, which captures the daily life of Jeju's seas, to her representative charcoal drawings and <Tree Leaf Diary>, we aim to provide a space where everyone can feel and experience together through HUH, Yun-hee's works that convey profound and authentic messages through the traditional method of drawing.

title: Blue Variations
short_description: This special exhibition features seven artists, including Ko Myung-Keun, a pioneer in Korean photography and sculpture, and Kwak Intan, a young sculptor renowned for his unique work combining sculpture and painting. Also featured is Korean-American artist Jen Pak, who won a special Porsche award last year for her "Legoscape" series. Finnish photographer Tiina Itkonen, who will have her first solo exhibition in Seoul this November, focuses on global warming. Chinese artists Chen Ruo Bing and Ma Shuqing, leading figures in monochrome painting, and British photographer Michael Kenna, one of the most prominent photographers in the UK, complete the lineup for this special exhibition.

title: 2025 Seoul Art Show
short_description: Please visit the Interpark Ticket website for detailed exhibition information.

title: From One Book to the World, K-Content: K-BOOK to the WORLD
short_description: This special exhibition departs from the perspective that "the beginning of K-content was books." Bringing together ancient books, manuscripts, translated books, magazines, albums, and video materials in one place, it showcases how Korean stories are recorded, read, and expanded into various content such as K-dramas, movies, webtoons, and K-POP. It demonstrates the process where past records become present content, and today's K-content becomes future cultural heritage. The National Library of Korea aims to highlight both the depth and global expandability of Korean record culture through a new exhibition experience connecting books and K-content.

title: LOCA 3rd Anniversary Commemorative Photo Exhibition: Walking Through New York
short_description:
LOCA: Walking Through New York.

LOCA embarks on a journey to New York. Strolling through alleyways, riding the subway, shopping, taking photos, and meeting various people.

In 1950, while dining at a restaurant in Manhattan, USA, an idea sparked to make payments solely through credit. This marked the birth of the first-ever credit card. In a similar vein, LOCA focuses on a card's essence. Inspired by the birthplace of credit cards, Manhattan, New York, LOCA has launched a card designed with the motif of the Manhattan map. To commemorate LOCA's 3rd anniversary, LOCA cards are embarking on a journey to New York, capturing everyday life and iconic landmarks in photos to convey a sense of inspiration and emotion.

title: Yoonkee & Guhong's Guhong & Yoonkee
short_description:
Paintings created under rules and conditions such as "Draw 9 circles on the canvas and fill each circle with a different color" and "Play acoustic guitar for the canvas to hear" will be exhibited. This exhibition, titled Guhong & Yoonkee, opens on July 3rd at Gallery Jiwooheon.
'Yoonkee and Guhong' is the name of a web-based music duo formed in 2023 by Kim Yoonkee and Min Guhong. Kim Yoonkee (hereafter Yoonkee), who debuted in 2000, has been actively working internationally as a musician, painter, and poet in countries including the UK and Japan. Min Guhong (hereafter Guhong) works as an editor and programmer at Ahn Graphics and Workroom, while also running his company Min Guhong Manufacturing and a coding language course called New Order. For over a decade, they have been supporting each other's activities by filling in the 'gaps' beyond their individual abilities, collaborating on performances and designs. Recently, they formed a duo and are presenting Guhong & Yoonkee as their first step. Yoonkee and Guhong prepared this exhibition out of curiosity about what would happen if artists, following the development of AI technology, designed rules and conditions like prompt engineers and created works accordingly. Guhong, a programmer, reveals his primary form of expression, coding, while Yoonkee candidly displays the painting format he has approached simply and comfortably. The process of creating the works is simple. Guhong creates 20 arbitrary rules and conditions, and Yoonkee combines the items he likes to personally paint 20 pieces. Notably, Guhong's rules include not only 'codes' for brush strokes but also actions like playing music for the canvas or discussing economics with it. Here, the coding method leads to a human twist that amplifies the analog aspect. Can the audience discern which canvas listened to Yoonkee's music? Can the canvas confess that it had a sincere conversation about economics with Yoonkee? Their attempt, which makes one imagine personified canvases, is also an optimistic thought experiment about the coexistence of digital and analog. This is why music or stories can be read in Yoonkee's paintings mediated by Guhong's coding. Additionally, four paintings by Yoonkee and two media works by Guhong will be exhibited. One of Guhong's works, Twenty Ways to Fall in Love with Canvas, shows the codes applied to Yoonkee's paintings flickering through kinetic typography. Visitors can deduce how these codes were applied to each of Yoonkee's paintings. Meanwhile, in the exhibition space, music first released on 'Yoonkee and Guhong's' website (https://www.yoonkeeguhong.com/) will be played randomly along with unreleased music. Yoonkee and Guhong described this exhibition as "improvised melodies drawn on a score of rules, twenty variables created by one algorithm." It sounds like an incantation suggesting that conforming to the inevitable technology of AI will open up possibilities for rich enjoyment rather than creating humans with submissive selves without will. This premise raises the fundamental question of "what questions to ask and what to enjoy in the face of rapidly changing technological environments." Thus, Guhong & Yoonkee presents results born more humanly within a mechanically generated framework, offering a light-hearted outlook on the future of art.

title: Olive Better Gwanghwamun Branch
short_description: Olive Better is a wellness-specialized store introduced by 'Olive Young,' a famous Korean Health & Beauty (H&B) store. The Gwanghwamun Branch is the first Olive Better store, and since it is close to Gyeongbokgung Palace and Gwanghwamun Square, it is easy to visit conveniently during sightseeing. It is curated to allow visitors to experience the wellness 'All The Better' and the healthy convenience food 'Well Express' on the 1st floor, and all 6 wellness routines tailored to the flow of the day on the 2nd floor. Additionally, at the tea brand experience space, 'Tea Bar,' you can experience a new tea every month.

title: Samseyoung
short_description: Samseyoung aims to be a cultural and artistic space that embraces the past, present, and future. Opened in December 2021, Samseyoung reflects on the past through the collection of antique art that the founder has gathered over 20 years. It is also a space where contemporary cultural and artistic figures come together to engage with the present while looking forward to the future.

title: Euphoric Proliferation
short_description:
Gallery Jiwooheon will host Euphoric Proliferation, an exhibition featuring Yi Young-uk and Jojae, from March 27th to May 4th. Both artists have recently received attention by winning awards for young artists at prominent domestic art museums. The exhibition focuses on their work, which is similar in the context of fragmenting, distorting, and amplifying images but differentiated by the abstract and figurative nature of the results.
Since 2018, Yi Young-uk has been boldly exploring methods of redefining the concept of the subject. His distinctive theme revolves around creating bizarre patterns by repetitively distorting parts of human and animal bodies, which have become a hallmark of his work.
JoJae's work originates in the virtual realm. Since 2016, she has been sculpturally translating digitally rendered images and their original analog counterparts. By shaping the gap between digital images and their unprocessed originals, she constructs a new sense of connection between the virtual and the real worlds.
In this exhibition, Jojae presents works that extend from his ongoing “Crumbs Series,” which involves the reconstruction of urban landscapes and byproducts of digital images collected over time.

title: 2025 ＆TEAM CONCERT TOUR ‘AWAKEN THE BLOODLINE’ in SEOUL
short_description: Please check the Interpark Ticket website for more details

title: 《Imagination Garden : Fantasy Time》  Exhibition
short_description: In December 2025, Superior Gallery will hold the solo exhibition Imagination Garden : Fantasy Time by artist Song Sujeong, which reveals an inner emotional world through an imaginary garden and the flow of light. This exhibition depicts landscapes where reality and imagination naturally connect, focusing on inner emotions, ideal scenery, and the symbolic images held by life in the garden. Recording scenes that remain in the heart through paintings, the garden that depicts a space where calmness stays is an imaginary place where the mind can rest for a moment at the point where reality and ideals meet. We hope this exhibition becomes a time to reopen the world that has been quietly breathing in each heart and to discover a new landscape of your own. The Imagination Garden : Fantasy Time Exhibition runs until January 13, 2026.

title: Cho Min-yeol ⟪Blue, Hidden, Nature⟫
short_description: The second theme of the exhibition, ECO, features the “Blue, Hidden Nature” showcase, presenting a creative transformation of denim scraps discarded by sewing factories near the artist's studio. Denim, an icon of the Industrial Revolution, is cut, layered, and reassembled, gradually returning to a state reminiscent of nature. Through the artist’s touch, the textured denim surface evokes the natural world's unaltered surface. May this glimpse of nature within the hanok building inspire thoughts of the warm spring to come.

title: Hanji House Docent Program/Permanent Experience Program/Hanji Print Studio
short_description:
Docent Program: A guided tour that provides professional commentary to help visitors understand the Hanji House. This program explains the culture of hanji and the significance of each space.

Permanent Experience Program: This is a permanent craft experience program where you can make hanji souvenirs using traditional hanji. Through programs planned according to the season, you can experience the various properties of hanji.

Hanji Print Studio: If you apply for photo printing using the QR code provided in the space, we will print your photo on the hanji of your choice. The process from application to printing and drying takes about 10 minutes, and you can pick up your photo on the spot.

title: 65th Anniversary of the April 19 Revolution Seoul City Commemorative Concert
short_description:
This commemorative concert is being held to remember the historical value of the April 19 Revolution that protected democracy, and to honor and inherit the spirit of sacrifice of democratic martyrs.

Following a classical performance featuring the KBS Symphony Orchestra, La Poem, and soprano Son Ji-soo, popular singers Yang Ji-eun, Kim Soo-chan, and Seol Ha-yoon will participate to create a gathering of harmony with citizens.

title: The 5th Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism
short_description: Since its inception in 2017, the Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism has established itself as an experimental platform to explore innovative solutions to urban challenges faced worldwide. This year, under the direction of globally renowned designer Thomas Heatherwick, the Biennale will focus on how to make urban architecture more engaging and appealing, encouraging public dialogue and exploration. From September 26 (Friday) to November 18 (Tuesday), 2025, visitors can experience diverse exhibitions and programs at the Open Songhyeon Green Plaza, the Seoul Hall of Urbanism & Architecture, and the surrounding areas.

title: 2025 Seoul Intangible Cultural Heritage Festival
short_description:
Experience the value and charm of tradition up close through a variety of programs such as performances, hands-on activities, demonstrations (and tastings), and exhibitions centered on Seoul’s intangible heritage.


[Event Overview]


Venue: Namsangol Hanok Village and Seoul Namsan Gugakdang


Period: September 27 (Sat)–28 (Sun), 2025 / 11:00–17:00


Content: Performances of Seoul’s intangible cultural heritage arts, hands-on activities and demonstrations (tastings) of functional heritage, and exhibition programs


Side Events: Wedding event photo zone, traditional experiences, and other programs

title: Smile Keeper 展
short_description:
Superior Gallery presents artist Kim Ba Reu's Smile Keeper exhibition, which conveys a message of positivity through captivating pieces of flowers and smiles.
Artist Kim Ba Reu captures attention by repetitively arranging vivid flowers and smile patterns, conveying a cheerful mood and encapsulating positive energy through smile images that evoke emotions. The artist creates embossed artworks of flower pieces to convey happiness through the transmission of accumulated emotions.
Through an exhibition that preserves and spreads the lovely feeling of ‘smile,’ we hope visitors who encounter the work will widely collect smiles at Superior Gallery.
Kim Ba Reu's Smile Keeper exhibition will be held until May 1st.

title: Haerang
short_description: Haerang is a spacious restaurant with 180 seats. The main menu here is spicy seafood stew that is overflowing with fresh and in season seafood. The side menu includes large grilled shrimp, oysters, and other fresh seafood. Lobster can be enjoyed both as sashimi or in a stew so keep in mind that this can be ordered in addition to the spicy seafood stew. The haemultang (spicy seafood stew) includes abalone porridge, blue crab, live octopus, scallops, mussels, steamed squid, shrimp, monkfish, and more.

title: Wolfgang's Steakhouse
short_description:
Named after its founder, Wolfgang Zwiener, Wolfgang's is a popular steakhouse with locations all over the world. Taking his 40 years of experience from working as a waiter at Peter Luger Steakhouse, one of the most successful steak restaurants in New York City, Wolfgang Zwiener opened his own steakhouse which has now become a popular steakhouse in its own right due to his know-how.

Try USDA prime black Angus that has been dry-aged for 28 days. With 13 branches all over the world, this is the first Wolfgang's Steakhouse to open in Korea. The restuarant can fit 225 people with a dining hall and bar on the first floor, and 7 private rooms on both floors. The rooms can accomodate anywhere between 6-20 people, perfect for business meetings or family gatherings. A private service is also availabl e.

title: Nanhyang
short_description: Ever since its opening in October 1993, Nanhyang has been recognized as an authentic Chinese Restaurant that is “clean and delicious.” Nanhyang handpicks its ingredients in an effort to provide its customers a healthier eating experience. Due to its large interior space, it’s also a popular spot for hosting birthday parties, large group gatherings, and other big events.

title: Sanho
short_description: Sanho is a Korean bar that uses traditional Korean cuisine as anju (food eaten with alcohol). The complimentary side dishes that are served are especially tasty. The interior atmosphere is very clean and modern.

title: Cuisson82
short_description: The pleasant atmoshpere of Cuisson82 will make you feel like you're visiting a typical French home.  Enjoy traditional home style meals at an affordable price at this French bistro.

title: Suyeon Sanbang
short_description: Suyeon Sanbang is a traditional tea house that was converted from a hanok (traditional Korean house), with a style that is classic and antique. Author Lee Tae Jun, a pioneer of Korean short fiction, used to write books in this house, and in 1998, one of his siblings' granddaughters opened a tea house here. Light refreshments, such as bamboo shoot rice cakes tossed in bean flour or filled with red bean paste, can be enjoyed with traditional Korean teas.

title: Goshen
short_description: Located on Cheongdam-dong Hill, this café has long been a fixture of Cheongdam-dong. In its early days, it was very famous for its unique atmosphere and classy interior. They have recently undergone renovations, with the restaurant now featuring a new, modern atmosphere.

title: Dublin Terrace
short_description: As you might guess from the name, Dublin Terrace is an Irish pub. It's a good place to enjoy Guinness on tap. Every March, they host an Irish dance party, called a "hooley," to celebrate St. Patrick's Day, and from 7 PM until 1:30 AM, it's all-you-can-eat-and-drink, including Guinness.

title: Guillaume
short_description: This is a traditional French bakery well known for its baguettes, macaroons, meringues and éclairs. The first floor was designed like a typical country home, while the 2nd floor is styled after a luxury French apartment.

title: Evans
short_description: Evans is one of the oldest clubs in the Hongdae area. They have different performances every day, and a new group of musicians takes over every month. You can enjoy a cocktail or beer while watching a concert. The live jazz performance starts after 9 p.m.

title: All That Jazz
short_description: Opened by Chinese-American Ma Myeong Deok in Itaewon in 1978, All That Jazz is the first jazz club in Korea. They have a collection of over 2,000 records and around 600 CDs, and the collection chronicles the history of jazz in Korea. From Monday to Thursday you can come and enjoy the jazz music without paying a cover charge, as long as you meet the drinks minimum (5,000 won). They have recently moved from their original location to a space near the Hamilton Hotel in Itaewon.

title: Romanee Conti
short_description: Enjoy a variety of French cuisine paired with one of the 180 wines they offer. One recommended item is the coq au vin (chicken braised in red wine), a home-style chicken dish from France. The restaurant was converted from a Korean traditional house (hanok) and has a traditional outdoor reception area where several groups of guests can get together.

title: Fresca 29
short_description: Cafe Fresca is a Dogok-dong area café famous for their excellent coffee. The café opens onto a terrace, so it looks quite spacious. They roast their coffee beans in-house, and also offer coffee-themed classes.

title: Pungwoldang
short_description: Pungwoldang is a classical music store and cultural space in Cheongdam-dong. Visitors can shop for classical music CDs and books on classical music. There is even a listening room dubbed "Pungwolchae." Pungwoldang hosts cultural events such as lectures on classical music, video screenings, and musical events. Pungwoldang also has a cafe that sells light refreshments.

title: Grill Ajisai
short_description: Enjoy regional Japanese cuisine prepared by a Japanese chef at Grill Ajisai. Given that this is an izakaya (a Japanese-style bar), it only seems right to have some sake with your meal. The lunch menus, such as tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet), sukiyaki (Japanese hot pot), and omelet with rice, are popular with local office workers, so much that you almost always have to wait in line.

title: Jangchu
short_description: Jangchu specializes in fresh-water eel at affordable prices. They partially pre-grill the eel for your convenience, so that it can be grilled more quickly on the cooking plate at your table. They serve a set menu of rice and savory chueotang (loach soup) boiled and served in an earthenware bowl.

title: Budnamujip
short_description: This is the place you come back to because of the memorable taste. The marbling of the meat is so even that it looks like a piece of art. This is the right place to visit if you would like to treat your family or important guests.

title: Taco Amigo
short_description: A place where you can taste Mexican food at an economical price. There are various types such as tacos, quesadillas, burritos, and fajitas, and you can choose the fillings from sausage, beef, chicken breast, cheese, etc.

title: Pyeongyang Myeonok (Nonhyeon Branch)
short_description: This branch of Pyeongyang Myeonok is located south of the Han River, and like the other branches this one also serves Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles), served either in a tangy broth or mixed with spicy chili sauce. The food here tastes so good that people say that it is better than at the main branch. Try the Pyeongyang-style mandu (Korean dumplings) and suyuk (boiled beef) with the naengmyeon. Expect long lines to get in.

title: Daebanggol
short_description: Daebanggol is famous for its delicacy savory, well-dried oysters which are eaten in green tea water -- as well as octopus, and skate and abalone from Heuksando Island.

title: Danme Green Bee
short_description: "Danme Green Bee" refers to a gentleman meeting a lovely woman and and the two living harmoniously together. Located on the edge of Daemosan (mountain), this is a restaurant to enjoy well-prepared courses while surrounded by nature.

title: Songjukheon
short_description: Songjukheon has served hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hôte) meals for over 20 years. Gujeolpan (a platter of nine colorful ingredients served with thin crepes), steamed abalone, various Korean pancakes, steamed fermented skate, grilled sweetfish, and grilled eel are the representative dishes at this restaurant, and the various dried pickled vegetables, salted and fermented dishes, and kimchi that they serve are appetizing. You can enjoy authentic food from Jeollanam-do, the southern province of the region of Jeolla, in a relaxing atmosphere, making this a good place to entertain foreign guests. Since they only prepare the food in advance based on reservations, advanced booking is required.

title: Omiga (Sinsa Branch)
short_description: This restaurant serves up nostalgia and the kind of delicious, homemade food that your mother fed you when you were little.

title: Yi Ning
short_description: Yi Ning serves authentic Szechuan and Cantonese Chinese cuisine in a stylish black Western-style interior decorated in a minimalist approach. One of the most popular dishes is the steamed rockfish garnished with coriander, ginger and shredded green onion, but if you'd like something more exotic, try the gajisaeu (a shrimp dish with eggplants) or the balchaejjim (steamed black moss-fat choy). In Cheongdam-dong, where restaurants are always coming and going, this one been running for a long time.

title: Yeongwol
short_description: Yeongwol isn't a fancy Korean restaurant, but the food is quite light-tasting and well-presented for the price. One popular dish is naksaejjim (steamed octopus, shrimp, and other seafood with chili powder). Kal-guksu (handmade noodle soup), sujebi (handpulled dough soup), and boribap (boiled barley rice with a variety of sautéed vegetables and chili paste) also good options for a tasty meal.

title: Haeju Naengmyeon
short_description: For 30 years, Haeju Naengmyeon has been well-known for naengmyeon, a chilled buckwheat noodle dish available either in an iced broth or mixed with a spicy red chili sauce. The bibim naengmyeon (with spicy chili sauce) is famous because it's very spicy, but also because it only costs 4,000 won. If you love spicy food, it's worth trying. Sugar is available on the table, and some people like to add some to their bibim naengmyeon to enhance the flavor. The mul naengmyeon (in an iced broth) is made with a perfect amount of mustard and vinegar, so the sweet and sour flavors are nicely balanced.

title: Ohsaegyehyang
short_description: A vegetarian restaurant that serves Korean, Chinese, and Western cuisines.

title: Choedaegamne
short_description: Converting seven traditional Korean houses into one large restaurant, Choedaegamne serves traditional han-jeongsik (Korean table d'hote) meals. A popular choice for lunch is shabu shabu served with Korean lettuce topped with rice balls and meat. The pork ribs and beef are also good.

title: Slunch Factory
short_description: Slunch specializes in healthy low calorie lunchboxes. The restaurant does not use any artificial flavorings and features a new lunch menu every day.

title: Bong Ee Bab Insadong Branch
short_description:
