Bong Ee Bap is a Korean restaurant that offers traditional flavors passed down through generations. As a true Korean cuisine specialty restaurant, its interior design highlights the beauty of Korean tradition. An English menu is also available, allowing locals and foreigners to experience the taste and charm of Korea.
In the rapidly changing modern dining culture, Bong Ee Bap aims to create distinctly Korean and universally appealing food, offering unique flavors at reasonable prices. Their goal is to craft dishes that current and future generations will love.

title: Korea House
short_description: You can enjoy fine-quality beef skillfully served at Korea House. They provide top-grade meat for grilling, such as outside skirt and well-marbled ribeye roll.

title: LUNA VINE
short_description: Korean fusion cuisine is the main fare at Luna. Classic Korean dishes, like bossam (steamed pork and kimchi), boiled hangjeongsal (pork neck meat), roast beef, and mero gui (grilled toothfish) are updated with a contemporary twist. The multi-course set menu meals offer a good variety of dishes at reasonable prices.

title: Byeokje Galbi
short_description: The galbi (beef short ribs) served at Byeokje Galbi is reputed to be the most delicious in Seoul. They use only choice cuts of prime Korean beef, matured for four to seven days. Their secret is the marinade, a mix of soy sauce, syrup, spices, and salt flavored with seven ingredients. Though a meal here won't be easy on the wallet, your taste buds will thank you.

title: Gwangyangbulgogi
short_description: Bulgogi is a common dish in the Republic of Korea, but Gwangyangbulgogi has a unique taste based on a special seasoning so that it carries on the tradition. The side dishes are very delicious, not only the bulgogi.

title: Sariwon
short_description: Where you can taste the home-made healthy Bulgogi made by Sariwon grandmother, which she made for her diabetes  husband. The delicious beef with 12 fruits sauce and vegetable juices(pineapple, apple, orange, salad, onion, kiwi, pear, etc) without artificial seasonings and sugar is served.

title: Buminok
short_description: Buminok is a yukgaejang specialty restaurant located in Dae-dong, Jung-gu, that was beloved by office workers during the 1980s and 1990s. Founded by an owner from North Korea who established the business based on his experience running a shop in Bumin-dong, Busan during the Korean War, Buminok's yukgaejang is characterized by its generous portions of scallions and beef, offering a clean and light flavor. In the evenings, many patrons visit to enjoy yukgaejang paired with soju. The restaurant provides a comfortable dining atmosphere with spacious table arrangements.

title: Ssangdari Doaeji Bulbaek
short_description: Ssangdari Doaeji Bulbaek has been run by two generations for over 30 years. Lots of people come to have meat grilled over charcoal briquettes. You can't cook the pork yourself at the table like at most barbeque restaurants, which is this restaurant's only shortcoming. But you don't have to wait a long time, and the affordable price is a big plus, making it easy to enjoy.

title: Palsun
short_description: Palsun is one of the best Chinese restaurants in Seoul, with a selection of several hundred authentic Chinese dishes from Guangzhou, Szechuan, and Beijing. The food, atmosphere, and service live up to their reputation. The kitchen will even cater to the individual tastes of loyal customers. Many famous names from the political and business worlds frequently drop by.

title: Daejangjangi Hwadeok Pizza Jip
short_description: Daejangjangi Hwadeok Pizza Jip is a very famous for their oven-baked pizza. The pizzas come topped with generous amounts of high-quality ingredients. Reservations are recommended on weekends and public holidays.

title: Kangkangsullai (Sanggye)
short_description: Ganggangsullae (Sanggye) is the place between Mt. Surakand Mt. Dobong. The popular menu, grilled assorted Korean beef uses only 100% Korean beef that is fresh and carefully chosen. Such as thin skirt, ribs, meat attached to the spleen, fleshes from the inside ribs, meat on short ribs and sirloin are served.

title: Nolboo Sulfur Duck Restaurant
short_description: Sulfur duck roasted in mud is cooked for 3 hours in an earthen ware oven at 450° so that this dish takes a long time and devotion. There are plenty of Danggui (radix angelicategigantis), ginseng, antlers, licorice roots, gingko nuts, figs and pine nuts with steamed rice inside the duck.

title: Mokpo Jamaejip
short_description: Run by four sisters from Haenam, Mokpo Jamaejip specializes in the regional food of Jeollanam-do (the southern province of the region of Jeolla). The Namdo-style side dishes are made with natural ingredients delivered from Haenam and taste delicious.

title: Sangrakwon
short_description: Specialized, high-quality restaurant in the downtown, in which lawn and garden are mixed. The place with quiet, wide garden, home atmosphere and comfortable mother’s taste. It improves the real value of traditional Korean table d’hote by cooking pollution- free material delivered from producing area.

title: Samil Jeongyuk Sikdang
short_description: Samil Jeongyuk Sikdang is a barbecue restaurant where you can grill fresh meat. Any of their cuts of beef, such as brisket point cut, are good choices for dinner, and at lunch time, spicy marinated pan-fried pork with rice is popular.

title: Taerim Sanchae Jeongsik
short_description: This restaurant is famous for its dishes of wild vegetables, Deodeok and roots of balloon flowers. Grilled sliced pork, comes with Table d’hote of assorted wild vegetables and grilled Deodeok and is also very tasty. Water kimchi made from mineral wateris deliciously spicy as well.

title: Hachiho
short_description: Hachiho is a sushi restaurant doesn't use expensive fish, but the sushi they prepare is elaborately presented and made with good-quality ingredients. Seating is very limited, so reservations are required.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Chamnureongso
short_description: Chamnureongso serves Korean ribeye, chuck tail flap, outside skirts, and marinaded galbi (ribs) as well as various other side dishes.

title: Dobongsan Galbi
short_description: Situated at the front of Dobongsan (mountain), Dobongsan Galbi is a restaurant with a 30-year history and tradition of using the best ingredients and high-quality Korean beef.

title: Busanbokjip
short_description: This is a specialty restaurant of fresh swellfish dishes that have been loved by customers for the past 35 years. Crispy and moist radishes and leeks, the taste of soup made from sea tangle are memorable for a long time. This place is quite busy so that it is better to make reservations in advance during the winter.

title: Hanwoori
short_description:
Exclusive Authentic Shakuma Shop
 This place specializes in shabu shabu with 24 years of tradition that insists on using original Korean beef fillet. The best Korean beef is mouthwatering as it is directly delivered from the farm in Gwangju, Jeonnam, each day. The organic seasonalvegetableswith shabu shabu, the hand-made soy bean curd and the springy noodles with the rich broth are so tasty.

title: Gungnara Naengmyeon-Mukbap
short_description: Acorn-starch jelly with gravy and seasonings mixed with rice together is called rice with acorn-starch jelly. This restaurant prides itself on using acorn-starch jelly hand-made instead of buckwheat jelly. Jelly, slippery enough to escape from spoons,softly melts once it reaches the mouth without giving a moment to chew.

title: Miel
short_description: This stylish gallery café harmoniously blends the concepts of an art gallery and a café. The interior is all white, so the atmosphere is bright and hip. Light desserts like waffles are popular here.

title: Heachorok
short_description:
The serene waters literally moved now operation Abalon shop

Natural live fish restaurant originated from clean area of Namhae. You can taste the best seasonal raw fish here. (Spring - sole, Summer - parrot fish and flat fish, Fall - gizzard shad and Winter - roughscale sole)You can find the generous mind that treats each customer preciously with discriminated service and atmosphere.

title: Dalgaebi
short_description: ‘Cafe & Side Dish Shop’ operated by Conference House Dalgaebi consists of a cafe and side dish shop where you can experience food culture using kimchi as an ingredient. Dalgaebi Side Dish Shop is where you can experience the food philosophy of Dalgaebi Kimchi CEO Ham Sun-hyo.

title: Lamb Land
short_description: Lamb Land specializes in Korean-style lamb barbecue. Served with garlic, kimchi, and cucumbers, the lamb chops are grilled right at your table. The fried lamb here follows a Chinese recipe, and their freshly-grilled lamb tastes delicious with salad and a little mustard sauce made of olives, perilla seed powder and lemon juice, all wrapped up in 'geolle' bread, which is similar to Indian naan bread. They use mutton, which is similar to lamb but has its own strong distinctive taste.

title: Chaesundang (Sinnae)
short_description: Chae Sun Dang stands for "where the vegetables are fresh" and serves fusion Korean shabushabu mixed with Thai Suki. Well-being dishes with organic vegetables, fillet and fresh seafood in soup will energize the fatigue and tired modern people up.

title: Bukakjeong(Isanggalbi)
short_description: Where you can find the nature inside city. Grilled beef ribs marinted soy sauce with 26-year know-how provides you with the delightful world. You can feel the owner's consideration through free tea lounge allowing chat.

title: Jangwon Bugeoguk
short_description: This bugeoguk (dried pollack soup) restaurant has a great reputation in the Yeouido area. The clear broth with thinly sliced tofu and beaten egg has a light, refreshing taste. In the morning, this place is a popular stop for people trying to get over a hangover, as dried pollack soup is reputed to be a good remedy.

title: Kangkangsullai(Sillimbondong)
short_description:
Warm heart at & customs space

The interior and decorations of small mud walls with a wooden rafter brings a warm atmosphere to Ganggangsullai (sillim-dong branch). The popular menu, grilled sullae seasoned Korean beef is cooked with the best quality of Korean beef, so that youcan taste very well the seasoning of the sullae beef ribs.

title: Seokparang
short_description: This place is a Korean table d’hote restaurant in a detached house in SeokpaJeong. Food at the royal table is served in antique vessels. A full course dinner starts using traditional rice porridge and consists of a colorful platter of nine ingredients with thin crepes, lean meat (short ribs) mixed with vegetables, grilled fresh abalone, and Korean royal court casserole (shinseollo).

title: Ju Bean
short_description: Ju Bean is a cozy hand-drip coffee shop. They have more than 150 kinds of coffee beans from coffee-producing regions throughout the world, and you can be sure that they are as fresh as possible since they roast them on the premises. To extract the optimum flavor from the freshly-roasted beans, they brew their coffee using special cotton flannel.

title: Norangjugory (Gangnam)
short_description: Norang Jeogori that has an antique mood of traditional Korean house in the complex downtown. You feel that you are important here. You can enjoy warmful dishes in the wide front yard, back garden and reception room of traditional Korean house. More than 10 dishes, which are sincerely prepared with a mind of new bride of the head family, and local side dishes are very tasteful.

title: Miseongok
short_description: Miseongok has been famous for their seolleongtang (ox bone soup) ever since it opened in 1966. Their seolleongtang is made with quality ox bones and beef for which they have a loyal following.

title: Yeachon (Shinga)
short_description: Single path with Traditional Korean Cuisine for 46 years Specialized local food restaurant opened by the chief of Cheongdam and Nonhyeon Todamgol and the manager of Hotel Shilla. You can feel the heartful taste of hometown from doenjang, ganjang and gochujang because they are made here directly. You can try each kind of jjigae made of organic materials such as sigoldoenjangjjigae, haemulsundubujjigae, gopchanggimchijjigae and congbiji.

title: Samho Jjangttungi
short_description: At Samho Jjangttungi, you can enjoy the authentic taste of food from Jeollanam-do, the southern province of the region of Jeolla, which is a bit salty and uses lots of salted and fermented ingredients. They either grind jjangddungeo (bluespotted mud hopper), bones and all, and boil it with dried napa cabbage, or they boil the fish whole, to make delicious maeuntang (spicy fish soup).

title: Gaehwaok
short_description: This restaurant has re-interpreted traditional Korean cuisine into a more modern and stylish cuisine. Although its main menu item is bulgogi, Gaehwaok serves many other delicious dishes such as grilled vegetables and soybean noodles. The traditional Korean dinnerware the food is served in also adds to the overall taste and atmosphere.

title: Jinjin Mandu
short_description: At this famous mandu (Korean dumpling) restaurant in Yeouido, you can have manduguk (Korean dumpling soup) made with thick beef broth and tasty mandu.

title: Gomguksijip
short_description: Gomguksi is proud of homemade noodle and deep soup of boiled brisket of beef. The cooked beef made by boiling the brisket of beef is a very special delicacy Japanese, as well as Korean come and visit this place to taste home-made style dishes. Very deliciousside dishes also attract you here.

title: Spain Club
short_description: Spain Club is a Spanish tapas-style bar. One advantage is that, since the food is served in small portions, you can sample a wide variety of Mediterranean-style dishes. The food tastes even better when accompanied by sangria or Spanish wine.

title: Mayfield Hotel
short_description: 30-year traditional Korean food store. You can enjoy the aesthetical Korean food, which is tasty and neat, under the beautiful landscape that enables you to feel the comfort of nature. The hand that serves the side dish shows the feeling of health.

title: Kwak Kyung Chan's Sigol Bapsang
short_description: The owner of Kwak Kyung Chan's Sigol Bapsang hails from the province of Jeolla-do, which is well known for its delicious and hearty foods. Here food is served the old fashioned way, with rice, jjigae, and numerous side dishes that take up the entire table. The interior of the restaurant adds to the traditional atmosphere and makes the food that much more delicious.

title: Nammuntobang
short_description: At this place, you can taste crushed loach soup In Gyeongsangdo style and fried loach. Sulfur duck shabu shabu with ducklings fed with sulfur and vegetables, as well as sulfur duck casserole are also very delicious.

title: Hanilgwan
short_description: After years of success in the Jongno area, this famous restaurant, Hanilgwan, recently opened in Gangnam.

title: Bongraeheon (Mayfield Hotel)
short_description: Bongraeheon, serves noble and delicious Korean dishes. You can enjoy natural royal Korean dishes displaying clean and neat taste and harmony of ingredients because the restaurant uses the best ingredients. The restaurant is frequently used for the receptionof domestic and foreign customers.

title: Nampomyeonok
short_description: Nampo Myeonok, established in 1972, was founded by owner Kwak Bong-sun, a native of Jinampo in Pyeongan Province, who settled in Seoul after the Korean War and introduced North Korean-style cold noodles. Now operated by the third generation, the restaurant's Pyongyang cold noodles are characterized by using dongchimi fermented underground in the traditional Pyeongan Province method as the broth. It is said that past presidents have also frequented Nampo Myeonok to enjoy its cold noodles. Inside, there are traditional floor-seating tables where you sit cross-legged, allowing you to experience Korea's traditional seating culture while dining.

title: A Table
short_description: A Table is a French restaurant that features comfortable and stylish French cuisine. The daily special depends on what ingredients are bought fresh each day. They serve only set menus, and their specialties are tenderloin, sirloin steak, and marinated lamb chops.

title: Wooraeok
short_description: Pan-fried beef (Bulgogi) and cold noodles are popular dishes. Customers especially never forget the true taste of cold noodles and come back again. This is because the simple flavor of broth is made solely from beef. While it keeps the tradition for 60 years, it entered the market of the USA and tries to globalize the dishes.

title: Panax
short_description: This restaurant specializes in samgyetang (chicken and ginseng soup), which they have served for over 15 years. The samgyetang here is simple with a traditional flavor, and is served with ginseng wine.

title: Gayang Kalguksu Beoseonmaeuntang
short_description: The speciality at this restaurant is beoseot maeuntang, a refreshingly spicy mushroom stew. As the stew first starts boiling, oyster mushrooms and traditional Korean herbs are simmered in the broth, then removed and served. Handmade cut noodles are added to the broth next. After most of the soup has been eaten, a nutritious mixture of stir-fried rice with eggs and diced vegetables is prepared using some of the flavorful broth.

title: Jihwaja
short_description: Operated by “Living Treasure Of Korean Royal Cuisine” since 1991, Jihwaja is a high-class traditional Korean restaurant located in the center of downtown Seoul. It has enjoyed a high reputation as the finest restaurant that offers The Legitimacy of Korean Royal Cuisine, the essence of the Korean food culture.Jihwaja reflects the sophisticated ambiance of the neighborhood that features a 600-year Joseon Dynasty history. And has been offering very healthy and nutritious dishes, as they are prepared with only natural ingredients and royal culinary techniques, without using any MSG, artificial flavors or additives. Jihwaja has been committing to promote Korea's authentic traditional food culture-Korean Royal Cuisine across the world through the generations.

title: Gumasan
short_description: Gumasan has long been famous for loach soup and sizzling marinated beef ribs. The beef, brought to your table freshly grilled, can be a little sweet, but it pairs nicely with the Masan loach soup.

title: Iseungnamui Kkotgwa Ppang
short_description: The bakers at Iseungnamui Kkotgwa Ppang made a name for themselves by using flowers to decorate their cakes. You can also taste various cupcakes. You need to place an order one day in advance for one of their flower-decorated cakes. Produced and sold on the same day, so it’s fresh.

title: Sujeong
short_description: Sujeong specializes in saengtae (fresh pollack) dishes, and their saengtaetang (spicy pollack soup), which is full of egg sacks and innards, is especially excellent. Many people come for saengtaetang at lunchtime, so expect long lines.

title: Daeyeo
short_description: This restaurant has maintained its reputation as a juk (porridge) specialty restaurant ever since it opened in the Yeouido financial district in 1983. The juk here are savory and crisp-tasting due to their use of fresh, seasonal ingredients. The mostpopular dishes are the abalone juk, the mushroom and oyster juk, and the shrimp juk.

title: Jindong Hoetjip
short_description: You can enjoy jabeohoe (sashimi made with various small fish) and sekkosi (shredded raw fish). Customers mostly order the assorted platter, or sekkosi, which in this restaurant is a platter of shredded flatfish, flounder, and sole. With every order of sashimi, they serve a refreshing and delicious seaweed soup with fish. They offer an assortment of fishes, such as spot belly rockfish, yellowtail amberjack, black rockfish, black sea bream, gizzard shad fish, sea bream, and horn fish, depending on seasonal availability.

title: Neobijip
short_description: Neobijip is famous for spicy galbi jjim (braised short ribs). The beef ribs are marinated in a spicy sauce and then are steamed with rice cakes. It is a very popular dish with Japanese tourists in the Myeongdong area. The fresh galbi and vegetable hot pot are also excellent. They also offer yukhoe, a Korean version of beef tartare in which seasoned, marinated beef is served raw.

title: Ariake
short_description: Ariake is one of the best Japanese restaurants in Seoul, particularly famous for the freshness of their ingredients. They offer a selection of around 90 authentic dishes, showcasing the light-tasting and stylish cuisine of the Kansai prefecture. There is a private room featuring a dignified, modern atmosphere and a harmonious black and white decor that can accommodate four to ten.

title: Sodo
short_description: Sodo in Yeouido serves Japanese cuisine exclusively. The sashimi course offered at dinnertime is excellent. This is a good place to entertain guests.

title: Mado
short_description: Mado is famous for fried noodles. You'll find noodle dishes named for the main ingredient they're stir-fried with, whether it's seafood or beef. Savour a harmony of flavors: a sauce of simmered seaweed, radish, and grilled garlic, onions, and shallots; katsuobushi (dried, fermented, smoked tuna); and udon noodles of perfect thickness.

title: Seongminchon
short_description: Seongminchon is a shabu shabu restaurant with a 20-year history. They serve fresh seafood delivered daily directly from Yeosu. For lunch, the noodles and dumpling hot pot are popular with office workers in the area.

title: Huijeong Sikdang
short_description: Huijeong Sikdang serves budae jjigae (spicy sausage stew) made with generous amounts of sausage and ham. The broth is somewhat spicy and light. This place is well-known among the business people in the Yeouido area.

title: Hwangsaengga Kalguksu
short_description: Hwangsaengga Kalguksu (formerly Bukchon Kalguksu) is one of the most popular restaurants in Samcheong-dong. Big meat dumplings and noodles served in beef broth – this is what Hwangsaengga is all about. The dumplings contain nine different types of vegetables. Try to steer clear of the busy lunch and dinner hours if possible to avoid long waits for seats.

title: Ttalgigol Bunsik
short_description: The reasonable prices at Ttalgigol Bunsik have made it a favorite among students of Ehwa Women's University for over 40 years. You can choose from a variety of Korean food, but the bulgogi dolsot (marinated thinly shredded beef in a stone pot of rice)and sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) are the most popular.

title: Mamma KiKi
short_description: This wine bar is a great place to relax and enjoy some wine. Boiled eggs are served as a basic side dish, and there are also such fusion side dishes as samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) and salmon, which are excellent. They have a good selection of wines in the 30,000 and 40,000 won range. The recommended side dish is samgyeopsal seasoned with horseradish sauce. It is fully packed at dinnertime, but unfortunately they do not take reservations, so arriving early is recommended.

title: Miumiu
short_description: Miumiu serves Hanwoo The meat is grilled over charcoals in a ceramic brazier. A selection of wines are available to accompany the meat, and the décor of the restaurant is modern.

title: Dorim
short_description: Enjoy Chinese cuisine in an atmosphere that seamlessly combines the classic and modern with great views of Seokchon Lake and Jamsil.

title: Alladinui Yanggogi
short_description: Alladinui Yanggogi is a restaurant that specializes in Arabic-style lamb. Lamb is seasoned Arabic-style and chargrilled. The lamb meat wrapped in pita is delicious.

title: Eoyang
short_description: Eoyang's speciality is seafood. Fish, such as sea bream and rockfish, are caught on the fly from a large aquarium in a corner of the kitchen. They offer an assortment of sauces that go nicely with shrimp or meat, and you can order your choice of sauce, just like in China. They are also well-known for eoyang duban juice, made by boiling pork shanks with Asian medicinal ingredients, and then steaming them.

title: Retrooven
short_description: Located in a quiet residential neighborhood, Retrooven is a bakery that is well known for its tasty bread. They offer many kinds of bread, like ciabata and olive bread, and their primary concern is the taste of the bread itself, rather than the amount of fillings. The bread has an excellent chewy texture. Most of their bread is sold-out early in the afternoon, it is advisable to either visit early or call ahead.

title: La Bonne Tarte
short_description: La Bonne Tarte dessert shop's mission is to make snacks that are healthy, even for children. They offer pies made with various ingredients, such as walnuts, walnut cream cheese, walnut chocolate chips, sweet potatoes, pumpkins, chocolates, apples, andblueberry cheese. You can also enjoy a cup of tea with your pie

title: Musha
short_description: Musha is one of the izakaya (Japanese-style bars) which have recently become so popular in the Seorae Maeul area. Their sake list is quite good. They have an open kitchen, rooms with Japanese tatami floor mats, as well as outdoor tables.

title: Biwon Son Kalguksu
short_description: Biwon Son Kalguksu is a kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) restaurant that has been in the Changkyunggung palace area for 30 years. The noodle soup is made with Korean beef flank and is light-tasting and delicious. Their mandu jeongol (dumpling hot pot) is also very good. The delicious dumplings are stuffed with mushrooms and other ingredients.

title: Aji Gen
short_description: At Aji Gen you can get a drink accompanied by Japanese tempura and odeng (skewers of fish cake cooked in a broth). The restaurant is Japanese-owned, so the majority of the customers are Japanese. The fried dishes are the best, like the crispy deep-fried chicken karaage or agedashi tofu, which is battered and served drizzled with soy sauce.

title: Chuncheonjip Dakgalbi Makguksu
short_description: Chuncheonjip Dakgalbi Makguksu is a dakgalbi restaurant. Dakgalbi is a dish of spicy chicken and vegetables that is grilled on a massive hot plate right at your table. The meat is boneless, making it easy to eat. Macaroni salad and kimchi comes as sides.

title: Niwa
short_description: Niwa is a cozy izakaya (Japanese-style bar) located within the traditional market that is in the center of Korea's Japanese neighborhood of Ichon-dong. It is quite hard to find, but they always have many customers at dinner time.

title: Builgalbi
short_description: Builgalbi is the Seoul branch of a famous galbi restaurant in Busan. The representative dish here is sogeumgui, partly-frozen thinly-sliced sirloin that is grilled and dipped into an egg yolk-based sauce. To cleanse your palate after the meat course, take the opportunity to try their naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles),  available either in an iced broth or mixed with a spicy chili sauce. Popular choices for lunch are their yukgaejang (spicy beef soup) and galbi-tang (short rib soup).

title: Bongsanjip
short_description: Bongsanjip is renowned for grilled chadolbagi (brisket point cut). The great taste comes from the marinade, a mix of soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, green onions, onion, and chili pepper.

title: Namseoul Minmul Jangeo
short_description: The food is very fresh at Namseoul Minmul Jangeo; eels are put on the grill only once the order has been taken. The first course is eel bone tempura, eel porridge, and sauce. Fresh live eel is grilled front and back and basted with seasoning sauce five times, for about half an hour. The eel soup is made from eel bones that have been boiled and reduced for about five or six hours and is flavored with Chinese cabbage and Korean soy bean paste, yielding an exquisite flavor.

title: Winenara
short_description: ​Located at the entrance to Seorae Village, this premium wine select shop offers wine classes and space rental on the basement level.

title: Nodeulgang
short_description: Nodeulgang is famous for croaker, a type of fish eaten (particularly in summer) for its energizing properties. The croaker is cured, giving the fish a nice firmness. After the croaker sashimi, a soup is served, made with the same fish. In addition tothe croaker, their hongeo samhap (a combination of three ingredients: aged skate, boiled pork, and fermented kimchi) also tastes great.

title: Obaltan
short_description: Obaltan makes delicious grilled beef tripe and large intestine. The secret behind the great taste is the marinade; red pepper powder, pineapple, garlic, ginger, sugar, and starch syrup are added to soy sauce and reduced with green onion and licorice root.A nice way to end the meal is with savory cheonggukjang (a stew of fermented soy bean paste) and nurungji (a thin crust of scorched rice from the bottom of the pot). Recommended for lunch are gopchang jeongol (a spicy casserole of beef intestines andvegetables) and yangbap (rice fried with sliced tripe on a griddle).

title: Macha Hoejip
short_description: You can enjoy wild hoe (sashimi) and seafood here. This restaurant isn't luxurious, but their food is quite satisfactory for the price. The restaurant is not very big, but it is very clean. Both wild and farm-raised fish are available.

title: Hakoya
short_description: Hakoya specializes in Japanese ramen, udon, and soba (buckwheat noodles). They serve regional varieties of ramen, such as Hakata-style tonkatsu ramen (with pork broth) and Hokkaido-style shoyu ramen (with soy sauce). The noodles are all imported directly from Japan.

title: Daewoo Budae Jjigae
short_description: Daeu Sikdang is the place to go to have spicy budae jjigae (spicy sausage stew). The main ingredients of this stew are ham, sausage, minced beef, rice cakes and noodles. The restaurant is comfortable and spacious, making it great for company dinners.

title: Western China
short_description: This is a traditional Dim Sum restaurant. If you’d like to try various kinds of dim sum and other Chinese dishes, try the set menu. In addition, the salad and fruit bar buffet is open to all.

title: Sicily
short_description: Sicily is a cafe that specializes in hand-drip coffee, and is well-known for its excellent-tasting coffee. Here, you'll find raw coffee beans which are also available for purchase. They also offer light fare such as pasta dishes served with salad, bread, and coffee. The atmosphere here is classic and comfortable.

title: Itsumo
short_description: At Itsumo you can enjoy a variety of Japanese side dishes, such as tofu tempura and octopus salad seasoned with vinegar, both of which go nicely with ponzu sauce. Recommended is the Nagasaki chanpon, a spicy noodle soup with seafood and vegetables. The broth made from pork bones is poured over fried vegetables at high heat, and the resulting soup tastes refreshing and good to the last drop.

title: DUBLIN
short_description: This Irish pub offers Guinness on tap for which they are quite popular. You can enjoy other imported beers fresh on tap besides Guinness. A wide variety of bottled beers are also available, including Hoegaarden, Kilkenny, Erdinger, and Sapporo.

title: Sushi Gen
short_description: Lots of people come here for chirashizushi, sushi presented on top of a bowl of rice, rather than on bite-sized clumps of rice, which is more common. On top of the chirashizushi, you'll find generous portions of tuna, salmon, eel, flounder, sea bream, squid, shellfish, or sea urchin roe. For dinner, they offer a unique dish of warm changkonabe (a Japanese stew of meat and vegetables) and anju (Korean side dishes consumed with alcohol).

title: Sohojeong
short_description: Sohojeong specializes in gukshi, the traditional food of the Korean gentry from Andong, a city in the Gyeongsang region of Korea. A variety of other Korean dishes are on the menu as well. The special set menu, which comes with meat, jelly, Korean pancakes, and even noodles, is a substantial meal.

title: Manbongnim
short_description: At Manbongnim specializes in traditional Chinese cuisine that has been adapted to suit Korean tastes. Before moving to their current location, this restaurant was located in the Tower Hotel.

title: Tour du Vin
short_description: Tour du Vin boasts a wine list of over 500 varieties, including quite a few unusual wines that are hard to find. Cheese plates, salads, and pasta dishes are also available.

title: Songnimwon
short_description: The owner of Songnimwon hails from Shandong Province in China, and has been running this traditional restaurant for over 50 years. Although the interior is shabby, the prices are reasonable and the food is quality. Here, you can enjoy Chinese food the way it was prepared in the 70s and 80s.

title: Di Matteo
short_description: The specialty of Di Matteo is traditional Naples pizza. Authentic Italian restaurants are everywhere nowadays, but when this restaurant first opened, their thin crust Italian-style pizza was a rarity and became a big hit. They offer 26 different kinds of pizza, but since any of their pizzas can be ordered with either Italian or Danish cheese, you could say they offer over 50 kinds.

title: Doenjang Yesulgwa Sul
short_description: The representative dish at Doenjang Yesulgwa Sul is their savory doenjang bibimbap (soybean stew served with a bowl of mixed rice and vegetables), served in a large bowl.

title: La Saveur
short_description: La Saveur offers authentic classic French cuisine like Bourgogne-style snails, goose liver, and Dijon-style sirloin. The tenderloin steak is recommended, as is the Bulsora, a small conch-like shellfish from Jeju Island, served as an appetizer with herbed butter.

title: Darakjeong
short_description: A specialty of this restaurant is the dumpling casserole boiled in soybean broth with a lot of seafood. Other popular menu items include dumpling soup, Korean pancakes and bulgogi. Both Korean and Western tables are available.

title: Yeonhuidong Kalguksu
short_description: A broth made from beef leg bones boiled down for twelve hours forms the base of Yeonhuidong Kalguksu's enjoyable kalguksu, handmade knife-cut noodle soup. In addition, their suyuk (steamed meat) is also worth trying.

title: Eulmildae
short_description: For more than 40 years, Eulmildae has been offering Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon, made with handmade noodles served in an icy-cold broth. Because they use a lot of starch in their noodle dough, the noodles may not be to everyone's liking, but some people are crazy about them. Suyuk, a boiled beef dish made with brisket point cut, is also excellent.

title: Ojangdong Heungnamjip
short_description: The Ojangdong-area has many restaurants that serve Hamheung-style naengmyeon, a North Korean style of cold buckwheat noodles, but Ojangdong Heungnamjip is supposed to be the best and is the most popular among Koreans whose families originated in the north. Their bibim naengmyeon (chilled buckwheat noodles mixed with chili sauce) is served with sliced beef and the hoe naengmyeon comes topped with raw skate. As you might guess, the mixed naengmyeon includes both beef and raw skate. The noodles made from sweet potato starch and the sour flavor of the raw skate really stand out.

title: Dongbuk Hwagwawang
short_description: Dongbuk Hwagwawang specializes in the regional cuisine of Yanbian in northeastern China, the representative dishes of which are lamb skewers and huǒguō (Chinese hot pot). They also serve Cantonese dishes, including several varieties of tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) with tomato sauce, pineapple, and lemon. Prices are relatively low.

title: Won Daegutang
short_description: Won Daegutang has made daegutang, codfish soup, for over 30 years. Every morning, they buy cod and vegetables and boil them in a cauldron which makes two hundred servings at a time to make their rich tasty soup. The spicy broth is a good cure for a hangover. They do not take reservations, so you'll have to wait in line.

title: Hyundae Kalguksu
short_description: At Hyundae Kalguksu, you'll probably have to wait in line to have their kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup). Their broth is made with seven ingredients, including anchovies, kelp, dry shrimps, and pollack, and is very refreshing. They replenish your noodles and rice as often as you want. In the summer, another good choice is kongguksu (noodles in cold soybean soup).

title: Ja-in Mungtigi
short_description: Ja-in Mungtigi uses only premium beef from cows raised in Jainmyeon, Kyeongsan in the North Gyeongsang province. "Mungtigi" refers to the rump bone, which is cut in large portions and served raw. To prepare mungtigi, the meat is served on rice and topped with sauce. Yukhoe, seasoned thinly-sliced beef tartare, is also worth trying.

title: Rosehill
short_description: At this fusion Korean restaurant, sirloin and grilled short ribs are the main fare. They have an à la carte menu of about thirty different dishes, as well as full-course set menus. The Korean-style filet of grilled tenderloin in cognac sauce is outstanding.The decor is stylish and modern, and reminiscent of a wine bar.

title: Mongnan
short_description: The house specialities are tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) and jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup). As dongpayuk (steamed and braised pork) takes quite a while to prepare, advance reservations are advisable.

title: Philkyungjae
short_description: Philkyungjae is a centuries-old hanok that was once home to members of Korean nobility and is now an acclaimed hanjeongsik restaurant. The building holds the designation of Traditional Structure No. 1. In 1999, a hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hote) was established at Philkyungjae and the restaurant has won plaudits ever since its opening.

title: Vicolo
short_description: Vicolo is an affordable Italian restaurant. Here the most popular dish is the seafood cream spaghetti covered with a dough crust. Break through the crust to reveal spaghetti with a cream sauce and a nice mix of mussels, clams, shrimps, and squid. Their light-tasting pizza and soft tiramisù are also good.

title: The Green Table
short_description: The Green Table is a "semi-bistro" run by three sisters. Here you can enjoy casual bistro-style French cuisine. The interior is uniquely decorated with various plates and pastel colors.

title: Gangnam Gyoja
short_description: Following a 30-year stint at Myeongdong Gyoja, a famous kalguksu (noodle soup) restaurant in Myeongdong, the chef opened this second branch in Gangnam. Here the kalguksu broth is made from chicken bones. Noodles and rice are unlimited here. The mandu (Korean dumplings) and bibim guksu (noodles mixed in a spicy sauce) are also recommended. Take-out is available.

title: Baengnihyang
short_description: The terrific views from Baengnihyang, situated on the top floor, and the luxurious décor of the restaurant create a nice dining atmosphere. Serving authentic Chinese-style cuisine, the restaurant has become a popular setting for business meetings and family get-togethers.

title: Michiru Sushi
short_description: Michiru Sushi is quickly gaining popularity due to their reasonably priced sushi. Their neta-style sushi is made with generous portions of fish. Sake makes a great accompaniment. Reservations are required due to limited seating.

title: Jangwonjip (Jangwon Jokbal)
short_description: At Jangwonjip, you can enjoy jokbal (pigs' feet) and bindae-tteok (mung bean pancake). It was a very popular restaurant in the Pimatgol area for a very long time, but it had to move because of redevelopment in the area. The restaurant's current atmosphere is pleasant and less gritty than the previous location's atmosphere.

title: Baegwon
short_description: At Baegwon, you can enjoy four regional styles of Chinese cuisine, which are equally represented on the menu, including such famous dishes as steamed abalone with shark's fin, steamed shark's fin, Beijing-style duck skin dishes, sautéed assorted seafood and vegetables, and bird's nest soup. The restaurant boasts excellent views of the river and Yeouido Park. Also available are private rooms of various sizes, ideally suited for business meetings.

title: Hwangtogil
short_description: Hwangtogil specializes in hangari sujebi, which is hand-torn noodle soup, and sanchae bibimbap, which is a mixed-rice dish served with sautéed traditional Korean vegetables, seasoned bean sprouts, spicy julienned radish, sautéed zucchini, oak mushrooms, and deep-fried soy bean curd. The sujebi dough is made with bean flour and ground peanuts mixed with flour and aged for two or three days.

title: Cheongjinok
short_description: Cheongjinok began in 1937 under the name "Pyeonghwagwan" as a small haejangguk (hangover soup) restaurant frequented by woodcutters. After liberation, it changed its name to Cheongjinok and established itself as the epitome of haejangguk in Seoul. Boasting a deep and savory taste by simmering beef bones for 24 hours and adding various ingredients like intestines, tripe and intestines, and seonji (beef blood pudding), the flavor is certainly guaranteed, having specialized in haejangguk for nearly 90 years. The interior is spacious and clean, with photos depicting the history of Cheongjinok displayed on the walls.

title: Cheongiljip
short_description: Cheongiljip is famous for crispy Bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and Jokbal (pigs' trotters cooked with soy sauce and spices). To make their Bindaetteok, ground mung beans are placed on the grill and then garnished with meat, kimchi, and other ingredients.

title: Seogung
short_description: Seogung is famous for gunmandu (fried Korean dumplings). Here the gunmandu is stuffed with beef rather than pork, and there is a wonderful hint of ginger. A good variety of Chinese cuisine is also on the menu.

title: Piyang Kong Halmoni
short_description: Piyang Kong Halmoni specializes in dishes made with soybeans, like doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew), kongbiji jjigae (puréed soybean stew), sundubu jjigae (spicy soft tofu stew), and kongguksu (noodles in chilled soybean soup). There are four kinds of soybean pulp stew; plain, kimchi, radish, and mushroom. The North Korean-style piyang mandu (Korean dumplings) are somewhat small but are handmade fresh daily and are available for take-out. Soybean liquid is also sold in 1.5 L plastic bottles, it's a bit like soy milk.

title: Haenghwachon
short_description: Haenghwachon is a Chinese restaurant run by a Chinese immigrant. Their food is the most authentic original Koreanized Chinese food in the alley. They are famous for their samseon jjamppong, a spicy white noodle soup with generous amounts of seafood.

title: Geumhong
short_description: Geumhong is a small, Japanese-style Chinese restaurant with mainly black décor. The food is low fat and light-tasting. Among their most popular menu items are kansosaewu (chili shrimp) and sacheontangmyeon, a Szechuan-style clear and spicy noodle soup with Shiba shrimp.

title: Sinheung Jeongyuk Sikdang
short_description: Sinheung Jeongyuk Sikdang, located in the butcher-restaurant alley near Daechi Intersection, is worth a visit. They specialize in Korean beef sirloin which they serve but also sell in their butcher shop. Interestingly, they grill the meat on iron plates that are heated up and greased with beef tallow.

title: Sinmi Sikdang
short_description: Sinmi Sikdang has been in operation for 20 years. Their gamjatang (pork backbone stew), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), and chargrilled spicy pork ribs are excellent. The portion of ribs is generous and quite satisfying. On weekdays, they can get very busy, making it difficult to find a seat.

title: Songane Noodles
short_description: Korean beef bulgogi (marinated thinly-sliced beef) and gomguksu (wheat flour noodles in a thick beef bone soup) are the most popular items here. Another popular menu item is the North Korean-style wangmandu (large dumpling). Because they serve simple main dishes and elaborate side dishes, this place is a favorite with many.

title: Busan Yanggopchang
short_description: At Busan Yanggopchang, you can enjoy small intestines at a relatively low price. One big plus is that they grill the food over charcoals. The plump small intestines seasoned with fresh garlic are quite nice. Another favorite is the tripe hot pot with generous portions of small and large intestines.

title: Urang
short_description: Urang is an izakaya (Japanese pub) where you can have yakiniku (grilled thinly-sliced marinated beef) and sashimi. The yakiniku is served with its own small brazier, so that you can grill the meat, vegetables, and onigiri (rice balls) right at the table. Food here greatly complements the sake.

title: Sinseonggak
short_description: Sinseonggak is a Chinese restaurant that uses only handmade noodles in their jajangmyeon (noodles with black soybean sauce). Although their menu doesn't offer the usual main dishes that can be found at Chinese restaurants in Korea, but there are a few noodle dishes, tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork or beef), and japchae (clear noodles stir-fried with meat and vegetables). Their jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup) is made with mussels, clams, zucchini, napa cabbage, cabbage, and shitake mushrooms, and has a nice spiciness that enhances the flavor of the ingredients. Alcohol is not served here.

title: Ouga
short_description: Ouga is a Korean barbecue restaurant that offers both pork and beef. Various vegetable side dishes are served along with the main meal, so it's quite healthy. The rice is served in a bamboo container that you can take with you when you are finished with your meal.

title: Gohyangjip
short_description: This simple handmade noodle restaurant has been around for 20 years. At Gohyangjip, there are no secret recipes or elaborate garnishings on their food, just great-tasting kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup)—the kind that Korean grandmas would cookfor you at home. Their manduguk (Korean dumpling soup) is also popular.

title: Myeongpum Janchiguksu
short_description: Myeongpum Janchiguksu specializes in noodles, but they are especially famous for their refreshing janchi guksu (vermicelli-style noodles in anchovy broth seasoned with soy sauce) and slightly sour-tasting bibim guksu (noodles mixed with assorted vegetables in a spicy sauce). The prices are low and and the portions are generous, so expect long lines at mealtime.

title: Potala
short_description: Potala specializes in Tibetan cuisine made by Tibetans. Thukpa is a Tibetan noodle soup, and momo is akin to dumplings. The interior is decorated in traditional Tibetan style. You can download discount coupons from the website

title: Itaewon Sutbulgui
short_description: Itaewon Sutbulgui is a premium Korean barbeque restaurant and butcher shop. The prices here are quite high, but that is expected for high-quality fresh meat. They grill the beef over charcoals in a gridiron. If you plan on ordering premium sirloin, advanced booking is required since quantities are limited.

title: Goo STK 528
short_description: Goo STK 528 has become famous for their aged beef steak. The storeroom here is located right near the entrance so as soon as you come in, you'll be able to see where the meat is being aged. The price depends on how well-aged the available meat is, so you should be prepared to sometimes pay more than you were expecting.

title: Mano di Chef
short_description: Mano di Chef is an Italian bistro where you can enjoy pizza and pasta comfortably. Their cranberry pizza is well-known, as is their unique gorgonzola pizza, with its black squid ink crust. Enhance your meal with one of their 250 varieties of wine.

title: Herzia
short_description: The name of this Italian restaurant, Herzia, means sunflowers in Spanish.  Also good is their dish of fried sirloin, seafood, and vegetables seasoned with sauce. The basement floor has special seating for couples with a blind that can be lowered so you can enjoy your meal without interruption. You can enjoy a nice view of Myeongdong and Namsan (Mt.) at night from the second floor.

title: Gulbi Maeul
short_description: Gulbi Maeul's specialty is gulbi, grilled dried yellow croaker, although all kinds of seafood are available here, including stingray. Highly recommended is the barley-aged yellow croaker; the dried fish, which are buried in barley and matured for a month,are served with rice soaked in cool green tea.

title: Mandujip
short_description: This restaurant has been serving large Pyeongyang-style stuffed mandu (Korean dumplings) from the same location for more than 20 years. The original owner hailed from Pyeongyang, and now her children continue to offer the same great-tasting food. Their menu is simple, but the mandu jeongol (mandu hot pot) and the manduguk (mandu soup) they serve are full of nutritious ingredients and quite filling.

title: Yamamoto Sushi
short_description: Authentic sushi prepared with pride by Yamamoto Tsudao, a master of sushi with 40 years of experience can be enjoyed at this sushi restaurant. They carefully select only the best pieces of bluefin tuna every day. One item on the menu that they take particular pride in is their negitoro, thinly sliced otoro (the front part of the bluefin tuna belly) garnished with chopped leeks and seaweed and eaten with genuine wasabi.

title: Grand Ciel
short_description: Grand Ciel serves open-faced sandwiches on German-style yeast bread, herb salads, various pasta dishes, and other western fare. The yellow exterior wall and open terrace make you feel as though you are at a European cafe. It's packed with young people on the weekends who come for brunch.

title: Geumseong Steak
short_description: This restaurant in the Apgujeong area has been famous for a long time, primarily for their budae jjigae, a spicy sausage stew with ham and kimchi, which is very popular. Because they use mature, spicy kimchi to make their budae jjigae, it`s a bit on the spicy side. Enjoy it with modum-gui, a combination of steak, bacon, ham, sausage, and vegetables all grilled together on an iron griddle, for a savoury meal.

title: Rossini
short_description: Rossini is a restaurant that features many different kinds of northern Italian style pasta and steak. Here, the flavors are authentic and not flashy. The restaurant itself is very quiet as well.

title: Yeosu Dongchon
short_description: Although the styles of Jeollanam-do (the southern province of the region of Jeolla) cuisine are varied, Yeosu Dongchon features the traditional cooking of the Yeosu area. The representative dish at this restaurant is the local variation of samhap (a dish of pork neck, aged kimchi, and cockle shellfish), and shellfish like cockles and comb pens. In the summer, hamo (pike eel) shabu shabu is recommended. For lunch, you can enjoy meongge bibimbap (a bowl of rice topped with fresh chopped sea squirt, sautéed and seasoned vegetables, and chili paste), and raw crabs marinated in soy sauce, in addition to many other dishes.

title: Vitamin Cafe&Pub
short_description: The concept behind Vitamin Cafe is health and beauty, and so all of the beverages on offer here are enriched with vitamins. The interior décor is brightly colored and full of vitality, so the atmosphere here is energizing as well.

title: Mongno
short_description: Mongno specializes in Pyeongyang-style mandu (Korean dumplings). In addition to mandu they also serve manduguk, a soup in which these dumplings are cooked in a clear beef broth made from slowly boiled beef bones. The soup is a hearty and clear. Also recommendedis the nokdujeon (Korean pancakes made with mung bean) and their various other noodle and rice dishes.

title: Yeongdong Seolleongtang
short_description: Yeongdong Seolleongtang has been developing their expertise at cooking for 30 years. Their best dish is seolleongtang, a milky-white soup made by slowly simmering oxtails and bones. The only other dish on the menu is suyuk (steamed meat). If you're trying to eat less fat or are on a diet, you can order a lighter version of seolleongtang that contains less fat.

title: Chez Flo
short_description: Chez Flo is a French pub recently opened by Kitchen Flo, a well-known French fusion restaurant in Seorae Maeul. They offer French and Japanese cuisine. It is a good place to go for a drink as the prices are relatively low.

title: Inamjang (Samseong-dong Branch)
short_description: This is the Samseong-dong branch of Inamjang in Euljiro that, for 30 years, has been maintaining the same great taste of their seolleongtang (ox bone soup). The broth is simmered for two days, making it thick and flavorful, and to this they add thick slices of high-quality meat. If you order a large bowl, they add slices of very tender beef tongue. The kimchi and radish kimchi that is served at the restaurant is available for purchase to take home.

title: Just Steak
short_description: Just Steak specializes in dry-aged Korean steaks. The prices are attractively low. Reasonably-priced wine is also available to enjoy with your steak.

title: Samseong Wonjo Yanggopchang
short_description: Samseong Wonjo Yanggopchang is famous for their stuffed gopchang-gui (grilled intestines). After your main meal is done, delicious fried rice is prepared on the same griddle. The cheonggukjang (soup prepared with fermented whole and ground soy beans) with the fried rice is thick, and consistently delicious.

title: Bongpiyang (Bangi Branch)
short_description: This is the Bangi branch of Bongpiyang, which is famous for dwaeji galbi (spareribs) operated by the same owner as Byeokje Galbi, a beef galbi restaurant. Though the prices are not cheap, the taste and quality of the food here is excellent. Their naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles served either in a tangy iced broth or mixed with spicy red chili sauce) is very popular and said to be true to the way it is made in Pyeongyang. They have a savoury lunch set that includes galbi and your choice of naengmyeon or doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew).

title: Gran Gusto
short_description: Gran Gusto has gained popularity for its innovative approach to Italian cuisine, especially with its mackerel and anchovy pasta. They also cater to those with a taste for more traditional Italian fare. A very pleasant dining experience for the price

title: Gisoya
short_description: At Gisoya specializes in home-style Japanese food. The chefs here create an exquisite harmony of flavors with Japanese udon (thick noodles) and Korean kimchi or chili powder. Various bento set meals are available, including tonkatsu (breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet) and katsunabe (breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet in broth with beaten egg), all of which include a bowl of udon.

title: Mi Piace
short_description: Mi Piace is one of the oldest restaurants in Cheongdam-dong. offers a combination of homemade authentic French and Italian styles. The décor, tableware, and accessories are quaint, and their appetizers, entrées, and desserts are comparable with the very best. The menu changes every season, revealing new delights. Mi Piace Vino on the second floor is a nice place to enjoy wine until late at night.

title: Hanseong Kalguksu
short_description: This famous kalguksu restaurant in Gangnam has a proud 20-year history. The guljeon, savoury pancakes made with fresh oysters, are fantastic in the colder months. The kalguksu (handmade, knife-cut noodle soup) is served in beef broth is worth trying. This is a good place to have a drink because there is a good selection of side dishes, such as jeyuk (spicy beef with vegetables) and bindae-tteok (mung bean pancakes).

title: Cavallo Bianco
short_description: Cavallo Bianco is an Italian restaurant that specializes in set-menu meals. The restaurant has several private rooms to suit your individual needs, however, an advanced reservation is advisable. Both the first and second floors have a terrace, and there is a live concert performed on the first floor every day (except on Sundays).

title: Myeongdong Hamheung Myeonok
short_description: Myeong-dong Hamheung Myeonok is a naengmyeon specialty restaurant that was established in Myeong-dong in the late 1970s. Featuring luxurious interior decorations and air conditioning, along with outstanding food quality, it gained popularity among professionals and artists, who referred to it as "Myeong-dong crowd." The first-generation owners, a married couple from Hwanghae Province, are renowned for their Hamgyong-style hoe naengmyeon. The restaurant is characterized by its spicy sashimi and mixed sauces made with over 30 fresh ingredients, seamlessly blending modern sensibilities with traditional flavors

title: Kkotji
short_description: Kkotji uses blue crabs delivered from Seosan to make their ganjang gejang (crabs marinated in soy sauce) and other crab dishes. You can also enjoy specialty dishes local to the west coast of Korea, such as steamed blue crabs, live octopus, and octopus soup with gourds. They offer a set menu for two people which includes half a crab per person, making it an affordable way to try ganjang gejang.

title: Jeonju Sikdang Cheonggukjangjip
short_description: Jeonju Sikdang Cheonggukjangjip is famous for cheonggukjang (fermented soybean paste stew). Their cheonggukjang doesn't have the usual strong distinctive smell, but it still has plenty of flavor. The cheonggukjang also tastes great with the accompanying side dishes, like kongnamul (cooked soybean sprouts flavored with sesame oil) and musaengchae (julienned white radish in sweetened vinegar). Their raw crab marinated in soy sauce is also famous.

title: Baetgodong
short_description: It was Baetgodong that first introduced ojingeo bulgogi (spicy marinated squid) to Seoul, so you can imagine this restaurant is quite popular. Expect to wait in line, even on weekdays. The octopus and squid are quite spicy, but also have a pleasant sweetness.

title: Cheongdam Bokjip
short_description: This luxurious restaurant specializes in pufferfish. The pufferfish sashimi set menu comes with pufferfish sashimi, "konee" ribs, pufferfish bulgogi, pufferfish tempura, and clear pufferfish soup with watercress and mung bean sprouts, followed by pufferfish rice porridge and dessert. Only fresh pufferfish is used, so prices are quite high.

title: Daechi Jeongyuk Sikdang
short_description: Daechi Jeongyuk Sikdang is a meat barbeque restaurant that also operates a butcher shop. They serve many cuts of beef, like beef from the inside ribs, thin skirt, and thick skirt, all of which you can barbecue over charcoal. Their pork is also good, including gabeurisal (cheek meat) and hangjeongsal (meat from the back of the neck). The house speciality is their meat, so there are few side dishes.

title: Jinjujip
short_description: This place is well known for its noodles in soybean soup. Other than the rich soybean soup noodles, there is also spicy noodles and noodle soup with chicken. Jinjujip is a favorite with nearby office workers.

title: Jungsik Seoul
short_description: Opened by an ambitious chef who studied and worked in Spain, the United States, and elsewhere, Jungsik Seoul is the pioneer of a new style of cuisine: New Korean. Although still not fully formed, the style re-approaches Korean dishes from a French perspective. The plating is avant-garde, and the blending of Korean and Western cuisine is evident in their choice of ingredients and menu. Lunch and dinner are both served in one full-course set menu which changes every two or three months.

title: Saebyeokjip
short_description: Serving a varied menu featuring grilled beef, haejangguk (a spicy soup), and shabu shabu, Saebyeokjip is open 24 hours and is often crowded with people. The ddarogukbap (a kind of soup made with meat, coagulated ox blood, and bean sprouts) tastes great and is the recommended remedy for curing a hangover. An order of yukhoe bibimbap (white rice topped with garnished raw beef) includes a bowl of seonjitguk (soup made with coagulated ox blood). The shabu shabu is quite satisfactory for the price, so it is popular. The restaurant is packed in the morning, with people sobering up, and in the evening, with people who come for the grilled meat.

title: Papaho
short_description: This Vietnamese restaurant specializes in authentic pho (rice noodle soup) and banh xeo (savory stuffed pancakes). You can enjoy Vietnamese food in a comfortable atmosphere at reasonable prices. Another recommendable dish is the deep-fried crispy rice wrapper "chajo", stuffed with minced pork, black mushrooms, and cellophane noodles.

title: Cheongdamgol
short_description: Cheongdamgol became famous for its savory Nurungji Baekban (scorched rice set meal). It is served with Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi stew), a main dish, and at least ten excellent side dishes, such as steamed eggs with chopped vegetables, crabs marinatedin soy sauce, and seasoned vegetables. It is hard to find this kind of comfortable Baekban restaurant in the Cheongdam area.

title: Keungiwajip
short_description: Keungiwajip is a hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hote) restaurant that specializes in set menu meals that feature Jeolla-do-style side dishes and Pyeongyang-do main dishes made with seasonal ingredients. Their most famous dish is ganjang gejang (crab marinated in soy sauce). The restaurant was created from a traditional Korean tile-roofed house.

title: Dukkeobi Jeongyukjeom Sikdang
short_description: This butcher shop/restaurant carries premium-grade beef. Here, you can grill quality Korean-bred beef on copper grills over oak charcoal. The meat is purchased directly from the butcher, and then grilled at your table. Vegetables are an additional 3,000 won.

title: Byeokje Galbi Tower Palace
short_description: Named one of the five best restaurants in Asia by Wall Street Journal Asia, this restaurant has also been called one of the 50 best restaurants in a major metropolis. Come here to try domestic Seolhwa beef and delicious beef stock.

title: Cafe Monday To Sunday
short_description: Cafe Monday To Sunday is decorated with chairs from famous furniture designers. The exterior brick walls are painted white, which gives the place a clean appearance and a vintage look. In addition to the usual cafe beverages, waffles, pasta dishes, andwine are also available. Brunch is available as well.

title: Cake House Wien
short_description: This bakery is over 20 years old and sells old-style Korean breads. A popular menu item is the monaka ice cream sandwich, originally from Japan.

title: Lisian
short_description: Lisian is an American-style Chinese restaurant, like the ones you would find in Chinatowns back at home. Seafood is picked out fresh directly from their fish tank. One popular dish is the shrimp in wasabi cream sauce.

title: Bistro de Yountville
short_description: This is a casual French bistro. The course menu is a little pricy, but comes with a dessert of your choice. Individual dishes are reasonably priced.

title: Hongneung Galbijip
short_description: Hongneung Galbijip boasts 30 years of tradition. Their grilled galbi (short ribs) is very famous in the Hongneung area for its mild and delicious flavor. Their marinated beef galbi is made with 20 different kinds of ingredients. Bones from the galbi and four leg bones are reduced to make naengmyun yuksu (meat broth), which is rich and flavorful.

title: Madang
short_description: This café surrounds a garden in the middle of the Hermès Dosan Park building. At this high-class café, you can expect premium service and quality, offered in an elegant atmosphere featuring Hermès tableware and accessories. Madang is a joint operationof Hermès and the Shilla Hotel.

title: Hadonggwan
short_description: Hadongkwan is a gomtang (beef soup) restaurant that opened in Suha-dong in 1939 and has been passed down for three generations. Upholding the founding owner's philosophy, they do not operate in the evenings or offer delivery, strictly adhering to the principle of closing the restaurant once all the prepared food is sold out. Even after relocating to Myeong-dong, they continue to use high-quality beef simmered for a long time to provide a light and clean Seoul-style gomtang. They insist on offering only two menu items: gomtang and suyuk (boiled beef). By maintaining the practice of serving food in traditional brass bowls, they continue their consistent taste and tradition.

title: Galbi Myeongga Yisang
short_description: This galbi specialty restaurant consistently serves up the highest quality meat.

title: Shanti
short_description: Enjoy Indian and Nepalese food at affordable prices at Shanti. Nepalese food is generally milder than Indian food, and as the owner of this restaurant is from Nepal, the food here is milder on the whole.

title: Hanuso (Insadong Branch)
short_description:
Serving the highest-quality Korean beef

The Insadong branch of Hanuso exclusively serves beef from cows raised in the Jeonnam Hampyeong region. They offer a wide variety of dishes as well as set courses.

title: Jony Dumpling
short_description: The juicy, homemade dumplings here are fried or steamed, and you can choose from various assorted filings, including meat, shrimp, or even vegetarian.

title: Sushi Cho
short_description: Formerly located in the basement of the Westin Chosun, Sushi Cho was newly opened on the 18th floor. They have a reputation for using fresh ingredients delivered from Japan and for having the longest Japanese "hinoki dai" table in Korea. The chef is Japanese and comes from the legendary sushi restaurant Kyubi in Tokyo. This place is currently one of the best sushi restaurants in Seoul.

title: MAO
short_description: Mao is one of the few Peking duck restaurants that exist in Seoul. In addition to peking duck, there are also a wide range of Cantonese dishes. The trendy interior is decorated with a portrait of Chairman Mao. The atmosphere here is a lot like what you'd find in a restaurant in mainland China. Prices are relatively low.

title: Sinsa Myeonok
short_description: This is a chilled buckwheat noodles (naengmyeon) restaurant well known for its sweet and spicy sauce. The dish is so popular that long lines at lunchtimes are the norm. The dumplings and bulgogi are also recommended.

title: Mapo Sutbulgalbi
short_description: Mapo Sutbulgalbi offers pork galbi (short ribs), served properly with the bone attached. Also worth trying are the samgyeopsal (pork belly) and boneless beef ribs. The restaurant is big enough to accommodate large groups.

title: L'Espoir du Hibou
short_description: Here you can taste true French cuisine. The Duck Confit and Onion Soup are specially recommended by the chef. Half bottles of wine are available, and there is also a delicious dessert menu.

title: Kuai 19
short_description: Kuai 19 is a fusion-style Chinese restaurant that prepares their food with minimal use of oil. The mainly peach-colored interior is impressive.

title: Ganggangsullae (Yeoksam)
short_description: A Korean beef restaurant, in which traditional Korean beauty and warm hearts are abundant, by using Giwa (roofing tile) and raw lumber for interior. The beef at Gang gang sullai satisfies a customer’s eyes, ears and mouths because of its freshness. You will have a good time while appreciating the installation works and pictures surrounding the interior beautifully.

title: Hanchu
short_description: The main menu item here is fried chicken, although Han Chu is especially crowded at dinnertimes by people wanting a cool beer after a long day at work. Although the fried chicken and seasoned chicken are the most popular, spicy fried peppers are alsohighly recommended.

title: Xingkai
short_description: This fine dining restaurant has an ambiance like Shanghai in the 1930's. They serve mainly Cantonese and spicy Szechuan cuisine, Chaozhou-style cuisine with fresh live fish and seafood quickly stir-fried over high heat, as well as Thai- and Malaysian-influenced cuisine. Dinner set menus are also available for business meetings.

title: Ribuk Sonmandu
short_description: This restaurant is famous for their delicious kimchi maribap (kimchi-wrapped rice). Their light-tasting and savory mandu (Korean dumplings), served either on a platter or as part of a soup, are also popular. Their fist-size dumplings are stuffed with seasoned bean sprouts and different kinds of meat, for a delicious filling meal. Expect lines at lunchtime.

title: Serim
short_description: Serim is famous for noodle hot pot. Your choice of mugwort or bean noodles are boiled with par-boiled meat and vegetables. If the noodles don't fill you up, you can have rice porridge at the very end.

title: Moodeungsan
short_description: is well known for its barbecued beef, especially the rib eye. Top quality beef is served with many side dishes, and the chilled buckwheat noodles (naengmyeon) served afterward are also delicious.

title: Chungmu Gimbap
short_description: When Chungmu Gimbap first introduced Halmae gimbap (seaweed rolls), a style of gimbap that originated in Chungmu (present-day Tongyeong), it became a sensation throughout Seoul. These little seaweed rolls filled only with rice are served with roughly-cubed radish kimchi and seasoned squid. The seasoned squid and radish kimchi are the only side dishes, but they can be replenished as often as you'd like.

title: Munhwaok
short_description: Munhwaok is a seolleongtang (ox bone soup) restaurant with a 50 year tradition. Their seolleongtang broth is thick and delicious, made from beef leg bones and ribs. Their joktang (ox foot soup) includes well boiled cow knee bones and tastes similar totheir seolleongtang.

title: Bada Sikdang
short_description: Also called, "Johnson Stew," Ocean’s sausage stew is different from other varieties in that aside from the basic ingredients of meat and vegetables, it also contains cheese. Another recommendable dish is the steak and sausage grill.

title: Chungmu Sanghoe
short_description: Chungmu Sanghoe has been in the same location for 20 years and specializes in the regional cuisine of Tongyeong. Main dishes on the menu include sekkosi (shredded raw fish) and grilled fish. In addition, they serve grilled dried sole, Chungmu-style steamed ray, and raw anchovies. Another popular dish, spicy freshwater catfish stew, is a savory remedy for a hangover. All of the dishes come with seodeol seaweed soup made from small fish boiled in a fish broth.

title: Lanna Thai
short_description: Lanna Thai is the place to go for inexpensive and nicely presented Thai food. The chef is from Thailand, and the interior is simple and neat.

title: Hwangtae Bonga
short_description: Hwangtae Bonga is famous for dishes made with hwangtae (dried pollack). The most popular items on the menu are hwangtae-gui (grilled dried pollack), hwang taeguk (dried pollack soup), and siraegit guk (dried radish soup). To make the scrumptious hwangtae-gui,dried pollack is marinated in red chili paste for about a day, grilled, and served appetizingly garnished with sliced green onion and sesame seeds. The hwangtae-gui set menu comes with a variety of tantalizing side dishes, like ojingeo muchim (squid andvegetables) and myeolchi bokkeum (fried anchovies).

title: Garam Guksi
short_description: Garam Guksi specializes in Gyeongsang-do-style noodles. The sogogi guksi (a noodle dish served in beef broth) and the myeolchi guksi (a noodle dish served in anchovy broth) are popular, and the kongguksu (a seasonal Korean noodle dish served in a coldwhite soybean broth) and the dumplings are good, too.

title: Baekje Samgyetang
short_description: Baekje Samgyetang has been serving samgyetang, ginseng chicken soup, for over 40 years. Their tongdak (whole chicken) is equally popular.

title: Nwijo
short_description: This restaurant specializes in medicinal foods made with wild vegetables and natural seasonings. Recommended dishes include geunchaessam, or vegetables wrapped in potato slices marinated with enzymes, and bburi beombeok, ground lotus root, sweet potato and pumpkin wrapped in mulberry leaf.

title: Changgo 43
short_description: Changgo 43 is a high-quality meat barbeque restaurant. When you're done with your meat, they prepare savory fried rice flavored with the sauce from ggakdugi (spicy pickled radish). Most customers make a reservation, so it is advisable to do so as well.

title: Tenkai
short_description: At Tenkai, which specializes in authentic Japanese yakitori, you can enjoy grilled skewers. All of the tables are covered with tatami, so the rooms are cozy and comfortable. More than 40 different kinds of skewers are available, featuring seasonal ingredients such as meat, poultry, kinds of seafood, and vegetables, and they also feature a variety of liquor, including sake, soju, and fruit wines.

title: Mazue Ramen
short_description: At Mazue Ramen, they make matsu ramen, a variation of the classic Japanese noodle soup in a broth made from freshwater clams. Here, they use fresh noodles that they make themselves. Their yaki gyoja (pan-fried pork and vegetable dumplings) are also excellent. Japanese-style izakaya bar food is also served at dinnertime.

title: Busan Bokjip
short_description: Busan Bokjip has a reputation for being an affordable place to enjoy great-tasting bokguk (pufferfish soup). This spicy soup is made with pufferfish, and a generous amount of dropwort, bean sprouts, and garlic, making it loaded with flavor. At dinnertime, the pufferfish bulgogi is good to have with a glass of soju. Busan Bokjip is proud of its 30-year history.

title: Jinachun
short_description: Jinachun, established in 1925, is the oldest Chinese restaurant in Seoul and a place rich in history dating back to the Japanese colonial period. Located in Daehak-ro, it was popular among Seoul National University students in the 1960s and 1970s; students who lacked money would even pawn their wristwatches just to enjoy a bowl of jajangmyeon. The signature dish is a classic jajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce) that stays true to tradition, featuring an excellent harmony of chewy noodles and sauce. Inside the restaurant, photos related to its long history are displayed, allowing diners to glimpse stories of the past even during their meals.

title: Sandeulhae
short_description: Sandeulhae is a hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hôte) restaurant converted from a two-story traditional Korean tiled-roof house. The dishes for the set meals here fill up the entire table and include dolsotbap (stone-pot rice) made with rice from Icheon, well-known for good-tasting rice; ganjang gejang (crab marinated in soy sauce); assorted grilled fish; buchimgae (pan-fried vegetable pancakes); bossam (Chinese cabbage wraps with pork; and japchae (cellophane noodles stir-fried with vegetables) among many other dishes. On the second floor, you can sit on the floor, as is customary in Korea, or at a table with chairs as is customary in Western countries, on the first floor. They also have Icheon rice and seaweed available for purchase.

title: Biyangdo
short_description: Biyangdo specializes in hoe (sashimi) set menus and regional Jeju food. One unique item on the menu is dombe pork, which pork belly meat of Jeju native black pig steamed over pine needles with oriental ingredients and served on a chopping board.

title: Jeonju Seolleongtang
short_description: Jeonju Seolleongtang has been serving seolleongtang (ox bone soup) made with Korean beef for over 30 years.

title: HANS
short_description: HANS specializes in Korean-style cakes, famous for the excellent design and taste. Their creative yet simple look also draw significant appeal as a premium quality product. While these classy customized cakes are available for order, mousse cake and cheese cake stand out as their most signature cakes.

title: Dongpyo Golbaengi
short_description: Dongpyo Golbaengi in the Myeongdong area offers golbaengi muchim (spicy salad with sea snail). This restaurant is famous for generous portions and kind service. The strong flavor comes from a mix of red chili pepper powder, minced garlic, and fresh scallions.All golbaengi dishes come with complimentary pan-fried vegetable egg rolls.

title: Heukdonga
short_description: Headquartered in Jeju-do Island, this restaurant specializes in black pork. Black pork is chunkier and meatier than regular pork. Black pork at Heukdonga is dipped in a special Jejudo-style salted anchovy sauce.

title: Nariuijip
short_description: Nariuijip is famous for their delicious samgyeopsal (pork belly) and cheongjukjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew). The pajeori (green onion salad), when eaten with the samgyeopsal, is especially great. It is very crowded at lunch and dinner time, so you should avoid these times if you want to relax while eating.

title: Manbal
short_description: Manbal specializes in Korean-bred beef delivered from Hampyeong of the Jeolla region and Hongseong of the Chungcheong region. The sirloin is vacuum-sealed and matured on site and thus tastes great when grilled over charcoals. The side dishes are neatlypresented and also excellent. The restaurant was converted from a house, and has a small garden which is quite cozy.

title: Sinanchon
short_description: Sinanchon is a traditional cuisine specialty restaurant that reflects the traditional dishes and food culture of the Shinan region in Jeollanam-do. Founder Lee Geum-shim developed signature dishes like Nakji Kkuri and yeonpotang using ingredients from her hometown. Nakji-kuri features fresh live octopus grilled with sesame oil seasoning, boasting a light and savory taste, and they also offer yeonpotang, known for its refreshing broth. They offer course meals that include sashimi and soups, making it a place where you can enjoy Korean food along with the warm atmosphere of a traditional Korean house.

title: Seogeulleongtang
short_description: For over 20 years, Seogeulleongtang has been a popular place for charcoal-grilled samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly). The samgyeosal is marinated in soy sauce seasoned with oriental herbal medicine and then grilled over charcoal, giving it a unique, delicious flavor that eliminates the strong pork taste. To make their popular haejangguk (hangover soup), they add coagulated ox blood, dried Chinese cabbage leaves, and bean sprouts to a delicious broth made from beef bones. It is quite popular, so much so that getting a table at dinner time can be difficult.

title: Home Sukki
short_description: Home Sukki combines two styles of hot pot, Thai suki and Japanese shabu shabu. Enjoy set menus served with vegetables, beef shabu shabu, and haemul juk (seafood rice porridge). After shabu shabu, you can have kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) and juk (rice porridge).

title: Hanujib Wi
short_description: Hanujib Wi built its reputation by using only premium-quality Korean beef. The special lunch set menu is popular because they serve a nicely-balanced.

title: Namdo Mirak
short_description: Namdo Mirak specializes in the cuisine of Jeollanam-do (the southern province of the region of Jeolla). Popular choices are the hongeo samhap (a combination of three ingredients: aged skate, boiled pork, and fermented kimchi) and galchi jorim (braisedhairtail). The mustard leaf kimchi served as a side dish, is also very good. The restaurant has a 20-year history and is a good place to treat your guests as it was recently renovated and now features a modern and neat interior.

title: Seongbukdong Nurungji Baeksuk
short_description: Seongbukdong Nurungji Baeksuk is famous for their memil sujebi (buckwheat hand-torn noodle soup). The popular dishes here are deulggae memil sujebi (sujebi with perilla seed powder) and nurungji baeksuk (scorched rice in chicken broth).
