Dessert can be enjoyed on the small second-floor terrace with its panoramic view of the whole Seongbuk-dong area.

title: Samjungbokjip
short_description: The well-known swellfish restaurant of Korean-first swellfish course. The theme of swellfish is sublimated in a total cooking culture here. Its R&D of menu is actively performed in cooperation with Japanese famous restaurants. Live swellfish are served in sasimi, in 5minutes after removing its poison.

title: Mami Cheonggukjang
short_description: Mami Cheonggukjang is famous for cheonggukjang (fermented soybean paste soup). This restaurant recently underwent renovations, so the interior is pristine.

title: Seongbukdong Dwaejigalbijip
short_description: Seongbukdong Dwaejigalbijip is a famous dwaeji galbi (pork short ribs) restaurant that has been in operation in the Seongbuk-dong area for over 30 years. The set menu of chargrilled dwaeji galbi is excellent. Since it is grilled over charcoal briquettes,the pork is enfused with a smoky flavor and loses most of its fat.

title: Yeouido Yangjitang
short_description: Yeouido Yangjitang is famous for yangji seolleongtang, ox-bone soup made with beef brisket and flank. Their kimchi is delicious, and they will repleni.

title: Gaehwa
short_description: Three generations have been running this Chinese restaurant for over 40 years. Gaehwa is famous for its delicious noodle dishes. The jajangmyeon, handmade noodles topped with black soybean sauce, potatoes, onions, carrots, and pork is very good; the honghap jjamppong, a spicy noodle soup, comes loaded with mussels; and the chili shrimp and the pan-fried pork balls with vegetables are also worthy of a recommendation.

title: Hampyeong Myeonok
short_description: Hampyeong Myeonok is popular for their jeongol (hot pot) varieties and is famous for their generous portions. The scrumptious beosot mandu jeongol (mushroom dumpling hot pot) with meat and noodles is made with a variety of mushrooms and kimchi dumplings in beef broth. Their other popular dish, kimchi mari guksu, is noodles in cold kimchi soup served in an earthenware bowl.

title: Songajeossi Bindaetteok
short_description: At this Korean pub, you can enjoy assorted jeon (Korean-style pancakes) such as haemulyachae jeon (seafood vegetable pancakes) and makgeolli (Korean rice wine). The restaurant interior is tastefully decorated all in wood and bamboo. The dongdongju (anotherkind of Korean rice wine) and gyeranjjim (steamed scrambled eggs with chopped vegetables) are also served in bamboo containers. The modeum jeon (assorted pancakes) are popular, but only 11 plates a day are served.

title: Naegohyang Sikdang
short_description: Naegohyang Sikdang is one of the best galchi jorim (braised hairtail fish) restaurants in Namdaemun. Hairtail is garnished with several different kinds of seasoning and is boiled down in an earthenware pot over high heat, yielding a dish with a rich and rather spicy flavor. The complimentary deep-fried hairtail tails taste excellent. Although this little place is a bit shabby, it is popular enough that you have to wait in line to be seated.

title: Cheolcheol Bokjip
short_description: Fresh pufferfish is grilled in a rectangular grilling basket to make Cheolcheol Bokjip's unique pufferfish bulgogi. Also available is bokguk (pufferfish soup), which is a good remedy for a hangover. Because they use fresh pufferfish, the prices are somewhat high.

title: Banpo Chicken
short_description: Banpo Chicken as its name states, specializes in chicken. Their representative dish, maneul chicken (garlic chicken) is rotisserie-baked, greatly reducing fat content. Because the fresh chicken is stuffed with garlic, it has a strong garlic flavor. You can also have regular roasted chicken here. Only bottled beer is available.

title: Deutsch House
short_description: At this German pub you can enjoy a variety of European beers alongside eisbein (ham hocks) or cordon bleu schnitzel (tonkatsu) at reasonable prices. They offer a variety of sausages like bratwurst, grilled sausages, pork sausages, fresh sausages, and white sausages, all imported directly from Germany.

title: Donga Naengmyeon
short_description: Donga Naengmyeon is a naengmyeon (buckwheat noodles in an iced tangy broth) restaurant with a 30-year history. Naengmyeon here is typically served spicy but can be ordered less spicy, more sweet or more sour according to taste. Takeout is possible.

title: Baengnyeonok
short_description: Baengnyeonok specializes in tofu. Tofu is a high-protein ingredient made by soaking beans, grinding them, and squeezing them to form a curd. This restaurant offers representative dishes such as kongbiji baekban (puréed soybean soup, a bowl of rice, and side dishes), all-natural soft tofu, and vegetable-tofu bibimbap (mixed rice). The all-natural soft tofu baekban comes with unflavored chunks of tofu served in warm broth with a seasoning sauce. They also offer soft tofu which is sprinkled with red pepper powder for a spicy kick and served in an earthenware bowl.

title: Jangsarang
short_description: Listen to a solo musical performance played on a gayageum (Korean zither) while you enjoy dishes like gondre sotbap (rice steamed with a rare mountain vegetable in a traditional cast-iron cauldron), jellied acorn salad, and soup with pulled dough morsels topped with powdered perilla. One unique item at Jangsarang is the black bean makgeolli (thick rice wine).

title: Akasaka
short_description: Akasaka is one of the leading Japanese restaurants in downtown Seoul. There is a separate teppanyaki bar and sushi bar, and they have a reputation for their extensive selection of sake. They have a great view of the pool at the Hyatt Hotel and of the Hangang (River).

title: Baegam Wang Sundae
short_description: At Baegam Sundae, you can try Pyeongando-style sundae, a Korean blood sausage made with dried cellophane noodles. Instead of the North Korean recipe which includes coagulated ox blood, these sausages are made from a mixture of tofu, ferns, and more than 30 different vegetables in a natural casing.

title: Maple Tree House Itaewon Branch
short_description: At Maple Tree House, you can enjoy grilled pork or beef in a Western-style atmosphere. The interior is luxuriously decorated with trees.

title: Dugahun
short_description: This French cuisine restaurant is set in a traditional Korean house. It is located in the backyard of Gallery Hyundai, so you can soak in the culture afterward. Especially popular at Dogahun is the steak.

title: Napoleon Bakery
short_description:
One of the top 5 bakeries in Korea and one of the top 3 bakeries in Seoul. It was founded in 1968 in Seongbuk-gu, Seoul, and has been in the family for two generations. It is a long-established bakery that has influenced the Korean baking industry, with many people learning the art of baking here. Napoleon Confectionery, which first opened in Samsungyo, Dongsoomun-dong, Seongbuk-gu, Seoul, reopened in 2007 at the entrance to Seongbuk-dong after moving its location 100 meters due to the reconstruction of Seongbukcheon River, and operates as a bakery-cafe consisting of a bakery on the first floor and a cafe on the second floor.

This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

title: Songlimga
short_description: From the Korean table d’hote, steamed beef ribs, and seasoned beef ribs, you can taste the best meat in the Republic of Korea. The cook uses yeast instead of artificial seasoning so that the taste of the food is refreshing and rich. When you place an order of table d’hote, you can also enjoy at least six different kinds of kimchi as well.

title: Seocho Galbi
short_description: At Seocho Galbi, you can enjoy chargrilled wanggalbi (king-sized short ribs) and fresh sirloin. Although the restaurant expanded into a Western-style 5-story building, but they've retained their original taste. Service is very good here.

title: Paul & Paulina
short_description: This is a European-style bakery popular for its breads and dinner rolls. The fewest ingredients possible are used in order to leaven the bread slowly. You can sample breads before buying.

title: Artise
short_description: This is the Dosan Park branch of Artise, a European café and bakery. Here you can enjoy European-style breads, simple salads and pasta dishes. Sandwiches made on Italian panini, ciabatta, and French baguette are also available.

title: Tumbler Beer
short_description: Tumbler Beer is a western-style pub where you can enjoy beer and snacks like nachos. The crowd here is predominantly young because the draft beer is all-you-can-drink between 5 p.m. and 8 p.m. (Fridays and weekends excluded).

title: Jubilee Chocolatier
short_description: Jubilee Chocolatier is a homemade chocolate shop. You can enjoy chocolates, cakes, and espresso. Chocolate beverages also go nicely with the chocolates and cakes. They will make your chocolate beverage as rich as you'd like.

title: Gilson
short_description: For a long time, this Apgujeong-area restaurant has been serving up robatayaki (Japanese-style grilled dishes). Grilled delicacies, like chicken wings and gaibashira (shellfish adductor muscle), make good accompaniments for drinks. Another popular dish is yaki onigiri (grilled rice balls).

title: Yeolhae
short_description: Yeolhae is a small Japanese restaurant where you can enjoy authentic sashimi. Unlike many other sashimi restaurants, they use fresh fish rather than live fish. A unique thing about this restaurant is its graceful and rustic Japanese-style atmosphere.

title: Jaha Sonmandu
short_description: Jaha Sonmandu is well-known as a handmade mandu (Korean dumpling) house offering somandu, mandu stuffed with walnuts and pine nuts; and pyeonsu, mandu stuffed with mushrooms. When you order the manduguk (dumpling soup), you'll notice it contains rainbow mandu, with pink, yellow, and blue stripes. The most popular items on the menu are ddeokmanduguk (sliced rice cake and dumpling soup), which is made with fresh tricolor mandu, and their mandu jeongol (dumpling hot pot).

title: Gamchon
short_description: To make the broth for their sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew), Gamchon boils beef leg bones for 24 hours, yielding a broth that is thicker than you'll usually find in sundubu jjigae. Their loyal clientelle is made up of many foreign customers as well aslocal office workers.

title: Sabal
short_description: Sabal specializes in noodles, but the interior is like that of a café. Here, traditional noodle dishes are transformed into fusion creations. Popular dishes are noodles in chicken broth topped with chicken, and hwangtae bibimguksu (spicy mixed noodles topped with winter-dried pollack). The bowls and plates are very attractive, as well.

title: Son Kalguksu
short_description: At Son Kalguksu, you can enjoy humble homemade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup). The kalguksu is served in a rich beef broth, and jeon, a Korean-style pancake, is included with your order as a plus. Dinner service ends at 6 p.m, so you should call ahead to find out whether they can accommodate you.

title: Daeryeonjip
short_description: The popular item to order at Daeryeonjip is kalguksu, handmade knife-cut noodles in a broth made from beef leg bones; but they also offer a variety of other Korean dishes, such as bossam (boiled pork eaten with a salty sauce and wrapped in greens), steamedskate, and pajeon (savory green onion pancakes). The restaurant is popular with both Koreans and foreigners. After you've had some drinks and eaten some side dishes, kalguksu is a nice way to end your meal.

title: Myeonghwadang
short_description: With a long tradition of over 30 years, Myeonghwadang is legendary for their gimbap (Korean rolls). They also make a fantastic tteokbokki (spicy stir-fried rice cakes) and bibim jjolmyeon (cold wheat noodles served with vegetables in a spicy sauce). Inthe early days their menu was limited to just tteokbokki and gimbap, but they have since added a variety of other dishes, such as mandu (Korean dumplings) and udon noodles. Prices are reasonable.

title: Cheombeong Agujjim
short_description: Cheombeong Agujjim is very famous for its soft and chewy agujjim, a spicy dish made from monkfish and bean sprouts. Another specialty here is the rice balls topped with crumbled seaweed, which goes very nicely with the spicy agujjim. There are also quitea lot of people who come for the ganjang gejang (crab marinated in soy sauce).

title: Standing Coffee
short_description: This is a take-out coffee shop famed for its great coffee beans. Standing Coffee’s ‘blue lemonade,’ made with blue curacao syrup, is a popular drink with customers during the summer.

title: Daemun
short_description: Daemun table d’hote consists of delicious Mung bean jelly cake mixed with beef and vegetables, sweet vegetable salads with fruit sauce, five colors of pan-fried flour dough with duck and cold jellyfish salad with mustard dressing. Tasty side dishes such as bulgogi and outer leaf of cabbage mixed with soybean paste with rice in hot stone pot and soybean paste stew come right after the main course.

title: Walking On The Cloud
short_description: Located inside 63City, Walking On The Cloud provides fine European dining. It offers a superb view of the Hangang (River), and Seoul.

title: Pyeonggaok(Yangjae Branch)
short_description: This is the Yangjae-dong branch of Pyeonggaok, a restaurant in Bundang specializing in North Korean cuisine. Two of the most popular items are the eobok jaengban (pressed beef served on a brass plate) and the Pyeongyang naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles served either in a tangy iced broth or mixed with spicy red chili sauce). The naengmyeon here is decadent: it's topped with slices of beef, pork, chicken, and pheasant meatballs, and the rich broth is made from beef and pheasant. The Pyeongyang-style dumplings and mung bean pancakes are also quite popular.

title: Gangseomyeonok
short_description: The noodles from Gangseomyeonok are famous in part because they were served to representatives of North Korea at the time of the South Korea-North Korea Red Cross Conference. This restaurant has successfully carried on the tradition of Pyeongyang noodles for over 50 years. Domestic buckwheat from Gangwon-do Province is mixed with starch to make the delicious noodles, and the broth is made from beef brisket and white radish kimchi for a light and refreshing savory flavor.

title: Joseonok
short_description: Joseonok makes their sogalbi (beef short ribs) in the traditional way, marinating the meat for a full day in a sauce of aged soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and sugar, and then grilling it over charcoals. This sweet marinade is not too strong, allowing the original flavor of the meat to come through. The restaurant opened before the Korean War and was one of the top three restaurants in the Euljiro area, even up till the mid-1970s.

title: Hwangsojip
short_description: Hwangsojip has been specializing in doganitang (ox knee soup) for 40 years. They simmer it for a long time in a Korean cast-iron cauldron, and it is so popular that there are usually lines to be seated. For dinner, many people have dogani jjim, braised ox-knee served on the stone plate, along with some soju. The stone plate is heated over charcoal, so the food stays hot throughout the entire meal.

title: Neulpureun Mokjang
short_description: Neulpureun Mokjang specializes in boneless ribs and only offers two things on their menu: boneless ribs and yukhoe (sliced raw beef seasoned with various spices and sauces). The boneless ribs are lightly marinated and grilled over oak charcoals. It'sbusy enough that you'll likely have to wait in line to be seated. Prices are reasonable.

title: Florian
short_description: Florian specializes in fresh coffee beans. On the board, they write which coffee was roasted that day, so you can enjoy fresh coffee made with freshly-roasted coffee beans. There is a bit of a wait after you order your coffee because it is made to order and the beans are ground just before brewing. The toast set meal that includes thickly-sliced toast is also recommended. The owner's attention to detail is evident in the charmingly-decorated atmosphere and the high-quality coffee cups they use.

title: Gomone Restaurant
short_description: The proprieter and cook of 40 years uses 100% domestic Korean beans to make her tofu (podubu and gundubu). Her dishes are healthy and served in beautiful dishes made by Lee Bong-ju, who was named a Korean intangible cultural asset.

title: Gwangjang-dongGaon
short_description: Gaon opened in April 2008, and their reputation for handmade mandu (dumplings) and gomguk (noodles in thick beef soup) has been growing ever since. This Korean restaurant is situated in front of the Han River, perfect for watching a lovely scenery unfold.

title: Burimjeong Sutbulgalbi
short_description: Come here to taste beef and pork that’s been personally procured by the owner and aged, along with slices of fresh apple and pear, with various ground vegetables and fruit. They serve galbi, pork ribs, pork belly, and galbitang (beef rib soup).

title: geukrakdon
short_description: Taste the highest quality meat at a low price at Geukrakdon, which has the best hygiene management system certification HACCP, which raises and slaughters directly with antibiotic-free feed and delivers directly

title: Duremidam (Seoul National University Branch)
short_description: Enjoy all-you-can-eat, self-service meals and made-to-order meals at the Seoul National University cafeteria.​

title: Mapo-ok
short_description: This is an ox bone soup restaurant with a 60- year history and tradition. The ox bone soup here is very meaty and is served with many different kinds of kimchi, including cabbage kimchi, radish kimchi and green onion kimchi.

title: Seoseokdae
short_description: "Seoseokdae" is originally the name of a rock on Mudeungsan (mountain) in Gwangju.  The restaurant buys beef directly from Jeolla-do (province) and grills the meat on fiery charcoal to bring out the beef's unique flavor and scent.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Yukjeon Hoegwan
short_description: From 1929 to 1958, this restaurant operated under the name Hosam Restaurant in Yeong-dong in the city of Suncheon.  In 1962, the family moved the restaurant to its present location in Yongsan, Seoul, renaming it Yeokjun Restaurant.  Now in itsthird generation of family ownership, Yukjun Hoegwan has well-preserved their family's original taste and history.

title: Omiga (Yangjae Branch)
short_description: This restaurant serves up nostalgia and the kind of delicious, homemade food that your mother fed you when you were little.

title: Subin Tteokgalbi
short_description: The restaurant specialties are the tteokgalbi and the crabs marinated in soy sauce, but every item is made with the best ingredients and served with plentiful side dishes, including homemade kimchi.

title: Cham Seolnongtang
short_description: The restaurant carefully selects the beef and beef brisket that goes into their soups and and stews, cures it for at 6 hours, then finally cooks it for a minimum of 12 hours to achieve that clean, flavorful taste.  Instead of thinly slicing theiroxtail, they serve it in small chunks for a unique taste.

title: Bonga Pyongyang Myeonok
short_description: The restaurant grinds the buckwheat in-house to make their Pyongyang-style noodles. It produces a savory flavor in the noodles, which perfectly complements the deep, rich flavors of the broth.

title: Wangga
short_description: Wangga is scenically located at the bottom of Samgaksan (mountain) and offers high-quality Korean beef at reasonable prices.

title: Galbi Myeongga Yisang (Gireum Branch)
short_description: Yisang is a restaurant to taste the finest selection of meat, fresh ingredients, and unique spices.

title: Marimo
short_description: This izakaya (Japanese-style pub) specializes in tofu dishes. Typical dishes are Goma Tofu made with black sesame seeds, and mochi tofu made with cheese.

title: Wooldolmok
short_description: Uldolmok Ganeungil prides itself on making traditional Korean dishes with fresh seafood. One look at at the stir-fried noodles made with finely sliced burdock and steamed pollack will be enough to get your taste buds rolling.

title: Gami Udon
short_description: The noodles at this udon restaurant are made on-site, and the broth is especially tasty. The fried chicken and udon set is very filling and recommended. The décor is modern and simple.

title: Samcheonggak
short_description: Samcheonggak is a traditional arts and cultural complex used as a meeting place for high-ranking politicians from the ruling and opposition parties, inter-Korean Red Cross, and Korean-Japan talks. Comprising a performance hall, Korean restaurant, tea house, and guest rooms, Samcheonggak hosts traditional performances throughout the year, except on Mondays. The buildings in Samcheonggak are Hanoks, where you can feel the architectural beauty of Korea, and are made up of the main building, Ilhwadang, and five separate buildings, including Dongbaekheon, Yuhajeong, Chuwidang, Cheonchudang, and Cheongcheondang. Among these is the Samcheonggak Korean restaurant on the first floor of Ilhwadang. The restaurant is a great place to enjoy high-quality Korean food with the elegance of nature.

title: Geumgang Barbecue Chicken
short_description: At Geumgang Barbecue Chicken, you can have draft beer and chicken without paying a lot. There are a variety of chicken dishes on the menu, and their barbecued chicken and garlic chicken are representative.

title: Hanaro Hwaegwan
short_description: Hanaro Hwaegwan has been preserving Korea's traditional tastes for 28 years in Insadong.

title: Bulia (Gangnam branch)
short_description: This is the Gangnam branch of Bulia, a restaurant in front of Hongik University that is famous for huǒ guō (Chinese hotpot). Unlike the main branch, which specializes only in huǒ guō, this branch serves other neatly-presented Chinese dishes. The interior is quite sleek, as well.

title: Donsoobaek
short_description: The motto of this restaurant, known for its Dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice), is: "Let's eat well-cooked pork, enjoy life, and live to be 100 years old."

title: Jinsadaek
short_description: Jinsadaek is located inside a hanok, surrounded by the hustle and bustle of the city, and harmoniously brings together the traditional foods of each of Korea's regions.

title: Suldamje Seolleongtang
short_description: A hot pot of Seolleongtang in Sul Dam Je warms you up on cold days. This hot soup made from slow cooked boiled ox bones served with steamed rice and fresh kimchi is amazingly delicious. Generous servings and warm hospitality make the visit enjoyable.

title: L'Amitie
short_description: The chef personally takes orders at this small restaurant, which only has a few tables overall. L’Amitie is especially well-known for its foie gras and offers many other traditional French dishes, depending upon the available ingredients.

title: Pooja
short_description: Pooja is a restaurant that serves Indian and Nepalese cuisine adapted to suit the tastes of Koreans. They serve light-tasting naan and traditional curries. The name of the restaurant, Pooja, means "prayer" in Hindi.

title: Seolmaene
short_description: Seolmaene is famous for their Pyeongyang-style mandu (Korean dumplings). Their mandu is filled with bean sprouts and pork, yielding light flavors. They are also well-known for their pork bossam (steamed pork wrapped in lettuce) and tangpyeongchae, a Korean royal court dish made with mung bean starch jelly, mung bean sprouts, watercress, red pepper, and seaweed.

title: Camapkahd (Samarkand)
short_description: Camapkahd offers Uzbek dishes based on Russian cuisine. All of the employees, including the cooking staff, come from Russia. They prepare a variety of Russian and Central Asian dishes, including lamb and beef skewers, a lamb hot pot-style dish called chyeplatochicken tabaka, plov, and shurpa. Lamb and beef shashlyk are recommended.

title: Songuksi
short_description: Songuksi is a noodle restaurant. The noodles at Songuksi have a nice chewy texture because the wheat-flour dough is kneaded by hand and left to rise in the fridge, and only cooked once you place your order. Sujebi (hand-torn noodle soup) and kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) makes an enjoyable meal for two or three people.

title: Ilpumdang
short_description: Enjoy Japanese shabu shabu (thinly-sliced beef fondue) and sukiyaki (hot pot), made with a tasty broth flavored with katsuobushi (dried skipjack tuna shavings) and dashima (a kind of seaweed). Homemade sukiyaki sauce and soy ponzu sauce also add a unique flavor to the dishes. Your meal comes with your choice of rice porridge or noodles. The décor is modern and luxurious, so you can feel confident about inviting your guests here.

title: Ilpumhyang
short_description: This famous Chinese restaurant in front of the Chinese Embassy is run by a Chinese immigrant. They serve high quality Chinese food at reasonable prices. The deep-fried dishes, such as kkanpunggi (fried chicken with hot pepper sauce) and tangsuyuk (sweet and sour beef or pork) are recommended. Also popular are the ohyang ("five spice") ham hocks, which have a nice aroma and tender texture.

title: Wonju Chueotang
short_description: For four years, Wonju Chueotang has been making their own fermented chili paste for use in the stock for their chueotang (loach soup). Because they make their broth from brisket and beef intestine, the smell of the loach is hardly noticeable, and the soup tastes rather like yukgaejang (spicy soup with minced beef). The soup is available with your choice of either ground or whole loach. Besides loach soup, they offer loach tempura and spicy catfish stew.

title: Chai797
short_description: Uniquely, Chai 797 specializes in both Chinese and Thai cuisine. There is a dim sum kitchen at the entrance, and flowers are also displayed for sale in one corner of the restaurant.

title: Hanuso
short_description: A chef with 15 years of experience only uses first-grade Korean beef from Hampyeong and delivers excellent food and earnest service. Modern interior design is one of the points that make you want to visit. A group reservation is possibile, and the parking lot is capable of 50 cars.

title: Red Marble House
short_description: At Red Marble House, you can enjoy premium-quality Korean beef in a luxurious atmosphere. When you order the grilled beef, your table is filled with neatly-presented side dishes as if you had ordered Korean table d'hôte. They have remarkably high-tech equipment, so it's easy for diners to make adjustments to control the smoke right at the table.

title: Sarangbang Kalguksu
short_description: The owners of Sarangbang Kalguksu have been making kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) for 40 years. The kalguksu mixed with anchovy broth is classic, and the boiled whole chicken eaten with its specially made sauce is a true delicacy. This is a famous place for actors and movie industry people in the Chungmuro area.

title: Myeongdong Kyoja
short_description: For a taste of authentic kal-guksu (noodle soup), visit Myeongdong Kyoja. The noodles here are made fresh with flour dough. The noodles here are both soft and chewy and the strong, savory flavors of the chicken broth will leave you wanting second helpings. After a visit here, you may not be able to get enough of kal-guksu!

title: Tsuruhashi Fugetsu
short_description: Tsuruhashi Fugetsu is the Korean branch of a chain of Japanese restaurants serving Osaka-style okonomiyaki (a Japanese savory pancake with a variety of ingredients) that are grilled on a hot plate. They add chewy thick yakisoba (fried noodles) to okonomiyaki for a popular “modern yaki” variation. All of the cooking is done on a hot plate right at your table.

title: Goryeo Samgyetang
short_description: Founded by Lee Sang-rim shortly after the Korean War in the 1950s, Goryeo Samgyetang is a specialty restaurant for samgyetang that has accumulated longstanding tradition and know-how, evolving into a unique culinary experience. By preparing seven-week-old young chickens, it offers a chewy exterior and tender interior, delivering deep flavor with its rich and clean broth. The restaurant is also spacious and comfortable, allowing you to enjoy a healthy and nourishing meal in a pleasant atmosphere.

title: Halmeoni Hyeondae Nakjijip
short_description: Halmeoni Hyeondae Nakjijip is famous for spicy octopus. They are also famous for their ganjang gejang, crabs marinated in soy sauce, and generous portions of gamjatang, pork backbone and potato soup. Prices are relatively high.

title: Heohyeongman Apgujeong Cafe
short_description: This is one of the best coffee houses in Korea. Here, you can taste coffee made by the famous roaster, Heo Hyeong-man.

title: Wonhalmeoni Bonga
short_description: This is a specialty restaurant of boiled pork wrapped in kimchi with 30 years of history. It succeeded in bringing the taste of the dish to the modern world with carefully chosen ingredients. Salted vegetables are prepared everyday with fresh oysters making a delicious dish with boiled pork. The elegant and simple interior of the restaurant using rafters reminds one of the culture of a wooden floor in the Republic of Korea.

title: Arirang
short_description: The difference is clear - Arirang uses only the best Korean beef available, and you'll know it in the taste and smell.

title: Maple Tree House
short_description: Maple Tree House is a barbeque restaurant where you can enjoy grilled meat in a comfortable Western style atmosphere. One of the main dishes on the menu is pork hangjeongsal (pork from the back of the neck). The meat is very tasty grilled over perfectly fired charcoals and wrapped with lettuce or pickled perilla leaves.

title: Onmaeul
short_description: Onmaeul specializes in tofu. Two favorites here are the savory tofu made with black beans, and the tofu soup seasoned with myeongran jeot (salted fermented roe of flathead mullet), both attractively served in brass bowls with a brass spoon.

title: Jeonggam Eorin
short_description: A Korean restaurant with 30 years of tradition, Jeonggam Eorin is a place where visitors can enjoy tasty meals made with carefully selected ingredients.

title: Yonggeumok
short_description: Yonggeumok, which opened in 1932, is a long-established restaurant specializing in chueo-tang (loach soup.) It sells Seoul-style Chueo-tang and Namdo-style Chueo-tang with ground-boiled loach. All dishes are carefully prepared with the best ingredients and with love by the owner, Yong Geum-ok.

title: Gangnam Ttaro Gukbap
short_description: Over the past 20 years, this restaurant has maintained the traditional taste of the one dish on their menu, seonjittaro gukbap (beef tripe and rice soup). Their soup is served with generous helpings of soybean sprouts, green onions, and beef. The thick broth, made from green onions and beef, is light and refreshing.

title: Buddha's Belly
short_description: This is the place to go if you really want to taste authentic Thai food. Thai chefs will adjust the level of spice according to your taste and are willing to cook you up something that is not on the menu. Most of the menu costs around 8,000 won. At lunchtime, you can choose from several lunch sets, all which come with rice.

title: Gami Bunsik
short_description: G amibunsik has been operating near Ewha University Station for over 40 years, since 1975. Many middle-aged customers who have graduated from Ewha Womans University come here for memories, and young people come here as their mom's favorite restaurant. Their signature dish, " G ami udon," is characterized by round noodles that are boiled twice in flour with only salt, making them soft and plump. A bowl of kami udon and onigiri is a meal in itself. The restaurant opens at 10:00 a.m., but it's so popular that you'll already have to wait in line to get a reservation number.

title: BONO BONO
short_description: This seafood buffet restaurant offers a nice selection of sushi, rolls, seafood, hot-plate dishes, tempura, and roast beef, among others. The ingredients are relatively high-quality.

title: Gaenmaeul
short_description: Gaenmaeul is a very famous mandu (Korean dumpling) restaurant in Ichon-dong. Two of their specialities is their kimchi mandu, which are made bite-sized, and their nokdu buchim, griddled mung bean pancakes made with mung beans which have been hand-groundin a stone mill, mixed with kimchi and vegetables.

title: Yeosu Odongdo
short_description: Yeosu Odongdo serves Yeosu-style sashimi and is best known for their butter fish, which is mixed with an abundance of vegetables and served garnished with vinegary red chili pepper paste. They serve jangeotang (eel stew), a delicacy of the Yeosu area, and in the summer, you can enjoy hamo (pike eel).

title: Namaste
short_description: This is an Indian / Nepalese restaurant that is generally cheaper than other similar restaurants. The ‘Veggie Lunch’ includes a vegetable curry or palak paneer.

title: Nammaejip
short_description: This restaurant in Bukchangdong alley has been serving up grilled dishes seasoned with hot chili pepper paste for 30 years. Different kinds of meat are marinated in hot chili pepper sauce and then chargrilled. Their marinated medallions of pork loin, called dongeurangttaeng, is especially famous.

title: The Restaurant
short_description: This Japanese-style French restaurant is well known for its food and the interior décor. It also offers a great view of Gyeongbokgung Palace and has a dessert café.

title: Ton Kiang
short_description: This Chinese restaurant is a small but popular because of their light-tasting food. Their bukwi shrimp dish is a mixture of deep-fried shrimp and sliced strawberries in a light white sauce sprinkled with lemon juice. The yuringi (deep-fried chicken) is made with chicken leg meat, not chicken breast, so it is very tender.

title: Doenjang Yesul Toenmaru
short_description: Meals in this bibimbap restaurant are served in a large bowl with a bevy of vegetables and healthy leeks. The traditionally styled interior also makes for a great opportunity to experience a true Korean dining experience.

title: La Callas
short_description: La Callas is an Italian restaurant that offers antipasti, salads, main entrees, pizza, and desserts on the menu. Various lunch and dinner sets are also available. The interior is decorated with a motif based on soprano Maria Callas.

title: La Cucina
short_description: With a sophisticated interior décor, this is the first restaurant known to have served Italian cuisine in Korea. It is on the way to Namsan Mountain so you can enjoy the view while trying the delicious course meals on offer.

title: Lamb House
short_description: Specializing in lamb, this restaurant serves grilled lamb chops, lamb broth, steamed lamb with vegetables in a spicy sauce and lamb hot pot, all made with well-aged, tender lamb meat. The lamb broth, which is made with a large helping of perilla powder, makes a good meal served along with steamed meat.

title: Little Saigon
short_description: At Little Saigon you can enjoy Vietnamese pho, rice vermicelli in a flavorful beef broth. The Vietnamese wraps, filled with generous amounts of fresh ingredients, are also popular. Another popular dish is the deep-fried Vietnamese egg roll, stuffed with a mixture of pork and vegetables.

title: Mangnae Hoetjip
short_description: Mangnae Hoetjip is one of those few places where people can dine on thickly-cut sashimi. The fish they serve is delivered live every two days from a local distributor and kept in their aquarium for about a day. The hoedupbap (rice topped with sashimiand vegetables) comes with maeuntang (spicy fish stew) and braised mackerel. This restaurant offers highly satisfying meals for the price.

title: Myeongdong Tonkatsu
short_description: This was the first restaurant to introduce the famous thick Japanese-style pork cutlets to Korea. With a 30-year history of excellence, Myeongdong Tonkatsu’s cordon bleu is the most popular menu item.

title: Mugyo-dong Bugeo-guk
short_description: This restaurant has been serving up bugeo-guk (dried pollack soup) since 1968. Their soup is made fresh, with firmly-dried pollack, and not the frozen variety that many similar restaurants use. Their nutty and light-tasting soup draws a large crowd, making lines common at lunchtime.

title: Mijin
short_description: The traditions of this restaurant stretch back 60 years, when they first began to make memil guksu (buckwheat noodles). The broth for the noodles is made from anchovies like the Japanese Gatsobushi, which makes their noodle broth clear and more refreshing. This is one of the most famous memil guksu restaurants in Seoul.

title: Gyeongin Misulgwan Jeontong Dawon
short_description: Gyeongin Misulgwan is a very unique restaurant that has restored the features of a traditional Chosun Dynasty house. Guests can sip on traditional Korean tea in a beautiful flower and tree filled garden. Traditional Korean snacks are always served with tea.

title: Gobau
short_description: At lunchtime, Gobau offers himjultang (beef tendon soup) and doganitang (a soup made from veal knuckles), and its dinner menu is an assortment of grilled beef dishes, including ahrongsatae (beef shank), chadolbaki (thinly-sliced brisket), and jebichuri (inner skirt steak). Their culinary history goes back 50 years.

title: Gwanghwamun Jip
short_description: This cozy and very welcoming restaurant is well-known for its kimchi stew. The ripe kimchi and pork neck stew is spicy, yet soothing and very filling. The egg rolls are an ideal accompaniment to this dish.

title: Mabongnim's Son's Tteok-bokki
short_description:
The teok-bokki restaurant owned and operated by the son of the original creator of the spicy red teok-bokki.

Located in Sindang-dong Teok-bokki Town.

title: Samgeori Pocha
short_description: Samgeori Pocha is an eatery located in Hongdae that is especially popular with young Seoulites in their 20s. The menu is focused mainly on alcoholic drinks and Korean foods that pair well with liquor. One famous menu item is their spicy whole squid tteok-bokki. The interior is done in a retro 70s and 80s theme. Visitors must present photo ID to enter.

title: Guksijip
short_description: Guksijip is famous for its fresh, handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup). Reservations are essential as there are usually no seats available for walk-in customers. After the day's noodles have been sold out, usually between 12 p.m. and 2 p.m., no more are served. The noodles and seasoning sauce are simply served in a broth made from beef brisket, but the noodles are very thin and amazingly delicate and soft.

title: Menya Sandaime
short_description: This is a traditional Japanese ramen house, which closes for the day when staff run out of ingredients. Although it specializes in tonkotsu ramen, the tsukemen ramen, whereby the noodles and broth are served separately, is also recommended. Although small in size, Menya Sandaime has a very comfortable atmosphere.

title: Gukhwa Jeongwon
short_description: Gukhwa Jeongwon specializes in traditional Korean set menu meals. Instead of serving a wide variety of side dishes, every course is accompanied by a few side dishes, selected to complement one another. Those that book in advance are provided with a dish of chopped abalone, grilled abalone, and a mixed sushi platter. The interior is particularly impressive, as the antique roofing tiles that decorate the interior are tiles that were retained from the original construction of the building in 1925.

title: Majeonteo
short_description: Majeonteo's speciality is yukgaejang, a spicy beef stew, for which they are always have tons of customers. Steamed barley rice and bossam are also popular here. When the weather is cold, beef gukbap, boiled rice served in beef soup, is great as a warm pick-me-up. The broth they use for the soup is made from fresh, good-quality brisket, to which they add a generous amount of bean sprouts.

title: Ilmi
short_description: Ilmi specializes in jangeo-gui (grilled eel). Despite the smoke and the smell of charcoal braziers that makes them an increasing rarity, at this restaurant you can enjoy chargrilled eel that has been seasoned with only salt. The eel with Korean pickled leeks and mixed rice with seasoned soy sauce are also excellent.

title: Gung
short_description: Gung's specialty is Kaesong-style North Korean mandu (dumplings), and they’ve been serving their brand of it to customers for over 30 years. Unlike Pyeongyang mandu, which are large, Kaesong mandu are slightly smaller and go extremely well when served in broth. Gung also serves a variety of traditional Korean liquors that can be enjoyed with the meal.

title: Club NB2
short_description: Hip-hop dance clubs located at Hongdae and Gangnam Station. The first club to open in Hongdae in 1999. The beginning of the Hongdae club boom.Frequented by famous celebrities

title: Yetgol
short_description: The specialty of Yetgol is kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) made with mature kimchi and canned herring. Their kimchi jjigae exhibits traditional flavor, a sour yet refreshing taste.

title: New York New York Restaurant (Kensington Hotel)
short_description: New York New York, is a New York-style steak house located in the Kensington Hotel in Yeouido. The restaurant has an opulent interior as well as private dining rooms. New York New York has been used as a shooting location for many Korean dramas. Dramas like "My Too Perfect Sons," "Temptation of Wife," "Queen of Housewives," and "The Greatest Love" have all filmed at this restaurant.

title: Bongsanok
short_description: Bongsanok presents the regional food of Bongsan, Hwanghae-do. Here, you can try handmade Hwanghae-do-style dumplings stuffed with a filling of napa cabbage, bean sprouts, tofu, beef, and pork. Other delicacies include kimchi and bean sprout soup and kimchi mari guksu (cold noodles in chilled kimchi soup).

title: Seocho Jangeo Town
short_description: Seocho Jangeo Town's is an eel specialty restaurant. Their fresh chargrilled eel tastes phenomenal, as it is grilled over oak charcoal, and minimally seasoned only with salt. Try it wrapped in pickled sesame leaves.

title: Namdo Sikdang
short_description: At Namdo Sikdang, you can eat your fill and not have to worry about your wallet. The restaurant is usually crowded with people who come specifically for the spicy charcoal-grilled pork, a dish that has been famous for several decades. Besides Korean table d'hôte, they offer hyeonmi baekban (a set menu meal of brown rice, soup and side dishes) for those who are dining alone.

title: Haedong Bokguk
short_description: Haedong Bokguk serves spicy bokguk, pufferfish soup made with an abundance of bean sprouts, served in an earthenware bowl. The pufferfish stew is hot and spicy and tastes great, as does the light-tasting jiri (pufferfish soup with watercress and mung bean sprouts). Although this restaurant is not luxurious, the pufferfish dishes they serve are very popular.

title: Sanmotungi
short_description: Cafe located at the foot of Bukhansan Mountain that boasts a spectacular view. There is a traditional low table in one room on the first floor; a good place to have a conversation. The second floor of Sanmotungi is a café that has a great view of the mountain surrounding neighborhood, and the city walls. In addition to being featured in the K-drama, Coffee Prince, the cafe was also featured in, My Princess, with Song Seung-heon and Min Ho of SHINee. Taking a taxi to the cafe is advised, as it is difficult to find and get to on foot.

title: Coffee Chingu
short_description: At Coffee Chingu, patrons can enjoy hand-drip coffee made with hand-roasted beans. You can choose from a variety of coffee beans, and freshly roasted coffee beans are also available for sale.

title: Liberte
short_description: At Dining at Liberte, you'll feel like you've been invited over to somebody's house to enjoy a French meal. They offer only set menu meals, which have around ten courses, including an appetizer and a dessert. The set menu is arranged by the chef daily depending on available ingredients, so the menu is always changing. They open only for reservations, so it is essential to book ahead.

title: The Lounge
short_description: Located on the top floor of the six-star Park Hyatt Hotel, The Lounge offers great panoramic views of the city, particularly at night. This restaurant and bar offers visitors Korean dishes and desserts, as well as beverages such as juice and tea, wine, and cocktails. Afternoon tea is available daily from 12pm to 5:30pm.

title: Izumi
short_description: Izumi offers fresh sushi and sashimi. Whereas only about 20 to 30 kinds of sushi are offered at most Japanese restaurants, sushi constitutes an essential part of the this restaurant's menu and is prepared from 60 different kinds of fish and seafood.

title: Ogu Banjeom
short_description: Ogu Banjeom has over 60 years' experience behind it. One look at the old-style tables and chairs and you can see how long this restaurant has been around. It is run by an ethnic Chinese, and the interior is impressively decorated with red tile, a hallmark of Chinese restaurants. Enjoy fried dumplings made the proper way. All of their fried dishes are better than you'll find in most places, as is their oh-hyang-jang-yuk (braised thinly-sliced pork). Their wealth of experience is even evident in the egg drop soup that accompanies their fried rice dishes.

title: Dubai
short_description: Enjoy Arabic food at this Middle Eastern restaurant run by Iraqis. Besides the wide variety of curries and kebabs they offer, appetizers like hummus and falafel are also available. After your meal, try a Middle-eastern waterpipe, with eight different flavors available, including apple, mint, strawberry, rose, etc.

title: Hyeongje Galbi
short_description: This galbi (marinated grilled ribs) restaurant, with nearly 40 years of history, is a well-known gem in the Sinchon area. The charcoal-grilled beef ribs are exceptional, with both the savory unmarinated galbi and tender marinated galbi being popular choices. While galbi is the specialty, the restaurant offers affordable Korean meals such as dolsotbibimbap (hot stone pot bibimbap), galbitang (short rib soup), and boribap (Steamed Barley Rice.) The sweet bulgogi is another crowd favorite, just as popular as the ribs. The restaurant is divided into different floors according to menu items like galbitang, reserved guests, charcoal-grilled galbi, and bulgogi, providing a comfortable dining environment. The spacious interior makes it ideal for families and groups, and the staff grills the meat for you, ensuring a convenient dining experience.

title: Mongnyeon Sikdang
short_description: Mongnyeon has been selling nurungji for more than 20 years. Nurungji is a Korean favorite. It's cooked and crunchy rice that's been browned at the bottom of a hot pot or earthenware bowl. Mongnyeon sells several different kinds of it and it is very popular here. Some of their offerings come with twenty different side dishes to enjoy, and lunch time is a great time to drop by for a taste.

title: Oebaek
short_description: Oebaek is a Chinese-owned Chinese restaurant. Owing to their reliable skills, the fiery-flavored dishes they produce with fresh ingredients rarely disappoint.

title: Busanjip
short_description: Busan Agu serves delicious agwi jjim (steamed anglerfish with bean sprouts) which is chewy and a little spicy, but not too strong. Another popular item on the menu is their ganjang gejang, perfectly-aged crab marinated in soy sauce, which is quite light-tasting.

title: Seongcheon Makguksu
short_description: Seongcheon Makguksu serves light-tasting makguksu, cold thick buckwheat noodles made with a broth of pure dongchimi (watery kimchi). The noodles are very high-quality and made with a high proportion of buckwheat. Their popular set menu comes with jeyuk (spicy marinated pork), makguksu, and dongchimi-mu (watery kimchi with radish). Wrapping marinated pork in seasoned dongchimi radish tastes delicious.

title: Anjip
short_description: Dining in Anjip's comfortable atmosphere, you'll feel like you're are eating at home. You can try various Korean set menus, meat, and anju (side dishes eaten with alcohol).

title: La Cantina
short_description: La Cantina is a long-established Italian restaurant in Seoul, founded in the 1960s at the recommendation of Lee Byung-chul, the founder of the Samsung Group. It became a favored destination for prominent figures in Korea's political, business, and diplomatic circles. True to its name, which means underground wine cellar in Italian, the restaurant offers an atmosphere reminiscent of an Italian wine storage cellar. La Cantina developed Korean-style Italian dishes such as Spaghetti Con Vongole and also features a special menu called the Samsung Set, which was a favorite of Lee Byung-chul.

title: Yujin Sikdang
short_description: Yujin Sikdang, which specializes in mulnaengmyeon (noodles in a tangy iced beef broth), commands a loyal following. The noodles here are made of a mix of buckwheat flour and starch. The broth is made from beef and beef bones.

title: Bigeumdo
short_description: Bigeumdo specializes in jeon (Korean pancakes) and the regional food of Jeollanam-do (the southern province of the region of Jeolla). After the jeon dishes, they serve steamed rice, ten different Jeollanamdo-style side dishes, soup, and nurungji (reboiled scorched rice). The Jeollanamdo-style side dishes, such as pickled perilla leaves, abalone intestines, and gatkimchi (pickled mustard leaves and stems), are attractively presented and are delicious.

title: 10 Corso Como Café
short_description: If you are interested in the latest trends in Seoul, you must visit this place. This is a hip Milano-esque caféstyle casual dining and dessert restaurant. Originally a designer boutique, the 10 Corso Como Café also operates a shop on the side that carries fashion and make-up.

title: Umigak
short_description: Umigak is a meat restaurant that offers fresh Korean-raised beef. The meat is tender, with good marbling. The beef here is chargrilled with mushrooms and rounded sticks of rice cake on a copper hot plate. Also popular is their shabu shabu, meat boiled with vegetables in broth.

title: Tteurak
short_description: Tteurak is a barbeque restaurant where you can grill meat over oak charcoal. It's even more enjoyable to eat in the garden, surrounded by the jujube, persimmon, grape,and plum trees.

title: Lagrillia
short_description: Lagrillia offers a variety of dishes grilled over an intense oak charcoal fire. The ingredients they use are high quality, and at the dessert bar, you'll find a nice selection of twenty different varieties of homebaked desserts, made daily by the baker.

title: Madam Ming
short_description: This Chinese restaurant offers Peking and Szechuan cuisine at relatively low prices. Their spicy and refreshing jjamppong naengmyeon (chilled spicy seafood noodle soup) is a popular choice in the summer. You'll also find a variety of noodle and rice dishes on the menu such as jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), jajangmyeon (thick noodles topped with a rich black soybean sauce), and gesalbokkeumbap (crab fried rice), all of which can be refilled as often as you like.

title: Yeongcheon Yeonghwa Sigyuk Sikdang
short_description: Yeongcheon Yeonghwa Sigyuk Sikdang is the Seoul branch of the famous Daegu restaurant, Yeongcheon Yeonghwa. Here you can chargrill properly-matured Korean beef. The side dishes served with the beef are quite tasty.

title: Waraku
short_description: Enjoy authentic Japanese kushiyaki (grilled meat skewers) at Waraku. The skewers make a great accompaniment for drinks. Rumor has it that, among the izakaya (Japanese bars) that have sprung up recently, this place serves the most authentic-tasting grilled skewers.

title: Bogeonok
short_description: Bogeonok is famous for kimchi jjigae (a stew made with mainly kimchi, pork, and tofu). However, it is only served at lunch time. In addition, they offer high-quality beef bulgogi (marinated thinly-sliced beef).

title: Busan Galmaegi
short_description: Busan Galmaegi takes pride in their saengtaetang (fresh pollack soup), which is quite thick and rich-tasting, due to the generous portion of fish organs such as egg sacks, milt, and hard roe they add to their soup, giving it a rich and meaty flavor. The combination of soft pollack flesh and fish organs is excellent.

title: Busan Sikdang
short_description: Busan Sikdang serves simple home-style baekban (a simple set meal of rice, soup or stew, and side dishes). The owner, who is originally from Busan, makes the fermented soybean paste with which the soup broth is made from. Freshly steamed kongbap (rice with beans) is served about half an hour after your order has been taken. Their saengtae jjigae (pollack soup) and tofu are also very famous.

title: Bulia
short_description: Bulia specializes in Chinese-style hot pot made a little less spicy to suit Korean tastes. The set menu with beef, lamb and assorted vegetables is the most popular menu item.

title: Daedongmun
short_description: Daedongmun, run by a woman from Pyeongyang, her son, and her daughter-in-law, has been faithfully reproducing Pyeongyang traditional cuisine for over 20 years. Menu items include eobok jaengban (pressed beef served on a brass plate), manduguk (Korean dumpling soup), kongbiji (puréed soybean soup), and nokdu jijim (mung bean pancakes).

title: B-hind
short_description: Espresso is freshly brewed from Italian Molinari beans and poured over vanilla ice cream to produce B-hind's unique affogato al caffè. This café is well-known for its comfortable atmosphere, ideal for couples. They often hold a flea market.

title: Odarizip
short_description: Odarizip is a unique restaurant in Myeong-dong that combines Korean cuisine with live musical performances. Odarizip specializes in ganjang-gejang (soy-marinated crab), but there are many other tasty menu items like Odarizip's Korean beef andKorean pork dishes. The restaurant has live performances of K-pop every evening starting at 19:00 on the restaurant's 3rd floor. Odarizip is especially popular with Chinese and Japanese tourists.

title: Pomodoro
short_description: Before pasta was commonplace in Korea, Pomodoro was already a spaghetti house so famous that you had to wait in line for an hour to get in. Their pasta sauce, which is made to order, is still very popular.

title: Yangmani
short_description: Here, you’ll find the freshest and finest yang, or tripe, in Seoul. The dish is marinated in a special sauce for 24 hours and then grilled. Other cuts are also available.

title: Sadong Myeonok
short_description: Sadong Myeonok specializes in Hwanghae-style mandu (Korean dumplings) that are bigger that an adult fist. The special characteristic of this dumpling is that it is boiled, not steamed. Other items on the menu include doganitang, a special beef broth made by slowly boiling beef bones; nokdujeon, Korean style pancakes made with mung bean; and pajeon, Korean style pancakes made with green onions, all of which come with high recommendations. The interior of the restaurant is decorated in traditional Korean style and is very elegant.

title: Malta Chamchi
short_description: Malta Chamchi specializes in tuna. The prices are reasonable, but cuts like otoro (front part of tuna abdomen), beggop (the underside of the chutoro cut) , and kamatoro (abdomen part around the gills of tuna) are of quite good quality.

title: Songok
short_description: Songok has specialized in Memil Guksu (buckwheat noodles) for over 40 years. Their pleasing broth is made with bold-tasting katsuobushi (a traditional Japanese soup base) and soy sauce. The restaurant demonstrates their expertise with udon (thick wheat-flour noodles) that are chewy and delicious.

title: Sandong Gyoja
short_description: Sandong Gyoja looks a bit run down, but the Chinese couple that runs it makes true, authentic Chinese food. They are famous for their steamed dumplings, which are wrapped with very thin dough so that the savory stuffing of Chinese leeks and braised pork is front and center.

title: Songjuk
short_description: Songjuk is a great place to try out several kinds of juk (porridge). What sets the juk here apart from other places is that they use short grain rice that has been cooked in sesame oil and beef bone soup. Mushroom oyster juk and oyster intestine cookedoyster juk are some of their most popular dishes.

title: Forest of Music
short_description: Forest of Music is a music-themed cafe with a large archive of old vinyl records. The owner DJs at the cafe and takes song requests. Every object in the shop is a reminder of the analog past. The walls are covered with autographs from celebrities who have visited the shop in the past. Forest of Music was featured in the Korean movie "Sunny" and the Jayuro Gayoje episode of Infinite Challenge featuring G-Dragon.

title: Daeryeodo
short_description: Daeryeodo serves authentic Beijing cuisine, a favorite among Koreans. For 40,000 - 50,000 won, you can enjoy set menus of ten different dishes, including seasoned cold vegetables, shark's fin, stir-fried bamboo shoots and sea cucumber, shrimp, and other Beijing delicacies.

title: Samo Jjukkumi
short_description: Samo Jjukkumi has specialized in jjukkumi (small octopus) for over 30 years. Jjukkumi here prepared in a special way, by grilling it and also frying it with a unique red chili pepper paste and other spices, giving it a delicate flavor to go along with the octopus’s natural chewyness. Prices are low and customer satisfaction is high.

title: Yangmani (Cheongdam branch)
short_description: At Yangmani, you can enjoy intestines in a clean, comfortable atmosphere. Here the grilled ox stomach and large intestines are especially popular. They use New Zealand ox stomach and Korean ox large intestines. Also worth trying is their yangwutang (ox tripe simmered in a broth made from dried cabbage leaves). The main branch is located in Yeouido.

title: Yeolchajip
short_description: At Yeolchajip, you can enjoy a bowl of makgeolli (Korean rice wine) with bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), guljeon (oyster pancakes), or one of their other delicacies. They grind mung beans in a millstone and place the mixture on a hot plate topped with a few pieces of pork, which yields mung bean pancakes that are crispy and delicious. At dinnertime, the place is packed with people who come to have the pancakes with makgeolli.

title: Tao Yuen
short_description: This Chinese restaurant has been run by a hotel for 30 years, so you can expect high standards. Their menu features a balanced selection of the four main Chinese regional cuisines, ensuring a dining experience with a variety of different flavors. It's not uncommon to spot heads of large corporations and politicians dining here.

title: Dohyangchon
short_description: The traditional Chinese confections served in this shop are all-natural, with the distinctive aromas and rich flavors of Chinese sweets. Their jasmine tea, which includes 16 ingredients, goes very well with the variety of Chinese sweets they offer, particularly the moon cakes.

title: Seogang 8-gyeong
short_description: As a classy restaurant with a view of Hangang。Seogang 8-gyeong offers a wide selection of beverages during the day and whiskey and wine at night. Their motto is to entice the diner’s taste buds with French cuisine and offer an eyeful of Hangang. Seogang 8-gyeong was featured on King of Ambition, Incarnation of Money, and My Love from the Star. The restaurant is sectioned into six-themed private rooms where guests can enjoy a full French course meal while taking in the view of the river. The 9th floor is a sky lounge that serves wine, cocktails, and whiskey. Seogang 8-gyeong is a reservation-only restaurant.

title: Encore Kalguksu
short_description: Encore Kalguksu is a Kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) restaurant affiliated with Baengnyeonok, a very famous tofu restaurant. Here you can enjoy Baeknyeonok's most popular dishes, like the Maesaengyi Kalguksu (soup with noodles made with a type of seaweed) and Pat Kalguksu, which is Kalguksu with red beans.

title: Saemban Makguksu
short_description: Saemban Makguksu is the Seoul branch of Sambat Makguksu in Chuncheon. They use noodles made of 80% buckwheat flour. In addition to the popular representative dish Makguksu (buckwheat noodles in a spicy sauce), gamjajeon (Korean-style potato pancakes), and bossam (steamed pork with fresh unfermented kimchi) are also recommended. The assorted Korean-style pancakes, made with shrimp, king oyster mushrooms, meat and vegetable skewers, zucchini, and fish are good, too.

title: Pungyoram
short_description: Pungyoram has been in operation in the same location, specializing in beef loin and pork ribs for nearly 35 years. An order of diced beef loin also comes with a sampling of 3 or 4 pieces of chadolbagi (brisket). After you are done with the meat, they fry a generous serving of rice on the same hot plate, a delicious way to end your meal.

title: Cafe Noshi
short_description: Cafe Noshi is a dessert cafe that serves desserts in artisanal brassware. The brassware used at the cafe is made by master craftsmen at the Dubooja Workshop. Popular menu items are watermelon sherbet, persimmon-flavored ice cream, and red bean-flavored ice cream. The beautiful brassware makes the delicious menu items even more delectable. Visitors can purchase brassware at the cafe's gallery or online at the official Cafe Noshi website.

title: Seorin Nakji
short_description: Those who like spicy foods should definitely try out this place. If the stir-fried octopus looks too spicy, try the Bacon Sausage, cooked on a hot plate with octopus broth. The jeon, egg roll, and clam soup are also recommended for countering the spiciness.

title: Seogang Kkeopdegi
short_description: ​Seogang Kkeopdegi is considered the best pork rinds place in Seoul. The restaurant specializes in pork dishes of all kinds and their roasted pork is also very popular. For K-pop fans, the restaurant is known as a favorite dining spot for the idolgroup BigBang; the group often ate here before their debut. It is a must-visit spot for BigBang fans.

title: Yeongdeokhoe Sikdang
short_description: Some twenty years ago, Yeongdeokhoe Sikdang first introduced restaurant-goers in downtown Seoul to Makhoe (a few different kinds of sliced small fish) mixed with vegetables and vinegar chili paste. In the winter, the partly dried Pacific herring has anexquisite flavor, and Mulhoe (thinly sliced fish or squid seasoned with green onions, garlic, and chili pepper power) and hoedupbap (raw fish on rice) make for a good meal.

title: Somunnanjip Chueotang
short_description: Although the name of this restaurant translates to "famous loach soup", Somunnanjip Chueotang doesn't actually serve chueotang (loach soup). They have gained their reputation for haejangguk (a soup eaten as a remedy for hangover). They used to sell chueotang, but now, regardless of the name of the restaurant, they serve only haejangguk, a spicy soup made with dried napa cabbage. Here food is prepared without you needing to order; you only have to tell them how many people are in your group.

title: Yeongnak Golbaengi
short_description: Yeongnak Golbaengi and the restaurant next door, Yeongdong Golbaengi, were the first to introduce golbaengi (freshwater snailsl) in Euljiro's famous Golbaengi Alley. Here, you'll find side dishes to have with beer, with generous portions at modest prices. Alongside the golbaengi, you'll also be served gyeranmari, a Korean omelet with chopped vegetables, which is also good.

title: Songpa Naru
short_description: Songpa Naru specializes in fish dishes, such as grilled hairtail, grilled mackerel, and braised sole. They offer gomchi haejangguk (a soup made with moray eel, commonly eaten as a remedy for hangovers), which is hard to find in other restaurants in Seoul, and the steamed sablefish also tastes fantastic. Even better are the delicious Haemulpajeon (seafood and green onion pancakes) and guljeon (oyster pancakes).

title: Ranju Ramien
short_description: Ranju Ramien is famous for dosakmyeon, noodles made by holding the dough on the shoulder and slicing off long strips. The Szechuan dosakmyeon tastes a lot like jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), and the Lanju dosakmyeon is topped with a sauce similar to black soybean paste. Also available are Korean dishes, such as kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup), bossam (steamed pork and kimchi), and shabu shabu (hot pot).

title: Sokcho Saengtaejip
short_description: There is no fixed menu at Sokcho Saengtaejip; what they offer depends on the available ingredients, so they decide on a new menu and prices every day. They typically serve saengtaetang (pollack soup) at lunchtime, and for dinner, you can enjoy hoe (sashimi) made from wild fish and maeuntang (spicy fish soup) prepared with various kinds of fish.

title: Yeongyang Center
short_description: This place is the home of Korean-style rotisserie chicken.  The outside of the chicken is crispy while the inside is moist and tender.  Although good as a lunch or dinner, the chicken is also good as a side menu item for beer.

title: Songbaek Sikdang
short_description: Songbaek Sikdang is famous for budae jjigae (spicy sausage stew). Their budae jjigae contains more ham and sausage than at most places, and they'll refill your rice and ramen noodles as often as you'd like. The addition of bean sprouts gives their budae jjigae a more refreshing taste. The kimchi, sausage, ham, and bacon fried with butter on the hot plate is especially delicious.

title: Mugunghwa
short_description: The interior of Mugunghwa is decorated in a traditional Korean style, and a lot of foreign guests also visit the restaurant in the evening to listen to a live performance of Kayageum (a twelve-stringed Korean zither).  All side dishes are neatly presented, and it's clear a lot of sincerity and care goes into making and serving the food.

title: Yeongchunok
short_description: Yeongchunok is famous for their steamed ox tail, gomtang (a thin soup with a rich flavor from simmering ox bones), and haejangguk (a soup of congealed ox blood, napa cabbage, and vegetables in a hearty beef broth). Starting at 3 p.m., they serve their popular ddagwi, an earthenware bowl filled with meaty bones that have been boiled to prepare haejangguk broth. However, only 40 orders are available each day, so they quickly sell out.

title: Myeongdong Budae Jjigae
short_description: The specialty of Yennal Myeongdong Budaejjigae is a dish called budae jjigae, which is made with pork, ham, and sausage. Serving sizes are big and the broth is fantastic. This restaurant is also known for its samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly).

title: Osuheugdubu
short_description: Osu specializes in tofu, and most of the dishes here are made with nutritious homemade tofu made of black sesame seeds and black soybeans. The popular favorite of Osu is heukdububossam, steamed pork and black sesame tofu that is eaten with rice served in a hot stone bowl and wrapped in seaweed and napa cabbage.

title: Soseonjae
short_description: Soseonjae offers healthy dishes prepared with wild plants. Their full-course set menu includes root vegetables with leafy green wraps, dandelion and wild herb salad, wild herb vegetable pancakes, boiled pork with soy-sauce kimchi wraps, stuffed tofu, plus chicken salad and grilled Patagonia toothfish at additional cost. This small restaurant, transformed from a hanok (traditional Korean house), has only about ten tables.

title: Jogeum
short_description: This place is popular for its Japanese style stone pot rice and udon noodles. There are three varieties of stone pot rice, of which the Jogeum Stone Pot Rice with seafood is the most popular. Dori King also has a clean Japanese style interior.

title: Ojangdong Hamheung Naengmyeon
short_description: Ojang-dong Hamheung Naengmyeon is a naengmyeon restaurant started by President  Han Hye-seon  in Ojang-dong after the Korean War. It became the place that introduced Hamheung Naengmyeon—a dish enjoyed by people from Hamgyong Province—to the entire country. Since the 1970s, many Hamheung-style naengmyeon restaurants in Ojang-dong have disappeared due to redevelopment and changing times. However, Ojang-dong Hamheung Naengmyeon has maintained its presence to this day by creating an appealing naengmyeon that deepens the flavor of thin noodles with spicy sauce and fresh raw fish toppings, adding savoriness through the harmonious blend of sugar, sesame oil, and vinegar.

title: Pulhyanggi Sonkalguksu
short_description: Pulhyanggi Sonkalguksu has been serving up kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) for 20 years. The noodles here are very soft and chewy. Another recommended dish is their haemulpajeon (seafood and green onion pancakes), loaded with shrimp and clams. Also excellent is the bossam, thinly-sliced steamed pork with napa cabbage wraps served with wrapped kimchi that is made fresh daily.

title: Yeoksamdong Bugeojip
short_description: At Yeoksamdong Bugeojip, you can enjoy mildly spicy bukeojjim (seasoned simmered dried pollack). At lunch time, they only serve bukeojjim with rice and side dishes. Many people come to cure their hangover by having bukeojjim and soup.

title: Café Rosso
short_description: Cafe Rosso is a quiet and beautiful cafe in Samcheong-dong with a quiet and luxe atmosphere. The cafe has a distinctive red sign. Cafe Rosso serves Brazil Fazenda drip coffee and delicious cakes. The cafe is well-known for its quality dessertsand visitors should also check out the cafe's wine menu.

title: Omokjib
short_description: Omokjib serves pork hocks with homemade soybean paste. It is a great restaurant to visit in family units thanks to its wholesome and welcoming atmosphere. Omokjib pork hocks are known for its excellent texture, which is appreciated by all guests regardlessof age and gender. All pork hocks come with a seafood casserole.

title: Wan Chai
short_description: Wan Chai is a Chinese restaurant in the Sinchon area that is rather small, but it is famous enough that you'll see long lines in the alley to get into this restaurant in the evening. Their popularity is due to their unique dishes and low prices. The Hong Kong-style spicy mussel dishes are famous, and their spicy Szechuan-style dishes are very good as well.

title: Jineo
short_description: The owner of Jineo has been in the tuna business for about 30 years, earning himself the moniker, "The Tuna Doctor". If you sit at the counter, you can get detailed descriptions of the various tuna varieties as you taste them. The quality is quite satisfactory for the price. Since there are only seven places at the counter, reservations are necessary for those seats.

title: Wangseong Sikdang
short_description: Koreans love their Galchi Jorim. Galchi(Cutlassfish) is a long, thin fish that tastes great when it is boiled in a spicy mixture of kelp and mixed vegetables. Wangseong Sikdang is famous for this dish, so expect long lines at lunch time. It is located in a narrow alley in Namdaemun Market.

title: Jinju Hoegwan
short_description: This place is famous for its noodles in cold soybean soup (kongguksu), one of Korea’s favorite summer meals. The dough for the noodles here is also noteworthy for containing assorted nuts and potato starch. Thick and savory kongguksu is popular in the summer while winter is the season for kimchi fried-rice. Expect to wait for a table during peak hours.

title: Tsukushi
short_description: This Japanese-style bar offers a variety of side dishes and Japanese sake. At lunch time, they serve Nagasaki-style jjamppong, a seafood and vegetable soup made with a thick broth from simmered pork leg bones. The noodles, which are a little thicker than normal, and the savoury broth are what make this jjamppong so popular. Be sure to also try the homemade-style Japanese side dishes and sashimi.

title: Urimil Guksi
short_description: Urimil Guksi specializes in Sagol Kalguksu, handmade knife-cut noodle soup. The 'sagol' broth is made with four leg bones of Korean-bred cows for high quality taste, and the noodles, which are thinner than regular kalguksu, have a nice chewy texture. Kalguksu is best enjoyed garnished with beef brisket and zucchini and topped with spicy seasonings.

title: Chakraa
short_description: At Chakraa you can enjoy tandoori chicken, lamb kebabs, and five different types of curry with an unlimited amount of naan bread and white rice. You can also try the pan-fried uttapam, and dosa (South Indian crepes made from rice and black lentils). Anotherpopular dish is the crispy sambar vada. A lunch buffet is also available.

title: Ujeong Nakji
short_description: If you like spicy foods, this is the place for you. The stir-fried octopus here is some of the spiciest you’ll find in Seoul. To help fan the flames, the octopus is served with bean sprouts and clam soup. At night, office workers fill the restaurant to unwind after a hard day’s work.

title: Hangangjip
short_description: Hangang Saengtae is famous for its spicy fresh pollack soup made with a broth from 14 different kinds of seafood, including blue crab and lobster. The soup is spiced up with chili paste, red pepper, and garlic. Besides pollack stew, samgyeopsal (grilledpork belly) is also famous. Reservations for lunch are advisable as the place gets quite busy.

title: Hyehwa Kalguksu
short_description: Hyehwa Kalguksu is a kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) restaurant that has been a fixture of Hyehwa-dong for almost 30 years and faithfully maintains its long-standing traditions. To their four-leg broth, they add beef brisket and simmer it for24 hours, so the finely-sliced noodles that they serve in it taste fantastic. Besides kalguksu they also serve thinly-sliced bulgogi-style beef flame broiled in a grid iron, fish tempura, and octopus.

title: Ceci Cela (Seorae Village branch)
short_description: This is the Seorae Village branch of Ceci Cela, the main branch of which is in front of Dosan Park. This café offers mainly waffles. With its bright and cheerful Mediterranean-style interior, this cafe is a good place to enjoy weekend brunch. They also offer easy wireless Internet access.

title: Yurimmyeon
short_description: Yurim Myeon is a noodle specialty shop that opened in 1960 and is now operated by the third generation. Located in Seosomun-dong, it is a place where you can feel the tradition and history of Korea. At the time of its opening, when flour came in as relief supplies, they started a noodle shop where many people could enjoy a meal at an affordable price. Now, with the know-how accumulated over generations, it has grown into a shop loved by many. To achieve a chewy texture, the noodles are aged in advance, and as soon as an order comes in, they are immediately boiled. The signature dish is bibim buckwheat noodles, where the chewy noodles and sweet and spicy sauce harmonize, and fresh toppings and a sprinkle of sesame enhance the flavor.

title: Andongjang
short_description: Even though Andongjang is one of the oldest Chinese restaurants in Seoul, it has maintained the same classic tastes since 1948. It is famous for their delicious guljjamppong (spicy noodle soup with oysters), and you can choose either the mild or the spicy variation according to your taste.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Imun Seollongtang
short_description: Imun Seollongtang is one of the oldest Seolleongtang (ox bone soup) restaurants in Seoul with over 100 years of proud history. The family that owns it has passed it down from one generation to the next since the beginning of the 1900s. The current chef has been making Seolleongtang made from slowly simmered meat and beef bones for the last 20 years.

title: Yeouido Ttaro Gukbap
short_description: Yeouido Ttaro Gukbap specializes in ttarogukbap, a bowl of beef shank and rice in a thick broth. Kkori jjim, braised ox tail, is also popular. They've been in operation in the Yeouido area for about 30 years.

title: Cheong
short_description: Cheong offers fusion dishes based on Chinese cuisine but with a Western twist. Their black vinegar tenderloin steak is quite unique.

title: Cheongsujeong
short_description: This restaurant is famous for their honghapbap, a dish of fried rice with sea mussels and dried clam, seasoned with soy sauce and sesame oil. The meal can also be purchased for takeout with three or four side dishes, all at a reasonable price. The restaurant version of the meal comes with more than 10 delicious side dishes.

title: Canadian Lobster
short_description: Canadian Lobster serves a variety of dishes that feature lobster prepared in a variety of ways, such as sashimi, grilled with butter, chili, steamed, and au gratin. Set menus come with your choice of sashimi, a steamed dish, and two grilled dishes. They import wild North-Atlantic lobsters caught off the coast of Nova Scotia, Canada.

title: Wasedaya
short_description: Wasedaya specializes in Japanese-style charcoal barbecue, known as yakiniku. Yakiniku is Korean bulgogi (marinated thinly-sliced beef) that has been adapted for Japanese tastes. Recommended dishes are grilled beef tongue garnished with sliced green onions, sesame oil, and salt, and cheonyup sashimi (beef omasum). You can also enjoy rib eye roll, beef short ribs, fresh sirloin, and hangjeongsal (meat from the back of the neck).

title: Hwangu Yanggopchang
short_description: Hwangu Yanggopchang is a high-quality tripe and small intestine restaurant. Their menu has only this one dish, but you can order it with or without seasoning. The small intestines are cooked on a traditional oil drum grill in a grilling basket.

title: Kkongsi Myeongwan
short_description: The main dish at Kkongsi Myeongwan is xiǎolóngbāo, dumplings steamed in a small bamboo basket. The boiled pork ribs are a special treat and have the authentic taste of Chinese spices. The delicious taste of garlic pork ribs is also famous. It is interesting to find omurice on the menu because it seems out of place, but it is very creative for its use of interesting ingredients like eggplant and shrimp.

title: Eunseongjip
short_description: Eunseongjip is famous for Korean-style teppanyaki, and offer a selection of steak, sausages, and vegetables for broiling on the iron griddle. One of their specialities is an assorted sausage hot plate with ham, sausage, bacon, tenderloin, onions, and potatoes, sprinkled with pepper. Interestingly, young radish kimchi is substituted for the usual pickles. Also, they are famous for their budae jjigae (spicy sausage stew).

title: Huirak
short_description: The dented tin pots they use are the hallmark of Huirak, a restaurant specializing in galchi jorim (braised hairtail). They roughly cut radishes into large rounds and place them in the bottom of a tin pot; then add water, sauce, and large pieces of hairtail.This is boiled down halfway and finished when you place your order. They also take a lot of pride in making their own red pepper paste made from chili peppers that they dry and grind themselves. Rice is refilled as many times as you'd like. This is theoriginal branch of Huirak in Namdaemun.

title: Eunho Sikdang
