short_description: For three generations, Eunho Sikdang has been steadily maintaining the same taste of the original kkori gomtang, (oxtail soup) that they first made when they operated a street vendor stall in Namdaemun Market 70 years ago. In addition to oxtail soup, you can also have doganitang (ox knee and beef stew), seolleongtang (a thin, milky-white beef soup made from slowly simmered oxtails and bones), and suyuk (steamed pork).

title: Myeongnyun Sonkalguksu
short_description: The most popular item of Myeongnyun Sonkalguksu is kalguksu, handmade knife-cut noodles in beef broth. The thick boiled brisket and flank and lightly boiled octopus are also good. You can order half portions of each and taste a bit of everything. Therestaurant closes relatively early in the evening and they often close early if ingredients run out.

title: Pyeongando Mandujip
short_description: Pyeongando Mandujip is a home-style Pyeongyang mandu (Korean dumpling) shop. Besides dumplings, another popular item on the menu is bossam (sliced boiled pork wrapped in spiced napa cabbage), with generous amounts of fresh oysters and spring onion salad.Their pure mung bean pancakes made with finely-ground mung beans are another delicacy. The food here is subtle and light-tasting, and some would claim it doesn't suit young people, who are accustomed to stronger flavors.

title: About Shabu
short_description: At About Shabu, you can relax and enjoy Korean-style shabu shabu. Fresh vegetables, meat, and seafood are parboiled in one of three different pots (spicy red soup, milky beef broth, and skipjack tuna broth) and then eaten with chili or lemon sauce.

title: Seocho Namsunnam Sundaeguk
short_description: The sundaeguk (blood sausage soup) at Seocho Namsunnam Sundaeguk doesn't exhibit the usual strong, distinctive smell of sundaeguk, so those who don't normally like this soup will find it pleasing. The soup is served with a generous amount of pork tripe. Salted and fermented shrimp, chopped seasonings, green perilla seed powder, and black pepper can be added to taste, making the soup savory and a bit spicy.

title: Chungmuro Jjukkumi Bulgogi
short_description: At Chungmuro Jjukkumi Bulgogi, you can have delicious baby octopus marinated in red pepper sauce and lightly chargrilled. They buy large quantities of baby octopus between October and February, when they taste the best, and freeze them for use throughoutthe year.

title: Muntaro
short_description: This is a Japanese-style pub where you can enjoy a drink with grilled chicken and pork belly shish-kebabs.

title: Gitdaebong Naengmyeon
short_description: Gitdaebong Naengmyeon is a naengmyeon restaurant with over 40 years of history. They are famous for spicy bibim naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles and vegetables mixed with spicy sauce). Compared to traditional North Korean naengmyeon, theirs is said to be like the naengmyeon served in snack bars, but they have a loyal following. You can choose the level of spiciness; not spicy, mildly spicy, and spicy.

title: Park Ruan
short_description: With its synthesis of antique and modern, what better place is there to enjoy authentic Chinese cuisine than in this beautiful restaurant? A great place for family gatherings and entertaining guests.

title: Seodaemun Gopchang
short_description: Seodaemun Gopchang is a gopchang (tripe) restaurant with a 30-year history. The gopchang grilled with potatoes and onions on the hot plate are excellent. When the gopchang is are fully grilled, restaurant workers add a finishing touch in the wayof a light sprinkle of soju for a fiery display.

title: Taj
short_description: The Indian chef at Taj reproduces the cuisine of northern India with ingredients flown in from India. All of the dishes are available in vegetarian and non-vegetarian variations. Because Indians are primarily vegetarian, they prepare a variety of excellent vegetable curries and tandoori dishes that are popular with vegetarians. The restaurant interior is very luxurious.

title: Afternoon Tea
short_description: Afternoon Tea offers a selection of four hundred varieties of tea brought in directly from ten different countries. Three tea masters are always on hand at the shop. One of the most popular teas is Tiangpang tea, the name of which means "the best of all"in Chinese. When hot water is poured in, the tea swells up like chrysanthemums blooming, and although it tastes similar to green tea, there is a light lingering fragrance of chrysanthemums.

title: Pajuok
short_description: To produce their very thick broth, the cooks at Pajuok simmer beef leg and tail bones in a large cauldron for more than five hours. They are as famous for their geotjeori (fresh napa cabbage tossed with kimchi seasonings) as they are for their seolleongtang(a thin, milky-white soup made from slowly simmered oxtails and bones). The restaurant originally started in Pyeongtaek, but there are now branches in Seoul.

title: Pyeongnaeok
short_description: Pyeongnaeok is famous for its chogyetang, a kind of chicken soup. Their pheasant naengmyeon is made with the same broth as ordinary naengmyeon but comes topped with pheasant meatballs. The tasty nokdujeon (mung bean pancakes) and spicy stir-fried pork are also very good. Most of the clientele here tends to be a bit older. This restaurant moved from its former location when the area was re-developed, but ever since re-opening in its new location, they have been very popular.

title: Beijingkoya
short_description: The chef at Beijingkoya presents traditional Peking duck, building on the skills gained at Jeonchiduck, the most famous duck restaurant in China. Having the bite-sized duck on a Chinese pancake and topping it off with sliced cucumber, shallot, and dark plum sauce, is highly recommended. Besides Peking duck, they also offer a variety of Chinese cuisine.

title: Mokpojip
short_description: Mokpojip is said to faithfully reproduce the cuisine of Jeollanam-do (the southern province of the region of Jeolla), including such dishes as hongeohoe (spicy skate sashimi in vinegar), hongeojjim (steamed skate), tteokgalbi (grilled minced ribs), octopus,yeonpotang (small octopus soup), and home-style meals with rice.

title: Ca'del Lupo
short_description: Ca'del Lupo is an Italian restaurant converted from a traditional Korean house. Enjoy a comfortable meal in a unique atmosphere. Their set menus are quite reasonably priced, and you can make a reservation to enjoy your meal in one of their cosy, detached buildings.

title: N Grill
short_description: N Grill is a fine dining restaurant in Namsan N Seoul Tower. They serve full-course set menus,  and are known for their steaks. The restaurant is a high-end establishment, and this is reflected in the prices. However, in addition to delicious food, there is a beautiful panoramic night view of Seoul that is hard to beat. N Grill is a good place to have dinner with someone special on an anniversary or a special occasion. Reservations are required. One way to reach N Grill is via the Namsan cable car.

title: Sinyetchatjip
short_description: With its tranquil atmosphere, this traditional tea house seems separate from the rest of the world. As soon as you enter, you'll hear the sounds of the many birds and animals that are kept here. Pretty multi-colored rice cakes are served with your tea. Everything is rustic and cozy, so that you feel like you're in a natural setting.

title: Nunnamujip
short_description: The main menu item here is the cold kimchi noodles, which go well with the sweet beef rib patties or mung bean pancakes on offer. The clean and simple interior, moderate price range and delicious food keep the customers coming back for more.

title: La Stella
short_description: La Stella is an authentic Italian restaurant serving a variety of steak and Italian pasta dishes. The wine bar also stocks two hundred varieties of wine. As an appetizer, the seafood platter, which includes lobster, mussels, clams, squid, and sea bream, is recommended.

title: Hosu Samgyetang
short_description: Hosu Samgyetang's samgyetang (chicken and ginseng soup) is characterized by its thick and aromatic broth due to the addition of perilla seeds. There are many restaurants with the same name in the neighbourhood, so be sure that you have the right one.

title: Chamasineun Tteul
short_description: Enjoy a soothing traditional tea at a cozy teahouse filled with the traditional flavors and atmosphere of Old Korea. Also recommended are the sweet steamed rice cakes made on the premises.

title: Chamnamu Sutbure Dalgi Mannaneun Sungan
short_description: The chicken at Chamnamu Sutbure Dalgi Mannaneun Sungan is marinated for three days in a sauce made of more than ten ingredients, such as garlic, red pepper, ginger, sugar, and soy sauce, and grilled to order, so the chicken is very tender and full offlavor.

title: Mapo Naru
short_description: At Mapo Naru, which looks like a traditional Korean tavern, you can enjoy a variety of folk dishes such as jeongol (hot pot), bossam (steamed pork with kimchi), jeon (Korean pancakes), ssambap (rice wrapped in assorted vegetables), and generous amountof a variety of side dishes. They also serve alcohol, so it is a good place to have a family gatherings or all sorts of get-togethers.

title: Mangnae Hoe Center
short_description: At Mangnae Hoe Center, you can have Korean-style sashimi, prepared from live fish. They offer a range of small wild fish that are not easy to find in other restaurants, such as perch, gizzard shad, yellowtail, tochigi, and mullet, among others. Full-courseset menus come with a diverse selection of delicacies, including mackerel, sea cucumber, prawn, kingfish, and various smaller fish.

title: Cheongsongok
short_description: Cheongsongok is famous in Seosomun-dong for jangteogukbap, rice served with ox blood soup made from beef broth and radish, into which noodles are added. It is a good remedy for a hangover.

title: Taschen
short_description: Taschen is an art book café where you'll find various art books by Taschen, one of the most famous publishing companies. You can enjoy reading while having one of their various and wiches, a cup of coffee or tea. The Taschen art books are also available for purchase.

title: Samho Bokjip
short_description: Samho Bokjip has been very popular for bogeo (puffer fish) dishes for about 30 years. Their tang (soup), made with fresh puffer fish and fresh vegetables, has a delicious and refreshing taste. Another popular menu item is their bok 'shabu shabu', whichinvolves dipping thinly-sliced puffer fish wrapped around mushrooms and vegetables in boiling broth. Other delicious choices on the menu include the bok sushi, beoseot jjim (mushrooms steamed with seasonings), and doenjang ttukbaegi (soybean paste stewin an earthenware bowl).

title: Tower Chai
short_description: Tower Chai specializes in shark's fin. They serve standard Chinese cuisine, but the main attractions are the various dishes made with shark's fin, such as soup and steamed shark's fin. One advantage of this place is that instead of the processed frozen shark's fin that is commonly used, they use processed white shark's fin shipped directly from the South Pacific.

title: Persian Palace
short_description: Persian Palace is an Iranian spicy curry restaurant run by an Iranian immigrant. Their best dish is curry made with lamb marinated in seasonings for three days. The smoked chicken curry is also recommended. Their Persian full-course set menus includevarious kinds of curries, six pieces of chicken, and Iranian-style rice cakes. In addition to curries, you can enjoy various kinds of exotic food, such as Iranian-style bread, yogurt, and alcoholic beverages.

title: Pyeongyang Myeonok
short_description: This is a 3rd generation naengmyeon restaurant. The restaurant also has Eobokjaengban, beef slices served in a copper dish.

title: Pyeongyangjip
short_description: The most popular dish of Pyeongyangjip is chadolbagi (beef brisket point cut) chargrilled in a rectangular steel grilling basket which comes with a delicious sweet and sour dipping sauce. The tripe and small intestines are also popular. Cabbage and raw garlic are the only side dishes. Fried rice with sliced tripe and cubed radish kimchi is the only rice dish, but it is also very popular. As soon as they open early in the morning, naejangtang (innards soup) is available for breakfast.

title: Pildong Myeonok
short_description: Pildong Myeonok features authentic Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles in an iced broth). To properly enjoy naengmyeon, it should be eaten together with Pyeongan-style mandu (Korean dumplings) or jeyuk (steamed pork slices). Their bibimnaengmyeon (spicy mixed buckwheat noodles) is served with a bowl of the water used to cook the noodles rather than beef broth.

title: Pyeongandojip
short_description: Even in the Jangchung-dong area, where the dish originates, this restaurant has a good reputation for its jokbal (sliced pigs trotters in soy sauce). They serve their jokbal neatly sliced and arranged on a tray. It is very tender and chewy and tastes excellent. According to the staff, they only prepare enough jokbal each day to fill the day's orders.

title: Seoncheon
short_description: Seoncheon has served hanjeongsik (Korean set menu) meals for over 40 years. The full-course meal is based on cuisine from the province of Pyeongan-do and includes 10 to 13 different dishes, such as gujeolpan (a platter of nine colorful ingredients served with thin crepes), sashimi, soup, steamed meat or fish, jeon (Korean-style pancakes), skewered bulgogi (marinated thinly shredded beef), and spicy pork. At lunch time, they serve a popular lunch set menu of main dishes and side dishes selected from the full-course meal.

title: Seopji Koji
short_description: Seopji Koji is dedicated to serving the regional cuisine of Jeju, particularly wild abalone. They use wild abalone delivered directly from Jeju. Also good is their sashimi such as rock bream, coral fish, and saw-edged perch. The interior is neat.

title: Taj Palace
short_description: Taj Palace is an Indian restaurant that serves authentic cuisine made by Indian chefs. Recommended is the assortment of various tandoori barbecue dishes. There are also various dishes for vegetarians available at reasonable prices.

title: Passion 5
short_description: This is a landmark of the Hannam-dong region. Although a bit expensive, the luxurious interior and great tasting desserts will make up for it.

title: Oegojip Seolleongtang
short_description: Oegojip Seolleongtang is famous for their authentic seolleongtang (a thin, milky-white soup made from slowly simmered oxtails and bones). What sets their seolleongtang apart is their use of Hoengseong-raised beef and domestic ingredients (napa cabbage,radish, chili pepper powder, and sun-dried salt). Selected for the Michelin Guide Seoul 2025.

title: Teumsae Ramyeon
short_description: Go to Teumsae Ramyeon to enjoy various kinds of ramyeon, Korean-style instant noodles (also known as ramen). Most of the ramyeon here is spicy, and is even more delicious when eaten with either gimbap (Korean rolls) or tteok (broiled rice cakes). The smooth and sweet bbalgyetteok made with pepper flakes, egg and rice cakes is also popular. The cold ramen with crunchy young radish and ice is unique and delicious.

title: Jangsuwon
short_description: Jangsuwon serves excellent bulgogi (marinated thinly-sliced beef) and naengmyeon (noodles in chilled broth). The Pyeongyang-style noodles are rather thin, but are made with a high proportion of buckwheat flour. The broth is also very close to authentic Pyeongyang-style. The food is here is quite satisfactory for the price.

title: Anseong Ttosuni
short_description: Anseong Ttosuni specializes in saengtae tang (pollack soup). The great-tasting soup comes in a pot filled with tofu, green onions, water dropwort, and pollack boiled in a spicy broth. Other popular dishes here are their jeyuk bossam (Napa wraps with stir-fried pork) and samhap (fermented skate and steamed pork slices served with kimchi).

title: Ilsang
short_description: Ilsang is a hand-drip coffee shop where you can enjoy a cup of excellent cup of coffee while relaxing and reading one of the many domestic and foreign publications that take up one of the cafe's walls entirely. There are free lessons on hand-drip coffee given by the owner, who has a deep affection for coffee.

title: Hong Yuan
short_description: Hong Yuan is a Cantonese restaurant that recently opened within the Chosun Hotel. The steamed live lobster with black soybean sauce is recommended. They also offer traditional Chinese tea, and the interior design, with its red carpet and black pillars and tables, makes for a strong impression.

title: Halmeoni Kalguksu
short_description: Halmeoni Kalguksu is famous for kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) made using anchovy broth. They are also famous for their low prices. Uniquely, they add a little sujebi (hand-torn noodles) to their kalguksu. Also available is a dish called kaljebi,which is half kalguksu and half sujebi.

title: Urban Garden
short_description: At Urban Garden, you can enjoy homestyle Italian food. They are proud of their rooftop garden with various herbs and fragrant flowers. The rooftop garden is charming, perhaps even more so than the main restaurant, and has two themes, the "healing garden", taking your blues away with its natural fresh scent, and the "kitchen garden", planted with lettuce and chicory.

title: Myeongdong Gomdori
short_description: Myeongdong Gomdori serves an excellent guksu jeongol (noodle hot pot) made with thinly-sliced shabu shabu meat and crown daisy leaves in a thick anchovy broth. Their fried chicken is also worth trying.

title: Danggojip
short_description: Danggojip specializes in a kind of Koreanized Japanese rice cake skewer called tanggo. Round rice cakes are put on skewers and garnished with sweet red beans, green tea-flavored red beans, or strawberry-flavored red beans. They also offer Japanese-style curry and onigiri (Japanese rice balls).

title: Ju
short_description: Ju is a Chinese restaurant with a modern interior and is run by Chef Ju Deok-seong, one of founding members of Hogyeongjeon, a restaurant in the Westin Chosun Hotel. To properly bring out the best flavors of the ingredients, they cook over open flame. This is a small restaurant with one room and four tables.

title: Kkachine
short_description: Kkachine is famous for their dakbokkeumtang (braised chicken with potatoes). Because this dish takes a while to prepare, gyeranbeombeok, another one of this restaurant's delicacies, is a great starter. This dish is a kind of pancake made with sausages and eggs.

title: Inosisi
short_description: Inosisi, the Izakaya (Japanese-style pub), became famous in the Yeonnam-dong area for its fresh sashimi and low prices.  Recently, they have adopted an Omakase approach (the selection being left up to the chef, rather than chosen a la carte) and now also have a 'reservation only' policy. You are advised to book well in advance because of the very limited seating.

title: Dongbinggo
short_description: Dongbingo makes great-tasting traditional patbingsu using only milk, red beans and rice cake. Many find the rather chunky and sweet red bean sauce to be very addictive.

title: Eunjujeong
short_description: Eunjujeong offers only two dishes: samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) and kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew). You get a nice big helping of kimchi to have with your grilled pork. The vegetable side dishes are nice, and the kimchi is nicely made.

title: Sultan Kebab
short_description: An authentic Turkish-owned eatery, offering a choice of chicken or lamb kebabs. You can eat in or take out.

title: Jidaebang
short_description: Jidaebang is a traditional tea shop in Insadong where you can chat over tea. There are more than 60 types of traditional teas to choose from, and they use only hand-harvested or naturally grown teas, so you're guaranteed to get a fresh cup of traditional tea. When you order tea, you'll be served a thermos with hot water in a tea set, and the owner will guide you through the process. The interior has a natural feel, and 40 years of tradition is evident. It is a quiet refuge in the bustling streets of Insadong, and is loved by locals and foreigners alike, young and old alike.

title: Poom Seoul
short_description: This is a Korean cuisine restaurant that specializes in food from the Joseon Dynasty. Poom has modified the cuisine of the Joseon upper-class to satisfy modern palates. Because it uses fresh seasonal ingredients and natural seasonings, the menu changeswith the season. The grilled sirloin steak is a popular dish, and reservations are required.

title: Hangang Chicken
short_description: Hangang Chicken is a fried chicken restaurant that serves chicken in a delicious fried batter coating. Its the kind of place you'd find in your own neighborhood back home, so it's very comforting to have a beer here with a plate of hot fresh fried chicken.This restaurant is very popular so expect it to be busy when you go.

title: Primo Bacio Baci
short_description: Primo Bacio Baci is the best-known pasta restaurant in front of Hongik University. You always have to wait in line for about an hour to be seated. They do not take reservations. Prices are quite low.

title: Star Chef
short_description: Star Chef makes delicious fusion-style Chinese cuisine. As there are only twelve tables, reservations are highly recommended, especially at dinner time. Popular dishes include their sweet and sour beef and sirloin steak salad made with premium beef.

title: Deogwon Kkorigomtang Bangchitang
short_description: Deogwon Kkorigomtang Bangchitang is famous for soups made with special cuts of beef, such as kkorigomtang (oxtail soup) and bangchitang (hip bone soup) The portions of meat are quite generous, and it's nice to just pick it up and eat it right off thebone.

title: Singyechi
short_description: Singyechi is a Ramyeon (ramen) noodle restaurant that has been in operation for 25 years. They serve Korean instant ramen, not the Japanese variety. Their patented "shin-gye-chi" Ramyeon (spicy ramen with eggs and cheese) is very popular.

title: Square Garden
short_description: Square Garden is a famous hand-drip coffee shop in Seorae Maeul. Their home-style burgers and quesadillas also taste excellent. This is a very small place with only four tables, but it is charmingly decorated, so it is the hideaway of choice for manypeople.

title: Bella Praha
short_description: Bella Praha has become famous for hand-drip coffee and trdlo, a kind of Czech pastry. One nice feature is that you can choose the brewing method for your coffee: espresso, hand drip, cotton-flannel drip, syphon, or Dutch style. To make trdlo, dough iswound around an iron bar and baked. The interior is charmingly decorated with eye-catching accessories imported from the Czech Republic.

title: Jangsu Sikdang
short_description: Jangsu Sikdang is famous for their kimchi samgyeopsal, pork belly that is grilled together with kimchi on a thin cast-iron pan and stir-fried with sesame leaves and spicy seasoning. After the meat course, you can have rice that is stir-fried on the same pan, which tastes excellent.

title: Paolo de Maria
short_description: Paolo de Maria is the first restaurant opened by Paolo de Maria, the former executive chef of the Italian restaurant Bona Sera. They style themselves as a 'fine-dining trattoria'. The dishes show the chef's attention to detail, and the desserts are quite pleasing. The atmosphere is modern, with an indoor terrace.

title: Yeojaman
short_description: Yeojaman is run by a female film director, Ms. Mirye Lee. The name of the restaurant, "Yeojaman (Yeoja Bay)", comes from the name of a geographical location between Goheung and Yeosu. The restaurant expertly specializes in the cuisine of Jeollanam-do,the southern province of the region of Jeolla. The kkomak (ark shell) set menu is very popular.

title: Bruce Lee
short_description: This dim sum and noodle restaurant was opened by the owners of Mao, a restaurant specializing in Peking duck. The prices here are quite reasonable.

title: Busan Galbi
short_description: For 40 years, Busan Galbi has been serving galbi. They have a good reputation in their area. After enjoying a meal of galbi, it's nice to have naengmyun (buckwheat noodles either served in a chilled broth or mixed with spicy sauce). They also offer beoseot saeng-bulgogi (fresh, thinly sliced beef and mushrooms), galbi-tang (beef rib soup), and naengmyun set, which are quite popular with office workers in the neighbourhood.

title: MK2
short_description: Enjoy coffee at MK2 while perusing the accessories that decorate its interior. These accessories are also available for purchase. The surrounding area is very quiet, making this a good place to enjoy a peaceful moment.

title: Pancake Original Story
short_description: Pancake Original Story is a brunch cafe where you can enjoy brunch items, such as pancakes and toast. The most popular choice on the menu is their light, fluffy pancakes, but they also offer a wide variety of other items, such as omelettes and pancakes sets.

title: Manjok Ohyang Jokbal
short_description: Manjok Ohyang Jokbal serves ohyang jokbal ("five spice" pigs trotters), and it has a loyal following of ardent fans. Their jokbal is so popular because they use five different spices that reduces the intense smell of the meat. They provide manduguk (dumplingsoup) with your meal. They open at 4 p.m, but if you want to have jokbal for dinner, its recommended that you arrive early as they usually run out quickly. Their sign reads "Jokbal Mandu", so be careful not to miss it.

title: Samgakjeong
short_description: Samgakjeong is famous for samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly). Because you can enjoy good-quality samgyeopsal and the atmosphere is folksy and comfortable, this place is very popular. They are also famous for mosori-sal, a part of the jowl or cheek. People often visit this restaurant for the crispy grilled pork rinds.

title: Jaembaeok
short_description: Jaembaeok, which has been run for three generations, specializes in Seolleongtang (ox bone soup). Another popular item on their menu is the assortment of steamed beef, with cuts such as head meat, brisket point cut, brisket, and flank, Swiss-cut tongue, shank, and spleen.

title: Leonidas
short_description: Leonidas is a chocolate cafe opened by Leonidas, a famous Belgian chocolate company. Enjoy luxurious chocolates made from real cocoa butter. Beverages here are inexpensive.

title: Le Brunchic
short_description: Le Brunchic is a French restaurant where you can enjoy brunch. The food is high quality, and the atmosphere is comfortable.

title: Sogong Jukjip
short_description: At this famous Bukchang-area rice porridge house, you can choose from over ten different varieties of rice porridge, all of which are great. Another popular dish here is their nutritious rice cooked in a cauldron with oysters and prawns.

title: Mongjungheon
short_description: Mongjungheon offers Cantonese cuisine, Hong Kong-style dim sum, and congee (rice porridge). You can even watch dim sum being prepared in the kitchen located near the entrance. The restaurant has a classy atmosphere, and service is good. Prices are on the high side.

title: Jeongdong Guksi
short_description: This Jeong-dong area restaurant is quite famous for their light-tasting kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings). They prepare sagol (four legs) broth (made using the four leg bones of a cow), but the real delicacies at this restaurant are the white kimchi and red kimchi they offer as side dishes. They use napa cabbage that is grown in cold climates, and the seasonings are not strong, so it is a perfect match with the noodles. Their gookbap (rice in beef broth) and bossam (steamed pork with napa cabbage wraps) are also very good.

title: Namu Sairo
short_description: Namu Sairo is a peaceful place to have a cup of coffee in the Gwanghwamun area. In the summer, it's nice to have your coffee on the terrace. They offer hand-drip coffee in addition to other kinds of coffee.

title: Banjjakbanjjak Binnaneun
short_description: This is a fusion teahouse that combines modernity and tradition. Especially popular here are the slow brewed organic teas and traditional Korean drinks such as sweet rice drink (sikhye) and cinnamon punch (sujeonggwa). Visitors can also see on displaytraditional arts and crafts.

title: Om
short_description: Om is a Nepalese and Indian restaurant run by the manager of the Nepal Tourism Board. You can have a variety of curries and tandoori chicken, which is marinated in traditional spices for one day and baked in a tandoori oven. The smells and flavors of the dishes here are typical of Indian cuisine, although not as strong.

title: Yeongdong Jokbal
short_description: Yeongdong Jokbal has been serving up Jokbal (pigs' feet) for over 30 years. Along with Nolbu Mandu and Seongsu Jokbal, Yeongdong Jokbal is considered one of the three best Jokbal restaurants in Seoul. The meat is tender, thick, and slightly salty for that perfect Jokbal flavor.

title: The Kings
short_description: At The Kings buffet restaurant, the food is cooked in front of you, and they offer a selection of over 150 dishes including dim sum, Peking roast duck, and barbecued dishes freshly made to order. All of the seafood they use, including the lobster, is notably fresh.

title: Ayajin Saengtae Jjigae
short_description: Ayajin Saengtae Jjigae is famous for saengtae jjigae (fresh pollack stew), which they make with a generous portion of hard roe. They thoroughly boil the whole fresh pollack in a tin pot. The soup is spicy and flavorful, so saengtae jjigae on its own can make a satisfying meal.

title: Heungjinok
short_description: For over 40 years, Heungjinok has been offering traditional Gyeongsang-do-style haejang-guk (hangover soup). The soup is loaded with beef omasum, intestines, and coagulated ox-blood. There is also plenty of a lot of napa cabbage, dried napa cabbage, andmung-bean sprouts, and they prepare the broth made with beef bones, so the soup is rich but refreshing. Although not particularly clean-tasting, the soup is very rich and flavorful.

title: Chuncheon Son Kalguksu
short_description: At Chuncheon Son Kalguksu, which has been in business for 30 years, the big hit in the summer is makguksu (thick buckwheat noodles in chilled broth with hot sauce) is popular, and in the winter, it's their kalguksu (handmade knife-cut noodle soup). The kalguksu is topped with chicken and ground peanuts. They make their own chicken broth and their own noodles. The interior is decorated with artwork by the owner, who used to be an artist.

title: SamhakdoA
short_description: Enjoy Samhakdo-style cuisine from Mokpo, Jeolla-do. They use fresh ingredients delivered daily from Mokpo. Their specialties are kingfish, octopus, and skate, and the skate samhap (a combination of three ingredients: aged skate, boiled pork, and fermented kimchi) is recommended.

title: Suchiku
short_description: Suchiku opened recently, following the renovation of 63 Building. You can have sushi and sashimi prepared with very fresh ingredients. The view from the sushi counter on the 58th floor is said to be the best in Seoul.

title: Donggyeong Jeontong Yukgaejang
short_description: This Gangnam-area restaurant is famous for yukgaejang (spicy beef soup). They make their yukgaejang with less gosari (bracken fern) than other restaurants do, but it tastes very refreshing and is very popular. Their side dishes are also neatly presented and nicely accentuate the flavor of their yukgaejang.

title: Pohang Sikdang
short_description: Pohang sikdang specializes in gwamegi (winter-dried Pacific saury) delivered from Pohang. This gwamegi does not have the usual fishy smell, so it can be enjoyed even by those trying it for the first time. They also offer giant octopus and agu suyuk (boiledtender slices of puffer fish).

title: The NiNth Gate Grille
short_description: This restaurant was the first in Korea to specialize in French cuisine. They have an atmosphere of a casual brasserie. With a sporty, casual interior, their menu now offers more selection at a wider range of prices, so you can enjoy dining here without concern for the cost. They offer Korean beef steak, and from the menu, you can choose which cut you want and the amount, making ordering very convenient.

title: Donggyeong Sikdang
short_description: Donggyeong Sikdang offers home-style Japanese dishes prepared in modern Japanese style. You can have neatly-presented Japanese dishes in a modern Japanese-style atmosphere. They are famous for their home-style oden (fish cakes). This is a good place to enjoy sake at dinner time. The prices are somewhat high.

title: Andong Mungtigwa
short_description: At Andong Mungtigi, you can enjoy excellent yuk-sashimi (fresh beef sliced like sashimi and served raw and unmarinated) made with Korean beef from Andong. It is a specialty restaurant serving Mungtigi yukhoe, where meat slaughtered on the same day is sliced ​​into large chunks and dipped in a fantastic sauce.

title: Oworui Jong
short_description: This bakery is known for its leavened breads. May Bell supplies bread to many of the restaurants in the area. Prices are reasonable and portions generous.

title: Dakgomtang
short_description: Dakgomtang is a well-established restaurant that serves dakgomtang (chicken soup), and their dakgomtang is so popular with their patrons because of the clear broth. They have been in operation for nearly 50 years.

title: Buwonmyeonok
short_description: Buwonmyeonok specializes in Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles served either in a tangy broth). They have been operating in Namdaemun Market for around 50 years. This restaurant is especially popular with customers from North Korea. Two popular dishes on the menu are dakmuchim (shredded boiled chicken served with salt and pepper) and bindaetteok (Korean-style pancake made of ground mung beans, green onions, and kimchi)

title: Yangcholli
short_description: Yangcholli is famous for chargrilled samgyeopsal (pork belly) and has a neat atmosphere. At dinner time, fresh samgyeopsal cooked on a charcoal brazier is recommended, and at lunch time, the kimchi jeongol (kimchi hot pot) and sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) is recommended. A plus is you can cook the hot pot and stew over oak charcoal. The restaurant has an airy feeling because both the first and second floor are open to the outside and each has its own outdoor terrace.

title: Coffee Tour
short_description: Coffee Tour specializes in house-roasted hand-drip coffee. It is quite small, but their great-tasting coffee has garnered a loyal following. They also carry a wide range of coffee-making equipment that is available for purchase.

title: Daedong
short_description: Daedong is a Seoul branch of a famous Peking duck restaurant in Beijing. Enjoy authentic Peking duck prepared by Chinese chefs. The open kitchen gives the restaurant an airy feeling. Besides Peking duck, they offer a variety of other regional Beijing dishes.

title: Jungguk
short_description: Despite its small size, the restaurant China is very famous for delicious jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), jajangmyeon (stir-fried noodles with black soybean sauce), and tangsuyuk (sweet and sour beef or pork).

title: Sanchon
short_description: The owner of Sanchon, a former monk who learned to cook while living in a temple, prepares authentic temple food which is rustic and neatly presented. Your table is filled with a wide variety of side dishes. Their dishes are prepared without meat from seasonal vegetables and mountain herbs, so it is suitable for those with a vegetarian diet.

title: Buheung Dongtae
short_description: For many years, this Yeoido-area restaurant has been serving dongtaetang (frozen pollack stew). It is very popular with people who work in the area, so be prepared to stand in line if you visit around lunchtime. The soup is prepared with a generous portion of ingredients and seasonings, so it is spicy and rich but also light tasting.

title: Patisserie Kim Youngmo
short_description: It is a store run by CEO Kim Young-mo, a Korean confectionery master, and is a few private bakeries that have been consistently loved for more than 30 years. In particular, Mont Blanc, which is eaten round and round along the grain, melts in the mouth.

title: Trattoria Moro
short_description: Trattoria Moro is a casual Italian restaurant where you can enjoy Italian cuisine and wines. Their pasta is excellent, and a wide variety of main dishes are also available. It's a good place to enjoy wine as they are open until the early morning.

title: Insadong Sujebi
short_description: Sujebi is hand-pulled noodles boiled in broth. Served in an earthenware bowl, the sujebi here is particularly delicious. Spicy sujebi with oysters and haemul pajeon (seafood and green onion pancake) are this restaurant’s specialties. Patrons can experience a very traditional Korean atmosphere at Insadong Sujebi.

title: Soonhee's Bindaetteok
short_description: Mung beans are freshly ground into paste with authentic millstones.  Savory bindaetteok is made with the freshly made mung bean paste.  Mung bean bindaetteok and meat pancakes are the only 2 items on the menu.  You can eat hot made bindaetteokat one of the tables or take it to go.  Enjoy with a drink of makgeolli.

title: Mother and Daughter's Gimbap
short_description:
One of the main reasons why everyone should go to Gwangjang Market is for the original "addictive gimbap." It's "addictive" attribute comes from it being so delicious and snackable thanks to its miniature size. People just keep going back for more. 

Though most other stores here claim that they are the original, Mother and Daughter's Gimbap is the real original with over 40 years of history.

title: La Lune Violette
short_description: La Lune Violette is a bistro-style French restaurant with quality foods at an affordable price.  Escargot, Ballotine (French stuffed chicken) and their signature Miso pasta are a few of their specialty dishes.  Immerse yourself in gourmet French cuisine and wine.

title: Wonjo Halmeoni Tteokbokki
short_description: This food stall has been run by Kim Lim Ok for over 30 years. Unlike the tteokbokki that's found everywhere else Korea, the rice cakes are lightly fried in oil in the lid of a large iron pot. The crispy, yet savory rice cake cannot be found anywhere else.  Though many nearby stores immitate the original, nothing comes close to it.

title: Mansuui Jeongwon
short_description: At Mansuui Jeongwon, you can enjoy traditional Korean dishes, such as bibimbap (rice mixed with vegetables, hot sauce, and other ingredients) and tteokgalbi (chargrilled beef and pork patties). You can have a light meal, but it's also a nice place for dinner and drinks.

title: Chai Lyn
short_description: Chai Lyn offers neatly-presented dishes in the stylish atmosphere. It is one of the more up-scale restaurants in the area. Many options are available à la carte, but their course set menus are more popular.

title: Eonnyang Bulgogi
short_description: Eonnyang Bulgogi has been in operation for 30 years. Their menu features only two items: deungsim (sirloin) and Eonnyang-style bulgogi (thinly sliced beef seasoned in sesame seeds oil, perilla seeds oil, and pine nuts). As soon as an order is placed, Korean sirloin is seasoned, grilled in a rectangular grilling basket, and served with perilla and sesame seeds oil for dipping.

title: Unknown Diner
short_description: Unknown Diner is an intimate Italian restaurant in a quiet neighborhood. You can enjoy a casual meal of pasta or pizza. Their lunch set menus are very popular, and this is also great place to enjoy a glass of wine with pasta at dinnertime.

title: Gold Fish
short_description: Gold fish is a dim-sum restaurant that was recently opened by a chef who used to live in China and Hong Kong. Enjoy quality dim sum that are packed with fillings. Other items on the menu are also good, like their stir-fried rice and noodle dishes.

title: Mongmyeok Sanbang
short_description: At Mongmyeon Sanbang, you can enjoy neatly-presented Korean dishes in a traditional Korean house. They offer only a few dishes such as bibimbap (rice mixed with vegetables, hot sauce, and other ingredients), buchu jeon (Korean leek pancakes), dotori muk(acorn jelly), and traditional teas which they make themselves.

title: Gusto Taco
short_description: At Gusto Taco, you can enjoy warm tacos made by a graduate of a New York cooking school. The dishes are not complicated, but you should be prepared to wait as they make everything to order. It is quite a small place, so customers tend to order their food to go.

title: Kongji POTji
short_description: The building of Kongji POTji, a casual Italian restaurant boasting the best sky view in Bukchon Hanok Village, is also well known as an architectural structure that embodies modern aesthetics within the old urban landscape of Seoul, where the artistic perspectives of the past and present, and of the East and West, coexist. It offers visitors delicious food along with an excellent cultural experience.

title: July
short_description: This is a cozy, yet elegant French restaurant that uses fresh Korean ingredients and serves only the best dishes made with quality ingredients like snail, sea bream and premium beef tenderloin.

title: Seongsan Wanggalbi
short_description: Seongsan Wanggalbi is famous for saeng dwaeji galbi (fresh pork short ribs). The restaurant is popular because their dwaeji galbi tastes very good and the portions are generous. The gyeranjjim (steamed scrambled eggs with chopped vegetables) and doenjangjjigae (soybean paste stew) that accompany the galbi are also excellent.

title: Hannam Bugeotguk
short_description: Hannam Bugeotguk is a good place to go for a drink as they offer a wide variety of side dishes, including bugeotguk (dried pollack soup). Their many varieties of jeon (Korean savory pancakes) and suyuk (steamed pork hocks) are very popular, and ojingeo muchim (squid salad) is also good.

title: Saffron
short_description: Saffron is a Middle Eastern restaurant. Many of the dishes here bear some similarity to Indian dishes, but they only use meat prepared according to Sharia Islamic law. The preparation of halal meat involves draining all of the blood, so the meat does not have its usual characteristic smell and tastes great.

title: Mouse Rabbit
short_description:
European café Mouse Rabbit, featuring a beautiful terrace, is a café run by Super Junior’s Yesung and his brother. The store, featuring 3 floors with different atmosphere and charm, provides the fun of selecting different floors and tables according to individual taste. The basement floor, called "rabbit hole" and "underworld," has tables and fireplaces, providing a comfortable place to relax and hangout. The first floor features the ordering counter and the outer terrace, and the second floor is decked out with decorations and other stores. There are various products available such as toys, cell phone cases, mugs, and eco bags, which are designed and produced by hand by Mouse Rabbit and are popular with its fans.
Mouse Rabbit was named after the animals mouse and rabbit representing Yesung and his brother running the café. The showcase within the store is full of Yesung’s pictures, and because visitors can purchase art products created by Mouse Rabbit, fans are unceasingly visiting the café.

title: Making a Better Place
short_description:
Live café run by the father of EXO’s Chanyel. Making a Better Place provides various music and liver performances from the K-POP that the teenagers like and old pop songs of the middle-aged people. On the weekday evenings, live performances are provided, and band performances are provided on Saturdays. You can enjoy the music of talented artists, and the foods including handmade burgers, fried chicken, beer and drinks. The place can be rented for bands and club activities.


This is the live café run by EXO Chanyeol’s father, with Chanyeol’s instruments displayed. Here you can discover the source of Chanyeol’s talent and communicate with him. Numerous EXO fans are attracted to the store. You can enjoy the Korean, Chinese and Japanese songs sung by talented artists, and the café is loved for the various performances and as the event hall of Crayon Pop and other singers’ fan meeting.

title: Modern Nülang
short_description: In the 1930s, Shanghai was considered the Paris of the East and Shanghainese women of that era were bright and fashionable. Modern Nülang's concept is a nod to that era and to the modern women of that time. The restaurant's name itself means modern woman. "Modern" speaks for itself and "Nülang" is the Korean transliteration for the Chinese word for woman. Modern Nülang offers a fresh interpretation of Chinese classics in a romantic and stylish setting.

title: Eid
short_description: Located near a mosque, Eid is one of the few restaurants to be recognized as a Halal restaurant by the Korea Muslim Federation. The three side dishes and soup offered with meals are made fresh everyday with organic ingredients and no additives, giving the food at Eid a refreshing taste.

title: Sudam
short_description: Sudam specializes in high-end han-jeongsik (Korean table d'hote) and the head chef has over 26 years of experience in the kitchen. Only fresh ingredients are used to create the meals at Sudam and the dishes are as nutritious as they are tasty. Sudam is also well-suited to hold large parties of diners, whether for celebrations or business dinners.

title: Texas de Brazil
short_description: Texas de Brazil is a restaurant that mixes American-sized generous portions with the best of Brazil’s churrascaria culture. Texas de Brazil prides itself on using only the highest quality ingredients and employing expert chefs and carvers. As a result, there is probably no other place in Seoul where diners can experience an authentic churrasco. There are 15 different cutsof meats available and a salad bar stocked with seasonal offerings. Cuts of meat are grilled directly over open flames on the churrasco grill. No MSG is used, only natural herbs and spices flavor the food at Texas de Brazil. This Western-style restaurant is luxuriously styled and offers premium service. The house carver carves the meat at each table, and service touches like that just to add to the dining experience at Texas de Brazil. Dine at Korea’s first churrascaria fora culinary experience you won't soon forget.

title: God Eat
short_description: The atmosphere at God Eat is so relaxing that a meal at this restaurant feels like a mini-vacation. God Eat offers healthy fusion cuisine that combines the best of Korean and Western flavors. The food at God Eat is made with mild, fresh ingredients and the food is as healthy as it is tasty. Service is fast, so diners don’t have to wait long between ordering and receiving their meals. Everything on the menu is also available for take-out, so stop by when the weather is nice, get a meal to go, and have a fun picnic lunch or dinner.

title: Gireum Tteokbokki at Tongin Market
short_description: Tongin Market is the place to go for traditional gireum tteok-bokki. The market is well-known as the best place in Korea for gireum tteok-bokki, and even foreign tourists come to have a taste. Gireum tteok-bokki is made by stir-frying rice cakes in oil and seasonings. There are two types of gireum tteok-bokki sold here. One kind is seasoned with just oil and soy sauce; the other is seasoned with spicy red pepper flakes and oil. Three of Tongshin Market’s gireum tteok-bokki eateries are particularly famous and popular. One such eatery is Original Grandmother's Gireum Tteok-Bokki. The shop has been featured on TV programs. Another is Hyoja-dong’s Old School Tteok-Bokki, once visited by John Kerry in 2014 while he was the U.S. Secretary of State.

title: Hyoja Bakery
short_description: If you go around the Blue House and down the alley, you will find a bakery located next to Tongin Market. Hyoja Bakery has been in business for 35 years, since 1987, and its signboard is old-fashioned and nostalgic. It is the first bakery in Seochon that has been viralized through broadcasting and media for a long time, and has a wide range of options, including sweets, donuts, croquettes, and other traditional bakery items, as well as fermented bread and bagels that are popular these days. The shop is so famous and popular that many items are sold out on weekends.

title: Seochon Traditional Sundae Soup House
short_description: Seochon Traditional Sundae Soup House is considered a must-visit destination. It was shown in the Korean drama series, “Doctors, as a restaurant owned by the father of the main character, Yoo Hye Jung (actress: Park Shin Hye). It is known for its special deep-tasting beef broth, which they brew with marrowbone for 24 hours. Its old-fashioned, traditional style Hanok architecture and its neat interior evokes the Korean traditional castle: Gyeongbokgung and its surroundings. Not only is the Sundae Soup first in its class, the in-house Kimchi is one of the best in its category as well. After the meal, don’t forget to take a photo where the “Doctors” couple, Jiho-Hyejung, enjoyed rice soup.

title: BHC Sadang Branch
short_description: BHC Sadang Branch is a chain restaurant. It specializes in making fried chicken. The restaurant is very spacious with two floors; one underground floor and one ground floor. The restaurant’s recent hit is a spicy chicken feature in the menu called, “Mapster,” and another being, “Curry Chicken,” in which curry is applied to fried chicken. Another popular feature in the menu is called, “Sunflower Fried Chicken,” which is fried with Sunflower Oil instead of regular oil making the chicken more nutty.

title: Anthracite Coffee Roasters (Hapjeong Branch)
short_description: Anthracite Coffee Roasters is a well-known cafe in Hapjeong-dong that brings new meaning to the term industrial chic. Anthracite's building was once a shoe factory and the cafe has maintained many of the factory's industrial elements and added modern decor. Beer and coffee are among the menu selections offered at Anthracite and one of the most popular coffees is the Butter Fat Trio. The coffee roasts are named after famed authors, so visitors can order a "Natsume Sōseki" or a "Pablo Neruda." Anthracite's pastry chef bakes the cafe's desserts on the premises. Patrons can choose from cakes, financiers, madeleines, and cookies.

title: Onion
short_description: The epitome of industrial chic, Cafe Onion operates out of a converted factory that was built in the 1970s. The building has actually seen a variety of businesses open shop in the past; there was once a supermarket and even restaurants throughout the years and at one time the building was even a regular residence. More recently, before Cafe Onion opened, the building housed an industrial factory that made small parts. Traces of the building's industrial past are still visible throughout Cafe Onion. The cafe even kept and converted many of the factory's design elements. There are over 20 varieties of bread at the cafe. Cafe Onion also sells the famed Bread 05 Bakery's butter bread. Korean patrons will have seen the butter bread on several Korean TV shows.

title: Pro Soy Crab (Main Branch)
short_description: Pro Soy Crab first opened in 1980 and it is considered by many to be Korea's foremost ganjang-gejang (soy sauce marinated crab) restaurant. Pro Soy Crab's main branch is located at Sinsa-dong but there is another location in Samseong-dong, Seoul. Pro Soy Crab uses only the freshest high-quality ingredients to create their crab and seafood dishes. Diners can enjoy a range of seafood such as ganjang-gejang (soy sauce marinated crab), yangnyeom-gejang (spicy marinated crab), kkotge jjim (braised blue crab), and sannakji (sliced raw octopus). In a fun design touch, the walls of the restaurant interior are decorated with photos and autographs of famous Korean baseball players and Hallyu stars.

title: Solbin Superdog
short_description: Loved by fans from all over Asia, Super Junior has been an A-list K-pop star for almost a decade now. A lesser known fact about the group is that the charming and witty member Kim Hee-chul has refined interest in food. One of the restaurants in Seoul that he has recommended is Solbin Superdog located in the Apgujeong Rodeo Street. On the menu are tacos, hot dogs and rice bowls. The foodie K-pop singer’s favorite menu item is the spicy dog, which is extremely hot yet highly addictive. The signature dish is the galbi (grilled beef ribs) rice, which comes with nachos, sour cream, jalapeño peppers and vegetables.

title: Oriental Roast Chicken
short_description: The exterior of the restaurant may seem rather humble, but Oriental Roast Chicken’s list of clientele is world class. The small eatery is filled with numerous autographs of K-stars including the two-time Olympic medallist Kim Yuna to Hallyu stars Ahn Sung-ki, Lee Jong-suk, Han Hyo-joo and Ahn Jae-wook. Roasted with glutinous rice, chestnuts and jujubes, the chhicken is juicy and tender, with distinctively nutty and sweet aromas. Take-outs are available as well.

title: Lamese Cadeau
short_description: Owned by the parents of Lee Hi, Lamese Cadeau specializes in Korean seafood dishes. The K-pop star’s favorite food on the menu is the ganjang-gejang (soy sauce-marinated crabs) made with fresh crabs sourced from the Incheon sea shore. The ganjang-gejang meal is served with several side dishes (banchan), featuring locally-sourced conch, abalone, and seaweed. Upon request, the dishes can be delivered directly from the restaurant. As for the interior, a large poster of Lee Hi hangs by the entrance while autographs of Lee’s fellow artists from YG Entertainment―such as Bobby and Lee Soo-hyun―decorate the walls.

title: Dep Trai
short_description: Have delicious, authentic Hanoi-style pho and Vietnamese food at Dep Trai (literally meaning, "good-looking man" in Vietnamese). Dep Trai offers a range of delicious Vietnamese food such as banh mi, pho, rice bowls, and more.

title: Gino's NY Pizza
short_description: Dok2 has opened up a pizza joint in the Apgujeong area offering authentic New York-style pizza with a buttery, crispy crust. The most popular item on the menu is Brooklyn's Best, featuring Italian sausage, hand-crushed plum tomatoes, mozzarella cheese, extra virgin olive oil, and red onions. Dok2’s favorite dish is known to be the earthy, aromatic Truffle Mushroom pizza. The pizza is certainly worth trying as it has turned Dok2 from a loyal patron into a restaurateur.

title: Harmonium
short_description: Located in Hannam-dong, the Italian restaurant Harmonium is a space named after the Latin word for “harmony.” Serving modern and sophisticated Italian cuisine, it features a terrace and private rooms, making it ideal for both dining and business gatherings. Experience a memorable meal in a sophisticated atmosphere.

title: Ibis Styles Ambassador Seoul Myeongdong (Le Style Restaurant & Bar)
short_description: Ibis Styles Ambassador Myeongdong’s Le Style Restaurant & Bar is a rooftop space that captures panoramic city views, sunsets, and nightscapes, offering the most vivid way to experience the charm of Seoul.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Samwon Garden
short_description:
Expression of the highest peaks of the abdomen​

This restaurant has served great ribs for the past 30 years. State dinners are often held here due to the beautiful traditional Korean house (hanok) exterior and private rooms available.

Samwon Garden is a veteran of the local restaurant scene, first opening its doors in 1976, quickly achieving fame as being not only Seoul’s largest restaurant, but a place serving quality and authentic traditional Korean cuisine.

title: ON River Station
short_description: A multi-recreational venue, On River is designed to provide quality service for food and beverages as well as banquets. Consisting of 3-storey complex, guests can enjoy an excellent dining experience thanks to top on-site chefs and a variety of quality menu options suitable for all ages in a stylish and comfortable atmosphere.

title: Naeja Peanuts
short_description: Naeja Peanuts was founded 50 years ago when the current CEO's father was 26 years old, and he learned the art of making peanut pancakes from a relative. When you enter Naeja Peanut, which has been baking hot pot for more than half a century, you can see the machine that makes peanut hot pot opposite the entrance. It's still the same as it was in the old days, except that it's been switched from briquettes to gas. The twice-roasted peanuts are embedded with large peanuts, making them savory. The peanut pancake, which is made only about 130 bags a day, is their signature item. The green onion and ginger pancakes are also popular.

title: Sonmat Gimbap
short_description: The current owner, who inherited 'Grandma Gimbap' from his mother in 1980, reopened it as 'Handmade Gimbap' and has been in Tongin Market for two generations. At her mother's request, she helped her mother sell gimbap every day since she had just entered university. Her second daughter suggested, "Since your mother has a good taste, let's call it 'Sonmat Gimbap' instead of 'Grandma's Gimbap,'" hence the current name. Tongin Market also operates a unique experience where you can purchase gimbap with Ipjeon, a currency unique to Tongin Market, and use the packed lunch cafe.

title: Eulji Dabang
short_description: Opened in 1985, Eulji Dabang is a charming cafe with a neo-noir feel. The owner runs the shop with the belief that he never plays with his food. The owner's friendly explanation of how to make the egg yolk-filled ssanghwa tea, which is served like a full moon, will quickly make you a fan. You can enjoy a unique experience in a place that has retained the appearance of an old-fashioned tea room among skyscrapers.

title: Hakrim Dabang
short_description:
A stalwart on Daehak-ro for more than 60 years since 1956, Hakrimdabang was a popular meeting place for university students who led the Hyehwa Station democracy movement, as well as a regular coffee shop for people in the arts, including music, art, theater, and literature. Today, it's the oldest cafe in Seoul, and the LP and paintings inside give it a nostalgic feel. Also the filming location for the drama "You from the Stars," Hakrimdabang is still loved by all generations.

 

• This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

title: Sushi Kaisin
short_description: Like the many eateries commonly found along Japan’s streets of Ginza, Sushi Kaisin is a cozy, little sushi restaurant. From procuring and preparing the ingredients to plating and serving up the delectable morsels, the Japanese chef does everything from beginning to end, ensuring the utmost quality in taste for his customers. The restaurant has a counter which seats only 6 people, making it crucial for visitors to make reservations in advance.

title: Duru
short_description: EXO member D.O. recommended this place to a magazine while other EXO members Xiumin and Sehun are regulars to this restaurant. The restaurant has received great reviews as seen in three blue ribbons in the Blue Ribbon Survey, a representative guidebook for Korean restaurants.  D.O. recommends nakji-bokkeum (stir-fried octopus) and jumeok-bap (riceballs), both popular dishes at Duru, with its clean and neat ambience. The harmony between the spicy yet clean flavored Nakji-bokkeum, savory Jumeok-bap that soothes the mouth, and flavorful homemade side dishes are amazing. The icing on the cake is the purple sweet potato makgeolli. This cheeky pink drink is a go-to-drink item for patrons since it boasts great harmony with the Nakji-bokkeum.

title: Nagwon Rice Cake
short_description:
Nagwon Rice Cake, with a 90-year tradition that has been passed down through three generations since the 1920s, is the home of Korean rice cakes. It is a certified restaurant that has been introduced through various TV media and still makes rice cakes by hand to maintain the unique flavor of Korean traditional food. The representative Duteop tteok is famous for its luxurious flavor. The restaurant is also designated as a Seoul Cultural Heritage Site, as it makes rice cakes using techniques inherited from a court lady of Wonseo-dong.

 

• This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

title: Biwon Tteokjip
short_description:
In 1949, Biwon Tteokjip, known as "Grandma Hong's Tteokjip," first opened its doors. It all started when Grandma Hong Gannan's rice cakes, which she served at Changdeokgung Palace's Nakseonjae, caught the eye of Han Hee-soon Sanggung, the last court caterer of the Joseon Dynasty, who personally taught her the secrets of court rice cakes during the chaotic period after the liberation of Korea and before the Korean War. The shop, which used to make and sell rice cakes in a house near Changdeokgung Palace, still uses the same recipe for royal rice cakes that was presented to the king, and the entire process, from selecting the finest ingredients to making the rice cakes, is done 100% by hand.

 

• This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

title: Soonhee Food
short_description: The owner started selling side dishes at his own stall after his brother's business failed. She sold delicious side dishes such as kimchi and crab paste at the stall, which went viral, and opened the first side dish shop in Gwangjang Market. She named the shop 'Soonhee's Banchan' after her eldest daughter. Nowadays, everyone uses the name 'Soonhee', but the original 'Soonhee' in Gwangjang Market is Soonhee's Banchan, which is the pride of the owner. Regular customers say that this place is like a second home.

title: Taegeukdang
short_description: Since 1946, this bakery has been a favorite among generations of Seoulites. The founder, who dreamed of national liberation, created the Mugunghwa logo and the name Taegukdang to capture the ideals of the nation. The long-established bakery has continued to build on its reputation by developing numerous types of bread. In keeping with the spirit of the founder, who did not want to become a franchise, they take care to ensure that the flavors do not change. This is a place where you can find bread that appeals to both children and grandmothers.

title: Haha & Kim Jong-guk’s 401 Restaurant
short_description: Haha & Kim Jong-guk’s 401 bbq restaurant is located in Hongdae. Since the restaurant is already famous as a great place to dine in Hongdae, the entrance is full of people waiting in line. Looking at the numerous photos of celebrities and the two owners is one of the joys of coming to the restaurant. Its signature dish is a set where all different cuts including ohgyupsal, moksal, and hangjeongsal are served, and the order can be placed by the number of people in a group. Juicy meat is very tasty when dipped in the fermented anchovy and home-made sauce provided upon ordering. Chadol soybean soup will also be the perfect addition for a soft texture and spicy finish.

title: Daehan Gopchang (Jangan Branch)
short_description:
Hwasa, a member of a powerful girl group Mamamoo, ate at this place on a reality show "I Live Alone", and a gopchang (grilled intestines) craze was caused in Korea. The name of the place is Daehan Gopchang in Jangan near Janghanpyeong Station. After the show was aired, so many people came over that the restaurant now closes early everyday as they sell out their food. 
Gopchang gets more savory as you chew it, and makchang has a very attractive chewy texture, and Daechang is very soft. The all-in-one set where you can taste all three is what the restaurant recommends. Enjoy their homemade sauce, onions, cheese, and curry seasoning to your taste. No meal will be more perfect than when you wrap up your meal with fried rice, just like Hwasa did.

title: Samgeori Pujutgan Central City
short_description: Samgeori Pujutgan, operated by YG Entertainment, recently moved from Hongik University to a bigger location in Central City. Big Bang’s Seungri, Sandara Park, and other entertainers at YG, including Lee Seung Gi, Lee Seo Jin and other popular entertainers have also visited the place. Winner and other artists from YG often have parties here. It is also fun to look at celebrity photographs and signatures hanging on the wall. Though the location has moved, it still tastes the same. The signature pork ribs boast thickness and not overpowering sweetness, making it popular. Pyongyang noodles, made with buckwheat noodles and Korean beef broth, and Korean beef with soybean rice are also delicious.

title: Neungra Bapsang
short_description: Neungra Bapsang is a North Korean restaurant run by a North Korean owner. He opened his restaurant in hopes of letting people know more about North Korean food and dishes like Pyongyang Onban and Gaeseong Mujjim.

title: Cafe Armoire
short_description: Yesung from Super Junior opened Cafe Armoire following Mouse Rabbit. Though it just opened in August, it has already become famous. Once you step in to the cafe, a room with antique furniture and ornaments appear, so be prepared. Once you open the door of the furniture, that is how you get to the actual cafe. Rustic light, tables, and organ create an elegant and retro ambience, as if you came visiting a world from the Chronicles of Narnia. Their signature dishes are cutely-shaped cheesecake and the 24 hour milk tea that features boiled and matured milk with various types of earl grey.

title: Cafe Mujabee
short_description: This cafe, operated by Block B’s B-bomb, is located near Sookmyung Women’s University Station on line 4. The simple single story building has a very calm and clean interior. B Bomb frequently comes when he isn’t busy, which is why you can easily see his signatures or fan selfies on social networking services. The signature item is the bitter and sweet mujabi, meaning "merciless,"" latte, made of espresso, chocolate, and steamed milk. Aside from drinks, cakes, including carrot cake, are prepared and phone cases with printed cafe names and t-shirts are sold as souvenirs.

title: RoyaD
short_description: RoyaD is a homemade dessert shop which uses traditional Korean ingredients to make fusion desserts. Their mini tteok cake and seolgi madeleine are their most popular menu and their tteok sandwiches are well received as a quick breakfast meal among busy businessmen.

title: Jeongaematdam
short_description: Located in Namsung Market, Jeongaematdam is a fusion rice cake store that sells traditional rice cakes with a modern twist. Their most popular snacks are injeolmi (rice cake) with grain coating and angbeotteok, red bean and butter rice cake. A variety of freshly made traditional rice cakes are also available every day, giving visitors plenty of options to choose from.

title: Siroo Cake
short_description: Siroo Cake is a dessert cafe located in Sangsu-dong. They're known for using only Korean rice, milk, and whipped cream in their rice cake menu. Visitors looking for a modern and unique Korean dessert are highly recommended to visit this place. On top of selling delicious rice cakes, they also offer various cooking classes here.

title: Yebindang
short_description: Yebindang is a traditional Korean dessert cafe locatd in Seongsu-dong. They're well known for their Duteoptteok (Steamed Rice Cake with Red Bean and Nuts), Kkot Songpyeon (Flower-shaped Rice Cake), and Seolgi (Snow White Rice Cake).

title: Gyeonggi Tteokjip
short_description: Since 1958, the history of the shop, which started at Heungin Mill in Jongno, has been continued by moving to Mangwon-dong. Gyeonggi Tteokjip's founder, whose sons inherited his father's rice cake-making skills, is the second generation to run the business, and one of his sons holds the title of the youngest rice cake master. Their signature product is 'Ittitteok', a North Korean-style injeolmi with a unique shape of a rice cake wrapped around an egg. With the goal of preserving and carrying on the tradition, they have been researching rice cakes as a healthy dessert that modern people can enjoy lightly.

title: Koggiri
short_description: This is one of the famous restaurants in Gongdeok-dong's instant tteokbokki street and has been operating for three generations. It has been featured in the Korean restaurant guidebook Blue Ribbon Survey for two consecutive years in 2017 and 2018 because of its delicious taste. After you finish eating the instant tteokbokki, it is a specialty to fry rice with the seasoning. Both the tteokbokki and tempura have long maintained affordable prices.

title: Pimatgol
short_description: Pimatgol is a food alleyway that extends from Jongno 1-ga to Jongno 6-ga. During the Joseon Dynasty, when commoners walked along the main road and encountered an aristocrat, they had to bow down before them regardless of the circumstances. Finding this bothersome, more and more commoners chose to walk along the alleyways next to the main road. These alleyways would lead and connect to pubs, liquor shops, and gukbap (Rice Soup) stores, becoming a beloved place among commoners, and was aptly named “Pimatgol” a shortened form of “alleyway to avoid the horses”.

title: Dok-Dabang
short_description:
Doksuridabang was a dormitory for nearby university students in the 1970s and 80s, a meeting place and a place for public discussion. It originally started as a music room and was loved by literary figures such as novelist Seong Seokje and poet Ki Hyung-do. It was closed in 2005 due to the popularity of coffee shops, but reopened in 2013 by the owner, who is the grandson of the original founder, who promised to continue the history and identity of the place. There is a bulletin board where people used to exchange notes and share news, as well as old photos of the history of the cafe.

 

• This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

title: Jokbal Alley
short_description: Located inside Gongdeok Market, Jokbal Alley is an alley filled with Jokbal stalls and stores. It was first created 30 years ago as more and more people gathered to eat Jokbal and Sundaetguk (Korean Blood Sausage Soup). Many of the stores found in Jokbal Alley has been around for more than 30 years.

title: Jeon Alley
short_description: Located next to Jokbal Alley inside Gongdeok Market, Jeon Alley became famous after appearing on a Korean TV show. After choosing from the wide array of fried food on display by placing selected food into a basket, visitors can pay for their food by weight and be seated in the inner areas to eat their food. On top of common fried food like fried sweet potatoes and fried octopus, visitors can also find unusual fried food like fried potato shrimp, fried shrimp chives jeon, mushroom jeon and much more.

title: Starbucks Coffee (Ewha Store)
short_description: The first Starbucks store to be created in Korea, Starbucks Coffee Korea 1st Branch is a 3-story store with wide, comfy seating areas. Images of when it first opened its doors back in 1999 are still on display for visitors to browse through.

title: PeterPan 1978
short_description: Peter Pan 1978 is a bakery that has been operating for over 40 years with two generations. The bakery has been in business for two generations and has been learning techniques from French and Japanese artisans to make better bread, and uses naturally fermented seeds imported from France. The bakery uses good ingredients such as organic rye and unrefined sugar, and its breads are popular for their unique names, such as "Baby Bun" and "Bread Stolen by Jang Baljang," and their healthy flavors. The bakery is frequented by both locals and foreigners.

title: Cocky Pub Hongdae
short_description: Located near the entrance of Hongik University, Cocky Pub Hongdae is a sports pub serving American-styled bar food. Serving from simple snacks to full-sized meals, Cocky Pub attracts many customers interested in watching sport matches. Pretty much an oasis for die-hard sports fans, Cocky Pub also features dart boards, beer pong, shuffle board, and many other recreational games for those not interested in sports. This establishment is frequented by many foreign residents and exchange students studying at nearby universities.

title: Sam Ryan's Sports Bar & Grill (Itaewon)
short_description: Located in Itaewon, Sam Ryan's Sports Bar & Girl is a Western-style sports pub where customers can enjoy live sport channels with snacks and beer. At this Itaewon sports pub, visitors can enjoy watching a variety of sports or play beer pong, battle ship, shuffle board, and more in the gaming area. A place to enjoy beer and simple snacks at an unbeatable price, Sam Ryan's Sports Bar & Grill is a popular establishment frequented by both Korean and foreign customers.

title: Sillim-dong Sundae Town
short_description: A must-visit spot for foodies in Seoul, Sillim-dong Sundae Town is the place to go for sundae (Korean Sausage). Often frequented by nearby businessmen looking for a hearty dinner, this area is also located near various facilities like shopping centers and a movie theater, making it a very popular date spot among couples as well.

title: Jangchung-dong Jokbal Alley
short_description: Jangchung-dong Jokbal Alley is one of the many must-visit alleyways in Seoul. Jangchung-dong became famous for its jokbal (Pig's feet) because of Jangchung Arena. In the past, most sporting events or concerts were held at Jangchung Arena. This lead to an influx of people who'd go and stop by nearby jokbal restaurants after the match or concert, eventually coming to create what is known as Jokbal Alley today. This area continues to attract many visitors even today with its delicious jokbal and side menus like bindae-tteok (Mung Bean Pancake) and pajeon (Green Onion Pancake).

title: Famille Station
short_description: Famille Station is a space of trendy, delicious restaurants all gathered in one place. Attracting many trendsetters with various brand names and diverse cuisine, Famille Station has been built to look like New York's Grand Central Station, incorporating both tradition and modern elements in its design. Consisting of three floors, the first floor is made up of popular restaurants while the second and third floor is made up of a beauty salon and cafes.

title: Seongsu-dong Galbi Alley
short_description: Attracting many visitors with large servings and low cost, Seongsu-dong Galbi Alley is the place to go for galbi (grilled ribs). The creation of a racetrack back in the 70s brought an influx of galbi restaurants around the area of Seongsu-dong, bringing this alley to become what it is today. Serving pork ribs with various side dishes, each restaurant offers slightly different tasting galbi due to their own special marinating sauce and methods.

title: Kim Yong-an Patisserie
short_description: Kim Yong-an Patisserie has been in business since 1967. The founder Kim Yong-an's know-how in making sweets has made it possible for people to enjoy delicious hot pot to this day. Senbei was made by following the Japanese confectionery technology to make a living during the Japanese occupation, but there is a clear difference in the way they have been reborn under the hands of the owner. Since its opening, the shop has maintained its flavor with good ingredients and craftsmanship from father to son, and today it still produces savory and crispy sweets with an eggy flavor.

title: Kervan Itaewon Branch
short_description: Kervan Itaewon Branch is a Turkish restaurant serving food made with Halal-certified ingredients. It is a popular date spot due to its great atmosphere.

title: PB Plus
short_description: Owned by an Iranian, PB Plus is a restaurant serving pizza and burgers made with Halal-certified ingredients. Serving big portions at a reasonable price, Pizza Burgers Plus is a popular place among diners. Their signature menu is their Special Beef Slices Burger, a delicious savory burger that never gets old.

title: Bombay Grill Itaewon
short_description: Located in Yongsan-gu, Seoul, Bombay Grill Itaewon is a restaurant serving Indian and Pakistani cuisine. Using only the freshest ingredients, Bombay Grill Itaewon offers a great selection of Indian and Pakistani dishes, providing a wonderfully exotic dining experience to its visitors.

title: Kervan COEX Branch
short_description: A popular restaurant in Samseong-dong COEX, Kervan is a Halal-certified Turkish restaurant. Serving hard to find Turkish cuisine in Korea, Kervan COEX Branch also boasts of a pretty interior made with Turkish lamps and tiles.

title: The Halal Guys Itaewon Branch
short_description: Starting as a food truck in New York City, The Halal Guys offer delicious servings of halal food on a platter or inside a sandwich. All branches of The Halal Guys coming into Korea are Halal-certified and serve food made with Halal ingredients.

title: Kervan Famille Station Branch
short_description: Kervan is a chain of restaurants which serves Halal, or "permitted" food. As a Halal-certified restaurant, Kervan offers Turkish food made by a Turkish chef. The interiors is also adorned with various Turkish decorations, lending an exotic atmosphere to the restaurant.

title: Kervan Banpo Branch
short_description: Kervan Banpo Branch is a Halal restaurant located inside Shinsegae Department Store. A restaurant to enjoy Turkish food made by a Turkish chef, Kervan's interiors is also adorned with various Turkish decorations, lending an exotic atmosphere to the restaurant.

title: Kervan Bakery
short_description: Kervan Bakery sells traditional Turkish desserts made by a Turkish pastry chef. The bakery's displays are filled with a variety of Turkish pastries and desserts, such as Turkish delights, Baklava, pudding, jam, and more.

title: Namhangang Maeuntang
short_description: A restaurant famous for their maeuntang ( a spicy fish stew cooked with freshly caught catfish, Mandarin fish, and freshwater fish)  in Gangdong-gu, Namhangang Maeuntang uses fish caught by fishermen in Gyeonggi-do, Yanggu and Gangwondo, Yangpeong to make their refreshingly spicy fish stew. Using a special seasoning made together with a food engineering professor in Korea National University of Transportation, the restaurant offers a special type of Mauentang that will not only prevent illness, but offers a tasty fish stew for visitors who love to eat fish.

title: Seolnun
short_description: Seolnun is a Korean restaurant specialized in Pyeongyang Naengmyeon dishes. A restaurant operated by a North Korean chef, Seolnun is a great place for visitors to try out and enjoy North Korean food.
