Also known for their delicious dumplings, nokdujeon (mung bean pancakes), and suyuk (boiled pork slices), Seolnun was featured on various TV programs.

title: Hamcho Ganjang Gejang
short_description: Hamcho Ganjang Gejang is a Korean seafood restaurant specializing in a soy-sauce marinated crab dish called Ganjang-gejang. They are most famous for their Ganjang-gejang marinated in a special type of fermented herb soy sauce. A restaurant with a traditionally Korean atmosphere, Hamcho Ganjang Gejang is a popular attraction among foreign tourists and has their menu available in Chinese, Japanese, and English.

title: Ooh Breado
short_description: Leaving out common allergen like egg, milk, and butter, Ooh Breado makes their bread using healthy domestically grown ingredients like rice, brown rice, and organic flour. Their signature menu is their "Sweet Pumpkin Cube," a flour-less bread made with a dough mixture of rice, brown rice, organic whole wheat, and other healthy ingredients, filled with pumpkin puree and red bean paste, topped with almond streusel.

title: Gurkha Restaurant
short_description: Gurkha Restaurant is a restaurant specializing in Indian and Nepalese food. Serving delicious curry, naan, tandoori chicken, lassi, and other Indian and Nepalese food, this restaurant is the perfect place to go for authentic tasting exotic food.

title: Byeolnan Ori (Duck Cuisine)
short_description: Byeolnan Ori is a restaurant specialized in duck cuisiune. The restaurant serves mainly two dishes called Electric Smoked Duck (smoked duck) and Special Duck (spicy duck soup). Customers can also order half and half, trying both the smoked duckand spicyduck soup and finish off the meal with a tidying-over of fried rice to complete their course.

title: Balwoo Gongyang
short_description: The only restaurant to be directly run by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddism, Balwoo Gongyang is a Michelin starred restaurant serving authentic temple cuisine. Serving authentic temple food made with traditional recipes passed down through temples, Balwoo Gongyang is a place to not only enjoy the taste of temple food but also experience the tradition and culture of temple food.

title: Kali
short_description: Kali is an Indian restaurant serving authentic Indian food made by local Indian chefs. A popular restaurant where there’s already a line forming outside by the end of lunch break, Kali boasts of an unique and exotic-looking interior decorated with props and accessories gathered and collected by the owner on his travels to India, Nepal, and Tibet over the years.

title: Couscous
short_description: Couscous is a Seochon-based restaurant serving Tunisian and North African dishes. A place to try out staple Tunisian dishes, a rare find in Korea, this place is highly recommended for diners wanting to expand their taste palate. Various Tunisian set meals are available at a price range from 16,000 won to 35,000 won.

title: Luna Asia
short_description: Luna Asia is an Indian restaurant run by an Indian chef. Serving curry made with 100% organic spices and perfectly golden oven-baked naan, Luna Asia highly recommends their two signature dishes, Tandoori chicken and Prawn Vindaloo, to first time visitors.

title: Ildossi Dakgalbi Gwanghwamun Branch
short_description: Ildossi Dakgalbi is a dakgalbi (spicy stir fry chicken) restaurant with a classy atmosphere. They sell a variety of dakgalbi menu including “Cheese Dakgalbi” and “Dakgalbi with Bean Sprouts”, making it a popular restaurant among visitors.

title: Sushi Hiroba (Samsung-dong Branch)
short_description: Sushi Hiroba is a domestic brand and one of the biggest conveyor belt sushi restaurants in Korea. Serving sushi suited for the Korean palate, they offer interesting fusion menu like “Rib-eye Steak Sushi”, “Original Flatfish Kimchi Sushi”, and more.

title: Ganga Yeoksam Branch
short_description: Ganga is an Indian restaurant serving authentic Indian cuisine. Everything on their menu are traditional Indian dishes and are very popular among Koreans for their great taste.

title: Ganga Mugyo Branch
short_description: Ganga is an Indian restaurant serving authentic Indian cuisine. Serving Indian food made by chefs with over 20 years of experience, Ganga is a popular restaurant with easy accessibility.

title: Ganga Jamsil Branch
short_description: Starting as a restaurant in Sinsa back in 2000, Ganga is currently a chain restaurant with many branch stores available throughout the country. Their food is made with over 20 different spices by chefs with over 20 years of experience and does not contain any MSG.

title: Kali Sadang Branch
short_description: A restaurant serving food made by an Indian chef, Kali Sadang Branch offers visitors a wide range of dishes and beverages from their menu.

title: Nammi Plant Lab
short_description: Nammi Plant Lab is a 100% vegan restaurant run by a Colombian owner. They serve healthy food using the freshest ingredients. They offer a variety of vegetable dishes, and Italian dishes such as cheese vegetable pizza and spinach cream lasagna are especially delicious. Many customers come from far away to try this menu, so the taste is guaranteed. They also allow pets, so you can comfortably visit while traveling with your pet. If you want to experience the charm of vegetarianism for yourself, I recommend visiting.

title: Delhi India
short_description: Delhi India is a Indian fusion restaurant run by an Indian chef. It’s the perfect place to try samosa, Indian fried rice, fried noodles, and other Indian dishes.

title: Durga Main Branch
short_description: Durga is an Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Featuring over 70 Indian and Nepalese dishes, the restaurant also boasts of an unique and exotic interior featuring both Indian and Nepalese designs.

title: Himalaya Jonggak Branch
short_description: Himalaya is an Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Although both Indian and Nepalese cuisine is made with the heavy use of spices, they’re still popular among many Korean locals.

title: Gamkkotdang
short_description: An Ikseon-dong hanok cafe built around a very old persimmon tree, Gamkkotdang is a beloved spot among both locals and visitors alike. Gamkottdang's signature menu includes their apple pie, scones, and egg tarts.

title: Viking's Wharf (Coex Mall)
short_description:
[Advantages & Tips for When Visiting Viking's Wharf] 


Viking's Wharf strictly abides by only the best ingredients to ensure that each visit rewards you with the utmost of quality.


  • 1. Only the finest lobster selection from Canada!
    Viking's Wharf makes it a yearly tradition to venture out to Canada each year and observe the fishery process, as well as perform detailed food inspections conducted for various purposes that include the processing of food, the freezing of food, product yield, taste, substance, aroma, the differences of food before and after cooking, and more. The head chef of Viking Group Inc., a former food specialist from a five-star hotel, then tries the food to provide feedback. Viking's Wharf lobster is a lobster carefully selected via the meticulous inspection as described above.


  • 2. All this cuisine from only lobster? And it's unlimited?!
    Once a menu item only available on special days, prepared by the best of chefs, lobster is now available to have at as much you please! Try the wide array of lobster cuisine that includes such menu items as whole steamed lobster, prepared to order, lobster bisque, baked lobster, lobster steak, lobster ceviche, and a lobster mango tower.


  • 3. Fresh seafood brought to your seat!
    Enjoy in-season seafood to your heart's content, prepared to order upon selection from aquariums filled with a variety of seafood that includes oysters, triploid oysters, abalones, scallops, sea squirts, clams, blood clams, octopus, seashells, small octopus, baby clams, and sea cucumber. Take advantage of the delicious sushi, as well, prepared with a variety of fish ranging from snappers, flatfish, and swordfish to tuna, salmon, red drums, and shrimp.


  • 4. Enjoy fresh grilled seafood!
    Savor a delicious grilled menu, whether it's baked lobster, beef short ribs, or shrimp, or even abalone, grilled chicken, or salmon steak! Besides just being known as an all-you-can-eat lobster buffet, Viking's Wharf is known around social media as a tasty rib house, too!


  • 5. Quality speaks for itself - From premium water to delectable desserts!
    For starters, Viking's Wharf serves up Aquafina water and S.Pellegrino sparkling water, meeting the Michelin restaurant standard, while also offering fruit extracts and other health drinks!


And don't forget to save room for dessert with all the premium brand products to choose from! Some items include G.Fassi, the classic Italian gelato brand since 1880, TWG Black Tea, a tea brand enjoyed across the globe, Paul Basset Coffee, Noah's Bakery,listedamong one of the top three bakeries in Apgujeong, and more! A great selection of fruit is also available, including grapefruit, mango, and pineapple, with the mango prepared right on the spot!

title: Git-teol (Feather)
short_description: Located along one of the many branching side streets of the infamous "Yeontral Park," Git-teol offers some respite to solo-goers out there looking to enjoy a leisurely cocktail. All you need to do is keep an open mind, and your manners, and you'll make new friends in no time! There's a plethora of different whiskey and liquor available with a vast menu of cocktails at the ready for a reasonable price. If luck is on your side, you can also enjoy the occasional open party or exhibition that takes place from time to time. During the big holiday seasons of Seollal and Chuseok, they even hold festive potluck celebrations as well! Stop on by and enjoy good company among new friends for memories you're sure not to forget. Git-teol is the perfect solution for those late nights when you're stuck alone, when you simply need a drink on a starry city night, or even when Netflixing at home just doesn't seem to cut it. Hope to see you there!

title: Shilladang Ikseon
short_description: Shilladang’s handmade hangwa, prepared fresh every morning, are filled with dedication. Deliver your heartfelt message to your loved ones with a Shilladang hangwa gift set!

title: Slow Brew Pub (Gangnam Branch)
short_description: Also known as Neurin Maeul in Korean, the Slow Brew Pub is Korea's first-ever Seoul-based distillery that offers a unique array of food that is the perfect match for the wide selection of smooth, traditional alcohol, featuring freshly-distilled makgeolli and herbal liquor that are distinctive with the flavors of each season of fermentation all year round! The Slow Brew Pub was founded on the desire to make a makgeolli distillery accessible in the heart of the city so that people can experience makgeolli at its best. The pub distillery features a unique line of "downtown makgeolli food" provided by Bae & Brewing Co. so as to better accentuate that of a respite amid the business of modern daily life. Stop by and enjoy the delicious drinks and food that are prepared each day with the utmost of care.

title: Hangang Brewery
short_description: Hangang Brewery is a unique distillery that centers its operations around promoting the resurgence and identity awareness of traditional alcohol from the grounds of Seongsu-dong, a neighborhood located by the Hangang River in eastern Seoul. Known as Seoul's primary manufacturing district, Seongsu-dong is the perfect spot to help better realize the vision of Hangang Brewery where the past and the present coexist with one another amid all the factories, cafes, commercial areas, and people of various backgrounds. Hangang Brewery utilizes Korea's traditional rice liquor, makgeolli, as a medium to bridge the past and the present by capturing past traditions and culture in such a way so as to be relevant in the present.

title: With Dalgyalbbang (With Egg Bread)
short_description: Infamous around the Sookmyung Women's University area, With Dalgyalbbang reinvents one of Korea's traditional street foods, gyerang-bbang, or egg bread, in a variety of different flavors. The bakery takes the delicious Korean snack off the streets and transforms into one of the area's most popular cafe treats. With Dalgyalbbang has even appeared on television, reflecting its popularity and original brand identity as a Korean dessert.

title: TABLE-A
short_description: In this cafe, you can not only enjoy delicious drinks, but also watch and interact with cute animals. The difference between this cafe and other types of animal cafes is that there are many different types of animals that live here: cats, raccoons, meerkats, parrots and various reptiles. Direct interaction, including touching is permitted. Even rare animals like chinchillas, cusimanzas and genetas live in the cafe. For a fee, you can buy food and feed the animals.

title: Richemont Bakery The Hyundai Seoul Branch
short_description: Richemont Bakery, originally established in Mapo-gu in 1979, can be found in Tasty Seoul, the Hyundai Seoul’s food hall. Richemont Bakery's sweet and savory chestnut pastries are a dessert loved by many. In addition to this, we recommend trying their bread that is stuffed with chestnuts and their delectable cream puffs filled with thick cream!

title: Cafe Layered The Hyundai Seoul
short_description: Cafe Layered, famous for its various types of lightly toasted scones, can be found at The Hyundai Seoul’s food hall, Tasty Seoul. The pretty displays in the shop catch any visitor’s eyes and the delicious scones, baked goods and cakes will make them raise their cameras. Cafe Layered's atmospheric lighting and display props enhance the beautiful details of their desserts. There are a variety of choices that guests can choose from to enjoy their scones, such as cranberry cream cheese scones filled with cream cheese and wrapped in a crispy dough, and black sesame ang butter scones that provide a unique taste when the seeds meet the ang butter, a delicious mixture of red bean paste and butter.

title: Cafe Layered Anguk Branch
short_description: Cafe Layered's main store in Anguk is famous for its various types of lightly toasted scones. The pretty displays and the delicious scones, baked goods and cakes catch the eyes of every visitor. Cafe Layered's atmospheric display props and ornaments enhance the visuals of the already beautiful desserts. There are a variety of tasty options to try, such as cranberry cream cheese scones stuffed with a cream cheese filling in a crispy dough, and black sesame ang butter scones that combines black sesame seeds and ang butter to create a unique and delicious taste

title: Richemont Bakery Seongsan Branch
short_description: Richemont Bakery, which started in Mapo-gu in 1979 and boasts a long history, has its main branch in Seongsan. The bakery is known as one of the top 3 bakeries in Seoul. The confections at the Richemont Bakery Seongsan Main Branch are filled with sweet and savory chestnuts. Bam Pie is a dessert loved by many people. In addition to the bam pies, visitors should try their moist chestnut bread and their cream puffs filled with a sweet and thick cream!

title: Si Gan Eul Deul I Da (Take Time)
short_description: Si Gan Eul Deul I Da (Take Time) is a dessert restaurant that features croissants that are crispy on the outside and filled with various creams on the inside. There are many options available, such as chocolate cream croissants with a creamy, raw chocolate taste, ang butter croissants that are filled with the savory taste of red beans and butter, and red bean cream croissants made with fragrant red beans and light cream.

title: Base is Nice
short_description: Base is Nice is a vegetarian-friendly restaurant that uses vegetables as the main character in their dishes to deliver fresh and natural flavors. Visitors can find a variety of options made with vegetables that change with the seasons. In particular, the grilled tofu rice with red pepper puree is the signature dish of Base is Nice. Experience a fast, comfortable and unforgettable meal.

title: Seochon Daeha Restaurant
short_description: Seochon Daeha Restaurant, located on Sejong Village Food Street, is famous for its fresh grilled pork. Both the exterior and interior have a vintage atmosphere, as well as the menu board, which is all handwritten, making it an even more attractive space with its long-established history. The special feature of Daeha Restaurant is that visitors can enjoy rich and golden pork belly by grilling kimchi, green onion, and garlic together on a hot pot. Since it is close to Inwangsan Mountain, it is a perfect stop where visitors can fill their hungry stomachs with delicious food after a day of hiking.

title: Cafe Highwaist Ikseon Branch
short_description: Cafe Highwaist, located in Ikseon-dong, is a place visited by many people as a popular dating spot and for being a dessert cafe with a unique look and a cute and warm atmosphere where white walls and hanok buildings come together. The interior of the cafe is decorated like a fairy tale, and the bakery has cute and colorful visuals that catch the eye. Visitors can find various types of scones such as classic butter scones and double chocolate scones, puffy cakes with cute dog figures, and rich chocolate cakes made with cream cheese and chocolate.

title: Dewey Coffee
short_description: Visitors looking for a cafe with a good atmosphere in Sangam-dong should check out Dewey Coffee and its fantastic desserts. The interior of the cafe has a modern yet warm feel. There are sweet cookies, savory scones, and various types of coffee with Dewey Coffee's unique touch. In particular, it is a pet-friendly cafe, so visitors can enjoy their coffee with their dog. Enjoy tea time in a place full of good vibes both inside and out!

title: Charmandre Seoul Forest
short_description: Located in Seoul Forest, Charmandre Restaurant specializes in British home-cooked food. It is run by a chef from a Michelin restaurant in the UK and offers a variety of delicious British dishes such as chicken tikka masala, fish & chips, and Shepherd's Pie. It has a cozy and warm interior and a window overlooking Seoul Forest, making it a popular date spot. Indulge in fresh and delicious British home-cooked meals at the beautiful Charmandre restaurant, no matter the season.

title: Gallery SOWYEN Cafe
short_description: If you walk along the stone road of Seosulla-gil to the west of Jongmyo Shrine, you will find Gallery SOWYEN Cafe. Here, you can enjoy warm tea, drinks, and food while looking at the jewelry and metal crafts in the small exhibition room. A well-kept flower garden along with the quaint cafe creates the perfect atmosphere for some quiet and relaxing moments while watching the artists creating their crafts.

title: Seoul Coffee Ikseon Branch
short_description: Within the oldest hanok village in Seoul lies the Ikseon branch of Seoul Coffee, where the past and present coexist. Here, memories of the past easily arise due to the various menu items inspired by traditional Korean flavors amidst a peaceful atmosphere. With items such as vienna coffee and milk tea, pumpkin sikhye (a sweet rice drink), sweet rice cake tiramisu, and chocolate twisted donuts, it's captured the hearts of many thanks to it's modern interpretation and unique combinations of Korean flavors.

title: The Spot Fabulous
short_description: The Spot Fabulous, famous for its various premium handmade desserts, is a cafe loved not only for its taste but also for its beautiful view. Here the atmosphere is notable as it was renovated from modern buildings. On the first floor, visitors can find decadent and delicious desserts such as fig tiramisu, financier, and macaroons. Visitors who order a drink can get it from a place that makes double-decker beverages. On one side of the store, windows that have a refreshing view to the outside have become the biggest attraction of The Spot Fabulous, where you can see the changing each of the four seasons.

title: MUNEI Cafe
short_description: MUNEI cafe, well-known for being a magnifying glass cafe in Euljiro - an area with many hip and unique cafes, is popular with people who like coffee shops that have a trendy and unique atmosphere. It's a place where visitors can enjoy coffee and wine together. Visit the wine bar with a great atmosphere and charming lights at night or the cafe during the day. On one side of the cafe, items such as accessories, perfumes, cups, and beans are displayed for sale. The signature of MUNEI cafe is the Munei Latte, while the famous dessert is a chewy brownie sprinkled with popping candy, icestones, and soft vanilla ice cream on top. Visit for the incredible atmosphere of the cafe and enjoy their specialty drinks at MUNEI cafe, a space created by artists.

title: Index Shop (Gwangjin-gu)
short_description: Within Common Ground sits Index Shop, a book cafe with a unique collection. Index Shop is the perfect place to bask in a patch of sunlight while reading a great book and having one of their delicious café drinks. Book shelves are arranged in alphabetical order, adding to its charm. Visitors can also find different hip and unique magazines, goods, and books of a wide variety of genres.

title: Cafe Comma Hapjeong Branch
short_description: Cafe Comma is a wonderful book cafe run by Munhak Dongne, one of Korea’s leading publishers, and has an entire wall made up by a bookshelf. As charming as something from a movie, the shelves are filled with books of various genres, and visitors can enjoy reading with a delicious drink in a space filled with literature and culture.

title: Colline
short_description: With the cafe and flower shop operating as one, cafe Colline is filled with the fragrance of flowers from the entrance. If you have recharged your body and mind with the help of various flowers and plants, satisfy your appetite with Colline's signature menu: cotton latte, topped with giant cotton candy and shaved ice.

title: The Baker's Table
short_description: A bakery located in Gyeongridan-gil, Itaewon, sells German bread. The store is designed to make you feel like you are in Germany the moment you enter. Besides bread, there are other delicious items on the menu such as soup, so try various things if you stop by.

title: ALPEDO
short_description: A place in Seoul where you can get a taste of Turkey Alpedo in Itaewon has a variety of Turkish bread and coffees, and the most popular menu is kaymak, which translates to heaven’s taste.

title: Dido Jazz Lounge
short_description: A cultural space where you can enjoy delicious food and wine along with live jazz performances. Live performances are held every day, and related information such as the performance lineups can be found on the Dido Jazz Lounge Instagram.

title: Live Jazz Cafe Chunnyun
short_description: The name of the place translates to “for a thousand years,” meaning that jazz performances will live on. Since its opening in 1996, it has been offering people great live jazz performances. In 1996, it was the club that allowed band performances inside restaurants, which were illegal at the time. Until this day, it remains a place that is constantly striving for the development of jazz culture.

title: Yeonnam 5701
short_description: It is a jazz bar where you can enjoy various food and wine. Different from other jazz bars, Yeonnam 5701 has one section where you can focus only on the live performances and another area where you can dine while watching the performances. You can check the performance lineups on Yeonnam 5701 Instagram and Facebook pages.

title: 3Daesamgyejangin
short_description: Since its opening in 1973, this Samgye-tang restaurant has been passed down for three generations, hence the name of the restaurant. It sells three types of Samgye-tang such as pine nuts, mung bean, and mugwort, and sous vide chicken stir-fry soup. If you are tired of the heat, head over to 3Daesamgyejangin and revitalize yourself with a bowl of hot Samgye-tang.

title: Rafre Fruit
short_description: Rafre Fruit is a fruit shop where you can enjoy the natural taste of premium fruit. All food items use frozen fruit and fruit syrup, and all fruit juices use cane syrup instead of sugar. Would you like to try a variety of fruit desserts such as bingsu (shaved ice,) smoothies, cakes, and ice cream? Check out Rafre Fruit.

title: Ssangmun-dong Coffee
short_description: Ssangmun-dong Coffee is a coffee shop in Ssangmun-dong that feels like a hideout and a cozy mountain cabin. Enjoy retro props and special coffees and desserts aptly named by the owner!

title: Uphill Namsan
short_description: A casual dining bar located at the end of an uphill road on Gyeongnidan-gil. Enjoy a delicious meal at this scenic spot.

title: Boogie Woogie
short_description: A go-to live bar if you like robust and fast-beat piano performances and jazz music. On a Friday night, go to Boogie Woogie if you want to start the weekend with upbeat music.

title: Pets Sounds Music Pub
short_description: Enjoy performances of many music genres, such as retro, post-punk, heavy metal, and dream pop. Enjoy the music and satisfy your hunger with pizza, chicken wings, fries, and delicious cocktails

title: Champ Coffee 3rd Workroom
short_description: Champ Coffee is located in Sewoon Plaza, in the center of Euljiro. The signature coffee carefully made by the owners of Champ Coffee continuously attracts people.

title: 1in1jan
short_description: If you want to enjoy a café with a gorgeous view on a beautiful day, head to 1in1jan. Drinks and desserts full of Korean flavor and taste await you.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Gunsan Squid
short_description:
The beginning of Gunsan Squid, which started with seven tables in Seokchon-dong, Seoul, in 1988, was not grandiose. Rather than cutting costs, the basic principle is to provide enough healthy ingredients on a family's table. Gunsan Squid's unique and pleasantly spicy taste is a secret sauce made of natural ingredients without synthetic capsaicin. It is the stronghold and pride of Gunsan Squid that has been around since its foundation.


Gunsan Squid can be purchased online to enjoy the food at home easily. It has advanced into overseas markets to spread the excellence of Korean food.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Cho Rong's Aunt Budaejjigae
short_description:
Chorong’s Aunt Budaejjigae is a traditional budaejjigae restaurant that has been trusted for over 30 years since its opening in 1990. The original taste is maintained with the best ingredients and cooking methods.
Kimchi is made in-house with domestically produced ingredients using cabbage from the highlands that are aged for a long time at a low temperature. Here, dried shiitake mushrooms add a savory taste, and the broth brewed with 100% Korean beef bones and ginseng gives a deep flavor. The fresh and clean taste is excellent, with the best ham and sausage used in various ways, the water parsley, and bean sprouts. These ingredients differentiate it from other budaejjigae

Like ‘old restaurants’ and ‘restaurants recognized by regulars,’ Chorong’s Aunt Budaejjigae wants to be known as a kind and friendly restaurant. In addition, it strives to maintain a consistent taste. It continues to make great efforts to develop other colorful and professional food that various people can find and enjoy, rather than the simple menu item called Budaejjigae.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Janggun Galbi
short_description:
Janggun Galbi, a restaurant specializing in meat and galbi soup, has been thoroughly practicing the principle of ‘authentic food’ for 41 years since its establishment in 1980.
The representative, who has worked as a manager at Janggun Galbi since 1983, has earned the founder’s trust with innate diligence and sincerity and has been operating the restaurant since 2011.
Janggun Galbi always tries to provide authentic food and always serves big portions while considering high-cost rates. Except for some imported products, the meat is graded Hanwoo 1++. The quantity is more significant than other competitors, and the price is set low so that customers can eat more meat. The price is set low so that customers can eat more meat. Cold Buckwheat Noodles, with an impressive broth made by boiling beef bone, brisket, and landslide in an old-fashioned way, is prepared by the chef who has been with the restaurant for 32 years. All the side dishes consumed at Janggun Galbi are not bought but homemade. The ingredients come from a family member who farms in Boryeong, Chungcheongnam-do.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Minjeong Siktang
short_description: Minjeong Siktang, famous for its various foods made by native people living in Jayang-dong for five generations, was founded in 1995 and celebrated for nearly 30 years. Minjeong Siktang, which always buys and cooks the best ingredients, entertains customers as if they were guests at home and boasts friendly service. Ox Bone Soup, Boiled Pork Slices, and Pork Cutlets are the main menu items, and they almost perfectly satisfy the tastes and needs of customers that vary according to their age. The ingredients are purchased daily and prepared on the same day to maintain freshness. Due to word of mouth that the restaurant is healthy, the number of customers visiting is increasing little by little every day. The restaurant is operated on the first floor, giving you the feeling of being invited to eat at someone’s home. The quiet and straightforward interior gives you the feeling of visiting your grandmother's or friend's house.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Hyangho Myeonok
short_description:
The name of Hyangho Myeonok, located in the northernmost part of Gangneung City, where the fragrant smell of the sea and beautiful scenery are in harmony, is derived from the name of Hyangho Village in Jumunjin, the hometown of CEO Lee Ki-chang's father.

At Hyangho Myeonok, based on the management philosophy of ‘taste and price are competitive,’ all ingredients are airlifted from domestic production areas, and noodles are cooked with a noodle machine immediately after ordering. As for the dumplings, the mother, who has a Korean cooking license, prepares only the amount she will use daily every morning. Vegetables and red pepper powder are purchased directly from Garak Market daily, and the fresh kimchi is also made with domestic ingredients daily. Lee Ki-chang, the second-generation CEO, has taken over and is running the restaurant where his parents have worked hard. Barley rice is provided as a service with the hope that it would be nice if even a single guest could eat to the fullest.

Hyangho Myeonok's dumplings and noodles, made every morning with customers in mind, are becoming local specialties through word of mouth.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] 3Daesamgyejangin
short_description:
All year round, the sound of broth boiling and the smell of thick broth never cease. 3Daesamgyejangin is a hot place that opened in 1973 in 1-dong, Seocho. Samgye-tang(Ginseng Chicken Soup,) made by carefully boiling the broth for three days, gained excellent customer feedback and 3Daesamgyejangin became a famous Samgyetang restaurant. Even after rising to the ranks of popular restaurants, the effort to make the perfect Samgyetang did not stop. 

Although it is convenient and economical to boil meat in water, in 1991, the chicken was steamed in a steamer to preserve the texture and taste. This restaurant was the first to develop pine nut samgyetang and mugwort samgyetang and succeeded for 30 years. Recently, a sous-vide machine that cooks meat at a low temperature has been used to remove the tough texture of chicken and bring out a soft texture. With a passion for the best Samgyetang, the sous-vide machine was also made by purchasing parts to keep it in optimum condition. In addition, all kinds of sauces and gochujang for dak doritang (Chicken Stew) are also developed and made to create the unique taste of 3Daesamgyejangin.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Naju Beef Bone Soup Friendship House
short_description:
Naju Beef Bone Soup Friendship House started in 1989 when the owner quit his job and started the restaurant in Daejeon. The founder, who accumulated know-how in Daejeon through thorough analysis and systematic management, moved to Seoul in 2009 and opened the current Naju Beef Bone Soup Friendship House. Without special skills, the first CEO, Lee Wan-gu, benchmarked the taste and management methods of many famous restaurants across the country. Through such efforts, the current Naju Beef Bone Soup Friendship House was successful. Naju Beef Bone Soup Friendship House’s main menu, Naju Beef Bone Soup, features a clear soup topped with green onion and egg yolk, and the food’s taste reflects the founder’s angst and effort.
Fresh meat from Majang-dong is used every morning, and laurel, soju, garlic, and onions are used to make the soup. Beef Tripe Soup is also very hearty. To remove the unique smell from the cow's stomach, the meat is washed with cold water more than 20 times, and side dishes are also served unconditionally.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Jinseong Siktang
short_description:
Jinseong Siktang, which has been selling kalguksu for nearly 30 years in Cheongdam-dong, which is said to be the center of Seoul, has been striving to be tastefully consistent since its establishment in 1990. The owner experienced countless failures in the early days of the business due to limited experience. Still, by benchmarking visited famous restaurants nationwide and through efforts to directly improve food taste, Jinseong Siktang was created.

Kalguksu, the main menu item, is made by boiling beef bones and mixed bones for more than 8 hours from morning to evening and topped with shiitake and red pepper. Jumbo Mandu is also made and consumed with fresh ingredients from nearby Garak Market every morning and afternoon. The soybean noodles made with 100% domestic soybeans ground every morning with a millstone are a delicacy in summer.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Boulangerie (Le Pain)
short_description:
Boulangerie Lepain is a baeknyeon-gage that has been converted into the region’s main bakery for nearly 28 years. Having walked on a single path to confectionery and baking for 41 years, the founder’s technical skills help make healthy aged bread with 100% organic flour, natural butter, bay salt, and natural fermentation substances.


Boulangerie Lepain's signature menu is Gongju chestnut bread made with plenty of domestic chestnuts and squid ink cream cheese bread made with squid ink, cream cheese, and nuts. These are common bread found in any bakery. Still, Boulangerie Lepain's Gongju chestnut bread and cream cheese bread are special bread made with devoted care and authentic ingredients. Even when making a single dough, numerous natural ingredients such as peas, coconut water, grain syrup, pea juice, and sea salt are used, and bread is made with a recipe that was completed after countless failures. The ingredients are always of the highest quality.


The most commercially available chestnut in Korea is used, the squid ink is from Spain, which is recognized as the best, and the cheese is from Philadelphia. This is because the principle unique to Boulangerie Lepain is that good bread comes from the best ingredients and craftsmanship.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Gguigguijjuggumi
short_description: Gguigguijjuggumi, famous for garlic chives webfoot octopus, opened in 1994 in Banghwa-dong, Gangseo-gu. The charm of Gguigguijjuggumi is that it uses domestic spicy stir-fried webfoot octopus and blends it with fresh chives to make the soft and firm texture of the spicy stir-fried webfoot octopus. Chive webfoot octopus, the most famous menu item, was developed by CEO Park Chun-rye himself. After cooking domestic webfoot octopus, seasoned chives are placed on top of the webfoot octopus. The compatibility between webfoot octopus and leek is exquisite. This dish is a must if you visit Gguigguijjuggumi.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Donghunkwan
short_description:
The weight of 70 years in one place is piled up all over the store. Donghung, founded by a father of Chinese origin, has been passed down from son to grandson. Donghung was established in 1951 when the fires of the war had not gone away. The actual business registration certificate was issued in 1950, which is recorded in the data of the Seoul Metropolitan Government and is the oldest business registration in Seoul for Chinese cuisine restaurants. Donghung is a 100-year-old store made up of chefs from China and overseas Chinese without any Korean employees. It is trying to differentiate itself by maintaining local cooking methods from China and Taiwan and constantly striving to develop traditional Chinese food that suits the taste of Koreans.

Based on traditional menus of Chinese restaurants such as jajangmyeon, jjamppong (Spicy Seafood Noodle Soup,) and tangsuyuk (Sweet and Sour Pork,) signature menu items such as dim sum are provided, and various sauces are prepared directly without using ready-made products, maintaining Donghung's unique quality.

Donghung, which has been reborn as a landmark in Geumcheon because it has been operating in one location for 70 years, has been firmly established as a baeknyeon-gage with memories of children becoming fathers and grandfathers holding hands and visiting again.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] La Francaise Bakery
short_description:
The main menu items of Française Bakery are unique bread created through research by the Pastry & Bakery Research Institute. Various types of bread have been developed, such as Sweet Potato Marinated Bread, Onion Bread, and Brown Rice Bread. All bread uses naturally fermented species, not artificial yeast, so they are easy to digest, and you can feel the taste and nutrition of the bread as it is. Among the numerous pieces of bread, the most popular signature menu items are pumpkin bread and walnut pie. Pumpkin bread made with the unique technology of Française Bakery using domestic pumpkins boasts a light yet soft texture.


The famous walnut pie made by the owner is also popular as a gift because of its soft texture and thick thickness, even though it is a nut. In addition, onion bread and sweet potato rubbing bread created a mania and drew good customer feedback.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Goryeojeong
short_description:
Goryeojeong has been serving Korean food at the exact location for nearly 35 years. Goryeojeong offers Wang Galbi Tang (Premium Beef Rib Soup,) Woogeo-naejang-tang, Yang Gomtang (Beef Tripe Soup,) Seonji haejangguk (Ox Blood Hangover Soup,) Ocha stone pot rice, and Chadol Doenjang Jjigae (Soybean Paste Stew with Beef Brisket) made in-house. They specialize in serving meals and meat such as Chadolbagi (Beef Brisket,) Chimatsal (Flank,) and Somakchang (Ocha stone pot rice.) The marbled beef and the soybean paste stew are by far the most popular among customers. The special sauce containing the founder's 30-years-of-experience personal touch, and soybean paste stew made with Goryeojeong’s traditional soybean paste method, are drawing favorable reviews by further enhancing the flavor of the meat.

Apart from the meat, all of Goryeojeong’s menu items are imbued with the rich taste of motherly cooking that everyone has experienced at least once in their childhood. The founder and the second-generation heirs of the family business directly participate in the cooking process, providing consistent quality food to customers over a long period.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Songjugjang
short_description: Songjugjang, the first Chinese restaurant, started in 1952 and run by Shin Moo-song, former chairman of the Overseas Chinese Restaurant Association, has the taste of its food preserved by Shin Yeon-kyung, the eldest son. This Chinese cuisine restaurant with 70 years of history has been handed down to grandchildren. Menu items are kept at affordable prices so that ordinary people aren’t burdened, and the entire third floor is open to customers, which is highly convenient. The secret of Songjugjang’s unique food is red pepper oil and noodles pulled out by hand. The spicy yet soft red pepper oil is Songjugjang's 70-year know-how secret. The noodles, pulled out of the noodle-making machine immediately after an order is placed, have increased texture and are well-appreciated by customers. Gochu jjamppong (Spicy Seafood Noodle Soup with Korean Chili Peppers) and Red Pepper Tray Black Bean Noodles, which use red pepper oil and noodles, are signature dishes of Songjugjang. Songjugjang, which has been purchasing ingredients from Shinsanghwahoe in Bukchang-dong since it started 70 years ago, provides Mul Mandu (Boiled Dumplings) and various Chinese dishes to the needy in the region every holiday.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Pungnam Golbaengi
short_description:
In one corner of Euljiro, where the nostalgia of Seoul remains, the smell of seasoned golbaengi (sea snails) spreads. Pungnam Golbaengi is a golbaengi restaurant with the oldest tradition in Golbaengi Alley in Euljiro. Pungnam Golbaengi, started by parents in 1984 and inherited by their children, is a 100-year-old store that seeks constant development to maintain its traditional taste.
The main menu, seasoned golbaengi, is cooked by only the second-generation CEO and founder, who inherited the family business from his parents. All ingredients are purchased after seeing and checking them in person. The noodles, which determine the taste of the golbaengi salad, are extracted from the noodle shop. The golbaengi is supplied by selecting fresh domestic products tasted by the founder or the children. Food ingredients such as red pepper powder and perilla oil are also provided by perilla oil companies that have been trading for more than 30 years to create fresh food. The taste was excellent, so there were many franchise suggestions, but Pungnam Golbaengi refused, fearing that the quality of the food would deteriorate. Customers have loved this 100-year-old store as a golbaengi specialty store that has maintained the traditional taste for over 40 years in the alley.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Jonggajib
short_description:
As you enter the narrow, winding alleys of Insa-dong, you will find a quiet yet friendly shop. Jonggajip is a Gopchang-jeongol (Beef Tripe Hot Pot) restaurant, one of Seoul's native restaurants that have been in business for over 20 years in a narrow alley in Insa-dong. Jonggajib, which struggled through the IMF, the mad cow disease crisis, and Corona, alongside the entire nation, is making various efforts to maintain unwavering taste and honesty.
The fire show, produced by pouring soju on a hot grill to catch the unique smell of tripe enjoyed by customers and provide a fresh experience, is a fantastic scene that can only be seen in Jonggajip. Based on the philosophy that all ingredients must be fresh, fresh tripe is airlifted from Majang-dong every day. The bulgogi and vegetables used in the hot pot are purchased directly from the Cheongnyangni Market. Jonggajip's main menu items, gopchang gui (Grilled Beef Tripe) and Casserole, are well-appreciated by customers for their ample amount and differentiated tastes.

title: Yennaljip Nakwon Agwijjim
short_description:
Nakwon Agwijjim is a Oraegage and Baeknyeon-gage that is confident that it is the originator of Seoul-style Agwi-jjim (Braised Spicy Monkfish) and has been in business for nearly 40 years since 1977. The founders of Nakwon Agwijjim moved to Seoul with the ambition to cook Masan-style Agwi-jjim, which is cooked by drying monkfish on the seashore. However, there was no place to dry monkfish in Seoul, so they had no choice but to develop and serve Seoul-style Agwi-jjim, made by trimming living monkfish right away. Seoul-style Agwi-jjim was well received by customers and became the main menu of Nakwon Agwijjim. The second-generation CEO, who succeeded in the family business, always does his best to airlift fresh ingredients to preserve the dish’s original name and authentic taste. Every morning at dawn, fresh monkfish are airlifted to Noryangjin Market, and only domestic ingredients are used for seasoning.

The food taste is so delicious that it even received a franchise offer once, but it was rejected due to the monkfish’s unstable supply and demand. The decision was to preserve the food taste that could not be compromised no matter what. Thanks to the efforts of the second generation to protect tradition, Nakwon Agwijjim was selected as a Seoul Future Heritage in 2019 and received a certificate of modern and contemporary cultural heritage, showing the tradition’s dignity.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Jinmi Siktang
short_description:
Jinmi Sikdang is a Korean restaurant that has been serving Kong-guksu (Noodles in Cold Soybean Soup) with devotion for 45 years at the corner of Munbae-dong, Yongsan-gu. The founder who started and operated Jinmi Siktang moved to Seoul 45 years ago and made Kong-guksu and Ramyeon (Ramen.) The tradition of Jinmi Siktang, handed down from parents to sons, is that only fresh local ingredients are to be used.

Even now, they only use wangtaeman purchased from Mungyeong, Gyeongsangbuk-do, to make fermented soybean paste. In the summer, the delicacy Kong-guksu is served. Cheonggukjang (Rich Soybean Paste) and Kong-guksu, made with wangtae beans, which have no fishy smell and are suitable for health, are receiving favorable reviews from customers for their light and rich taste. Jinmi Siktang’s unique rule of purchasing only the ingredients needed for the day and consuming them all is still thoroughly maintained even after 45 years.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Sigol Gamjatang
short_description:
In the steaming soup, the thick broth's deep taste and savory aroma stimulate the nose, and the soft and flavorful meat tickles the tongue of the eater. Sigol Gamjatang, which has been making the same Gamjatang for nearly 33 years in Eunpyeong-gu, has Ugeoji Gamjatang (Pork Back-bone Stew) as its main menu item.

Sigol Gamjatang is an emblematic gamjatang restaurant in Eunpyeong-gu, designated as a local restaurant in Eunpyeong-gu. Currently, sons, daughters, and sons-in-law run the restaurant together. They are raising brand awareness by operating packaging and delivery services so that although far away, people can have warm food anytime and anywhere.
In addition, the sole signature menu of Sigol Gamjatang is made by boiling domestic pork backbone thoroughly for 4 hours by removing blood and trimming, then adding whole potatoes and beef brisket and broiling it again. The menu is simple, but the sincerity and effort put into serving a bowl of gamjatang are far from simple.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Ssaligol
short_description:
Galbi immersed in broth and deliciously cooked saeng samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) tempt customers’ chopsticks. Since its opening in 1990, this restaurant has been running for 31 years, intending to serve homecooked meals. The main menu, “dwaeji galbi soup,” made by marinating fresh pork ribs and neck meat in more than ten different seasonings and then stewing them, is popular among customers.

For freshness and chewiness, non-frozen pork bellies are cut directly with a knife without using a machine. Many repeat customers love kimchi and Mu-saengchae (Julienne Korean Radish Salad). Kimchi has been made with domestic ingredients since the restaurant opened. The operating principle is to faithfully provide the basics without resorting to technical skills. Many regular customers visit Ssaligol; not only do many come more than twice a week, but they are highly praised to the extent that customers who have visited once are said to come again.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Renaissance Bakery
short_description:
Parents who enter the store holding their children's hands were regular customers of Renaissance Bakery when they were young. Renaissance Bakery, a bakery filled with memories that children return to as parents, is an old bakery that opened in 1982 as a permanent fixture of Mapo. Intending to create a friendly bakery that anyone of any age can visit and eat at any time, they have been striving to maintain the best technology, quality, and variety. In particular, they insist on fresh ingredients, organic flour grown in clean regions, and the best ingredients from Europe.


Renaissance Bakery offers a variety of delicious products, ranging from old-fashioned bread to trendy bread, that satisfy the needs of the modern youth. The neighborhood bakery, which started in 1982, is looking forward to a renaissance bakery that will indeed greet the next 100 years by continuing the family business for the second generation.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Big Grandma's House
short_description:
Pictures of braised pigs’ feet decorate the front of the store. One of the famous braised pigs’ feet restaurants in Jangchung-dong and Korea’s No. 1 braised pigs’ feet restaurant that attracts customers is Big Grandma’s House. The 1st founder, Jeon Sook-ryeol, recalled the taste of pigs' feet cooked by his mother in the 1960s and started the Big Grandmother's House. As the taste of braised pigs’ feet went viral, braised pigs’ feet restaurants were naturally created around it, and the current braised pigs’ feet Alley in Jangchung-dong was born. Since then, CEO Kim Myung-sook, the second daughter-in-law, and director Kim Song-hyun, the third granddaughter, have continued the tradition of Big Grandmother's House.

Big Grandmother's House stands out among the many braised pigs’ feet restaurants. When all the competitors raised prices, they were the only ones who maintained prices and kept customers satisfied. In addition, the restaurant quickly reflects trends by developing single-person and set menus and introducing delivery services and various promotions. This is very differentiated because most long-established stores are late in reflecting new trends.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Podonamu
short_description:
For 25 years, Podonamu has been a restaurant specializing in spicy mudskipper stew, one of the main southern island dishes.
Spicy Mudskipper, a food that lives only in clean tidal flats and is difficult to access due to its small population, is rich in amino acids and taurine and has been called "sea beef" since ancient times. In particular, it is a stamina health food that people of all ages can enjoy because it is rich in unsaturated fatty acids and is effective in antioxidant action, skin beauty, and liver function improvement. On top of that, the Korean table setting with freshly cooked pot rice and hand-torn raw kimchi is a pleasant taste that reminds people of their hometown's home-cooked meal. In addition, there are various dishes and foods, such as 4-year-old kimchi, skate, pork, kimchi combo, and octopus’ pancake, so you can enjoy the excellent taste of the mainland of Namdo no matter which menu you choose.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Pyeongyangok
short_description: Pyeongyangok, with its clear and deep chicken bone soup, represents Seodaemun. The CEO has been boiling chicken soup for the second generation in a cauldron in the traditional way inherited from his mother. Every day at 3:00 am, the day begins by adding water to the cauldron. This is because the first step is to boil the medicinal ingredients, the second is to boil the chicken bones and chicken, and the third is to boil everything with additional water. That way, the broth in the cauldron blends with the well-boiled native chicken to create the best taste. The CEO also believes that all ingredients purchased on the day will be sold out on the same day, maintaining the food's freshness.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Elysee Bakery
short_description: Elysee Bakery is a bakery specialty store that mobilized all the capabilities of national confectionery representative who entered the baking industry at 21 and has demonstrated competitiveness for 38 years. The founder, Choi Hyung-il, the 1st CEO, started as an assistant at Napoleon Confectionery and went up to the deputy head of production. In 2002, he obtained a Master’s of Confectionery Skills. He is a bakery expert who participated in the world competition as a member of the national confectionery team in 2011. Elysee Bakery consists of the main store and two branches. More than 200 bread and cookies created by constant baking and baking research are awaiting customers. All pieces of bread are made with high-quality ingredients such as wheat flour, rice, and animal cream, and the bakery has been certified as a trans-fat-safe bakery.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Samcheonpo Restaurant
short_description:
When the meat is placed on the heated stone plate, a pleasant smell catches the nose with light smoke and a sizzling sound. Samcheonpo Restaurant, named after Samcheonpo, the hometown of the founder's spouse, is a stone-grilled grilled pork belly restaurant that has maintained its tenacity by pursuing the taste of grilled pork belly that has not been imitated for 30 years. The founder’s spouse, who is in charge of the kitchen of Samcheonpo Restaurant, worked at restaurants serving items such as grilled pork galbi, ox bone soup, and ox knee soup for three years, learning the skills before starting the business. She has such a high level of cooking skills that she was recommended to become an assistant after completing the Sudo Culinary Institute as a top student. At first, it started as a spicy seafood stew restaurant, but soon after, it was changed to grilled pork belly. At that time, the owners came across stone grilling by chance and began to dig into it professionally. The main menu of Samcheonpo Restaurant is a thinly sliced stone-grilled frozen pork belly.
Stone-grilled frozen pork belly, which is different from the once famous low-priced imported frozen pork belly, is made from 60-90 kg female pigs that are not too big. When meat comes in, it is aged for 24 hours in the refrigerator, exposed to room temperature for a short time, then sliced thinly and rapidly cooled according to the temperature and season of the day. Like grilled pork belly, made through a complicated process, their secret kimchi is also made systematically by measuring and reconciling all seasonings without adding salted fish. The tradition of Samcheonpo Restaurant, made with excellent cooking skills, has been passed down to the son, who has been involved in the management for six years.

title: Ham’s brot
short_description: Since 1999, Korea's Confectionery Master No. 8 has been in business and is famous for its bouquet cakes. It is a holy place for bakery pilgrims and a bakery that retains the personality of an old neighborhood bakery. The bakery uses naturally fermented seeds rather than yeast to make healthy bread. The owner, an unrivaled cake decorator, has the skill to add Korean flowers as decorations. If you want to see more than just a cake, but a work of art that gives you a glimpse of Korean beauty, a visit is recommended.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Seomjingang Minmul Jangeo
short_description:
Since its opening in 1984, Seomjingang Minmul Jangeo has been serving the best eel dishes and offering the best service for over 40 years. It is an emblematic restaurant in Suyu-dong, Gangbuk-gu. All ingredients are sourced directly from the production area, and quality and freshness are controlled. The whole eel is supplied, and when an order comes in, fresh fish are taken out and cooked with a sauce and marinade for 10 hours with fresh vegetables and herbs according to a unique secret method. The side dishes are also handmade daily with domestic ingredients, adding to the richness.
The secret to Seomjingang Minmul Jangeo’s long-lasting appreciation is that it provides friendly customer service, such as handwritten letters to guests who make reservations, while sparing no extra services for regular customers.

title: [Baeknyeon-gage] Chungsoojang
short_description:
Chungsoojang, which opened in 1984, is the best restaurant in Jeongneung. Chungsoojang’s main dish is, without a doubt, ‘chungsoo grilled pork galbi.’ The grilled pork galbi cooking and eating methods are different from usual. The meat is usually marinated in seasoning, which softens the original texture and flavor.
To preserve the meat’s texture and taste, Chungsoojang grills it immediately without marinating it in a special 'black sauce.' The grilled meat is then dipped into that 'black sauce' and eaten. This sauce can only be enjoyed at Chungsoojang. The salty and somewhat spicy taste gently stimulates the palate, and the sweetness and bitterness linger tantalizingly in the mouth. The crisp texture of raw meat, the rich local flavor, and the subtle taste of seasoning have been loved by many generations.

title: Sool Market Gunja Main Branch
short_description: This liquor store, operated by Sool Market, an online shopping mall for traditional liquor, is the largest and boasts the largest number of traditional liquor bottles. There is a bar in the basement where you can immediately drink the purchased traditional liquor. The slogan ‘Bring your food’ aims to be a free drinking space where outside food can be brought in.

title: Bistro MEXI
short_description:
BistroMEXI sets a captivating atmosphere with its blue, emerald hues evoking the Caribbean Sea, energized by vibrant red tones symbolizing the passion of Latin America and drawing inspiration from Aztec patterns. Amidst this ambiance, a 10-meter-wide large-scale media wall displays NFT artists’ works, providing a unique experience of a Mexican tapas lounge where tradition and modernity harmoniously coexist.
 
"Step into a Vibrant Latin Vibe"
With three sides adorned with floor-to-ceiling glass, BistroMEXI offers a refreshing sense of openness, capturing the lively ambiance of Itaewon Street at a glance, a view rarely experienced indoors. Here, you can immerse yourself in an exhilarating atmosphere created by renowned domestic and international DJs, blending Latin and African world music with genres like Pop, Hip Hop, and Disco.


"Authentic Mexican Tapas Experience"
Treat yourself to a delectable selection of over six diverse tacos and various flavorful fajitas, all prepared in the genuine Mexican tradition. At BistroMEXI, you can also enjoy a creative twist on Caribbean cocktails and savor high-quality, rare non-alcoholic concoctions that are not easily found elsewhere. Additionally, we proudly offer the country's largest selection of tequila and mezcal, providing you with a distinctive and exclusive experience that can only be found at BistroMEXI.

title: Café SangGuk
short_description: Café SangGuk is a roastery café that roasts its own beans, offering drip coffee and a variety of latte art. The café, built by remodeling an old vintage-style house, harmonizes beautifully with the serene atmosphere of the neighborhood. Located next to Changdeokgung Palace, it offers a wonderful view to enjoy while having coffee. Pets are allowed on the first floor, and the rooftop overlooking Changdeokgung Palace is highly recommended.

title: Yonggi Susan
short_description: Located in Garak Mall, Yonggi Susan offers the freshest seasonal sashimi. Guests can enjoy premium assorted seasonal sashimi, various live fish sashimi, king crab, snow crab, and more. The restaurant can be very crowded during weekend dining hours, so it is recommended to visit outside of peak hours to reduce waiting time. Takeout and delivery are also available.

title: Aftertaste
short_description: Aftertaste chooses freely scattered incompleteness over elaborately polished forms, and empty spaces where others' minds can permeate over densely packed completeness. Operating as both a cafe and a bar simultaneously with a modern wood-tone atmosphere, it can be enjoyed as a cafe during the day and a bar at night. Both coffee and alcoholic beverages can be comfortably ordered without any time restrictions.

title: Yena Tteokbang
short_description: Located within Gyeongdong Market, Yena Tteokbang specializes in Yeonggwang mugwort rice cakes (mositteok). The sweet fillings come in two flavors—red bean and black sesame—and are not overly sugary, making them popular with customers of all ages. Freshly made tteok is sold daily, and the shop bustles with visitors every time a new batch comes out. If you’re planning to visit Gyeongdong Market, be sure to try this as a tasty snack.

title: Bricksand Yeouido Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: ium 1966
short_description: ium 1966 is a café that has transformed an old hanok built in 1966 into a space filled with vintage charm. The original wooden beams, traditional fireplace, courtyard, and wooden porch have been preserved, allowing visitors to experience the tranquil ambiance of an old hanok. The café is adorned with vintage items such as old speakers, record players, cauldrons, and jars, providing plenty of interesting sights. The café features various harmoniously designed spaces, from the courtyard to the attic and basement, making it an excellent spot for capturing photos full of Korean charm. Traditional food and beverages include lotus flower tea with lotus leaves, manggae tteok (rice cake), and Jeju mugwort red bean bread. Located in the trendy Hongdae area, ium 1966 offers a warm and authentic experience of Korean beauty.

title: KERVAN Bakery & Cafe
short_description: A little piece of Turkey in Itaewon. Enjoying authentic Turkish desserts with tea and coffee gives you the feeling of traveling to Turkey itself. They also sell baklava and lokum, which are hard to find in Seoul, making them perfect souvenirs during your trip.

title: Parole & Langue
short_description: Parole & Langue is a famous dessert café in Yeonnam-dong known for its square signature pies. The café, created by renovating a house on the edge of Yeonnam-dong, exudes a cozy and modest charm. There is a waiting line, and a reservation system is available with options in English, Chinese, and Japanese. Experience the happiness that comes from the perfect layers within each pie.

title: Pastel Coffee Works
short_description:
Established in 2011 as a 10-square-meter small café, Pastel Coffee Works became a specialized coffee company, focusing solely on delicious coffee and expertise.
They taste coffees from around the world and meticulously research roasting profiles to deliver excellent coffee. They strive for artisan roasting, completing their works with delicate and refined techniques rather than uniform mass production.

title: Bricksand Gangnam Station Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: SEOUL-IYA
short_description: This casual Korean restaurant reinterprets Korean cuisine through Halal food, creating a place where you can deeply experience the harmony of Malaysian and Korean flavors and culture. Its signature dish is Chicken Kimchi Jjim—slow-braised chicken with kimchi in a rich, spicy sauce. The dish carries a warm, home-cooked flavor that reflects both care and comfort.

title: Cafe Kakariko
short_description: Walking through Changsin-dong Toy and Stationery Market, you can spot Cafe Kakariko, which stands out from the exterior with its piles of cute plush toys. The interior is decorated with Ghibli sensibilities, making it a charming themed cafe that sells various props centered around capybara plushies. The cafe space is somewhat small, and ordering one menu item per person is mandatory when using a table.

title: Chamasineun Teul Chatteul
short_description: At the traditional teahouse specialty shop Chamasineun Teul, you can enjoy a variety of Korean style teas. As befits a traditional teahouse, seating is arranged with floor tables, and enjoying traditional tea at tables with visible wood grain allows you to feel the atmosphere of the hanok more deeply. It mainly sells Korean traditional teas and fruit teas, and there are snack menus that go well with tea.

title: Café Grey Lab
short_description: Located in Hapjeong, Grey Lab is a popular hotspot known as one of Seoul’s famous cherry blossom cafés. During the spring season, visitors can enjoy not only coffee but also a variety of drinks and desserts on the terrace with a view of cherry blossoms. A must-do is taking a photo in the photo zone on the second floor, surrounded by blossoms. As it’s a popular cherry blossom spot, there is a time limit of two hours per group to ensure smooth use of the space.

title: Undebt
short_description: Undebt is a highly atmospheric cafe that has gracefully inherited its unique mood into its interior space, aiming to enjoy nature within this city based on the natural environment. From the unique interior of Hanok and cave concepts, the texture of wood, natural lighting, exotic carpets, perfectly leveled music, and even the small stones and props placed in the corners of the stairs. We hope you enjoy comfort in this space, where every detail embraces the warmth of a relaxed life without being excessive.

title: Little India Seoul
short_description: This is a renowned restaurant in Itaewon that delivers authentic Indian curry flavors, with tender, savory tandoori chicken and rich, flavorful chicken curry as signature dishes. Run directly by locals, it carefully recreates the authentic taste of India.

title: Parc Hannam Main Branch
short_description: “Parc” means “park” in Catalan, the language spoken in Barcelona, Spain. The restaurant’s name reflects its wish to share the relaxed feeling of resting in a park amidst the busy city life, expressed through thoughtfully prepared Korean home-style dishes. Using no artificial seasonings, Parc follows “mom’s recipes,” cooking with the same ingredients found in everyday Korean homes. The result is sincere, hearty Korean meals that feel like home cooking.

title: FIKEE
short_description:
Fikee is a book cafe located on Seosulla-gil. It is operated as a “base camp for explorers who enjoy books and drinks” and provides a small hideout in the city to visitors (finders) who visit Fikee. Visitors can freely explore the books and stories scattered throughout the space while enjoying beverages and cakes. In this beautiful place, with a view of the stone walls outside the large windows, embark on an everyday life adventure.

finders keepers, FIKEE
"Finders keepers" is an English proverb that means "the person who finds something owns it."

title: SUNNY BOWL
short_description: Located near Ewha Womans Univ. Station, this vegan restaurant embraces a nature-friendly approach to cooking. Drawing inspiration from Asian and Italian cuisines, it offers healthy yet flavorful vegan dishes made with an abundance of ingredients such as vegetables, tofu, tempeh, and quinoa.

title: Jungang Galchi Restaurant
short_description: This is a Korean restaurant specializing in braised hairtail fish located in the hairtail alley of Namdaemun Market, which has gained much love after being featured multiple times on TV food programs. The braised hairtail fish with tender, meaty flesh in a lightly simmered broth is the restaurant's signature dish, making it a must-recommend restaurant for those visiting Namdaemun Market

title: Hanok Seosulla-gil Branch
short_description: Hanok Seosulla-gil Branch is a fusion Korean dining establishment that introduces unique dishes interpreting familiar ingredients with the sensibility of Hanok. Lay down the weight of everyday life for a moment and experience the complete joy of delicious food and traditional liquor.

title: Teumari Cafe
short_description: Nestled along Seosulla-gil beside the Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path, Café Teumari is a hidden gem. It is a delightful hanok café and wine bar, remodeled from a Joseon-era hanok. This cozy yet unique space exudes a rich and inviting atmosphere. The café’s first and second floors are designed with warm wooden accents that create a relaxed ambiance. Climbing up the narrow, steep stairs reveals a rooftop with a breathtaking view of the Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path, perfect for soaking in the surroundings. At Café Teumari, guests can enjoy carefully brewed coffee, desserts, beer, wine, and light snacks. This makes it an ideal spot for relaxed conversations with friends, loved ones, or family. Enjoy the cozy, nostalgic atmosphere and create memorable moments in this unique setting.

title: Bongijeon
short_description:
Makgeolli(Korean rice wine) and jeon (Koreanstyle pancakes) have long been a beloved pairing in Korean culture, especially 

after a hike. Many hikers stop by for a drink and a warm bite on their way down the mountain. If you're coming down from

 Gwanaksan toward Seoul National University Station, Bongijeon is a great spot to unwind. The menu offers a wide variety of

 jeon, along with an impressive selection of makgeolli, hearty side dishes, and hot soups.

title: Sobamae Nigo
short_description: Drawing on 35 years of life in Japan, this restaurant brings authentic Japanese soba to the table. Known among enthusiasts for its hand-pulled noodles and deeply flavorful broth, it has become a beloved spot in Seongsu. The signature dish is kamo seiro, featuring tender duck with a savory, umami-rich taste.

title: Anthracite Yeonhui Branch
short_description: Anthracite Yeonhui, a café in Yeonhui-dong named after "smokeless coal," features an interior with a striking sense of depth. The design contrasts light and dark elements, leading you from a dim hallway into a bright space with a large, floor-to-ceiling window. The spacious second floor, furnished with a long communal table and plenty of seating, provides an ideal setting for working. In addition to a selection of desserts and coffee, the café offers wine and herbal teas. Drinks are served directly to your table, eliminating the need for buzzers, and convenient parking is also available.

title: Cosmos Snack Bar
short_description: This snack bar, which has remained in the same spot for over 40 years near Gusan Station, is cherished as a nostalgic place for local students. Its sweet and spicy instant tteokbokki evokes school memories. The retro interior preserves the old charm, offering nostalgia for adults and novelty for younger generations. In the 1990s, singer Kim Jang-hoon reportedly played music requests from customers as a DJ here.

title: Soba Lab Sinchon
short_description: This restaurant is renowned for soba, carefully prepared with in-house milling and noodle making. While it offers classics such as zaru soba, its true charm lies in the unique soba dishes it has newly developed. Highlights include the perilla oil soba, made with nutty oil pressed directly at a local mill, and the flat soba, a one-of-a-kind creation first developed here.

title: Titch
short_description: Titch is a quiet cafe near Hongjecheon Stream known for its delicious sandwiches. The signature menu includes the Onion Chutney Sandwich and a Vegan Avocado Sandwich, available for vegetarians. Its proximity to Hongjecheon Stream makes it an ideal spot for packing sandwiches for a picnic or enjoying a walk after a meal.

title: Sinrakwon
short_description: The family business began when the first grandfather opened a Chinese restaurant called Anrakjeong. The second-generation father took over and operated the restaurant, and the third-generation son changed his name to "Sillakwon" and continued his family business. the third-generation owner of the business, had a splendid career as a Chinese chef for the president and a Chinese chef at a famous hotel in Korea until he took over the business from his father eight years ago. Stir-fried Jjamppong Sillakmyeon is a popular menu, and Nurungji-tang Meal-kit made by Sillakwon is sold at the supermarket.

title: Curry in
short_description: An Indian curry restaurant run directly by an Indian owner, it offers authentic flavors in a cozy, home-like atmosphere. Start your meal with banana pudding, then choose from a variety of curries with adjustable spice levels to suit your taste. The restaurant is Halal-certified, ensuring a comfortable and worry-free dining experience.

title: Jeju Mihyang Haejang
short_description: Located inside Gyeongdong Market, this popular eatery is famous for its rich hangover soup made with a deeply boiled broth, generous amounts of blood pudding (seonji), and fresh napa cabbage greens (ugeoji). Loved by local vendors, neighborhood residents, and even MZ generation visitors to Cheongnyangni, this spot offers signature Jeju-style dishes such as Momguk, Bomalkuk, and Jeju-style beef hangover soup. Each bowl is filled to the brim, offering not only a generous portion but also a comforting warmth that fills you up from the inside. Come experience the taste for yourself!

title: GMH Dabang
short_description: Located in Sangsu-dong, GMH Dabang offers over 200 carefully selected wines, paired with delectable dishes, enhancing your special occasions with meaningful experiences. With meticulous tasting sessions, they provide detailed guidance on wine characteristics. Even beginners can gradually find joy in wine appreciation after a few visits. During the day, it operates as a café and at night, it transforms into a saloon, making it a favorite spot for various Hongdae artists. The quiet ambiance also makes it an ideal wine bar for dates.

title: Gongneung Chicken Hanmari
short_description: A well-known spot in Sinchon, this restaurant has gained a reputation among international visitors for its Dakhanmari (Whole Chicken Stew). The dish’s charm lies in savoring tender chicken dipped in sauce and finishing with the rich, flavorful broth. To complete the experience, it’s a must to add noodles or porridge at the end of the meal.

title: Gabongnu
short_description: Gabongru is a place where you can experience the charm of Korean-style Chinese cuisine, boasting over 50 years of history. It features a simple interior and a nostalgic atmosphere reminiscent of the past. The food generously uses ingredients and emphasizes a taste that stays true to the basics. Their fried meat—a dish rarely found in other Chinese restaurants—is Gabongru's signature menu item, seasoned with salt and pepper to offer a light and clean flavor. The taste of their jjambbong (spicy seafood noodle soup), tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork), and jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) is also exceptional.

title: Avelop Hongdae Flagship
short_description:
Avelop, a coined term from 'advance' or 'art' and 'develop', reflects the meaning of continuously advancing while deepening artistic sensibility. Located in a house designed in 1972 by Kim Chung Up, a representative figure of modern Korean architecture in the 20th century, the space has been sensitively remodeled.


Preserving as much as possible the stories carried by the original walls, windows, and floors, the building has been modernly reinterpreted. Operated as a bakery café, all bread is baked fresh daily, and leftovers are discarded at the end of the day.

title: Byeolmi Gopchang
short_description: Located near the Seochon food alley, Byeolmi Gopchang is a popular gopchang (grilled tripe) restaurant where locals often line up early, making it a must-visit area. Featured on the well-known Korean food show "Heo Young-man's Baekban Journey," it has solidified its reputation as one of Seochon's top dining spots. The restaurant offers a single dish: stir-fried pork gopchang with vegetables, with the option to add fried rice. The flavor is mildly spicy with a satisfying kick, as the gochujang (Korean chili paste) deeply infuses the pork intestines, making it irresistibly delicious. Pairing it with a cold beer or soju completes the perfect meal. With only about five tables inside, arriving before peak hours is best to avoid long waits.

title: Lowkey
short_description: Lowkey is a Seoul-based roastery specializing in specialty coffee. Since 2010, it has been roasting and supplying beans and operates four Seoul stores. Prioritizing quality, Lowkey roasts small batches to ensure that coffee is served at its freshest and most flavorful. The company is dedicated to delivering each coffee bean's full taste and story. Stop by one of their locations to enjoy Lowkey's best coffee. Lowkey also offers various products, including drip bags for convenient brewing, all the necessary coffee tools, snacks that pair perfectly with coffee, and a selection of apparel that reflects the brand's unique vibe. Lowkey’s bean subscription service is worth exploring for true coffee enthusiasts.

title: Rust Bakery
short_description: Rust Bakery is the most famous bakery cafe in Mullae dong. The interior space, remodeled from a factory, features an industrial atmosphere that preserves traces of its factory days. More than thirty kinds of bakery items such as cakes, puddings, and pastries are prepared, along with coffee beverages and seasonal drinks that change every season. We invite you to enjoy delicious cakes and bread baked directly in the store.

title: New Delhi
short_description:
This authentic Indian restaurant creates its flavors without artificial seasonings, using only healthy, high-quality natural ingredients. The cozy, comfortable interior accented with Indian-inspired décor makes simply stepping inside feel like a

special experience. A wide-ranging menu covers curries, tandoori dishes, appetizers, salads, and soups, along with thoughtfully prepared set menus.

title: Dwaeji Gomtang HAU Seongsu Main Branch
short_description: The name HAU means summer rain and expresses the refreshing feeling Koreans associate with being restored and revived, similar to the cool sensation of a summer shower. The restaurant offers clear pork gomtang made from pork broth slowly simmered at low temperature and high pressure, as well as Pyeongyang style mul naengmyeon and pork cheek seaweed soup. As suggested by the name HAU, the warm gomtang refreshes the body while the cold noodles provide a cooling experience that helps overcome summer heat.

title: Unique Cafe 'Tiki Room'
short_description: Tiki Room is a unique interactive cafe with a 'Bungeoppang Tycoon' concept where you can directly make and enjoy Bungeoppang (fish-shaped pastry) in Sinsa-dong. You can experience the process of completing your own warm Bungeoppang by pouring the batter into the mold, choosing your desired fillings, and baking it yourself. Going beyond a cafe where you simply enjoy beverages and desserts, its greatest charm is feeling the fun of making and the joy of eating together. Since you can also take photos in the cutely conceptualized space, it is well-suited for a special date with a friend or lover, or a family outing course with a child.

title: Wangjjanggu Restaurant
