short_description: Opened in 1986, Wangjjanggu Restaurant is the fourth oldest eatery on Bukchon Gyedong‑gil, a historic street that has preserved its position over the years. Starting as a snack bar, Wangjjanggu Restaurant has traces of time scattered throughout the premises. There, you can enjoy not only hearty stew dishes but also taste Korean snacks such as sweet potato stew, fish cakes, and sikhye (Sweet Rice Punch). Wangjjanggu Restaurant's signature dish is Gogumamattang (Deep-fried and Sugar-Glazed Sweet Potatoes), which pairs excellently with freshly cooked ramen. It has been in business for 40 years and offers a taste of traditional Korean flavors.

title: Hongdae Dakgalbi
short_description: With a tradition of 30 years, Shin Migyeong Hongdae Dakgalbi is a must visit restaurant in Seoul that is famous in Hongdae, Seongsu, and Yeonnam dong. With a 30 year secret recipe and cooking on an extra large cast iron griddle, it offers deep and rich flavors. As the original restaurant of the most famous cheese fondue dakgalbi in Seoul, it is an essential destination representing Korean gourmet culture. You can experience authentic K Dakgalbi with the aroma of the Maillard reaction completed on an 86 kg cast iron griddle. The signature menus, cheese fondue dakgalbi and snowflake cheese fried rice, are the courses most loved by foreign visitors. With English and Chinese service and an official website supporting nine languages in eight countries, it is very convenient for overseas tourists.

title: Dosan Butchery Cheongdam Main Branch
short_description: Dosan Butchery's Main Branch is Dosan's representative restaurant that considers the essence of meat as the number one priority. Experience meat’s sticky and condensed taste through Dosan Butchery's systematic aging process!

title: Namsan Sul Club
short_description: Namsan Sul Club is a traditional liquor bar operated by a foreign owner, where you can experience 100 different types of Korean liquor by the glass, curated by a certified traditional liquor sommelier. Recommendations are tailored to each guest’s preferences, so even those unfamiliar with traditional liquor can enjoy it without hesitation. Each drink is served in a cup that best matches the liquor, offering the added delight of appreciating unique Korean drinking vessels.

title: Imi Coffee
short_description: At this café, you can select your favorite dessert, and a perfectly paired coffee will be prepared for you. The roaster expertly identifies the flavors and aromas of the coffee while the pastry chef crafts desserts that complement it. The barista then prepares the ideal coffee to match the dessert. Featuring seasonal fruits, the desserts are meticulously crafted with attention to sweetness, ensuring guests enjoy them at their best. The clean and atmospheric setting enhances the experience, making the pairing of desserts and coffee even more enjoyable. Many customers become regulars, delighted by the experience of tasting seasonal desserts. Given its popularity, reservations are essential.

title: Sulbing
short_description: Sulbing is a traditional Korean dessert café brand that offers a variety of Korean-style desserts throughout the year. Its signature menu includes various types of bingsu (shaved ice dessert) topped with traditional ingredients or seasonal fruits. The sweet and refreshing bingsu, made with shaved milk ice, is a summer delicacy that helps momentarily forget the heat. Among them, the Injeolmi Sulbing, which includes nutty soybean powder and chewy rice cakes, is a bestseller that is popular with people of all ages. Besides bingsu, the café also sells a variety of Korean desserts such as cheese garaetteok (rice cake stick), kkul hotteok (honey-filled Korean pancake), and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cake). This dessert cafe captivates Koreans and foreigners with its traditional, creative, and popular desserts.

title: Doyajip
short_description:
Doyajip is a pork specialty restaurant built in a space that was once a family home for over 40 years. The name "Doyajip" combines "doyaji," an old Korean word for pig, with "jip," meaning house.


Though famous for its samgyeopsal in Yongsan, the signature dishes here are bone-in pork belly and pork neck. Each cut is full of rich juices and offers the true flavor of quality pork. You can also order individual cuts à la carte, and corkage service is available for a fee.

title: Scoff Seochon
short_description: Scoff Seochon is a British bakery cafe famous for its scones. You can order bakery items made directly in the store on the first floor and taste them on the second floor while taking in the atmosphere of the Seochon alley. The 2nd branch is located near the 1st Seochon branch (main branch), and if both the 1st and 2nd branches are full, you can enjoy Scoff's desserts at Hyoja Cafe, where outside food is permitted.

title: NOR
short_description: NOR, located in Seoul, is the first restaurant to offer an innovative dining experience where media art projection mapping and crab dining harmoniously blend. At this place, customers are welcomed with a unique 'LIFE' concept that allows them to embark on a transcendent journey, from the rising morning sun to the creation of the Milky Way. We recommend it to those who seek a unique gastronomic journey, offering a different culinary experience.

title: Baekpal (108)
short_description: Baekpal is a bar located at the end of Huam-dong, Yongsan, beneath the 108 steps of Haebangchon. It sells both coffee and alcoholic beverages, and a wide variety of coffee, whiskey, wine, beer, and cocktails are prepared. With the large windows opened wide, you can view the Huam-dong rotary and Namsan Tower at a glance, so we encourage you to sit by the window and properly feel the unique, relaxed sensibility of Haebangchon.

title: Eoe Seoul
short_description: This dessert café, located in Bukchon, offers desserts made with famous ingredients from various regions of Korea. The interior design features light blue colors, reflecting traditional Korean aesthetics. The café's signature menu item, the "Giwa Financier," is inspired by Korean ingredients and introduces new flavors each season. Special treats include the "Eoe Coffee," made with aged barley milk, and seasonal teas.

title: Proper Coffee Bar 2nd Branch
short_description: Located near Bangi Station, the second branch of Proper Coffee Bar is a beloved spot for brunch and bakery delights. The cafe offers a variety of bakery items and brunch menus, along with a daily soup lineup that changes with the seasons, allowing you to choose dishes that suit your taste. The spacious store and clean interior are standout features, and attentive service is provided throughout. The large terrace seating area outside is particularly popular when the weather is warm. Additionally, their cold brew is highly recommended for coffee enthusiasts. Due to its popularity, especially on weekends and holidays, note that the dining time is limited to two hours.

title: Andongjip Sonkalguksu
short_description:
Andongjip Sonkalguksi is a renowned kalguksu (noodle soup) restaurant located in Gyeongdong Market, run by Chef Kim Mi-ryeong, who became famous as Auntie Omakase #1 on the Netflix cooking competition show Culinary Class Wars. The restaurant is known for its unique dough, blending 40% soybean flour with regular flour, rolled thin, and hand-cut to create soft noodles and a flavorful, aromatic broth.

 

 The signature dish is handmade kalguksu, served in a clear anchovy-based broth with fresh cabbage, providing a clean and delicate taste. Customers can adjust the flavor to their liking by adding soy sauce, extra spicy chili peppers, and minced garlic. Cabbage leaves served as a side dish can be used to make wraps with soybean paste and millet rice, offering a unique and flavorful experience.

 

 In addition to kalguksu, popular dishes include chewy boiled pork slices and crispy cabbage pancakes. Enjoy a memorable and satisfying meal at Andongjip Sonkalguksi, which brings the best of Korean cuisine to your table with its rich, traditional flavors.

title: Zoosindang
short_description: Zoosindang is a uniquely themed cocktail bar based on the 12 zodiac animals. It is an oriental speakeasy bar that originated in Sindang-dong. The name Sindang-dong originally meant “a neighborhood that worships gods,” as many shamans settled around Gwanghuimun Gate, though its Chinese characters have changed over time. This historical and cultural significance has been reinterpreted through the 12 zodiac animals, creating a mysterious and enchanting atmosphere unique to Zoosindang. At Zoosindang, you can enjoy 12 Zodiac Signature Cocktails made with traditional Korean liquor and various whiskies. The bar also offers distinctive dining menus, developed through extensive research and experimentation with Korean ingredients and cooking techniques, embodying Zoosindang's unique style.

title: HANCOOK
short_description:
HANCOOK is a Korean restaurant located at the observation deck of Namsan Tower, offering an unforgettable dining experience with panoramic views of Seoul. The large windows blend nature and urban scenery, creating a serene and tranquil atmosphere away from the city's hustle and bustle. 

The restaurant's signature dish is the premium hanu (Beef), grilled to perfection over charcoal and layered with the delicate flavors of smoked wood chips and pine needles. In addition, HANCOOK offers various modern and elegantly plated courses that showcase the unique charm of Korean cuisine. This restaurant is a must-visit for tasting HANCOOK's distinct ambiance and exquisite dishes.

title: Durga Gangnam
short_description:
Durga has been sharing the charm of authentic Indian and Nepalese cuisine in Seoul for over 20 years, and this is its Gangnam branch. While staying

true to local flavors, the dishes are not overly spiced, making them enjoyable for all ages. Just a five-minute walk from Gangnam Station, the spacious and comfortable interior makes it an easy spot to visit.

title: The Makan
short_description: A Malaysian bistro led by chefs from five-star hotels in Kuala Lumpur, it brings authentic flavors to life with the same ingredients and cooking methods used locally—earning a spot in the Blue Ribbon Survey, one of Korea’s leading restaurant guides. The resort-like interior and tranquil view of Jamsil’s streets create a relaxing atmosphere.

title: Namsan memories
short_description: Namsan Gieok is a Japanese restaurant featuring a wonderful panoramic view of Namsan Tower unfolding above the rooftop. Leave unforgettable memories in a space with a warm mood and a rooftop overlooking Namsan Tower at Namsan Gieok, located at the highest point of Haebangchon.

title: Sultan Kebab
short_description: As the first kebab restaurant to establish itself in Itaewon, this place has been beloved for its consistent taste and dedication over many years. Visitors can casually enjoy authentic Turkish cuisine including chicken and lamb kebabs, as well as falafel, and it is now considered one of Itaewon's representative halal food destinations.

title: Art Sushi
short_description: This sushi restaurant lives up to its name, offering flavors as artful as its carefully prepared rice and fresh ingredients. It also features a cozy atmosphere that makes it welcoming for solo diners, including travelers. If you’re near Gangnam Station and looking for high-quality sushi at a reasonable price, this spot comes highly recommended.

title: Nirvana
short_description: The dishes here, prepared using traditional Indian methods, are especially beloved by those longing for authentic Indian flavors. Among them, the butter chicken curry is renowned for its rich and satisfying taste.

title: The Rabbit
short_description: This is a special spot where you can enjoy a variety of desserts made entirely with plant-based ingredients. A wide selection of cream cheese flavors—such as onion, fig, maple pecan, and lemon-dill—pairs with bagels in styles like Italian, corn crumble, and mashed potato, offering endless combinations and the joy of discovering new tastes.

title: Staff Picks
short_description: Located in Seochon, Staff Picks is a café known for its natural and beautiful outdoor terrace. Perched on a high vantage point, it offers a panoramic view of Jongno’s streets. The giant ginkgo tree in the garden is a popular photo spot for visitors. In autumn, many return to capture the tree’s golden leaves. Famous for its rich-flavored coffee and sweet pound cake, the café also showcases a variety of charming knick-knacks. Since it doubles as a concept store, guests can browse retro-themed items while enjoying the café’s atmosphere. On the second floor, a cozy bookstore is a great spot to explore during your visit.

title: Aqua Garden Cafe
short_description: Aqua Garden Cafe is a distinctive venue that combines an aquarium with a cafe. It offers visitors the chance to enjoy coffee while admiring the underwater scenery. Large tanks that vividly recreate a natural aquatic ecosystem surround the cafe, providing visitors with a rich visual experience from anywhere in the venue. The tanks, decorated with driftwood and aquatic plants, house dozens of different fish species, and the sound of flowing water and lighting create a mysterious atmosphere. It is a popular spot where people of all ages can relax and unwind. The cafe also provides high chairs for children. Additionally, there is a small shop where visitors can purchase fish, aquarium supplies, and mini terrariums. Since the entrance fee is included in the price of the beverages, it is relatively more expensive than other cafes.

title: Public Garden
short_description: Public Garden is a hidden rooftop brunch café in the heart of Seoul. Tucked away in an alley among the fabric shops of Gwangjang Market, a staircase leads you to this bright and sunny brunch spot. Here, you’ll find delicious dishes like sandwiches, pasta, arancini, roasted chicken, and a selection of quality beers and wines. The café also offers a wide range of menu items and desserts, providing a moment of relaxation for city dwellers. As the afternoon sunsets, the rooftop view becomes even more beautiful, making it well worth a visit.

title: Durga Gwanghwamun
short_description:
This restaurant has been delivering the rich flavors of authentic Indian and Nepali cuisine in Seoul for over 20 years. With more than 40 carefully

prepared dishes crafted by local chefs, it has long been cherished for its aromatic spices and diverse tastes. In a cozy atmosphere, guests can enjoy both the exotic ambiance and a comforting meal.

title: Mirrorroom, a Mirror Hanok
short_description:
The Mirrorroom, a hanok cafe in Samcheong-dong, offers a contemporary take on the 100-year-old birthplace of the renowned artist Jang Seung-eop. The spacious area preserves the traditional hanok rafters, while the outdoor terrace features a wooden veranda, providing a peaceful and authentic hanok ambiance. The cafe's most striking feature is its mirrored walls, which, paired with large windows framing lush greenery, create an airy and refreshing atmosphere. The lights reflecting off the mirrors in the evening produce a beautiful and distinctive visual experience.

Aligned with its nature-inspired ethos, the cafe serves a menu made from fresh, natural ingredients. Guests can savor a selection of fruit teas and wines, such as apple tea, plum tea, and omija tea, along with dessert options like apple tree croffles.

title: Jongno Seonbiok
short_description: You can enjoy delicious homemade dwaeji galbi (Spareribs) from fresh meat directly delivered from the Gwangju slaughterhouse in Jeollanam-do, along with naengmyeon (Cold Buckwheat Noodles) made from freshly kneaded and prepared noodles. The outdoor seating along the stone walls of Tapgol Park attracts those wanting to soak in the unique atmosphere of Jongno. Indoor seats are also available for a comfortable dining experience, even during summer.

title: Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town
short_description: Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town, located in Jung-gu, Seoul, is known as the birthplace of jeukseok tteokbokki, a style of rice cake dish that is cooked and eaten directly at the table. Beginning with the restaurant opened by Grandma Ma Bok-rim in 1953, the entire alley became lined with specialty tteokbokki restaurants. It is a place where visitors can experience the history and tradition of Korean street food culture while enjoying a variety of flavors and nostalgic charm. Variations such as seafood, jjajang (black bean sauce), and dakbal (spicy chicken feet) tteokbokki are also available. Popular restaurants include Ma Bok-rim Tteokbokki, I Love Sindang-dong, and Samdae Halmeonne. Although the number of visitors has declined in recent years, it remains a well-known destination for street food lovers and tourists as one of Korea’s representative snack streets.

title: KERVAN Restaurant
short_description: This is a Turkish specialty restaurant where you can taste various traditional Turkish dishes including chicken shish kebab, lamb shish kebab, kaymak, pide, and hummus. The interior, delicately decorated with tiles imported from Turkey, adds an exotic atmosphere, and you can enjoy authentic Turkish flavors and culture together in a warm family restaurant setting.

title: ITAEWON KITCHEN
short_description: Located in Itaewon, this cozy retreat faithfully recreates authentic local flavors and is beloved by many locals. In particular, the koobideh kebab is praised for capturing the genuine taste of Iran.

title: DAWNING
short_description: This Yongridan-gil dessert cafe is genuinely passionate about cakes, crafting healthier and more delicious 100% handmade creations by baking preservative-free sponge layers in-house and using natural dairy cream with seasonal fresh fruits. Whole cake orders can be conveniently reserved in advance, with same-day reservations also available.

title: SLUNCH FACTORY
short_description: This restaurant offers a variety of vegan dishes inspired by both Italian and Korean cuisine. Designed for both vegetarians and general diners, it has been listed in the Blue Ribbon Survey—one of Korea’s leading restaurant guides—for seven consecutive years. It also develops eco-friendly meal kits, reflecting Hongdae’s youthful and creative spirit.

title: Vegan Kitchen
short_description: One of Seoul’s leading vegan restaurants, it features signature dishes such as light yet flavorful vegan stir-fried noodles and soft tofu rice served hot from the grill. With carefully selected ingredients and sincere preparation, it offers a healthy dining experience in a modern, relaxing setting.

title: Veganature
short_description: This spot serves delicious, satisfying desserts for those following a vegan diet. Its signature item is the Emmental Potato Cheese Rice Bagel, where the savory nuttiness of vegan cheese meets the shop’s secret potato filling. Pair it with a creamy oat milk–based vegan latte for a perfect match.

title: Temple Food-Specialized Restaurant  Balwoo Gongyang
short_description:
This is the only temple cuisine restaurant directly operated by the the Cultural Corps of Korean Buddhism. Based on traditional cooking methods,

it offers dishes that preserve the authentic flavors of temple cuisine, allowing visitors to experience the profound traditions and culture of temple food.

title: Chick By Chick Seolleung Station Branch
short_description: Chick By Chick is a fast-casual chicken brand where you can enjoy a variety of healthier chicken menu options at reasonable prices. They offer a menu consisting of direct-fired grilled chicken made from raw chicken thigh meat grilled over an open flame, burgers made with grilled King Prawn, ricebowls, and specialty chicken.

title: I.O MEAL
short_description: I.O MEAL utilizes seasonal ingredients to provide a healthy one-plate Japanese home-style table setting and various foods prepared with great care. In the morning, you can enjoy a meal while looking at the Gyeongui Line Forest Trail Park, and in the afternoon, you can enjoy Japanese liquor that pairs well with the dishes offered exclusively during the evening time.

title: chachaithe
short_description: Chachai Tea is a cozy teahouse in Hannam-dong where guests can enjoy a tea course paired with both Eastern and Western-style desserts. Unique confections, many of which are likely to be first-time experiences, are available and can also be purchased as gifts. A luxurious tea time experience in the tea room requires a reservation. On the second floor, an elegant display of teaware collected from Korea and abroad adds to the charm, making it an ideal spot for couples or friends seeking a special moment together.

title: DDP SPECIAL DUCK
short_description: This restaurant offers a half-and-half menu of grilled duck and duck soup, allowing you to enjoy both dishes in one meal. The grilled duck is a smoky, tender roast with crispy skin and juicy meat, while the duck soup features a rich broth and the delicate texture of duck meat.

title: Meoktong Nakji
short_description: Located near Yeongdeungpo Traditional Market, this restaurant specializes in octopus dishes. Its highlights include yeonpotang, a hot pot made with live octopus from the southern coast, and nakji bokkeum, stir-fried octopus with a spicy, chewy texture. For those seeking everyday Korean seafood cuisine loved by locals, this spot offers an authentic neighborhood experience

title: Picniq Seonyudo Hanok Branch
short_description: "Picniq" is a combination of "Picnic" and "Unique," expressing the wish that every moment spent here feels like a special picnic. The Seonyudo Hanok Branch is the main store of Picniq, established in 2018 by renovating an old hanok. This nearly 100-year-old hanok is one of the oldest in the Yeongdeungpo area. Here, you can enjoy sweet desserts in the quiet and serene atmosphere that only a hanok can offer, making for a peaceful and relaxing experience.

title: Teobangnae
short_description: This is called "Chungang University Cafe" and is a representative cafe in Heukseok-dong that has been flavored with siphon coffee since 1983. The interior of the 1980s is still the same, so it is impressive to see middle-aged people who were young at the time coexist with young people who wanted to experience the feeling of the era. Siphon Coffee is an old coffee brewing method that uses different roasting techniques for each coffee bean, so you can taste special coffee. You can feel the owner's love for his regular customers and his hard work of maintaining a low price for many years

title: Taetea Flagship Store
short_description: The Taetea Flagship Store offers a spacious and comfortable environment where you can brew and enjoy a variety of Da Yi Pu’erh teas using traditional tea tools such as gaiwan and zisha teapots. The store also sells Da Yi teas and tea utensils. Even if you are not familiar with tea brewing methods, the café staff will guide you through the techniques, making it easy for anyone to enjoy Pu’erh tea. In addition to the tea brewing menu, the café offers a range of unique beverages made with their custom espresso machine, including Kingpresso (a machine-pressed Pu’erh tea), tea ades, and tea smoothies. You can also indulge in Korean-style café desserts, such as milk tea and shaved ice.

title: Kwanho Yeouido
short_description:
Kwanho Yeouido specializes in premium Halal-certified lamb grilled to perfection over charcoal fire. Using only high-quality charcoal, it brings out

the smoky flavor of lamb at its best. The menu ranges from various cuts of grilled lamb to hot pots, fried dishes, and even lamb tartare, offering a truly

diverse dining experience.

title: The Kitchen Asia Daehak-ro
short_description: This is a restaurant where you can taste a diverse array of Indian cuisine. The signature dish is curry, where various spices are harmoniously blended to deliver deep and rich flavors. Through heartfelt Indian cooking, you can experience the authentic taste and culture of India.

title: H COFFEE ROASTERS SEOCHON
short_description: H COFFEE ROASTERS SEOCHON makes coffee that many people can relate to and enjoy every day. At the Seochon store, which boasts an interior that brings out the feel of a traditional Hanok while maintaining a modern touch and directly roasts specialty coffee, you can enjoy high-quality coffee beans and homemade desserts. Good balance, an unadorned and honest taste. Experience comfortable coffee that approaches you amicably.

title: Apgujeong Door to Door
short_description:
Door to Door is an all-day brunch café and wine bar specializing in Italian-style focaccia sandwiches, baked fresh in-house.

Located in the heart of Gangnam, Apgujeong Rodeo, it quickly became a beloved weekend spot for locals thanks to its open-style interior and outdoor seating.

By day, it operates as a brunch café offering focaccia sandwiches, healthy soups, freshly brewed coffee, and desserts. By night, it transforms into a stylish dining bar with ambient lighting and music, serving house-made tapas, wine, and beer.

It’s a true all-day dining space where your day can begin and end in one place.

title: RERE PLAY
short_description: Rereplay combines 'Replay' with an added 'Re', embodying the message that “if you live for yourself, the Earth becomes clean naturally.” The old inn has been transformed into a sensuous café, preserving its complex structure and adding elements of stone, soil, and wood to create a natural atmosphere. Alongside its eco-friendly ambiance, guests can enjoy specialty coffee, organic tea, and organic desserts.

title: Bittle’s Pizza Yeonnam
short_description:
Located at the end of the Gyeongui Line Forest Trail, also known as “Yeontral Park,” this Yeonnam-dong pizzeria features an outdoor terrace with a panoramic view of the park.


The exterior gives off an exotic vibe, and stepping inside feels like entering a trendy American shop.


It operates together with a neighboring liquor store called Beetle Beetle, and guests are free to use both spaces. Due to limited seating, table use is restricted to 2 hours for all guests.

title: Space K Nodeul
short_description:
Located on Nodeulseom Island in the Hangang River, Space K Nodeul is a place reborn as a media art cafe and complex cultural space by remodeling the old Noryangjin Water Intake Station.

You can feel the retro sensibility of the old water intake station itself, which bears the traces of time,

and because it is situated at a point overlooking the Hangang Bridge and Nodeulseom Island, you can appreciate a beautiful night view. In addition, media art programs and cultural events are held, transforming the space to be even more colorful.

title: Lounge Heeum
short_description: Café Lounge Heeum, Korea’s first fine drink omakase café, began as a project by artist Kim Jihee. Much like crafting an art piece, Lounge Heeum’s art brew omakase course is designed to offer connoisseurs a refined and meaningful experience. Behind the art studio, the space has been transformed into a modern interpretation of a 19th-century European train, inspired by Kim Jihee's artwork 'The Trunk Series.' Bringing the spirit of a journey into the unknown through taste, aroma, art, and atmosphere, Lounge Heeum delivers a dynamic and curated experience with each season. With a blend of elegance and freedom, Lounge Heeum invites guests to leave the mundane and savor a truly memorable moment.

title: Gosame Sinchon
short_description: This grilled fish restaurant has been a longtime favorite in Sinchon for 20 years. Fish grilled over an open flame sizzles to perfection, releasing a burst of juicy flavor with every bite. In addition to grilled fish, it offers a variety of Korean set meals and other dishes, making it a beloved spot not only for local residents but also for visitors to Seoul.

title: Mongol Nomadic
short_description: A rare Mongolian restaurant in Seoul, it features an interior reminiscent of a traditional ger, evoking the feeling of a trip to Mongolia. Along with khushuur, the famous Mongolian fried dumpling, tsuivan—Mongolian home-style stir-fried noodles—is also a must-try. Its reasonable prices make it easy to enjoy a variety of dishes.

title: Ddoddo
short_description: Ddoddo is a cozy Korean-style pub in front of Hongjecheon Stream, popular among locals for its neat food and clean space. True to its Korean pub style, it offers japchae as a basic side dish and has a wide selection of traditional liquors. The pub is particularly famous for its delicious side dishes, with the signature menu item being the Minja Budae-jjigae.

title: Cafe Sinola
short_description: Sinola Seochon is a charming café nestled along the stone wall path of Gyeongbokgung Palace, leading into Seochon. With two locations—one in Seochon and another in Bukchon—this café offers a tranquil and cozy atmosphere as soon as you step inside, making it the perfect place to experience Sinola’s distinctive charm. The space is adorned with vintage decor, adding visual warmth. At the same time, the gentle sound of LP records playing in the background enhances the peaceful ambiance, creating an ideal setting for focus and relaxation. Known for its exceptional drip coffee, Sinola also serves a highly praised brunch menu. The soft, decadent French toast is a favorite among visitors, drawing many to return for its delightful taste.

title: Roi garden
short_description: Located along Seosulla-gil, famous for its stone wall path, Roy Garden is a traditional Korean hanok-style pub where you can enjoy a tranquil atmosphere and a beautiful stone wall view. The view from the windows on the 1st and 2nd floors is lovely, but on pleasant weather days, the outdoor seating area is highly recommended for a more immersive experience. The menu includes a variety of dishes that pair well with wine, as well as a wide selection of drinks including glass wine, highballs, beer, whiskey, and traditional Korean liquor.

title: Hwandae Coffee Work
short_description: Hwandae Coffee Work is a small cafe prepared with the hope that your day will become a little warmer. If you walk along a quiet residential area not far from Daeheung Station, you can find it on the first floor of a brick building. Because everyone enjoys conversation here, you can experience an atmosphere closer to a cultural exchange 'salon' rather than simply a cafe. We hope you comfortably enjoy the coffee, sandwiches, and desserts made with utmost care and a willing heart.

title: LunaAsia
short_description: This restaurant serves authentic Indian cuisine crafted by native chefs. Its curries made with 100% natural spices and freshly baked naan from the tandoor are especially popular. Signature dishes include tandoori chicken with a smoky flavor and prawn vindaloo, where the shrimp’s savoriness meets the curry’s spicy heat in perfect harmony.

title: Jeong-dong Chueotang
short_description: Jeong-dong Chueotang is a popular restaurant for chueotang (loach soup) located in Jeong-dong. During lunchtime, it is bustling with nearby office workers. Chueotang is a soup dish made with loach as the main ingredient, along with various vegetables and seasonings, resulting in a rich and deep flavor. The special feature of Jeong-dong Chueotang is that it comes with rice cooked in a stone pot, allowing you to enjoy crispy rice at the end of the meal. They also serve thin noodles, which can be added to the chueotang along with various prepared sauces. For those who are not fond of loach, there are alternative options such as pork chueotang (donchutang), loach soup with beef brisket (usamgyeop chueotang), and beef stew (soegogi tteokbaegi bulgogi). Additionally, side dishes like fried loach (chuotwigim) and loach dumplings (chuomandu) are recommended. This restaurant is a great place to visit on a cold day, for a hangover remedy, or to replenish energy.

title: Another Side
short_description: Another Side Cafe is a large cafe operated with the concept of Green Mind, Green Life. The interior changes each season according to the concept, becoming a lilac forest in spring and a luxury Mediterranean resort in summer, and when the cold wind begins to blow, it transforms into a fairy tale Christmas forest to bring joy. As a specialty coffee shop, without going far, we hope you will heal in the city and feel the leisure of a cup of coffee.

title: House of Shinsegae Dessert Salon
short_description: House of Shinsegae Dessert Salon is a café where one can appreciate the dignity of Korean traditional desserts and teas. It researches Korean nature, seasons, and confectionery heritage, presenting Korean teas and byung-gwa (traditional confections) reinterpreted with modern sensibilities. Accessible to all generations, it is also ideal for visiting with parents. The confections are available not only for in-store enjoyment but also as gifts, making them a satisfying choice for thoughtful presents.

title: Zaffran
short_description: An Indian restaurant run directly by Indian locals, where the most popular dishes are tender tandoori chicken and curry loaded with generous chunks of meat.

title: Kensington Hotel Broadway
short_description:
Kensington Hotel Broadway recreates the vibrant atmosphere of New York’s Broadway in an all-day dining restaurant. Guests can enjoy a wide selection of live dishes freshly prepared by professional chefs, alongside a curated wine list selected by expert sommeliers.

title: Joseph's Coffee Tree
short_description: Joseph's Coffee Tree is a specialized roastery cafe where you can taste specialty coffee brewed directly by a Barista Championship judge, allowing you to experience high-class cafe coffee. Through the know-how and skills of a professional coffee roaster and barista with a 30-year tradition, it provides smooth hand-drip coffee that minimizes caffeine without any astringent taste.

title: Kebab inn
short_description: This restaurant offers an authentic taste of Türkiye, with fresh, flavor-packed dishes that highlight the country’s rich culinary tradition. Kebabs made with lamb, beef, and chicken each bring out their own unique character, complemented by fresh vegetables and fragrant sauces that enhance the flavors even further. To finish, the traditional dessert kaymak delights with its nutty, creamy taste.

title: Café Tajagi
short_description:
This vintage-inspired café blends great views with quirky touches like typewriters, retro posters, and soft music humming in the background. There's a quiet elegance to the space, with sunlight filtering through the large windows and the smell of freshly brewed coffee hanging in the air.

But the true gem is view—a table side vista with sweeping views of the Seoul city skyline. It’s the kind of place where time slows, and the world feels delightfully analog.

title: Chang-dong Pocha Street
short_description:
Chang-dong Pocha Street is a long-standing alley of red tent bars located just outside Exit 1 of Chang-dong Station. These iconic street pubs have formed a row over the years, creating a vibrant yet cozy atmosphere.


The area is clean and well-organized, making it convenient to visit. Guests can enjoy a variety of classic Korean street food and drinks in an open-air setting that captures the unique charm of traditional pocha culture.

title: Mr. Kebab
short_description: As a pioneer of domestic kebab franchises, this restaurant carefully prepares kebabs using traditional Turkish methods. Along with fresh salads and diverse menu options, it faithfully recreates authentic local flavors and has gained widespread popularity.

title: Room of Requirement
short_description: On the third floor of a building filled with lighting shops, there’s a hidden café without any sign. Although it’s a small space, the unique interior design, sunlight streaming through the windows, and soft music from the well-placed speakers make it a one-of-a-kind, distinctive spot. Here, visitors are welcomed with unique drinks and desserts such as chai, an Indian milk tea; Swedish cardamom buns; and cheddar cheese meat pies. Especially popular is the filter coffee, which changes monthly with a new specialty bean, drawing people back regularly. While finding the entrance can be challenging, this only adds to the charm, making it a fun mystery for visitors.

title: Café Layered Yeonnam
short_description:
Café Layered Yeonnam is a bakery café located in Yeonnam-dong, Mapo-gu, Seoul. It is well known for its warm, European-style interior reminiscent of a family home and its wide variety of scones and cakes.


The interior is decorated with antique objects and art pieces, creating a vintage atmosphere inspired by London and Paris. On the 2nd and 3rd floors, guests can enjoy sunlit window seats and a terrace.

title: Everest Restaurant Yeongdeungpo
short_description: Since 2007, this restaurant has brought the essence of traditional Indian and Nepalese cuisine to Korea. With a team of local chefs, it delivers authentic flavors true to their origins. A traditional tandoor oven, handmade in Nepal and imported here, gives the dishes added depth. Its signature Chicken Makhani, blending cheese, tomato, and cream, is especially renowned.

title: Bricksand Myeongdong Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: Tung Empty Life
short_description:
Tung Empty Life is a cafe and beer bar with a great view located at Anguk Station. Tung (Cafe) and Empty Life (Beer Bar) are operated together, and you can enjoy various beverages with leisure in front of large glass windows that capture the scenery of Jongno.

Located on the 7th and 8th floors, you can appreciate a beautiful view of Changdeokgung Palace and Inwangsan Mountain to the north, and Unhyeongung Palace and Namsan Tower to the south.

title: Cafe Jinjeongseong Hangang Coffee House
short_description: Cafe Jinjeongseong, which began as a small café in Gimpo’s Hangang New Town and later expanded to Incheon, Gwangju, and Jeju, opened its new location on top of Yanghwa Bridge in October 2024. True to its name, "Jinjeongseong" (meaning "sincerity"), the café uses organic ingredients and has gained popularity for its healthy beverages. Situated on the southern end of Yanghwa Bridge, the café is divided into two sections: the Tea House on the east side and the Coffee House on the west. The Tea House offers Korean traditional woojeon green tea and house-ground matcha, blended directly by the barista. The Coffee House serves signature drinks including milk tea and coffee.

title: Bali in Mangwon
short_description: This restaurant recreates the authentic flavors of Bali with fresh ingredients, greeting guests with a vibrant island atmosphere from the moment they step inside. Along with Indonesia’s signature dishes like mie goreng and nasi goreng, a variety of local specialties are ready to delight the palate. Take a break from your busy routine and enjoy a flavorful journey to Bali, right here in Mangwon.

title: Jangsu Medicinal Herb Ginseng Chicken Soup
short_description: In addition to the classic samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) with its clear broth, this restaurant also offers distinctive variations such as medicinal herb ginseng chicken soup and perilla-seed ginseng chicken soup. As the weather turns cold, people flock here for its deep, warming broth, and the nutty perilla-seed samgyetang is also highly recommended as a seasonal specialty.

title: HIT COFFEE ROASTERS Itaewon Branch
short_description: HIT COFFEE ROASTERS is a specialty coffee brand, and at the Itaewon branch, visitors can enjoy the space as a cafe during the day and as a bar at night. During the day, guests can enjoy specialty coffee, signature beverages, and a variety of desserts in a bright sunlit space. In the evening, signature cocktails, craft beer, and whiskey are available. Visitors may choose their preferred coffee type, and coffee bean tasting is available, allowing customers to find the coffee that best suits their preferences at HIT COFFEE ROASTERS.

title: Myeongdong Chungmu Gimbap
short_description: This is a local restaurant that has been serving Myeongdong for over 40 years, stubbornly focusing only on a single menu item: the Chungmu gimbap set. The simple gimbap is accompanied by spicy seasoned squid and crispy pickled radish, creating a simple yet profound flavor that has been beloved for a long time.

title: Bbobbai Bunsik
short_description: Located in Jamsil, Bbobbai Bunsik is a beloved tteokbokki restaurant that has been a local favorite since 1983. Now a cornerstone of the Jangmi Shopping Center, the restaurant is especially renowned for its "tteokjjolla," a unique dish that combines chewy noodles and ramen with traditional tteokbokki. Their fried rice is also highly recommended, and it's perfect for sharing if you visit with a friend. Having operated for decades, Bbobbai Bunsik attracts many customers who come to relive childhood memories, as well as young people who enjoy the nostalgic ambiance. It's also a hit among office workers at lunchtime, thanks to its great value. Most visitors love how the tteokbokki evokes memories of the snacks they used to enjoy outside their schools.

title: Bricksand Seongsu Factory
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: Bongchu Jjimdak  Myeongdong Jungang Post Office
short_description: A popular franchise known for Andong-style braised chicken, this restaurant offers a spicy-sweet royal court–style braised dish of chicken, potatoes, and glass noodles reinterpreted with a modern touch. The deep, savory sauce and tender chicken create a perfect harmony that continues to win many fans.

title: Petra Palace
short_description: This place showcases healthy, high-quality Middle Eastern cuisine and is particularly renowned for its signature menu featuring Mezza platters that combine hummus and falafel.

title: Insaeng Sliced Raw Fish Jonggak Main
short_description:
This specialty restaurant offers a variety of fresh assorted sashimi. After enjoying the vibrant sashimi platter, finishing the meal with a seafood

stew (seodeori-tang) simmered with ramen and hand-pulled dough flakes creates a warm and comforting bowl full of ocean flavors.

title: Hyunseonine Yongsan Main Store
short_description: Featured on the TV show Find It! Delicious TV as one of the top five tteokbokki restaurants in Seoul, Hyunseonine became even more popular after its appearance. It first began as a pojangmacha (street cart) in 2004 and still resembles one in its building design today. The menu is divided into set menus, single items, and instant tteokbokki. Both takeout and delivery are available. You can choose your preferred spice level from spicy, medium, or mild.

title: Four Seasons Hotel Seoul Charles H.
short_description: Charles H. Bar, named after legendary American writer Charles H. Baker, is a hidden underground bar exuding exotic and glamorous charm. It offers a perfect cocktail menu for enthusiasts, accessible via a secret passage. Discover innovative cocktails crafted with seasonal Korean ingredients, paired with carefully curated food menus available exclusively here.

title: Sinheung
short_description: This is a representative super bean sprout ramen restaurant in Mullae Creative Village that has been around since 1975. It is a family-run restaurant that serves both anju and haejangramyeon, and a shop that serves as a neighborhood love room. The owner's heart for the ironworkers who work early in the morning has been conveyed to the customers, making them feel like neighbors. A bowl of noodle soup with the pride of being not just an iron business, but a shop that has been around for a long time, thin as noodles, leaves a warm feeling even today.

title: LaiLai Yeonhuidong Main Branch
short_description: Located in Yeonhui-dong, LaiLai is a Chinese restaurant where you can enjoy a variety of Chinese dishes. Its signature dish, Chili Eggplant, is particularly famous; it combines a unique crispiness with a garlic-infused chili sauce that can’t be found elsewhere, making it a must-try for anyone visiting LaiLai. In addition to this, you can enjoy a wide range of Chinese dishes commonly found in Chinese restaurants, such as Jjajangmyeon, Jjamppong, Sanlatang, and Lazogibap. The Jjamppong is both flavorful and clean-tasting, and the tender, savory Tangsuyuk are also highly recommended dishes. The restaurant is divided into a main dining hall and private rooms, so if you prefer a quieter dining experience, reservations can be made for private room use.

title: Overdeep Yeonnam
short_description: This is a unique cafe created by three designers from different fields with an unparalleled deep-sea concept. It's a large cafe converted from a house, where you can even use the rooftop. The interior design features a theme reminiscent of the ocean depths, with media art, jellyfish lighting, coral, and shells. You can find various photo spots throughout, and experience the deep sea in everyday life. We recommend trying the signature Wave Cream Latte, where blue foam resembles an ocean within your coffee.

title: Sunmine Haengbok Gejang Dongdaemun
short_description: Specializing in soy sauce marinated raw crab, this restaurant follows authentic Korean recipes without using artificial seasonings to bring out deep flavors. Located across from DDP, one of Seoul’s landmark attractions, it is loved by both local and international visitors. Another highlight is the unlimited crab refill offered at a reasonable price.

title: Muguok
short_description: Muguok is a chicken specialty restaurant that exclusively uses domestic chicken and a rich broth boiled thoroughly in an "Anseong Gamasot," an intangible cultural heritage of Gyeonggi Province. The signature menu, Northern-style Samgye Baekban (Ginseng Chicken Set Meal), features a broth that is thick and milky white, achieved by simmering chicken in an iron cauldron for a long time. It is highly popular not only among foreign tourists but also among local office workers and the younger generation, making it a place where waiting is essential.

title: Naerimson Samgyetang Euljiro
short_description:
Samgyetang, a nourishing soup made with fresh chicken and ginseng, is a beloved health food enjoyed by people of all ages. This restaurant is an

excellent choice for family or friends to gather and savor a variety of delicious chicken dishes.

title: Tandoor
short_description: One of the representative Uzbek restaurants on Dongdaemun’s Central Asian street, it is especially famous for its somsa, a meat-filled pastry baked in a traditional tandoor oven. The large oven set just outside the entrance immediately catches the eye, and one bite of the pastry releases a burst of savory juices.

title: Bricksand One Grove Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: Saeng Gopchangjip Sangam
short_description: This restaurant specializes in grilled beef intestines, serving only fresh raw gopchang without pre-grilling. The beef intestines are carefully prepared to remove any odor, offering a clean, nutty flavor with a crispy outside and tender inside. Well-known among gopchang lovers, it’s considered one of the best spots for beef intestines in Sangam-dong.

title: Bourbon
short_description: Bourbon, located near the Constitutional Court, primarily specializes in whisky. Its unique setup does not include a traditional bar counter but tatami room-style seating areas. The space and menu are thoughtfully curated to offer guests a new whisky experience. In addition to whisky, the bar offers a wide range of beverages, including wine, beer, and cocktails. Their house-infused whiskies, featuring flavors like strawberry, mugwort, and mokmil, are ideal even for whisky newcomers. The bar also offers thoughtfully paired dishes such as rice cakes, yakgwa (honey cookie), cherry cheesecake, and basil pesto parfait, offering a satisfying experience for both taste and sight.

title: Bakery Agung
short_description: Bakery Agung is a large hanok cafe with the concept of an old traditional feast, uniquely capturing Korean sensibility in its interior. As soon as you enter the store, you can encounter the unique sight of bread being baked and fried directly. You can purchase items such as Feast Focaccia that expresses Korean jeon as focaccia, Gat Financier that contains the history of the Joseon Dynasty, and Guksundang Makgeolli Bread that captures traditional flavors using Guksundang makgeolli. This is a Jonggak Station bakery cafe that freshly uses mugwort, red beans, and domestic ingredients to create its menu. It is a new cafe in Jongno gu that creates satisfaction with excellent bread taste, affordable menu prices, and perfect visuals.

title: Mabongnim Halmeonijip
short_description: Mabongnim Halmeonijip, established in 1953, is the starting point of Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Alley and a legendary place that elevated tteokbokki from a simple snack to a celebrated dish. Owner Mabokrim developed a secret recipe by mixing gochujang and chunjang black bean paste), which is characterized by its sweet flavor. A major attraction is the ability to cook tteokbokki directly at the table, allowing customers to enjoy personalized tteokbokki by adding a variety of toppings. Five years before her passing, Owner Mabokrim passed her secret recipe to her daughter-in-law, and the restaurant continues to uphold that delicious flavor to this day.

title: Gong Gan
short_description: This bar located in Bukchon offers a variety of concept cocktails, all made in-house. The interior features a central courtyard, allowing you to experience the space's diverse charm both day and night. Additionally, you can enjoy cocktails from famous bartenders worldwide through occasional guest bartending events. Situated in a quiet alley near Anguk Station, the bar is a unique cocktail bar that blends modern renovation with traditional hanok architecture. In line with its concept, it offers signature cocktails with distinctly Korean names. Reservations and group visits are available, and the bar is pet-friendly.

title: Lounge Continuum
short_description: Lounge Continum, nestled in Mangwon-dong, greets visitors with a welcoming and cozy atmosphere as soon as they step inside. The space is adorned with shelves filled with CDs, antique furniture, and retro decor, creating a relaxing environment for guests. The lush green trees visible through the windows provide a serene view that enhances concentration, while the inviting aroma of hand-drip coffee, freshly brewed by the owner, fills the air. The space is thoughtfully arranged with seating options for both groups and those who prefer a quiet moment alone, making it a perfect spot for all. In addition to coffee, the menu includes a selection of alcoholic beverages such as whiskey and cocktails, making it a great place to visit in the evening for those looking to enjoy a drink.

title: Rain Report Rainbow
short_description: Rain Report introduces 'Rainbow', bringing color to your day in a cafe where it rains all year round. In a monochromatic yet atmospheric hanok space, discover colorful handmade desserts crafted to your taste. Rain Report Rainbow, a dessert cafe in Ikseon-dong, adds vibrancy to the rainy mood and offers a truly special experience.

title: Tashkent Kebab
short_description: The juicy, flavorful kebab patties make for a satisfying meal when served with a side of fries. Particularly rare in Seoul, the fish kebab is loved for its freshness and unique texture. A strong recommendation for visitors looking to try a different take on kebabs.

title: Seobu Gamjaguk
short_description: During the time when the slaughterhouse was located in Eungam-dong, potato soup restaurants flourished in the area. Seobu Gamjaguk is one of the few that has remained in its original location since then. Its signature potato soup is made from carefully trimmed pork backbone, resulting in a clean and mild flavor. The restaurant is also famous for its delicious Kimchi, prepared fresh daily. They even make separate Kimchi for fried rice and sell fresh oysters during the winter, offering various ways to enjoy a unique delicacy.

title: MONKS BUTCHER
short_description: This is a trendy restaurant that presents a modern reinterpretation of vegan and Korean cuisine. The dishes, which blend traditional sensibilities with creative flair, create a sophisticated dining experience and offer a new culinary adventure that transcends vegan boundaries for everyone to enjoy.

title: Aino Garden Kitchen
short_description: Aino Garden Kitchen is a Korean restaurant located in Seochon, highly popular for its neat food, interior remodeled from a Hanok, and a terrace. The 1st floor of the building is a cafe, and the 2nd floor is operated as a Korean restaurant.

title: Manhole Coffee Western Bookstore
short_description: Manhole Coffee is a cafe where you can feel a vintage atmosphere, meaning that when you open a manhole cover and go underground, a new world unfolds. Manhole Coffee Western Bookstore, the second branch of Manhole Coffee, is a book cafe with an American West vibe, and with a wide space from the first to the third floors and an atmosphere decorated like a log cabin lodge, it is good for quietly working or reading books. In addition, it roasts various coffee beans every day and allows you to smell them directly and choose your beans. We recommend tasting the signature menu, Manhole Cream Coffee.

title: Nammi Plant Lab
short_description: This vegan restaurant is especially known for its Italian dishes such as cheese vegetable pizza and pasta verde. Pets are welcome, making it a comfortable stop even when traveling with animal companions. If you want to experience the appeal of plant-based dining firsthand, this is a spot worth visiting.

title: Bermuda Samgakji
short_description:
Bermuda Samgakji is a fusion restaurant that blends Mexican and Western cuisine. Even if it’s your first time trying Mexican food, the Korean-style sauces make the flavors approachable and familiar.


Here, you can enjoy a variety of alcoholic drinks alongside fusion Mexican dishes you won’t find anywhere else. It’s perfect for a full meal or just a light drink and snack after work. The restaurant spans two floors, offering a Hawaiian and Mexican-inspired atmosphere where you can experience truly unique flavors.

title: SAMARKAND CITY
short_description: An authentic Uzbek restaurant beloved by both Koreans and the local community. It offers a special dining experience with a wide variety of traditional skewered dishes known as shashlik. The Central Asian–style interior further enhances its exotic atmosphere.

title: BOMBAY GRILL
short_description: This is an Indian cuisine specialty restaurant where you can truly enjoy authentic Indian flavors, with dishes prepared directly by chefs from India. Various menu items are available including lamb curry, samosas, and pakoras.

title: La Yeon
short_description: The Korean restaurant La Yeon, located on the 23rd floor of the Seoul Shilla Hotel, offers a place where you can appreciate the beautiful views of Namsan Mountain and experience Korea's tradition and modern sophistication. The use of traditional Korean patterns in the interior, tableware inspired by Joseon white porcelain, and the use of seasonal ingredients sourced from all over the country have added authenticity and elegance to La Yeon. La Yeon's cuisine delicately reinterprets the flavors of Korea with modern cooking techniques, and it pairs well with wine to offer a unique culinary experience.

title: Jinmi Sikdang
short_description: Jinmi Sikdang specializes in soy-marinated crabs made exclusively from crabs caught in the West Sea. During peak crab seasons in June and December, they purchase crabs in bulk, rapidly freezing and storing them at -35°C. This process ensures that fresh and flavorful crabs are available year-round, with the use of female crabs adding an extra layer of taste to the dish. The soy-marinated crabs at Jinmi Sikdang are aged for three days in soy sauce fermented with Seosan ginger before being served. The meal comes with over ten side dishes, including gyeranjjim (steamed eggs), spicy crab stew, eoriguljeot (spicy salted oysters), and gamtae (seaweed), providing a rich variety of flavors. The restaurant is also a popular spot among celebrities and well-known figures.

title: SAMARQAND SHAHJAHON CHAYHONA
short_description: It is the first Silk Road food restaurant in Korea run by Uzbek locals. Popular among both Koreans and the Uzbek community living in Seoul, it offers dishes that appeal to all. The restaurant’s signature dish is shashlik— lamb marinated in a special  seasoning and grilled in a stone oven until crispy on the outside and tender inside.

title: Mokro Garden
short_description: Mokro Garden is a gardening space introducing flowers, plants, tea, and coffee, offering vegan and gluten-free desserts. Inside the store, it is filled with plants and flowers, giving the feeling of being surrounded by nature, allowing you to relax leisurely while enjoying coffee and desserts.

title: EPI
short_description: Located near Seolleung Station, EPI is a cozy bakery café known for its handcrafted breads and pastries. Signature items include baguettes, salted butter rolls, ciabatta, and an assortment of baked goods. Their specialty coffee, made  from premium Latin American beans, features nutty flavors balanced with soft acidity. To enjoy their bread fresh out of the oven, check their weekly baking schedule on Instagram.

title: Yongyong Teacher Maradowon
short_description: Yongyong Teacher Maradowon is a paradise for mara lovers. This flagship store, inspired by traditional Chinese eateries, captures the craftsmanship of Yongyong Teacher, who is deeply devoted to both mala and kaoliang liquor. It offers a bold dining experience featuring intensely smoky charcoal-grilled mala soup and a special performance zone, creating a new kind of culinary destination.

title: L'OIGNON
short_description: This restaurant presents French cuisine tailored for pescatarians, using vegetables, seafood, eggs, and dairy products. Its delicate dishes, harmonized with the refined atmosphere of Garosu-gil, have earned it a place in the Michelin Guide. Every dish is served as part of a full course menu, crafted with fresh seasonal ingredients.

title: Kihoo
short_description: At Kihoo, the menu changes with the seasons, expressing spring, summer, autumn, and winter through a single meal. As its name suggests, Kihoo offers only seasonal menus carefully crafted by the chef using ingredients of the season. The restaurant presents omakase cuisine based on Japanese style, infused with Korean elements.

title: First by Three
short_description: First by Three is the first space created by graphic design studio TRIANGLE-STUDIO. The cafe stands out with its stylish decor and interior, featuring carefully curated items. Large windows offer views of Hongjecheon Stream and the village scenery, enhancing the peaceful and cozy atmosphere. Signature menu items include Ari Latte, Ang pang Latte, and Panna Cotta Peach Milk Pudding.

title: Dongjak Sunset Café
short_description: Dongjak Sunset Cafe is an establishment overlooking the Hangang River, located at the southern end of Dongjak Bridge, where you can leisurely enjoy the Yeouido view that is often missed while crossing the bridge. Situated on the western side among the cafes at the southern end of Dongjak Bridge, Dongjak Sunset Cafe allows you to enjoy various desserts and coffee along with a beautiful Hangang River view during sunset.

title: Glam Lounge
short_description: As the country’s first and largest lounge club and its unique concept and style, Glam Lounge has established itself as an iconic destination in Itaewon and South Korea. The exotic furnishings and vintage arched windows harmoniously blend to create a unique, restrained yet strikingly glamorous atmosphere. The minimalist and tasteful interior design with a mid-century modern style and trendy lounge music further enhances the opulence. Together, they create an ambiance of limitless charm and appeal. Glam Lounge takes inspiration from Japanese cuisine and incorporates various Asian flavors to develop a diverse menu. Using seasonal fresh fish, the lounge creates sushi and sashimi dishes that offer a gourmet experience not commonly found in traditional lounges. In addition, a carefully curated selection of signature cocktails and a trendy wine list complement the culinary offerings, providing the utmost service to stylish and discerning consumers. The menu and beverage list are updated annually to ensure that Glam Lounge stays harmoniously with the latest trends.

title: CAFE POKPO
short_description: This is a waterside open-air cafe situated around the artificial waterfall of Hongjecheon, dubbed 'Seoul-type Waterside Emotional City No. 1', a space where you can relax while admiring a 25m-high and 60m-wide artificial waterfall. Seodaemun-gu has established the Youth Hope Dream Fund, utilizing proceeds from Cafe Pokpo, which opened in 2023, to provide scholarships that support students' dreams. Many foreign tourists also visit this place. We hope you will enjoy the leisure of a cup of tea while listening to the sound of a falling waterfall.

title: Romantic LP Bar Jamsil Bangi Branch
short_description: Romantic LP Bar is a bar that offers real LP listening experiences with drinks and good music, pursuing a comfortable atmosphere that welcomes visitors in their 20s and 30s. The collection includes LPs across diverse genres such as Korean pop, pop, rock, J-pop, jazz, hip-hop, and EDM. Song requests are accepted freely without restrictions by era or genre. Guests are advised to inquire in advance whether their desired LPs are available before visiting. With acoustics professionally tuned to suit the space, this is a romantic LP bar ideal for conversation and relaxation.

title: Hearts House
short_description: Located in a residential alley, Hearts House is a cafe created by renovating a regular house. The warm and comfortable atmosphere in every corner of the space allows visitors to express forgotten or unspoken thoughts in writing. Letter paper and pencils are provided in a corner of the space so that visitors can enjoy a leisurely moment writing a letter while having a cup of coffee. Letter paper is provided free of charge, and letter envelopes and various accessories are available for purchase.

title: Myeongin Deungsim Mapo
short_description: Operating since 2009 under the slogan “A Place for Premium Hanwoo (Korean Beef) Sirloin,” this restaurant specializes in top-grade hanwoo. It sources 1++ hanwoo directly from large-scale ranches in Andong, Gyeongbuk, ensuring high-quality cuts and ingredients at reasonable prices. For anyone wishing to experience the taste of hanwoo at its best, this is the place to be.

title: Coccinelle
short_description: Coccinelle is a French bistro opened by a chef with fifteen years of experience working in France. As a farm to table restaurant, it collaborates with Marche farmers to offer French home style cuisine. Seasonal salads and vegetables come directly from farmers’ fields and are either organic or grown using organic farming methods. Although it is a French bistro, the restaurant mainly uses Korean ingredients grown in Korea, allowing guests to taste French cuisine adapted to local ingredients.

title: OMOT
short_description: OMOT is a Korean tea specialty teahouse nestled in Seongsu-dong near Seoul Forest. It offers a private, reservation-based storytelling tea course featuring seasonal teas and traditional Korean sweets (dasik). (Reservations can be made via Naver TalkTalk or Instagram DM. A la carte menu items are available for walk-in guests.) Located in the heart of the city, OMOT provides a healing experience where guests can fully enjoy personal time while embracing a new tea culture and a healthy, meaningful lifestyle. The shop also sells signature niche teas, single-origin teas, tableware, and handcrafted items.

title: Bangul & Kkomak
short_description: Bangul & Kkomak is a reasonably priced seafood tavern where you can enjoy high-quality seasonal seafood. It is a must-visit for seafood lovers. The outdoor tables create the lively ambiance of a pojangmacha (street food tent bar). Although there is often a wait, reservations can be made in advance through the Catch Table app.

title: SZIMPATIKUS Yongsan Branch
short_description: Located at the heart of the hot spot Yongsan’s Yongridan-gil, SZIMPATIKUS Yongsan is a fine casual restaurant that reinterprets European cuisine in an Asian style. It provides high-quality dishes at reasonable prices in a stylish yet comfortable space, aiming to make each meal a meaningful moment shared with loved ones. A professionally curated wine bottle shop is also available, where a wide variety of wines can be purchased at accessible prices.

title: Riverside Library
short_description:
Riverside Library, located inside the National Assembly in Yeouido, is a unique café where visitors can enjoy reading while overlooking the Han River. It is ideal for taking a break during a riverside walk or spending a leisurely time while traveling.


The wide glass windows offer panoramic views of both the Han River and the National Assembly. In spring, it is also a recommended spot for cherry blossom viewing.

title: KOREA HOUSE Kohojae
short_description: 고호재는 '옛것을 사랑하는 이들을 위한 집'이라는 뜻의 프리미엄 로열 디저트 브랜드입니다. 전통 한국 가옥 분위기 속에서 선보입니다. 예약제로 운영되는 코호재 프로그램은 프리미엄 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울 재료로 맞춤 제작된 계절별 디저트 세트를 제공합니다. 다문화 공간인 KOREA HOUSE에서 전통 한국 문화와 요리의 아름다움을 경험하며 왕실 디저트와 한낙의 고요한 우아함을 즐길 수 있습니다.

title: BAN COFFEE SHOP
short_description: Located near Dangsan Station, BAN Coffee Shop is a hip sensibility cafe and a large cafe where Han River bicycle riders can comfortably visit. It sells not only coffee and desserts but also bicycle equipment. For bicycle rider customers, indoor bike racks and air pumps for inflation are available, along with hex wrenches for simple part adjustments, and scales for measuring bicycle weight outside are provided free of charge. Try the handmade scones, carefully kneaded in-store, and signature menu items: the BAN Cheese Latte and the BAN Almond Cream Latte.

title: ALT.a
short_description: A vegan Chinese restaurant that recreates the deep flavors of Korean-style Chinese cuisine using only plant-based ingredients, it was listed in the 2025 Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand. Beyond the label of ‘vegan food,’ it delights diners at home and abroad with refined Chinese dishes that highlight the new appeal of plant-based cuisine.

title: Daebok
short_description: This is a traditional pufferfish cuisine specialty restaurant that has been conveying the essence of bok-jiri (pufferfish soup) since the 1970s. Using fresh pufferfish and meticulous cooking methods, you can enjoy bok-jiri with deep and clean flavors. If you want to properly taste bok-jiri, this restaurant is highly recommended.

title: jumjumjumjumjumjum
short_description: More than just a vegan restaurant, this space also serves as a hub for vegan culture and an exhibition venue. The eight-course, reservation-only lunch features house-made sauces and pestos for exceptional flavor and craftsmanship. Its interior, crafted with recycled aluminum, embodies the value of sustainability and deepens the space’s message.

title: Mexitiger
short_description:
MexiTiger is a city of Mexican hippie spirit. Inspired by the cantinas of San Cristóbal, this Mexican-Chinese tequila pub brings a tough and moody charm that captivates you from the moment you step inside.


Step into a dark, secretive tiger’s den glowing with orange flames, where intense stares and loud toasts fill the air. In the basement, beneath glowing red neon lights, an uninhibited tequila lounge unfolds—perfect for bold conversations and fiery energy.


Signature Mexican dishes like tacos, quesadillas, and nachos are infused with a Chinese twist, creating a truly unique flavor. A tequila-glazing performance over a blazing 300-degree open flame adds to the full sensory experience. MexiTiger is one of Gangnam’s must-visit gourmet destinations.

title: Oddhaus Osteria
short_description:
Oddhaus Osteria is a brunch and wine bar located on the garden terrace of the Shin Ah Memorial Hall, a 100-year-old modern cultural heritage building. Constructed in the 1930s, the building once served as an annex of the Shin Ah Daily newspaper. After the newspaper’s closure in 1980, it was renovated as a memorial hall, and now offices and commercial facilities are annexed.


Situated on the ground floor, Oddhaus Osteria retains the charm of retro architecture while welcoming guests in a modern space illuminated with warm orange lights.

title: Marly
short_description: Located in the Seongsu-dong café street, Marlely is a large café spread across two floors with a total area of over 140 pyeong. The wide windows allow plenty of natural light, and the artistic objects and stylish interior design create a gallery-like atmosphere. Specializing in cakes and scones, Marly offers a perfect place to enjoy desserts with coffee.

title: Cafe Gongmyung Mangwon Book Bakery
short_description: Cafe Gongmyung Mangwon Book Bakery is the largest book cafe in Mangwon-dong, a neighborhood with the highest density of bookstores in Seoul. In addition to being a great space to work with excellent interior design, you can taste top-quality coffee and bakery goods made fresh every morning using the finest ingredients. Equipped with a rooftop and terrace, you can fully enjoy the emotional scenery of Mangwon-dong according to the seasons.

title: LOW ROOF
short_description: LOW ROOF is a large café located in Bukchon Hanok Village, offering a blend of traditional and modern sensibilities. Guests can enjoy coffee while looking out at a hanok view through the large windows of the contemporary interior. Each floor features spacious, open areas with stylish design and cozy natural lighting. The outdoor terrace connected to the first floor retains the beauty of traditional architecture, making it one of the most popular spots in the café to experience both hanok charm and seasonal scenery.

title: Nokum Space
short_description: This atmospheric restaurant not only serves refined vegan cuisine but also hosts live performances across various genres every Friday and Saturday. With dishes accented by Korean flavors, a sophisticated ambiance, and live music all coming together, it offers a unique space where you can truly experience Seoul’s unique cultural and artistic spirit.

title: Everest Restaurant Dongdaemun History & Culture Park
short_description: Run by a Nepali couple, this restaurant specializes in authentic Nepalese cuisine. Its most popular dishes include chicken makhani curry, made with butter, cream, and tomatoes, and chicken tikka, marinated in a variety of spices and roasted in a tandoor. For 20 years, it has been loved not only as a place to enjoy food but also as a venue for cultural exchange.

title: plat å[o:]
short_description:
This vegan brunch cafeteria is located on Yangjaecheon Café Street. It’s a relaxing spot to visit after a stroll along Yangjaecheon Stream, and it’s also

pet-friendly, making it a favorite among local residents. If you’d like to broaden your experience of vegan cuisine with rich and diverse flavors, this is a place we highly recommend.

title: Apple House
short_description: Apple House started as a food stall in Banpo in 1987, and as word of mouth spread, customers flocked to set up shop. In 2022, it moved from Banpo to Isu due to redevelopment. Currently, the owner is passing on the recipe to his daughter to continue the business for the second generation. The owner attributes the restaurant's longevity to its "unchanged flavor". Regulars are happy that it tastes the same as it used to, and younger customers come for the old flavors.

title: THE SSANGHWA
short_description: Located deep inside an old alleyway near Dongdaemun Market, THE SSANGHWA   headquarters is a place where you can taste traditional teas naturally integrated into our daily lives. It is a traditional herbal tea specialty cafe operated based on the know-how of the Food Business Division of Jongno Gangnam Oriental Medicine Clinic, established in 1967. Traditional herbal teas recreate the exact methods historically used to present offerings to the king, while adapting the flavors to suit modern tastes, allowing them to be enjoyed comfortably.

title: Bonghwa Mukjip
short_description: This restaurant has been serving delicious mukbap and dumplings next to Jeongneung since 1982. The family business has been passed down from mother-in-law to daughter-in-law from Bonghwa, Gyeongbuk. They make their own homemade miso and soy sauce, and continue their philosophy of not cheating customers with their food. The restaurant has been renovated from an old family house, giving it a homey atmosphere, and many regular customers come from far and wide to enjoy the exquisite food.

title: Yeonbaek Naengmyeon
short_description: Yeonbaek naengmyeon is a renowned cold noodle restaurant known for its thin, chewy noodles and rich broth. The noodles have a delightful texture, being both chewy and soft, while the broth is prepared by simmering beef bones and various secret ingredients to create a deep and flavorful taste. If you are in Seoul, we highly recommend a refreshing bowl of cold noodles at Yeonbaek naengmyeon.

title: Midong Sikdang
short_description: Located on the 1st floor of an over 50-year-old residential-commercial apartment building, Midong Sikdang is a budget-friendly pub with an atmosphere reminiscent of a small Japanese izakaya. A place for comfortable conversations with good people, accompanied by delicious food and drinks; when you order according to the number of guests, the kitchen serves carefully prepared Omakase snacks selected at their discretion. Ordering one drink per person is mandatory, with options ranging from cold draft beer to affordable bottled sake.

title: Bean Brother Coffee House
short_description: Bean Brothers Coffee House is a specialty café located in Sangsu. Offering a variety of beans, it caters to all tastes, guided by detailed tasting notes. A highlight of this café is its expansive view of the Hangang River, which enhances the coffee-drinking experience. Large windows offer panoramic views of Seogangdaegyo Bridge, Bamseom Island, and the National Assembly Building. This creates a unique atmosphere that perfectly complements the rich coffee flavors, ensuring customers keep coming back. On the 6th floor, the coffee bar offers a chance to explore Bean Brothers' seasonal coffees in diverse ways. From the “Coffee Flight,” which features three different coffees from various origins, to the coffee of the month and cocktails, there is a wide range of special seasonal beverages to enjoy. However, the seasonal coffee bar operates on a reservation basis, so be sure to book your visit in advance.

title: Petra
short_description: A Middle Eastern cuisine restaurant that opened in Itaewon to introduce Jordanian food and culture to Korea, offering authentic and heartfelt dishes made only with halal meat and fresh ingredients, along with warm service.

title: Onmigwan Anguk
short_description: Onmigwan is a renowned restaurant near Anguk Station, carrying on the history of Korean cuisine in a traditional neighborhood. It offers honest, subtle flavors of traditional Korean dishes that deliver warmth without being overly stimulating. Its signature dish is Eobok Jeongban, a Pyongyang-style hotpot where secret broth is poured over special beef cuts and vegetables, creating a clean and mild taste.

title: Chowol
short_description:
Transcending makgeolli — Chowol is an urban brewery located between Mapo Station and Gongdeok Station.

Chowol follows traditional brewing methods using only rice, nuruk, and water. It uses Haenam rice, grown in Korea’s southernmost tip where fertile plains meet sea breezes. Through makgeolli, Chowol connects past and present, and bridges the rural and the urban.

title: Seonchae Seongsu
short_description: Seonchae is a small Korean dining restaurant that serves a meal unique to Seonchae using fresh ingredients from the eight provinces of the country, presenting our most familiar yet new ingredients. The seating consists of a single bar table. Alcoholic beverages are mandatory during dinner, but non-alcoholic menus are also prepared, allowing you to use the restaurant without any burden.

title: Sindangdong Cheon Patjuk
short_description: Sindangdong Cheon Patjuk is a restaurant that specializes in traditional Korean dishes, red bean porridge (patjuk) and red bean paste noodle soup (patkalguksu). The menu offers only these two items, showcasing the owner's pride in their food. Each order is cooked immediately, allowing you to savor the rich red bean flavor and the chewy texture of the rice dumplings (ongsimi). Many regular customers return for its soft and rich taste that they can't forget. If you find it lacking in seasoning, you can adjust the flavor to your taste with the sugar and salt on the table. The friendly owner and delicious side dishes make this restaurant a favorite among people of all ages. A hearty bowl of warm red bean porridge is perfect for cold winter days, and visiting the restaurant on Dongji (the Winter Solstice) is highly recommended.

title: AMMA HONGDAE
short_description: With 15 years of history, this Indian restaurant recreates authentic flavors  using 32 ingredients sourced directly from India. The atmosphere immediately transports you to the country itself, making you  feel as if you’re dining in India. The set menus, offering a wide range of dishes at great value, come especially recommended.

title: VIEW376
short_description: VIEW376 is a Han River cafe within walking distance from Apgujeong Rodeo Station. With a wide, unobstructed view of the Han River, it offers a peaceful escape in the heart of the city. Its rooftop seating makes it perfect for enjoying the beautiful night view. Brunch is served from 10 AM to 4 PM, and the café also offers coffee, a variety of drinks, and a selection of desserts. The indoor space is spacious with ample seating and wide table spacing, making it a comfortable and quiet place for conversation. Pets are welcome, and aside from the rooftop on the 3rd floor, terrace seating on the 2nd floor is also available.

title: Sadelleʼs at Kith Seoul
