short_description: Located on the 3rd floor of KITH Seoul, Sadelle’s is a renowned brunch restaurant that originated in New York. Guests can enjoy classic brunch dishes such as bagels, smoked salmon, and French toast in a stylish setting. The interior is filled with natural light through large windows and features arched frames and an elegant bar counter that evoke the vibe of New York. Terrace seating is also available, offering a relaxing and pleasant view of Seoul’s greenery.

title: Daddy's Lamb Steakhouse
short_description: If you want to experience truly premium lamb in Seoul, this is a must-visit restaurant. It uses only Halal-certified young lamb and applies a meticulous water-aging process that gives each cut a firm exterior and tender, flavorful interior. From lamb chops and loin to belly cuts, every piece is expertly prepared, and the menu also features nutritious lamb soups perfect for revitalizing the body

title: House of Vinyl Mangwon Branch
short_description: House of Vinyl Mangwon Branch is an LP café where guests can listen to music in a space characterized by a vintage aesthetic and interior design. The stylish interior, both inside and outside the café, creates an exotic atmosphere, and the space feels more like a warm living room than a typical café. Each guest may request one song. All music, except for requested tracks, is played on LP records; however, if a requested song is not available on vinyl, it may be played in digital format.

title: Pyeongtaek Rice Store
short_description: This shop has been making and selling noodles the old-fashioned way for 30 years. Here, you can find noodles that are dried naturally in the sun and wind, not in a factory with a hot air dryer. The noodles are made by people and nature, not machines. In addition to plain noodles, you can find noodles of various colors such as pumpkin noodles, barley noodles, mugwort noodles, and white lotus plant noodles, and noodles of various thicknesses such as small, medium, and large noodles. In the past, they also sold rice, but now they only make noodles because there are more people looking for noodles.

title: CaféCité
short_description: Café Cité is a dessert café where guests can enjoy exclusive beverages inspired by cities around the world, along with baked pastries and cakes prepared by in-house pâtissiers. The signature menu item, 'Seongsu Brick Latte', is a rich latte combining the sweetness of almonds with chewy coffee jelly. Enjoy a relaxing moment while gazing at the open view through the floor-to-ceiling windows that cover the building, creating the feeling of being inside a greenhouse.

title: Protocol Yeonhui Branch
short_description: Protocol is a specialty coffee roastery café themed around “time and records.” At Protocol Yeonhui, roasters document coffee profiles daily in the roasting room, while baristas experiment with extraction recipes at the bar, creating an archive-like workspace. The café also serves as a showroom offering experiences that blend coffee, learning, and play.

title: Samu Chicken Center
short_description: This fried chicken restaurant has been in business since 1972 and has been passed down to the second generation. Some customers have been coming to the restaurant for three generations because it has remained in the same place for a long time with flavors that stimulate the childhood feelings of people in their 70s and 80s. The interior of the restaurant, which has maintained the same interior as it was in those days, is a place filled with memories of regular customers. The ingredients are carefully prepared daily, and the flavors of the hand-dipped chicken radish, savory and crispy fried chicken, and chewy electric whole chicken will continue to be enjoyed for years to come.

title: Troy Kebab
short_description: It is a restaurant specializing in authentic Türkiye kebabs run by a local Turkiye. The restaurant offers a wide variety of kebabs, from tortilla-wrapped kebabs to rice kebabs, and it is fun to choose a menu. You can choose how spicy you would want it to be. If you prefer a spicy taste, you can ask the chef for it separately.

title: Mur Mur
short_description: After a stroll around Seokchon Lake, Murmur is the perfect place to indulge in some delightful desserts. Known for its cozy ambiance and seasonal fruit cakes and charlottes, this charming cafe offers a variety of treats that keep people coming back. The friendly owner and welcoming atmosphere make it a favorite for many. Their strawberry charlotte and Basque cheese chocolate cake are particularly popular, made with the finest ingredients. Beyond the delicious desserts, their coffee and drinks are also highly praised. During the holiday season, you can even reserve their signature strawberry charlotte, making it a special treat to look forward to.

title: Paldo Milbang Gangnam Main Branch
short_description: A Korean dining space near Gangnam Station where you can enjoy various kalguksu and a traditional Korean table setting. Including kalguksu menus, it provides Korean dishes suitable for both lunch and dinner gatherings, such as pork cutlet, steamed pork bones, and seafood green onion pancakes.

title: NIROSHA Restaurant
short_description: This is an authentic Indian cuisine specialty restaurant featuring dishes prepared by a local Indian and Nepalese chef with 20 years of experience. The signature menu items are curry that brings out deep and rich flavors using traditional cooking methods and carefully selected ingredients, along with freshly baked naan.

title: Joseon Choga Hankki Mapo Branch
short_description: Joseon Choga Hankki Mapo Branch is a Korean restaurant where you can enjoy traditional Korean food while feeling the old-time charm in the middle of the city. With an interior reminiscent of a 100-year-old main beam, thatched-roof house structure, a small garden, and a traditional market, it creates a serene atmosphere like a folk village. It neatly provides hearty Korean menus such as Stir-fried Pork (Jeyuk-bokkeum), Assorted Pancakes (Modum-jeon), Soup with Rice (Gukbap), and Galbi dishes along with various side dishes. Equipped with spacious seating and private rooms, it is also well-suited for family dining, corporate gatherings, and meals with foreign guests.

title: CAMEL’S KITCHEN
short_description: This restaurant presents a variety of pesco-vegan dishes inspired by Thai cuisine and other Asian flavors. With its charming Mangwon touch reflected in both the menu and the space, it has become a beloved spot among visitors. Using mushrooms and tofu to capture not only flavor but also texture, the restaurant was even selected for Taste of Seoul.

title: CU Seongsu Dessert Park Branch
short_description: CU Seongsu Dessert Park Branch is a K-dessert-specialized convenience store opened in Seongsu-dong. It expands dessert products by about 30% compared to regular stores and operates a curation zone gathering popular desserts. A DIY experience of making your own dessert using an air fryer, whipped cream, and toppings is also available. Equipped with a smoothie machine and a fresh fruit kiosk, you can enjoy shopping and experiences together.

title: Byeoryangjip
short_description:
This restaurant offers the essence of Korean beef offal barbecue, with its richly flavored grilled large intestine (daechang) as a standout. A proven

favorite visited by many celebrities, it has also been listed in the Blue Ribbon Survey, one of Korea’s leading restaurant guides. Open until 5 a.m., it’s an ideal place to stop by after enjoying the night view of Gangnam.

title: Moknojip
short_description: Known to every Eunpyeong resident, Moknojip offers a unique style of Bossam that differs from the usual boiled pork. Here, pork is stir-fried with green onions and wrapped in lettuce with red chili paste. The name “Mokno” refers to the long wooden planks once used as tables in old taverns, where customers placed their drinks and food. Inside the restaurant, writings left by the late father of the current owner remain intact, allowing visitors to feel a sense of nostalgia that keeps loyal patrons returning for decades.

title: ROOTED
short_description: This vegan café serves seasonal plant-based dishes and drinks. The nurungji hummus platter offers a rich, nutty harmony of crispy scorched rice and creamy hummus, while the watermelon “tuna” summer salad captures the refreshing taste of the season. Ever-changing seasonal dishes make this café a delightful spot to enjoy fresh vegan flavors year-round.

title: Before It Melts
short_description: <Before It Melts> is an ice cream specialty shop that makes its ice cream directly in the store every day. The name of the shop contains the meaning, 'staying in the most beautiful moment before the ice cream melts'. You can taste a variety of flavors and new flavors that come out each season.

title: Lamb Camp
short_description: This is a restaurant that serves only tender lamb without any gamey smell, so that even those trying lamb for the first time can enjoy it comfortably. The method of eating it wrapped in tortillas with homemade special sauce enhances the lamb's flavor even more deeply, creating a special culinary experience.

title: Himalaya Jonggak
short_description:
An Indian restaurant led by chefs from India and Nepal, it has long been a favorite lunch spot for office workers in the Jonggak area. Enjoying a meal

here while gazing out at the iconic Bosingak Pavilion offers a refreshing, exotic escape right in the heart of Seoul.

title: Sobamae
short_description: A charming restaurant run by a true soba master, capturing the unique vibe of Seongsu’s backstreets. The niku soba features a rich, beef-infused broth, while the zaru soba lets you savor the noodles’ pure aroma and flavor. Even the tempura is served gluten-free, making it a welcome choice for health-conscious diners.

title: Hyeongje Yukhoe Main
short_description: Located in the Yukhoe Alley, this traditional restaurant specializes in Yukhoe, a Korean-style raw beef dish. Thinly sliced fresh beef is served with savory seasonings, offering a tender texture and rich flavor. As a unique Korean delicacy, Yukhoe combines fresh ingredients and meticulous preparation to deliver a mouthful of nutty aroma and umami.

title: Hippo Brunch House
short_description:
Hippo Brunch House is a Yeonnam-dong brunch café run by a team of chefs with experience ranging from hotels to Michelin-starred restaurants. The café focuses on expertise and quality, making its own dressings and sauces using fresh and safe ingredients. In line with its “Hippo” concept, it serves large, hearty portions.


With its spacious interior, the café is ideal for visits with pets or children.

title: Travel writer's Azit
short_description: This Italian restaurant is run by a professional travel writer who has visited over 150 countries. Alongside a wide variety of pizzas, pastas, and risottos, the menu also includes Halal-friendly options and Korean dishes, inspired by the owner’s global experiences. Adding to the charm, the restaurant is decorated with souvenirs from around the world, creating an atmosphere full of discovery.

title: Lee Seok-deok Raw Noodle Pasta
short_description: This restaurant, run by Chef Lee Seokdeok, a graduate of an Italian culinary school, boasts exceptionally high quality, to the point of supplying fresh hand-pulled noodles nationwide daily. While pasta prices can often exceed ten thousand won elsewhere, their white wine and oil pasta is priced at just three thousand nine hundred won. To savor authentic Italian pasta at an affordable price, visit Lee Seok-deok Raw Noodle Pasta.

title: The Kitchen Asia Hongdae
short_description: This is a traditional Indian restaurant in Hongdae. With a wide variety of set menus, it offers a refined way to experience authentic Indian cuisine all at once, making it popular with both tourists and locals. The weekday lunch menu, in particular, is known for its reasonable prices and generous portions, making it an easy and satisfying choice for lunchtime.

title: Pub Whitney
short_description:
Pub Whitney is a well-known destination among baseball fans, celebrated for its craft beer and cocktail selection. Originally a high-end café in the 1990s and a popular dating spot, Whitney later became a 24-hour café and a beloved retreat for late-night visitors until the mid-2010s. Today, it has transformed into a vibrant pub that retains the original name “Whitney.”

The pub offers a wide range of unique and refreshing international beers, an extensive selection of whiskies, wines curated with food pairings and ambiance in mind, over 100 cocktails, as well as a variety of non-alcoholic beverages and mocktails for non-drinkers. With a large indoor screen for live sports, it’s a perfect hangout spot for game nights.

title: Everest Restaurant Dongdaemun
short_description: Run by a Nepali couple to share the flavors and culture of Nepal, this traditional restaurant offers a special culinary experience with rich flavors created by diverse spices and a tandoor oven. The interior, decorated with folk items and Nepali-style ornaments, conveys the atmosphere of the homeland.

title: ASHLEY QUEENS SEONGSU NAKNAK BRANCH
short_description:
Want to immerse yourself in the Korean lifestyle? Dine where Koreans really line-up! Ashley Queens is Korea's No. 1 Buffet Brand that serves 20 million customers yearly. With over 260 seats, Ashley Queens Seongsu Naknak Branch accommodates all occasions. Come with your friends, family and loved ones or by yourself!


100 Minutes of Unlimited Food, Come Enjoy our 130 Menus and pair with the drink of your choice!

From Korean delicacies to Western favorites, try new flavors while indulging in your favorites.

title: Mohssens Sweets Daehak-ro
short_description: The signature menu items here are kaymak, which is called 'heavenly dessert' for its soft and creamy texture, and kunafa, a premium dessert popular in the Middle East. Additionally, thanks to the excellent coffee, this is a perfect place to enjoy sweet desserts alongside coffee after a meal.

title: Myeongdong Busanjib
short_description: This is a representative halal Korean restaurant located in the heart of Myeongdong, offering everyday Korean flavors such as jjigae (stew), bibimbap (mixed rice), and ganjang-gejang (soy sauce marinated raw crab) prepared according to strict halal standards, providing a trustworthy and comfortable culinary experience. This is a must-visit place if you want to experience the true charm of Korean food in Seoul.

title: Cochon Tonkatsu
short_description: Located near Exit 3 of Sinchon Station, close to the Hyundai Department Store, Cochon Tonkatsu is renowned for its excellent value for money and exceptional taste. This place specializes exclusively in one item - tonkatsu (pork cutlet). You'll receive a hearty meal of one piece of tonkatsu, rice, soup, and salad when you order the basic menu. Experience a meal overflowing with cost-effectiveness at Cochon Tonkatsu, where the crispy coating on the tonkatsu tantalizes your appetite.

title: Daelim Warehouse Gallery in Seongsu-dong
short_description:
Daelim Warehouse is a cultural complex that preserves the original structure and finishing of a 1970s rice mill, featuring elements such as a gabled roof, red bricks, and steel columns. It has become a landmark in Seongsu-dong, offering a unique blend of café, bar, dining, and gallery space.


Visitors can enjoy curated exhibitions hosted and organized by Daelim Warehouse, and the gallery is open during café operating hours. The venue’s open, industrial vibe creates a distinctive atmosphere for art lovers and coffee enthusiasts alike.

title: KERVAN Cafe, Dessert & Brunch
short_description: This dessert & brunch cafe allows you to savor unique Turkish-style coffee and tea sip by sip, offering a diverse array of desserts including creamy kaymak, kaymak muhallebi (similar to yogurt), Turkish cookies, and baklava.

title: Jingogae Dongdaemun
short_description: Jingogae Dongdaemun is a Korean restaurant that won the Grand Prize at the National Culinary Competition in 1974. It offers a variety of Korean dishes such as galbijjim (braised beef short ribs), jeongol (hot pot), gejang (marinated crab), and bulgogi (marinated beef). Particularly, their galbijjim is slow-cooked for a long time with medicinal herbs, boasting a deep flavor and tender texture, making it a menu favorite loved by people of all ages. Located near Dongdaemun Station, it can be enjoyed alongside a stroll along the Seoul City Wall.

title: Makinochaya Black 31 Lotte World Tower Branch
short_description: Makinochaya Black 31 is the premium branch of the renowned buffet restaurant Makinochaya, located on the 31st floor of the Lotte World Tower. Here, you can enjoy panoramic views of Seoul's beautiful landscapes, including the Hangang River and the Seokchon Lake. The restaurant offers higher culinary satisfaction with various barbecue live stations, unique menu items served at each table, and signature dishes prepared by experienced chefs from top-tier hotels. To dine at Makinochaya Black 31, reservations are required. After making a reservation, following the visitor regulations, you can obtain an entry pass from the information desk at the EAST GATE entrance of Lotte World Tower.

title: sobb
short_description: Wiee, a popular cafe in Seogwipo, Jeju, has newly opened in Hannam dong, Seoul under the name sobb. The cafe space and the brunch and dining restaurant space are operated separately, and pets are allowed on the terrace seats. As the cafe opens at 7:30 in the morning on both weekdays and weekends, many customers visit and there may be waiting times.

title: Antique Coffee Yeonnam Branch
short_description: As its name suggests, Antique Coffee is a coffee and dessert café brand that aims to deliver the value of deep, meaningful moments. Every day, professional baristas and pâtissiers craft sophisticated and delicious top-quality coffee and desserts. Signature menu items include Dirty & Cream Coffee, Cherry Chocolat Cake, and Dirty & Cream Croissant. The interior is adorned with bright flowers, creating a refined antique and elegant atmosphere.

title: BBQ YUL Gangnam Branch
short_description: BBQ YUL is a premium Korean barbecue restaurant that serves carefully selected pork weighing over 98 kilograms, aged for 336 hours to create a deep flavor and tender texture. The attentive service includes staff grilling the meat for customers, complemented by a variety of side dishes and events. Loved by both locals and travelers, it offers the finest experience of traditional Korean aged barbecue.

title: Lumbini Restaurant
short_description: This restaurant offers both authentic Indian and Nepali cuisine. Its signature dish is chicken malai kebab, a tender barbecue made by marinating chicken in a sauce of cashew nuts, cheese, cream, and spices. A wide variety of curries is also available, giving diners the fun of choosing their favorites.

title: Hoonyook
short_description: Hoonyook is a specialty aged pork BBQ spot tucked inside Haebangchon’s Sinhung Market. Guests can enjoy the nutty flavor and tender texture of aged pork cuts, with the neck cut (moksal) being the most popular menu item. Meat is ordered per portion per person. During busy hours, dining time is limited to 1 hour and 30 minutes. Corkage fee is 20,000 KRW per bottle. Due to potential wait times, it is recommended to reserve in advance and explore Sinhung Market while waiting.

title: Dongdaemun Grilled Fish Alley
short_description: 'This is the only grilled fish alley in Seoul, formed by restaurants specializing in charcoal-grilled fish dishes. Around 1979, the number of grilled fish restaurants gradually increased, offering mackerel, Spanish mackerel, and yellow croaker grilled over charcoal braziers. In the 1990s, the alley thrived due to workers from nearby sewing factories, and even today it attracts visitors of all ages, both domestic and international.

title: Gyeongsong
short_description: A modern-style barbecue restaurant specializing in charcoal-grilled, marinated beef short ribs. Its signature garlic-marinated galbi brings together the bold flavor of garlic—much loved by Koreans—with the savory richness of beef. Assorted set menus featuring different cuts are also available. For a taste of the latest trends in K-barbecue, this spot is not to be missed.

title: Star Samarkand
short_description: One of the highlights of Dongdaemun’s Central Asian street, this restaurant stays true to traditional Uzbek cooking methods. From plov, a traditional pilaf, and shashlik, skewered grilled meat, to borscht, a hearty soup loved across Central Asia, it also offers a wide selection of Uzbek juices and teas to broaden the dining experience.

title: The Queen’s Guard
short_description: The Queen's Guard, located on Seosulla-gil, is an English-style pub. It offers a selection of infused gin, various London dry gins, British beers, ciders, and other lesser-known British drinks and foods. The terrace seating, overlooking the cobblestone streets, is highly popular for enjoying the ambiance. As a popular pub, it tends to have long wait times even before opening. Every year, a Christmas event is held that requires first-come, first-served reservations.

title: HHSS House
short_description: Nestled in Mangwon-dong, the design studio and cafe HHSS House was created with the idea that having trees right in front of you would be a perfect sight while working. True to this vision, the interior is thoughtfully arranged with a row of seats facing the lush greenery outside the large windows, providing a refreshing and tranquil view. The gentle fragrance of incense sticks fills the space, adding a soothing touch. The menu offers a delightful selection of beverages and charming desserts, with a range of alcoholic drinks available in the evening. While it’s not a spot you might casually discover, it’s a hidden gem for both focused work sessions and quiet solo visits. Tucked behind the building and away from the main street, the entrance is elusive. Head up to the 3rd floor, look for the door marked with a red ‘H’ made from tape, and step inside to experience the unique and welcoming ambiance of HHSS House.

title: Manis Kitchen
short_description: This unique Itaewon restaurant combines Korean street food with halal cuisine. You can enjoy familiar dishes from K-dramas such as tteokbokki, gimbap, and fish cake prepared in halal style, and it is considered one of the places that best captures the multicultural spirit of Itaewon.

title: Palgyejip
short_description: Palgyejip is a Korean cuisine specialty restaurant offering flash-frozen pork belly, various types of hot pot rice, and stews, as well as colorful and unique side menus that add fusion to Korean food through Palgyejip's own reinterpretation. Enjoy Korean food while feeling the tranquil atmosphere provided by the Hanok interior and the urban camping sensibility felt in the outdoor space.

title: Hongs Jjukkumi Hongdae Branch
short_description: Hongs Jjukkumi, a long-standing jjukkumi (spicy stir-fried baby octopus) restaurant in Hongdae, attracts locals and foreigners alike. Despite its popularity, the spacious restaurant ensures that wait times are short. The signature dish is jjukkumi, but you can also enjoy a variety of combinations such as jjukkumi with samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) jjukkumi with shrimp, and jjukkumi with chadol (beef brisket). You can choose the level of spiciness, making it accessible for those who can't handle very spicy food. Additionally, a variety of side dishes pair well with jjukkumi and help balance the spiciness. A special treat is the complimentary fried rice you can enjoy after your meal. The restaurant also offers English menus, making ordering convenient for foreign visitors.

title: Gosame Hapjeong
short_description: This Korean restaurant specializes in grilled fish, serving satisfying meals with fresh seafood cooked over an open flame. The grilled mackerel, bursting with savory flavor, and the spicy stir-fried squid are must-try favorites. Well-known among international travelers looking for halal-friendly Korean food, the restaurant has earned glowing reviews from countless visitors.

title: Persian Palace
short_description: Curry with rice, characterized by a slightly spicy taste, is the signature menu. The spicy level can be adjusted to suit the customer's taste, so even those who are not good at spicy food can enjoy it without any worry.

title: Root
short_description:
Root aims for a deep understanding and reinterpretation of food culture. The name "Root" is a reversed stacking of the Korean characters ㅅㅜㄹ (sul), meaning alcohol. Root explores the origins of all food and sheds new light on familiar culinary traditions to present them from a fresh perspective.

Signature dishes include Hangjeong Ssam (pork jowl wraps), charcoal-grilled Yukhoe (Korean-style beef tartare), bite-sized dishes, and a pairing menu featuring over 150 varieties of traditional Korean liquor.

title: Geumsu Bokguk Jamsil Sofitel
short_description: This is the Seoul branch of Geumsu Bokguk, a renowned pufferfish restaurant from Busan founded in 1970 and featured in the Michelin Guide. It offers various dishes showcasing different types of pufferfish, with musttry favorites including the clean and rich-tasting Brown Backed Puffer Soup and the crispy Fried Yellowfin Puffer.

title: Mullae Pocha 1422
short_description: Famous for its rooftop setting, Mullae Pocha 1422 offers the charm of outdoor dining (yajang) from a rooftop space. The head chef, with over 30 years of experience in Chinese cuisine, serves not only Chinese-style dishes but also a variety of other menu items. The bar operates on a self-service system with kiosk pre-payment: choose a table based on your party size, pay at the kiosk using your table number, and pick up your drinks, gas burner, and table setup yourself.

title: Hanok Gukbap 'Songam Onban'
short_description: Songam Onban is a newly born Korean restaurant based on a 100-year-old Hanok in Ikseon-dong and the deep history of Songam. Reinterpreting the tradition and dignity of Songam, which was once considered one of the top three yojeong (high-end traditional restaurants) in Korea, with a modern sensibility, it has been renewed as a famous restaurant in Ikseon-dong. It presents a variety of Korean menus such as Dwaeji Gukbap (Pork Soup with Rice), Suyuk (Boiled Pork Slices), Jeon (Korean Pancakes), Mandu (Dumplings), and traditional liquor. We hope you spend a special time where the history and gastronomy of Ikseon-dong harmonize in a serene Hanok atmosphere.

title: Oldy’s Taco Euljiro Main Branch
short_description:
Oldy’s Taco, famous in Euljiro for its tacos, operates two branches in the area. The main branch is very small but attracts long queues of customers. The second branch, located in an alley, offers a larger space with faster service.


Although most orders are taken to-go due to limited seating, dining inside is also available. All dishes contain cilantro by default, but it can be removed upon request. However, the cilantro flavor at Oldy’s Taco is not overpowering, so it is recommended to try it together.

title: Mailroom
short_description: Nestled in the alleys of Sindang-dong Market, Mailroom is an espresso bar with a unique mailbox concept. Here, you write your desired menu on a piece of paper and receive a numbered mailbox key. When your order is ready, you open the corresponding mailbox to collect your menu, replicating the thrill of receiving a letter. This special ordering method brings the excitement of opening a mailbox to your coffee experience. At Mailroom, you can enjoy coffee and write letters, creating memorable moments in your own way. Furthermore, Mailroom is a popular hotspot known for its vintage interior and inviting atmosphere, making it an ideal date spot. The signature menu features espresso coffee, espresso-based cocktails, and a variety of desserts that perfectly complement the coffee.

title: Cobbler Yeonhui
short_description: In a residential area in Yeonhui-dong, there’s a building that, from the outside, looks like an ordinary house. But when you step through the green gate, an outdoor seating area in the garden warmly welcomes you. Cobbler Yeonhui, a whiskey and cocktail bar, is a remodeled residence that used to be a private home. Here, there’s no menu. Instead, guests order their drinks through a conversation with the skilled bartenders, allowing them to discover personal tastes and drinks they may not have known about. Of course, you can also request specific drinks. With trustworthy bartending skills and a charming atmosphere, this place offers more than enough reasons to visit.

title: Sammijung
short_description: Sammijeong is nestled between old buildings in Euljiro and is known for its nostalgic yajang (outdoor dining) atmosphere. The space is divided into indoor and outdoor seating, but most customers opt for the outdoor area to enjoy the full yajang experience. The main (and only) dish is grilled pork belly (samgyeopsal), with optional add-ons like soybean paste stew (doenjang-jjigae) and fried rice. It's the only place among Euljiro’s yajang samgyeopsal spots that offers a "hidden menu" of fried rice—highly recommended after finishing your meat. As a popular hotspot in Euljiro, expect a wait.

title: Palgakdo Main Branch
short_description: Palgeokdo is a restaurant specializing in charcoal-grilled chicken special cuts. The meat, pre-grilled over charcoal, is tender and juicy. It offers a variety of rare chicken parts that you might not have tried before, along with delicious side dishes and sauces. Inspired by the Octagon Pavilion (Palgakjeong), Palgeokdo features unique exterior and interior designs, making it a great place for dates and group gatherings.

title: Thweet
short_description: Thweet is a refined dessert space designed for adults who find coffee too light and day drinking a bit too much. This unique ice cream bar offers premium ice creams infused with whiskey, along with a selection of sophisticated desserts, all served in an elegant atmosphere. If you're looking to try something different, Thweet is worth a visit. Please note that while it’s a dessert bar, its signature menu features whiskey ice cream—therefore, entry is limited to adults only.

title: Myungga Tteokjip
short_description: This rice cake shop has been in business for two generations, using a recipe inherited from his aunt in 1980. When the current owner was 14 years old, his father died and he and his mother started working in the rice cake shop. Every day at 2 a.m., they prepare to make rice cakes and continue to make rice cakes the old-fashioned way. Their red bean paste is aged for 24 hours with radish and mulberry leaves, then boiled for eight hours. Glutinous rice cakes are the most famous, but they also make rare rice cakes.

title: SWALLOW BAKERY & CAFE
short_description: This is a vegan bakery café and grocery that pursues a zero-waste philosophy, reducing plastic use and incorporating recycled materials. Its clean, sophisticated interior and wide glass windows create a relaxing atmosphere. Here, you can enjoy meals, desserts, and drinks that are not only eco-friendly but also delicious.

title: Dotori Yongsan Branch
short_description:
Located in Yongsan's popular Yongridan-gil area, Dotori Yongsan is a charming bakery café that resembles a cozy cottage from a fairy tale. With its whimsical design and warm, forest-like ambiance, the café offers a peaceful and inviting atmosphere that feels straight out of an animated film.


Dotori Yongsan is kid-friendly, making it a comfortable space for families. The café also welcomes dogs, as long as they are kept in a carrier.

title: BOOK AND REST
short_description: According to people's different preferences for rest, we divided the space into Stay Zone, Rest Zone, and Private Room, allowing each person to spend time in their preferred way, with emphasis on the space. The single-person private rooms operate on an hourly basis, allowing you to rest quietly in your own space or conduct work or meetings. Additional hourly fees apply when using these spaces.

title: MANOKAMANA Daehak-ro
short_description: This is an Indian cuisine specialty restaurant that serves authentic Indian dishes prepared directly by local Indian chefs. The moderately spicy chicken makhani is particularly popular among families with children, as even young diners who don't handle spicy food well can enjoy it comfortably.

title: Independent Bookstore Odd's Book
short_description: The recording bookstore, Odd's Book, is an unmanned, reservation-based bookstore and book cafe where you can enjoy reading and contemplation in a quiet and private atmosphere. The Room of Records on the 1st floor is a space to leave something behind through writing or drawing. The 2nd floor is a secret study decorated like a secret hideout dreamed of in childhood. Each space can be used by reserving on an hourly basis. Recommended books by MBTI type and books fitting the keywords of the month are curated, and various props can be purchased.

title: SAMSAMSAM Lotteworld mall Branch
short_description: SAMSAMSAM Lotte World Mall Branch builds on the success of the original SAMSAMSAM in Yongridan-gil. This spot offers top-notch dishes like pasta, salads, risotto, and lasagna, prepared by chefs with experience at Michelin 3-star restaurants in the U.S. The Lotte World Mall Branch features exclusive items such as lasagna, Sam House steak, jambon beurre pasta, porcini gnocchi, and shrimp oil pasta, drawing many visitors. The interior creates a whimsical, fairy-tale ambiance, with plenty of space between tables for a comfortable dining experience. For added convenience, use the elevator near the Lotte World Mall Aquarium to access the restaurant.

title: Vegan Insa
short_description: This vegan restaurant harmonizes with the unique ambiance of a traditional hanok, conveying a refined sensibility and depth. Featuring clean, sophisticated dishes rooted in Korean cuisine with subtle variations, it offers a distinguished culinary experience. After exploring the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, dining here completes the day as a cultured and memorable experience.

title: Bricksand Shinsegae Duty Free Myeongdong Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: SAMARKAND
short_description: Beloved by the Central Asian community seeking the taste of home, this restaurant offers authentic Uzbek cuisine. Traditional dishes, prepared with unique spices and authentic methods, deliver not only rich flavors but also the aroma of culture, offering diners a distinctive culinary experience.

title: Home-Cooked Meal Gim Seonsaeng
short_description: This restaurant offers the essence of halal Korean cuisine, presenting Korea's everyday home-cooked meals in neat, traditional table settings. With dishes ranging from bulgogi, japchae, and kimchi jjigae to halal budae jjigae(Korean army stew), Muslim visitors can comfortably enjoy Korea's diverse food culture without any concerns.

title: Huirak Galchi
short_description: This is the oldest establishment in Namdaemun Market's hairtail alley, widely known for its braised hairtail fish with a spicy yet sweet flavor. It's a renowned spot that provides a satisfying dining experience to many people with generous portions and deep, rich flavors.

title: Dalmaji Gwangjang Barbecue
short_description: Dalmaji Gwangjang Barbecue is a K-BBQ house specializing in made-to-order barbecue, situated in a spacious plaza under the moonlight that unfolds when you follow the narrow alleyways of Euljiro 3-ga, which are bustling with people at night. Instead of reheating pre-cooked chicken, fresh chicken is cooked immediately upon ordering, allowing you to experience charcoal barbecue with moist juices and rich flavors. Furthermore, fresh, perfectly balanced draft beer boasts a fantastic harmony with the freshly made barbecue.

title: Camouflage
short_description: Camouflage, meaning 'disguise,' is a vegan restaurant in Itaewon that serves soy-based plant chicken dishes so convincing that they are nearly indistinguishable from real chicken unless you're told they're vegan. Their orange chicken, featuring a sweet and tangy orange sauce, has been a beloved signature dish for a long time.

title: Dojeongyukgwan
short_description: Located near Gangnam Station in Seoul, this premium Korean dining restaurant offers freshly milled rice pot dishes and aged meat with refined presentation. The nutty flavor of rice germ and the deep richness of meat come together to create a beloved meal for gourmets. Each table setting at Dojeongyukgwan, completed with honest ingredients and the delicate temperature of fire, embodies the essence of Korean cuisine. It is a place that presents a new gastronomic experience representing Seoul.

title: Maji
short_description:
This restaurant specializes in traditional Korean vegetarian cuisine, offering distinctive dishes that highlight the natural flavors of vegetables,

such as burdock japchae and pear naengmyeon, leaving a lasting impression. In particular, the lunch and dinner sets are thoughtfully composed to provide a rich experience of a full Korean meal.

title: Saffron Restaurant
short_description: This restaurant specializes in Arabic cuisine prepared exclusively with halal-certified meat. Featuring unique dishes like Mizza and Chicken Handi, it offers an authentic taste of traditional Arabic flavors.

title: Seochon Dagwabang
short_description: Seochon Dagwabang is a Hanok cafe near Gyeongbokgung Station where you can leisurely enjoy traditional elegance. Savor traditional tea and handmade traditional Korean desserts in a Hanok courtyard that feels like coming to a small garden.

title: Yankees Grill
short_description: Yankees Grill is located in Mullae Creative Village and is a representative original restaurant of Mullae dong that has firmly established itself since the early days of the creative village. It insists on the wet aging method, and most steaks are cooked using a grill. It offers steaks that anyone can enjoy 부담없이 at an affordable price of 250 grams for 25,500 won, along with cost effective dishes. You can enjoy American style food in an interior that feels like dining in the United States.

title: iftar
short_description: This restaurant offers a variety of traditional Korean dishes prepared using ingredients certified under strict halal standards. Set against the serene backdrop of Gyeongbokgung Palace, the space is a renovated hanok where you can savor the deep flavors of traditional Korean cuisine and fully experience the unique atmosphere and cultural resonance of Seoul.

title: Lepak Laa
short_description: Lepak laa, which means 'let's relax leisurely' in Malay, is a restaurant where you can enjoy authentic Malaysian cuisine in a comfortable atmosphere, just as its name suggests. Through signature dishes such as Nasi Lemak, Mee Goreng, Satay, and Laksa, you can experience exotic flavors that are difficult to find in Korea.

title: Green Field Restaurant
short_description: This restaurant showcases the appeal of vegetarian Korean cuisine by serving traditional dishes in plant-based versions. The mushroom dumpling hot pot offers a rich harmony of earthy mushroom aroma and deep broth flavor, while the noodle soup with perilla seeds combines a nutty broth with chewy noodles for a hearty taste. Vegetarian dumplings are also among the popular choices.

title: Busanjib Fried Chicken
short_description: This is a place that serves Korean-style chicken using halal food. The freshly fried crispy chicken is popular, as well as the intensely spicy seasoned chicken.

title: Summer Lane
short_description: With its sunny yellow awnings and large murals depicting beaches and waves, Summer Lane is a lively brunch spot loved by locals for its genuine Australian vibe, so much so that there is often a line to get in. Opening early at 7:30 AM,  it's perfect for travelers looking to start their day ahead of the crowd. Don’t miss their signature croissant French toast and waffle eggs Benedict for a truly elevated brunch experience.

title: Ferments
short_description: Ferments started as a kombucha specialty shop in Seogyo-dong in 2021, and it has since evolved into a vegan restaurant now located in Yongsan. What sets Ferments apart is its commitment to offering healthy food made from plant-based ingredients that are fermented in-house without using chemical seasonings or artificial additives. From 12 PM to 5 PM, it operates as a kitchen and café, then transitions into an atmospheric kitchen and wine bar after 5 PM. The rooftop features an outdoor terrace where visitors can enjoy wine while enjoying city views on pleasant days. Inside, the space is filled with books, DVDs, and charming decor items that line the shelves, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. On special occasions, such as during the "Ferments Daydream" event, guests can enjoy meals while watching performances by various artists, making it a must-visit spot for those who love music and natural wine.

title: Heukwoojeong Gangnam
short_description: This restaurant offers a premium beef experience, featuring only the finest cuts of Kobe beef and Hanwoo. The same high standards are applied not just to the meat but also to every ingredient—from rice and water to noodles—ensuring a dining experience worthy of Gangnam’s luxury. From the moment you step inside, the refined atmosphere makes you feel like a truly special guest.

title: Cotati
short_description: Located in Haebangchon, the natural gelato shop Cotati sells gelato made from pure, natural ingredients without artificial colors or synthetic flavors. You can enjoy the unique taste of each gelato menu item, with new flavors to discover with the changing seasons. Ice cream for dogs is also available, and the store is pet-friendly. Packaging in cups or cones is unavailable, but you can choose from 2, 3, or 4 flavors. When packaging ice cream, the maximum transport time is 1 hour and 30 minutes.

title: Oeyang-Gan
short_description: A famous meat restaurant in Sadang known for its long queues, it offers a unique combination of assorted beef specialty cuts, pen shell scallops, and aged kimchi grilled together at the table. After enjoying the barbecue, finish with brisket soybean paste ramen or brisket fried rice—a satisfying way to unwind after a busy day.

title: Makinochaya Mapo Branch
short_description: Makinochaya Mapo Branch, under the slogan 'From My Sea to Your Table,' is a premium buffet restaurant that carefully selects premium menus, including Korean, Western, Chinese, Japanese, and desserts, to offer customers. The aim is to provide a simple ‘buffet’ experience and a 'valuable' and 'meaningful' daily experience through food. Rather than being a flashy and trendy place, the focus is on introducing 'honest and wholesome food' and creating an environment where customers can enjoy the food they desire in a 'hygienic and safe' manner.

title: HANI KALGUKSU
short_description: Hani Kalguksu has become a popular hot spot for visitors seeking the best restaurants in Sindang-dong, blending retro charm with a youthful and stylish atmosphere. The exterior resembles a modest old alley eatery, but upon entering, guests are greeted by a surprisingly modern and refined interior. It is well loved for its spicy pollock roe and tripe kalguksu and rich ox bone broth kalguksu. Its fame and flavor have been featured in numerous TV programs and by well-known YouTubers and celebrities.

title: MAPO-OK
short_description: Mapo-ok is a Seolleongtang restaurant that has been in operation since 1949 for three generations. The restaurant’s soup, made only from beef without any additives, is highly regarded for its rich and pure flavor. The building, used since the 1970s, preserves the traces of the times in Yonggang-dong, Mapo-gu, and has been designated as a Future Heritage of Seoul. It was frequented by famous singers of the past, including Lee Mi-ja, Ha Chun-hwa, and Nam Jin. It is said that the composer of the song “Mapo Terminal” by the Eunbangul Sisters drew inspiration while dining here.

title: Dekad
short_description: Seochon has a spot where you can savor European-style brunch and dinner. By day, you can enjoy a variety of brunch options, including Dekad’s signature pancakes, while the evening offers carefully crafted seasonal dishes paired with a wide selection of drinks. The seasonal menu changes with the times, allowing guests to embrace the flavors of each season. Outdoor seating is also available, letting you dine in the fresh air—a unique feature of Dekad. As night falls, the ambiance is enhanced by perfectly set lighting, creating a cozy atmosphere in which to enjoy Seochon’s nightlife. The friendly service and warm hospitality further elevate the experience, ensuring guests feel satisfied.

title: Cinora Yeonhui Branch
short_description: Cinora Yeonhui is the third branch of the popular brunch café, following Seochon and Bukchon. Inspired by a hotel in Sri Lanka, the space embodies Cinora’s signature warmth and understated elegance. With a vintage wood-toned interior and classic decorative touches, the café offers a serene atmosphere perfect for a leisurely brunch experience.

title: Yukjeon Gukbap Daehak-ro
short_description: Rice soup (gukbap) is a traditional Korean dish combining soup and rice, and is one of the country’s signature foods. It’s a staple meal that warms you up on cold days. Along with rice soup and buckwheat noodles, you can also enjoy various dishes such as pan-fried beef slices (yukjeon).

title: Gurkha India Restaurant
short_description: This authentic restaurant is directly operated by locals from India and Nepal, delivering genuine local flavors intact. It serves unique Indian dishes that can typically only be tasted in their home countries, such as mutton curry and malai kofta curry, providing a distinctive culinary experience.

title: Somunnan Seongsu Gamjatang
short_description:
The restaurant operates in two separate indoor spaces, providing plenty of seating, but it’s still a popular spot with a wait. There are no numbered tickets or queue slips, so guests are guided in order while seated in the waiting area.

There are designated seats for solo diners, so if you're alone, you can go directly to the counter without waiting in line.

Open 24 hours a day, year-round, so you can enjoy a meal anytime. Takeout is also available.

title: Chammallo Jotsudak 273
short_description: This restaurant lets you fully enjoy the charm of K-chicken, loved worldwide. In a clean and modern setting, it serves boneless chicken that is both light and crispy. A highlight is the option to choose your preferred cut, such as breast or thigh meat. Come and see for yourself why it has been a longtime favorite among local residents.

title: Taejo Daerim Gamjaguk
short_description: Located at the entrance of Eungam-dong Potato Soup Street, this restaurant was the first to open on the street. Its name, “Taejo Daerim Gamjaguk,” was inspired by King Taejo of the Joseon Dynasty. While most people call the dish “Gamjatang,” restaurants in this area refer to it as “Gamjaguk” after the owner, Mr. Bae Ik-hoon, suggested using the term to encourage humility among neighboring restaurateurs. It is the only restaurant in the area open 24 hours a day, maintaining long-standing ties with early-morning regulars.

title: Happy Brick Sand
short_description: Bricksand is a healthy dessert made with high-quality ingredients and a brick-shaped design. It offers freshness derived from good ingredients, a fantastic texture with a crispy exterior and moist interior, and a liveliness that can only be felt in the store. Try pairing the sweet and smooth Bricksand with coffee or tea. It's also perfect as an elegant dessert gift for your loved ones. The desserts are made diligently every day with wholesome and high-quality ingredients.

title: Rhubarb
short_description: Located in Yeonnam-dong,  Rhubarb is a brunch café offering healthy meals made with fresh ingredients. Its signature menu is the carrot pasta topped with pollack roe and carrot râpé, highly recommended for those seeking unique brunch options. A one-meal-per-person order is required, and all beverages are discounted with a food order.

title: lick sip
short_description: Lick sip is a café and bar designed for adults, offering a unique dessert experience featuring whiskey ice cream and wine smoothies. It’s a cozy, antique-style space perfect for a quiet visit, even solo. Beyond its signature whiskey ice cream, the menu includes coffee, whiskey, wine, and beer, allowing guests to enjoy a wide variety of drinks in a relaxed setting.

title: Babjitgo Tiurim (Cooking Rice and Brewing Tea)
short_description: Babjitgo Tiurim is a Korean restaurant with a clean, non-stimulating taste, and it is a place where tea is brewed, rice is cooked, and alcohol is aged with sincere hands. It uses natural ingredients made into seasonings for all dishes, and provides more natural food using ingredients sourced from various production areas nationwide.

title: Dongyang Tea House Suraksan Branch
short_description: A calm and refined tea house with an atmosphere reminiscent of a traditional herbal medicine shop offers Korean traditional teas such as Ssanghwa tea, as well as coffee and various herbal teas. The signature Ssanghwa tea can be chosen in either a rich or mild flavor according to your preference. Another popular menu item is the traditional red bean shaved ice, topped with mildly sweet red beans and rice cakes, which can be enjoyed in all seasons. For an even more flavorful experience, try adding the nutty seeds, roasted grain powder, and condensed milk that come on the side.

title: Sun Tomato Ramen
short_description: Sun Tomato Ramen is a ramen restaurant specializing in a unique style of Japanese ramen with fresh tomatoes added. The richly simmered tomato broth delivers a refreshing yet deeply savory flavor, harmonizing perfectly with the noodles for a clean yet full-bodied taste. Its light, non-greasy flavor appeals to all ages, and the spiciness level can be adjusted to suit personal preferences, making it an excellent choice for those who enjoy spicy food.  If you're looking for a special ramen experience during your trip to Seoul, be sure to stop by!

title: Italy Two-Story House
short_description: This fusion Western restaurant showcases the expertise of a chef with 30 years of experience in Western cuisine and is well-known among Yongsan locals as a must-visit destination on Yongridan-gil. Featuring interior design that captures a scene straight from Beauty and the Beast, you can savor Italian fusion cuisine at reasonable prices within a romantic and elegant atmosphere.

title: Myeongdong Chaeum Hanjongshik
short_description: This halal restaurant specializes in traditional Korean table d’hote, offering a full set meal with 18 freshly prepared side dishes, soup, and stew made daily with care. The Korean table d’hote is a traditional course meal that showcases the variety and richness of Korean cuisine in one setting.

title: La Pluma & Bohemian
short_description: Lafluma Anbohemian, the originator of drip coffee in Korea, has been in business since 1990. Today, it's run by a first-generation Korean barista who took over from Mr. Park Yichu, and it's recommended to visit in person if you want to savor the true flavor of the coffee. While there are a variety of drip coffees available, the Ethiopian Geisha Forest coffee variety is the cafe's signature. If you're looking for a relaxing cup full of refreshing acidity and unique flavors, this is the place to go.

title: Room Temperature
short_description: Room Temperature is a vegan brunch café in Seoul that focuses on healthy meals centered around organic and vegan dishes. The café features a cozy space with a Nordic-style interior where guests can enjoy a relaxing dining experience. It also offers outdoor terrace seating, perfect for enjoying brunch in the fresh air on a clear day. Takeout discounts are available, and pets are welcome, allowing visitors to dine with their dogs. It is the perfect place to enjoy a relaxing moment with healthy food.

title: PalGakdo Seongsu Station
short_description: Grilled over charcoal, the dakgalbi(chicken BBQ) boasts a rich smoky flavor, with a texture that is crispy on the outside yet tender and juicy on the inside. The chicken neck meat is a special highlight—softer and more succulent than regular dakgalbi. With the staff grilling the meat for you, travelers can relax and enjoy without any worries.

title: Bricksand Gran Seoul Jonggak Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: HIVE PLAYGROUND
short_description: Remodeled from an inn built in 1970, Hive Playground was reborn to embody new culture and sensibility. Far from a simple cafe, the entire building acts like a piece of content, offering a sanctuary where you can experience inspiration beyond just staying. Feel free to explore and make special memories across the space: the 1st floor is a media gallery connecting brands and culture; the 2nd floor is a lifestyle space where fragrance and design coexist; the 3rd floor is a modern lounge filled with calm food and urban leisure; and the 4th floor is a space opening up to city views and sensibilities.

title: Seongsudarak
short_description: From the joy of finding the hidden entrance to the secret and special experience of climbing the attic stairs, Seongsudarak is a Western-style restaurant where you can enjoy delicious food made with care, along with a warm and cozy atmosphere filled with sunlight. In addition to pasta dishes, be sure to try Seongsu Darak’s signature omurice. As this restaurant is known for long waiting times, making a reservation in advance allows you to enter without waiting.

title: Daramgee Bar
short_description: Situated opposite the wall of the Jongmyo Shrine on Seosulla-gil, Daramgee Bar offers a comfortable evening dining experience with delicious drinks, food, and engaging conversations. Various traditional liquors are available. Please note that ordering alcoholic beverages is a requirement, and they don’t offer regular soju or beer. Additionally, the establishment features amusing ornaments throughout the venue, providing not only enjoyment for the palate but also for the eyes.

title: MaeHwa Lamb Skewers Myeongdong
short_description: This restaurant specializes in lamb, using only tender meat from young sheep under one year old. With its clean flavor and soft texture free of any gamey smell, it’s an easy choice for first-time diners and a great option for food lovers seeking something unique.

title: Busanjib KBBQ
short_description: This is a Korean-style meat restaurant using halal meat, where you can taste various cuts such as Korean beef sirloin, wagyu rib fingers, and lamb ribs alongside Korean-style side dishes. Located in the heart of Myeongdong, it's a popular destination that has been consistently loved by Muslim tourists.

title: Songane Dakhanmari
short_description: Songane Dakhanmari is a restaurant specializing in dakhanmari(whole chicken soup), a traditional Seoul dish. Customers enjoy dipping chicken and vegetables cooked in a rich, garlic-infused broth with seasoning, and can choose to eat it either plain or spicy according to their preference. Additionally, the remaining broth can be enhanced by adding kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) or porridge for a more fulfilling meal. The restaurant is renowned for its hearty, garlic-laden broth. The founder previously operated a rice set meal restaurant near Cheonggyecheon and decided to add dakhanmari at the encouragement of regular patrons, eventually evolving into a single-menu establishment. The interior is cozy and welcoming, featuring multilingual menus and guides on how foreigners can enjoy their meals, making it an ideal spot for both locals and tourists.

title: Korean Beef Omakase - WUMOK
short_description: WUMOK is a Korean beef omakase restaurant based on the core philosophy of fire (火), wood (木), beef (牛), and smoke. The name 'WUMOK' is derived from the combination of the characters for beef (牛) and wood (木), as well as beef (牛) and smoke, reflecting its concept. Through cooking methods such as genshiyaki and smoking, it newly interprets the essence of Korean beef. The dishes that harmonize the aroma of wood and premium beef stimulate sight, smell, and taste. With the motto 'A Table of Fire with Philosophy', it provides a special gastronomic experience for memorable occasions. With a corkage-free policy, guests can enjoy dining with their own wine.

title: Suyu Fish Cake Factory
short_description: The boss, a former fish cake factory owner, started the Suyu Fish Cake Factory in a small space in Suyu Market, and now his son is carrying on the tradition by learning the skills from his father. The owner even takes the weather into consideration when mixing the fish meat. The shop is famous for its fish cake bars and vegetable squares. The vegetable square fish cakes are especially popular because they require a lot of labor and delicate techniques.

title: Cheiljemyeonso Mugyo Branch
short_description: Cheiljemyeonso Mugyo Branch is a Korean dining brand that serves hearty and satisfying shabu-shabu and noodles during the day, and various gourmet dishes based on Korean cuisine with trendy traditional liquor in the evening. The restaurant is very spacious, and both indoor and outdoor seating is available. At lunchtime, the shabu-shabu and various side dishes attract many office workers. The well-prepared meal options and pleasant interior environment also make it a popular spot for families and groups.

title: Dotori Oven
short_description: Located in Seongsu, Dotori Oven is a dessert cafe that serves food calmly prepared by carefully timing and temping the oven without rushing in front of the fire. The menu is structured around oven-baked items. Popular items include financiers in various flavors and fresh Greek yogurt topped with abundant toppings, which we hope you enjoy in a comfortable and cozy cafe space.

title: aff seoul
short_description: aff Seoul, which stands for Asian Funky Flavor, is an Asian-local-based dining and wine bar located in Euljiro. It is ideal for enjoying natural wines. The restaurant offers a variety of seasonal dishes paired with wine and features a rooftop spanning the 3rd and 4th floors. Even if you're not well-versed in wine, a sommelier can recommend wines that suit your taste. The green curry at aff Seoul is particularly noteworthy.

title: Namdo Hansik Jeongdeunnim_Gounnim
short_description: Namdo Hansik Jeongdeunnim is a restaurant that shows the essence of traditional Korean dining, known as "hansang-charim.", that provides traditional Korean table settings and showcases a variety of Southern dishes using seafood and seaweed from Wando, Jeollanam-do. It features a bountiful array of dishes such as seasoned stingray, half-dried pollack, barley-dried yellow corvina, soy sauce marinated crab, allowing diners to enjoy a meal reminiscent of a festive feast from the countryside. Business meetings held here are said to be successful, as the generous and delicious food leaves a lasting impression, reflecting the dedication and care put into the traditional Korean table settings.

title: Starbucks Gyeongdong 1960 Branch
short_description: Located inside Gyeongdong Market, Starbucks Gyeongdong 1960 Branch is a special location remodeled from the original Gyeongdong Theater, built in 1960. The café retains the original tiered seating and stage layout, creating a nostalgic movie theater atmosphere. Order numbers are displayed on one of the walls, and the ceiling features unique interior design elements that add a playful touch. As it gets crowded on weekends, visiting on a weekday is recommended.

title: Blue Roof Town Hongdae Branch
short_description: With the signature menu, Suwon Wang Galbi, which is shaped like wings, LA Galbi, and free wine corkage service are also available. The interior design draws inspiration from the atmosphere of LA Koreatown, creating an inviting ambiance. Additionally, proficient English staff ensures a seamless experience for foreign visitors.

title: Cafe Haven
short_description: HAVEN means a sanctuary, providing a comfortable and happy space to everyone who visits alongside the slogan 'the place where people feel safe, secure and happy'. From the outside, it does not look like a traditional Hanok, but the moment you step inside and look up at the ceiling, the wooden structure of the Hanok is revealed, allowing you to feel a unique harmony between tradition and modernity.

title: IDA
short_description: This contemporary restaurant, located at the end of Seosulla-gil, is nestled in a picturesque spot ideal for a stroll. It offers creative cuisine using traditional Korean ingredients. Fresh seasonal ingredients evoke the essence of each season in the dishes. The restaurant's charm is its changing menus according to the seasons. Additionally, it is located very close to Jongmyo Shrine and Changdeokgung Palace, which boasts unique scenery each season, making it an excellent spot for a stroll.

title: Club Espresso
short_description: Since its opening in 1990, Club Espresso has been a staple café in Buam-dong. Renowned for its excellent coffee, it continues to be beloved by many. The signature menu includes Club Blend and Moon Blend coffee, various other options, and a tasting corner for guests to find their perfect brew. Visitors can enjoy a quiet, charming atmosphere, savoring a cup of coffee while appreciating the traces of the café's long history scattered throughout the space. Coffee beans, drip bags, and other coffee supplies are sold inside the cafe and on the website.

title: Amazing Brewing Company Seongsu Brewpub
short_description:
Amazing Brewing Company Seongsu Brewery is the place where Amazing Brewing Company began in 2016 and is now a cultural landmark of Seongsu-dong.

At this brewpub, which has an annual production capacity of 60 tons, you can enjoy around 50 kinds of fresh craft beer brewed on-site, along with firewood oven pizza made with house-made dough.

title: Project Haru
short_description: Project Haru is where you can taste desserts that reinterpret 'yeongwa,' a snack documented in Joseon Dynasty literature, to suit modern tastes. To express the ingredients' original taste and unique texture, limited quantities are produced by hand daily. The establishment offers convenience to diverse customers through thoughtful measures such as creating an English menu for foreigners and implementing a universal design that ensures easy access for those using wheelchairs or strollers.

title: Ingkko Tteokbokki
short_description: This restaurant has been making tteokbokki in Mangwudong since 1978. It is a restaurant that has remained in the memories of many people since the days when the tteokbokki stall village was formed due to the gathering of seven schools. The business has been in the family for three generations, from mother-in-law to daughter-in-law and now to son. Tteokbokki, which is made the same way as the first owner taught, without any additives, is a sign of courtesy to customers. When you take a bite of the big and shot-tempered tteokbokki, you can taste the same flavor as the old days when you ate in front of the school.

title: Yeogi Inga (Seochon Cafe)
short_description: Yeogi Inga is a cafe with a cozy atmosphere utilizing a Hanok in Seochon, a space where you can enjoy tea and beverages amidst the serenity of traditional architecture. With indoor floor-seating areas and outdoor seats available, it is a great place to take a short break while strolling through the alleys of Seochon. The warm atmosphere of the Hanok and the emotional interior harmonize, making it well-suited for quiet conversations or relaxed dates.

title: Mokseokjeong
short_description: Mokseokjeong is a hidden gem of a hanok restaurant nestled in a quiet alley of Samcheong-dong, Seoul, offering seasonal Korean dining in an omakase-style format. Instead of serving all dishes at once, each course is presented calmly in accordance with the guest’s dining pace, always centered around freshly cooked rice from a traditional cauldron. Ingredients are carefully selected every morning from Garak Market and Majang Meat Market, featuring premium Hanwoo++ beef and fresh seasonal seafood, prepared in limited quantities. This ensures that every dish reflects the finest quality and the flavors of the season. The warm, restrained atmosphere of the hanok space, where sunlight filters through lattice windows, creates a cozy setting suitable for couples, families, and international visitors alike. Each dish goes beyond simple plating to convey the stories, seasonal impressions, and dedication of the chef, offering not just a meal but a special moment to be remembered.

title: Zesty Saloon Seongsu
short_description: Welcome to Zesty Saloon, a unique and charming homemade burger joint located in Seoul Forest. With its exotic exterior, large signboard, and adorable characters welcoming you, Zesty Saloon aims to create authentic American-style burgers. Their popular menu items include the Wasabi Shrimp Burger and the Zesty Garlic Burger. If you're in Seongsu and craving the taste of America, make sure to visit Zesty Saloon and satisfy your burger cravings.

title: bricksand Seoul Station Branch
short_description: It is bricksand, Seoul's representative dessert gift. bricksand is a brick-shaped financier, made carefully every day with honest and quality ingredients. The freshness coming from good ingredients, the fantastic texture that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, and the liveliness that can only be felt on-site. It is highly suitable as a wonderful dessert gift for your precious acquaintances.

title: Baek nyeon Baekse Ginseng Chicken Soup
short_description: With 30 years of tradition, this restaurant specializes in samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) that showcases the true essence of the dish. Featured on TV and in the Michelin Guide, it offers visitors a taste of Korea’s unique culture of enjoying samgyetang for energy and vitality. The menu also includes dakbokkeumtang (spicy braised chicken) and fried chicken.

title: Cherry Garden
short_description: This restaurant is loved by the multicultural community for serving halal Korean cuisine. The owner, who spent 25 years in Singapore sharing Korean food with people from diverse cultural backgrounds, opened the restaurant in Dongdaemun based on that experience. With both halal and vegan options available, it welcomes all visitors without concern.

title: Fizz Social Club
short_description: Fizz Social Club is located on the fourth floor of a building near Bangsan Market in Euljiro—where you wouldn't expect to find a café. Climbing the steep stairs might make you wonder if you're on the right path, but as soon as jazz music drifts down, any doubts disappear. A cozy atmosphere greets you when you step through the rugged metal door, contrasting with the exterior. Here, you can enjoy a quality drip coffee accompanied by jazz played on LPs, creating an unexpectedly unique experience. Fizz Social Club is a hidden gem in Euljiro, where music and coffee blend perfectly.

title: Yusukdan Buja Nakji
short_description: This is a specialty restaurant for octopus dishes, beloved by Koreans who enjoy spicy food, featuring stir-fried octopus mixed with bean sprouts. You can also taste various other octopus dishes such as yeonpo-tang (octopus soup), octopus hot pot, and seasoned octopus salad.

title: Deungchon Choewolseon Kalguksu
short_description: This nostalgic restaurant is located in a small alley in a residential neighborhood, and instead of a sophisticated signboard, the words "Kalguksu" and "Mushroom Spicy Soup" are crudely written on the old door. The only meal on the menu here is mushroom hot and sour soup. If you order the hot and sour soup, it comes with noodles and fried rice, so you can enjoy a hearty meal at a reasonable price. The soup is flavored with fresh garlic, enoki mushrooms, and watercress, and the noodles are chewy and plump, more like udon noodles than kalguksu.

title: Tongyeong Gulbap
short_description: Located in the arcade that connects Gyeongbokgung Station's underground area with Jeokseon Hyundai Building, Tongyeong Gulbap is a well-known restaurant among nearby office workers. Its signature dishes include Tongyeong Gulbap (oyster rice), Maesaengi Oyster Soup, Jeongsik, and Oyster Pancakes. The restaurant also offers a variety of seafood dishes, such as octopus, cockles, and abalone. People return frequently for the fresh oysters and the mild, clean flavors that aren’t overpowering. The oysters are sourced directly from Tongyeong, allowing diners to experience a taste of fresh oysters that are hard to find in Seoul. Through flash freezing, the restaurant maintains the freshness of the oysters, allowing customers to enjoy them in winter and summer.

title: Original Jobak House
short_description: Jobak House was named after its founders, Mr. Jo and Mrs. Park, and has been serving pork ribs since 1979 for more than 40 years. Many regular customers who dined here as children now return with their own families. The sweet and savory pork ribs are enjoyed by all ages, and the house-brewed fermented liquor “Chopaju,” made with Kooksoondang Makgeolli, is a specialty available only here.

title: Travertine
short_description: Café Travertine is a distinctive café on Yongsan Ginkgo Road, known for its ambiance and coffee. It beautifully blends the tranquility of its former residential appearance with the sophistication of newly added remodel elements. Customers can choose their seating based on their mood for the day, whether on the terrace, at a desk in the yard, or on a cozy sofa in the corner, allowing them to enjoy both time and atmosphere to their liking. As the official Korean partner of the Danish specialty coffee brand La Cabra, Café Travertine offers a high-quality coffee menu. Among them, the standout is the signature hand-drip filter coffee. Those who prefer non-coffee options also offer alternatives like milk tea or lemon mate tea.

title: Il Deung Restaurant
short_description: Il Deung Restaurant, opened in 1986, has devoted itself to perfecting a single dish, pork backbone soup, preserving its deep flavor for decades. The broth, made without soybean paste but with green onions and shiitake mushrooms, has a rich umami taste complemented by well-boiled greens. The restaurant is frequented by Mangwon-dong residents and celebrities alike and has been featured on several TV programs.

title: byTOFU
short_description: This is a vegan restaurant that creates unexpectedly unique dishes using tofu and plant-based ingredients. As tofu is one of the key ingredients in Korean-style vegan cuisine, it is particularly recommended for those who want to experience the new appeal of tofu.

title: Baba India
short_description: This restaurant offers the true taste of India, crafted by local chefs from the region. A wide variety of curries are available to suit different preferences, while signature dishes include chicken tikka, a barbecue-style dish made with boneless chicken, and chicken makhani, known for its rich and creamy flavor.

title: Motungi Jip
short_description: As its name suggests, this restaurant has been located on the corner of a building since the days when Gangnam downtown was a residential area. It was originally named 'Somunnan Noodle Collection' and sold anchovy noodles to students in the library. Motungi Jip's best-selling items are tteokmyeon and oden kimbap, which have become so popular among foreign tourists that they often ask for the restaurant's name on maps and translators.

title: Tailor Coffee Seochon Gyeongbokgung Branch
short_description: Seen while walking along the stone wall path west of Gyeongbokgung Palace (Hyoja-ro), Tailor Coffee Seochon Gyeongbokgung Branch is a large-scale coffee shop. The Gyeongbokgung Branch presents its own bakery menu, and the floor-seating space is prepared in the main hall facing the counter. We hope you take a moment to feel relaxed while sitting at a window seat looking at the Gyeongbokgung stone wall path view.

title: Folv Yeonnam
short_description:
For a long time, we have welcomed guests under the name Yeontral Dabang Yeonnam on the cherry blossom path next to Yeontral Park in Yeonnam-dong. We are starting another story with a new name, Folv Yeonnam. Folv is not merely a space with a changed name, but a space created by gathering accumulated experiences, learning, and the desire to deliver better tastes.


We prepare pies and French toast baked with the utmost care using techniques learned directly from an artisan in Karuizawa, known as the home of jam in Nagano Prefecture, Japan. Furthermore, a cup of coffee is completed by hands that have built up experience as a barista in several European countries. Techniques and experiences learned in different times and places connect into a single taste in this small space.

From those who have visited this space for a long time to those who first learned about Folv today. We hope you stay here for a while and take away a warm time and delicious memories.

title: Hanjungsun
short_description: This dessert features chewy glutinous rice cakes filled with fresh fruit, offering a texture that is soft and elastic on the outside and refreshingly sweet on the inside. In addition to fresh fruit, you can also enjoy variations like persimmon, red bean with butter, and Dubai-style glutinous rice cakes. As a take-out only store, there are no tables for dine-in. While there is usually a line, it moves quickly. The rice cakes are packaged like lucky pouches, symbolizing blessings, making them a perfect gift option.

title: Moowee Nakwon
short_description: Located in Ikseon-dong, this rooftop hanok cafe is perfect for brunch. It offers a variety of seasonal brunch menus accompanied by wines. The rooftop space is decorated with 100-year-old traditional Korean tiles, Danish vintage furniture, and fabrics. Various indoor seating options also allow you to choose the atmosphere that suits your preference.

title: Miro Restaurant
short_description: Miro Restaurant, located in Hongdae, is a Korean-style pub where you can enjoy a variety of Korean dishes, such as side dishes. The menu includes sogalbijjim (braised beef short ribs), salted galbi (marinated grilled ribs), Korean beef tartare, ojingeobokkeum (stir-fried squid), and traditional Korean liquors. If you're lucky, you might taste tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cake), which is not on the regular menu. The restaurant is small but consistently busy, thanks to its clean and upscale food offerings. One of the charms of Miro Restaurant is admiring the neatly sliced vegetables accompanying the dishes. The owner is dedicated to using high-quality ingredients and pays meticulous attention to cutting vegetables and preparing them fresh upon order. This attention to detail gives the vegetables a distinct texture and flavor that feels refreshingly different.

title: Bicena
short_description: Bicena is a Korean restaurant that serves exquisite Korean food on beautiful Korean ceramics and offers the finest Korean dining experience along with Korean alcohol. With the goal of globalizing Korean cuisine, Bicena presents a harmonious blend of Korea's tradition and modernity in its Korean cuisine.

title: Kensington Hotel The View Lounge
short_description: Located on the 14th floor, The View Lounge offers a panoramic view of the Han River, providing a private and elegant urban staycation experience. Guests can enjoy an all-inclusive service ranging from breakfast, tea time & desserts, to unlimited beverages and finger foods.

title: GOUM
short_description: It is a premium Gomtang dining restaurant located near Yeoksam Station in Seoul. Centering on Gomtang (beef bone soup) boiled with the utmost care for a long time, it presents course dishes containing the essence of ingredients and the depth of time. From clear initial broths to deep and rich combined broths, it features unraveling the changing process of the soup into a single flow of dining. Adding the composition of dining upon the basics of Korean cuisine completes a neat table setting. It is a space where you can experience new Gomtang dining in Seoul.

title: Cheongdonok
short_description: Cheongdonok is a charcoal BBQ restaurant located between Hongik University Station and Hapjeong Station. Its signature dish is domestic female pork belly, cross-aged wet and dry for 240 hours, which is more tender and less greasy than standard raw meat. It also offers sets where you can taste pork belly, pork neck, and donmahawk (pork tomahawk) all at once, as well as aged beef and beef tartare. Because the staff grills the meat directly at the table, first-time foreign visitors can enjoy the meal without any language barrier, and it provides an English menu along with free corkage (bringing in outside alcohol). It has been selected by the Korean Blue Ribbon Survey for four consecutive years.

title: Homilbat
short_description: Located between Ewha Womans Univ. and Sinchon, near Sinchon train station, this bingsu (shaved ice dessert) specialty shop has served customers for over ten years. Their signature dish is the soft, sweet milk bingsu, topped with freshly made red beans and rice cakes. The shop also offers other delicious variations such as green tea bingsu and coffee bingsu, each offering a unique taste experience. Known for its affordable prices, the shop allows customers to explore various menu items. Besides bingsu, they also serve coffee and tea, which are perfect for soothing your palate after a cold dessert. The cozy interior, featuring brick and wood decor, enhances the warm and inviting atmosphere. A standout feature of this shop is the complimentary refill of red beans and rice cakes with every bowl of bingsu.

title: l’oubli
short_description:
l'oubli, located in Seorae Village, means 'oblivion' in French.

With a verse from 'Le Lethe' from Baudelaire's poetry collection  as its motif, it encapsulates the hope that everyone who visits will momentarily forget the burdens of a tiring day and rest comfortably, at least while they are here.

title: Soodowon
short_description: Located in Hyehwa, Soodowon is a bar tucked away in the basement of a red brick building reminiscent of a medieval monastery. The bar offers a wide selection of beverages, including Soodowon beer, various bottled beers, two types of draft beer, wines, cocktails, and whiskey.
