The menu provides detailed descriptions of beers and wines, making choosing a drink that suits your taste easy. Various plates and snacks are also available to pair perfectly with your drink. The interior, designed with brick walls and wooden furniture, creates an authentic monastery-like atmosphere, enhanced by jazz music and dim lighting that highlight the bar's unique charm.

title: Gobong Samgyetang
short_description:
Located near the National Assembly, Gobong Samgyetang is a popular restaurant frequented by lawmakers, government officials, journalists, and broadcasters.


Its signature dish is Sanghwang Mushroom Samgyetang, made with Sanghwang mushrooms known for their potential anticancer effects, boiled in mineral-rich water. The broth is rich, and the chicken is stuffed with glutinous rice, jujube, and medicinal herbs, offering a hearty and nourishing meal.

title: Munjeonseongsi
short_description: Famous even among local residents, Munjeonseongsi, a restaurant specializing in Jeon (Korean pancakes), derives its name from the idiom meaning "a constant stream of visitors making the doorway look like a bustling market." With a welcoming heart, we devote our utmost sincerity to providing generous portions and warm hospitality so you can comfortably come and enjoy. There are various types of Jeon, such as traditional assorted Jeon, cheese potato Jeon, and meat Jeon. We invite you to fully experience the charm of Korean dietary culture by pairing them with Makgeolli, which features an appealing subtle rice aroma and fermented flavor.

title: Bali Holiday
short_description: This restaurant captures the authentic taste and culture of Indonesia. It offers a variety of dishes such as mie goreng (fried noodles), nasi goreng (fried rice), sate ayam, and tempe. All dishes are prepared with halal ingredients, and a prayer room is available, making it a welcoming place for Muslim visitors.

title: DUBAI Restaurant
short_description: This is an Islamic food specialty restaurant directly operated by local Arabs, featuring a diverse menu including Arab-style appetizers, curries, and barbecue. It captures authentic flavors and atmosphere, offering a space where you can vividly experience rich Arab culture in the heart of Seoul.

title: Pooja 2 Indian Halal Food
short_description: Named after ‘puja,’ the daily prayer ritual performed to communicate with the divine, this Indian restaurant prepares its food with the same reverence. With a chef invited from India who has over 30 years of experience, it presents the true essence of Indian cuisine.

title: Sahara
short_description: Everything changes, but the Sahara Desert remains the same, so a restaurant named after it is a place that captures the history of life over the years. Sahara was once a place where protesting university students could hide during the democratization movement, and the students who made that connection have continued to visit as adults. It is said that Sahara is like a bar and a love room, where even strangers quickly share a laugh and people who come alone can easily socialize.

title: Suraksan Pungcheon Eel
short_description: This restaurant specializes in eel dishes and is a popular spot for Korean hikers to recharge after descending Suraksan Mountain. It uses only fresh, locally sourced eel, caught right before cooking. The grilled eel is served in two styles, salt-grilled and sauce-grilled. For those who wish to savor the eel’s natural flavor, the salt-grilled option is recommended. The restaurant also takes great pride in its house-made green onion kimchi, so be sure to enjoy it together with the fresh eel for a unique and flavorful experience.

title: Yeonhui dong Gukhwabbang
short_description:
Yeonhui dong Gukhwabbang is a neighborhood specialty dessert cafe operated by two sisters in the alleyways of Yeonhui dong.

All batter, choux cream, and red bean paste are made directly by the owners, offering freshness and high quality, and the cafe presents the unique charm of gukhwabbang with fillings that change every season.

Gukhwabbang with distinctive fillings such as choux cream, Earl Grey, matcha, and peanut butter elevates the familiar street snack to a new level. Along with gukhwabbang, a representative winter snack, ice cream is also sold, providing an appealing combination of warmth and coolness at the same time.

Despite the absence of elaborate interiors or packaging, people line up because of the ever changing menu and the high quality flavors created with carefully selected ingredients. There may be days off due to pop up and flea market schedules, so please check Instagram before visiting.

title: Saowol Surasang
short_description: Saowol Surasang is renowned for its soy-marinated and spicy marinated crabs (ganjang gejang and yangnyeom gejang), featuring large crabs with a savory, not overly salty flavor. The restaurant also serves royal-style dishes made using traditional palace recipes, including grilled beef short ribs (galbisal), and Seongju-tang—an abundant, rich soup made from Korean beef, domestic dried radish greens, and a beef bone broth simmered for eight hours. Group seating and reservations are available, and two hours of free parking is provided.

title: Samcheong-dong Sujebi
short_description: Samcheong-dong Sujebi began in the 1980s when owner Han Ki-young started a small snack shop in Samcheong-dong and gained fame with handmade sujebi crafted according to customers' requests. In 1982, it officially opened as a sujebi specialty restaurant, and unlike other sujebi establishments, it serves the dish in an earthenware pot. By adding potatoes, zucchini, and seaweed flakes, they maintain a simple yet savory and nutty flavor using minimal ingredients. It remains a popular restaurant today, visited by many Koreans and tourists seeking a nostalgic taste.

title: Marinier
short_description: Marinier is a yoshoku restaurant created with the concept of a small food and beverage space inside a fictional yacht called Marinier. Japanese style Western dishes and small dishes are prepared, and coffee, tea, bread and desserts, wine and sake are served. During the day, it operates as a casual cafe where you can enjoy coffee and light meals, and at night, as a bar where you can enjoy carefully selected wine and appetizers. If you visit while imagining enjoying drinks and food lightly on a fictional yacht, you will have an even richer experience.

title: Esperanza Roasters Hong Eun Main Branch
short_description: Esperanza Roasters is a roastery cafe that insists on using fresh crop green beans. Every morning, defective beans are hand sorted before roasting to ensure clean coffee free of mold toxins. The cafe offers a variety of beans in small quantities and operates a coffee bean shop as well. The cafe highlights the distinctive natural flavors inherent in each type of bean.

title: Guanho Yeouido Main Branch
short_description: Guanho Lamb Ribs is a Halal-certified lamb specialty restaurant using premium young lamb from New Zealand and Australia. The staff directly grills the meat from start to finish on a 100% charcoal brazier to provide it in its best condition. The representative menu, Rice Straw Grilled Lamb, is a signature dish that harmonizes special soy sauce seasoning with the scent of rice straw smoke. All seats are configured in the form of private rooms, making it suitable for business meetings and entertaining foreign guests. We also offer a high level of dining by directly developing various stews and side dishes.

title: Prost Pub & Grill
short_description:
Frost Pub & Grill is a European-style pub that can only be found in Itaewon. It boasts a relaxed and laid-back atmosphere, making it a unique place to enjoy. The exotic interior, combined with Frost's sense of modernity, captivates customers from various cultural backgrounds, creating an enchanting space with a global appeal. Throughout the day, Frost offers a special ambiance that blends a true sense of freedom with a sporty vibe, making it the perfect place to experience a new burst of energy late into the night.
Frost serves a variety of European-style dishes infused with Asian-inspired sauces, providing a taste of the exotic. They also craft American-style handcrafted burgers with homemade buns, perfect for pairing with their selection of beers from around the world and a range of diverse cocktails. Frost Pub & Grill truly opens up a new night in Itaewon, inviting guests to indulge in a mix of flavors and experiences.

title: Coffee Fiel
short_description: Coffee Fiel is dedicated to providing customers with heartfelt coffee. They start with the direct importation of carefully selected green beans from renowned farms around the world. Their coffee is roasted by a national champion roaster, ensuring a top-tier coffee experience for their customers. Each season, they offer a variety of specialty coffees sourced from different regions, allowing customers to enjoy unique and diverse flavors. In addition to coffee, Coffee Fiel offers desserts crafted by an in-house pâtissier, enhancing the overall experience. Customers can also purchase premium coffee beans in-store, guaranteeing fresh coffee daily. Moreover, Coffee Fiel collaborates with famous artists, providing visitors exclusive artistic experiences that can only be found in their space. This artistic ambiance has made Coffee Fiel popular for photo shoots in well-known shopping malls. The name "FIEL" in Spanish means "faithful" or "loyal," reflecting the brand's commitment to coffee and its promise to deliver coffee that lives up to the name "Coffee Fiel."

title: Inhyeon Golbang
short_description: Located in Euljiro, this music bar is perfect for quietly enjoying music when you need comfort after a hectic day. Relax on a reclining sofa, create your own playlist, and enjoy a highball or whiskey of your choice while immersing yourself in music. To maintain focus on music appreciation, conversation between guests is not allowed. If you’re looking for a comforting solo night out, Inhyeon Golbang is highly recommended.

title: Cafe Relax
short_description:
Cafe Relax, situated near PARASPARA SEOUL in Bukhansan Mountain, is a unique retreat where visitors can escape from the hustle and bustle of city life and unwind in nature. Originally a private home, the café offers beautiful landscapes throughout the year. In the summer, it’s an ideal place to dip your feet in the stream and enjoy the cool, refreshing breeze.

The interior consists of six spacious halls, each with its own distinct charm, providing a fun experience that caters to different preferences. There is a no-kids zone for those seeking quiet relaxation and a family zone for visitors with children, ensuring that everyone can enjoy their time in comfort. The café serves freshly made drinks, healthy baked goods, and brunch, allowing guests to savor a delightful meal amid nature.

Plenty of parking space makes it convenient to visit, and the ever-changing scenery offers a refreshing experience year-round. For those longing for a peaceful escape from the rush of daily life, Cafe Relax is the perfect destination to embrace the soothing tranquility of nature.

title: Haebangchondak
short_description: Haebangchon Dak, located in Sinheung Market in Haebangchon, offers a unique take on traditional fried chicken. Unlike conventional fried chicken, which is typically oily, salty, spicy, sweet, and intense in flavor, Haebangchon Dak's slow-cooked chicken is filled with fresh domestic chicken, Geumsan ginseng, jujube, and glutinous rice. It is cooked for an hour and a half to reduce the oil content, resulting in a healthier and delicious slow-cooked chicken. You might think that the electrically roasted herbal whole chicken is too bland, but it is enhanced with a specially developed mustard and yogurt sauce that elevates its tender flavor. Additionally, Haebangchon Dak's unique leek kimchi, carefully prepared and fermented weekly, pairs perfectly with the glutinous rice stuffed inside the chicken, creating a delightful harmony of flavors.

title: Durumi Bunsik N Seoul Tower Branch
short_description: Durumi Bunsik means "all-around delicious taste" (Duru + Mi) and is a Korean Diner selling Bunsik, the soul food of Koreans. Located at N Seoul Tower, you can taste a variety of Bunsik while appreciating the magnificent downtown panoramic view of Seoul. Experience a new taste of Bunsik at Namsan, a landmark of Seoul, along with the active and friendly animal character, 'Durumi' (Crane).

title: Anderson C
short_description: Anderson C, a vintage furniture gallery favored by Korean celebrities, is composed of two spaces—a café facing the street and another within the gallery area in the back. With just one drink order, guests receive an entry ticket to explore the gallery filled with tastefully curated vintage furniture. Each piece is carefully selected by the owner for its quality and aesthetic. Visitors can sit on or touch the furniture freely while enjoying their café time, making it a uniquely special experience for those who appreciate interior design.

title: cofe de palezze
short_description: Located at the beginning of the path leading from Gwanghuimun along the Seoul City Wall, cofe de palezze is a cafe where you can feel relaxed while looking at the fortress wall view through wide, open windows giving a sense of openness. The signature menus, Black Sesame Latte and Matcha Latte, offer a taste of the harmony between a soft, fluffy texture and savory milk. We hope that the moments spent here by everyone who visits cofe de palezze will feel like a journey.

title: Cheonghwa Sushi
short_description: As a long-standing favorite in Bangi-dong Food Alley, this restaurant always draws a waiting line. Alongside its thick, fresh sashimi, the aged kimchi braised fish served as a side dish is another must-try specialty. Popular choices include assorted sashimi platters and the special sushi set, where the tender texture of the fish pairs perfectly with the rice.

title: Bongchu Jjimdak Apgujeong Rodeo
short_description: Jjimdak is a traditional dish from the Andong region, made by braising chicken with glass noodles and vegetables in a soy-based sauce for a deep, savory flavor. Bongchu Jjimdak is a popular franchise among Koreans, offering a reliable and approachable place to enjoy authentic jjimdak.

title: gaga
short_description: This Korean wine bar, located in a 300-year-old hanok, features a terrace and is run by owner-chef Choi Jung-sook, who personally curates the menu for this private restaurant. At gaga bar, multiple groups share a table while ordering their preferred dishes, except for the outdoor terrace seating. The dishes are renowned for their use of sauces, offering a variety of rich flavors.

title: O'pato
short_description: Opatto is a brunch and bakery venue serving breakfasts crafted from freshly baked bread. Opening at 8 AM, it offers sandwiches and brunch options featuring daily-changing soups and just-baked bread. The store is divided into two sections: "O’pato," where bread is baked and sold, and "Ori," where brunch is served. There are three designated parking spaces near the store, and it is kid-friendly.

title: etba seoul
short_description:
Etba is an espresso bar located in Seongsu, styled with an antique atmosphere full of Italian sensibility. From the research stage of bean blending to roasting at their in-house roastery, etba is deeply involved in the coffee-making process, allowing visitors to enjoy a rich and flavorful cup.

As expected from an espresso bar, the menu is centered around espresso-based drinks, but there are also non-coffee options and desserts available, so even those who do not drink coffee can enjoy the unique atmosphere of etba.

title: Daepo Zzimdak Sinchon
short_description: Popular among young travelers, this restaurant offers a unique experience with chicken-themed décor and toy chickens used for ordering. The adorable character topping on jjimdak (braised chicken) makes for perfect photo moments, while the dish itself delights with tender chicken, assorted vegetables, and a sweet and spicy sauce.

title: Pyeongtaek Go Yeosa House Cold Noodles
short_description: Pyeongtaek Go Yeosa House Cold Noodles traces its origins to the founder, who brought his father’s noodle-making tradition from Pyeongan Province during the Korean War. In 1974, he opened “Pyeongtaek Go Doctor House” in Pyeongtaek, named after his nickname “Go Doctor,” earned for his cool and open personality. The restaurant moved to Sinchon in 1982, and later, his daughter Ms. Go Hee-seung continued the legacy, relocating to Yeonhui-dong in 2008. Loved for its refreshing broth and chewy noodles, the restaurant is also known for its unique topping of thinly sliced cucumber peppers on cold noodles.

title: Coffee Hanyakbang Hyehwa Branch
short_description: The Hyehwa branch of Coffee Hanyakbang is a newly opened branch that expands beyond the iconic Euljiro location, offering a variety of beans and hand-drip filter coffee. Each bean's unique characteristics are conveniently displayed, allowing customers to select their perfect match. In addition to coffee, their milk teas, ades, and other beverages boast exceptional flavors. The cafe also features desserts and bread from Hyemindang, crafted with seasonal ingredients for a distinctive taste. The interior, adorned with antique furniture and wooden accents, enhances the elegant ambiance. A large fish tank inside serves as Coffee Hanyakbang Hyehwa's signature photo spot.

title: Hyangdonga Hannam Annex
short_description: Hyangdonga Hannam Annex, renowned for its Pyongyang naengmyeon, offers a harmonious blend of traditional hanok ambiance and clean, modern interior design. The noodles, made from buckwheat milled with a stone grinder, have a rough, slightly firm texture that pairs beautifully with the rich and lingering Korean beef broth. Each bowl is filled with a sense of excitement and depth, making it an enjoyable experience even for first-time visitors to Pyongyang-style cold noodles. The beef-infused broth softens the flavor, allowing for a more approachable and widely appreciated taste.

title: KERVAN COEX Mall
short_description: This restaurant offers an authentic taste of Türkiye, with dishes prepared by Turkish chefs and a menu that showcases both the diversity and depth of its traditional cuisine. Conveniently located in COEX Mall, it’s easy to visit and also appealing for travelers with its reasonably priced lunch sets.

title: La Croute Seoul Main Branch
short_description: La Croute Seoul is a French bakery with a fairy tale sensibility inspired by the Alsace region of France, which was the background of Howls Moving Castle. La Croute makes bread by following three principles. First, it uses French flour and butter. Second, all menus in the store are made directly by us. Third, even if it takes time, it uses the traditional natural fermentation method. Feel the originality created with traditional recipes in a space resembling Alsace.

title: noop cafe
short_description: noop cafe is a massive café and pub in Haebangchon, spanning over 1652 square meters. It is especially famous for its expansive views of N SEOUL TOWER. Inside the antique-themed interior, you can enjoy a game of pool or relax on bean bags placed by the large windows, taking in the scenery. The rooftop area upstairs features artificial grass, swing beds, and sunbeds, giving you a resort-like feeling, especially at sunset. Enjoy a refreshing draft beer and delicious snacks on the outdoor terrace while taking in the view of N SEOUL TOWER and capturing some memorable photos.

title: Booyas Gopchang Hongdae Branch
short_description: As it is a long-established gopchang specialty restaurant in Hongdae, it is a place with a steady flow of domestic and foreign customers. There are so many visitors that a wait forms during dinner hours, but the quick turnover makes it easy to visit without feeling burdened. You can enjoy the highly addictive vegetable gopchang, al-gopchang, and green onion gopchang—the representative menus of the Booyas Gopchang Hongdae main branch—according to your various tastes. The satisfaction level is high with side combinations like whole garlic, sundae, Cheongyang peppers, cheese toppings, and steamed egg, as well as the signature fried rice eaten at the end. Thanks to Hongdae's unique retro sensibility and subtle atmosphere, it is also a highly popular place for a date or a drinking gathering.

title: Janggagu
short_description: Jangga-gu has remained in the same location in Eunpyeong-gu for over 40 years. The restaurant insists on using domestic ingredients and prepares all dishes upon order, which may take time but ensures sincerity in every meal. Inside, you can still find air conditioners from the 1960s to 1980s and interior details that preserve an old-fashioned charm. While delivery is available, dining inside offers a truly enjoyable nostalgic experience.

title: Yell-O! Chicken
short_description: This is a fried chicken specialty restaurant that enjoys high popularity among Muslims living in Korea, consistently receiving praise for its unique flavors perfectly tailored to Muslim tastes through distinctive spice combinations.

title: Cosmos Grocery Seongsu
short_description: A vegan lifestyle hub that offers both a vegan brunch café and a grocery corner with plant-based products. Recognized as one of Seongdong-gu’s top vegan spots, it ranked third on <HappyCow>, the world’s largest vegan app. Surrounded by flowers in a cozy setting, you can enjoy a wholesome meal while soaking in the unique charm and atmosphere of Seongsu.

title: mueh
short_description: Cafe Mueh, a roastery cafe in Bukchon, is celebrated for its well-balanced acidity, delightful sweetness, and lingering coffee flavors. The cafe roasts its signature blend daily to deliver a consistently perfect cup. Cafe Mueh also offers a seasonal dessert menu with a serene and peaceful ambiance, allowing guests to enjoy a rotating selection of unique treats throughout the year. Prioritizing comfort over extravagance, Cafe Mueh is known for its smooth, easy-to-enjoy coffee. The gentle coffee flavors and seasonal desserts often draw visitors. The modern, minimalist interior creates a cozy space perfect for reading, studying, or simply unwinding.

title: ASHLEY QUEENS HONGDAE BRANCH
short_description:
Want to immerse yourself in the Korean lifestyle? Dine where Koreans really line-up! Ashley Queens is Korea's No. 1 Buffet Brand that serves 20 million customers yearly. With over 220 seats, Ashley Queens Hongdae Branch accommodates all occasions. Come with your friends, family and loved ones or by yourself!


100 Minutes of Unlimited Food, Come Enjoy our 130 Menus!

From Korean delicacies to Western favorites, try new flavors while indulging in your favorites.

title: Eosachultto Jongno 3 Ga
short_description: This restaurant offers fresh seafood at great value. Enjoy a generous assortment of thickly sliced seasonal sashimi along with a variety of other seafood dishes, providing plenty of options to choose from.

title: Chani Oden
short_description: This is a restaurant that reinterprets traditional fish cake in a new way. Their signature menu item, squid odeng-katsu, features fresh fish meat ground in a stone mortar mixed with squid and vegetables, then deep-fried to create a crispy yet moist texture.

title: Woomoolzip
short_description: A specialty restaurant for hot pot and rice dishes, nestled in a serene setting crafted by Glow Seoul, providing a private space to enjoy serene landscapes. Decorated with interior design inspired by Korean tradition, featuring a century‑old well as its centerpiece, this establishment offers a charming and sophisticated ambiance. You can savor dishes like hot pot and rice cooked with fresh vegetables, premium Hanwoo beef brisket in a clear broth, and a sampler platter of Hanwoo beef brisket.

title: Gonghang Kalguksu
short_description: Established in 1979 and operated for 45 years by successive generations, Gonghang(Airport) Kalguksu is a rumored restaurant in front of Gimpo Airport. For 45 years, customers have been coming to this restaurant because of the sharp soup of mushroom kalguksu made with beef broth and spicy seasoning. After finishing the noodles, the fried rice made with the soup is also considered a specialty. The restaurant also sells meal kits so that you can cook the same dish at home.

title: Mirim Bunsik
short_description: This tteokbokki restaurant has been standing next to Mirim Girls' High School since 1988. It doesn't have a proper signboard, but it hasn't changed over the years, so it's a place that keeps the memories of school days alive. Miribunsik's signature dish is instant tteokbokki, which you can choose according to your taste, including glass noodle, dumplings, ramen, and fish cakes. Actor Seol Kyung-gu, the main character of the movie "Bulhan-dang," filmed a scene where he ate tteokbokki here, so some people visit the restaurant as a movie spot.

title: Whitturu
short_description:
Whitturu is an izakaya where you can savor Japanese dishes like oden, kushikatsu, and yakitori, all in an authentic Japanese atmosphere. It’s run by the “black spoon” chef, who gained recognition after appearing on Netflix’s Black and White Chef: Culinary Class Wars, ensuring top-notch flavors. The restaurant also features occasional pop-up events, introducing a variety of new and exciting dishes, perfect for a fresh and unique dining experience. It's an ideal spot to enjoy warm oden paired with a cold draft beer during the cold winter months. The cozy interior offers a range of seating options, from communal tables to more intimate settings, all thoughtfully designed for a detailed and welcoming ambiance. 

Closed: July 10th - July 30th

title: Tuna Jinuh
short_description: This is a place where you can feel the dedication and sincerity of true tuna experts. A wide range of cuts from premium tuna are served fresh, offering distinct flavors and textures at reasonable prices. The restaurant has also been featured several times in the Blue Ribbon Survey, a well-known restaurant guidebook in Korea, confirming both its quality and customer satisfaction.

title: Jincheongyujeom
short_description: Jincheongyujeom is a contemporary Korean restaurant nestled in the middle of Yeonnam-dong's maze-like alleys. Upon opening the door, you are first greeted by the aroma of sesame and perilla oils, pressed fresh in the store every morning. This fragrance naturally permeates menus such as Perilla Oil Makguksu, Seasonal Bibimbap, Gangdoenjang Ssambap, Beef Tartare Gamtae Gimbap, and Grilled Mackerel with Bracken Risotto. It provides a novel impression even to those highly familiar with Korean cuisine without being overwhelming, making it an excellent destination for travelers experiencing Korean food for the first time to comfortably clear their plates.

title: Haemok Nonhyeon
short_description: This restaurant serves hitsumabushi, a traditional Japanese-style eel rice bowl, prepared in the authentic way. The tender, flavorful eel is lightly seasoned so you can enjoy it to the very last bite. With both its exterior and plating faithfully recreating a Japanese atmosphere, the experience feels almost like dining in Japan itself.

title: CARAVEL East Asia Hannam
short_description: There is no need to take a flight to experience authentic local flavors. CARAVEL in Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and China presents the foods that people in those places order as part of their everyday lives, the flavors truly loved by locals but not found in tourist guidebooks. Small dishes and beverages that have crossed borders continue into new stories at CARAVEL.

title: Sinjindo Ganjang Gejang
short_description: Just steps from Hongik Univ. Station, this ganjang gejang(soy sauce marinated raw crab) restaurant is loved by both locals and international visitors. Order the set meal to enjoy not only crab and rice, but also steamed egg and a variety of side dishes for a truly satisfying spread. The spicy crab soup is another highlight—perfect to share alongside ganjang gejang when dining with friends.

title: Jongno Eunhaengnamujip
short_description: Jongno Eunhaengnamujip is a beef galbi (grilled ribs) restaurant that opened in 1986. It modernly recreates the beef short ribs that noblemen enjoyed during the Joseon Dynasty. Using high-quality beef, they serve beef short rib dishes that excel in taste, aroma, and texture. Particularly, the rich marinade deeply penetrates the meat, and its sweet fragrance stimulates the senses. The founder was captivated by a traditional Korean house (hanok) with a 150-year-old ginkgo tree (unhaengnamu), leading to the establishment of "Jongno Eunhaengnamujip." Not only is the food delicious, but the service is also outstanding—so much so that the president of a certain organization once recommended that his staff learn from the kindness of the restaurant’s employees.ness of the restaurant's employees.

title: Hanguk Jip Lotte World Mall
short_description: This is the Seoul branch of a restaurant specializing in Jeonju bibimbap, the city’s iconic dish. Conveniently located inside Lotte World Mall, it’s easy to find and offers a comfortable dining atmosphere. Try the authentic Jeonju bibimbap, served pre-mixed, or the yukhoe bibimbap topped with fresh seasoned beef tartare—both showcasing the true essence of Korea’s signature dish.

title: Bukchonmakguksu
short_description: Enjoy Makguksu noodles crafted from 100% pure buckwheat, renowned for their chewy texture and healthy flavor. Beyond Makguksu, this place specializes in kalguksu and buckwheat rolled dumplings, each a unique culinary delight.

title: MGM Hongdae Branch
short_description: MGM, located in Hongdae, is a Korean BBQ restaurant where you can enjoy grilling a variety of meats such as samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), galbi (ribs), and moksal (grilled pork neck) on a cauldron lid. One of the standout features of this place is grilling samgyeopsal with minari (water parsley). At the MGM Hongdae branch, the staff expertly grills the meat for you, allowing you to fully savor its true flavor. They also move around the restaurant, refilling any vegetables you might need, ensuring attentive and friendly service. Additionally, MGM offers a variety of side dishes, including cold noodles, bibim noodles, and stews, providing diverse combinations to complement the meat. With its spacious and comfortable setting, along with convenient parking in front of the restaurant, it is an excellent choice for group visits.

title: Leedorim Blot Coffee X Bake
short_description: Located just a 5-minute walk from Gyeongbokgung Station, Leedorim Blot Coffee X Bake is a popular Seochon café known to locals and foreign tourists. It blends traditional Korean style with modern interiors, offering a comfortable setting across its 1st to 3rd floors and a rooftop view of Inwangsan Mountain that enhances the experience. Opening at 8 AM, it's perfect for grabbing a quick breakfast before starting a sightseeing tour. The café serves specialty coffee made with high-quality beans and freshly baked goods each morning, all in a cozy and inviting atmosphere.

title: Original Hongdukkae Kalguksu
short_description: Famous even among local residents, Original Hongdukkae Kalguksu is a Kalguksu (handmade chopped noodles) restaurant that is fully packed every time you visit due to its reasonable prices, generous portions, and friendly taste. Chewy noodles kneaded directly and a refreshing broth made with Manila clams serve as the base. If you place spicy kimchi on top of the Kalguksu, which can taste somewhat mild on its own, you can taste a fantastic harmony, and adding the provided seasoning sauce is also a distinct delicacy.

title: Seoul Rabbit
short_description:
Seoul Rabbit is a specialty carrot juice shop for travelers visiting Seochon and the residents. Our signature product is carrot juice, and we’ve developed the most diverse range of carrot-based beverages in Korea. Some of our offerings include 100% pure carrot juice, carrot coffee, Danke juice (a drinkable carrot cake), vitamin C-enhanced orange carrot ginger juice, and Carrot Lemon Soda, a refreshing option perfect for hot summer days.

While carrots' health benefits are well-known, they are often seen only as a side dish. We believe juice is the most delicious and convenient way to enjoy carrots. However, we can’t ignore that carrots are a polarizing ingredient. This led us to create a variety of drinks to make carrots more approachable for those who may initially dislike them.

In addition to carrot-based beverages, we also offer Ginseng Yogurt Smoothies, making the health benefits of Korean ginseng more accessible. These have been especially popular with international travelers seeking to refreshingly experience Korea’s iconic ginseng.

The large rabbit mural in front of our store was designed to reduce the sense of hesitation toward carrots and instead evoke a feeling of familiarity. It has now become a popular photo spot for travelers wanting to commemorate their visit to Seoul.

title: Kwanho Gwanghwamun
short_description: Welcome to Kwanho Gwanghwamun, your go-to destination for grilled lamb chops. They pride themselves on using only the finest quality lamb sourced from New Zealand and Australia, ensuring an exceptional dining experience. From the moment you arrive, they take care of grilling the meat to your specifications so you can savor it just the way you like. Their lamb is halal-certified, making it an excellent choice for Muslim guests. Plus, they offer private rooms to provide a peaceful atmosphere for groups dining.

title: Heritage Club
short_description: Heritage Club operates as both a cafe and a bar, functioning as a 'Cafe' until 7:00 PM and as a 'Bar' thereafter. We invite you to enjoy fragrant coffee during the day, and light, easy-drinking alcoholic beverages and cocktails at night, while appreciating the night sky and the silhouette of Jongmyo Shrine beyond the serene courtyard ceiling.

title: Arigyegok Jonggak Branch
short_description: Arigyegok is a modern reinterpretation of traditional Korean taverns, offering chicken-based dishes and traditional liquor in a serene, nature-inspired atmosphere. With stone, wood, restrained lighting, and classic details, the space creates the tranquility of a mountain stream within the city.

title: Everest Restaurant Yangjae
short_description: This is the Yangjae branch of Everest Restaurant, a Nepalese-Indian restaurant that has been introducing the authentic flavors of its homeland to Korea for over 20 years. The freshness of the Himalayas is reflected in its cuisine, where a rich array of spices and fragrant herbs bring new joy to the senses. The restaurant is especially well known for its wide variety of chicken dishes.

title: CHILGAPSAN
short_description: Chilgapsan is a Korean restaurant that offers a healthy and filling meal with mild, clean flavors. It is a local favorite in the neighborhood, known for its non-spicy and comforting dishes. Signature menu items include Gondre Bibimbap, Beef Soup with Rice (Sogukbap), and Bulgogi, along with a variety of savory pancakes and à la carte dishes.

title: Hamcho Ganjang gejang
short_description: This restaurant specializes in soy sauce marinated crab (ganjanggejang), a traditional Korean fermented seafood made by aging fresh blue crab in a special soy sauce. Enhanced with glasswort for a deep umami flavor, the dish offers a unique culinary experience that embodies the essence of Korean food culture.

title: Korea House
short_description: Korea House is a cultural complex in Korea created to preserve and promote traditional culture. It offers traditional cultural experiences like royal cuisine, art performances, and wedding ceremonies. Built in 1957 as Yeong Bin Gwan to accommodate distinguished guests from home and abroad, the Korea House has undergone extensive renovations. It stands today as a high-quality, multi-cultural space dedicated to preserving and promoting Korea's beautiful traditional culture through vivid historical scenes. It is also renowned for its "Kohojae" program, which allows visitors to experience royal court cuisine, and it has gained popularity as a filming location for popular entertainment programs, movies, and dramas.

title: Neungdong Minari
short_description: You can indulge in a delightful array of minari (water parsley) dishes, such as minari suyuk jeongol (pork hot pot with water parsley), minari kkori jjim (braised oxtail with water parsley), and minari yukhoe (raw beef with water parsley). These dishes use Hanjae minari, cultivated on Hwaaksan Mountain in Cheongdo, where it grows in ample sunlight and pure underground water, resulting in tender stems infused with the rich aroma of minari. At Neungdong, you can also enjoy gomtang (beef bone soup), served with rice in a clear broth made from premium-grade hanwoo, prized for its tender texture and savory umami flavor. The food's gentle, clean, and non-spicy taste continually draws patrons. The meticulously crafted dishes and warm, attentive service earn high praise from visitors. While a wait is often expected, visiting on a weekday provides faster access compared to the busier weekends.

title: Yukjeupdang Gwanghwamun Branch
short_description: Yukjeupdang specializes in aged meat, offering a wide range including lean Korean pork, chewy and flavorful 100% Jirisan black pork, and the finest 1++ Korean beef grilled over charcoal. Meats are wet-aged for one to five weeks to retain juices and tenderness, and dry-aged to reduce drip loss, ensuring maximum flavor.

title: Figaro
short_description: Figaro is a bar located in Gosichon, also called Nokdu Street, next to Seoul National University. It has been a regular store for students for so long that they say they are not even Seoul National University students if they don't know Figaro. Test takers with light pockets are always grateful for the same low price. At the height of the student movement on Nokdu Street, students who were protesting here used to hide. Figaro was a place where students visited to relieve their anger and stress.

title: Sanchon
short_description: This traditional Korean restaurant specializes in temple cuisine. True to its name, "Sanchon," it offers clean and elegant vegan dishes centered on wild mountain herbs and fresh vegetables. The interior, imbued with the charm of a traditional hanok, enriches the dining experience, leaving a lasting impression.

title: Jazz Story
short_description: Jazz Story, which started in Samcheong-dong and relocated to Seongbuk-dong, is closer to a house for listening to music rather than simply a live cafe where you drink alcohol and watch performances. We invite you to sweetly experience the live jazz under the unique underground interior and the soft glow of incandescent lights.

title: Bobae Banjum Myeongdong Branch
short_description:
Bobae Banjum Myeongdong Branch is a Chinese franchise store located in the center of Myeongdong, a representative commercial district in Seoul, offering a variety of Chinese dishes at reasonable prices.

It features popular menus such as authentic Jajangmyeon and Jjamppong, as well as Tangsuyuk and Yusanseul. With its clean interior and hygienic cooking environment, it is highly praised even by foreign tourists.

It is equipped with Chinese and Japanese menus, allowing tourists to order conveniently, and its accessibility is also excellent as it is located within a 3-minute walk from Myeongdong Station.

title: Dongbu Goryeo Bakery
short_description:
Since its opening in 1974, the bakery has continued its tradition of making delicious bread rather than just pretty buns. The custom of running a supermarket-like bakery for customers visiting the racetrack in the 70s remains, creating a unique scene. The shop is filled with a wide variety of handmade breads, from old favorites like manchurian and doughnuts to garlic cream bread and ciabatta. The owner says that the secret to the shop's longevity is that the bread is naturally fermented, making it easy to digest.

 

• This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

title: Scene
short_description: Located in the Seongsu-dong café street, Scene is a large café also used as a pop-up store rental space, attracting many visitors. The first floor operates as a café, while the second floor functions as a select shop. On nice days, you can enjoy your coffee at the outdoor tables, and the café is pet-friendly.

title: Jamdubong The Nine
short_description:
Jamdubong The Nine is a barbecue restaurant located in Mapo-gu, Seoul, created by remodeling a former Han River dock. Situated in the heart of the city, it offers views of the Han River while serving its signature dishes — samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) and tteokgalbi (grilled short rib patties).


The restaurant has been featured in various broadcasting media, attracting many foreign visitors, and is also popular among families. Enjoy barbecue while watching the sunset over the Han River and make unforgettable memories at this one-of-a-kind dining spot.

title: Hongdae Soy Sauce Marinated Crab  Hongilpum
short_description: This restaurant, often featured in domestic and international media, is Hongdae’s go-to spot for soy-marinated crab (ganjang gejang). From selecting fresh blue crabs to preparing the marinade and even the broth for crab stew, the owner handles everything personally. The sauce is made not with commercial bases but with fruit extracts and traditional herbs, giving it a light and delicate flavor rather than being overly salty.

title: Shinleedoga
short_description:
Shinleedoga, located between Hapjeong and Hongdae, is a delightful café that allows you to experience the beauty of traditional hanok.

The open space, surrounded by large windows looking out onto the center yard, boasts a refreshing sense of openness. A warm fire pit at the center of the yard adds to the cozy atmosphere. The exposed ceiling rafters showcase the traditional elegance of hanok. Shinleedoga offers not only coffee but also a diverse selection of teas, catering to every taste. It’s the perfect spot to unwind in a tranquil and serene environment.

title: Mannadang
short_description: A a royal confectionery store opened in 1991, with a craftsman who researches and produces royal confectionery, and a successor is taking over the family business. The signature product is the flavorful yakgwa with jochung. Mannadang has inherited and maintained the traditional flavors of confectionery, rice cakes, and Korean confectionery that are served at feasts in the palace and noble families. It is the only place in Seoul that produces and sells royal rice cakes and royal Korean confectionery that are used in traditional banquets.

title: Seokgyo Restaurant
short_description: Opened in 1986, Seokgyo Restaurant has been a family business for two generations, specializing in Sundae soup. Fresh ingredients are prepared daily and simmered for four hours to create a clear yet rich broth without the need for heavy seasoning. The rice, made from grains milled in Seosan, Chungnam, is also notable for its quality. On weekdays, it attracts office workers and merchants, while on weekends, hikers from nearby Ansan and Inwangsan enjoy Sundae soup with Makgeolli.

title: KERVAN Famille Station
short_description: Located inside Famille Station, the premium dining arcade of Central City Terminal, this restaurant specializes in authentic Turkish cuisine prepared by a native chef. It’s a must-visit for those who want to experience genuine flavors from Türkiye, especially the pide—a Turkish specialty rarely found in Seoul, known for its unique taste.

title: Cheongdam Musin
short_description: This fusion Japanese restaurant specializes in grilled eel and kappo cuisine (dishes prepared on the spot by professional chefs). Above all, it is renowned for its focus on quality ingredients and attentive service, highlighted by the extra-large tidal flat eel sourced from Ganghwa Island. With private dining rooms available, it’s the perfect place to experience the luxurious dining trends of Cheongdam.

title: Smore Market
short_description: Smore Market Samcheong Branch is a theme cafe and character prop shop that encapsulates the worldview of Disney/Pixar animations, especially Toy Story. The entire store is decorated with familiar character ornaments and toys such as Woody and Buzz, presenting a charming atmosphere that stimulates childhood innocence. You can browse and purchase character goods, and enjoy coffee, cookies, and s'more desserts together. Since there are many photo spots to leave pictures, it is well-suited as a unique date course or family visit course during an outing to Samcheong-dong or Bukchon.

title: Donut Jungsu
short_description: Located in Changsin-dong's Cliff Village, Donut Jungsu is a café offering both delightful treats and panoramic views of Seoul. Renovated from traditional houses, it offers a serene and peaceful atmosphere, allowing you to enjoy the breathtaking views of Namsan Mountain and beautiful Seoul city through large windows. Donut Jungsu specializes in Korean-style donuts, offering unique treats like corn donuts and mugwort chocolate donuts.

title: Manpo Myeonok
short_description: Opened in 1972 and now in its third generation, Manpo Myeonok specializes in Northern-style cuisine such as Pyeongyang Cold Noodles and Eobok Jangban. Its deep yet refreshing flavor, created by blending meat broth with dongchimi, follows the authentic Pyongan Province style rarely found in Seoul. The recipe has been faithfully handed down from the founder from Pyongan Province to the current owner. Out of pride and sincerity for their food, the restaurant refuses to open franchises to preserve its original taste, offering a dining experience filled with unchanging devotion.

title: Osullok Tea House Bukchon Branch
short_description: The first floor is a space where tea, snacks, and souvenirs are sold. Guests can taste and enjoy tea on site. The tea house on the second floor offers a wide view of the rooftops of Bukchon Hanok Village through large windows. On the third floor is a special tea tasting area unique to Osulloc, which is updated according to seasonal menus. Inspired by seasonal teas, the tea house presents tea cocktails, tea cakes, tea sparkling water, and other tea snacks. The tea tasting experience is available by reservation only, so please check the reservation methods in advance via the official website or on site.

title: Seowoo Bakery
short_description: Since 1980, the savory smell of puffed rice has never left this restaurant. The father, who had been in the puff pastry business, and his son, who was majoring in mechanical engineering and physics, collaborated to develop nurungji snacks using puff pastry technology. The rice crackers, flavored with garlic baguette and condensed milk, became the shop's signature product. Today, the shop's doors are still open, as customers say, "Seowoo Bakery is the standard for puffed rice crackers.“

title: Blgre
short_description: Blgre is a name created by combining the first letters of the three primary colors of light: Blue, Green, and Red. Like the intersection of these three primary colors creates white, it embodies an open-minded approach to reinterpreting Korean cuisine. It represents the intention to express Korean cuisine in a new way, with an open mind and creativity. The interior space with a white tone incorporates media art that represents the sense of seasons, adding dynamism to the interior design. The dishes served in tapas style are based on recipes from ancient literature but reinterpreted with a modern touch. The cuisine at Blgre utilizes fermented ingredients such as ganjang (Soy Sauce) and doenjang (Soybean Paste ) made from Paju soybeans and kimchi. The dishes aim to preserve the original flavors of the ingredients. Various Korean liquors and wines are available, allowing for pairing with Korean-style tapas.

title: Cheongsong Headquarters Hamheung Naengmyeon
short_description: Cheongsong Headquarters Hamheung Naengmyeon was founded by the current owner, who inherited the philosophy and technique from her mother, who ran a cold noodle restaurant in Busan after fleeing during the Korean War. Loved for its consistent taste and sincerity, it is a local favorite in Yeonhui-dong. Its signature dish is raw fish cold noodles, topped generously with aged flatfish from Yeonan, offering a distinctive delicacy.

title: Jusindang Yongsan Branch
short_description:
This is the Jusindang Yongsan Branch, the next generation of the Jusindang brand that transformed Sindang-dong into hip-dang-dong. Jusindang Yongsan Branch is a Korean dining bar that features a facade and interior that modernly interprets Korean shamanic aesthetics, serves fusion Korean cuisine presented by internationally trained chefs, and offers a harmonious blend of original cocktails and premium whiskey—from the first floor reached through a mystical transitional space to the second floor that maximizes openness. Jusindang Yongsan Branch offers a time that satisfies all five senses with various seating options and private rooms. Experience the level of meticulous Korean dining that cannot be found in existing dining bars, from dinner to the lingering atmosphere of the bar! Experience it all at once at Jusindang Yongsan Branch!

Beyond a simple visit, a memorable space. We look forward to seeing you at the Jusindang Yongsan Branch.

title: PLANT
short_description: A 100% vegan restaurant and bakery cafe that promotes a healthy vegan lifestyle. It offers a diverse range of vegan dishes including salad bowls, rice bowls, wraps, pasta, and burgers, while their cakes made entirely from plant-based ingredients can also be custom-ordered to make special occasions even more meaningful.

title: Ongoing
short_description: Café Ongoing, run by a Seochon native, offers a thoughtfully curated selection of drinks and desserts with a soft, refined flavor. Their standout, the "Ongoing Latte," blends misutgaru (roasted grain powder), ice cream, and espresso, creating a rich, nutty drink with deep flavor and just the right touch of sweetness—ideal for those who enjoy something distinct. Another must-try is the roasted sweet potato brûlée, a favorite among regulars for its unforgettable flavor. Paired with sweet treats like Basque cheesecake, financiers, and sablé cookies, the café's offerings perfectly complement a quiet moment. The interior reflects the owner’s warm, careful attention to detail, creating an inviting space to sip coffee and unwind while gazing out at Seochon’s charming streets. It feels ideal for reflecting on a creative project or soaking in inspiration—perfect for those who enjoy places with heart and soul.

title: Myeongdongjeong
short_description: This is an authentic Korean traditional full-course meal (hanjeongsik) specialty restaurant using halal meat, presenting the depth of Korean cuisine and elegant table settings based on royal court dishes. It's a place where you can experience Korean traditional food culture with dignity through refined and harmonious flavors.

title: Seongwon Jeonju Kongnamul Gukbap
short_description: Seongwon Jeonju Kongnamul Gukbap is a specialty restaurant founded in 1937 by Kim So-seon, the original owner who introduced this bean Kongnamul Gukbap. The restaurant began in Myeong-dong and boasts a long history. Despite the turmoil of war, Kim So-seon opened the restaurant to support her family. The crispy kimchi pancake served before the main meal stimulates the appetite, while the signature bean sprout soup, with its blend of various ingredients, offers a perfectly spicy and refreshing taste. The multilingual menu also makes it easy for international tourists to visit and enjoy the food.

title: Busanjib Hongdae
short_description: This is the Hongdae branch of Busanjip, a Myeongdong landmark famous among tourists for halal Korean food. Here, visitors can enjoy not only a variety of traditional Korean dishes but also Korean-style fried chicken and charcoal barbecue, all in one place. This is a must-visit gourmet spot for experiencing diverse Korean cuisine made with Halal ingredients you can trust.

title: ASHLEY QUEENS DUNDUN DONGDAEMUN BRANCH
short_description:
Want to immerse yourself in the Korean lifestyle? Dine where Koreans really line-up! Ashley Queens is Korea's No. 1 Buffet Brand that serves 20 million customers yearly. With over 320 seats, Ashley Queens Dundun Dongdaemun Branch accommodates all occasions. Come with your friends, family and loved ones or by yourself!


100 Minutes of Unlimited Food, Come Enjoy our 130 Menus!

From Korean delicacies to Western favorites, try new flavors while indulging in your favorites.

title: Youthmungan
short_description: Youthmungan is a restaurant led by Father Lee Moon-soo, who has also appeared on the popular variety show 'You Quiz on the Block.' It was established to provide a warm meal to young people under the auspices of the Claret Missionary Society. This place, well-known for its value-for-money dining, is a beautiful restaurant operated with the support of sponsors and volunteers. You can enhance the flavor of the kimchi stew by adding extra side dishes and the main ingredients, tofu and meat, for an additional cost. Additionally, unlimited refills of plain rice are provided.

title: Taj Palace Itaewon
short_description: This is an Indian cuisine specialty restaurant offering various menus and courses including tandoori chicken, butter chicken curry, plain naan, and thali, as well as vegetarian menu options. All food is prepared with halal ingredients, and the restaurant operates as a buffet on weekends.

title: Yundal Ori
short_description: A true local favorite in Yeongdeungpo, this restaurant has been loved by neighborhood residents for years. Diners can enjoy duck prepared in many ways, from fresh unseasoned duck for grilling and Spicy Stir-Fried Duck to richly flavored smoked duck. More than just a tourist-friendly spot, it’s the perfect place to discover a hidden gem with genuine culinary depth.

title: Necktie Man Galchi Dongtae
short_description: This is a braised hairtail fish specialty restaurant located in the hairtail alley of Namdaemun Market, characterized by generous portions and carefully prepared side dishes. The braised hairtail fish, featuring rich broth combined with spicy seasoning, is the restaurant's signature dish and has been consistently loved by diners visiting Namdaemun Market.

title: House of Vinyl Yeonhui Branch
short_description: A striking white building catches the eye, and following the music inside, you're welcomed by a spacious interior. The white walls are paired with carefully placed wood and black furnishings, creating a modern yet comfortable ambiance. Large windows and the high ceiling connecting the first and second floors lend the space an open, airy feel. Music played directly from an LP player fills every corner, with the subtle crackles adding to the venue’s charm. Enjoy the serene atmosphere with a pavlova topped with cream and a selection of filter coffees brewed with beans to suit your taste.

title: GlutenFree 6Day-Chicken
short_description: See  Seoul`s  Panted Korean  Crispy  Rice-flour  Chicken. A patented gluten-free restaurant loved by people around the  world.  Trusted by individulas with celiac disease from the United States,the United Kingdom,Australia,and beyond.  6Day Chicken is a reliable K-food chicken brand you can enjoy with confidence.   With its irresistibly crispy texture anad outsanding flavor,  6Day Chicken proves that gluten free can be truly delicious.

title: India Chef
short_description: This Indian restaurant is led by a chef with 30 years of experience who prepares dishes firsthand. Through authentic tandoori chicken, freshly handmade naan, and a variety of curries, it delivers the rich flavors of traditional spices and the essence of India’s unique culinary culture.

title: Upstanding Coffee
short_description: Located in Haebangchon, the Upstanding cafe is a must-visit hotspot featuring a unique interior. This cafe has undergone a major transformation from a rundown and old neighborhood market into a hip and atmospheric space, featuring a stylish spiral staircase inside. It's a great place to enjoy a comfortable cup of coffee with family, friends, or a partner.

title: Palpan-dong Little Gimbap & Toast
short_description: Featured on the TV show You Quiz on the Block, Palpan Gimbap is a famous eatery known for its long lines. The menu includes gimbap, toast, and fish cake soup. The signature item, Palpan Gimbap, has less rice and is filled generously, allowing customers to enjoy the original taste of the ingredients. The seating consists of a bar table for four, and most customers choose takeout.

title: Delhi India
short_description: This fusion Indian restaurant is run by an Indian owner, offering flavors that even first-timers can enjoy without being overwhelmed by the strong spices of traditional Indian cuisine. Its signature dish is butter chicken, served in a mild curry that highlights the dish’s tender richness. With a variety of appealing options, the restaurant invites you to discover a new side of Indian food.

title: Nusantaraku
short_description: This bistro, rooted in Indonesian cuisine, offers a clean and refined take on Asian local food. Its appeal lies in authentic flavors recreated with ingredients sourced directly from Southeast Asia and halal-certified meats. The signature dish is nasi goreng, where diners can choose chicken, lamb, or beef prepared in various styles—grilled, fried, or seasoned.

title: King Kebab Itaewon
short_description: This is a kebab specialty restaurant that faithfully recreates authentic Turkish flavors, where a Turkish chef personally makes everything from bread to sauce, delivering the true essence of kebab.

title: Ihwa Ohana
short_description: Located in an alley in Ihwa-dong, Ihwa Ohana is a Japanese restaurant whose name means the flower of Ihwa-dong. Although the indoor space is somewhat compact, consisting of an indoor bar counter, tables are placed outside in the alley to create an outdoor street atmosphere. You can enjoy your meal while looking at the warm alley scenery from the outdoor tables, and since it is operated together with 508shop located right next door, you can purchase food and drinks there to enjoy together.

title: Cheil Jemyunso Yeouido IFC Mall Branch
short_description:
It is a casual dining restaurant that presents exquisite kalguksu and shabu-shabu, containing the long-standing know-how and secret recipes of Cheil Jemyunso, along with premium Korean dishes that pair well with traditional liquor. You can enjoy a variety of Korean food in a space that captures the mood of Korea in a modern way, and there are cozy private room spaces available for intimate gatherings. Furthermore, through spatial lighting direction, you can feel distinctly different atmospheres during the day and night.

For lunch, enjoy a neat and hearty meal with high-quality noodle dishes, suyuk (boiled beef slices), and jeon (Korean pancakes). For dinner, savor various alcoholic beverages, including traditional liquor, alongside premium dishes, and host a meal for your esteemed guests or enjoy an atmospheric gathering.

title: Jayondo Salt Bread in Seongsu
short_description:
Jayondo Salt Bread offers a single signature item 'salt bread' crafted through extensive testing of over 100 ingredients and 1,000 baking trials. The result is a uniquely flavorful bread made with just three special ingredients and plenty of patience.


Only salt bread is available, and it is sold exclusively for takeout. Due to high demand, a wait is often expected. The bread is freshly baked and sold six times a day, so it’s recommended to visit according to the baking schedule:

(9:00 AM / 12:30 PM / 2:00 PM / 3:30 PM / 5:00 PM / 6:30 PM)

title: YANG IN HWAN DAE Hongdae
short_description: This restaurant presents marinated lamb barbecue reinterpreted through Korean cuisine. Amid Hongdae’s trendy food culture, it offers a unique charm, while its Halal-certified lamb allows visitors to dine with peace of mind. Inspired by the Korean tradition of “food as medicine“, the marinades bring out flavors that are both refined and wholesome.

title: Koraebul
short_description:
Koraebul Gangnam Yeoksam Main Branch is a Korean fine dining restaurant specializing in seafood, located in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul. Established in 2002 by the first-generation owner, a native of Yeongdeok, with the intention of introducing East Coast seafood cuisine to Seoul, it has been operating in the same location for 24 years as a single flagship establishment. It is a premier seafood restaurant in Yeoksam, Gangnam, visited by approximately 30,000 customers annually.


The menu is primarily composed of seafood sourced directly from the East Coast. Seafood is managed in in-house aquariums, and ingredients of the day are prepared and served immediately. Major menu items include Dokdo Shrimp, Botan Shrimp, Spiny Lobster, 10-Year-Old Wild Rock Oysters, Mulgomtang (Snailfish Soup), Dodari Ssukguk (Flounder and Mugwort Soup), Mineotang (Croaker Soup), Whale Meat, and Pohang-style Mulhoe (Cold Raw Fish Soup). For lunch, meal sets accompanied by side dishes and hot stone pot rice are served, while dinner offers seafood course meals and signature menu-centric compositions.


Koraebul has been featured in various media outlets, including being introduced as one of CNN's Best Restaurants in Seoul in 2012, as well as on France's France3TV, tvN's Wednesday Food Talk, SBS's Live Broadcast Today, MBC's Omniscient Interfering View, and SBS's Running Man. Additionally, it has been continuously selected by the Blue Ribbon Survey for 15 consecutive years from 2012 to 2026.

title: London Bagel Museum Dosan
short_description: A bagel specialty bakery café with an interior that seems to have transported the atmosphere of London and a simple yet chewy taste that is exceptional. More than 10 types of bagels, cream cheese, and jam are available, and soup that goes well with bagels is also sold, so be sure to try it if you come to Seoul.

title: Wonhalmae Wonjo Dakhanmari
short_description: Originating in Seoul’s Dongdaemun and now loved internationally, Dakhanmari(Whole Chicken Stew) is the star dish here. Among the many restaurants on Dongdaemun Dakhanmari Street, this place is regarded as one of the originals. Featured on TV multiple times, it invites you to experience the harmony of broth, chicken, and noodles simmering together in a single pot.

title: Gonggangab
short_description: Gonggangab is a cafe in Euljiro that offers a creative space and a unique menu. The cafe attracts a steady stream of visitors with its trendy exposed concrete interior and lighting. One of its signature dishes is the Vanilla Custard Pudding Bingsu, which features vanilla pudding, custard cream, milk bingsu, and nougatine, offering an impressive visual and taste experience. Other popular desserts include the Pudding Choco Mousse Plate and Mint Choco Basque Cheesecake. Specialty drinks like Space Milk Coffee and Crème Brûlée Latte are also available. You can also order whole cakes by contacting us via Instagram DM two days in advance.

title: Dosuhyang
short_description: Dosuhyang is a renowned North Korean-style injeolmi specialty store and is considered one of Seoul’s top three rice cake shops. It is especially famous for its injeolmi coated in geopi red bean powder—red beans with the skins removed. Adhering to the principle of same-day production and sale, advance reservations are required. The shop gained popularity after celebrities were seen purchasing its products as gifts. Dosuhyang is also well known as a souvenir shop for traditional Korean tteok. Available in small, medium, and large sizes, the rice cakes can be wrapped in luxurious traditional Korean wrapping cloth (bojagi), making them ideal for elegant gift-giving.

title: Café Turtle
short_description: Turtle is a vegan café that offers desserts so flavorful that they do not taste like vegan desserts. It serves a variety of desserts, including Strawberry Shortcake, Pistachio Raspberry Cake, Red Bean Bingsu, and Mango Bingsu. The café is frequented by both vegans and non-vegans who appreciate healthy and delicious treats. It is a perfect destination for those seeking special and tasty desserts.

title: Coffee Hanyakbang
short_description:
Coffee Hanyakbang opened its doors in a timeless alley of Euljiro, embodying Korean aesthetics and the sentiment of the enlightenment period. While European styles dominated the era, the café focused on reviving forgotten native elements.


The space is filled with objects such as old mother-of-pearl cabinets, woodwork, and tiles, each carrying the memory of time. Located on the site of Hye Min Seo, where the historical physician Heo Jun cared for the people, the café offers a heartfelt cup of coffee and a piece of sweet comfort.

title: Cafe Sasa
short_description: Named after the sound of "trees swaying in the wind," Sasa is a hanok café that reinterprets traditional and modern flavors with its unique desserts and drinks. Located along Seosulla-gil, it provides a quiet, reflective space for visitors looking to pause and unwind. The menu features a variety of Korean-inspired desserts and drinks, each named to harmonize with the character of Seosulla-gil, enhancing the space's ambiance. One of Sasa’s highlights is its seasonal menu, which complements the changing scenery along Seosulla-gil, making each visit a refreshing experience. Housed in a beautiful hanok building, Sasa occasionally hosts pop-up stores, offering guests a chance to try new and creative beverages in a unique setting.

title: Lazy Burger Club Buam Branch
short_description:
Lazy Burger Club is a famous spot in Buam-dong for handmade burgers. Located on the second floor, the restaurant features a clean, comfortable American-inspired atmosphere, with a wide window on one side. On sunny days, it's the perfect place to enjoy a burger while leisurely enjoying the Buam-dong view.
Lazy Burger Club allows customers to customize their burgers to their tastes. You can choose the weight of the meat and add toppings like patties, cheese, and bacon, making it possible to enjoy a personalized burger experience.

title: Jeonjuzip
short_description: Located in an alley within the market, Jeonjujip exudes the authentic vibe of a true old eatery, from its menu to its pricing. You’ll find a wide variety of dishes ranging from street food-style side dishes to meals and noodles. The most popular items are Spicy Braised Chicken (Dakbokkeumtang) and Grilled Pork Belly (Samgyeopsal). On cool days, you can enjoy Seoul's unique Yajang (outdoor drinking) culture—eating and drinking delicious food in the heart of the city.

title: Darak
short_description: Darak is a famous restaurant in Jangan, Seoul, famous for instant tteokbokki that appeared on TV programs as a tteokbokki master. Tteokbokki is served in two types: a tray and a hot pot, and you can choose a variety of sauces in addition to the basic ingredients. The wall of the store is covered with the names and dates of the customers who came here. It's clear that the restaurant has not only spent years, but also shared a rich, inexpensive, simple yet nostalgic taste.

title: Ginkgo Seoul
short_description: Ginkgo Seoul is a hanok cafe. Built in 1956 beside a ginkgo tree that has long been a fixture of Sangsamaeul Village, this house was restored to its old appearance after 22 years and designated as a preserved house by Seoul Metropolitan Government. This single species ginkgo tree, which has endured for a long time and cannot survive alone, felt very similar to this hanok space that has protected this place for a long time, so the name of this space was chosen as Ginkgo Seoul after the scientific name of the ginkgo tree, ginkgo biloba. Ginkgo Seoul does not allow pets and is a no kids zone, allowing entry for those aged 12 and above.

title: Tosokchon Samgyetang
short_description: Tosokchon Samgyetang, located near Gyeongbokgung Palace, is a famous traditional Samgyetang specialized restaurant in Seoul, visited by many foreign tourists. Operating since 1983 under the founding philosophy of "making the healthiest food in Korea," Tosokchon Samgyetang strives to preserve food culture and tradition with its unique, differentiated taste developed through strictly selected ingredients and long years of research. We hope you enjoy Korean food culture in a Hanok with a traditional atmosphere that blends well with the sensibility of Seochon.

title: Yeokjeon Hoegwan
short_description: Founded in 1929 and currently in its third generation, Yeokjeon Hoegwan boasts 97 years of tradition as one of Mapo’s most renowned restaurants. Its signature “Crispy Bulgogi” is grilled over charcoal using fresh beef from Majang-dong, offering a taste loved by all generations. The restaurant’s house-made “Yeokjeonju,” brewed in its own distillery, won the Grand Prize in the Takju Raw Makgeolli General Category at the 2021 Korea Liquor Awards. Frequented by loyal patrons and celebrities alike, it is also famous as the restaurant visited by Hollywood actor Tom Cruise during his stay in Korea.

title: Jongno Samgyetang
short_description:
This is a samgyetang (Korean ginseng chicken soup) specialty restaurant that has been carefully operated with dedication for two generations.

This establishment is favored by regulars seeking rich and hearty samgyetang, offering a variety of flavors including abalone, herbal, and perilla seed samgyetang.

title: ALADDIN’S LAMB
short_description:
Aladdin‘s Lamb in Jamsil is a rare place in Korea where you can enjoy authentic Arabic-style lamb barbecue. Loved not only by tourists but also by

local food enthusiasts, this restaurant offers more than just Arabic lamb dishes — the menu also features Korean-style reinterpretations such as

barbecues, stews, and hot pots, delivering a truly unique dining experience.

title: Surokgok Giroksil
short_description: Surokgok Giroksil is a bookstore and book bar created to remember and record Korean songs and lyrics for a long, long time. Individual listening to LPs, CDs, and cassette tapes is possible at each seat, and it provides a space where you can read a book while listening to music, have quiet conversations, work, or just simply rest. We hope you can meet your songs recorded in a certain era here, and please enjoy Surokgok Giroksil.

title: PLAYDOGS
short_description: PLAYDOGS is a pet experience cafe located near Konkuk University and Children's Grand Park in Gwangjin-gu, where you can meet both dogs and cats. It is a great space even for those who love animals but find it difficult to raise them directly, as you can comfortably spend time interacting with and giving treats to people-friendly companion dogs and cats. Equipped with various entertainments such as board games and individual spaces, it is well-suited as a venue for unique dates, gatherings with friends, and family outings. For the safety and pleasant environment of the pets, bringing personal pets is restricted, so it is recommended to check the usage regulations before visiting.

title: The Makan Yeouido
short_description: This is the Yeouido branch of The Makan, a Malaysian restaurant recognized in the Blue Ribbon Survey, one of Korea’s leading dining guides, for its refined cuisine created by chefs with five-star hotel experience in Kuala Lumpur. Here, you can enjoy authentic Malaysian flavors in a setting that blends Yeouido’s urban sophistication with the laid-back atmosphere of a Southeast Asian resort.

title: Café Kiiro
short_description: Café Kiiro is a quiet space dedicated to the enjoyment of desserts. Guests can taste seasonal cakes that change with the time of year. Due to its small size, there is usually a waiting line, but takeout is available without waiting. Feel the sense of the seasons through Café Kiiro’s unique desserts in a space that feels like a cozy attic.

title: KAMPUNGKU
short_description: This restaurant features various types of nasi goreng and nasi lemak prepared by a Malaysian chef, as well as popular Korean dishes made with halal ingredients. It's the perfect place for travelers seeking a diverse menu they can trust.

title: Bookhaebingsu
short_description: Bookhaebingsu is a café in Sindang-dong, renowned for its finely textured snowflake bingsu. Their signature item is the snowflake milk bingsu, but they offer various options, including snowflake strawberry bingsu and snowflake Oreo bingsu. Each bingsu is served in a single serving size, perfect for solo visits and groups wanting to sample different flavors. The red bean topping is served separately, allowing you to add it for a rich and sweet taste gradually. Except for Fridays and Saturdays, Bookhaebingsu stays open late into the night so that you can enjoy bingsu even during the late hours. In addition to bingsu, the café also offers coffee, various drinks, and desserts. Its spacious and pleasant antique atmosphere makes it an ideal place to cool off on a hot summer night.

title: Gyeongseong Gogikun
short_description: This restaurant offers quality beef at reasonable prices, with a variety of cuts to choose from. Charcoal-grilled beef and the rich flavor of beef radish soup are must-tries. You can also enjoy yukhoe bibimbap with fresh beef tartare and the special basil doenjang sulbap, where basil and soybean paste blend in perfect harmony.

title: MOWa
short_description:
MOWa was created to provide a space where people can create cherished memories around wine. In addition to a wine tunnel showcasing a wide variety of wines, MOWa provides a tranquil "empty" space for a minimalist vibe and a private, comfortable "full" space for a more intimate setting.
Indulge in exquisite contemporary cuisine at MOWa that pleases your eyes and taste buds. The perfect spot for a special anniversary date in Myeongdong or for meetings and gatherings where privacy matters.
Memories of wine and a wine dining experience completed by your own interpretation—this is MOWa.

[Variations of Colorful Flavors]  
A new harmony of flavors created from familiar ingredients.  At the contemporary dining hotspot MOWa, you can savor unique fusion dishes that bring fresh twists to traditional Korean cuisine.  Led by talented Head Chef Moon Won-gi, who honed his skills at renowned restaurants such as SABU Seoul, Gourmetry, and Mingles.

[Wine with Different Depth]
At Myeongdong's MOWa, you’ll find over 1,000 varieties of wine, along with a selection of 30 whiskies, cocktails, and non-alcoholic cocktails, offering a wide range of choices.  Each drink is served in the optimal glass to enhance its flavor, elevating the tasting experience of both wine and spirits.

[An Artistic Space and Atmosphere]  
MOWa transforms its interior into a work of art. Its 50-meter-long wine tunnel is filled with over 1,000 varieties of wine and has a mysterious ambiance created by green lighting.  With spaciously arranged tables, thoughtfully divided areas, and private rooms, MOWa is the perfect spot for anniversary dates, private meetings, and gatherings where privacy is key.

title: Eid
short_description: This is a Korean restaurant that prepares food with halal ingredients, and it has been consistently loved by Muslim tourists. It offers a variety of Korean dishes including samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), bibimbap, bulgogi, and seasonal dishes made with fresh seasonal ingredients.

title: チョンゲチョン(清渓川)
short_description: チョンゲチョン(清渓川)はソウル市の西東を横断するように流れる10.84kmの河川です。朝鮮王朝時代(1932～1910年)には、生活排水を流出させる下水道の役割を果たしていました。その後、覆蓋事業の一貫で埋め立てられ、高架道路と姿を変えた時期もありました。しかし、2003年からチョンゲチョン(清渓川)の復元工事が行なわれ、2005年には現在の姿へと修復されました。チョンゲチョン(清渓川)は「清渓広場」を始点にハンガン(漢江)へ向かって流れており、その間には全部で22の橋が架かっています。見どころも多く、中でも様々なイベントも開催される「チョンゲ(清渓)広場」はチョンゲチョン(清渓川)のランドマークになっています。

title: ロッテ百貨店本店
short_description:
ロッテ百貨店本店は韓国を代表するショッピングスペースで、海外の有名ブランドから中低価の韓国内ブランドに至るまで、様々なアイテムを販売しています。また、免税店やギャラリーなどもあり、ショッピング以外の見どころも満載です。さらに地下1階の食料品売り場はお土産ショッピングにも最適です。


きめ細やかなサービス
ロッテ百貨店は韓国内ブランドから海外の有名ブランドまでを取り揃えた充実のラインナップと、きめ細やかなサービスに定評があります。館内には、授乳スペースや乳児用のバスルームを備えた乳児休憩室など乳幼児対応のサービスをはじめ、荷物を保管できるロッカーや憩いのスペースも設けられています。また、案内デスクでは、日本語・英語・中国語で基本的な通訳をはじめ、事後免税制度案内などの案内を受けることができます。

明洞での観光
さらに、百貨店前にはソウルの名所の中で外国人観光客にもっとも人気の高いミョンドン(明洞)の街が広がっています。明洞は大型ショッピングモールや人気ブランドのショップなどが軒を連ねているほか、韓国初の歴史ある聖堂「ミョンドン・ソンダン(明洞聖堂)」、ソウル市街地の夜景を一望できる「Nソウルタワー」などにも近く、観光にも最適です。ソウル最大のショッピングエリアであると同時に、飲食店や屋台も多いエリアです。

title: セジョン(世宗)文化会館
short_description: セジョン(世宗)文化会館は、地下3階、地上6階建てで、韓国の古い建築様式を現代的に組み合わせて造られた複合文化スペース。大劇場や小劇場、美術館、コンベンションセンター、コンファレンスホール、小会議室、噴水広場、デッキプラザ、サムチョンガク(三清閣)などがあります。地下鉄5号線クァンファムン駅1番出口を利用すると便利。

title: ミョンドン(明洞)実弾射撃場
short_description: ミョンドン(明洞)実弾射撃場は繁華街のミョンドン(明洞)にある射撃場で、最先端の安全装置を配備し、射撃専門安全要員の指導のもと安全に射撃体験ができます。様々な銃器類と完璧な防音施設が備わっています。

title: ロッテワールドアイスリンク
short_description: ロッテワールド アイスリンクは、チャムシル(蚕室)ロッテワールドの室内にあります。アイスリンクの周りには合計850席の座りやすい椅子が用意され、世界中の料理が味わえるレストラン街やゲームセンターやなど様々な施設も備わっています。フィギュアスケートやスピードスケートの講習も行われています。

title: ポンウンサ(奉恩寺)
short_description: ポンウンサ(奉恩寺)は新羅時代に建立された寺院で、その歴史は千年を超えます。華厳経や、木に文字を彫り印刷した木版本をはじめ、数多くの有形文化財を保有しています。毎週木曜日には、外国人のための｢木曜テンプルライフ｣も開催しています。寺院案内、蓮花作り、茶道試演、僧侶との談話など、すべてのプログラムが英語で行われます。ポンウンサ(奉恩寺)の入口すぐの場所にある外国人案内所で即日の受付ができます。参加費用は1人20,000ウォンです。

title: 文化駅ソウル284(旧ソウル駅舎)
short_description: 文化駅ソウル284は日本統治時代に建築されたソウル駅舎で、現在は複合文化スペースとして使用されています。1階は様々な公演と展示のためのスペースで、2階は展示とセミナー、会議のためのスペースとして利用中。文化駅ソウル284の観覧料は無料で、各公演と展示の入場料は別途。

title: ギャラリア百貨店名品館
short_description:
洗練された狎鴎亭・(アックジョン)・清潭洞(チョンダムドン)エリアに位置する高級デパートです。世界の有名ファッションブランドを取り扱い、若いファッションリーダーを対象にした「EAST」と、厳選した韓国内外の高級ブランドをメインに扱う「WEST」に分かれています。また地下には食品館があり、マーケットやデリ、フードコートも揃っています。建築家Ben Van Berkelによって設計されたLEDのユニークな外観は、名品館WESTに華やかさを添えています。
名品館EASTには、韓国ではギャラリア百貨店でのみ店舗を持つフランスの老舗ブランド「ゴヤール(GOYARD)」、ハンド・クラフトによる高級感あふれるクラシカルなメンズ・ファッションのイタリア発ブランド「ステファノ・リッチ(STEFANO RICCI)」などが入店しています。

title: 戦争記念館
short_description:
地下鉄６号線三角地(サムガクチ、Samgakji)駅から出てすぐのところにある「戦争記念館」。その名の通り、韓国が関わった戦争の博物館で、全部で13,000点以上の実物やレプリカが展示されています。およそ全体の３分の２が「朝鮮戦争(1950-53)」をテーマにした展示となっています。毎週金曜日には、戦争記念館前で国軍儀仗隊のパレードが行われます。メインは何と言っても陸海空の三軍揃ってのファンシードリル。ライフル銃を右左に回したり投げたりしながらフォーメーションを作っていくさまは、見ごたえたっぷりです。無料で観覧することができます。
日時：毎年４・５・６・10・11月の毎週金曜日(酷寒期と酷暑期を除く) 　14：00～14：50

title: ヤンファジン(楊花津)外国人宣教師墓地
short_description: ヤンファジン(楊花津)外国人宣教師廟院はソウル市マポ(麻浦)区ハプチョンドン(合井洞)にある外国人宣教師の共同墓地で、韓国を愛し韓国に骨を埋めることを願った外国人宣教師とその家族の安息の地となっています。韓国基督教宣教100周年記念教会が管理しており、韓国宣教記念館が設立されました。

title: Leeum美術館
short_description:
Leeum美術館は、サムスングループの創始者、イ・ビョンチョル氏が生前に所蔵していた美術品約15,000点を一般にも公開するためにオープンしました。館名の「Leeum」とは、イ・ビョンチョルの名字の英語表記「Lee」と「Museum」を用いた造語です。

Leeum美術館は韓国の伝統美術品を展示する「ミュージアム1」と、韓国や世界のアーティストによる現代美術品を展示する「ミュージアム2」、子供達のための「サムスン児童教育文化センター」の3棟で構成され、それぞれの建物を世界的な建築家であるマリオ・ボッタ、ジャン・ヌベール、レム・コールハースが1棟ずつ設計しました。Leeum美術館は建物そのものが芸術作品であるだけでなく、屋外にいたるまでアート界の世界的巨匠達の作品が展示されています。

Leeum美術館についてよくある質問
Leeum美術館の観覧は予約が必要ですか？
Leeum美術館は、事前予約が必要です。予約は、観覧日の14日前から可能で、一度に最大4人まで予約ができます。美術館での入場券購入は、事前予約に余りがあった場合にのみ可能です。(2025年基準)
Leeum美術館のデジタルガイドは無料で利用できますか？
はい。無料でレンタルできます。デジタルガイドとは、展示作品の前に近づくと作品の解説が自動再生されるデジタル端末です。小学生以上からレンタルが可能で、パスポート、外国人登録証などの身分証明書を美術館に預ける必要があります。デジタルガイドは、韓国語、英語、中国語、日本語に対応しています。(2025年基準)
Leeum美術館の常設展示は無料で観覧できますか？
はい。常設展示は無料で観覧できます。常設展示も予約制で運営されていますので、予約をしてからお越しください。(2025年基準)

title: スペース・シー (SPACE C)
